In it, the invisible one, from your substance, appeared visibly in our flesh; and, being one with you, he came to us, begotten not in time, not inferior in nature, but born in time. Through him, etc.

**For the conclusion** [Note: In the Swedish Queen manuscript and in Pamelianus this is read after Communion. In Pamelianus there follows a prayer over the people, absent from the Swedish Queen manuscript, as is another prayer for Vespers.].—Grant us, O Lord, we ask, to draw breath through the celebration of the recently commemorated Nativity of your Only-Begotten Son, whose heavenly mystery nourishes and refreshes us. Through the same Christ our Lord, etc.

**At Vespers.**—Grant, merciful God, that both the minds of believers may be prepared and the hearts of unbelievers may be subdued to receive the unique mystery of the Nativity of your Son. Through the same Christ our Lord.

## On the Vigil of the Lord during the Night

O God, who have made this most holy night shine with the illumination of the true light, grant, we ask, that just as we have come to know on earth the mysteries of that light, so may we also enjoy its joys in heaven. Who live with you, etc.

**6** [Note: In the Pamelian manuscript: “secret prayer,” contrary to the Swedish Queen manuscript.] **Over the offerings.**—May the offering of today’s festival be acceptable to you, O Lord, we ask, so that, by your gracious gift, through these most holy exchanges we may be found in the likeness of him in whom our substance is with you. Who lives and reigns, God, in unity.

[Col. 0030A] **Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and conducive to salvation, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, [Note: In Pamelianus: “because through the mystery of the incarnate Word,” etc., as in modern missals. The Swedish Queen, Gemeticus, and Theoderic manuscripts agree. After the preface Pamelianus has: “within the action, ‘Communicating and celebrating the sacred night,’ etc.,” as in the missal. The Theoderic and Gemeticus manuscripts support this. It is absent from the Swedish Queen manuscript. The manuscripts differ so greatly from one another that observing all the variant readings requires almost immeasurable labor.] through Christ our Lord. The power of whose divine Nativity was generated by the greatness of your innate virtue. We proclaim him whom you have always had as Son, begotten before eternal ages, since you have never lacked the name of eternal Father in its fullness and perfection; and we confess him equal to you in honor, majesty, and power, with the Holy Spirit, and we believe one Majesty in the triune name. Therefore, with angels and archangels, with thrones and dominions, and with the whole army of the heavenly host, we sing the hymn of your glory, saying without end:

Therefore, most merciful Father, etc.

[Col. 0030B] **Blessing.**—Almighty God, who by the incarnation of his Only-Begotten dispelled the darkness of the world and by his glorious birth illumined this most holy night, may he drive away from you the darkness of vices and illumine your hearts with the light of virtues. Amen. And he who wished the great joy of his most holy Nativity to be announced by an angel to shepherds, may he himself pour over you the most welcome shower of his blessing and, with that shepherd himself, lead you to the eternal pastures of everlasting joys. Amen. And he who through his incarnation joined earthly things to heavenly things, may he fill you with the nectar of inward peace and good will and make you companions of the heavenly host. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, etc. [Note: This blessing, which does not appear here in the Vatican and later editions, occurs in the *Book of Blessings* edited by Lambecius, which is found in the Gussanville edition. All the other blessings inserted into the Mass offices in the Menardian manuscript are also found there. In Lambecius it concludes: “May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom and dominion remain without end for ever and ever. Amen. May the blessing of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and the peace of the Lord be always with you.”]

**For the conclusion.**—Grant us, we ask, Lord our God, that we who rejoice in frequently celebrating the Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ may be worthy, through lives worthy of him, to belong to his company. Who lives with you, etc.

**At Matins.**—Look upon us, merciful God, and, as Christ is born, graciously display to human minds the light of supreme truth. Who lives and reigns with you.

## 7. Mass at Dawn on the Lord’s Nativity, or of Saint Anastasia

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who are flooded with the new light of your incarnate Word may reflect in our works what shines by faith in our minds. Through the same Christ our Lord.

**Another.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnity of your blessed martyr Anastasia may experience her intercession with you. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**Over the offerings.**—May our gifts, we ask, O Lord, prove suitable to the mysteries of today’s Nativity, so that, just as the one born as a human being shone forth as God, so may this earthly substance bestow upon us what is divine. Through the same Christ our Lord.

**Another.**—Receive graciously, we ask, O Lord, the gifts offered, and, with the merits of blessed Anastasia assisting, grant that they may serve for the help of our salvation. Through your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives with you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and conducive to salvation, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because today the true light of our Savior has gone forth, which has made all things clear to us both in understanding and in sight. Therefore, with angels and archangels, with thrones and dominions, and with the whole army of the heavenly host, we sing the hymn of your glory without end, saying.

**For the conclusion.**—May his sacrament, O Lord, continually renew us, whose unique Nativity drove away the old condition of humankind. Who lives with you.

**Another.**—You have satisfied your household with sacred gifts, O Lord; we ask you always to refresh us through the intercession of him whose solemnity we celebrate. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, etc.

## 8 Kalends of January.—On the Day of the Lord’s Nativity

[Note: In the Roman Calendar, as in the Pamelian edition and most manuscripts, “at Saint Peter” is read, where the station is indicated.]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the new Nativity in the flesh of your Only-Begotten Son may free us whom an ancient slavery holds beneath the yoke of sin. Who lives with you.

**Over the offerings.**—Sanctify, O Lord, the gifts offered by the new Nativity of your Only-Begotten, and cleanse us from the stains of our sins. Through the same Christ our Lord, etc.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and conducive to salvation, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because through the mystery of the incarnate Word a new light of your brightness has shone upon the eyes of our mind. Thus, while we visibly know God, may we be carried away through him by love of invisible things. Therefore, with angels …

Therefore, most merciful Father, etc., as above [Note: In Pamelianus after the preface appears: “within the action, ‘Communicating and celebrating the most sacred day on which the blessed and inviolate virginity of Mary …’” —with *nativitas* mistakenly printed for *intemerata virginitas*—etc.; these words are read in the Vatican and Gussanville editions and also in the Gemeticus manuscript. They are absent from the Swedish Queen manuscript.].

**Blessing.**—May almighty God bless you and stir up your attention toward heavenly things, he who made this most holy day solemn through the Nativity of his Son. Amen. And he who made him who is the Bread of angels become the food of the faithful in the manger, may he himself grant you in the present age to taste the sweetness of eternal joys and in the future lead you [Col. 0032A] to the fullness of eternal rewards. Amen. And he who wished his infancy to be clothed in humble cloths, may he himself clothe you with the adornments of heavenly garments. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom and dominion remain without end for ever and ever. Amen. May the blessing of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit be upon you. And may the peace of the Lord be always with you.

**For the conclusion.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the Savior of the world, born today, just as he is the author of our divine birth, may himself also be the giver of immortality. Who lives and reigns, God.

**Other prayers.**—Grant us, almighty God, that your Salvation, wondrous through the new light of heaven, which has gone forth today for the salvation of the world, may always arise in our hearts, which are continually being renewed. Who live with you.

**Another.**—Almighty and eternal God, who consecrated this day through the incarnation of your Word and the childbirth of the blessed virgin Mary, grant your peoples fellowship in this celebration, so that those who have been redeemed by your grace may be secure through your adoption. Through the same Christ our Lord.

**Another.**—God, foundation of our faith, who establish the gates of eternity in holy minds, as though on lofty mountains, with justice as their guardian, grant us to believe gloriously in you and to proclaim that your Son, our Lord, became human for the redemption of souls. Who live with you, etc.

**Another.**—Grant, we ask, O Lord, an increase of faith and security to your servants, so that those who glory in the Nativity of your Son, our Lord, may, under your guidance, feel no adversity from the world and may receive without end what they desire to celebrate in time. Through him.

**Another.**—O God, who, through the childbirth of the blessed virgin Mary, brought forth without human desire, made those who come into the members of your Son free from ancestral prejudices, grant, we ask, that, having received the newness of this creature, we may be stripped of the contagions of ancient corruption. Through the same Christ our Lord.

**Another.**—O God, who wondrously created the dignity of human substance and more wondrously restored it, grant us, we ask, to share in the divinity of him who deigned to become a sharer in our humanity, Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives with you.

**Another.**—Almighty and eternal God, who granted that in the Nativity of your Son, our Lord, the beginning and perfection of the whole of religion should stand firm, grant us, we ask, to be counted among those who share in him, in whom the whole sum of human salvation consists. Who lives and reigns, God.

**Another.**—Grant, we ask, O Lord, inviolable firmness of faith to your people, so that those who confess your Only-Begotten, eternal with you in your glory, [Col. 0033A] born in the truth of our body from a Virgin Mother, may be freed from present adversities and joined to enduring joys. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives with you.

## 7 Kalends of January.—The Nativity of Saint Stephen

[Note: In Pamelianus, “martyr,” as in the Vatican and Gussanville editions. It is absent from the Swedish Queen manuscript and the Roman Calendar, where no station is assigned; instead, for the Gospel is indicated: “Jesus said to the crowds of the Jews,” through “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord,” Matthew XXIII.].

Grant us, we ask, O Lord, to imitate what we celebrate, so that we may learn also to love our enemies, because we celebrate the birthday of him who knew how to pray even for his persecutors, O Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, O Lord, the gifts offered for the commemoration of your saints, [Note: After this prayer Pamelianus has the prayer “May they be pleasing to you,” etc., which is lacking in the Swedish Queen manuscript and absent from the Vatican, Gussanville, and other editions.] so that, just as passion made them glorious, devotion may make us innocent. Through the Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and conducive to salvation, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, as we recall the birthday of blessed Stephen, both Levite and martyr: he set before us venerable examples of faith, of sacred service, of excellent stewardship and chastity, of preaching and wondrous steadfastness, and of confession and patience. Therefore, rightly above all others, he follows the Nativity of your Son with the festival of his passion, [Col. 0033B] since the first martyr went before the glory of that Son’s eternity. Through whom your Majesty, etc.

**10. Blessing.**—May God, who crowned blessed Stephen the protomartyr both through the confession of faith and through the contest of martyrdom, surround your minds and lead you, in the present age, to the crown of righteousness and, in the future, to the crown of glory. Amen. Through the intercession of him who strove to possess this even amid the attacks of those who hurled stones, may he grant you always to abound in love of God and neighbor. Amen. Strengthened by his example and protected by his intercession, may you deserve to be blessed by him whom Stephen saw standing at the right hand of God. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, etc.

**For the conclusion.**—May the mysteries we have received assist us, O Lord, and, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Stephen, strengthen us with everlasting protection. Through him.

**Another.**—Almighty and eternal God, who consecrated the first fruits of the martyrs in the blood of the blessed Levite Stephen, grant, we ask, that he who prayed even for his persecutors may be an intercessor for us. Through him.

[Col. 0033D] **Another.**—O God, who mercifully redeemed us through the incarnation of your Only-Begotten, grant us the continual protection of your saints, by which we may be able to receive a share in the mystery of salvation. Through the same Christ our Lord.

**Another.**—We give thanks, O Lord, for your multiplied mercies toward us: you save us through the Nativity of your Son and sustain us through the supplication of the blessed martyr Stephen. Through the same Christ our Lord.

## 6 Kalends of January.—The Nativity of Saint John the Evangelist

[Note: In the Roman Calendar no station is mentioned. The same Gospel is noted as that which we read in modern missals. In Pamelianus entirely different prayers are assigned; one begins “at Saint Andrew.” The Swedish Queen manuscript contains some of them, but not all; indeed, the first three are absent.]

[Col. 0034A]

Enlighten your Church kindly, O Lord, so that, illuminated by the teachings of the blessed evangelist John, it may attain eternal gifts. Through him.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, O Lord, the gifts we bring to you on his solemnity, by whose patronage we trust to be delivered. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and conducive to salvation, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, as we commemorate the venerable birthday of your blessed apostle and evangelist John: who, accepting the call of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, rejected his earthly father so that he might find a heavenly one; having obtained in the kingdom [Col. 0034B] of heaven the seat of apostolic eminence, he who had despised the merely carnal nets of his father; and who was loved so familiarly by your Only-Begotten and approved by the gifts of immense grace that the same Lord, already placed upon the cross, appointed him as a substitute son for his virgin Mother, so that the virginity of the tested and beloved disciple might serve the integrity of the blessed Mother. For at the sacred banquet of the mystical supper he had reclined upon the very source of life, namely, the breast of the Savior. Drawing from it the heavenly streams of teaching that flowed perpetually, he was imbued with revelations so profound and mystical that, transcending every creature, he perceived them with an exalted mind and proclaimed with the evangelical voice that “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Therefore, with angels …

**Blessing.**—May almighty God deign to bless you through the intercession of the blessed apostle and evangelist John, through whom he wished the mysteries of his Word to be revealed to the Church. Amen. May he grant you that what John, inspired by the gift of the Holy Spirit, poured into your ears, you may be able to grasp in your minds through the gift of that same Spirit. Amen. Thus, instructed by his teaching concerning the divinity of our Redeemer, loving what he handed down and carrying out what he commanded, may you deserve to attain the gifts that the same Jesus Christ our Lord promised. May he himself deign to grant this.

**For the conclusion.**—Refreshed by heavenly food and drink, our God, we humbly entreat you that, in whose commemoration we have received these gifts, we may also be defended by his prayers. Through him.

**At Vespers.**—Being appeased, we ask, O Lord, by the supplication of the blessed evangelist John, grant us pardon and bestow eternal remedies. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—May we be helped, O Lord, by the prayers of the blessed evangelist John, so that what our ability cannot obtain may be granted to us through his intercession. Through him.

**Another.**—May the blessed evangelist John, we ask, O Lord, be the helper of our frailty, so that, pleading for us to you, he may be heard more abundantly. Through him.

**Another.**—O God, who through the mouth of your blessed apostle John opened to us the mysteries of your Word, grant, we ask, that what he poured excellently into our ears we may grasp through suitable instruction in understanding. Through him.

**Another.**—Almighty and eternal God, who have granted the venerable and holy joy of this day through the festival of your blessed apostle and evangelist John, grant, we ask, to your Church both to love what it has believed and to preach what he taught. Through him.

**Another.**—May your blessed evangelist John, we ask, O Lord, be present to your Church, so that he who is its perpetual teacher may never cease to be its intercessor. Through the Lord.

**Another.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may both understand suitably and confess truthfully the excellence of your Word which the blessed evangelist John affirmed. Through the same Christ our Lord.

## 5 Kalends of January.—The Birthday of the Innocents

[Note: In Pamelianus: “the Nativity of the holy Innocents.” “Holy” is absent from the Swedish Queen manuscript, the Roman Calendar, and the Vatican and Gussanville editions. In the same Pamelianus it is read “at Saint Paul.” The Roman Calendar is silent about the station; there the same Gospel is designated as in today’s Mass of the Holy Innocents.]

O God, whose proclamation the innocent martyrs confessed today, not by speaking but by dying, mortify in us all the evils of vices, so that the faith which our tongue speaks may also be confessed by the conduct of our life. Through him.

**Over the offerings.**—Be present, O Lord, to the gifts consecrated on the festival of the Innocents, and grant, we ask, [Col. 0035C] that we may imitate the sincerity of those whose infancy, dedicated to you, we venerate. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and conducive to salvation, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and that, in the precious deaths of the little ones whom wicked Herod slew with beastlike savagery because of the infancy of our Redeemer, we should proclaim the immense gifts of your clemency. In them grace alone shines forth more than will, [130] confession is clear before speech, [131] and suffering precedes limbs capable of suffering. They are Christ’s witnesses who had not yet come to know him. O infinite goodness! O ineffable mercy, which does not allow the merit of glory to perish for those slaughtered for his name, but grants salvation through regeneration to those drenched in their own blood and reckons to them the crown of martyrdom. Therefore, with angels, etc.

**Blessing.**—Almighty God, for whose Only-Begotten’s venerable infancy the savage cruelty of wicked Herod slew the crowds of innocent infants, may he grant you the most welcome gifts of his blessing. Amen. And he who granted them to confess his only Son, our Lord, not by speaking but by dying, may he grant you that the true faith which your tongue professes may also be confessed by upright conduct and blameless life. Amen. And he who received them as the first fruit of his holy Church, may he bring you, with the fruit of good works, to the joys of the eternal homeland. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom …

**For the conclusion.**—We have received votive gifts, O Lord; through the prayers of the saints, grant, we ask, that they may provide us with help both for the present life and for the eternal one. Through him.

**13. Another.** [Note: This prayer and the final one, “Help us,” etc., are absent from the Swedish Queen manuscript.]—O God, although you are great in great things, you nevertheless work wonders more gloriously in the small; grant us, we ask, to rejoice in the festival of those who bore witness to your Son, our Lord, even without speaking. Through the same Christ our Lord, etc.

**Another.**—May those whose innocence we solemnly celebrate today themselves ask for purity of mind for us, O Lord. Through him.

**Another.**—Help us, O Lord, we ask, through the prayer of those saints who, though they did not yet profess your Son with a human voice, were crowned with heavenly glory because of his Nativity. Through the same Christ our Lord.

## The Day before the Kalends of January.—The Nativity of Saint Sylvester, Pope. (133) On the same day, Saint Fulgentius, bishop.

[Note: “Pope” is absent from the Pamelian manuscript but present in the Swedish Queen manuscript. Neither contains what is added here concerning Saint Fulgentius, nor do the other commonly printed editions. In the Roman Calendar, where the title “pope” is not given to Saint Sylvester and no commemoration of Saint Fulgentius is made, the Gospel prescribed is: “Jesus said to his disciples: Watch,” through “he will appoint him over all his goods,” with no station.]

[Col. 0036C]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the venerable solemnity of your blessed confessor and pontiff Sylvester may increase both our devotion and our salvation. Through him.

**Over the offerings.**—May the loving prayer of your saints never be absent for us, O Lord; may it reconcile our gifts and always obtain your forgiveness for us. Through him.

**For the conclusion.**—We ask, almighty God, that the gift of today’s solemnity, accepted through the intercession of your blessed confessor Sylvester, may grant health both to our bodies and to our minds. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Be present to our prayers, O Lord, and do not allow those whom the glorious confession of your pontiff, blessed Sylvester, protects to be subjected to any dangers of mind or body. Through him.

## On the Kalends of January.—Within the Octave of the Lord

[Note: Although this feast does not receive the name of the Circumcision in the Roman Calendar—and the sacramentary books, both printed and manuscript, agree with it—the Gospel of the Circumcision is nevertheless assigned, beginning “after they had completed,” and extending through “and the glory of your people Israel.” No station is mentioned. In the Pamelian printed editions, however, with the Swedish Queen manuscript agreeing, it is read “at Saint Mary at the Martyrs.” Four final prayers enclosed in brackets in Pamelianus are absent from this manuscript. The preface and blessing found here, in which the Circumcision is mentioned, are not read in the Pamelian or Swedish Queen manuscripts. In the Roman Calendar the birthday of Saint [Col. 0037D] Mary is noted on the same day; this agrees very well with Saint Gregory’s Antiphonary as presented by Pamelianus. Perhaps for that reason the office of the feast of the Circumcision even now belongs for the most part to the most blessed Virgin.]

O God, who have granted the human race the rewards of eternal salvation through the fruitful virginity of blessed Mary, grant, we ask, that we may experience her interceding for us, through whom we have deserved to receive the author of life, our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son.

**Another.**—O God, who grant us to celebrate the eighth day after the birth of the Savior, make us, we ask, secure through his perpetual divinity, by whose fleshly participation we have been restored. Who lives with you, etc.

**Over the offerings.**—Grant, we ask, O Lord, that through these gifts, by which we enact the mysterious Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ, we may attain an understanding purified in mind. Through the same Christ our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and conducive to salvation, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through [Col. 0037B] Christ our Lord: as we celebrate today the day of his Circumcision and the octave of his Nativity, we venerate your wonders, O Lord. For she who gave birth is both mother and virgin; he who was born is both infant and God. Therefore, with angels, etc.

### Blessing

Almighty God, whose Only-Begotten Son on this day received bodily circumcision so that he might not abolish the law which he had come to fulfill, may cleanse your minds by spiritual circumcision from every incentive to vice and pour his blessing upon you. Amen.

And may he who gave the law through Moses, so that through our Mediator he might bestow blessing, strip you of the mortification of vices and make you persevere in the newness of virtues. Amen.

May you thus live in this world in the perfection of the number six, and rest among the ranks of the blessed spirits in the number seven. Amen.

So may you, renewed in the resurrection on the eighth day and enriched by the remission of the jubilee, attain joys that will endure without end. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom …

### At the Conclusion

Grant, we ask, Lord, that what we have received through the repeated solemnity of our Savior may confer upon us the remedy of everlasting redemption. Through the same Lord.

### Over the People

Almighty and everlasting God, who in your Only-Begotten Son have made us a new creation for yourself, preserve the works of your mercy, and cleanse us from every stain of our former state, so that by the help of your grace we may be found in the likeness of him in whom our substance is with you. He lives with you.

[Note: Nothing survives of this Sunday in the manuscripts of Pamelio or in the Swedish Royal manuscript, except the prayer beginning “Almighty God …” In the Gometian manuscript the prayer is: “God, who [by] the fruitful virginity of blessed Mary [bestowed] eternal salvation …”]

## THE SUNDAY AFTER THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

[Col. 0037D]

Almighty and everlasting God, direct our actions according to your good pleasure, so that in the name of your beloved Son we may deserve to abound in good works. Who lives with you.

### Over the Offerings

Grant, we ask, Lord, that the offering presented before the eyes of your Majesty may obtain for us both the grace of devotion and the attainment of blessed perpetuity. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0038A]

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: you recalled to pardon and life, through the merciful forgiveness of your goodness, humanity banished from the bounds of salvation because of the sin of our first parent, by sending us your Only-Begotten Son, our Lord and Savior; through whom your Majesty …

### Blessing

May God, who sent his Only-Begotten Son to save the world, make you participants in that salvation and render you steadfast in it. Amen.

May he remove from you the wrath that remains over unbelievers and make you forever free from it. Amen.

May he grant you the Spirit of his Son and allow you to overflow abundantly with his gifts. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom …

[Col. 0038B]

### At the Conclusion

Through the working of this mystery, Lord, may our vices be cleansed and our righteous desires fulfilled. Through the Lord, etc.

### Over the People

Be gracious, merciful God, to our supplications, and guard your people with vigilant protection, so that those who confess that your Only-Begotten Son, our Lord, was born in the flesh of our body may not be corrupted by any deception of the devil. Through the same Lord.

## JANUARY 5 — THE VIGIL OF THE EPIPHANY

[Note: Saint Gregory calls the feast of the Epiphany by this name, Homily 38 on the Gospel: “Come; since I celebrated the Lord’s Nativity without you, let me now celebrate the holy Theophany with you.”]

### At Vespers

We ask, Lord, that the splendor of the coming feast illuminate our hearts, so that we may be able to escape the darkness of this world and reach the homeland of eternal brightness. Through …

### Over the Offerings

Grant, we ask, Lord, that we may sacrifice to him with these present offerings, and receive those pious gifts which foreshadow the coming solemnity. Through, etc.

[Col. 0038C]

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and praise you, the wondrous Lord, in all your works, through which you have revealed the most sacred mysteries of your kingdom.

For the star, herald of the Lord’s appearing, went before this feast: it announced to the increasingly astonished that the Lord of heaven had been born on earth. Thus God, who was to be manifested to the world, was proclaimed by a heavenly sign, and he who had been born in time was disclosed through the ministry of temporal signs. And therefore …

### At the Conclusion

Illuminate your people, we ask, Lord, and continually kindle their hearts with the brightness of your grace, so that, with the star serving the Savior of the world, the Nativity once revealed may also be disclosed, and may continually increase, in their minds. Through the same Lord.

## JANUARY 6 — THE EPIPHANY OF THE LORD

[Note: On this day Pamelio’s edition assigns the station at Saint Peter’s; this agrees very well with the title of Homily 10 on the Gospel, “When Jesus had been born in Bethlehem,” where it is read that it was delivered in the basilica of Saint Peter. The Roman Calendar omits the station and assigns only the Gospel “When Jesus had been born,” etc. In the same Calendar, three feast days are celebrated after the feast of the Theophany; on the first, the station is assigned at Saint Peter in Chains.]

God, who on this day revealed your Only-Begotten Son to the nations by the guidance of a star, mercifully grant that we who have already come to know you by faith may be led as far as the contemplation of the appearance of your majesty. Through the same Lord, etc.

### Over the Offerings

Look graciously, Lord, upon the gifts of your Church, in which no longer are gold, frankincense, and myrrh offered, but Jesus Christ our Lord, who is declared, sacrificed, and received through those same gifts.

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because, when your Only-Begotten Son appeared in the substance of our mortality, he restored us to the new light of his immortality. And therefore, with the angels, etc.

We therefore ask you, most merciful Father, etc.

### Blessing

May God, the true light, who on this day willed to reveal his Only-Begotten Son to the nations by the guidance of a star, deign to enrich you with his blessing. Amen.

May you, following the example of the Magi, offer mystical gifts to the Lord Jesus Christ, reject the ancient enemy and the contagions of vices, and return to the eternal homeland by the way of virtues. Amen.

May he who willed to demonstrate the Holy Spirit over his Only-Begotten Son through a dove grant you true innocence of mind; and may your minds be exercised by that power for understanding the mysteries of the divine law by which water was changed into wine at Cana of Galilee. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this.

### At the Conclusion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may attain through purified understanding what we celebrate in solemn worship. Through …

[Col. 0039C]

### Other Prayers

Almighty and everlasting God, splendor of the souls of the faithful, who consecrated this solemnity through the first fruits of the nations’ election, fill the world with your glory, and appear to the peoples subject to you through the brightness of your light. Through …

### Another

God, illuminator of all nations, grant your peoples joy in perpetual peace, and pour into our hearts that splendid light which you breathed into the minds of the three Magi. Through …

### Another

Grant us, we ask, Lord, to celebrate worthily the mystery which is declared by flashing miracles in the infancy of our Savior and manifested through the bodily growth that reveals his humanity. Through the same Lord.

### Another

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the manifest Nativity of the Savior of the world, with the star as guide, may be revealed and continually increase in our minds. Through the same Lord.

### Another

Illuminate your people, we ask, Lord, and continually kindle their hearts with the brightness of your grace, so that they may both recognize their Savior without ceasing and truly take hold of him. Through our Lord.

[Note: This Sunday is absent from Pamelio’s manuscript. In the Swedish Royal manuscript, everything is missing from January 13 through January 19.]

## THE FIRST SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

[Col. 0040A]

Mercifully attend, we ask, Lord, to the vows of your supplicating people, so that they may see what must be done and grow strong enough to accomplish what they have seen. Through …

### Over the Offerings

May the sacrifice offered to you, Lord, always enliven and protect us. Through …

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because, when your Only-Begotten Son appeared in the substance of our mortality, he restored us to the new light of his immortality. And therefore, with the angels.

### Blessing

May God, who made the temporal childhood of his Son wondrous, deign to enlighten and instruct your hearts with the spirit of wisdom. Amen.

May he who willed that the child be temporarily subject to his parents, in his mercy, shape you through the gifts of humility and devotion. Amen.

May he who granted him to advance in wisdom, age, and grace mercifully bestow upon you growth in spiritual progress. May he himself deign to grant this.

### At the Conclusion

We humbly ask you, almighty God, that those whom you refresh with your mysteries may also, by your favor, serve you worthily through conduct pleasing to you. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

Preserve your family, we ask, Lord, and mercifully purify it through the abundance of your blessings, so that it may continually increase through your instruction and gifts. Through …

[Note: For the octave of the Epiphany nothing is assigned in the Roman Calendar.]

## ON THE OCTAVE OF THE THEOPHANY

[Col. 0040C]

God, whose Only-Begotten Son appeared in the substance of our flesh, grant, we ask, that through him whom we recognized outwardly as like us, we may deserve to be inwardly reformed. He lives and reigns with you, etc.

### Over the Offerings

We bring you offerings, Lord, for the appearance of your newborn Son, humbly entreating that, just as he himself is the author of our gifts, so he himself may be their merciful receiver—Jesus Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with you as God.

### At the Conclusion

Go before us always and everywhere with heavenly light, we ask, Lord, so that we may see with pure vision and receive with worthy effect the mystery in which you have willed us to share. Through …

## JANUARY 14 — THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT FELIX

[Note: In the Roman Calendar and in the Swedish Royal manuscript, which Pamelio follows, “at Pincis” is added. Consult Bollandus, volume 1 of the January saints, and Tillemont, volume 4 of the Ecclesiastical Commentaries. The solemnity of this saint is noted on January 14 in the Roman Calendar and in Pamelio, but on January 13 in the Swedish Royal manuscript.]

[Col. 0040D]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the examples of your saints may call us to a better life, so that we may imitate the actions of those whose solemnities we celebrate. Through …

### Over the Offerings

We offer you sacrifices, Lord, in commemoration of Saint Felix the confessor, humbly beseeching that, just as you granted him generosity in the sacred faith, so you may grant us pardon and peace. Through …

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and not remain silent about the memorable confession of Saint Felix, who could be turned neither by heretical perversities nor by the flatteries of the world from the rectitude of his standing; but, an assertor of truth amid both dangers, he did not abandon the steadfastness of your faith. Through …

### At the Conclusion

We ask, Lord, that, filled with saving mysteries, we may be helped by the prayers of him whose solemnity we celebrate. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0041B]

Almighty and everlasting God, who govern heavenly and earthly things together, mercifully hear the supplications of your people and grant your peace in our times. Through …

So that the gifts of your supplicating people may be pleasing to you, cleanse them, we ask, from every contagion of perversity. Through …

Through him.

May God, who by his wondrous power changed water into wine, transfer you, withdrawn from your former state, into the newness of blessed life. Amen.

May he himself grant you spiritual understanding of the holy Scriptures, who, by changing water into wine, willed to signify this very thing. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this, whose …

### Over the People

[Note: Pamelio records this on January 18; in the Swedish Royal manuscript it appears on January 16, agreeing with the Roman Calendar.]

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you are glorified in the confession of your saints, and you not only reward the glorious merits of your martyrs with the more excellent prizes, but also graciously grant those who perform the sacred mysteries with appropriate service to enter into the joy of their Lord. Through Christ the Lord.

[Col. 0042B]

### At the Conclusion

You have satisfied your family with sacred gifts, Lord; we ask that, through the intercession of him whose solemnity we celebrate, you may always refresh us. Through …

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of your blessed martyr Prisca may both rejoice in the annual solemnity and advance through the example of such great faith. Through …

### Over the Offerings

May the sacrifice, Lord, which we offer while recalling the birthdays of your saints, both loosen the bonds of our perversity and obtain for us the gifts of your mercy. Through …

### At the Conclusion

We ask, Lord, that, filled with saving mysteries, we may be helped by the prayers of him whose solemnity we celebrate. Through …

[Note: In the Roman Calendar, the feast of Saint Sebastian precedes that of Saint Fabian; the order is reversed in Pamelio’s manuscript, the Swedish Royal manuscript, the Vatican edition, and others. Later the two solemnities were combined into one.]

Look upon our weakness, almighty God, and may the glorious intercession of your blessed martyr and bishop Fabian protect us, whom the burden of our own actions weighs down. Through …

### Over the Offerings

Refreshed by participation in the sacred gift, we ask you, Lord our God, that we may experience the effect of the one whose worship we perform. Through …

## ON THE SAME DAY — THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT SEBASTIAN, MARTYR

God, who strengthened your blessed martyr Sebastian in his passion by the power of steadfastness, grant us through imitation of him, for love of you, to despise the prosperity of the world and fear none of its adversities. Through …

### Over the Offerings

May our devotion, Lord, be acceptable in your sight, and may it become saving for us through his supplication, for whose solemnity it is brought. Through …

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because the venerable blood of the blessed martyr Sebastian, poured out for the confession of your name, both manifests your wonders, by which you perfect strength in weakness, and gives progress to our endeavors and assistance to the weak before you. Through Christ our Lord.

[Note: In the Swedish Royal manuscript: “of Saint Agnes.” In the Roman Calendar: “of Saint Agnes, concerning the passion.” Agnes is also read in the principal manuscripts of the homilies on the Gospel, where the eleventh homily concerns this holy virgin and martyr.]

[Note: Two other prayers follow this one in Pamelio’s manuscript. Three are absent from the Swedish Royal manuscript. In Pamelio they are enclosed in brackets. Nearly everything found within the brackets does not exist in the Swedish Royal manuscript.]

Receiving, Lord, everlasting joys from participation in the sacrament of the holy martyr Agnes’s feast, we humbly beseech you that what, with your gift, we perform through diligent service, we may receive through your gift with worthy understanding. Through …

## JANUARY 22 — THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT VINCENT, MARTYR

Be present, we ask, Lord, to our supplications, so that we who acknowledge ourselves guilty through our iniquity may be freed through the intercession of your blessed martyr Vincent. Through …

### Over the Offerings

We joyfully offer today’s sacrifice, Lord, by which, while commemorating the heavenly victory of blessed Vincent, we both proclaim your mighty works and rejoice that we have acquired his glorious assistance. Through …

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: for the sake of whose name the glorious deacon Vincent, an unconquered soldier, fearlessly approached the madness of the raging enemy, endured it with restraint, and mocked it securely, knowing that he was prepared to resist, but not knowing that he was exalted in order to conquer; in both respects following the footsteps of his Lord and Master, who showed his followers examples to imitate in preserving humility and triumphing over enemies. Through him.

### At the Conclusion

## JANUARY 25 — THE CONVERSION OF SAINT PAUL

[Note: The Roman Calendar and the Swedish Royal manuscript do not know this feast. Pamelio’s manuscript mentions it, but with the sign of brackets. Before it, the Theoderician manuscript 1 places the feast of Saints Emerentiana and Macarius, martyrs. The Gemetian manuscript assigns no feasts of saints here.]

God, who taught the whole world through the preaching of your apostle Paul, grant us, we ask, that we who celebrate his Conversion today may walk toward you by his examples. Through …

### Over the Offerings

Sanctify, Lord, through the prayers of your apostle Paul the gifts of your people, so that what is pleasing to you according to your institution may become more pleasing through the patronage of the one who supplicates. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly beseech your Majesty that you not allow your Church, instructed by the preaching of your apostle Paul, to be violated by any deception; and that, just as nothing is known to remain in true religion which his teaching has not seasoned, so through his favor efficacy may be granted to the faithful for carrying out what he taught, and the multitude of believing nations may perceive that the one whom they know to possess as their master and teacher is their intercessor with you. Through Christ our Lord.

### Blessing

May God, who by his grace made blessed Paul an apostle from a persecutor, deign to impart to you the spirit of holy remorse and devout conversion. Amen.

May he who deigned to reveal to him the mysteries of heavenly secrets deign to open to you the hidden things of his Scriptures. Amen.

And may he who deigned to give him perseverance in faith and unbending steadfastness in persecutions deign to strengthen and protect your weakness with the same gifts. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this.

### At the Conclusion

Sanctify us, Lord, we ask, through the saving mystery; and may the prayer of him whose patronage you have granted to govern us not be absent on our behalf. Through the Lord.

## ON THE SAME DAY — THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT PROJECTUS, MARTYR

[Note: Also “Prejectus,” as the Theoderician manuscripts give it. The Roman Calendar and the manuscripts of Pamelio and the Swedish Royal do not mention this martyr. He is mentioned in the Vatican edition and others.]

We have received votive gifts, Lord, for the passion of your blessed martyr Projectus; we ask that through his prayers you may grant us assistance equally for the present life and for the eternal one. Through …

God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed martyr Agnes, grant, we ask, that, just as we honor her through worship, so we may follow her example through devout conduct. Through …

### Over the Offerings

May an abundant blessing descend upon these offerings, we ask, Lord, which may mercifully bring about our sanctification and gladden us through the solemnity of the martyrs. Through …

We have received the votive mysteries of the annual celebration, Lord; grant, we ask, that they provide us with remedies both for temporal life and for eternal life. Through …

### Over the People

Be present to us, almighty God, as we repeat the feast of blessed Agnes, whom you raised up by an ineffable gift at the beginning of today’s celebration. Through …

## FEBRUARY 2 — THE PURIFICATION OF THE HOLY VIRGIN MARY

[Note: In two Theoderician manuscripts, the feast is called “Hypapante” (“Meeting”), as it is in many other manuscripts. It is absent from the Roman Calendar, where there is only: “On February 2, according to Luke: After he had fulfilled … as far as … the glory of your people Israel.”]

[Col. 0046A]

### At the Gathering

[Note: In the Vatican and Gussanville editions this prayer still belongs to the office of Saint Agnes; the other manuscripts, both printed and handwritten, contradict this. In Pamelio’s manuscript it is headed: “Prayer at the Gathering at Saint Adrian.” After the prayer one reads: “At the Mass at Saint Mary Major.” The same appears in two Theoderician manuscripts and in the Swedish Royal manuscript, except that in the latter, instead of “at the Mass,” one has “Mass.” In many manuscripts, as Pamelio observes, there is a blessing of candles. The Theoderician manuscript records many antiphons, especially “Adorna thal.”]

Instruct your people, we ask, Lord, and grant that what you give them to honor outwardly each year through devotion, they may attain inwardly through the light of your grace. Through …

### At Mass

Almighty and everlasting God, we humbly beseech your Majesty that, just as your Only-Begotten Son was presented in the temple today together with the substance of our flesh, so you may make us present ourselves to you with purified minds. Through the same Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Hear our prayers, Lord, and grant us the support of your goodness, so that the gifts which we offer before the eyes of your Majesty may be worthy. Through.

[Col. 0046B]

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because through the mystery of the incarnate Word a new light of your brightness has shone upon the eyes of our mind, so that, while we visibly know God, through him we may be drawn by love of invisible things. And therefore, with the angels and archangels.

### Blessing

Almighty God, who on this day willed that his Only-Begotten Son be presented in the temple in the flesh he had assumed, may make you, supported by the gift of his blessing, adorned with good works. Amen.

And may he who willed that the Son become a minister of the law in order to fulfill the law instruct your minds through the spiritual teachings of his law. Amen.

So may you be able to offer him, in place of turtledoves, gifts of chastity or charity, and may you overflow with the gifts of the Holy Spirit in place of the young pigeons. Amen.

May he himself …

### At the Conclusion

We ask you, Lord our God, that the holy mysteries which you have bestowed for the protection of our restoration may, through the intercession of the blessed ever-virgin Mary, become for us both a present and a future remedy. Through …

### Another

Perfect your grace in us, we ask, Lord, who fulfilled the expectation of righteous Simeon, so that, just as he did not see death before he deserved to see Christ the Lord, so may we also obtain eternal life. Through …

## FEBRUARY 5 — THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT AGATHA, MARTYR

[Note: Pamelio’s edition differs greatly from the Swedish Royal manuscript in the office of Saint Agatha.]

[Col. 0046D]

God, who among the other miracles of your power also granted the victory of martyrdom to the weaker sex, mercifully grant that we whose celebration commemorates her birthday may walk toward you by her examples. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Receive, Lord, the gifts which we bring on the solemnity of your blessed martyr Agatha, whose patronage we trust will free us. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: for the sake of whose name you granted to the faithful of every age, in both sexes, contempt for punishment and death, so that among the palms of blessed martyrs you might also crown Agatha, the most blessed virgin, with victorious endurance. Neither frightened by threats nor overcome by tortures, she triumphed over the devil’s cruelty because she remained steadfast in confessing your Divinity. And therefore …

### At the Conclusion

Trusting in the prayers of your blessed martyr Agatha, Lord, we ask your clemency that through what we have received we may obtain eternal remedies. Through …

### Another

May the martyr blessed Agatha implore pardon for us, Lord; she was always pleasing to you both by the merit of chastity and by her confession of your power. Through our Lord.

[Note: In the Swedish Royal manuscript and in Pamelio’s edition this Sunday, together with the others after the Epiphany, is omitted, which appears to indicate mutilation. In the Roman Calendar no Sundays are mentioned; instead, ten weeks after the Theophany are assigned, each with its own Gospel. Within those weeks, many weekdays are often marked as solemn, such as Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday, on which Gospels are also assigned.]

## THE THIRD SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

Almighty and everlasting God, mercifully look upon our weakness and extend the right hand of your Majesty to protect us. Through.

### Over the Offerings

This sacrifice, Lord, we ask, may cleanse our sins and sanctify the bodies and minds of those subject to you for the celebration of the sacrifice. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and praise and bless you at every moment, because in you we live and move and have our being.

There is no time and no moment that we pass without the benefits of your goodness. For, through the various occasions of solemnities, the memory of your saving works and gifts adorns the periods of our present life. Therefore, whether recognizing the time of past joy renewed by gladness or of enduring goodness, we pay unceasing thanks to your Majesty. Through Christ our Lord.

### Blessing

May almighty God cleanse you from the stains of every sin, he who deigned to cleanse the supplicating leper by his own touch. Amen.

May he who did not disdain to visit the centurion’s servant himself mercifully deign to enter the dwelling of your hearts. Amen.

And so may he form you in the fullness of his faith that he may grant you to recline with his saints in the kingdom of heaven. Amen.

May he himself grant this.

[Col. 0048A]

### At the Conclusion

Since you grant us to make use of such great mysteries, Lord, we ask that you deign to make us truly suited to their effects. Through.

### Over the People

May your propitiation be present, Lord, we ask, to your supplicating people, so that what they faithfully seek under your inspiration they may receive through your swift generosity. Through our Lord.

## THE FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

God, who know that, because of human frailty, we cannot stand amid such great dangers, grant us health of mind and body, so that, with your help, we may overcome what we suffer because of our sins. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the offering of this sacrifice may always cleanse and protect our weakness from every evil. Through.

[Col. 0048B]

### Preface

It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who deigned to set the human race, condemned for its transgression at the very root of its origin, free through the flower of a virginal womb, so that you might recreate through your Son, God and man, the human being whom you had created through the Only-Begotten; and so that the devil, who had conquered Adam in fragile flesh, might, with justice preserved, be conquered by God in the flesh he assumed. Through him your Majesty …

### Blessing

May the Lord remove from you the dangers of every temptation and, in his mercy, exclude the storms of disturbance. Amen.

May he dissolve the deceits and schemes of the tempter and make you wary and unconquerable against him. Amen.

May he grant you the gifts of continual peace and, in his favor, establish you in the harbor of tranquility and security. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this.

### At the Conclusion

May your gifts, God, release us from earthly pleasures and always furnish us with heavenly nourishment. Through.

## THE FIFTH SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

Guard your family, we ask, Lord, with continual goodness, so that those who rely on the hope of heavenly grace alone may always be protected by you. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

We offer you sacrifices of reconciliation, Lord, so that in your mercy you may both absolve our sins and direct wavering hearts. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and offer you this sacrificial victim, (173) which is the saving and ineffable sacrament of divine grace; it is offered by many, (174) yet by the infusion of the Holy Spirit is made one body of Christ. Each person receives Christ the Lord, and (175) in each portion he is wholly present; nor (176) is he diminished among the separate recipients, but presents himself whole in each. Therefore we who receive communion of this holy bread and cup (177) are made one body of Christ. And so, through his Majesty, we humbly beseech you that you cleanse us from every taint of the old condition and grant us to persevere in newness of life. Through Christ.

Blessing.—May God, who is accustomed to sow good seed in his Church, never cease to preserve and multiply it in you. Amen. May he drive far from you the sower of weeds, and unceasingly refresh you with the nourishment of his word. Amen. When the day of judgment has come, may you, separated from the rejected, be set at the right hand of the Judge and placed in his most blessed kingdom. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

28. At the Conclusion.—We beseech you, almighty God, that we may receive the effect of that salvation whose pledge we have received through these mysteries. Through the same Lord.

Over the People.—Graciously receive, O Lord, the prayers of your Church, so that, once all adversities have been destroyed, she may serve you in secure freedom. Through.

## SUNDAY VI AFTER THE EPIPHANY

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, always meditating on rational things pleasing to you, we may carry them out both in word and in deed. Through.

Over the Offerings.—May this offering, O God, we beseech you, cleanse, renew, govern, and protect us. Through the Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for it belongs to your immeasurable glory not only to come to the aid of mortals through your mercy, but also to provide us a remedy from our very mortality, and to save each of the lost by the very means through which they had perished. Through Christ our Lord.

Blessing.—May God, who made the sea passable beneath his feet, himself lay beneath you whatever is harmful. Amen. May he restrain the hostile movements of unclean spirits and strengthen you in his peace. Amen. May he steer you by the ship of his cross amid the waves of the world and lead you to the shore of blessed eternity. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—Fed, O Lord, with heavenly delights, we beseech you to make us always desire those same things by which we truly live. Through.

[Column 0049D] Over the People.—Preserve your people, O God, and make them devoted to your name, so that, subject to divine duties, they may bravely receive both temporal and eternal gifts. Through our Lord.

## 16 KALENDS OF MARCH.—(178) FEAST OF SAINT VALENTINE [Note: [Column 0049D] “Martyr” is absent from the Swedish Royal Manuscript. In the First Theoderic Manuscript, before the feast of Saint Valentine, there is noted: 7 Ides of February: Translation of Saint Helena the queen; and 4 Ides of February: Feast of Saint Scholastica, virgin. After Saint Valentine’s feast, the same manuscript adds: On the same day, the feast of Saints Vitalis, Felicula, and Zeno.]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the feast of your blessed martyr Valentine may, through his intercession, be freed from all impending evils. Through our Lord.

Over the Offerings.—Be appeased, O Lord, we beseech you, by the gifts offered, 29 and, with your blessed martyr Valentine interceding, defend us from every danger. Through our Lord.

At the Conclusion.—May this heavenly mystery be for us, O Lord, the restoration of mind and body, so that we may experience the effect of the action whose celebration we perform. Through.

## 13 KALENDS OF MARCH.—(179) [Note: [Column 0049D] In the Vatican and Gussanville editions: “The Chair of Saint Peter in Rome,” a title not found in the other published or manuscript codices. We therefore suspect that “in Rome” was added recently, [Column 0050D] to distinguish it from the other feast of the Chair of Saint Peter at Antioch, on 18 January—although whether it was known to the ancients [is uncertain]. Consult our observation on note 179. John Fronto’s Roman Calendar knows neither feast, nor does the Swedish Royal Manuscript.] THE CHAIR OF SAINT PETER.

O God, who entrusted to your blessed apostle Peter, when you gave him the keys of the heavenly kingdom, the authority to bind and loose souls, (180) grant that, with the help of his intercession, we may be freed from the bonds of our sins. [Column 0050B] You who live and reign.

Over the Offerings.—May the prayer of blessed Peter the apostle commend to you, O Lord, the prayers and offerings of your Church, so that what we celebrate for his glory may profit us toward forgiveness. Through the Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and praise you as the wondrous God in your saints, in whom you have been greatly glorified. Through them you adorn the sacred body of your Only-Begotten, and in them you establish the foundations of your Church, which (181) you founded in the patriarchs, prepared in the prophets, and established in the apostles. From among them, for the confession of your Only-Begotten Son, confirmed through the mouth of that same Word of yours, you made blessed Peter, chief of the apostles, the steward and guardian of the heavenly gates, as the foundation of your house, changing his name and granting him by divine right that (182) whatever he established on earth should be upheld in heaven. In his honor, on this day, we offer these celebrations to your Majesty and sacrifice a Victim of thanksgiving and praise. Through him to your Majesty.

At the Conclusion.—May the offering presented gladden us, O Lord, so that, just as we proclaim you wondrous in your apostle Peter, so through him we may receive the abundance of your forgiveness. Through.

Over the People.—Bless your people, we beseech you, O Lord, and grant them, through the prayers of your blessed apostle Peter, the help of your protection. Through.

## 6 KALENDS OF MARCH.— [Note: [Column 0050D] This feast is omitted in the Roman Calendar and in the Swedish Royal Manuscript. In the First Theoderic Manuscript, immediately after the feast of Saint Matthew, comes the feast of Saints Perpetua and Felicity.] FEAST (183) OF SAINT MATTHIAS THE APOSTLE.

[Column 0050D]

O God, who joined blessed Matthias to the company of your apostles, grant, we beseech you, that through his intervention we may always experience the inward mercy you show toward us. Through the Lord.

Over the Offerings.—O God, who supplied the downfall of the apostate traitor, so that the consecrated number of your apostles (184) might not lack its perfection, by the election of blessed Matthias, sanctify these offerings and through them strengthen us by the power of your grace. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and praise you as the wondrous God in your blessed apostles, in whom you have been greatly glorified. Through them you gather together the sacred body of your Only-Begotten, and in them you establish the foundations of your Church. Therefore we ask your clemency, most merciful almighty God, that through the intercession of your blessed apostle Matthias, whose triumph over suffering we solemnly celebrate, we may deserve to be released from the bonds of our sins, restored to the happiness of eternal life, and numbered among the assemblies of your saints. Through him.

Blessing.—May God, who has granted you to stand upon apostolic foundations, deign to bless you through the merits of his blessed apostle Matthias as he intercedes. Amen. May he defend you from every adversity by apostolic protection—he who wished you to be adorned and enriched by their examples and teachings. Amen. May you, through their intercession, reach the inheritance of the eternal homeland, through whose teaching you hold fast the integrity of the faith. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—Grant, we beseech you, almighty and merciful God, that through these holy gifts which we have received, with your apostle blessed Matthias interceding, we may obtain forgiveness and peace. Through the Lord.

Over the People.—May your people, O Lord, we beseech you, through the intercession of your apostle blessed Matthias, receive the mercy they ask for, and obtain the forgiveness and peace for which they humbly pray. Through the Lord.

## 4 IDES OF MARCH.—FEAST OF SAINT GREGORY THE POPE

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that your faithful may worthily celebrate the solemn feast of your bishop Saint Gregory, so that they may experience his assistance here and attain its eternal effects. Through.

[Note: [Column 0051D] In the Swedish Royal Manuscript this Prayer is read: “Grant us, O Lord, that the offering may benefit the soul of your servant Gregory, which, by being sacrificed, you have granted to release the sins of the whole world.” Pamelius observes that this is how it is read in certain codices.]

Over the Offerings.—May the prayer of Saint Gregory accompany, O Lord, the offerings which we present to be consecrated to your name; through it may you both cleanse and defend us. Through.

31. Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because you grant your Church to rejoice in the commemoration of your bishop Saint Gregory, so that you gladden her by his feast, train her by the example of his devout way of life, instruct her by the word of his preaching, and protect her by her acceptable supplication to you. Through.

At the Conclusion.—(185) May your holy gifts, we beseech you, O Lord, provide us protection which, through the merits of blessed Gregory intervening, may absolve us from all sins. Through.

## 8 KALENDS OF APRIL.—(186) [Note: [Column 0051D] John Fronto observes in his notes on the Roman Calendar that the Tenth Council of Toledo, in the year 656, canon 1, decreed [Column 0052D] that this feast should be celebrated on the eighth day before the Nativity of Christ, since it is unfitting to celebrate any of the solemnities of the saints during Lent. Nevertheless, in the Roman Calendar, in the Swedish Royal Manuscript according to Pamelius, and in all published books of the Sacramentaries, this feast is assigned to 25 March.] ANNUNCIATION OF THE ANGEL TO BLESSED MARY.

O God, who, when the angel announced it, willed your Word to assume flesh in the womb of the (187) blessed virgin Mary, grant to your suppliants that we who truly believe her to be the Mother of God may be aided by her intercessions with you. Through the same Lord.

At Mass.—O God, who on this day willed your Word to become incarnate in the womb of the (188) blessed Virgin, (189) make us celebrate the present (190) solemnity in such a way that we may be pleasing to you. Through the same Lord.

Over the Offerings.—May the Holy Spirit receive the gifts placed upon your altar, O Lord—the Spirit who today filled the womb of blessed [Column 0052B] Mary with the splendor of his power. Through our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: Gabriel the archangel announced that he would be born for the salvation of humanity; the Virgin Mary conceived him through the cooperation of the Holy Spirit; so that what the sublime angelic dignity announced, virginal purity might believe, and the ineffable Godhead might accomplish. Therefore, with your help, we desire to behold without confusion the face of him whose Incarnation we rejoice to celebrate. Through him to your Majesty.

At the Conclusion.—Confirm in our minds, O Lord, the mysteries of the true faith, so that we who confess the God conceived of the Virgin to be true God and human being may, through the power of his saving resurrection, deserve to attain eternal joy. Through.

Over the People.—Protect your servants, O Lord, with the supports of peace, 32 and, trusting in the patronage of blessed Mary, make them secure from every enemy. Through.

Another.—Pour your grace, we beseech you, O Lord, into our minds, so that we who learned, when the angel announced it, of the Incarnation of Christ your Son may be led through his passion and cross to the glory of the resurrection. He who lives and reigns with you as God.

Another.—Almighty and eternal God, who today, through the angelic ministry, revealed to blessed Mary, ever-virgin, that your co-eternal Son was to be conceived according to the flesh by the Holy Spirit for the salvation of the world, graciously be present to your people, so that, once peace has been granted, (191) we may approach his Nativity with freer hearts. Through the same Lord.

Another.—Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who deigned, through the overshadowing of divine grace over the sacred womb (192) of blessed Mary, to illumine the whole world; and grant that we may deserve to obtain through her protection what we cannot attain by our own merits. Through our Lord.

[Column 0053A] Another.—May the merits of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-virgin and Mother of God, obtain us, O Lord, we beseech you, and may they always implore your forgiveness for us. Through.

Another.—Stretch out your right hand to us, O God, and through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-virgin and Mother of God, bestow upon us the help of heavenly Power. Through the same Lord.

## IN (193) SEPTUAGESIMA [Note: [Column 0053D] In the Swedish Royal Manuscript and in the First Theoderic Manuscript: “In the Seventieth.” In both, “at Saint Laurence” is added, and in Theoderic, “outside the walls.” In the Pamelius Manuscript: “Station at Saint Laurence,” without any addition. The same station is assigned in the Roman Calendar with the Gospel that is still read today. The first Prayer everywhere is: “The prayers of your people,” as it is still found in the Office of Septuagesima.]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, a sufficient measure appropriate to our weakness, so that, through devout conduct, it may reflect upon the effect of its restoration and receive it with exultation.

Over the Offerings.—Grant us, merciful God, both always to serve your altars worthily and to be saved by perpetual participation in them. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because through the things that are seen we are instructed in the ways by which we ought to strive toward invisible realities. Finally, as the succession of the year leads us onward, we are reminded to pass from past things to future things, from oldness to newness of life, (194) so that, freed from earthly supports, we may receive more eagerly the abundance of the heavenly gift. And (195) 33 through that food which is supplied in alternating benefits, may we attain the nourishment that will endure without end, Jesus Christ our Lord. Through him.

Blessing.—May almighty God deign so to direct the course of your race that he may make you grasp the prize of eternal life. Amen. And may he so surround you with the weapons of abstinence that you may not be delayed by any burdens of this life from (196) reaching it. Amen. May he who deigned to call you his vineyard and send you holy laborers also deign to cultivate you by his grace, so that he may not refuse to reward you with the denarius of eternal life. May he himself grant this.

At the Conclusion.—May your faithful, O God, be strengthened by your gifts, so that by receiving them they may seek the same gifts, and by seeking them may receive them without end. Through.

Over the People.—Mercifully hear, we beseech you, O Lord, the prayers of your people, so that we who are justly afflicted for our sins may be mercifully freed for the glory of your name. Through the Lord.

## (197) IN SEXAGESIMA [Note: [Column 0053D] In Pamelius, with our manuscripts in agreement, the station is at Saint Paul. Thus also in the Roman Calendar, where the Gospel “When a great crowd had gathered,” and so forth, is prescribed, as it is in present-day Missals. What the ancients understood by a station seems to be taught by Tertullian, *On Prayer*: “Similarly, concerning station days, many do not think that one should intervene with prayers of sacrifice, because the station must be ended by receiving the body of the Lord.” Consult the notes of learned commentators on this passage.]

[Column 0053D] O God, who see that we place our confidence in no action of our own, graciously grant that we may be fortified against every adversity by the protection of the Doctor of the Gentiles. Through.

Over the Offerings.—Give heed, we beseech you, O Lord, to the offerings of your household, and grant that those whom you make participants in the sacred gift may (198) reach its fullness. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you deign to teach rational creation by such an ordering that, lest it fail to strive toward eternal rewards while devoted to temporal goods, it may neither grow weak under discipline nor become arrogant in prosperity, but rather may its glorious devotion be made evident by this: that, overwhelmed by no adversities, it is overcome by none. Through Christ our Lord.

[Column 0054B] Blessing.—May the Lord grant you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, who has already deigned to give you the hearing of his word. Amen. May he so fill your minds with the abundance of his seed that he may grant it to bear fruit pleasingly in you. Amen. And may he so guard you from every temptation that he may reward you with (199) thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold fruit according to the distribution of his grace. Amen. May he himself grant this.

34. At the Conclusion.—(200) May sacred food and saving drink be present for us, we beseech you, O Lord, to protect temporal life and grant eternal life. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—Guard your people, we beseech you, O Lord, and accompany them, as they recall the sacred solemnity, with the abundance of heavenly grace, so that, assisted by visible consolations, they may be more readily urged toward invisible goods. Through.

## SUNDAY [Note: [Column 0054D] In Pamelius and in our manuscript codices, “at Saint Peter” is added. Thus in the Roman Calendar, where the Gospel is “He took the twelve,” as it is still read today. The second homily of Saint Gregory on this Gospel was delivered on Quinquagesima Sunday in the Basilica of Saint Peter.] IN QUINQUAGESIMA.

Mercifully hear our prayers, we beseech you, O Lord, and, once freed from the bonds of sins, guard us from every adversity. Through.

Over the Offerings.—May this Victim, O Lord, we beseech you, cleanse our sins (201) and sanctify, for the sacrifice to be celebrated, the bodies and minds of those subject to you. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and (202) humbly beseech your Majesty (203) [Note: [Column 0054D] Thus also in the Gembloux Manuscript and in two Theoderic Manuscripts. The Vatican and Gussanville editions read “in a fitting manner.”] to look upon the measure of our earthly weakness and not rebuke us in your anger for our perversity, but purify, instruct, and console us through your boundless clemency. [Column 0055A] Since without you we can do nothing that is pleasing to you, your grace alone will grant us to live in a wholesome manner. Through Christ.

Blessing.—May almighty God strengthen you with his blessing and make you fit for the imminent abstinence of Lent. Amen. And may the most merciful Illuminator, who restored sight to the blind man who supplicated him through the power of his divinity, wipe away the blindness of your hearts and graciously enlighten your minds with the rays of his light. Amen. So that, cleansed from the filth of vices and made firm by the ardor of charity, you may be able to receive the heavenly inheritance unharmed. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

[Note: [Column 0055D] In the Swedish Royal Manuscript, the Prayer at the Conclusion is: “We beseech you, almighty God, that we who have received heavenly nourishment may through it be fortified against every adversity.” This Prayer is absent from the Pamelius Manuscript, as we note, showing that the manuscripts do not always agree.]

At the Conclusion.—Filled with participation in heavenly gifts, we have been satisfied, O Lord; grant, we beseech you, that we may continually receive the same gifts and unceasingly seek them. Through.

Over the People.—From the abundance of your mercy, O Lord, protect the people who confess you, and, having been governed bodily, make them more eager in the devotion of their minds to attain your gifts. Through our Lord.

35. WEDNESDAY.—(204) THE BEGINNING [Note: [Column 0055D] “Beginning of the fast” is absent from the Swedish Royal Manuscript, although it is read in Pamelius.] OF THE FAST.

(205) [Note: [Column 0055D] In the Pamelius Manuscript, with the Swedish Royal Codex in agreement, this is read: “Collect at Saint Anastasia. Grant us,” and afterward: “At Mass, station at Saint Sabina.” In the Roman Calendar only this appears: “Wednesday, at Saint Sabina.” The Gospel is: “Jesus said … When you fast.” The Gembloux and First Theoderic Manuscripts prefix the Blessing of the ashes.]

At the Collect.—Grant us, O Lord, to begin the defenses of Christian warfare with sacred fasts, so that, intending to fight against spiritual wickedness, we may be fortified by the aids of self-restraint. Through.

[Note: [Column 0055D] This is not read at all in the Swedish Royal Manuscript, in which many other things found in the Pamelius Manuscript for this Wednesday are also absent.]

At Mass.—Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that your faithful may both receive the venerable solemnities of the fasts with fitting devotion and complete them in secure dedication. [Column 0055C] Through.

Over the Offerings.—Make us, O Lord, we beseech you, suitably prepared to offer these gifts, with which we celebrate the beginning of that venerable (206) sacrament itself. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for by bodily fasting you restrain vices, raise the mind, and bestow both virtue and rewards.—Through Christ.

At the Conclusion.—May the sacraments (207) we have received, O Lord, provide us help, so that our fasts may be pleasing to you and profitable to us for healing. Through.

[Column 0056A] Over the People.—Graciously look upon those who bow before your Majesty, O Lord, so that those who have been refreshed by a divine gift may always be nourished by heavenly assistance. Through our Lord.
