[Note: [Column 0055D] In the Pamelius edition, after all the other Prayers, one is noted “at Vespers, on each day of Lent.” It is absent not only from the other published and manuscript codices but also from the Swedish Royal Manuscript, which rarely differs from Pamelius. The Theoderic Manuscripts contain these Prayers at Vespers.]

[Note: [Column 0056D] The Offices for Thursday throughout Lent are among those which Abbot Grimold says were formerly “slaughtered” by having strokes placed before them; Micrologus, chapter 49, testifies that they were instituted later by Gregory the Younger. This is Pamelius’s account. John Fronto holds nearly the same view in the Roman Calendar, where this Thursday is noted together with the following day, with stations added and the Gospels indicated that are still read on those days. Nothing is said of Saturday. In Pamelius, the station on Thursday is at Saint George, and on Friday at Saints John and Paul; in the Roman Calendar the latter is designated by the title of Pammachius. For the Saturday station, the Pamelius Codex has “at Saint Tryphon”; the Swedish Royal Codex has nothing for Saturday.]

## THURSDAY WITHIN QUINQUAGESIMA

O God, who are offended by guilt and appeased by repentance, graciously look upon the prayers of your supplicating people, and turn away the scourges of your anger which we deserve for our sins. Through.

Over the Offerings.—Graciously regard, O Lord, we beseech you, these present sacrifices, so that they may benefit both our devotion and our salvation. Through the Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, 36 holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because those feasts return on which an immortal exchange is arranged for our mortality and eternity is substituted for temporal life; and (208), through the punishment of sin, sins are cleansed, and salvation is brought forth in wondrous ways from destruction, so that the condition of human existence, which through the insolence of happiness came into sorrow, may through grief return, humble and restrained, to eternal joys. Through Christ.

At the Conclusion.—Having received the blessing of the heavenly gift, we humbly beseech you, almighty God, that this same gift may be for us both the cause of the (209) sacrament and of salvation. Through.

Over the People.—Spare, O Lord, spare your people, so that, chastened by deserved scourges, they may find relief in your mercy. Through.

## FRIDAY WITHIN QUINQUAGESIMA

[Column 0056C]

Accompany the fasts we have begun, we beseech you, O Lord, with gracious favor, so that we may also practice with sincere minds the observance we display bodily. Through the Lord.

Over the Offerings.—Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that the sacrifice (210) of paschal observance which we offer may make our minds acceptable to you and grant us the capacity for more willing self-restraint. Through the Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly beseech your Majesty to pour graciously into us the spirit of understanding, by which we may either discern rationally what ought to be done ourselves or indicate to those who (211) think useless things what ought (212) to be judged as such; and that we may not pursue our own interests, but submit to those who offer better counsel. For this is wisdom with you: it does not cling to its own vices but loves truth, from whatever source it is brought forth. Through Christ our Lord.

At the Conclusion.—Pour into us, O Lord, the Spirit of your charity, so that those whom you have satisfied with one heavenly bread you may make united through your mercy.

Over the People.—Govern your people, O Lord, we beseech you, and always increase them with your benefits, so that they may rejoice both in the supports of the present life and in those of the eternal life. Through.

## 37. SATURDAY WITHIN QUINQUAGESIMA

[Column 0057B]

Hear us, compassionate and merciful God, and graciously grant us the saving gifts of self-restraint. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—Prepare us, we beseech you, O Lord, for the festive offices of this abstinence, so that we may always celebrate these venerable sacrifices with sober minds. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly beseech your Majesty to make our mind graciously pleasing to you—a mind that not only displays the appearance of goodness but, illumined by the fruits of justice, shines forth, and, always devoted to your Majesty, receives the benefits it desires. You do not cease to pursue with necessary gifts those whom you have made suitably attentive to your worship. Through Christ our Lord.

At the Conclusion.—Grant us, almighty God, that we may continually experience as salutary the heavenly gifts which we regularly attend upon with the service that is due. Through.

Over the People.—Guard your people, O Lord, and mercifully cleanse them from all sins, because no adversity will harm them if no iniquity rules over them. Through.

[Note: [Column 0057D] Alternatively, “In the Fortieth.” In Pamelius, “At Saint John in the Lateran” is added. In the Roman Calendar only this appears: “At the Lateran,” with the Gospel assigned, “Jesus was led,” and so forth. The sixteenth homily of Saint Gregory on the Gospel is said to have been delivered in the basilica of Saint John called the Constantinian, on the First Sunday in Lent.]

## IN QUADRAGESIMA

At Mass.—O God, who purify your Church by the annual observance of Lent, grant your household [Column 0057D] that what it strives to obtain from you by abstaining, [Note: [Column 0057D] Thus the Swedish Royal Manuscript reads, with the other published and manuscript witnesses in agreement, except Pamelius, where the reading is “this through good morals.” The Swedish Royal Manuscript differs from Pamelius in many places.] it may accomplish through good works. Through the Lord.

Over the Offerings.—We solemnly sacrifice the offering of the beginning of Lent, beseeching you, O Lord, that, together with restraint from bodily foods, we may also refrain from harmful pleasures. Through the Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through [Column 0058A] Christ our Lord: who dedicated this fast by fasting for forty continuous days and nights without hunger; afterward he hungered, not so much for human food as for salvation; nor did he desire the feasts of worldly foods, but rather desired the holiness of souls. For his food is 38 the redemption of peoples. (213) His food is the accomplishment of every good will: he taught us to work not for food prepared from earthly dishes, but for that which is received through reading the divine Scriptures. Through him.

Blessing.—May almighty God bless you, who consecrated the number forty in the fast of Moses and Elijah and also of our Mediator, and may he grant you to pass through the course of the present life in such a way that, having received the denarius of your reward from the master of the household, you may reach the remission of all sins and the glorious resurrection with all the saints. Amen. May he also give you invincible [Perhaps: victorious] weapons of spiritual virtues, by which, following the Lord’s example, you may overcome the exceedingly crafty temptations of the ancient enemy. Amen. So may you, taking spiritual nourishment not from bread alone but from every word that proceeds from his mouth, through observing the fasts and displaying the other good works, deserve to receive the unfading crown of glory. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—May the holy draught of your sacrament, O Lord, restore us, and, having cleansed us from the old condition, make us pass into participation in the saving mystery. Through.

Over the People.—May an abundant blessing descend upon your people, we beseech you, O Lord; may forgiveness come, consolation be granted, holy faith increase, and eternal redemption be made firm. Through.

Another.—Grant us, we beseech you, almighty God, to seek the joys of the eternal promise and to find more quickly what we have sought. Through.

Another.—Be present, we beseech you, O Lord, to our supplications, and guard us, who trust in your mercy, from every adversity. Through our Lord.

Another.—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that through the annual exercises of the Lenten (214) sacrament we may progress both toward understanding the mystery of Christ and toward following its effects by a worthy way of life. Through.

[Column 0058D] (215) Throughout Lent, every day, when Mass has ended, the bishop and clergy depart and remove their sacred vestments, and then return for Vespers. And no cleric at any time stands in the church (216) with his head covered, unless he has an illness.

## MONDAY WITHIN LENT [Note: [Column 0058D] Pamelius, in agreement with the Roman Calendar, adds: “At Saint Peter in Chains.” In the Calendar no other Gospel is assigned than the one now read.]

Convert us, O God our Savior, and, so that the Lenten fast may benefit us, instruct our minds with heavenly disciplines. Through.

[Column 0059A] Over the Offerings.—May the offering of our devotion be acceptable to you, O Lord; through your working, may it sanctify our fast and obtain for us the forgiveness of your consolation. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: who give food to all flesh, and refresh us not only with bodily but also with spiritual foods, so that we may live not by bread alone but have life-giving nourishment in every word of yours; and may be fed not only by feasting but also by fasting. For just as bodies are fattened by food and drink, so souls are enriched by fasts and virtues. In this gift you have bestowed great health upon mind and body, because you consecrated the venerable fast for us, so that by fasting we might return more solemnly to the paradise from which we fell by not abstaining. Through Christ our Lord.

At the Conclusion.—Satisfied with the gift of your salvation, O Lord, we humbly beseech you that, by the effect of that whose taste gladdens us, we may be renewed. Through the same Lord.

Over the People.—Be favorable, O Lord, to your people, and do not leave without temporal consolation the people whom you wish to strive toward eternal things. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Column 0059D] The station for this day, according to Pamelius and the Roman Calendar, is at Saint Anastasia. The same Gospel is prescribed as appears in the present Office. The same is to be understood of the remaining weekdays, unless otherwise noted.]

## TUESDAY

Look upon your household, O Lord, and grant that our mind, which chastises itself by mortifying the flesh, may shine before you with desire for you. Through.

Over the Offerings.—Be appeased, O Lord, by the gifts offered, and defend us from every danger.

[Column 0059C] Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: in whom the faith of those who fast is nourished, hope advanced, and charity strengthened. For he is the living and true bread, which is the substance of eternity and the food of virtue. Your Word, through whom all things were made, is not only the bread of human minds but also of the angels themselves. You do not cease to minister this bread to us, and you urge us to hunger for it unceasingly. As we are fed by his flesh, we are strengthened; as we drink his blood, we are washed clean. Through him.

At the Conclusion.—We have received the votive sacraments of the annual celebration; grant, we beseech you, [Column 0059D] that they may bring us a remedy both for temporal life 40 and for eternal life. (217) Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Over the People.—May our prayers ascend to you, O Lord, and drive every wickedness from your Church. Through.

[Note: [Column 0059D] In Pamelius: “Wednesday of the first week of Lent, at Saint Mary Major.” In the Roman Calendar: “In the first month, at Saint Mary.” The Swedish Royal Manuscript differs slightly from Pamelius.]

## WEDNESDAY OF THE FIRST MONTH

Mercifully hear our prayers, we beseech you, O Lord, and extend the right hand of your Majesty against all things that oppose us. Through our Lord.

### Another Prayer

Lord, graciously regard the devotion of your people, we ask, so that those who are chastened in body through abstinence may be refreshed in mind through the fruit of good works. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Receive, almighty Creator God, what we fasting bring from the abundance of your generosity; and, in your mercy, turn what has been granted to us for temporal support into eternal life. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you commanded an abundance of crops to be produced as nourishment for the human body, and you placed in us the medicine of fasting as nourishment for souls. Therefore we humbly invoke you, that our fasting may be acceptable to you, and that, while fasting from foods, you may absolve us from sins. Through Christ.

### After Communion

By receiving your sacrament, Lord, may we be cleansed both from our hidden faults and from the snares of our enemies. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

Illuminate our minds, we ask, Lord, with the light of your brightness, so that we may see what must be done and be able to do what is right. Through our Lord.

## Thursday within Lent

[Note: [Col. 0060D] In the Roman Calendar: “At Saint Lawrence, at Formosus,” which Pamel presents as a variant reading. In his text it reads: “At Saint Lawrence outside the walls.” The first Theodulf manuscript supports this, while the second has: “At Lawrence in Formosa.”]

Receive, we ask, Lord, our prayers, and admit to the ears of your mercy the petitions of the people consecrated to you. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

May these sacrifices, Lord, save us: they have been established through the medicinal practice of fasting. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because religious fasts have been suitably and salutarily established for us, so that we may restrain the immoderate allurements of bodily pleasure and, with the insolence of earthly delight curbed, the purer and more tranquil desire of faithful souls may be rendered fit to contemplate heavenly mysteries. Through Christ our Lord.

### After Communion

By the generosity of your gifts, Lord, raise us up both through temporal support and renew us through eternal gifts. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Grant, we ask, Lord, that Christian peoples may both recognize what they profess and love the heavenly gift which they frequently receive. Through the Lord.

[Note: With broad agreement, Pamel, the Roman Calendar, the Swedish Royal Codex, and two Theodulf manuscripts record the station here as: “At the Apostles.”]

## Friday within Lent

[Col. 0061A]

Be favorable, Lord, to your people, and in your merciful kindness lovingly sustain those whom you make devoted to yourself. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Receive, we ask, Lord, what has been offered through our service, and graciously sanctify your gifts. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for through the observance of fasting and the most welcome generosity of almsgiving you have taught us to obtain remedies for our sins. Therefore we implore your mercy, so that, fortified by these observances and by the performance of other good works, we may do those things by which both hope and ability may be available to us for attaining eternal joys. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Through the working of this mystery, Lord, may our vices be cleansed and righteous desires fulfilled. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Preserve your people, we ask, Lord, and make them secure from all the adversities they deserve, so that, having received tranquility, they may serve you with a devoted mind. Through.

## Saturday with Twelve Readings of the First Month

(218)

[Note: [Col. 0061D] Thus all the printed and handwritten codices read it. In Pamel and in the Roman Calendar, “At Saint Peter” is added. Since the manuscripts have “Twelve Readings,” John Fronto suspects that one should read “in the twelfth reading,” namely, from the Gospel, which followed eleven others drawn from various books of Sacred Scripture. Following Pamel, this Saturday is called “of the twelve readings,” either because twelve different readings were customarily read, or because the same six readings were read once in Greek and once in Latin. Consult Pamel at this passage.]

Look favorably, Lord, we ask, upon your people, and mercifully turn away from them the scourges of your anger. Through our Lord.

### Another Prayer

God, who do not permit those who sin to perish, but wait for them to turn and live, we ask you to suspend the punishment due for our sins, and in your mercy grant that concealment may not accumulate vengeance, but rather that amendment through fasting may contribute to pardon. Through.

### Another Prayer

Look upon us, God, our protector, so that we who are weighed down by the burden of our ancestors, having received mercy, may serve you with a liberated mind. Through.

### Another Prayer

Be present, we ask, Lord, to our supplications, so that, by your generosity, we may be worthy to be humble amid prosperity and secure amid adversity. Through.

### Another Prayer

Go before our actions, we ask, Lord, by your inspiration, and accompany them by your help, so that all our activity may always begin from you and, begun through you, be brought to completion. Through.

### At Mass

God, who subdued the flames of fire for the three children, mercifully grant that the flame of vices may not consume us, your servants. Through Christ our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

By these present sacrifices, Lord, sanctify our fasts, so that what our observance professes outwardly may work inwardly. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: illuminator and Redeemer of our souls, who, after we had been expelled from paradise through the first Adam’s violation of the law of abstinence, recalled us by the stronger remedy of fasting, through grace, to the blessedness of our ancient homeland. You have also taught us through loving instruction by what observances we may be freed from all sins. Through Christ our Lord.

### After Communion

By your sanctifications, almighty God, may our vices be healed and eternal remedies come to us. Through Christ our Lord.

### Over the People

Mercifully absolve us, Lord, we ask, from all sins, so that, having received forgiveness of sins, we may serve you with free minds. Through.

## Sunday II in Lent

(219)

[Note: [Col. 0062D] Pamel reads here: “The Sunday is vacant.” But the reading should be taken from our manuscripts, especially the Swedish Royal Codex: “On Sunday it is vacant.” The same is read in the Roman Calendar. For why it is said to be vacant, consult John Fronto. Certainly, in the Swedish Royal Codex, Gemeticus, Theodulf, and others, the office of this Sunday is assigned as on the other Sundays, except for the station. Perhaps, therefore, because of the sacred orders conferred with great labor on Saturday evening, there was no procession or station, nor was a homily delivered.]

God, who see that we are deprived of every virtue, guard us inwardly and outwardly, so that we may be protected in body from all adversities and cleansed in mind from evil thoughts. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Graciously accept, Lord, the gifts of your Church, which in your mercy you have granted to be offered, and powerfully cause them to pass into the mystery of our salvation. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly beseech your Majesty to pour into our minds the gift of medicinal observance. And since you do not cease to bring aid even to the negligent, may you provide greater benefits to the devoted. Through Christ the Lord.

### Blessing

May almighty God, the author and lover of fasting and of the other virtues, sanctify you with his blessing. Amen. May he kindle in you the affection of pious devotion and, in his kindness, grant a gracious hearing to those who supplicate him. Amen. May your minds, cleansed by sincere fasts, abound in the increase of every good thing. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

### After Communion

Refreshed, Lord, by heavenly bread, may we be nourished for eternal life, we ask. Through.

### Over the People

Graciously enlighten your family, we ask, Lord, so that, cleaving to what pleases you, it may be worthy to receive all that is good. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0063D] In Pamel, with the agreement of the Swedish Royal manuscripts, Gemeticus, two Theodulf manuscripts, and the Roman Calendar, the station is at Saint Clement.]

## Monday in the Second Week

Grant, almighty God, we ask, that your family, which abstains from food by afflicting the flesh, may fast from guilt by pursuing righteousness. Through.

### Over the Offerings

May this offering of appeasement and praise, Lord, make us worthy of your propitiation. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and ask your loving kindness with humble devotion, so that, pleased by the offering of our fasting, you may grant us forgiveness of sins and free us from harmful snares. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 0063B]

### After Communion

May this communion, Lord, cleanse us from guilt and make us sharers in heavenly healing. Through.

### Over the People

Be present, we ask, Lord, to your supplicants, and amid the snares of worldly wickedness accompany our weakness with everlasting mercy. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0063D] In the Roman Calendar, supported by two Theodulf manuscripts, the station is at Saint Balbina, whose titular church is mentioned in a synod held under Saint Gregory, as John Fronto observes. Pamel reads: “At Saint Albina,” and the Swedish Royal Codex: “At Salbina.”]

## Tuesday in the Second Week

Perfect in us, we ask, Lord, in your kindness, the help of holy observance, so that what we have recognized must be done with you as its author, we may fulfill with you as its agent. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Being gracious toward us through these mysteries, Lord, work your sanctification in us, which may cleanse us from earthly vices and lead us to heavenly gifts. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you commanded bodies to be chastened through devotion to fasting for the healing of souls; grant, we ask, that our hearts may be able to practice the commands of your mercy in such a way that, with your help, we may be worthy to attain your promises. Through our Lord.

### After Communion

Make us worthy, Lord, of sacred gifts; grant that we obey your commands, we ask. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Grant your people, Lord, we ask, the help of consolation, and mercifully allow those laboring under prolonged calamities to breathe again. Through Christ our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0063D] The station for this day in the Roman Calendar, in Pamel’s Codex, and in our manuscripts is at Saint Cecilia, whose titular church is mentioned by the Roman synod under our Gregory.]

## Wednesday in the Second Week

Look favorably, Lord, upon your people, and grant that those whom you command to abstain from bodily foods may also cease from harmful vices. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Look favorably, Lord, upon the offerings we present to you, and through this holy exchange absolve the bonds of our sins. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: through whom you accomplished the reconciliation of the human race by a wondrous dispensation. Grant, we ask, that, purified by holy fasting, we may be wholly subject to you in heart and, amid the snares of worldly wickedness, by your mercy persevere unharmed. Through him your Majesty.

[Col. 0064B]

### After Communion

Having received the sacraments, Lord, may we advance, we ask, toward the increase of eternal redemption. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

God, restorer and lover of innocence, direct the hearts of your servants toward yourself, so that, having conceived the fervor of your Spirit, we may be found steadfast in faith and effective in action. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0064D] On this day the station, according to Pamel’s edition, with the agreement of the Swedish Royal Codex and two Theodulf manuscripts, is at Saint Mary across the Tiber. The Roman Calendar adds: “The title of Callistus.” It should be observed that, in these Lenten offices, the Vatican and Gussanville editions differ little—indeed scarcely at all—from ours.]

## Thursday in the Second Week

Grant us, Lord, we ask, the help of your grace, so that, suitably devoted to fasts and prayers, we may be freed from enemies of mind and body. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

May the gifts of our fasting be acceptable to you, Lord, we ask; may they both make us worthy through your grace by cleansing us and lead us to eternal promises. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and beseech your loving kindness with devoted hearts through the celebration of fasting, so that we who are oppressed by the weight of evils as sins assail us may both be freed from all sins and serve you with a liberated mind. Through Christ our Lord.

### After Communion

May your grace not abandon us, Lord, we ask; may it make us devoted to sacred service and always obtain your help for us. Through our Lord.

46

### Over the People

Be present, Lord, to your servants, and lavish perpetual kindness upon those who ask, so that for those who glory in you as their author and guide, you may both restore what has been gathered and preserve what has been restored. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0064D] The manuscripts, whose reading is supported by Pamel’s printed editions, have: “At Saint Vitalis.” In the Roman Calendar it reads: “At the Apostles among the Vestinae,” unless “in the title,” that is, “in the title of Vestina,” should be read instead of “among,” as John Fronto conjectures.]

## Friday in the Second Week

Grant, almighty God, we ask, that, purified by holy fasting, you may cause us to reach the holy things to come with sincere minds. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

May these sacrifices, God, both remain in us through sanctification and be strengthened through their effect. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you do not permit those who sin to perish, but exhort them to turn to you and live. Therefore we ask your loving kindness to suspend the punishment of your severity against our sins and mercifully grant us the forgiveness we desire; may the distress of our iniquities not provoke you to vengeance, but may the observance of fasting and amendment of conduct move you to the forgiveness of our sins. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 0065B]

### After Communion

Grant, we ask, Lord, that, having received the pledge of eternal salvation, we may advance toward it in a fitting way so that we may be able to reach it. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

Grant your people, Lord, we ask, salvation of mind and body, so that, cleaving to good works, they may always deserve to be defended by the protection of your virtue. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0065D] Here, with broad agreement, the station is read as being at Saints Marcellinus and Peter.]

## Saturday in the Second Week

Grant, Lord, we ask, a saving effect to our fasts, so that the chastisement undertaken by the flesh may pass into the quickening of our souls.

### Over the Offerings

Being gracious through these sacrifices, Lord, grant that we who pray to be absolved from our own offenses may not be burdened by external ones. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and continually implore your mercy, so that you may grant that our minds, which you see to be weighed down by earthly affections, may be relieved through medicinal fasts, and that through the affliction of our bodies the strength of our souls may arise. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May the divine libation of your sacrament, Lord, pour into the innermost recesses of our heart and powerfully make us its participants. Through Christ our Lord.

### Over the People

Guard your family, Lord, we ask, with continual mercy, so that what relies upon the sole hope of heavenly grace may also be fortified by heavenly protection. Through the same.

[Note: [Col. 0065D] The printed and manuscript codices agree no less in assigning today’s station to Saint Lawrence outside the walls. In the Roman Calendar, however, it simply reads: “At Saint Lawrence the Martyr.”]

## Sunday III in Lent

We ask, almighty God, that you look upon the prayers of the humble and extend the right hand of your Majesty for our defense. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0066A]

### Over the Offerings

Receive, we ask, Lord, the gifts of your devoted servants, and by your mercy purify those who serve your divine mysteries, through which you also justify the ignorant. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly beseech you that, together with bodily abstinence, our mind also may turn away from unlawful desires; and that what we deny ourselves in earthly pleasure through bodily banquets, we may cut away from the perverse intentions of the human will. Thus may we be made ready, through suitable fasting, to receive the Holy of Holies faithfully and beneficially. May these things be more certainly, readily, and continually present to us, the more pleasing we have been to their ordinances. Through.

[Col. 0066B]

### Blessing

[Note: [Col. 0065D] This blessing is absent from the Vatican and Gussanville editions, as well as from our manuscripts and Pamel’s Codex.]

May almighty God mercifully accept the sacrifices of your fasts and make you worthy of his blessing. Amen.

May he so fortify your minds against vices with the gift of moderation, instruct them through the teaching of his commands, and fill them with the gift of charity, that he may grant you to please him in all things. Amen.

May he grant that, having celebrated the days of the present Lent with the greatest devotion, you may approach the Paschal feasts with purified hearts. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this.

### After Communion

Graciously absolve us, Lord, from every guilt and danger, for you grant us to share in so great a mystery. Through our Lord.

48

### Over the People

May heavenly propitiation increase the people subject to you, Lord, we ask, and always make them serve your commands.

[Note: [Col. 0066D] The station is prescribed in Pamel’s Codex and in the manuscripts at Saint Mark, as in the Roman Calendar. John Fronto observes that the Saint Mark mentioned here is the Roman Pontiff celebrated on 7 October, whose name is borne by an ancient titular church in the city. Pamel notes that on this feria the first scrutiny of the elect, or catechumens, was customarily announced; it was celebrated on the following Wednesday.]

## Monday in the Third Week

[Col. 0066C]

Kindly pour into our hearts, Lord, we ask, so that just as we abstain from bodily foods, we may also withdraw our senses from harmful excesses. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Perfect as a saving sacrament the gift of our service which we offer to you, Lord. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and pray for your mercy with every supplication, so that through this observance of fasts the affection of our devotion may increase and a religious result may adorn our actions; so that, with your help, we may always be withdrawn from human excesses and, by your generosity, be able to cling to heavenly admonitions. Through Christ our Lord.

### After Communion

Grant, almighty and merciful God, we ask, that we may receive with a pure mind what we touch with our mouth. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Preserve your family, Lord, always instructed in good works, and console it with present assistance in such a way that, in your mercy, you may lead it to heavenly gifts. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0067D] The Roman Calendar, Pamel’s Codex, the Swedish Royal Codex, and other manuscripts add: “At Saint Potentiana.” She is the same as Saint Pudentiana.]

## Tuesday in the Third Week

Hear us, almighty and merciful God, and graciously grant us the gifts of saving self-restraint. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Through these sacraments, we ask, Lord, may the effect of our redemption come to us, so that it may always withdraw us from human excesses and lead us to every saving good. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you do not will the souls of sinners to perish, but their sins; and you do not always immediately judge those who sin, but wait for those summoned to repentance. Turn away from us, we ask, the anger we deserve, and pour out upon us the mercy we desire, so that, purified by holy fasting, we may be worthy to be enrolled in the company of your elect. Through Christ our Lord.

49

### After Communion

Purified through the sacred mysteries, Lord, may we obtain both forgiveness and grace. Through.

### Over the People

Grant, merciful God, that your people may always remain devoted to you and unceasingly obtain from your mercy what benefits them. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0067D] The station is prescribed at Saint Xystus, or, as it is read in the Swedish Royal Codex, at Saint Sixtus; his titular church is mentioned in the Roman synod under Gregory II in the year 721.]

## Wednesday in the Third Week

Grant us, Lord, we ask, that, instructed by saving fasts and abstaining also from harmful vices, we may more easily obtain your reconciliation. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Receive, we ask, Lord, the prayers of your people together with the offerings of sacrifices, and defend us from every danger as we celebrate your mysteries. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly implore your mercy, so that the sacred mysteries of our fasts may always be acceptable to your loving kindness; and grant that those whose bodies are chastened by the observance of abstinence may also be adorned in mind with virtues and heavenly instruction. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 0067D]

### After Communion

May the heavenly table by which we have been fed sanctify us, Lord, and, purified from every error, make us acceptable to the heavenly promises. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

Defend your family, Lord, and protect it, prostrate before you with its whole heart, from dread of its enemies; nor may it find with difficulty the good things for which both your saints and the angelic powers plead with you. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0068D] The frequently mentioned manuscripts, both handwritten and printed, have here: “At Saints Cosmas and Damian.”]

## Thursday in the Third Week

[Col. 0068A]

Grant, almighty God, we ask, that we who seek the grace of your protection, freed from every evil, may serve you with a secure mind. Through.

### Over the Offerings

God, from whose grace the dew descends so that we may approach your mysteries with purified senses, grant, we ask, that in the solemn honoring of their transmission we may offer fitting service. Through.

50

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly ask your boundless mercy, so that you may cause us, your servants, chastened by the austerity of fasting and instructed by the performance of other good works, to persevere sincerely in your commands and reach the Paschal feasts unharmed; and so console us with present support that we may be worthy to attain eternal joys. Through Christ the Lord.

[Col. 0068B]

### After Communion

May the venerable reception of your sacrament, Lord, cleanse us through its mystical effect and defend us by perpetual power. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

Preserve your people, we ask, Lord, and multiply in them the gifts of your grace, so that, freed from all offenses, they may not be deprived of temporal assistance and may rejoice in eternal instruction. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0068D] The station is at Saint Lawrence in the title of Lucina, or, as Pamel has it, with the agreement of the Swedish Royal Codex, “in Lucina.”]

## Friday in the Week

May you pursue our fasts, Lord, with kindly favor, so that just as we fast from food in body, we may also fast from vices in mind. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Look favorably, Lord, upon the gifts we offer, so that they may always be pleasing to you and beneficial to us. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: who, to reveal the mystery of his humility, sat down, weary, beside a well; who asked the Samaritan woman to give him a drink of water, he who had created in her the gift of faith. And he deigned to thirst for her faith in such a way that, while asking her for water, he kindled in her the fire of divine love. Therefore we implore your boundless mercy, so that, despising the dark depth of vices, abandoning the jar of harmful desires, and thirsting always for you, who are the fountain of life and the source of goodness, we may please you through the observance of our fasts. Through him your Majesty.

[Col. 0068D]

### After Communion

May the reception of this sacrament, Lord, cleanse us from guilt and lead us to the heavenly kingdom. Through.

### Over the People

May your people rejoice, Lord, we ask, always trusting in your blessing, so that they may be helped by temporal benefits and instructed by eternal ones. Through the Lord.

## Saturday in the Third Week

[Note: [Col. 0069D] Pamel and the Roman Calendar read: “At Saint Susanna,” and the manuscripts support them.]

Grant, almighty God, we ask, that the dignity of human nature, wounded by immoderation, may be restored through the discipline of medicinal moderation. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Grant, almighty God, we ask, that the gift of this sacrifice may always cleanse and protect our weakness from every evil. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: who consecrated the observance of Lenten fasting in Moses and Elijah and adorned it in your Only-Begotten Son, the Lord of the law and the prophets and of us all. Therefore we humbly ask your immeasurable goodness that, aided by his most abundant compassion, we may be able to fulfill what he completed through the uninterrupted continuance of constant fasts; and that, fulfilling what he commanded, we may deserve to receive the gifts he promised. Through him.

[Col. 0069B]

### After Communion

We ask, almighty God, that we may be numbered among the members of him whose body and blood we share. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

Extend, Lord, the right hand of heavenly assistance to your faithful, so that they may seek you with their whole heart and deserve to obtain what they rightly ask. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0069D] In Pamel’s Codex the station is at Jerusalem. The Swedish Royal Codex and two Theodulf manuscripts agree. In the Roman Calendar, however, it reads: “In Suxurius,” which John Fronto thinks means the same as “in the seat”; consult his notes at this passage.]

## Sunday IV in Lent

[Col. 0069C]

Grant, almighty God, we ask, that we who are afflicted because of the merit of our actions may recover our breath through the consolation of your grace. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Receive, Lord, the sacrifice by whose immolation you graciously willed to be appeased, and grant, we ask, that, cleansed through its working, we may offer you the pleasing affection of our mind. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and glorify you, Creator of all things, for past fruits, and humbly beseech you concerning those to come, so that, just as we are not found ungrateful for what we have received, we may not be judged unworthy of what we are to receive; but, by repeatedly presenting fasts with solemn devotion, may we gain, together with bodily support, progress also for our souls. Through Christ the Lord.

52

### Blessing

[Note: [Col. 0069D] This blessing is found in the Benedictional, but is absent from the Theodulf Codex and the Vatican edition.]

May God, who has deigned to lead you to the midpoint of these present Lenten days, himself deign to bless you through his mercy. Amen.

May he accept your past abstinence and make your future abstinence pleasing to him, so that, just as he grants you to abstain from unlawful foods, he may also grant you to abstain from every vice. Amen.

Thus, rendering him thanks for the fruits of graces past and future, may you be able to reach holy Easter unharmed. May he himself deign to grant this.

### After Communion

Grant us, merciful God, that we may handle with sincere service your holy things, with which we are continually filled, and always receive them with faithful minds. Through.

### Over the People

God, who in the desert region satisfied a multitude of people by your power, provide us also with spiritual food during the course of this passing age, lest we fail. You who live and reign.

[Note: [Col. 0070D] With broad agreement, the station for this feria is at the Four Crowned Saints.]

## Monday in the Fourth Week

[Col. 0070B]

Grant, almighty God, we ask, that, recalling the sacred observances with annual devotion, we may please you both in body and in mind. Through.

### Over the Offerings

May the sacrifice offered to you, Lord, always give us life and protect us. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly implore your mercy, so that the venerable exercise of saving fasting may return us cleansed from the stains of our sins and lead us to the fellowship of the heavenly citizens, so that here we may receive an increase of devoted acts and there obtain the reward of eternal blessedness. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 0070C]

### After Communion

Having been satisfied by the abundance of the divine gift, we ask, Lord our God, that we may always live in participation in it. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

May the people dedicated to you, Lord, advance in the affection of pious devotion, we ask, so that, instructed by sacred actions, the more pleasing they become to your Majesty, the more they may be increased with greater gifts. Through the Lord.

53

[Note: [Col. 0070D] The station for this feria, by equal agreement, is at Saint Lawrence in Damaso, or, as the Swedish Royal Codex has it, “in Damasus.” In the Roman Calendar it reads only: “In the title of Damasus,” omitting the name of Saint Lawrence.]

## Tuesday in the Fourth Week of Lent

Sacred fasts of observance, Lord, we ask, may provide us with both an increase of pious conduct and the continual help of your reconciliation. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Purify us, merciful God, so that the prayers of your Church, which brings you pious gifts pleasing to you, may become more acceptable when our minds have been cleansed. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through the Mediator of God and human beings, Jesus Christ our Lord: who, in the middle of the feast, ascended into the temple to teach; who descended from heaven to free the world from the darkness of ignorance. His descent instructs the human race with saving teaching, his death redeemed it from perpetual death, and his ascent leads it to the heavenly kingdom. Through him, we ask you, most high Father, that, taught by his instruction and purified through devotion to saving moderation, we may reach your promises secure. Through him your Majesty.

### After Communion

Having received heavenly gifts, we ask, Lord, do not allow us to come to judgment through what you have provided as a remedy for your faithful. Through.

### Over the People

[Note: [Col. 0071D] This prayer is read in Pamel’s Codex in the office of the preceding feria under the title “At Vespers.” It is absent from the Swedish Royal Codex, though Pamel’s edition closely resembles it.]

May your right hand protect your people as they pray, Lord, we ask, and may it graciously instruct them once purified, so that through present consolation they may advance toward future goods. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0071D] The station is assigned to Saint Paul in all our books that mention the stations.]

## Wednesday in the Fourth Week

Almighty and eternal God, who grant rewards according to merit to the righteous and forgiveness through fasting to sinners, have mercy on those who supplicate you and spare sinners, so that the confession of our guilt may be able to receive pardon for our offenses. Through our Lord.

### Another Prayer

Grant, almighty God, we ask, that those whom votive fasts chastise may also be gladdened by that same holy devotion, so that, with earthly affections subdued, we may more easily receive heavenly things. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

We humbly ask you, Lord, that through these sacrifices our sins may be cleansed, because then you grant us true health both of mind and of body. Through our Lord.

[Source ends here.]

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for by the illumination of his faith he dispelled the darkness of the world; and the human race, which the womb of its first mother had brought forth blind, he restored to illumination through the mystery of his Incarnation, and made children of adoption those who were held in the bonds of just condemnation. Through him we ask you that, in his most just judgment, we may be found such as we became in the most blessed rebirth of the saving bath; so that, imbued with the remedy of his Incarnation, washed by the cleansing of the most holy bath, and adorned with devotion to self-restraint, we may reach eternal joys unharmed. Through whom [be your] Majesty [glorified].

[Col. 0071D] At the Completion.—May the sacraments which we have received, Lord our God, both fill us with spiritual nourishment and protect us with bodily assistance. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—May the ears of your mercy, Lord, be open to the prayers of those who entreat you; and, so that you may grant those who ask what they desire, make them ask for what is pleasing to you. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0072D] A station at Saint Sylvester is prescribed in the Codices mentioned above that speak of stations.]

THURSDAY IN THE FOURTH WEEK.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who trust in your protection may, with your help, overcome all that opposes us. Through our Lord.

Over the Offerings.—May this Victim, Lord, we ask, become pleasing through the solemn observance of the fasts; and, that it may be more acceptable to you, may it be offered with purified minds. Through our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: whose goodness created humanity, whose justice condemned it, and whose mercy redeemed it. We humbly implore you: just as through unlawful desires we fell from the blessed realm, so may we return to our eternal homeland through abstinence. May your mercy so govern our weakness that our mortality may be sustained by transitory supports, while immortality is happily acquired through the growth of good works. Through Christ.

At the Completion.—May your holy things, Lord, both renew us by giving life and give us life by renewing us. Through our Lord.

55 Over the People.—God, founder and ruler of your people, drive away the sins by which they are assailed, so that, always pleasing to you, they may be secure under your protection. Through the same Lord.

FRIDAY IN THE FOURTH WEEK.

[Note: [Col. 0072D] In the same Codices mentioned above it reads here: At Saint Eusebius.]

God, who renew the world through ineffable sacraments, grant, we ask, that your Church may advance through eternal institutions and not be deprived of temporal aids. Through.

[Col. 0072C] Over the Offerings.—May the gifts offered, we ask, Lord, purify us and continually make you favorable toward us. Through our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. He is the eternal day, the unfailing light, the everlasting splendor. He commanded his followers to walk in the light in such a way that they might escape the darkness of eternal night and happily reach the homeland of light. Through the humility of the humanity he assumed, he wept for Lazarus; through the power of his divinity, he restored him to life; and he brought back to life the human race, buried beneath the fourfold burden of sins. Through him we ask that, by observing the fast, we may be released from the bonds of our sins, restored to the blessedness of eternal life, and numbered among the assemblies of the saints. Through whom.

At the Completion.—May participation in this sacrament, we ask, Lord, continually free us from our own guilt and protect us from every adversity. Through.

Over the People.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who are conscious of our weakness and trust in your power may always rejoice under your loving-kindness. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0073D] In the Roman Calendar it reads here: At Saint Lawrence at the Martyrs, although in the Pamelian Codex and in our manuscripts it reads: At Saint Lawrence outside the walls. Joan. Fronto likewise considers this the reading that should be adopted.]

SATURDAY IN THE FOURTH WEEK.

[Col. 0073A]

May the inclination of our devotion become fruitful through your grace, Lord, we ask, because the fasts we have undertaken will benefit us only if they are pleasing to your mercy. Through our Lord.

Over the Offerings.—Be appeased, we ask, Lord, by the offerings received, and in your mercy compel our wills—even when they rebel—to turn toward you. Through the Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: giver of mercy and author of all goodness, who through fasts, prayers, and almsgiving grant remedies for sins and increases of every virtue. We humbly and devoutly beseech you: you have given us the most salutary teaching for undertaking these things; grant us unfailing effectiveness for completing them, so that, obediently carrying out your commands, we may happily receive your promises. Through Christ our Lord.

At the Completion.—May your holy things, we ask, Lord, purify us and, through their operation, make us pleasing to you. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—God, who choose to show mercy rather than anger toward those who hope in you, grant us worthily to mourn the evils we have committed, so that we may be able to find the grace of your consolation. Through.

SUNDAY IN THE FIFTH WEEK OF LENT. [Note: [Col. 0073D] Thus it is read in all our books, both printed and handwritten, except the Roman Calendar, in which, as in the others, the station is given as: At Saint Peter.] ON THE PASSION OF THE LORD.

We ask, almighty God, graciously look upon your household, so that, by your gift, it may be governed in body and guarded in mind by your protection. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0073C] Over the Offerings.—May these gifts, Lord, we ask, both release the bonds of our wickedness and obtain for us the gifts of your mercy. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: earnestly imploring your Majesty that, as the day of the saving feast draws nearer, we may advance with ever greater devotion toward celebrating worthily its paschal mystery. Through Christ our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0073D] This Blessing is found in the Book of Blessings.]

Blessing.—May the Lord kindle in you the power of his love and, through observance of the fasts, pour into you the gift of his blessing. Amen. May you offer him the sacrifices of self-restraint in such a way that you please him through the sacrifice of a contrite and humbled heart. Amen. May your prayer, borne upward on the wings of fasting and almsgiving, ascend to the ears of your Creator, so that he may make you heirs of eternal blessedness and companions of the citizens above. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Completion.—Be present with us, Lord our God, and protect forever with your [Col. 0074A] [Note: [Col. 0073D] In the Pamelian Edition, “protect with supports” (*defende subsidiis*), while the Swedish Royal Codex, which differs, has “with defenses” (*praesidiis*).] defenses those whom you have refreshed with your mysteries. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—Grant, we ask, Lord, that in our days the people serving you may increase both in merit and in number through steadfast service according to your will. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0074D] The station for this day is at Saint Chrysogonus.]

MONDAY IN THE FIFTH WEEK.

Sanctify our fasts, we ask, Lord, and graciously grant us pardon for all our offenses. Through our Lord.

Over the Offerings.—Grant us, Lord our God, that this saving Victim may become both the cleansing of our offenses and the propitiation of your Majesty. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting [Col. 0074B] and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: earnestly imploring you that our fasts may be sanctified in such a way that pardon for all our sins may come to us, so that, as the passion of your only-begotten Son approaches, we may be able to please you by the presentation of good works. Through whom [be your] Majesty [glorified].

At the Completion.—May participation in your sacrament, we ask, Lord, provide us with salvation, purification, and healing. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—May a copious blessing, we ask, Lord, descend upon your faithful, and may they generously obtain what they seek with submissive hearts. Through.

TUESDAY [Note: [Col. 0074D] In Pamelius, with the Swedish Royal and Theoderic manuscripts agreeing, the station is at Saint Cyriacus. In the Roman Calendar it reads: At Saint Quiriacus. This title is mentioned especially in the Roman synod under our Gregory, which in the earlier editions was in Book IV, Letter 44, but is now at the end of the Register; Aventius, priest of Saint Quiriacus, subscribed to this synod.] IN THE FIFTH WEEK.

[Col. 0074C] May our fasts be acceptable to you, Lord, we ask, and, by cleansing us, may your grace make us worthy and lead us to eternal remedies. Through the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0074D] In Pamelius: “worthy of your grace” (*gratiae tuae dignos*). The manuscripts and the Swedish Royal Codex support our reading.]

Over the Offerings.—We bring offerings to you, Lord, to be sacrificed; we ask that they provide us with temporal consolation, so that we may more certainly not despair of the eternal promises. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and to beseech you with devoted minds to restore us inwardly and outwardly, and to cleanse us from the stains of sins through salutary self-restraint. Make those whom you do not wish to be hindered by seductive pleasures strong through the power of spiritual virtues, and so cherish us amid transitory things that you may grant us to cling to what is everlasting. Through Christ our Lord.

58 At the Completion.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, continually carrying out divine things, we may deserve to draw near to heavenly gifts. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—Free from sins and enemies the people who entreat you, Lord, we ask, so that, living in holy conduct, they may not be defiled by any adversities. Through the same Lord our God.

WEDNESDAY IN THE FIFTH WEEK.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] In Pamelius and the Roman Calendar the station is assigned to Saint Marcellus; the first Theoderic manuscript agrees with them. In the Swedish Royal Codex: At Saint Marcellinus. In the second Theoderic: At Saint Mary.]

Having sanctified this fast, God, graciously enlighten the hearts of your faithful, and kindly grant a merciful hearing to those who entreat you, to whom you grant the affection of devotion. Through the Lord.

Over the Offerings.—Merciful God, grant that we may bring offerings of appeasement and praise to you with sincere service. Through.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting [Col. 0075B] and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and to implore you with submissive devotion that, through the fasts which we observe according to sacred institutions, we may deserve to be cleansed from every guilt and be able to receive your favor, as we prepare to celebrate the passion of your only-begotten Son. Through whom [be your] Majesty [glorified].

At the Completion.—Having received the blessing of the heavenly gift, we suppliantly beseech you, almighty God, that this same gift may be for us both the cause of the sacrament and the cause of salvation. Through the Lord.

Another.—Hear, we ask, Lord, the groaning of your suppliant people; and although we distrust the quality of our merits, may we deserve to obtain not judgment but mercy. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] In the Roman Calendar and in Pamelius it reads for the station: At Saint Apollinaris. The manuscripts confirm this.]

THURSDAY IN THE FIFTH WEEK.

Grant us, we ask, pardon for our sins, so that we may undertake the prescribed fasts with dispositions pleasing to you. Through the Lord.

Over the Offerings.—Grant us, Lord, we ask, that, as we prepare to celebrate the sacred mysteries, we may possess not only bodily abstinence but, what is more important, purity of mind. Through.

59 Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: you grant us to offer a solemn fast to you in such a way that we hope to receive the aid of your pardon; you instruct us to celebrate the Paschal [Col. 0075D] feasts in such a way that through them we may acquire everlasting joys. Through Christ our Lord.

At the Completion.—May the libation of your table always strengthen and renew us, Lord; may it govern and protect our weakness and lead us into the harbor of perpetual salvation. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—Merciful God, grant that, just as you grant us to offer a solemn fast to you, so you may graciously provide us with the help of your pardon. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0075D] According to the same Codices, the station for this day is at Saint Stephen.]

FRIDAY IN THE FIFTH WEEK.

Kindly pour into our hearts, Lord, that, restraining our sins through voluntary discipline, we may be afflicted temporarily rather than assigned to eternal punishments. Through.

Over the Offerings.—Merciful God, grant us that we may always deserve to serve your altars worthily and be saved through perpetual participation in them. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0076B] Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: whose mercy goes before us so that we may do good, follows after us so that we may not act in vain, kindles the intention by which we burn to accomplish good works, and grants the effectiveness by which we may bring them to perfection. We therefore beseech your clemency with tireless voices: cleansed from sins through the sacrifices of fasting, make us devoted to celebrating the passion of your only-begotten Son, our Lord. Through whom [be your] Majesty [glorified].

At the Completion.—May the perpetual protection of the sacrifice we have received, Lord, not abandon us, and may it always drive away from us every harmful thing. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—Protect your people, Lord, and govern with perpetual defense those who trust in the patronage of your Majesty. Through.

60 SATURDAY [Note: [Col. 0075D] In Pamelius the title is: “Saturday is free. The Lord Pope gives alms. At Saint Peter.” In the margin, however, it says: “That this is the true title of this day, and therefore that the following office is not Gregorian, is clear from the Roman Order, p. 41.” Alcuin gives the reason for this title: although alms are given by the pontiff at all times, he does so more particularly today because the Gospel mentions the poor; the event narrated in that Gospel occurred on this day, six days before Easter. In the Swedish Royal Codex it reads: “Saturday, at Saint Peter, when alms are given.” The second Theoderic agrees with this reading; the first has the same as the Pamelian Edition. In the Roman Calendar, however: “On Saturday, leavened bread is given in the Lateran consistory.”] BEFORE PALM SUNDAY.

Almighty eternal God, we humbly implore your clemency: you always go before our evils with mercy; make us pleasing to you by cleansing us through pious actions and salutary fasts. Through.

Over the Offerings.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, appeased by the sacrifices of our fasts, you may accompany us with the forgiveness of your remission. Through our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: [Col. 0076D] faith in you stirs us, hope raises us, and charity unites us. Your gratuitous mercy purifies those whom the guilt of conscience accuses. Therefore we beseech you with inward groaning: disciplined by restraining bodily nourishment, may we be found fit to celebrate the paschal mystery. Through Christ.

At the Completion.—Be present with your faithful, Lord, and preserve from earthly dangers those whom you refresh with heavenly sacraments. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—May your people, Lord, we ask, receive the gift of holy blessing, through which they may both avoid every harmful thing and find what they desire. Through the Lord.

(233) SUNDAY ON PALM SUNDAY [Note: [Col. 0077D] In the Pamelian Edition, with the manuscripts agreeing: “At Saint John in the Lateran.” In the Roman Calendar only “in the Lateran” is read. In the Swedish Royal Codex this blessing of the branches is found, although it is absent from the Pamelian Edition and others. The first Theoderic has the same: “God, whose Son descended from heaven to earth for the salvation of the human race, and, as the hour of his passion approached, willed to come to Jerusalem on a donkey and to be called and praised as king, deign to bless these branches of palms and of other foliage, so that all who carry them may be so filled with the gift of your blessing that in this age they may overcome the temptations of the ancient enemy, and in the age to come may be able to appear before you with the palm of victory and the fruit of good works. Through the same [Lord].”]

Almighty eternal God, who, for the human race to imitate the example of humility, made our Savior assume flesh and undergo the cross, graciously grant that we may deserve both to possess the lessons of his patience and to share in his Resurrection. He who lives with you.

Over the Offerings.—Grant, we ask, Lord, that the gift offered before the eyes of your Majesty may obtain for us the grace of devotion and acquire the effect of blessed perpetuity. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0078D] The edition of Angelo Rocca, or the Vatican Edition, has another Preface.]

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: through whom pardon is bestowed upon us, peace is proclaimed throughout all ages, and instruction is handed down to all believers, so that the coming day may receive us as sanctified. And therefore, with the angels—

61 Blessing.—May almighty God bless you, whom you strive to please through the mortification of fasts and the observance of these present days. Amen. May he grant you that, just as you have striven to be presented to him with branches of palms and other foliage, so after death you may be able to appear with the palm of victory and the fruit of good works. Amen. And may you, who believe with pure hearts in the passion of his only-begotten Son and strive to venerate it with devoted minds, come to the feasts of his Resurrection and the rewards of your own recompense, supported by his protection. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Completion.—Grant us, almighty God, that, since our mortality is subject to vices, your medicine may purify us and your power protect us. Through.

Over the People.—Merciful God, grant that we, your faithful, may experience as salutary what the world inflicted in the passion of your Son. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0078D] In the Swedish Royal Codex and the second Theoderic the station is at Saint Praxedes. Pamelius has the same. But in the Roman Calendar and the first Theoderic it reads: At Saints Nereus and Achilleus.]

MONDAY AFTER PALM SUNDAY.

[Col. 0077D]

(235) Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who fail through our weakness amid so many adversities may recover our breath through the intervening passion of your only-begotten Son. He who lives with you.

[Col. 0078A] Another.—Remember your mercies, Lord, and sanctify your servants with eternal protection; for them Jesus Christ, your Son, established the paschal mystery for us through his blood. He who lives with you.

Over the Offerings.—May these sacrifices, almighty God, cleanse us by their powerful efficacy and make us come more pure to their source. Through the Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: whose humanity gathers us, whose humility raises us, whose betrayal releases us, whose punishment redeems us, whose cross saves us, whose blood cleanses us, whose flesh nourishes us. Through him, supreme Father, we beseech you with the services of fasting that we may approach with purified minds to celebrate his passion. Through whom.

At the Completion.—May your holy things, Lord, provide us with divine fervor, so that we may delight equally in their practice and in their fruit. Through our Lord.

Over the People.—Help us, God our Savior, and grant us to come rejoicing to recall the benefits by which you have deigned to restore us. Through our Lord.

TUESDAY AFTER [Note: [Col. 0078D] All the Codices agree in assigning the station to Saint Prisca.] PALM SUNDAY.

Almighty eternal God, grant us to carry out the mysteries of the Lord’s passion in such a way that we may deserve to receive pardon. Through the same [Lord].

Another.—Almighty eternal God, who restore us through the blessed passion of your Christ, preserve in us the works of your mercy, so that we may live in perpetual devotion during the celebration of this mystery. Through.

Over the Offerings.—May these sacrifices, we ask, Lord, restore us more fully, since they have been established through medicinal fasts. Through our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: the days of whose saving passion and glorious Resurrection are known to be approaching; in them the pride of the ancient enemy is overcome and the mystery of our redemption is celebrated. Therefore we ask your boundless clemency: just as the whole substance of our salvation rests in him alone, so through him may the sacrifice of our fasts and actions always be pleasing to you. Through whom.

At the Completion.—Filled, Lord, with the grace of the sacred gift, we humbly implore you that what we touch with sweet reverence through bodily taste, we may perceive as sweeter in our minds. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0079A] Over the People.—May your mercy, God, both cleanse us from every furtive influence of the old condition and make us capable of holy newness. Through the Lord.

WEDNESDAY [Note: [Col. 0079D] Everywhere the station is given as being at Saint Mary, namely Saint Mary Major, as all the Codices have it, except the Roman Calendar.]

[Note: [Col. 0080D] None of the prayers assigned here is found for this Wednesday anywhere except in the Codices of Angelo Rocca, or the Vatican Codices, reprinted by Guss. and Menard.]

At the third hour the pontiff proceeds with the clergy and his order to the altar in the major church and says the Solemn Prayers in this order: “Let us pray.” And the Deacon says: “Let us bend the knees.” After they have prayed, he says: “Rise.” And the pontiff gives the prayer.

God, from whom both Judas received the punishment of his guilt and the thief the reward of his confession, grant us the effect of your favor, so that, just as Jesus Christ our Lord in his passion allotted different rewards according to their merits to each of the two, so he may grant us the grace of his Resurrection once the error of the old condition has been removed. He who lives with you.

[Col. 0079B] After “Amen” follows, and he says the Solemn Prayers; he omits only the prayer for himself. The other priests say it for him in their own churches. And while they bend the knee in the other prayers, they do not bend the knee for the Jews.

63 Let us pray, beloved: for the holy Church of God, that God and our Lord may deign to grant it peace and protect it throughout the whole world, subjecting principalities and powers to it, and granting that we, leading a quiet and tranquil life, may glorify God the almighty Father.

Let us pray. The Deacon says: Let us bend the knees. After they have prayed, he says: Rise.

Almighty eternal God, who have revealed your glory in Christ to all the nations, preserve the works of your mercy, so that your Church, spread throughout the whole world, may persevere with steadfast faith in confessing your name. Through the same Lord our God.

Let us pray also for our most blessed pope N., that God and our Lord, who chose him for the episcopal order, may preserve him safe and unharmed for his holy Church, to govern the holy people of God.

Let us pray.—Almighty eternal God, on whose judgment all things are founded, graciously look upon our prayers and preserve in your mercy the bishop chosen for us, so that the Christian people, governed by such a leader, may increase under so great a pontiff in the merits of their faith. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Let us pray also for all bishops, priests, deacons, subdeacons, acolytes, exorcists, readers, doorkeepers, [Col. 0079D] confessors, virgins, widows, and for all the holy people of God.

Let us pray.—Almighty eternal God, whose Spirit sanctifies and governs the whole body of the Church, hear us as we entreat you for all its orders, so that, by the gift of your grace, you may be faithfully served by every rank. Through the same Lord.

Let us pray also for our most Christian king N., that God and our Lord may make all barbarian nations subject to him, for our perpetual peace.

Let us pray.—Almighty eternal God, in whose [Col. 0080A] hand are all powers and all rights of kingdoms, graciously look upon the rule of the Romans and the Franks, so that the peoples who trust in their own savagery may be restrained by the right hand of your power. Through.

Let us pray also for our catechumens, that God and our Lord may open the ears of their hearts and the door of mercy, so that, having received remission of all sins through the bath of rebirth, they too may be found in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Let us pray.—Almighty eternal God, who always make your Church fruitful with new offspring, increase faith and understanding in our catechumens, so that, reborn from the baptismal font, they may be joined to the children of your adoption. Through.

Let us pray, beloved, to God the almighty Father, [Col. 0080B] that he may cleanse the world from all errors, remove diseases, drive away famine, open prisons, loosen bonds, grant travelers a return, the sick health, and those at sea the harbor of salvation.

Let us pray.—Almighty eternal God, consolation of the sorrowful and strength of those who labor, may the prayers of those crying out to you from every tribulation reach you, so that all may rejoice that your mercy has been present to them in their needs. Through.

Let us pray also for heretics and schismatics, that God and our Lord may rescue them from every error and deign to restore them to the holy Catholic and apostolic mother Church.

Let us pray.—Almighty eternal God, who save everyone and desire no one to perish, look upon the souls deceived by the devil’s fraud, so that, having abandoned every heretical perversity, the hearts of those in error may come to their senses and return to the unity of your truth. Through our Lord.

Let us pray also for the faithless Jews, that God and our Lord may remove the veil from their hearts, so that they too may acknowledge Jesus Christ our Lord.

Let us pray.—Almighty eternal God, who do not reject even Jewish faithlessness from your mercy, hear our prayers, which we offer for the blindness of that people, so that, having recognized the light of your truth, which is Christ, they may be rescued from their own darkness. Through the same Lord our God.

[Col. 0080D] Let us pray also for the pagans, that almighty God may remove iniquity from their hearts, and that, abandoning their idols, they may be converted to the living and true God and to his only Son, Jesus Christ, God and Lord of ours, with whom he lives and reigns, God, with the Holy Spirit, forever and ever.

Let us pray.—Almighty eternal God, who always seek not the death of sinners but life, graciously receive our prayer and free them from the worship of idols, and join them to your holy Church for the praise and glory of your name. Through.

[Col. 0081A] (251) When these things have been completed, he kisses the altar and departs. Afterwards, at the eighth hour, they enter for Mass in this order: the schola sings the antiphon for the Introit. When it is finished, the pontiff gives the prayer.

(254) [Note: [Col. 0081D] Here the office of this day begins in the other Codices, whether printed or handwritten.]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who are unceasingly afflicted by our offenses may be freed through the passion of your only-begotten Son. Who—

Then one reading is read. The Responsory follows. Afterwards another is said.

Prayer.—God, who for us willed your Son to undergo the gibbet [Note: [Col. 0081D] In Pamelius, “made [him] undergo it” (*subire fecisti*). The Swedish Royal Codex favors our reading.] of the cross, so that you might drive away from us the power of the enemy, grant us, your servants, that we may attain the grace of the Resurrection. Through the same [Lord].

(255) Another reading follows, and afterwards the responsory “Lord, hear,” with its five verses. Then [Col. 0081B] the deacon proclaims, (256) “The Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ according to Luke.” When it has been read, the Mass is completed in its proper order.

65 Over the Offerings.—Receive, we ask, Lord, the gift offered, and graciously bring it about that what we enact through the mystery of the passion of your Son, our Lord, we may attain through devoted effects. Through the same [Lord].

Preface.—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who, innocent, willed to suffer for the impious and to be unjustly condemned for criminals. His death wiped away our offenses, and his Resurrection bestowed justification upon us. Through him we humbly implore your mercy: cleanse us today from sins in such a way that tomorrow you may satisfy us with the food of the venerable supper; today accept the confession of our sins, and tomorrow grant us an increase of spiritual gifts; today receive the vows of our fasts, and tomorrow lead us into the banquet of the most sacred supper. Through whom.

Blessing.—May almighty God, who through the passion of his only-begotten Son has given you an example of humility, grant you through that same humility to receive the ineffable gift of his blessing. Amen. May you share in the Resurrection of him whose lessons of patience you venerate. Amen. May you receive from him the gift of eternal life, through whose temporal death you believe that you escape eternal death. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.
