[Col. 0081D] At the Completion.—(257) Grant to our minds, almighty God, that through the temporal death of your Son, which the venerable mysteries attest, we may trust that you have given us everlasting life. Through the same [Lord].

Over the People.—Look upon this household of yours, Lord, we ask, for which our Lord Jesus Christ did not hesitate to be handed over to the hands of sinners and to undergo the torment of the cross. He who lives with you.

[Note: [Col. 0082D] Here the Codex varies. In the Roman Calendar it reads: “At the Lateran the chrism is prepared.” In Pamelius: “At Saint John in the Lateran.” In the first Theoderic, the station is at Saint Peter.]

THURSDAY.

At the third hour they enter the sacristy, put on [Col. 0082A] dalmatics, both the pontiff and all the deacons—or all the vestments—while the pontiff sits in his chair; and two flasks of oil are prepared. The better one is brought to the pontiff, so that, after receiving the balsam and mixing it with the oil, he may fill it with his own hand. The ministers retain the other one, full. Then the pontiff, having washed his hands, proceeds with seven [candle] bearers to the Mass. After the Introit antiphon has been said, he says, “Glory to God in the highest.” When this is finished, he says, “Peace be with you,” and gives this prayer. Everything else is done as in another solemn Mass.

God, from whom Judas received the punishment of his guilt and the Thief the reward of his confession, grant us the effect of your favor, so that, just as Jesus Christ our Lord in his passion allotted different rewards according to their merits to each of the two, so he may grant us the grace of his Resurrection once the error of the old condition has been removed.

Then the Epistle is read, and the Responsory follows, then the Gradual and Tract, and afterward the Gospel. When it has been read, the Mass is carried out in its proper order.

Over the Offerings.—May Jesus Christ our Lord himself, holy Lord, almighty Father, God, who showed his disciples through today’s tradition that this should be done in remembrance of him, make our sacrifice acceptable to you, we ask.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: for on this night, amid the sacred banquet, the conscience of the betrayer could not bear him reproving it; but, abandoning the company of the apostles, he accepted from the Jews the price of blood, so that he might lose the life which he had sold. Thus today the betrayer dined upon his own death, and with bloody hands received from the hand of the Savior the bread which he was about to leave, so that a greater punishment might constrain him, stuffed with food—him whom not even the sharing of the consecrated food could recall from his crime. Therefore our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, suffers to share his final banquet with an enemy whom he knew would immediately betray him, so that he might leave the world an example of innocence and complete his Passion for the redemption of the world. The gentle God suffers an unfeeling Judas, and the merciful one endures a cruel fellow-guest who deserved to perish by his own noose, because he had plotted against the Master’s blood. O Lord patient in all things! [Col. 0082D] O Lamb gentle amid his own banquet! Judas carried his food in his mouth and summoned the persecutors to whom he would hand him over. But your Son, our Lord, like a merciful Victim, both patiently permitted himself to be sacrificed to you for us and forgave the sin which the world had committed. We therefore ask that he who permitted himself to be handed over for our salvation may himself enrich us with the gift of his grace; and that he who exposed his betrayer through a morsel of bread may himself make us cling to him through the reception of his bread; and that he who deigned to wash the feet of his disciples today [Col. 0083A] may himself cleanse us from all offenses and join us to the assembly of the faithful disciples. Through him whose Majesty, etc.

Therefore, most merciful Father, etc.

**Communicantes**, and celebrating the most sacred day on which our Lord Jesus Christ was handed over for us; and also commemorating.

**Hanc igitur.**—Therefore, O Lord, we ask that, being appeased, you may regard this offering of our service and of your entire household, which we offer to you for the day on which our Lord Jesus Christ handed over to his disciples the mysteries of his body and blood to be celebrated.

Who, on the day before he was to suffer for the salvation of us all—that is, today—took bread into his holy and venerable hands.

[Col. 0083B] (269) Then the oil is offered to the bishop, and both he himself and all the presbyters bless it for anointing the sick, in these words:

[Note: [Col. 0083D] In Pamel. Ed. this is preceded by: “Blessing of the oil.” But “for the sick” should be added from Cod. Reg. Suec. In the same Blessing, “send forth,” etc., is lacking in Pamelius; so too “through whom you create all these things, O Lord,” etc., which is found in Cod. Reg. Suec.] Send forth, O Lord, your Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, from heaven upon this richness of the olive, which you deigned to produce from green wood for the refreshment of the body, so that by your holy blessing this ointment may be a protection of mind and body to everyone who touches it, for removing all pains, all infirmities, and every bodily sickness. From it you anointed priests, kings, prophets, and martyrs: your perfect chrism, O Lord, blessed by you in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Through him you always create all these things, O Lord, which are good; +you sanctify them, +make them alive, +bless them, and bestow them upon us. Through him, and with him, [Col. 0083C] and in him, to you, God the almighty Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, is all honor and glory.

For ever and ever. Amen.

Let us pray. Instructed by saving precepts and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name, etc.

But deliver us from evil.

Deliver us, we ask, O Lord, from all evils, past, present, and future; and, through the intercession of the blessed and glorious Mary, ever Virgin and Mother of God, and of your blessed apostles Peter and Paul and Andrew, and of all the saints, graciously grant peace in our days, so that, aided by the help of your mercy, we may always be free from sin and secure from every disturbance. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0083D] **Blessing.**—May God bless you, who through the Passion of his only-begotten Son willed that the old Passover should be changed into the new; and may he grant you that, once the contagion of the old leaven has been purged away, a new dough may continually remain in you. Amen. And because you have gathered with devoted minds to celebrate the Supper of the Redeemer, may you carry away with you a banquet of eternal foods. Amen. May you also, with his merciful aid, be cleansed from the filth of sins—he who, to set forth an example of humility, willed to wash the feet of his disciples. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom and dominion [Col. 0084A] remain without end for ever and ever. Amen. May the blessing of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and the peace of the Lord, be always with you. And with your spirit.

Then the bishop alone receives Communion, and the deacon offers him the chalice, on that day alone. After he has received Communion, he places the chalice upon the altar; then, having received the paten from the subdeacon, he places it beside the chalice on the left side. Immediately two deacons cover both vessels with a clean linen cloth, which they had previously prepared at the edge on the other side, spread out opposite the bishop behind the corporal. At once two acolytes hold the wrapped ampullae, with a white silk linen cloth, so that they can be seen from the middle, on their left arms; the cloths are thrown over the left shoulder so that they reach the right shoulder, in order that the hanging ends may be held. From these men, standing beneath the shoulder [Col. 0084B], the subdeacon comes and takes the mixed ampulla together with the cloth, gives it to the archdeacon, and he carries it before the bishop’s seat. Then the bishop, standing at his seat and (271) looking toward the east, while the archdeacon holds the ampulla before him on his left arm, its cloth wrapped around it as described above, breathes upon the ampulla and begins the consecration of the chrism in a loud voice:

The Lord be with you. And with your spirit. Lift up your hearts. We have them with the Lord. Let us give thanks to the Lord our God. It is worthy and just.

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; for in the beginning, among the other gifts of your goodness and mercy, you commanded the earth to produce fruit-bearing trees, among which olive trees were to grow as ministers of this most rich liquid, whose fruit would serve the sacred chrism. For David also, foreseeing the mysteries of your grace by the prophetic spirit, sang that our faces would be made joyful with oil. And when the crimes of the world were once being cleansed by the outpoured flood, the dove, showing the likeness of the gift to come, announced through an olive branch that peace had been restored to the earth. This was made manifest through visible effects in the last times, when, as the waters of baptism erase the offenses of all crimes, this anointing with oil makes our faces joyful and serene. For this reason also you gave a command to your servant Moses, that he should appoint his brother Aaron as priest, after first washing him with water, through the pouring on of this ointment. [Col. 0084D] A still greater honor was added when your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, required John to wash him in the waters of the Jordan, so that, after the Holy Spirit had been sent down from above in the likeness of a dove, you might show by the testimony of the following voice your only-begotten Son, in whom you were supremely well pleased, and most clearly prove that this was the one whom the prophet David had sung as to be anointed with the oil of gladness above his companions. Therefore we beseech you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through that same Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, that you would deign to sanctify by your blessing the richness of this creature [Col. 0085A], and mingle with it the power of the Holy Spirit, with the might of your Christ cooperating—from whose holy name the chrism has received its name; (274) from it you anointed priests, (275) kings, (276) prophets, and (277) martyrs—so that, for those being renewed by the baptism of the spiritual bath, you may confirm this creature of chrism as a sacrament of perfect salvation and life; so that, when the sanctification of anointing has been poured in and the corruption of the first birth has been swallowed up, the holy temple of each person, acceptable in life, may give forth the fragrance of innocence; so that, according to the sacrament of your ordinance, those who have been infused with royal, priestly, and prophetic honor may be clothed in the garment of incorruptible grace; so that for those born again of water and the Holy Spirit the chrism may be the chrism of salvation, and you may make them partakers of eternal life and companions of heavenly glory [Col. 0085B]. Through the same Lord [Note: [Col. 0085D] After this Blessing, Pamel. adds an exorcism of the oil: “O God, who by the power of the Holy Spirit,” etc.].

(278) When this has been completed, he blesses the ampulla in the order described above; likewise he breathes upon it, but blesses it silently.

The Lord be with you. And with your spirit.

Let us pray.—O God of spiritual growth and progress, who by the power of your Holy Spirit strengthen the beginnings of weak minds, we beseech you, O Lord, that by the anointing of this creature you grant those coming to the bath of blessed regeneration cleansing of mind and body, so that, if any stains of hostile spirits have clung to them, they may depart at the touch of this sanctified oil. Let there be no place here for spiritual wickedness, no opportunity for rebellious powers, no license left for evils lying in wait to hide [Col. 0085C] themselves; but, for your servants coming to the faith and to be cleansed by the working of your Holy Spirit, may the preparation of this anointing be useful for salvation, which they are also to obtain in the sacrament of baptism through the birth of heavenly regeneration. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire.

The ampulla containing the chrism, immediately after it has been blessed, is covered so that no one may see it; but while an acolyte holds it, everyone venerates it in order. For the bishop and all the deacons venerate it uncovered. When this has been completed, after washing his hands, the bishop goes before the altar, and (281) all the people receive Communion in their order; and they preserve some of the sacrifice itself for the following day, from which they may receive Communion.

[Col. 0085D] **For the Completion.**—Refreshed with life-giving nourishment, we ask, O Lord our God, that what we carry out in the time of our mortality we may obtain through the gift of your immortality. Through our Lord [Note: [Col. 0085D] In the Vatican Edition, or that of Angelus Rocca, there follows: “Likewise, a prayer for reconciling a penitent,” together with four other Prayers on the same subject. These are followed, for the Mass, by three Prayers: “over the offerings” and “for the completion.”]

(283) **FRIDAY** [Note: [Col. 0085D] In Pamelius, only “in Jerusalem” is read for the station. [Col. 0086D] In the Roman Calendar: “At Suxxurio, which is in the basilica of Jerusalem.”]

(284) At the third hour all the presbyters, both of the city and from the suburbs, and all the clergy with the people, gather in the appointed church within the City, though not in the [Col. 0086A] principal church, and await the bishop or whoever acts in his place. When he comes from the sacristy and has proceeded before the altar to pray in the order contained in the Sacramentary, as soon as he has risen, he silently ascends to the seat. When he is seated, the subdeacon immediately ascends to read. After this the song *Domine, audivi* is sung; then another reading follows, after which comes the Tract *Deus laudem meam*. When it is finished, the Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ according to John is read. When this has been completed, the bishop comes before the altar and says: “Let us pray, dearest ones, for the holy Church of God,” etc. (287) As on [Note: [Col. 0086D] In the Prayer for the emperor and the empire, which occurs fourth in the series of the other prayers, Cod. Reg. Suec. reads: “Look kindly upon the Christian emperor”; the first Theoderic: “For the most Christian [emperor].” Pamelius, supported by the second Theoderic, has: “For the Roman [emperor].”] Wednesday. When he has finished these, two deacons immediately strip the altar of the linen cloth which had previously been placed beneath the Gospel; they do all this silently and go out. The presbyters of the churches, whether from the city or the suburbs [Col. 0086B], go to their own churches, so that they may perform all these things in this order toward evening. They change only this: wherever the bishop mentions the Apostolic See, they name their own bishop.

At Vespers, both in the church where the bishop says the Prayers and in the other churches of the presbyters, after the Prayers a cross is prepared before the altar, with a space placed between it and the altar, supported on either side by two acolytes. When a prayer-stool has been placed before it, the bishop comes, venerates the cross, and kisses it. Then the bishops, presbyters, deacons, and the others in order, and then the people; the bishop returns to his seat until everyone has venerated it. The first two presbyters, immediately after they have venerated it, enter the sacristy—or wherever the Lord’s body, which remained from the previous day, has been placed—and put it on a paten [Col. 0086C]. The subdeacon holds before them a chalice with unconsecrated wine, and another holds the paten with the Lord’s body. While they are holding these, one presbyter takes the paten and another the chalice, and they carry them onto the stripped altar. The bishop remains seated while the people complete their veneration of the cross; for whenever the bishop or the people venerate the cross, the Antiphon *Ecce lignum crucis* is always sung. Psalm 118 is said. When the cross has been venerated and returned to its place, the bishop comes down before the altar and says:

Let us pray. Instructed by saving precepts and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name; thy kingdom come; thy will be done, as in heaven and on earth; give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors; and do not lead us into temptation. Response: But deliver us from evil.

Deliver us, we ask, O Lord, from all evils, past, present, and future; and, through the intercession of the blessed and glorious Mary, ever Virgin and Mother of God, and of your blessed apostles Peter and Paul and Andrew, and of all the saints, graciously grant peace in our days, so that, aided by the help of your mercy, we may always be free from sin and secure from every disturbance. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit. For ever and ever. Amen.

When they have said Amen, he takes a portion from the holy sacrament and places it in the chalice, saying nothing. And all receive Communion in silence, and everything is completed.

From Thursday evening, let the altars remain stripped until Saturday morning [Note: [Col. 0087D] At the end of the office of this day, Pamelius adds: “Order for making a catechumen,” which is not found, at least for the most part, in Cod. Reg. Suec.].

(298) [Note: [Col. 0087D] No station is mentioned for this day except in the Roman Calendar [Col. 0088D], where it reads: “On Holy Saturday, at the Lateran.”] **HOLY SATURDAY.**

At the eighth hour all, both clergy and people, come to the church. The clerics enter the sacristy and put on their vestments as customary. Then two candles are lit, held by two notaries, one at the right corner of the altar and the other at the left, and [Col. 0087B] the lector ascends the ambo and announces:

A reading from the Book of Genesis: “In the Beginning.” Likewise all those readings. Before “In the Beginning,” he does not say a Prayer. When the first reading is finished, he says this Prayer:

O God, who wondrously created humanity and more wondrously redeemed it, grant us to persevere by the reason of our minds against the allurements of sin, so that we may deserve to attain eternal joys. Through our Lord.

A reading from the Book of Genesis: “God tested Abraham.”

O God, who in the deed of your servant Abraham provided the human race with examples of obedience, grant us both to break the perversity of our will and to fulfill in all things the uprightness of your commands. Through.

71 A reading from the Book of Exodus: “The Lord said to Moses [Col. 0087C] and Aaron.”

O God, who by the Passion of your Christ, our Lord, dissolved the hereditary death of the old sin into which the entire race of posterity had entered, grant that, made conformed to him, just as by the necessity of nature we have borne the image of the earthly, so we may bear the image of the heavenly through the sanctification of grace, through Christ our Lord. Who lives with you.

A reading from the Book of Exodus: “It came to pass in the morning watch.”

Song: “Let us sing.”

O God, whose ancient miracles we perceive to shine even in the present age, grant, we ask, that just as you freed the former people from the Egyptians, so you may accomplish this for the salvation of the nations through the waters of baptism. Through.

[Col. 0087D] A reading from the prophet Isaiah: “This is the inheritance.”

O God, who continually enlarge your Church through the calling of the nations, graciously grant that those whom you wash with the water of baptism you may guard with continual protection. Through.

A reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Seven women shall take hold.”

Song: “Let us sing.”

O God, who instruct us to celebrate the paschal sacrament through the pages of both Testaments [Col. 0088A], grant us to understand your mercy, so that from our reception of present things our expectation of future things may be made firm. Through.

A reading from the prophet Jonah: “The word of the Lord came to pass.”

O God, who on this night above all pour forth the riches of your mercy, be reconciled to the entire order of priestly ministry, and sanctify every rank of our service through the perfect remission of sins, so that you may permit those who are about to minister your regenerating grace to be liable to no offense. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0088D] This reading, together with the following Prayer, is omitted in the Vatican Edition.] A reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord: On that day, the root of Jesse.”

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that as we celebrate the paschal feasts, set aflame by heavenly desires, we may thirst for the fountain of life. Through.

**Tract.**—As the deer longs for the springs.

**Another Prayer, on the same psalm.**—Almighty and eternal God, look graciously upon the devotion of the people being reborn, who, like a deer, seeks the fountain of your waters; and graciously grant that, through the mystery of baptism, the thirst of its faith may sanctify soul and body. Through our Lord.

When the readings have been completed, one of the ministers immediately comes carrying ampullae in his hands and stands at the right corner of the altar; he is to precede the bishop to the fonts. Then the schola goes down to the fonts to perform the litany, awaiting the bishop, ready. The second member of the schola holds a golden vessel in his left hand above the chasuble, from which the bishop is to pour chrism into the font. When instructed, they perform the sevenfold litany; and when they are already near its end, the bishop proceeds in full ceremonial splendor, supported by two deacons. Those two candle-bearers, which had previously been lit, always proceed before him until he has finished everything. As soon as he has come before the fonts, he blesses the fonts while standing, saying these words in the same voice as the other Prayers. The first Prayer begins with “The Lord be with you” and ends with “For ever and ever,” like the other Prayer at Mass.

The Lord be with you. Response: And with your spirit.

Let us pray.—Almighty and eternal God, be present to the mysteries of your great mercy; be present to the sacraments; and, for creating new peoples whom the baptismal font brings forth for you, send forth the spirit of adoption, so that what must be performed by the ministry of our humility may be fulfilled through the effect of your power [Col. 0088D]. Through the Lord.

The Consecration of the Font is sung like the Preface up to “And the Holy Spirit”; it does not begin with “It is truly worthy.” Then the following is sung.

O God, who wondrously bring about the effect of your sacraments through invisible power, and although we are unworthy to carry out such great mysteries, nevertheless, without abandoning the gifts of your grace, you incline the ears of your mercy even to our prayers. O God, whose Spirit was borne over the waters at the very beginning of the world, so that already then the nature of the waters might conceive the power of sanctification [Col. 0089A]. O God, who, washing away the crimes of the guilty world through the waters, marked the form of regeneration in the very outpouring of the Flood, so that through the mystery of one and the same element there might be both an end to vices and a beginning of virtues, look, O Lord, upon the face of your Church and multiply your regenerations within her. You make your city glad by the rushing abundance of your grace and open the baptismal font throughout the whole world for the renewal of the nations, so that by the command of your Majesty it may receive the grace of your only-begotten Son from the Holy Spirit.

+Here he divides the water with his hand in the form of a cross.

May he, who prepares this water for the regeneration of human beings, enrich it by the mysterious mingling of his light, so that, once sanctification has been conceived, a heavenly offspring may emerge, born anew from the immaculate womb of the divine font as a new creation [Col. 0089B]. And may grace, as one mother, give birth to all whom either sex in the body or age in time distinguishes, into one infancy. Therefore, at your command, O Lord, let every unclean spirit depart far from here; let all the wickedness of diabolical deceit stand far away. Let no mingling of hostile power have a place here; let it not fly around in ambush, steal in by hiding, or corrupt by infecting. May this holy and innocent creature be free from every attack of the assailant and cleansed by the departure of all wickedness; may it be a living fountain, regenerating water, a purifying wave, so that all who are to be washed in this saving bath may, through the Holy Spirit working in them, obtain the forgiveness of perfect purification.

[Col. 0089C] +Therefore I bless you, creature of water, +through the living God, +through the holy God who at the beginning of the world’s creation separated you by the Word from the dry land, whose Spirit was borne over you, who commanded you to flow from paradise and water the whole earth in four rivers; who made you drinkable in the desert, though bitter, by imparting sweetness, and brought you forth from the rock for the thirsty people. +I bless you also through Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, who at Cana of Galilee, by a wondrous sign and through his power, changed you into wine; who walked upon you with his feet and was baptized in you by John in the Jordan. He brought you forth together with his blood from his side and commanded his disciples that believers should be baptized in you, saying: Go, teach all nations, baptizing them [Col. 0089D] in the name of the +Father, and of the +Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

73 Here he changes his voice, as though reading a lesson:

As we observe these commands, may you, almighty God, in your mercy be present; in your goodness breathe upon us; bless these simple waters with your mouth, so that, besides the natural cleansing which they can provide for bodies being washed, they may also be effective for purifying minds.

(317) And the two aforesaid candles are placed inside the baptistery. Here he breathes three times upon the water.

Let the power of your Spirit, O Lord, descend into the fullness of this font, and make the whole substance of this water fruitful with the effect of regeneration. Here let the stain of all sins be erased; here let nature, created in your image and restored to the honor of its origin, be cleansed from every defilement of antiquity [Col. 0090A], so that every person entering this sacrament of regeneration may be born again into the new infancy of true innocence. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire.

Then, taking the golden vessel with chrism, he pours chrism into the font (319) in the form of a cross and spreads the water with his hand. Then infants are baptized, first the males and then the females. While the person by whom the infant is to be received holds the child, the bishop or priest asks as follows: What is your name? Response: N. The priest likewise asks: Do you believe in God the almighty Father, creator of heaven and earth? Response: I believe. He asks: And in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, born and having suffered? Response: I believe. He asks: Do you also believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy Catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the flesh, and eternal life? Response: I believe. He asks: Do you wish to be baptized? Response: I do. And he says: I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

When he has risen from the font, the person who receives him offers him to a presbyter, who makes the sign of the cross with chrism using his thumb on the crown of his head, saying:

Almighty God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has regenerated you from water and the Holy Spirit and has given you forgiveness of all sins, may he himself anoint you with the chrism of salvation unto eternal life. Response: Amen.

[Col. 0090C] They are baptized, and those who are to receive them are ready, with linens in their hands, and they take them from the presbyters who baptize them. The bishop, meanwhile, returns to the sacristy and waits until the infants have been clothed, so that he may confirm them. They are not forbidden to nurse before Holy Communion if this is necessary. Once clothed, they are arranged in order as written. The infants are held on the right arms; the older ones place one foot upon the foot of their godparent. Then, when instructed, the schola performs the litany *quinam* at the fonts [reading uncertain]. The bishop comes to the infants, while the archdeacon holds the chrism, his shoulders wrapped and his arms covered with linen cloth; and, raising his hand over the heads of all, he says:

Almighty and eternal God, who have deigned to regenerate these servants of yours from water and the Holy Spirit and have given them forgiveness of all sins, send upon them from heaven your sevenfold Holy Spirit, the Paraclete: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and fortitude, the Spirit of knowledge and piety. Fill them with the Spirit of your fear, and graciously mark them with the sign of the cross unto eternal life. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of that same Holy Spirit. Through.

When the deacons ask the names of each one, the bishop, having dipped his thumb in chrism, makes a cross on the forehead of one, and similarly on each of them individually. When this has been completed, those instructed begin the threefold litany in the church. [Col. 0091A] When they have said “Lamb of God,” the master of the schola says: “Ascend.” The church is illuminated, and the bishop proceeds from the sacristy with two candle-bearers as above; they stand as before, on the right and left sides of the altar. When the litany is complete, the bishop says: Glory to God in the highest. When this is finished, he says: Peace be with you. Response: And with your spirit. And he gives the Prayer:

O God, who illumine this most sacred night with the glory of the Lord’s Resurrection, preserve in the new offspring of your family the spirit of adoption which you have given, so that, renewed in body and mind, they may offer you pure service. Through that same Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit. Through.

Then the Apostle is read, and the Alleluia is sung.

[Col. 0091B] The bishop begins it first: “Give thanks to the Lord.” **Tract.**—“Praise the Lord, all nations.” The Gospel follows. They are not to sing the Offertory, the *Agnus Dei*, or the Communion.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, we ask, O Lord, both the offerings of your people and of those whom you have regenerated, so that, renewed by the confession of your name and by baptism, they may attain everlasting blessedness. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: to praise and proclaim you more gloriously at all times, but especially on this night, through Christ our Lord; for, breaking open the gates of the underworld, he took up the radiant standards of his victory and, having triumphed over the devil, rose victorious from the dead. And therefore with the angels.

Therefore, most merciful Father, etc.

**Communicantes**, and celebrating the most sacred night of the Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ according to the flesh. And also venerating the memory, first of all, of the glorious Mary, ever Virgin, Mother of the same God and our Lord Jesus Christ.

Therefore, O Lord, we ask that you graciously accept this offering of our service and of your entire household, which we offer also for those whom you have deigned to regenerate from water and the Holy Spirit, granting them forgiveness of all sins.

**Blessing.**—May God, who, producing new peoples from the inviolate womb of his Church, continually makes her fruitful with new offspring while her virginity remains intact, fill you with the gift of faith, hope, and charity, and pour into you the gifts of his blessing. Amen. And may he who willed to illumine this most sacred night by the Resurrection of our Redeemer make your minds, cleansed from the darkness of sins, shine with an abundance of virtues. Amen. May you strive to imitate the innocence of those who have just been reborn, and illumine the vessels of your minds by the example of these present lights, so that with lamps of good works you may enter, together with the wise virgins, the bridal chamber of that Bridegroom whose Resurrection you celebrate. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom.

**For the Completion.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, satisfied with the divine gift, we may be renewed both by the sacred mysteries and in our conduct. Through.

(340) **ON [Note: [Col. 0091D] In Pamelius: “Holy Easter Sunday.” “Of Easter” is omitted in Cod. Reg. Suec. In the Roman Calendar it reads: “On Easter, Holy Sunday.” In all witnesses the station is at Saint Mary Major at the manger. “Major” is absent from the Roman Calendar and is not found in the title of no. 21, in the Gospel read there on this day.] HOLY EASTER DAY.**

O God, who on this day, by your only-begotten Son, after conquering death, opened for us the way to eternity, further by your aid the desires which you inspire beforehand. Through the same.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, O Lord, we ask, the prayers of your people together with the offerings of sacrifices, so that, having been initiated into the paschal mysteries, they may, through your working, advance to bring us eternal healing. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: to proclaim you more gloriously at all times, but especially on this day, when Christ our Passover has been sacrificed. For he is the true Lamb who took away the sins of the world. He destroyed our death by dying and restored life by rising again. And therefore with the angels.

**Communicantes**, and celebrating the most sacred day, etc.

**Hanc igitur**, this offering of our service. And also of your entire household, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0091D] This Blessing is not found in the editions of Pamelius and Angelus Rocca. It is found in the Benedictional published by Lambecius and Gussan V.] **Blessing.**—May almighty God bless you, with the paschal solemnity intervening today, and in his mercy deign to defend you from every evil. Amen. And may he who restores you to eternal life in the resurrection of his only-begotten Son clothe you with the joys of immortality at his coming. Amen. And since, after the days of fasting or of the Lord’s Passion have been completed, you celebrate the joys of the paschal feast, may you, with rejoicing hearts and with his help, come to those feasts which are not annual but perpetual. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**For the Completion.**—Pour into us, O Lord, the Spirit of your charity, so that those whom you have satisfied with the paschal sacraments you may make united through your mercy. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0092D] In Pamelius’s edition this Prayer is preceded by: “At Saint John’s, at Vespers.” The following Prayer, “Grant . . . that we who have received grace,” is headed: “At Saint Andrew’s.”] **At Vespers.**—Grant, we ask, almighty [Col. 0092D] God, that as we celebrate the solemn rites of the Lord’s Resurrection, we may rise from the death of the soul through the renewal of your Spirit. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever.

**At the fonts.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that as we celebrate the solemn rites of the Lord’s Resurrection, we may deserve to receive the joy of our deliverance. Through the same.

**Another.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that as we have come to know the grace of the Lord’s Resurrection, we ourselves may rise from the death of the soul through the love of the Spirit. Through the same.

**Another.**—O God, who have bestowed upon us the paschal remedy, accompany your people with a heavenly gift, so that they may rejoice forever from that source from which they now rejoice for a time. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

[Note: [Col. 0093D] In the Roman Calendar and in Pamelius it reads: “At the Holy Fathers”; this agrees with the title of Homily 23, in the Gospel preached on this day. “In white garments” is absent from the Roman Calendar.] **MONDAY IN WHITE GARMENTS.**

O God, who have bestowed remedies upon the world through the paschal solemnity, accompany your people, we ask, with a heavenly gift, so that they may deserve both to attain perfect freedom [Col. 0093B] and to advance toward eternal life. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—As we present the paschal sacrifices, we ask, O Lord, that what we perform repeatedly in action we may comprehend in devotion. Through.

## Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and humbly entreat you to graciously grant your faithful this: that they may both receive the paschal sacraments and eagerly await what is to come, so that, remaining in the mysteries through which they have been reborn, they may be brought to new life by putting these things into practice. Through Christ.

Then, as at Easter.

[Note: [Col. 0093D] This is absent not only from the other Vulgate editions, Pamel(ius), the Vatican edition, and others, but also from the Benedictional already mentioned.]

**Blessing.**—May God, who accepted the injury of the cross for you, renew you in the joy of his Resurrection. [Col. 0093C] Amen. And may he who forgave the crime of the thief hanging with him on the cross (342) save you from every bond of sins. Amen. May he grant that you preserve the mystery of your redemption worthily in your conduct and enjoy more abundantly the reward of eternity. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May the holy partaking of the paschal sacrament, we beseech you, Lord, be fulfilled in us, and may it transfer us from earthly desires to a heavenly way of life. Through.

77 **At Vespers.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who are weighed down by the burden of our sins may, through these paschal feasts, be freed from all evils that threaten us. Through our Lord.

**At the font.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty [Col. 0093D] God, that we may also preserve in our way of life the paschal feasts that we reverently celebrate. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—O God, who freed your people from the servitude of the cunning enemy, mercifully regard their prayers and, by your power, overthrow those who oppose them. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0093D] The station of this feria is given in both the printed editions and the manuscripts as being at Saint Paul. It is lacking in the *albis* section of Cod. Reg. [Col. 0094D] Suec., here as well as in the following ferias.]

## Tuesday in White Week

[Col. 0094A]

O God, who continually multiply your Church by new offspring, grant your servants that by their manner of life they may hold fast the sacrament (343) they received through faith. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, Lord, the prayers of the faithful together with the offerings of the sacrifices, so that through these acts of devout worship we may pass over to heavenly glory. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. He, by the offering of his body and by removing the observances of carnal sacrifices, (344) offered himself to you as a sacred victim and, as the immaculate Lamb and supreme Priest, sacrificed himself for our salvation. Through him.

[Col. 0094B] Then, as at Easter.

**Blessing.**—May he who washed you with the water from his side and redeemed you by the outpouring of his blood himself confirm in you the grace of the Redemption you have received. Amen. May he through whom you were reborn from water and the Holy Spirit unite you to the heavenly kingdom. Amen. And may he who gave you the beginnings of holy faith also grant you perfection of conduct and fullness of charity. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the reception of the paschal sacrament may continually remain in our minds. (345) Through.

**At Vespers.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnities of the paschal festival may always live in your sanctification. Through.

[Col. 0094C] [Note: [Col. 0094D] In the edition of Angelo Rocca this prayer is not entitled “At the font,” as it is here and in Pamel(ius)’s edition, in agreement with the manuscripts.]

**At the font.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that through these paschal feasts, which we celebrate, we may always live devoted to your praise. Through.

78 **Another.**—O God, who see that your household is deprived of every human strength, guard it, as the paschal festival intervenes, by the protection of your arm. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0094D] For the station, Pamel(ius)’s edition adds: “At Saint Lawrence outside the walls.” The final two words are absent from the Roman Calendar, from the two Theoderic manuscripts, and from the title of homily 24 on the Gospel, delivered on this day.]

## Wednesday in White Week

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of the Lord’s Resurrection, mercifully grant that through the temporal festivals we celebrate we may deserve to arrive at eternal joys. Through the same.

**Over the offerings.**—We sacrifice these offerings, Lord, amid paschal joys, through which the Church is wondrously both born and nourished. (346) Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right [Col. 0094D] and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and earnestly implore your compassion with tireless prayers, so that we who celebrate the solemnities of the paschal festival may always live in your sanctification. Thus, through observance of the temporal festival, may we deserve to reach the continuation of eternal [Col. 0095A] joys. Through Christ our Lord.

Then, as at Easter.

[Note: [Col. 0095D] The Benedictional mentioned above does not include this blessing.]

**Blessing.**—May the Lord our God lead you to the tree of life—he who rescued you from the pit of misery. Amen. May he himself open for you the gate of paradise—he who shattered the gates of hell. Amen. May he himself rescue you from the scourge and lead confessing people into his kingdom—he who, though innocent, deigned to suffer for the ungodly. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Having cleansed us from all oldness, Lord, may the venerable reception of your sacrament transfer us into a new creation. Through our Lord.

**At Vespers.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty [Col. 0095B] God, that the wondrous sacrament of this paschal festival may grant us both temporal tranquility and eternal life. Through.

**At the font.**—O God, who gladden us through the paschal feasts, mercifully grant that, with your help, we may faithfully hold fast what we devoutly celebrate. Through.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the desire of Christian devotion may tend toward that place where our substance is with you. Through the same.

[Note: [Col. 0095D] By unanimous agreement among our books, both printed and handwritten, the station is assigned to the Apostles.]

## Thursday in White Week

O God, who united the diversity of nations in the confession of your name, 79 grant that for those reborn in the baptismal font there may be one faith of mind and one devotion in action. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Mercifully receive, we beseech you, Lord, the gifts of your peoples, so that, renewed by confession of your name [Col. 0095C] and by baptism, they may attain everlasting blessedness. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for through the paschal mystery he taught us to leave behind the oldness of life and walk in newness of spirit. Through him the bitterness of perpetual death is overcome, and the wholeness of eternal life is granted to the faithful. Through him your Majesty.

Then, as at Easter.

[Note: [Col. 0095D] Not even the Benedictional mentions this blessing.]

**Blessing.**—May you be filled with the blessings of almighty God and of our Lord, by whose precious blood you have been redeemed. Amen. May his unfailing grace fill you, whose ineffable power fashioned you, (347) and may he who granted you the condition of being born in this world himself grant you a dwelling in the eternal kingdom, where you may live without end. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Hear our prayers, Lord, so that the holy exchange of our redemption may both provide us with help for the present life and secure everlasting joys for us. Through.

[Col. 0096A] **At Vespers.**—O God, through whom you have granted us freer minds for celebrating the paschal sacrament, teach us both to fear what angers you (348) and to love what you command. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0095D] “At the font” is omitted in the Vatican edition and in Gussanville.]

**At the font.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that your Church may rejoice both in the steadfastness of its members and in ever-new fruitfulness. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Multiply, we beseech you, Lord, the faith of your people, so that what began through you may also attain increase through you. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0095D] For the station, the Roman Calendar, in Cod. [Col. 0096D] Pamel(ius), and elsewhere, reads: “At Saint Mary’s at the Martyrs.”]

## Friday in White Week

Almighty and eternal God, who bestowed the paschal sacrament in the covenant of human reconciliation, grant to our minds that we may imitate in action what we celebrate in profession. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Graciously accept, we beseech you, Lord, these victims, which we offer both for the expiation of those reborn and for the hastening of heavenly help. Through.

80 ## Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who, according to the unchangeable truth of his promise, having become the heavenly Pontiff forever, (349) alone among all priests had no need of the remission of sin, but rather, as the true Lamb, himself took away the sin of the world. (350) Through him.

Then, as at Easter.

[Note: [Col. 0096D] This is found in none of our books.]

**Blessing.**—May almighty [Col. 0096C] God bless you from heaven, he who deigned to redeem you on earth through the cross and the blood of his Passion. Amen. May he himself renew you from the oldness of sin, he who deigned to be crucified for you, and may he raise you to heavenly things, he who for you entered the underworld. Amen. May the Lord grant you his life, he who accepted and destroyed your death. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Look upon your people, Lord, and graciously absolve from temporal faults those whom you have deigned to renew through eternal mysteries. Through our Lord.

**At Vespers.**—O God, through whom both redemption has come to us and adoption has been granted, look upon the works of your mercy, so that to those reborn in Christ both an eternal inheritance and true freedom may be granted. Through the same.

**At the font.**—Be present, we beseech you, Lord, with your household, and graciously grant that to those to whom you have bestowed the grace of faith you may also grant an eternal crown. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0096D] For the station, Pamel(ius)’s edition reads: “At Saint John in the Lateran.” “In the Lateran” is absent from Cod. Reg. Suec. and from both Theoderic manuscripts. The Roman Calendar has only “at the Lateran.” In the title of homily 26 on the Gospel, “When evening had come, etc.,” which is read today according to the Roman Calendar, it is likewise stated that it was delivered in the basilica of Saint John called Constantiniana.]

## Saturday in White Week

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who have reverently celebrated the paschal feasts [Col. 0097A] may through them deserve to attain eternal joys. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that through these paschal mysteries we may always rejoice, so that the continual work of our renewal may become for us a perpetual cause of gladness. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: through whom we humbly ask that we may be able to grasp the manifest gifts of him whose pledge we have received. And may we deserve to attain, through his Resurrection, the ineffable mystery that the paschal sacrament faithfully bestowed on us to hope for. Through him.

Then, as at Easter.

[Col. 0097B] **Blessing.**

81 ## At the Conclusion

Strengthened by the gift of our redemption, we beseech you, Lord, that true faith may always perfect this aid of perpetual salvation. (351)

**At Vespers.**—O God, creator of every creature, graciously cause your servants, whom you renewed in the baptismal font and strengthened with the fullness of your grace, to be enrolled among those adopted as sons. Through our Lord.

**At the font.**—O God, who multiply your Church through the offspring of those reborn, mercifully make it rejoice in the progress of its children. Through our Lord.

## (352) Sunday of the Octave of Easter

[Note: [Col. 0097D] Pamel(ius) alone adds: “At Saint Pancratius.” No station is assigned in the Roman Calendar. The second Theoderic manuscript has: “At Saints Cosmas and Damian,” which is also prefixed in Cod. Reg. Suec. to the prayer at Vespers for this Sunday.]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who have completed the paschal feasts may, by your gift, preserve them in conduct and life. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, we beseech you, Lord, the gifts of the rejoicing Church, and grant perpetual fruitfulness of joy to her to whom you have given the cause of such great gladness.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and humbly beseech you not to allow us to return to that state over which the enemy rightly rules, but rather to make us persist in this absolution through which the devil was made captive when your Son conquered him. And therefore, with the angels.

[Note: [Col. 0097D] This blessing occurs nowhere among our sources except in the Codex of Grimoldus, published by Pamel(ius) in *Liturgica*, volume II; there, however, instead of “And he who from their breasts,” it reads: “So that he who from their breasts,” etc.]

**Blessing.**—May God, whose Only-Begotten Son deigned to appear to his disciples when the doors were closed, graciously enrich you with the gift of his blessing and open for you the gates of the heavenly kingdom. Amen. And may he who by the touch of his body removed the wound of doubt from their hearts grant that, through the faith by which you believe that he rose again, you may be free from every stain of sin. Amen. And since, with Thomas, you believe that he is God and Lord and invoke him with bowed voices, may you be able to be guarded by him from every evil in this age and to be enrolled among the assemblies of the saints in the age to come. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—We beseech you, Lord our God, that you may make the holy mysteries, which you have bestowed for the protection of our renewal, both a present remedy and a future one for us. Through.

**Another.**—O God, who have made us celebrate the paschal feasts on this day, grant, we beseech you, that we may rejoice in the heavenly kingdom. Through.

**At Vespers.**—O God, who have granted us to celebrate your Passover with exultant hearts, 82 grant, we beseech you, that we may rejoice both in the supports of the present age and in the desires of eternity. Through our Lord.

## (353) Other Paschal Prayers

[Note: [Col. 0098D] Pamel(ius) assigns many more Paschal Prayers, and most of them differ from ours.]

O God, who renewed believers in you through the baptismal font, [Col. 0098B] grant this protection to those reborn in Christ, so that they may not lose the grace of your blessing through any assault of error. Through the same.

**Another.**—O God, who restore us to eternal life in the Resurrection of Christ, raise us up to the author of our salvation who is seated at your right hand, so that Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, who came to be judged because of us, may come to judge for us. He lives and reigns with you.

**Another.**—O God, both restorer and lover of innocence, direct the hearts of your servants toward yourself, so that, freed from the darkness of unbelief, they may never depart from the light of your truth. Through the Lord.

**Another.**—O God, who multiply peoples believing in you by the abundance of your grace, mercifully look upon your [Col. 0098C] chosen people, so that those reborn through the sacrament of baptism may deserve to enter the heavenly kingdom. Through.

**Another.**—Almighty and eternal God, who restore human nature to a dignity surpassing that of its first origin, look upon the ineffable mystery of your compassion, and preserve within those whom you have deigned to renew through the mystery of regeneration your gifts by the protection of perpetual grace. Through.

**Another.**—Almighty and eternal God, lead us into fellowship with heavenly joys, so that you may cause those reborn through the Holy Spirit to enter your kingdom, and so that the humility of the flock may reach the place where the exalted Shepherd has gone before. He lives with you.

**Another.**—O God, who made the paschal sacrifice for the salvation of the world, be favorable to our supplications; and may the supreme Pontiff, (354) interceding for us, [Col. 0098D] reconcile us by that in which he is like us and absolve us by that in which he is equal to you—Jesus Christ, your Son.

**Another.**—Grant us, almighty and merciful God, to receive truly a share in the Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ. He lives with you.

**Another.**—O God, who restore us to eternal life in the Resurrection of Christ, [Col. 0099A] fulfill the ineffable mystery of your compassion, so that, when our Savior comes in his Majesty, you may clothe with blessed immortality those whom you caused to be regenerated through baptism. Through the same.

83 **Another.**—O God, creator and Redeemer of the human race, grant, we beseech you, that, with you continually inspiring us, we may follow the aids bestowed for our renewal. Through.

**Another.**—O God, who open the entrance of the heavenly kingdom to those reborn from water and the Holy Spirit, increase upon your servants the grace you have given, so that those cleansed from all sins may be deprived of none of the promises. Through.

**Another.**—Preserve your mercy in us, we beseech you, Lord, so that you may cause those whom you freed from the darkness of error to adhere more firmly to the teaching of your truth. [Col. 0099B] Through the Lord.

**Another.**—Guard us with your customary compassion, we beseech you, Lord, so that those redeemed by the Passion of your Only-Begotten Son may rejoice in his Resurrection. Through the same.

**Another.**—Almighty and eternal God, may we obtain your mercy more abundantly on these days, on which, by your gift, we have come to know it more fully. Through.

## 18 Kalends of May—Birthday of Saints Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus

[Note: [Col. 0099D] “Maximus” is absent from Cod. Reg. Suec. The Roman Calendar reads “Maximianus.” John Fronto observes in the Roman Calendar that the name Maximus is also omitted in the Antiphonary.]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnities of your saints Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus may also imitate their virtues. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—May this victim, Lord, which we offer as we commemorate the birthdays of your saints, both release the bonds of our wickedness and obtain for us the gifts of your mercy. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and praise you at the festival of your holy martyrs, for you are always wondrous in the commemoration of your saints; you bestow the disposition of great faith, grant endurance in sufferings, and cause the schemes of the ancient enemy to be overcome, so that your outstanding martyrs may encounter no restraint of enticements preventing them from attaining the blessedness of heavenly rewards. Through Christ.

**At the Conclusion.**—Having been nourished by a heavenly gift, we beseech you, Lord our God, that the blessed intercession of your martyrs may sanctify these gifts for us. (355) [Col. 0099D] Through.

## 84 9 Kalends of May—Birthday of Saint George the Martyr

[Note: [Col. 0099D] “Martyr” is absent from the Roman Calendar. In Cod. Reg. Suec., after “the birthday of Saint George,” one also reads “and of Saint Regulus, bishop.”]

O God, who gladden us through the merits and intercession of your blessed martyr George, mercifully grant that we who [Col. 0100A] ask for his benefits may obtain the gifts of your grace. (356) Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Sanctify, Lord, the gifts offered, and, through the intercession of your blessed martyr George, cleanse us through them from the stains of our sins. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: for the venerable confession of whose name blessed George the martyr endured various torments, and, conquering them, earned the crown of perpetual life. Through him your Majesty.

**At the Conclusion.**—Appeased by the support of your blessed martyr George, Lord, defend us through the power of your sacrament [Col. 0100B] that we have received. Through.

## 7 Kalends of May—Birthday of Saint Mark the Evangelist

[Note: [Col. 0099D] In the Roman Calendar and in Pamel(ius)’s edition, with the Regius manuscripts of Sweden, the two Theoderic manuscripts, and Gemetensis in agreement, this is entitled “The Greater Litany,” with no mention of Saint Mark, except in Pamel(ius), where “Office of Saint Mark” is placed in parentheses, indicating that it is absent from the ancient manuscripts.]

O God, who exalted your blessed evangelist Mark by the grace of evangelical preaching, grant, we beseech you, that we may always advance through his teaching and be defended by his prayer. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—As we bring gifts to you at the solemnity of your blessed evangelist Mark, we beseech you, Lord, that just as evangelical preaching made him glorious, so his intercession may make us acceptable to you in word and deed. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through [Col. 0100C] Christ our Lord: by whose grace blessed Mark was chosen for the priesthood, instructed by teaching for preaching, and strengthened by power to persevere, so that through the priestly insignia (358) he might attain the palm of martyrdom. Teaching his subjects, instructing them by the example of his life, and strengthening them by enduring, he reached you to receive his crown, having fearlessly overcome the threats of his persecutors. May his intercession, we beseech you, cleanse us from our sins—he who pleased you by so many prerogatives of gifts. Through him your Majesty.

[Note: [Col. 0100D] That is, “Require the Blessing.”]

**B. R.**

85 **At the Conclusion.**—May your holy gifts, we beseech you, Lord, grant us continual protection, so that through the prayers of your blessed evangelist Mark it may always guard us from every adversity. Through.

## 4 Kalends of May—Birthday of Saint (359) Vitalis the Martyr

[Note: [Col. 0100D] “Martyr” is absent from Pamel(ius)’s edition and from the Roman Calendar.]

[Col. 0100D]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Vitalis, we may be freed in body from every adversity and cleansed in mind from evil thoughts. [Note: [Col. 0100D] Pamel(ius), against Cod. Reg. Suec. and other manuscripts, reads “freed in mind.”] Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—May our devotion, [Col. 0101A] Lord, be acceptable in your sight, and may it become saving for us through the prayer of him for whose solemnity it is offered. Through.

**At the Conclusion.**—May your people rejoice, Lord, in the commemoration of your saint Vitalis, and may those who rejoice in his votive service be raised up by the support they desire. Through.

## Kalends of May—Birthday of the Holy Apostles Philip and James

[Note: [Col. 0101D] In the Vatican edition and in Gussanville, the vigil of those holy apostles is celebrated on the preceding day.]

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your apostles Philip and James, grant, we beseech you, that we may be instructed by the examples of those whose merits make us rejoice. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Mercifully receive, Lord, the gifts that we offer for the solemnity of your apostles Philip and James, and avert all the evils that we deserve. Through.

[Col. 0101B] **Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you established your Church upon apostolic solidity, and blessed Philip and James belong to their company; today we venerate the feasts of their Passion, asking that just as we are instructed by their teachings, so we may be protected by their examples and assisted by their prayers. Through Christ our Lord.

(360) **B. R.**

**At the Conclusion.**—Filled, we beseech you, Lord, with saving mysteries, may we be helped by the prayers of those whose mysteries we celebrate. Through the Lord.

**Over the people.**—May your people, Lord, continually rejoice in the honor of the blessed apostles Philip and James, and may they always be governed by these leaders, in whose teachings and merits they rejoice. Through.

## 86 5 Nones of May—Birthday of Saints (361) Alexander, Eventius, and Theodulus

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthdays of your saints Alexander, Eventius, and Theodulus may be freed from all evils that threaten us through their intercession. Through the Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—May abundant blessing descend upon these victims, Lord, and may it mercifully bring about our sanctification and gladden us through the solemnity of the martyrs. Through.

**At the Conclusion.**—Feed us everywhere, Lord, with the joys of your saints, for our salvation is increased whenever honor is bestowed upon those in whom you are proclaimed wondrous. Through.

## On the Same Day—(362) Finding of the Holy Cross

[Note: [Col. 0101D] This feast is entirely absent from the Roman Calendar and from the ancient codices. It is found, however, in the second Theoderic manuscript and in Pamel(ius)’s edition, although he admits that it is absent from his Cologne manuscript.]

O God, who, in the glorious finding of the life-giving cross, (363) revived the miracles of your Passion, grant that through the price of the life-giving wood we may obtain the aids of eternal life. You live and reign.

**Over the people.**—Look favorably, Lord, upon the sacrifice that we offer, so that it may strip us of every wickedness of wars and, through the standard of the holy cross of your Son, establish us in the security of your protection against the ambushes of hostile power. Through the same.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who (364) redeemed the world through the Passion of the cross and sweetened the bitterest taste of the ancient tree with the remedy of the cross. He conquered [Col. 0102A] by the trophy of the wood the death that had come through the forbidden tree, so that, by the wondrous dispensation of his mercy, we who through the taste of the tree had departed from the flower-bearing seat might through the wood of the cross return to the joys of paradise. Through him.

[Note: [Col. 0102D] It is found in the Benedictional under “At the festival of the Holy Cross.”]

**Blessing.**—May almighty God bless you, [Col. 0102B] who through the Passion and cross of his Only-Begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, redeemed the human race. Amen. And may he grant you, together with all the saints, (365) to comprehend with devoted mind the length, breadth, height, and depth of that same cross. Amen. So may you, denying yourselves and carrying the cross, follow our Redeemer through the course of this present life in such a way that after death you may deserve to be enrolled with him among the choirs of angels. Amen. May he grant this, and so forth.

87 ## At the Conclusion

Filled with heavenly nourishment and refreshed by the spiritual cup, we beseech you, almighty God, to defend from the wicked enemy those whom, through the wood of the holy cross of your Son, you commanded to triumph with the weapons of righteousness for the salvation of the world. You live with him.

[Col. 0102C] **Another.**—O God, who made all things by your word, we humbly beseech your ineffable mercy: for those whom you have deigned to redeem through the wood of the holy cross of your Son and his gracious blood, extinguish the deadly poisons of the serpent in all who believe in you, and through the grace of the Holy Spirit continually pour out the cup of salvation. Through the same.

## The Day before the Nones of May—Birthday (367) of Saint John before the Latin Gate

[Note: [Col. 0102D] This feast is omitted from the Roman Calendar. Its office is contained in Cod. Reg. Suec.]

O God, who see that our evils disturb us on every side, grant, we beseech you, that the glorious intercession of your blessed apostle John may protect us. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Having accepted our gifts and prayers, we beseech you, Lord, both cleanse us with heavenly mysteries and mercifully hear us. [Note: [Col. 0102D] The same codex reads “prayers that have been conceived.”] Through the Lord.

**At the Conclusion.**—Refreshed, Lord, by heavenly bread, may we, we beseech you, be nourished for eternal life. Through.

## 6 Ides of May—Birthday of Saints (368) Gordian and Epimachus

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnities of the blessed Gordian and Epimachus may be helped before you by their intercession. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Kindly accept, Lord, the offerings dedicated to you through the merits of the blessed martyrs Gordian and Epimachus, [Col. 0103A] and grant that they may become for us an everlasting aid. Through.

**At the Conclusion.**—We beseech you, almighty God, that we who have received heavenly nourishment may, through the intercession of your saints Gordian and Epimachus, be defended by it against every adversity. Through.

## 4 Ides of May—Birthday of Saint (369) Pancratius the Martyr

[Note: [Col. 0103D] In the Roman Calendar and in Pamel(ius)’s edition: “Birthday of Saints Nereus, Achilleus, and Pancratius.” Cod. Reg. Suec. mentions only Saint Pancratius. It should be observed that in the Roman Calendar the feast of Saints Nereus and Achilleus is noted first, followed by that of Saint Pancratius.]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday of your blessed martyr Pancratius may be freed from all evils that threaten us 88 through his intercession. Through the Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Sanctify, we beseech you, Lord, the gifts dedicated to you, and, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Pancratius, mercifully regard us through them.

[Col. 0103B] (370) **B. R.**

**Over the people.**—Appeased by the intercession of your blessed martyr Pancratius, Lord, grant, we beseech you, that what we celebrate in temporal action we may receive in perpetual salvation. (371) Through.

## 3 Ides of May—(372) Birthday of Saint Mary at the Martyrs

[Note: [Col. 0103D] In Pamel(ius)’s edition alone: “Dedication of the basilica of Saint Mary,” etc., against Cod. Reg. Suec. itself.]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, to reach the eternal joys of those whose virtue you grant us to celebrate annually with joy. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Upon these victims, we beseech you, Lord, may abundant blessing descend, which may mercifully bring about our sanctification and gladden us through the solemnity of the martyrs. Through.

**At the Conclusion.**—We humbly ask you, almighty God, that you graciously grant those whom you refresh with your sacraments also to serve you by conduct [Col. 0103C] pleasing to you. Through.

## 8 Kalends of June—(373) Birthday of Saint Urban, Pope

[Note: [Col. 0103D] Before this feast, Pamel(ius)’s edition reads: “The Ascension of the Lord, at Saint Peter.” It also has: “The Sunday after the Ascension.” Finally: “The feast of Saint Potentiana, virgin.” The Roman Calendar likewise gives this on 19 May, but under the name Saint Pudentiana.]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnities of your blessed martyr and pontiff Urban may be helped before you by his intercession. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—May this victim, Lord, cleanse our crimes, we beseech you, and, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Urban, (374) sanctify the bodies and minds of your subjects for the sacrifice that is to be celebrated.

**At the Conclusion.**—Appeased by the intercession of your blessed martyr and pontiff Urban, Lord, grant, we beseech you, that what we celebrate in temporal action we may receive in perpetual salvation. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0104D] This Sunday is omitted, together with the others, in Pamel(ius)’s edition.]

## 89 First Sunday after the Octave of Easter

[Col. 0103D]

O God, who raised up the fallen world through the humility of your Son, grant perpetual joy to your faithful, so that those whom you rescued from the dangers of perpetual death may be made to enjoy everlasting joys. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—May saving food and sacred drink make us serve your name worthily, we beseech you, Lord, so that the renewal of the human condition, which these mysteries contain, may continually be presented in our minds. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and humbly implore the immense compassion of your goodness, so that, considering the ignorance of our mortality, you may inspire us to ask for what is right and, in your mercy, grant us to obtain what we ask. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—[Note: [Col. 0104D] This blessing is assigned in Gregory’s Benedictional under “On the Resurrection,” after the blessing of the octave of Easter.]

May almighty God bless you, who created you by gratuitous mercy and, in the Resurrection of his Only-Begotten Son, granted you the hope of rising again. Amen. [Col. 0104B] May he raise you from the tombs of vices, who raised him from the dead. Amen. May he grant that you live happily with him without end, whom you truly believe to have risen from the dead. Amen. May he himself grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Graciously bestow upon us, we beseech you, Lord, the paschal remedies, so that, rejecting earthly desires, we may learn to love heavenly things. Through.

**Over the people.**—May your household, Lord, be perpetually surrounded by the help of your right hand, so that, as the paschal solemnity intervenes, it may be defended from every wickedness and accompanied by heavenly gifts. Through.

## Second Sunday after the Octave of Easter

O God, who show the light of your truth to those who have gone astray, so that they may be able to return to the way of justice, grant to all who are reckoned among Christians both to reject what is hostile to this name [Col. 0104C] and to pursue what is fitting for it. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—O God, who at the paschal solemnity mercifully work heavenly remedies for the world, accompany the gifts of this annual festival, so that temporal observance may benefit us unto eternal life. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you deigned to be born from a Virgin and, through your Passion and death, freed us from perpetual death, while through your Resurrection you bestowed eternal life upon us. Through him.

[Note: [Col. 0104D] It is read in the Benedictional after the preceding item.]

**Blessing.**—May God, who through the resurrection of his Only-Begotten Son has bestowed upon you both the good of Redemption and the dignity of adoption, grant you the rewards of his blessing. Amen. And as by his redeeming you received the gift of perpetual freedom, so, by his generosity, may you become sharers in the eternal inheritance. Amen. And may you deserve to be joined in the heavenly realm to him with whom you rose again through faith in baptism, by living well. Amen. May he himself grant this.

**At the Completion.**—We beseech you, almighty God, that we may no longer be held liable to the sentence of human condemnation, from whose bonds this Paschal redemption has released us.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who, renewed by the Paschal remedies, have escaped the likeness of our earthly ancestor may be transferred into the form of the heavenly Author. Who lives and reigns with you.

## THE THIRD SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

O God, who make the minds of the faithful one in will, grant your peoples to love what you command and to desire what you promise, so that amid worldly changes our hearts may be fixed where true joys are found. Through.

**Over the Offerings.**—May the grace of the Paschal sacrament, we beseech you, overflow in our minds, so that it may itself make us worthy of its gifts. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and to ask the mercy of your gift, so that we may treat with devout dedication the times during which, after his resurrection, our Lord Jesus Christ appeared bodily to his disciples, with his help, in such a way that we may remain free from all the stains of vice in them.

(377) **Blessing.**

**At the Completion.**—Grant, we beseech you, merciful God, that what we carry out according to the Paschal observances we may always experience as salutary. Through our Lord.

**Over the People.**—May the faithful people rejoice, O Lord; and, as they recall the beginnings of their own salvation, may they advance through its increase. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## THE FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

O God, from whom all good things proceed, grant your suppliants that, with you inspiring us, we may think what is right, and, with you governing us, may do the same. Through.

**Over the Offerings.**—We earnestly implore your clemency, O Lord, that we may receive with perpetual love the sacrament of the Paschal gift, which we recall in faith and eagerly desire in hope. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and earnestly implore your Majesty to keep our minds always fashioned for good works. For thus we shall be worshipers of the glorious gift with ready sincerity, if, continually advancing toward better things, we strive to possess the Paschal mystery forever. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**

**At the Completion.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, having received forgiveness of sins through the Paschal gift, we may thereafter avoid sins. Through our Lord.

## MONDAY

[Note: [Col. 0105D] In Pamele and in the Roman Calendar, a litany is not assigned here. The litany which Pamele presents for 25 April, where the Greater Litany is appointed, differs entirely from ours. The earlier Theoderic mentions the Greater Litany at this place and agrees for the most part with Pamele’s edition for 25 April.]

**In the Greater Litany.**—We beseech you, O Lord, through the intercession of blessed N., both to open the mind of your household by the gift of compunction and to hear it through the generosity of your mercy. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—O God, who strike the guilt of sinners by severely chastising them, do not refuse the tears of those who mourn, so that we who have come to know the burden of your displeasure may also experience the grace of your mercy. Through.

**Another.**—Spare, we beseech you, O Lord, spare your people, and no longer allow those whom you redeemed by the precious blood of your Son to be wearied by any adversities. Who lives and reigns with you.

**Another.**—O God, who strike our sins with merciful blows in order to cleanse us from our iniquities, grant us both to profit from your blow and quickly to rejoice in your consolation. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and, through the intercession of your blessed apostle Peter, mercifully protect those who hope in your mercy with heavenly aid. Through.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, crying out to you with our whole heart, through the intercession of your blessed apostle Peter, we may obtain the indulgence of your mercy. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0106D] After this prayer, in the edition of Angelo Rocca, or the Vatican edition, there follow four prayers prefaced by: “At the field.”]
