**At Mass.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who trust in your mercy amid our affliction may always be fortified against every adversity by your protection. Through our Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—While fasting, O Lord, we offer you the sacrifice of our repentance, beseeching you that, strengthened by its power, we may always hasten to the heavenly banquet. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and praise you as the author and sanctifier of the fast, through which you free us from the debts of our sins. Therefore receive the prayers of those who fast; and, so that in your favor you may rescue us from every evil, in your appeasement absolve our iniquities, by which we are deservedly afflicted. Through Christ.

[Note: [Col. 0106D] It exists in the Benedictional and is entitled “On Fasting.”]

**Blessing.**—May almighty God graciously regard your devotion and grant you the gifts of his blessing. Amen. May he forgive all the evils you have committed and grant the pardon you ask of him. Amen. May he receive the vows of your fasting and prayers in such a way that he turns away from you every adversity which you deserve as repayment for your sins, and pours into you the gift of the Spirit, the Comforter. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Completion.**—Pursue our vows, we beseech you, O Lord, with gracious favor, so that, while we receive your gifts in tribulation, we may grow in your love through our consolation. Through our Lord.

**Over the People.**—Extend your mercy to us, O Lord, so that what we seek in our vows we may obtain through a manner of life pleasing to you. Through.

## TUESDAY

Preserve your people, we beseech you, O Lord, and make them secure from all the adversities they deserve, so that, having received tranquility, they may serve you with devoted mind. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Look mercifully, we beseech you, upon the affliction of your household, so that, when forgiveness of sins has been granted, we may always glory in your benefits. Through.

**Another.**—Mercifully absolve us, we beseech you, from all sins, so that, having received forgiveness of sins, we may serve you with free minds. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Incline the ear of your mercy to our prayers, we beseech you, and, as knower of hidden things, graciously hear the prayers of your suppliants, so that, by your generosity, they may reach eternal life. Through.

**Another.**—We beseech you, almighty God, that we who are wearied by our offenses and afflicted by the merit of our iniquity may deserve to obtain the grace of your mercy. Through our Lord.

**At Mass.**

O God, who see that we cannot stand amid so many troubles, mercifully regard the groaning of the afflicted and avert all the evils we deserve. Through.

**Over the Offerings.**—Multiply, we beseech you, O Lord, the vows of those who offer, and illumine all with the instruments of true faith. Thus be mercifully present to us through this sacrifice, so that in your compassion you may absolve us both from sins and from every danger. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and humbly implore your Majesty that the inclination of your indulgence, not our wickedness, may always go before us, freeing us continually from harmful pleasures and graciously rescuing us from worldly disasters. Through Christ.

**At the Completion.**—Purify the hearts of your faithful, we beseech you, O Lord, so that, cleansed from earthly desire, they may be stripped of the dangers of the present life and strengthened by eternal gifts. Through.

## WEDNESDAY

Hear your people, wholly subject to you in mind, O Lord, so that, protected in body and mind, they may obtain by your grace what they devoutly believe. Through.

**Another.**—May heavenly propitiation increase the people subject to you, O Lord, and always make them serve your commands. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Have mercy now, we beseech you, O Lord, on your people, and gladden those laboring under continual tribulations by swift favor. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Help those who seek your mercy, O Lord, and grant pardon to those who confess; spare your suppliants, so that we who are scourged according to our merits may be saved by your compassion. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who have recognized the anger of your indignation may obtain the indulgence of your mercy. Through.

**At Mass.**—Give heed, we beseech you, O Lord, to our prayers, and let us, afflicted in tribulation and crying out, breathe again when heard, though by our failure to practice righteousness we deserve correction. Through.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty Father, that the intention of our mind may always attend to the place where the glorious author of today’s solemnity entered, and that our conduct may reach the destination toward which faith proceeds. Through the same Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—Mercifully regard, we beseech you, O Lord, the vows of your fasting suppliants; and, sanctifying these present gifts, through receiving them make us radiant by the hidden remedy of your mercy for our hearts, so that neither bodily works nor fleeting things may hold us, whom Christ the Lord, the institutor of fasting, has restored. Who lives and reigns with you.

**Another.**—We bring, O Lord, the sacrifice humbly offered for the venerable Ascension of your Son, which we now anticipate; grant, we beseech you, that through him we too may rise to heavenly things by these sacred exchanges. Through the same Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; for since it is your work whenever we think or do anything pleasing to you, grant us always the ability both to understand what is right and to carry it out. Through Christ our Lord.

**At the Completion.**—Grant, O Lord, we beseech you, that through these sacred things we have received, the inclination of our devotion may tend there where our substance is with you, who live and reign with you.

**Over the People.**—Be the protector of your household, we beseech you, O Lord, and grant mercy to those who ask it, so that they may always obey you and receive your gifts. Through.

## THE ASCENSION OF THE LORD

[Note: [Col. 0107D] In the Roman Calendar a vigil is assigned to this feast, and afterward one reads: “Thursday of the Ascension of the Lord.” There is no station there; but in Pamele’s edition one reads: “At Saint Peter’s,” which is absent from the Codex Regius of Sweden.]

**At Mass.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who believe that on this day you caused your Only-Begotten Son, our Redeemer, to ascend into heaven may ourselves also dwell in heavenly places in mind. Through the same Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—Receive, O Lord, the gifts we bring for the glorious Ascension of your Son, and mercifully grant that we may be freed from present dangers and reach eternal life. Through the same Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who, after his Resurrection, appeared manifest to all his disciples and, while they watched, was lifted up into heaven, so that he might grant us to be participants in his divinity. And with the angels.

Therefore, most merciful Father, etc.

Communicating, and celebrating the most sacred day on which your Only-Begotten Son, our Lord, placed the substance of our weakness, united to himself, at the right hand of your glory. But also commemorating, etc.

**Blessing.**—May God bless you, whose Only-Begotten Son on this day penetrated the heights of heaven and opened for you the way of ascent to where he is. Amen. May he mercifully grant that, just as he appeared manifest to his disciples after his Resurrection, so, coming for judgment, he may appear to you in favor. Amen. And may you who believe that he has taken his seat with the Father in his Majesty experience him remaining with you until the end of the age, according to his promise. Amen. May he himself grant this.

**At the Completion.**—Grant us, we beseech you, almighty and merciful God, that what we have received to be taken in visible mysteries we may obtain through invisible effect. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that through the gift of today’s feast the intention of your children may be directed there where our substance is with you in your Only-Begotten Son. Who lives and reigns with you.

**Another.**—Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, so that, just as we trust that the Savior of the human race has taken his seat with you in your Majesty, so we may experience Jesus Christ our Lord remaining with us until the consummation of the age, as he promised. Who lives and reigns with you.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the members of your faithful may follow where our head and origin, Jesus Christ our Lord, has gone before. Who lives and reigns with you as God.

**Another.**—O God, whose Son, ascending powerfully to the heights of heaven, led our captivity captive by his strength, grant, we beseech you, that Jesus Christ your Son may also bestow upon us the gifts he has conferred upon his participants.

## THE FIRST SUNDAY AFTER THE ASCENSION OF THE LORD

Almighty and eternal God, make us always to hold a will devoted to you and serve your Majesty with sincere heart. Through.

**Over the Offerings.**—May the unblemished sacrifices purify us, O Lord, and grant strength from heavenly grace to our minds. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who came to the aid of the human race by being born; through the death of his Passion conquered the world; through the glory of his Resurrection opened the way to eternal life; and through his Ascension granted us hope of ascending to heaven. Through him your Majesty.

[Note: [Col. 0109D] We find this blessing nowhere.]

**Blessing.**—May the Lord pour upon you the rain of his blessings and open to you the heavenly treasures of his charity. Amen. May the Lord make you participants in eternal life and coheirs of the heavenly kingdom. Amen. May the Holy Spirit find in you a worthy dwelling, so that his glorious Majesty may peacefully rest in your hearts. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Completion.**—Filled with sacred gifts, O Lord, we beseech you that we may always remain in thanksgiving. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—O God, life of the faithful, glory of the humble, and blessedness of the just, mercifully regard the prayers of your suppliants, so that the souls that thirst for your promises may always be filled from your abundance. Through our Lord.

## HERE BEGIN THE PRAYERS FOR PENTECOST

[Note: [Col. 0109D] In Pamele: “On Pentecost Saturday”; and in the Roman Calendar: “On Saturday, on the vigil of Pentecost.”]

**On Saturday before the descent into the font.**

Reading from the Book of Genesis: “Noah, when he was five hundred years old.”

O God, who continually increase your Church through the calling of the nations, mercifully grant that those whom you wash with baptismal water you may guard with continual protection. Through our Lord.

Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy: “Moses wrote.”

Canticle: “Give ear, O heaven.”

O God, who through the mouths of the prophets commanded us to leave temporal things and hasten toward eternal things, grant your servants that, through heavenly inspiration, we may be able to fulfill what we have recognized you have commanded. Through our Lord.

Reading from the Book of Leviticus: “When you have entered the land which I shall give you.”

O God, who have united the diversity of all nations in confession of your name, grant us both to will and to be able to do what you command, so that among the people called to eternity there may be one faith of minds and one devotion of actions. Through.

Reading from the prophet Isaiah: “Seven women shall take hold.”

Canticle: “The Vineyard.”

O God, unchangeable power and eternal light, mercifully regard the wondrous sacrament of the whole Church, and grant your servants that what we devoutly undertake we may also maintain through uprightness of life. Through our Lord.

Canticle from Psalm 41: “As the deer longs for the fountains.”

**After the Tract.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnity of the gift of the Holy Spirit, inflamed by heavenly desires, may thirst for the fountain of life. Through.

**Prayer at Mass after the ascent from the font.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the splendor of your brightness may shine upon us, and that the light of your light may strengthen the hearts of those reborn by your grace through the illumination of the Holy Spirit. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you as God in the unity of the same Holy Spirit.

**Over the Offerings.**—Mercifully regard the offerings of your people, we beseech you, O Lord, and, so that they may be acceptable when returned to you, may the salutary coming of the Holy Spirit cleanse our consciences. Through the Lord, etc., in unity.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: who, completing the Paschal sacrament, bestow through the Holy Spirit gifts of grace upon those to whom you granted, through fellowship with your Only-Begotten Son, to be adopted children; and now grant to the coheirs of the Redeemer the pledge of their heavenly inheritance, so that they may be the more certain that they will come to him, the more they know that they have been redeemed by him and enriched by the outpouring of the Holy Spirit. And therefore with the angels.

Therefore, etc.

Communicating, and anticipating the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit filled the apostles and the people of believers with the presence of his Majesty. Also venerating the memory, etc.

Therefore, this offering of our service, and of your whole household, which we offer to you also for those whom you have deigned to regenerate from water and the Holy Spirit, granting them remission of all sins, we beseech you, that, being appeased.

[Note: [Col. 0111D] It exists in the Vigil of Pentecost in Gregory’s Benedictional.]

**Blessing.**—May almighty God bless you, for whose Paraclete Spirit’s coming you prepare your minds by the observance of fasting and honor the present day with solemn praises. Amen. May you possess the innocence of newly born infants, so that, by his gift, you may be able to be a temple of the Holy Spirit. Amen. And may the same Holy Spirit make you worthy today of his dwelling in such a way that tomorrow he may pour himself into your minds, to dwell perpetually with you, and, when the course of this present life is completed, may lead you to heavenly gifts. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Completion.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, when the Holy Spirit comes, he may glorify the Majesty of your Son by manifesting him to us. Through the same. In the unity of the same.

**Another.**—O God, by whose Spirit the whole body of the Church is increased and governed, preserve in the new offspring of your household the grace of sanctification you have given, so that, renewed in body and mind and fervent in the unity of faith, they may deserve to serve you, the Lord. Through our Lord. In the unity of the same.

## THE HOLY DAY OF PENTECOST

O God, who on this day taught the hearts of the faithful through the illumination of the Holy Spirit, grant us in the same Spirit to have right understanding and always to rejoice in his consolation. Through. In the unity of the same.

**Over the Offerings.**—Sanctify the gifts offered, O Lord, we beseech you, and cleanse our hearts through the illumination of the Holy Spirit. Through. In the unity of the same.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who, ascending above all the heavens and sitting at your right hand, poured out on this day the promised Holy Spirit upon the children of adoption. Therefore the whole world throughout the earth exults with overflowing joys. And the heavenly powers and angelic authorities sing a hymn to your glory, saying without end.

Therefore, etc.

Communicating, and celebrating the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit appeared to the apostles in fiery tongues. Also venerating the memory.

Therefore, this offering of our service, and of your whole household, which we offer to you also for those whom you have deigned to regenerate from water and the Holy Spirit, granting them remission of all sins, we beseech you, that, being appeased.

[Note: [Col. 0111D] In the Benedictional it is assigned also for Pentecost.]

**Blessing.**—May God, who on this day deigned to illumine the minds of the disciples through the outpouring of the Spirit, the Comforter, make you filled with his blessing and overflowing with the gifts of the same Spirit. Amen. May that fire which appeared above the disciples cleanse the stains of your sins and illuminate your hearts through the outpouring of its light. Amen. And may he who deigned to unite the diversity of languages in confession of one faith make you persevere in the same faith and, through it, reach from hope to vision. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Completion.**—May the outpouring of the Holy Spirit cleanse our hearts, O Lord, and make them fruitful through the inward sprinkling of his dew. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Almighty and eternal God, who willed the Paschal sacrament to be contained in the mystery of fifty days, grant that the dispersion of the nations through the division of languages may be gathered by heavenly gift into one confession of your name. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—O God, who through the sacrament of today’s feast sanctify your Church in every people and nation, pour out the gifts of your Spirit over the whole breadth of the world. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0112D] In Pamele and in the Roman Calendar, “At the Chains” is read for the station. In both Theoderics: “At Saint Peter’s, at the Chains.”]

## MONDAY

O God, who gave your apostles the Holy Spirit, grant your faithful people the effect of their devout petition, so that those to whom you gave faith you may also grant peace. Through.

**Over the Offerings.**—Mercifully sanctify these gifts, O Lord, we beseech you, and, having received the offering of the spiritual Victim, make us ourselves an eternal gift to you. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who sent the promised Spirit, the Comforter, upon the disciples, so that at the beginning of the Church’s birth he might both instill knowledge of the Godhead in all nations and join the diversity of languages in confession of one faith. Through him we humbly implore your Majesty, that we may receive the effect of the manifold grace of him whose coming we celebrate. Through him your Majesty.

**At the Completion.**—Be present, O Lord, we beseech you, to your people, and defend from the fury of enemies those whom you have imbued with heavenly mysteries. Through.

**Another.**—O God, who deigned to send the Holy Spirit, the Comforter, to your disciples in the fervor of fire, grant your peoples to be fervent in the unity of faith, so that, remaining always in your love, they may be found steadfast in faith and effective in action. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0113D] In the same codices the station is at Saint Anastasia.]

## TUESDAY

May the power of the Holy Spirit be present with us, O Lord, we beseech you, both mercifully to cleanse our hearts and to protect us from every adversity. Through our Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—May the offering of the present gift purify us, we beseech you, O Lord, and make us worthy to participate in sacred things. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who filled the hearts of the faithful with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, so that by his marvelous working he might kindle in them the fire of his love and strengthen the nations in the unity of faith through the diversity of languages. By whose gift we ask that seductive pleasures be excluded from us and that spiritual virtues be built and planted in us. Through him your Majesty.

**At the Completion.**—May the Holy Spirit restore our minds through divine sacraments, O Lord, because he himself is the remission of all sins. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0113D] Pamele’s edition has for the station: “At Saint Mary Major and at Saint Peter’s.” The Roman Calendar has only: “At Saint Mary’s.” The two Theoderics add “Major.”]

## WEDNESDAY OF THE FOURTH MONTH

May the Comforter who proceeds from you illumine our minds, O Lord, and, as your Son promised, lead us into all truth. Who lives and reigns with you, in the unity of the same.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty and merciful God, that, when the Holy Spirit comes, he may graciously perfect us by dwelling in us as the temple of his glory. Through.

**Over the Offerings.**—Receive, we beseech you, O Lord, the gift offered, and graciously work so that what we perform in mysteries we may celebrate through devout effects. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Through him the Holy Spirit is given on earth because of love of neighbor, and sent from heaven because of love of you. We ask that his outpouring may burn away in us the stains of sins, nourish the fire of your love, and kindle us to fraternal love. Through him your Majesty.

**At the Completion.**—Having received the heavenly sacraments, O Lord, we beseech your clemency, that what we do temporally we may attain in eternal joys. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0113D] In Pamele, the station for this feria is at Saint Lawrence outside the walls. That this office is not Gregory the First’s is clear from the Roman Ordinal, p. 83, Alcuin, p. 69, and likewise the Micrologus, chapter 50. Nor, indeed, was it found in one of the Cologne codices, says Pamele. We also observe that it is absent from the Codex Regius of Sweden.]

## THURSDAY

May the Holy Spirit inflame us with that fire, we beseech you, O Lord, which our Lord Jesus Christ sent upon the earth and wished to be kindled intensely. Who lives and reigns with you as God in the unity of the same.

**Over the Offerings.**—Touch our gifts with the power of the Holy Spirit, O Lord, so that what the present solemnity has dedicated to your name he may make both intelligible to us and eternal. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Through him we humbly ask your mercy, that the Holy Spirit may cleanse our hearts and illumine them with the radiance of his light, so that in him who is the giver of graces we may have right understanding and rejoice forever in his consolation. Through him your Majesty.

**At the Completion.**—By the working of the Holy Spirit, O Lord, may our vices be cleansed through the heavenly sacrament, so that we may always be made fit for your gifts. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that the Spirit may remove carnal inclinations from our minds and powerfully pour spiritual gifts into us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you as God, in the unity of the same.

## FRIDAY OF THE FOURTH MONTH

[Note: [Col. 0114D] A station at the Apostles is appointed in the Roman Calendar, in agreement with Pamele’s edition and the manuscript codices.]

Grant, we beseech you, merciful God, to your Church that, gathered by the Holy Spirit, it may in no way be disturbed by hostile attack. Through our Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—May the divine fire that kindled the hearts of the disciples of your Christ through the Holy Spirit take up the sacrifices offered before your sight, O Lord. Through the same our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and humbly implore your Majesty that the Spirit, the Comforter, may come and, by dwelling within us, make us a temple of his Majesty; that you may always deign graciously to look upon this temple together with your Only-Begotten Son and illumine it forever with the splendor of your indwelling. Through him your Majesty.

**At the Completion.**—We have received the gifts of the sacred mystery, O Lord, humbly praying that what you commanded us to do in remembrance of you may, through the generosity of the Holy Spirit, advance toward the aid of our weakness. Through our Lord.

**Over the People, if it occurs during a fast.**—Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord, through the grace of the Holy Spirit, the discipline of a new spiritual observance of your Comforter, so that, when our minds have been purified by a sacred fast, they may be made more fit for all his gifts. Through our Lord. In the unity of the same.

## SATURDAY WITH TWELVE READINGS OF THE FOURTH MONTH

[Note: [Col. 0115D] Pamele’s edition and the Roman Calendar read: “At Saint Peter’s.”]

Mercifully pour the Holy Spirit into our minds, O Lord, by whose wisdom we have been formed and by whose providence we are governed. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—Grant, merciful God, that we who fell from the happiness of paradise by violating the divine commands may, with the Holy Spirit as our guide, return to the way of eternal blessedness through observance of your commandments. Through. In the unity of the same.

**Another.**—O God, who commanded bodies to be disciplined through the devotion of fasting for the healing of souls, mercifully grant us always to be devoted to you in mind and body. Through.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, instructed by salutary fasts and abstaining also from every vice, we may more easily obtain your favor. Through.

**Another.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we may abstain from bodily banquets in such a way that we likewise fast from the vices that assail us. Through our Lord.

**Another at Mass.**—O God, who moderated the flames of fire for the three young men, mercifully grant that the flame of vices may not burn us, your servants. Through.

**Over the Offerings.**—Almighty and eternal God, who are not appeased by the ostentation of sacrifices but regard the efforts of devout dedication, grant your household a right spirit and a pure heart, so that their faith may reconcile these gifts to you and their humility commend what is offered. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and implore your omnipotence with devout prayers, that the light of your Spirit may be poured into us, by whose wisdom you create us, whose goodness restores us, and whose providence governs us. Although he is in no way different from your substance, but consubstantial and coeternal with you and your Only-Begotten Son, nevertheless through the diversity of gifts he fills the hearts of your faithful. And therefore with the angels.

[Note: [Col. 0115D] This blessing is not read in the other editions, not even in the Benedictional. It exists in the first Theoderic.]

**Blessing.**—May almighty God bless you, who created all things from nothing and in baptism granted you remission of all sins through the Holy Spirit. Amen. Since he gave that same Holy Spirit to his disciples in fiery tongues, may he illumine your hearts through his illumination and continually kindle them with his love. Amen. So may you, cleansed from every vice by his gift and defended from every adversity by his help, deserve to become his temple. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Completion.**—May your holy things provide us, O Lord, with divine fervor, by which we may rejoice alike in their action and their fruit. Through.

## THE OCTAVE OF PENTECOST

[Note: [Col. 0115D] It is incorrectly printed in the Vatican and Gussanville editions as “on the night of Pentecost.” Perhaps the earlier editors read it that way instead of “on the octave,” through the addition of the letter *n*. Pamele has other prayers. In the margin, however, he writes: “The Sunday is vacant.” The title of this office itself sufficiently indicates that it is not Gregorian. Meanwhile Berno discusses at length the celebration of the octave of Pentecost, *On the Mass*, chapter 3, and proves this office authentic in chapter 5 from the agreement of this prayer with the antiphon and readings prescribed for this Sunday. The Micrologus also mentions it, chapter 59, etc.]

Almighty and eternal God, who have granted your servants, in confession of the true faith, to recognize the glory of the eternal Trinity and to adore the Unity in the power of its Majesty, we beseech you that we may always be defended from every adversity by firmness in this same faith. Through our Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—Sanctify, we beseech you, O Lord our God, through the power of your Only-Begotten Son, the Victim of this offering; and, with the Holy Spirit cooperating through it, make us ourselves an eternal gift to you. Through the same. In the unity of the same.

## Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: who, with your Only-Begotten Son and the Holy Spirit, are one God, one Lord—not in the singularity of one person, but in the Trinity of one substance. For what we believe concerning your glory because you have revealed it, that same thing we believe concerning your Son and concerning the Holy Spirit, without distinction of difference; so that, in confessing the true and everlasting Godhead, distinctness in the persons, unity in the essence, and equality in majesty may be worshiped. This equality the angels praise.

[Col. 0116D] [Note: I find nothing concerning this blessing except in the first Theoderic manuscript.]

### Blessing

May the almighty Trinity, one and true God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, grant you faithfully to desire him, truthfully to acknowledge him, and sincerely to love him. Amen.

May he so fix in your minds the equality and unchangeableness of his essence that he never permits you to stray from it through any fantasies whatsoever. Amen.

And may he grant you to persevere in faith, hope, and charity toward him, so that through these he may afterward lead you to the manifestation of himself and to unending vision. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this.

### At the Conclusion

May reception of this sacrament, Lord, we ask, advance the salvation of body and soul, together with confession of the eternal Holy Trinity and of that same undivided Unity. Through.

### Over the People

Lord God, almighty Father, bless and protect through your only Son, in the power of the Holy Spirit, the servants subject to your Majesty, so that, secure from every enemy, we may continually rejoice in your praise. Through the same.

## The Kalends of June

[Note: In Pamelius: the dedication of Nicomedes the martyr.]

### Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Nicomedes

[Col. 0117B]

O God, who gladden us through the merits and intercession of your blessed martyr Nicomedes, mercifully grant that we who ask for his benefits may obtain the gifts of your grace. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Sanctify, Lord, the offerings presented, and, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Nicomedes, cleanse us through them from the stains of our sins. Through the Lord.

### At the Conclusion

We humbly ask you, almighty God, that those whom you refresh with your sacraments may, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Nicomedes, graciously be granted to serve you in conduct pleasing to you. Through the Lord.

## The Fourth Nones of June

### The Birthday of the Saints Marcellinus and Peter

[Note: Added in the Roman Calendar: “on the Lavican Way.”]

[Col. 0117C]

O God, who gladden us each year with the solemnity of your blessed martyrs Marcellinus and Peter, grant, we ask, that we whose joy is in their merits may be stirred by their examples. Through.

### Over the Offerings

As we bring votive gifts, Lord, we venerate your magnificence in the passion of your martyrs Marcellinus and Peter, and through it we implore for ourselves the help of your mercy. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: with whom the life of the saints is always glorious, whose precious death gladdens and protects us. Therefore, as we recall the glorious birthdays of your martyrs Marcellinus and Peter, we offer you praises and humbly beseech your magnificence that we who venerate their martyrdoms may deserve to share in their blessedness. Through Christ our Lord.

### At the Conclusion

Through the intercession of your saints Marcellinus and Peter, Lord, grant assistance to your people, so that, freed from every harmful thing, they may accomplish everything beneficial to themselves. Through our Lord.

## The Fifth Ides of June

### The Birthday of the Saints Primus and Felician

[Note: This office, together with the following one, is absent from the Royal Swedish and Calense manuscripts. Both exist in two Theoderic manuscripts. The first is presented by the Gemetic manuscript, in which, besides the feasts contained in the other manuscripts and observed by us, many others of the English Church are recorded, such as Saint Dunstan the archbishop, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June; Saint Augustine the bishop, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June; and so forth. The same Gemetic manuscript contains the feast and office of Saint Barnabas the apostle on the third Ides of June, which we have encountered nowhere else.]

Grant us, Lord, we ask, always to follow the feasts of your saints Primus and Felician, so that through their intercessions we may receive the gifts of your protection. Through.

### Over the Offerings

May the Host to be consecrated become acceptable, Lord, we ask, through the celebration of the precious martyrdom; may it purify us from sin and win for you the vows of your servants. Through our Lord.

### At the Conclusion

We ask, almighty God, that the solemnity celebrated through the heavenly mysteries of your saints may obtain for us the forgiveness of your mercy. Through.

## The Day before the Ides of June

### The Birthday of the Saints Basilides, Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius

[Note: Absent from the Calense manuscript.]

May the birthdays of the saints Basilides, Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius shine upon us as an occasion of devotion, Lord, and may what eternal excellence bestowed upon them increase through the fruits of our devotion. Through.

### Over the Offerings

For the venerable blood of the saints Basilides, Cyrinus, Nabor [“Narboris” in the source], and Nazarius, we solemnly immolate Hosts to you, Lord, contemplating your wonders, through which such victory has been perfected. Through.

### At the Conclusion

May we always celebrate the solemnities of the holy martyrs Basilides, Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius, so that we may continually experience their patronage. Through.

## The Fourteenth Day before the Kalends of July

### The Birthday of the Saints Mark and Marcellian

[Col. 0118C]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthdays of the saints Mark and Marcellian may be freed from all impending evils through their intercession.

[Note: In the Royal Swedish manuscript: “through their intercessions.”]

### Over the Offerings

Receive, Lord, the votive gifts of your peoples, and grant that they may be pleasing to you through the prayers of the saints Mark and Marcellian, for whose solemnities they are offered. Through.

### At the Conclusion

Through the intercession of your blessed martyrs Mark and Marcellian, Lord, we ask that you nourish and restore us with mystical food. Through our Lord.

[Note 407: This does not occur in our manuscript copies, nor is it inserted in Pamelius or in the Roman Calendar.]

## Proclamation of the Fast of the First, Fourth, Seventh, and Tenth Month

[Col. 0118D]

Dearest brothers, the renewed devotion of the [fourth] month reminds us of the annual purity of fasting, through which holiness is acquired both by the body and by the soul. Therefore, gathering with diligent attendance on Wednesday and Friday, let us offer spiritual fasting to God. On Saturday, however, let us celebrate holy vigils with Christian devotion at the shrine of the blessed apostle Peter, whose intercessions we believe will assist us, so that through this salutary institution we may wash away by fasts and almsgiving the filth of sins that we contract through the frailty of our bodies, with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns as God, forever and ever.

### Another

The fasts of the [fourth] month are to be observed by us in this week. Therefore we exhort your holy faith: let us fast on Wednesday, Friday, or Saturday, so that, by adhering to the divine commandments, we may obtain the favor of our God through the perseverance of due service, with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns as God forever and ever.

## The Fourth Month: Wednesday

[Note 409: The fourth month.]

[Note 410: If it falls after the week of Pentecost.]

### Prayer at Mass

Almighty and merciful God, mercifully make us suited to your will, so that, just as we go astray when we pass beyond its path, so we may be directed along it in undiminished continuity, always returning to its proper order. Through our Lord.

### Another

Give us, Lord, a mind pleasing to you, because you will continually provide whatever is prosperous for such people. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Having been purified by solemn fasts, make us, Lord, fit for your mystery through this sacred gift, because you will be so much more salutary to us as we receive it with greater devotion. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because, after those days of joy that we spent in honor of the Lord rising from the dead and ascending into heaven, and after receiving the gift of the Holy Spirit, holy fasts have necessarily been provided for us, so that, while living in pure conduct, what has been divinely bestowed upon the Church may remain. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

Grant, we ask, Lord, forgiveness of sins to your people, so that what they do not presume upon through merits they may receive through the swift generosity of your forgiveness.

## Friday

Grant us abundance of the fruits of the earth, Lord, and make our minds fruitful with heavenly fertility. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Grant, we ask, Lord, that our fasts may be acceptable to you, and that through the gift of this sacrament we may offer you a purified heart. Through our Lord.

### At the Conclusion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, recalling the rites of your sacraments, we may be both relieved by temporal security and instructed by the ordinances of the Law. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Be mercifully generous with your mercy to your faithful people, Lord, and grant abundant bodily protection to those who implore you. Through the Lord.

## Saturday with Twelve Lessons

Grant, Lord, we ask, that by the generosity of your grace we may become such that we both confidently seek your good gifts and receive them without difficulty. Through.

### Another

Grant us, Lord, always to seek your kingdom and righteousness, so that you may mercifully make us abound in the things you see that we need. Through.

### Another

O God, who forbade us to be anxious about present assistance, grant, we ask, that for those who piously pursue what belongs to you, all things may be bestowed upon us for salvation. Through.

### Another

O God, who in your mercy go before those who do not ask, give us the disposition continually to implore your Majesty, so that in perpetual goodness you may defend suppliants with better gifts. Through our Lord.

### Another

O God, who do not despise the contrite in heart and those afflicted by miseries, mercifully hear your people crying out to you in the devotion of fasting, so that prosperity through your restoration may raise up those whom adversity has humbled. Through.

## After the Blessings

[Note: This is not read in the Vatican edition after the Blessings; the rest is similar.]

### At Mass

O God, who rescued the three children from the furnace of fire not only unharmed but also crying out in your praises, we ask that you snatch us, wrapped in the bonds of sins, as it were from a fiery abyss, so that, overcoming the flames of crimes and the conflagrations of carnal works, we may rightly and deservedly render to you the hymn that is your due. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Lord our God, who commanded that gifts be established and dedicated to your name in those very creatures that you created for the support of our frailty, grant, we ask, that they may become for us both assistance in the present life and a sacrament of eternity. Through.

### At the Conclusion

May the venerable sacrament we have received, Lord, we ask, nourish us with the supports of both the present life and the eternal one. Through.

### Over the People

May your people, Lord, dedicated to you with the affection of devout worship, advance, so that, instructed by sacred observances, the more pleasing they become to your Majesty, the more they may be increased with greater gifts. Through.

## The Thirteenth Day before the Kalends of July

### The Birthday of the Saints Gervasius and Protasius

May the blessed confession of your holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius strengthen us, Lord, and graciously obtain assistance for our frailty. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Grant us, almighty God, that through these gifts which we bring in honor of your holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, we may both please you through what is presented and be given life through what is received. Through.

### At the Conclusion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that through the power of the mysteries and the intercession of your blessed martyrs Gervasius and Protasius our life may be supported. Through.

## The Ninth Day before the Kalends of July

### Vigil of Saint John the Baptist

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that your household may walk along the way of salvation and, following the exhortations of blessed John the Forerunner, may reach safely the Lord whom he foretold—our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Sanctify, Lord, the offerings presented, and, through the intercession of blessed John the Baptist, cleanse us through them from the stains of our sins. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: as we offer the solemn fast by which we anticipate the birthday of blessed John the Baptist. His father, while doubting that he would be born, lost the use of speech; but when he was born, he received both the use of speech and the gift of prophecy. His mother, worn out by old age and punished with barrenness, not only lost her barrenness and acquired fruitfulness through his conception, but also received the Holy Spirit, by whom she recognized the Mother of the Lord and Savior. Through whom the Majesty.

### At the Conclusion

May the distinguished prayer of blessed John the Baptist accompany us, Lord, and may he ask that the one whom he foretold would come favor us, once reconciled. Through our Lord.

## The First Mass during the Night

[Note: In the Calense manuscript: “The eighth day before the Kalends of July, the birthday of Saint John the Baptist; in the first Mass, ‘Grant,’ and so forth.” The Royal Swedish, Gemetic, and Theoderic manuscripts agree. But in the old Gallican Sacramentary there is only one Mass on this day, for Saint John the Baptist. Later, however, there is a Mass for John’s Passion.]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnities of blessed John the Baptist may be protected before you through his intercession. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Sanctify, Lord, the offerings presented, and, through the intercession of blessed John the Baptist, cleanse us through them from the stains of our sins. Through.

### At the Conclusion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who have received heavenly food may, through the intercession of blessed John the Baptist, be protected through it against every adversity. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

Grant, Lord, we ask, that your people may be prepared by the birthday of blessed John the Baptist for the fulfillment of complete devotion. You sent him before your Son to prepare a perfect people, Jesus Christ our Lord. Who.

### Another

May the prayer of blessed John, Lord, ask both that we understand the mystery of your Christ and that we deserve to do so. Through the same.

## The Eighth Day before the Kalends of July

### The Birthday of Saint John the Baptist

O God, who have made this present day honorable for us through the birth of blessed John, grant your peoples the grace of spiritual joys and direct the minds of all the faithful into the way of eternal salvation. Through.

### Over the Offerings

We heap your altars with gifts, Lord, asking through them for the aid of the one whose birth we celebrate with due honor, who both sang that the Savior of the world would come and showed that he was present—our Lord.

### Preface

[Note: Nearly the same text is read in the Gallican Sacramentary.]

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and, on this feast day on which blessed John arose, to give high praise to your magnificence: he who, while not yet born, perceived the voice of the Lord’s mother and, still enclosed in the womb, signified the arrival of human salvation through prophetic exultation. He who, through his conception, removed his mother’s barrenness, and through his birth released his father’s tongue; and he alone among all the prophets showed the Redeemer of the world whom he had foretold. And so that the nature of water might receive the effect of sacred purification, by sanctifying the streams of the Jordan, he washed the Author of baptism himself with baptism. And therefore, with the angels.

### Blessing

[Note: It appears in the Benedictional and also in the edition of Grimoldus published by Pamelius.]

May almighty God bless you through the intercession of blessed John the Baptist, whose birthday you celebrate today, and grant that you may experience the protection of the one whose solemnities you celebrate. Amen.

Through his appeal may you be protected from every adversity and enjoy every good thing—he who, before he was born, recognized the coming of the world’s Redeemer, removed his mother’s barrenness by being born, and released his father’s tongue by his birth. Amen.

So may you be clothed with the wool of virtues and able to imitate innocence through the merits of that Lamb whom he pointed out with his finger and by whose immolation you were redeemed, so that you may be joined to him in the blessedness of the eternal homeland. May he himself deign to grant this.

### At the Conclusion

May your Church, O God, receive joy through the birth of blessed John the Baptist, through whom it recognized the Author of its own rebirth, our Lord. Who lives with you.

### At Matins

[Note: Perhaps it should read “At Vespers,” as it does in the Vatican edition.]

Almighty and merciful God, who by your providence sent blessed John the Baptist to prepare a perfect people for Christ the Lord, grant, we ask, that through the intercession of this herald your household may both be stripped of every sin and deserve to reach the one whom he prophesied—our Lord.

### Another

Almighty and eternal God, give our hearts that straightness of your paths which the voice of blessed John the Baptist, crying out in the desert, taught. Through our Lord.

### Another

O God, you see that our evils distress us on every side; gladden our hearts through the Forerunner of joy. Through our Lord.

### Another

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who have been placed within the womb of your holy Church may be justified from our iniquity by that Spirit by whom you taught blessed John within his mother’s womb. Through our Lord Jesus.

### Another

O God, who grant us to attend each year the solemnities of blessed John the Baptist, grant, we ask, that we may celebrate them with devout minds and, through his deserving patronage, receive an increase of complete security. Through.

## The Sixth Day before the Kalends of July

### The Birthday of the Saints John and Paul

[Col. 0123A]

We ask, almighty God, that the doubled joy of today’s festival may receive us—joy that proceeds from the glorification of the blessed John and Paul, whom the same faith and passion truly made brothers. Through.

### Over the Offerings

We place Hosts of appeasement upon your altars, Lord, honoring your power in the passions of your saints and imploring forgiveness of sins for ourselves through them. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: for love of him, the glorious martyrs John and Paul did not hesitate to undergo martyrdom. Kinship joined them by the law of birth; unity of faith joined them in the bosom of Mother Church; and fellowship in one love joined them in enduring the bitterness of their passion. Through him we ask to be aided by the prayers of those whose feasts we are known to venerate. Through whom the Majesty.

### At the Conclusion

As we celebrate the solemnities of your saints John and Paul, we have received heavenly sacraments, Lord. Grant, we ask, that what we undertake temporally we may attain in eternal joys. Through Christ the Lord.

## The Fourth Day before the Kalends of July

### The Birthday of Saint Leo the Pope

[Col. 0123C]

O God, who have made blessed Leo the bishop equal to your saints in merit, mercifully grant that we who honor the festivals of his commemoration may also imitate the examples of his life. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Grant us, Lord, that this offering may benefit the soul of your servant Leo—an offering by whose immolation you granted remission of the sins of the whole world.

[Note: Pamelius altered this prayer as follows: “That through the intercession of your servant Leo this offering may benefit us.” Nevertheless, he admits that the manuscripts do not agree with this alteration. It does, however, seem to be supported by the second Theoderic manuscript, where it reads: “That, through the intercession of blessed Leo,” and so forth.]

### At the Conclusion

O God, who bestowed the rewards of eternal blessedness upon the soul of your servant Leo, mercifully grant that we who are weighed down by the burden of our sins may be lifted up before you through his prayers. Through.

## On the Same Day

### Vigil of Saints Peter and Paul

When the apostolic celebrant celebrates two Masses on one day, he does not wash his mouth between them, but only after the office; the second begins immediately after the first has ended.

[Note: In place of this prayer, Pamelius’s edition reads, with the agreement of the Royal Swedish and Gemetic manuscripts: “Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you permit no disturbances to shake us, whom you have made firm upon the rock of the apostolic confession.” In the Roman Calendar you find: “The transfer of the body of blessed Leo.” Whether this refers to Leo II or another, consult the notes of Jean Fronto on this passage.]

O God, who grant us to anticipate the glorious birthdays of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant, we ask, that we may always be preceded by their benefits and aided by their prayers. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

We offer you, Lord, gifts for your glorification; may the intercession of the holy apostles, whose solemnities we anticipate, we ask, make them pleasing to you on behalf of our fasts. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: although with you the continuing festival of the blessed apostles and the perpetual and eternal celebration of heavenly triumph are always present, nevertheless you grant us to frequent their feasts in annual recurrence, so that their passion may receive veneration from our devotion and help may come to us from their most holy intercession. Through.

### At the Conclusion

Having received eternal remedies, Lord, may the hearts of your faithful be cleansed, so that with devout understanding they may grasp the solemn insignia of the birthday of the apostles Peter and Paul, which they carry out through bodily observances. Through.

### Over the People

O God, who bestowed upon your apostles the authority to bind and loose, grant, we ask, that through them freed from eternal vices we may be able to participate freely in the heavenly mysteries. Through the same Lord.

### At Vespers

Raise us up, Lord, we ask, through the apostolic protections of the blessed Peter and Paul, so that the more fragile we are, the stronger the assistance by which we are nourished may be. Through.

### At Matins

[Note: In the Calendar it reads: “At the vigils during the night.”]

O God, who consecrated your Church through the faith and name of your apostle Peter, and who graciously joined blessed Paul to him for preaching your glory to the nations, grant that all who have gathered for the solemnities of your apostles may be enriched with a spiritual reward.

## The Third Day before the Kalends of July

### The Birthday of the Same Saints Peter and Paul

[Note: In the old Gallican Sacramentary: “Mass for the birthday of Peter and Paul,” after which the Mass of Saint Sigismund the king is read.]

### At Mass

O God, who consecrated this present day through the martyrdom of your apostles Peter and Paul, grant that your Church may follow in all things the teaching of those through whom it received the beginning of its religion. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

May apostolic prayer accompany the Hosts, Lord, which we offer to be consecrated to your name, so that you may grant us to be purified and defended through it. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly beseech you, eternal Shepherd, not to abandon your flock, but to guard it continually through your blessed apostles, so that it may be governed by the same leaders whom, as the shepherds in charge, you appointed to preside over it as vicars of your work. And therefore, with the angels and archangels.

### Blessing

[Note: This is supplied by the Benedictional.]

May almighty God bless you, who established you in the solidity of ecclesiastical faith through the most saving confession of blessed Peter. Amen.

And may he whose most holy preaching instructed you—blessed Paul—protect you with his most gracious defense. Amen.

So may Peter with the key, Paul with his word, and both through their intercession strive to lead us into that homeland to which one by the cross and the other by the sword came on this day. Amen.

May he himself grant this.

### At the Conclusion

Protect from every adversity, Lord, those whom you have satisfied with heavenly food, through the intercessions of the apostles.

### Over the People

Mercifully look upon your household, Lord, we ask, and defend it through apostolic protection, so that it may be governed by the prayers of those whom, by your appointment, it relies upon as its leaders. Through.

### Another

O God, who, after giving the keys of the heavenly kingdom to your apostle Peter, entrusted to him the pontifical authority of binding and loosing, grant that through the help of his intercession we may be freed from the bonds of our sins. Through the Lord.

### Another

Almighty and eternal God, who rescue your Church, founded upon apostolic solidity, from the terror of the gates of hell, grant that, remaining steadfast in your truth, it may accept no fellowship with the faithless. Through.

### Another

Hear us, God our salvation, and protect us through the safeguards of your apostles, whose teachings you have granted us to be faithful to. Through.

### Another

Be the sanctifier and guardian of your people, Lord, so that, strengthened by apostolic protections, they may please you in their way of life and serve you securely. Through.

## The Day before the Kalends of July

### The Birthday of Saint Paul

[Col. 0125C]

O God, who taught the multitude of the nations through the preaching of blessed Paul the apostle, grant us, we ask, that we may experience before you the patronage of the one whose birthday we celebrate. Through.

### Over the Offerings

May apostolic prayer commend to you the prayers and Hosts of your Church, Lord, so that what we celebrate for their glory may benefit us for forgiveness. Through.

### Preface and Blessing

[Note: The same text is read in the Vatican and Gussanville editions. This indicates that the blessing mentioned above is supposed to occur at the feast of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, although it is not found there.]

The preface and blessing given above.

### At the Conclusion

Having received the sacraments, we beseech you, Lord, through the intercession of the blessed apostles, that what has been celebrated for their glory may benefit us for healing. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you permit no disturbances to shake us whom you have made firm upon the rock of the apostolic confession. Through.

## The Sixth Nones of July

### The Birthday of the Saints Processus and Martinian

O God, who surround and protect us with the glorious confessions of your saints Processus and Martinian, grant us both to advance through their imitation and to rejoice through their intercession. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Receive, Lord, the prayers and gifts, and grant that, through the prayers of your saints, they may be worthy of your sight. Through the Lord.

### At the Conclusion

Filled with the draught of the sacred Body and precious Blood, we ask you, Lord our God, that what we undertake with devout dedication we may attain with certain redemption. Through.

## The Day before the Nones of July

### The Octave of the Apostles Peter and Paul

O God, whose right hand raised blessed Peter as he walked upon the waves lest he sink, and rescued his fellow apostle Paul from the depths of the sea when shipwrecked for the third time, mercifully hear us and grant that through the merits of both we may attain the glory of eternity. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Receive with favor, Lord, we ask, the Hosts presented, so that, sanctified by you through the merits of your apostles Peter and Paul, they may become salutary for us. Through.

### At the Conclusion

As we recall the desired solemnities of your blessed apostles Peter and Paul, Lord, grant, we ask, that we may be protected by the supplications of those whose leadership governs us. Through.

### Over the People

Protect your people, Lord, and preserve them in perpetual defense as they trust in the patronage of your apostles.

## The Sixth Ides of July

### The Birthday of the Seven Brothers

[Note: In the Roman Calendar: “The seven brothers of the Appian and Salarian Ways.” Jean Fronto, however, thinks that it should be read “on the Appian and Salarian Ways.” Pamelius gives the names of the seven brothers, contrary to the testimony of the old manuscripts. After this feast, the Gemetic manuscripts and two Theoderic manuscripts read: “The transfer of the body or the birthday of Saint Benedict the abbot,” whose office, as it appears in both Theoderic manuscripts, we present here.

Prayer: Almighty and eternal God, who through glorious examples of humility showed us the eternal triumph, grant, we ask, that, with the aid of his splendid merits, we may follow without error the path of obedience pleasing to you, which the venerable Father Benedict led unharmed. Through.

Secret: Lord, we ask, may Saint Benedict obtain that the Hosts placed upon the sacred altars may come to us for salvation. Through.

Preface: It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and earnestly implore your glory: that we who venerate the feasts of your blessed confessor Benedict may, with your help, be able to imitate the examples of his holiness. And although we can in no way be made equal to him in merits, may we deserve to be aided by his prayers. Through Christ.

At the Conclusion: May blessed Benedict the abbot, by interceding for us, protect us, Lord, together with our reception of your sacrament, so that we may both experience the distinction of his way of life and receive the assistance of his intercession. Through.

Another: May the intercession of blessed Benedict the abbot commend us, Lord, so that we may attain through his patronage what we are unable to attain through our own merits. Through.]

O almighty God, grant, we ask, that we who have recognized the glorious martyrs as courageous in their confession may experience them as merciful before you in our intercession. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Look favorably, Lord, we ask, upon these present sacrifices, and, through the intercession of your saints, may they advance both our devotion and our salvation. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: as we humbly implore that you grant us this, so that just as your saints conquered the world through your power, they may likewise ask that we be freed from worldly errors. Through Christ the Lord.

### At the Conclusion

We ask, almighty God, that we may obtain the effect of that salvation whose pledge we have received through these mysteries. Through our Lord.

## The Eighth Day before the Kalends of August

### The Birthday of Saint James the Apostle

Be favorable to your people, Lord, sanctifier and guardian, so that, strengthened by the protections of your apostle James, they may please you in their way of life and serve you securely. Through.

### Over the Offerings

May the blessed passion of your blessed apostle James render acceptable the offerings of your people, Lord, we ask; and may those things that are not suited to our merits become pleasing to you through his supplication. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy, right, and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because, although the celebration of the divine sacrament always works salvation for us, we trust that it will profit us more abundantly if we are aided by the intercessions of your blessed apostle James. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

Lord, we ask, help us through the intercession of your blessed apostle James, on whose feast today you have refreshed us with the Body and Blood of your Son, and for whose solemnity we have joyfully received your gifts. Through the same.

### Over the People

Rejoicing in the increase of the apostolic solemnity, we implore your clemency, almighty God, that you may continually grant us to be blessed by their confession and nourished by their patronage. Through the Lord.

## The Fourth Day before the Kalends of August

[Note: Before this feast, the feasts of Saint Praxedes and Saint Apollinaris occur in the Theoderic and Gemetic manuscripts; those of Saint Nicasius and his Companions, martyrs, in both Theoderic manuscripts; and that of Saint Pantaleon in the Gemetic manuscript.]

### The Birthday of Saint Felix

Look upon our weakness, almighty God, and may the glorious intercession of your blessed martyr and bishop Felix protect us whom the weight of our own deeds burdens. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

For the commemoration of Saint Felix we offer Hosts to you, Lord—he whom no temptation separated from unity with your Body. Through.

### At the Conclusion

Pour into us, Lord, the Spirit of your charity, so that you who have satisfied us with one heavenly bread may, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Felix, make us united by your goodness. Through.

## The Third Day before the Kalends of August

### The Birthday of the Saints Abdon and Sennen

O God, who bestowed upon your saints Abdon and Sennen the abundant gift of grace by which they came to this glory, grant your servants forgiveness of their sins, so that, through the merits of your saints interceding for us, we may deserve to be freed from every adversity. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

We bring gifts to you, Lord, for the passion of your holy martyrs Abdon and Sennen. While they came to an end on earth, they became perpetual through heavenly light. We humbly ask that we may always be protected through their merits. Through.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and praise you as wondrous in your saints, whom before the foundation of the world you prepared for eternal glory, so that through them you might reveal to this world the light of your truth. You armed them with the spirit of truth in such a way that, through the weakness of the flesh, they overcame the fear of death. Among their company are your martyrs Abdon and Sennen, who flourished in the meadow of your Church like roses and lilies. The blood of your Only-Begotten drenched them with a rosy hue in the battle of their confession and, as the reward for their passion, clothed them in the snowy splendor of lilies. Through him the Majesty.

### Prayer after Communion

Defend your people, Lord, with perpetual protection, and grant that those aided by the merits of your saints may not find it difficult to obtain what they devoutly and justly ask. Through our Lord.

## 1 August — At Saint Peter ad Vincula

O God, who caused the blessed apostle Peter, released from his chains, to depart unharmed, we ask you: release us from the chains of our sins and, being reconciled to us, keep every evil away from us. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Receive, Lord, the sacrifice of human redemption; through the intercession of the blessed apostle Peter, graciously work salvation for us in mind and body. Through.

### Prayer after Communion

Filled with the sacramental draught of the sacred Body and precious Blood, we ask you, Lord our God, that what we undertake in devout devotion we may attain through certain redemption, with your blessed apostle Peter interceding.

[Note: In the Swedish Royal Codex: “what we carry out, may we attain through certain redemption.” “Through,” etc. In Pamelius’s edition there is another prayer.]

## 2 August — Feast of Saint Stephen, Bishop and Martyr

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed martyr and bishop Stephen, mercifully grant that, as we celebrate his feast, so also we may rejoice in his protection. Through our Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Sanctify, Lord, the gifts dedicated to you; and, with your blessed martyr and bishop Stephen interceding, graciously regard us through them. Through the Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

May this communion, Lord, cleanse us from sin; and, with your blessed martyr and bishop Stephen interceding, make us sharers in heavenly healing. Through.

## 6 August — Feast of Saint Sixtus, Bishop

[Note: From Saint Augustine’s Treatise 27 on John it is evident that the feast of Saint Sixtus was then celebrated on this same day.]

O God, who see that we subsist by none of our own strength, mercifully grant that, through the intercession of your blessed martyr and bishop Sixtus, we may be fortified against every adversity. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Receive with favor, Lord, the gifts offered, which the blessed Sixtus, priest and martyr, commends to your Majesty. Through.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and on this day of festivity, when the blessed Sixtus, priest and martyr, joyfully poured out devoted blood for you, praise you. He urged the sons of his teaching to strive for the same glory: those whom he instructed, he preceded by his exhortation and anticipated by his example. Through Christ.

### Preface for the Grapes

Admit us into their company, we ask, not as one who assesses merit, but as the giver of pardon. Through Christ.

### Blessing of the Grapes

Bless, Lord, these new fruits of the vine, which you, Lord, have deigned to bring to maturity through the dew of heaven, the abundance of rains, and the serenity and tranquility of the seasons; and you have given them to us to receive for our use with thanksgiving, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Through him are all these things.

### Prayer after Communion

Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that the sacraments whose votive celebration we have observed may, through his saving intercession, become salvation for us.

## On the Same Day — Feast of Saints Felicissimus and Agapitus

[Note: In the Roman Calendar: “On 5 August, the feast of Saints Sixtus, Felicissimus, and Agapitus.” The Saint Sixtus mentioned there is the same one as above. In the Swedish Royal Codex, the feast of Saint Xistus is also recorded, not on the sixth but on the fifth of this month.]

O God, who grant us to celebrate the feast of your holy martyrs Felicissimus and Agapitus, grant us to rejoice in their fellowship in eternal joy. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

We offer you, Lord, the gifts of our devotion. May they be pleasing to you in honor of your righteous ones, and, through your mercy, may they be made salutary for us. Through the Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

Grant us, Lord, we ask, through the intercession of your saints Felicissimus and Agapitus, that what we receive with our mouth we may take in with a pure mind. Through.

## 8 August — Feast of Saint Cyriacus

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed martyr Cyriacus, mercifully grant that, as we celebrate his feast, so also we may imitate the strength of his passion. Through our Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Receive, Lord, the sacrifice of reconciliation and praise. Through the intervention of your holy Cyriacus, may it lead us to pardon and establish us in perpetual thanksgiving. Through.

### Prayer after Communion

We ask, Lord our God, that, through the intervention of your blessed martyr Cyriacus, we may follow in deed and understanding the sacred mysteries that we have received. Through.

## 9 August — Vigil of Saint Lawrence

Be present to our supplications, Lord; and through the intercession of your blessed martyr Lawrence grant us perpetual mercy. Through our Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Graciously receive, Lord, the offerings that we present to you; and, with your blessed martyr Lawrence interceding, release us from the chains of our sins. Through.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and with devoted minds anticipate the feast of your blessed martyr Lawrence. As both a venerable levite and martyr, he was glorious in the office proper to him and shone resplendent in the martyrdom of his memorable passion. Through Christ our Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

Grant, we ask, our God, that just as we rejoice in the temporal observance of the commemoration of your blessed martyr Lawrence, so we may rejoice in perpetual sight of him. Through.

### Another Prayer

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may venerate with worthy ardor of faith the triumph of your blessed martyr Lawrence, which, having despised the flames, he completed on earth and which is now visible in the perpetual light of heaven. Through our Lord.

### At Matins

O God, Creator and ruler of the world, who consecrated this day through the martyrdom of your blessed levite Lawrence, mercifully grant that all who venerate the merits of his martyrdom may, through his intercessions, be freed from the eternal fires of Gehenna. Through.

## At the First Mass of the Night

[Note: Pamelius’s edition has “at first light.” The Roman Calendar has “at the first Mass,” with the rest omitted. It then reads: “On the day of the saints, at the public Mass, the feast of Saint Lawrence.” For this Pamelius reads: “On the day, at Mass”; the Swedish Royal Codex has: “Likewise, another Mass.”]

Raise up in your Church, Lord, the Spirit whom the levite Lawrence served, so that, filled by that same Spirit, we may strive to love what he loved and practice in action what he taught. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

May the holy prayer of your blessed Lawrence, Lord, commend our sacrifice to you, so that what is solemnly offered in his honor may become acceptable through his merits. Through.

### Prayer after Communion

We humbly ask you, almighty God, that those whom you have satisfied with heavenly gifts you may keep under perpetual protection, with your blessed martyr Lawrence interceding. Through.

## 10 August — Feast of Saint Lawrence

Grant us, we ask, almighty God, to extinguish the flames of our vices, since you granted blessed Lawrence to overcome the fires of his torments. Through our Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Receive graciously, Lord, the gifts worthily offered, and grant that, with the merits of blessed Lawrence aiding us, they may become an assistance for our salvation. Through.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and especially on this day of solemnity, when the blessed Lawrence was offered to you as a holy, living sacrifice pleasing to you. Inflamed by the fire of your love, he steadfastly endured the fire of his passion and, through the enormity of his torments, reached the fellowship of the citizens above. Through Christ the Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

We humbly ask you, almighty God, that those whom you have satisfied with heavenly gifts you may keep under perpetual protection, with your blessed martyr Lawrence interceding. Through.

### Over the People

O God, through the ardor of whose charity the blessed Lawrence, despising his persecutor, conquered the devouring flames of the fire, grant that all who venerate the merits of his martyrdom may be fortified by the help of your protection. Through.

### Another Prayer

May the holy prayer of Saint Lawrence protect us, Lord, and may what our conscience does not deserve be granted to us through the prayer of him who pleased you. Through.

### Another Prayer

May the blessing of your martyr Lawrence be with us, Lord, we ask, in the glorification of you whose confession in your power has today become our intercession. Through our Lord.

### Another Prayer

Grant, we ask, that the votive martyrdoms of the blessed Lawrence may always gladden us—martyrdoms that never cease to be worthy of wonder. Through.

## 11 August — Feast of Saint Tiburtius, Martyr

[Note: The Roman Calendar adds: “On the day of the saints,” namely the feast written above, “the feast of Saint Susanna.” On the following day it reads: “On 12 August, the feast of Saint Euplus.”]

May the continued protections of blessed Tiburtius cherish us, Lord, because you do not cease mercifully to look upon those whom you have allowed to be aided by such assistance. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Be present, Lord, to the prayers of your people; be present to their gifts, so that what has been offered in the sacred mysteries may please you through the intercession of your saints. Through our Lord.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God. As we venerate the glorious merits of blessed Tiburtius, we implore that the help of your protection may be present to us, for we believe that through the intercession of those who pleased you we obtain forgiveness for our sins. Through Christ.

### Prayer after Communion

We have received, Lord, the pledge of eternal redemption. We ask that, through the intervention of your blessed martyr Tiburtius, it may be both a help for the present life and for the life to come. Through.

## 13 August — Feast of Saint Hippolytus, Martyr

May the venerable feast of your holy martyr Hippolytus, Lord, grant us an increase of saving assistance. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Look favorably, Lord, upon the gifts of your people on this votive feast of the saints, and may the testimony of your truth advance our salvation. Through the Lord.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and implore your clemency with humble prayers, so that the intercession of blessed Hippolytus may obtain forgiveness for our sins. Through the torments of his passion he reached eternal glory. Through Christ.

### Prayer after Communion

May participation in your sacraments, Lord, save us and, with your blessed martyr Hippolytus interceding, confirm us in the light of your truth. Through.

## 14 August — Feast of Saint Eusebius, Confessor

[Note: In the Calense manuscript, “priest.” The same is also read in Pamelius’s edition, but “priest” is absent from the Swedish Royal Codex.]

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your confessor Eusebius, mercifully grant that, as we celebrate his feast, we may walk toward you by following his example. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings
