For the praise of you, Lord, we sacrifice offerings in memory of your saints. Through them we trust that we are stripped of present evils and of those to come. Through the Lord.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and implore your clemency with obedient minds, so that through the intercession of your confessor Eusebius you may strengthen saving devotion in our minds. Grant also that, just as we believe you alone to be the Author and worship you as Savior, so through his intervention we may have him as our helper forever. Through Christ.

### Prayer after Communion

As we celebrate the feast of Saint Eusebius, we humbly beseech you, Lord, that this same celebration may always be for us a cause of pardon and salvation. Through.

## On the Same Day — Vigil of the Assumption of Saint Mary

[Note: Pamelius judges that this office and the following one are not Saint Gregory’s, although he considers it probable that they are older than Gregory. They certainly exist in the Swedish Royal Codex, in both Theod. manuscripts, in Gemet., and elsewhere, also under the title of the Assumption. It is recorded in this manner in the Roman Calendar: “On 15 August, the solemnities of the Falling Asleep of Saint Mary.” The Gospel “Jesus entered a certain village” is also assigned there. Consult the notes of the most learned John Fronto on this passage.]

O God, who deigned to choose the virginal chamber of blessed Mary as the place in which you would dwell, grant, we ask, that, protected by her defense, she may make us rejoice in taking part in her feast. You who live and reign.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Great, Lord, is the prayer of the Mother of God before your clemency. For this reason you transferred her from the present age, so that she might confidently intercede with you for our sins. Through the same Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

Having been satisfied with the heavenly gift, almighty God, preserve us by your protection; and, with blessed Mary interceding, graciously grant peace of chastity to our minds and bodies, so that, when your Only-Begotten Son, the Bridegroom, comes with lamps burning, we may worthily await his arrival. You who live and reign, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit.

### Another Prayer

Grant protection to our weakness, merciful God, so that we who celebrate the repose of the holy Mother of God may, through the help of her intercession, rise from our sins. Through the same Lord.

### Another Prayer

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may reach the eternal joys of blessed Mary ever-virgin, whose venerable Assumption you grant us to celebrate with annual solemnity. Through.

## 15 August — Assumption of Saint Mary the Virgin

This day’s feast is venerable to us, Lord, on which the holy Mother of God underwent temporal death, yet could not be held down by the bonds of death, since from her she bore your Son, our Lord, incarnate. He lives and reigns with you, God.

### At Mass

Forgive the sins of your servants, Lord; and since we cannot please you by our deeds, may we be saved through the intercession of the Mother of your Son, our Lord. He lives with you.

### Prayer over the Offerings

May the prayer of the Mother of God come to the aid of your people, Lord. Although we know that she departed according to the condition of the flesh, may we perceive that in heavenly glory she prays for us before you. Through the same Lord our God.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and with exultant hearts praise, bless, and proclaim you in veneration of the holy virgins:

Among them the undefiled Virgin Mary, Mother of God, whose day of Assumption we celebrate, shone forth gloriously. She conceived your Only-Begotten through the overshadowing of the Holy Spirit, and, while the glory of her virginity remained, poured forth eternal light upon this world: Jesus Christ our Lord. Through him.

### Blessing

[Note: This blessing is contained in the Benedictional.]

May God, who through the childbirth of the blessed Virgin Mary deigned to redeem the human race, deem you worthy to enrich you with his blessing. Amen.

May you always and everywhere experience the patronage of her from whose undefiled womb you were found worthy to receive the Author of life. Amen.

And may you who have gathered today with devoted minds to celebrate her feast carry away with you gifts of spiritual joys and eternal rewards. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this.

### Prayer after Communion

Having become participants in the heavenly table, we implore your clemency, Lord our God, so that we who celebrate the feasts of the Mother of God may be freed from impending evils through her intercessions. Through the same Lord.

### Another Prayer

Extend your right hand to us, Lord, and through the intercession of the blessed and glorious ever-virgin Mary, Mother of God, grant us the help of heavenly power. Through the same Lord.

## 18 August — Feast of Saint Agapitus, Martyr

[Note: “Martyr” is absent from the Swedish Royal Codex. It is nevertheless read in the first prayer.]

May the merits of your precious martyr Agapitus, Lord, protect us. As we proclaim in them the works of your Majesty, may we receive both present and future assistance. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Receive, Lord, the gifts that we bring to you on his solemnity, whose patronage we trust will free us. Through the Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

May both participation in the heavenly banquet granted to us and the prayer of the saints bestowed upon us protect your people, we ask, Lord. Through our Lord.

## 22 August — Feast of Saint Timothy, Martyr

Mercifully extend your help to us, Lord, we ask, and, with your blessed martyr Timothy interceding, stretch over us the right hand of your reconciliation. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

May the offering of your consecrated people be acceptable to you, Lord, in honor of your saints, whose merits they recognize as having brought them help in tribulation. Through the Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

Satisfied by the generosity of the divine gift, we ask, Lord our God, that, with your blessed martyr Timothy interceding, we may always live through participation in it. Through.

## 24 August — Feast of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle

[Note: This feast is omitted in the Roman Calendar, in the Calense manuscript, and in the Swedish Royal Codex. It exists in Gemet., where on the same day is first read: “The feast of Saint Audoenus, bishop,” namely of Rouen, on 27 August. In both Theod. manuscripts and in Gemet. it is assigned as: “The feast of Saint Rufus, martyr.”]

Almighty and eternal God, who have granted the venerable and holy joy of this day through the feast of your blessed apostle Bartholomew, grant your Church, we ask, both to love what it has believed and to proclaim what he taught. Through our Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

We ask, Lord, that through the help of your blessed apostle Bartholomew, whose solemnity we celebrate, we may receive your benefits, for whom we offer you sacrifices of praise.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who do not abandon your Church through everlasting goodness, but continually instruct it through your blessed apostles and guard it without end. Through Christ our Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

We have received, Lord, the pledge of eternal salvation, celebrating the votive solemnity of your blessed apostle Bartholomew and venerating his perpetual merits. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Protect your people, Lord, and preserve forever under your defense those who trust in the patronage of your apostles. Through.

## 28 August — Feast of Saint Augustine, Bishop

[Note: Nothing concerning Saint Augustine is read in the aforementioned Calense and Swedish Royal Codices either, but his feast exists in the Gemet. and Theod. manuscripts after the feast of Saint Hermes.]

Be present to our supplications, almighty God, and mercifully grant the customary effect of your mercy to those to whom you grant confidence in hoping for your goodness, with your blessed confessor and bishop Augustine interceding. Through our Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

May the devout prayer of your confessor Augustine never be lacking for us, Lord; may it both commend our gifts and always obtain your forgiveness for us. Through.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who filled your blessed confessor Augustine with the teachings of knowledge and enriched him with the adornments of virtues. You imbued him with manifold forms of devotion in such a way that he himself was for you altar, sacrifice, priest, and temple. Through Christ our Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

So that your sacrifices may grant us salvation, let your blessed confessor and bishop Augustine, we ask, approach as an intercessor. Through our Lord.

## On the Same Day — Feast of Saint Hermes, Martyr

May the intercession of your martyr Hermes, Lord, never cease both to appease your justice toward us and to make our service devoted to you continually. Through our Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Graciously receive our gifts, Lord, we ask, and, so that we may serve your altars worthily, guard us through the intercession of your holy Hermes. Through our Lord.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, because with confidence we sacrifice offerings of praise to you, and ask that through the prayers of your holy martyr Hermes they may be acceptable to you. Through Christ.

### Prayer after Communion

Filled, Lord, with heavenly blessing, we ask your clemency: with your blessed martyr Hermes interceding, may we experience as salutary what we undertake humbly. Through.

## 29 August — Feast of Saint Sabina

Hear us, God our Savior, so that just as we rejoice in the feast of Saint Sabina, so we may be instructed by the effect of devout dedication. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Gladly, Lord, we gather to dedicate the gifts that we humbly sacrifice to your name for the solemnity of your holy martyr Sabina. Through our Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

May both reception of the divine sacrament and the glorious prayer of Saint Sabina purify us, Lord God. Through.

## On the Same Day — Beheading of Saint John the Baptist

[Note: In the Roman Calendar this feast is observed on the following day.]

May the venerable feast of Saint John the Baptist, your martyr, Lord, grant us the effect of saving assistance. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

We bring you, Lord, gifts for the passion of your holy martyr John the Baptist. While he was brought to an end on earth, he became eternal in the heavenly dwelling. We ask that, through his favor, these gifts may advance our salvation. Through.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who enriched the forerunner of your Son with so great a gift that he was beheaded for proclaiming the truth; and he who had baptized Christ with water was baptized by him in the Spirit and stained with his own blood for the sake of that same one.

For he was the herald of the truth, which is Christ. By forbidding Herod his brother’s marriage bed, he was thrust into the darkness of prison, where he enjoyed the light of your divinity alone. Then he underwent the sentence of death and descended to the underworld to precede the Lord. He whom he pointed out in the world with his finger preceded him into the underworld by a precious death. And therefore, with the angels.

### Blessing

[Note: It appears in the Benedictional at the feast of Saint John concerning his martyrdom.]

May God, who grants us to celebrate the solemnities of blessed John the Baptist, grant you both to celebrate them with devoted minds and to receive the gifts of his blessing. Amen.

And may he who for proclaiming his law was confined in the darkness of prison free you, through his intercession, from the impulses of dark deeds. Amen.

And may he who for the truth, which is God, did not hesitate to lose his head, through his intervention bring you to our Head, who is Christ. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this.

### Prayer after Communion

May the twofold solemnity of Saint John grant us, Lord, both to venerate worthily the magnificent sacraments we have received and to experience them as salutary for us. Through our Lord.

### Another Prayer

Protect us, Lord, with the perpetual safeguards of Saint John the Baptist; and the more fragile we are, the more lift us up with the help we need. Through.

## 30 August — Feast of Saints Felix and Adauctus

We humbly beseech your Majesty, Lord, that just as you continually gladden us by the commemoration of your saints, so you may always defend us through their supplication. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Look upon the offerings of your people, Lord, and may they feel that the offerings which they celebrate with devoted mind in honor of your saints advance their salvation. Through our Lord.

### Prayer after Communion

Filled, Lord, with sacred gifts, we ask that, with your saints interceding, we may always remain in thanksgiving for your gifts. Through.

## 8 September — Feast of Saint Mary the Virgin

[Note: Abbot Grimoldus holds the same opinion concerning this as we noted above concerning the office of the Assumption of Mary. Nevertheless, its antiquity is clear from the Roman Order, p. 84, where mention is also made of the station at Saint Adrian, to which this first Collect belongs, while the Masses belong to Saint Mary. Radulphus of Tongres also mentions this prayer and Collect, chapters 13 and 23, where he writes that on this day Saint Gregory instituted a litany from Saint Adrian to Saint Mary Major. PAMELIUS. This feast and office are nevertheless found in the Swedish Royal Codex and others, as well as in the Roman Calendar, where it is assigned to 9 September and the Gospel “Mary arose and went into the hill country” is prescribed.]

### Prayers at Matins

Be present to us, almighty God, as we celebrate again the feasts of blessed Mary, whom, brought forth at the dawning of today’s feast, you exalted by an ineffable gift. Through.

### At the Procession

Hear the supplication of your servants, merciful God, so that we who gather for the nativity of the Mother of God and Virgin may, through her intercessions, be rescued by you from present dangers. Through the same Lord our God.

### At Mass

Bestow upon your servants, Lord, the gift of heavenly grace, so that the votive solemnity of the nativity of blessed Mary may grant an increase of peace to those for whom the birth of the Virgin Mary became the beginning of salvation. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

May the humanity of your Only-Begotten, Lord, come to our aid. He was born of a virgin and neither diminished nor violated his mother’s integrity, but consecrated it. At the solemnities of her nativity, stripping us of our sins, may he make our offering acceptable to you. He who lives with you.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and especially for the merits of the blessed Mother of God and perpetual Virgin Mary, full of grace, praise, bless, and proclaim your omnipotence. Through him.

### Prayer after Communion

We have received, Lord, the votive sacraments of the annual celebration. Grant, we ask, through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin, that they may provide us remedies for both temporal life and eternal life. Through.

### Over the People

May the venerable intercession of Saint Mary aid us, Lord; we celebrate also the day on which her blessed nativity began. Through.

## On the Same Day — Feast of Saint Adrian, Martyr

[Note: It is absent from the Calense manuscript.]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who celebrate the feast of your blessed martyr Adrian may be freed from all impending evils through his intercessions. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Sanctify, we ask, Lord, the gifts dedicated to you; and, with your blessed martyr Adrian interceding, graciously regard us through them. Through.

### Prayer after Communion

Being reconciled through the intercession of your martyr Adrian, Lord, grant, we ask, that we may receive with eternal salvation what we undertake in time. Through.

[Note: After the feast of Saint Adrian there follows: “5 September, the feast of Saint Gorgonius, martyr,” in the Vatican edition, with the support of the Theod. and Gemet. manuscripts. The Pamelius edition, the Roman Calendar, and the Swedish Royal Codex are silent concerning him.]

## 11 September — Feast of Saints Protus and Hyacinth

May the precious confession of blessed Protus and Hyacinth cherish us, Lord, and may their devout intercession continually protect us. Through our Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

For your holy ones Protus and Hyacinth, Lord, we fulfill the offerings owed to you in their commemoration. Grant, we ask, that they may work for us as a remedy of perpetual salvation. Through.

### Prayer after Communion

We ask, Lord, that the prayer of blessed Protus and Hyacinth may implore that your holy gifts continually purify us. Through.

## 14 September — Exaltation of the Holy Cross

O God, who deigned to redeem the human race by the precious blood of your Only-Begotten Son, our Lord, mercifully grant that those who come to adore his life-giving cross may be freed from the bonds of their sins. Through the same Lord.

### Prayer over the Offerings

May help from your mercy precede, Lord, the devout prayers and sacrifices of our humility; and may faith in the wood once more open the salvation that reckless presumption had closed through Adam in the tree of paradise. Through.

For the Preface that is used at the Invention of the Holy Cross, see 3 May.

### Prayer after Communion

Having been nourished by the Body and Blood of Jesus Christ our Lord, through whom the standard of the cross was sanctified, we ask, Lord our God, that, just as we have been found worthy to adore it, so we may obtain the saving effect of its everlasting glory. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Be present to your family, we ask, merciful and compassionate God, so that you may hear its prayers in adversity and prosperity, and deign through the help of the holy cross to crush the wickedness of its adversaries, so that it may be able to reach the harbor of your salvation. Through.

## On the Same Day — Feast of Saints Cornelius and Cyprian

[Note: Cassiodorus mentions the renowned feast of Saint Cyprian in *Variae*, book VIII, letter 33, and Gregory himself mentions it in book II, indiction 10, letter 32. In the Roman Calendar, the six weeks following this feast take their name from it, which is evidence of its distinction as a celebration and solemnity. In Pamelius, with the support of the Swedish Royal Codex, the feast of Saint Cyprian is placed before the solemnity of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, which occurs on the same day.]

We ask, Lord, that the feasts of the blessed martyrs and likewise bishops Cornelius and Cyprian protect us, and that their venerable prayer commend us. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Look kindly, Lord, upon the gifts of your people, which are dedicated to your Majesty for the solemnities of your holy martyrs Cornelius and Cyprian. Through.

## Preface

Truly it is worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and proclaim your power in the feast of your saints Cornelius and Cyprian. In different regions of the earth, feeding sacred flocks with divine bread, you crowned them with one faith and, on the same day, with an equal confession of your name. Through Christ.

### Prayer after Communion

We ask, Lord, having been filled with saving mysteries, that we may be aided by the prayers of those whose solemnity we celebrate. Through.

## 15 September — Feast of Saint Nicomedes, Martyr

Be present to your people, Lord, so that, celebrating the distinguished merits of your martyr Nicomedes, we may always be aided by his patronage in obtaining your mercy. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Receive graciously, Lord, the gifts offered, which the prayer of your martyr Nicomedes commends to your Majesty. Through.

### Prayer after Communion

May the sacraments we have received purify us, Lord, and, with your martyr Nicomedes interceding, make us freed from every vice. Through.

## 16 September — Feast of Saint Euphemia, Martyr

Almighty and eternal God, who choose the weak things of the world to confound the strong, mercifully grant that we who celebrate the solemnity of your blessed martyr Euphemia may experience her patronage before you. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that, just as the death of the saints is precious in your sight, so the offering of those who venerate their merits may be made acceptable to you. Through.

### Prayer after Communion

May reception of your sacrament sanctify us, Lord, we ask, and may the intercession of your blessed martyr Euphemia make us acceptable to you. Through.

## On the Same Day — Feast of Saints Lucia and Geminianus

[Note: The Roman Calendar does not mention Saint Geminianus. His name is nevertheless recorded in manuscripts, even very ancient ones, such as the Swedish Royal Codex and those consulted by Pamelius.]

Grant, Lord, a fruitful outcome to our prayers with rejoicing, so that, as we recall annually the day of the passion of those whose feast we celebrate, we may also follow the steadfastness of their faith. Through.

### Prayer over the Offerings

Look favorably, Lord, upon the vows of your people, so that those whose solemnity you grant us to celebrate may cause us to rejoice in their intercessions. Through.

### Prayer after Communion

Hear our prayers, Lord, so that we may be continually strengthened by the assistance of your saints whose feasts we solemnly celebrate. Through.

## 12 Days before the Kalends of October

**Vigil of Saint Matthew the Evangelist.**

[Note: This Vigil is not mentioned in Pamelius’s edition or in the Roman Calendar, nor in the ancient codices. Indeed, in the Swedish Royal Codex and in the Calense manuscript there is no office for Saint Matthew. It is found in Pamelius’s edition, but enclosed within brackets. It is present in both the Theodorian manuscript and the Gemet manuscript.]

[Col. 0140A]

Grant us, almighty God, that the venerable solemnity of your blessed apostle and evangelist Matthew, which we anticipate, may increase both our devotion and our salvation. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—(482) As we offer you the sacred mysteries in reverence for the apostolic dignity, Lord, we ask that, through the intercession of the blessed evangelist Matthew, whose feast we anticipate, (483) your people here may always present their vows and receive what they desire. Through our Lord.

**At the Completion.**—Being appeased, Lord, by the supplication of your blessed evangelist Matthew, we ask that you grant us pardon and bestow everlasting remedies. [Col. 0140B] Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.**—May the blessed evangelist Matthew be, Lord, the helper of our frailty, so that, pleading for us, he may be heard by you all the more abundantly. Through you.

## 11 Days before the Kalends of October

**Feast of Saint Matthew the Apostle and Evangelist.**

May we be aided, Lord, by the prayers of the blessed evangelist Matthew, so that what our ability does not obtain may be granted to us through his intercession. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Lord, we ask that the offering of your Church, instructed by the splendid preaching of the blessed evangelist Matthew, may be commended to you through his apostolic prayers. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you make your Church everywhere strong in your faithful people and cause it to stand firm through apostolic teachings. Grant, we ask, that through those by whom it received the beginning of divine knowledge, it may receive from them (484) an increase of the heavenly kingdom until the end of the age. Through Christ.

**At the Completion.**—Having received the sacraments, Lord, we beseech you that, with your apostle and evangelist Matthew interceding, what has been celebrated for his glory may profit us as a remedy. Through you.

**Another prayer.**—(485) Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who are continually protected by apostolic defense may neither succumb to vices nor be overwhelmed by adversity. Through our Lord.

## In the Seventh Month, Wednesday

[Note: In Pamelius, in the Calense manuscript, and in the Roman Calendar, the station is assigned to Saint Mary; Pamelius adds “the Greater.” In the same source, with the agreement of the Swedish Royal Codex, Sunday is first noted, and its station is appointed at Saint Peter.]

[Col. 0140D]

May our frailty, we ask, Lord, endure through the remedies of your mercy, so that what is worn down by its own condition may be restored by your clemency. Through you.

**Another prayer.**—Grant, we ask, Lord, to the supplicating household that, while they abstain from bodily foods, they may fast from vices in mind. Through you.

[Col. 0141A] 132 **Over the offerings.**—Faithful God, who confirm faithful promises while justifying the nations called from faith, grant us knowledge of the undivided Trinity, so that we may live peaceably among the children of unity; and thus, when the sacrifice of this holy confession has been powerfully offered, may we continually deserve your visitation from on high. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you have willed that, through abstinence, we should give you thanks for the fruits gathered from the earth, so that from this very kind of devotion we might understand that we have received these things not for bodily abundance but for the support of frailty; so that what we consumed more sparingly from them might benefit the nourishment of the needy; so that salutary discipline might restrain the insolence of mortality; and so that the piety of the giver might commend us to your goodness. Thus may we use transitory gifts in such a way that we learn to desire things everlasting. Through Christ our Lord.

**At the Completion.**—As we take the heavenly gifts, Lord, we humbly beseech you that, by your gift, we may receive with worthy understanding what we perform through diligent service. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.**—We ask, almighty God, that you look upon our prayers and extend over us the depths of your compassion, so that we who are afflicted because of our guilt may mercifully be freed through your pity. Through you.

[Note: According to the Roman Calendar, Pamelius’s edition, and the manuscript codices, the station for this day is at the Apostles.]

## Friday

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, recalling the sacred observances with annual devotion, we may please you both in body and in mind. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—May the gifts of our fast be acceptable to you, Lord, we ask, so that, by cleansing us, your grace may make us worthy and lead us to the everlasting promises. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for, with just and devout governance, you both inflict scourges for sins and, when appeased after the scourges, grant pardon; and because, desiring the life of sinners rather than their death, you do not condemn them to destruction but mercifully await their correction. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 0141D] **At the Completion.**—We ask, almighty God, that, giving thanks for the gifts we have received, we may receive greater benefits. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## Saturday with Twelve Lessons

[Note: From the same books, the station is at Saint Peter.]

Almighty and eternal God, who through salutary self-restraint heal both bodies and minds, we humbly implore your Majesty that, appeased by the devout prayer of those who fast, you may provide us both present assistance and future aid. Through you.

**Another prayer.**—Grant us, we ask, almighty God, that by fasting we may be filled with your grace, and by abstaining may become stronger than all our enemies. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.**—Guard your household, we ask, Lord, so that the remedies of eternal salvation which we seek at your prompting we may obtain through your generosity. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.**—Grant, we ask, Lord, to your faithful people that they may be suitably fitted for fasting, and that the bodily discipline solemnly undertaken may pass over into the fruitfulness of our souls. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.**—Since you grant us, Lord, to offer you a solemn fast, grant us, we ask, the assistance of pardon in equal measure. Through you.

**Another prayer.**—(486) God, who granted that the flames of the fires should be subdued for the boys [the reading *pueris* is uncertain], mercifully grant that the flame of vices may not consume us, your servants. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—May this Victim, Lord, we ask, both release the bonds of our iniquity and obtain for us the gifts of your mercy. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and sanctify for you the fast which you have taught us to keep for the building up of souls and the discipline of bodies; for (487) when bodies are restrained, souls are nourished, and when our outward person is afflicted, our inward person is enlarged. Remember, we ask, Lord, our fasts and your mercies, which you have always devoutly bestowed upon sinners who fast; and grant that, abstaining not only from foods but from every sin, we may please you through the fast of our devotion. Through Christ the Lord.

[Note: We have found this Blessing printed nowhere, not even in the Book of Blessings.]

**Blessing.**—May God, the fountain of pardon, mercifully receive the offering of your abstinence. Amen. May he fill your hearts with delight in his Victims and grant you the ability to obey his commandments. Amen. May you deserve, through the abundance of his grace, to fulfill what you cannot accomplish because of bodily weakness. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Completion.**—[Note: These words are praised by Gratian, *On Consecration*, distinction 2, chapter 34, “Species”; likewise by Lanfranc, Guitmund, [Col. 0142D] and others who contended against Berengar.] May your sacraments, Lord, accomplish in us what they contain, so that what we now perform in appearance we may receive in the reality of things. Through you.

**Over the people.**—May your people rejoice, Lord, we ask, in the benefits obtained; and to those to whom you grant confidence in hoping for your mercy, kindly grant the fulfillment of the mercy they desire. Through our Lord.

## 5 Days before the Kalends of October

**Feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian.**

[Note: Before this feast the Roman Calendar reads: “On September 11, Saint Eustochius”; but John Fronto thinks that “Eustachius” should be read. It is found in none of our manuscripts.]

Be present, Lord, through the prayers of your holy martyrs, and make those whom you willed to suffer for your name intercede for your faithful. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—Merciful God, let your mercy anticipate us before the zeal of anger rages, and sanctify these gifts, so that, aided by the protection of the blessed whose blood was shed for you, we may obtain your forgiveness together with pardon for our sins. Through you.

**At the Completion.**—May the sure salvation of your sacrament, Lord, be ours when it is implored together with the merits of your blessed martyrs Cosmas and Damian. Through you.

## 3 Days before the Kalends of October

**Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Michael.**

[Note: In the Roman Calendar: “Dedication of the church of the archangel.” In the Calense manuscript: “of the holy angel.” In the old Gallican Sacramentary there is a Mass in honor of Saint Michael, very different from this one; in its Preface, or Contestation, mention is made of the dedication.]

God, who order the ministries of angels and the affairs of human beings in wondrous order, mercifully grant that, as those by whose ministry you are always served in heaven stand continually before you, so by them our life on earth may be protected.

**Over the offerings.**—We offer you sacrifices of praise, Lord, humbly beseeching you that, with the angelic intercession made for us, you may both accept them in your favor and grant that they may bring about our salvation. Through the Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, as we proclaim the merits of the holy archangel Michael; for although every angelic sublimity that stands in the presence of your Majesty is worthy of reverence, that which, in the dignity of its order, deserved the primacy of the heavenly army is nevertheless to be honored with greater devotion. Through Christ our Lord.

[Note: Our other books do not know this Blessing.]

**Blessing.**—May God, who uses the ministry of his angels for our salvation, protect you with their common (488) guardianship. Amen. May he who promised equality with all his chosen angels grant you purity of mind and continual chastity of body. Amen. May he who gave them the most certain confidence of remaining with him strengthen you with enduring faith, hope, and charity, and lead you to fellowship with their blessedness. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Completion.**—Supported by the intercession of your blessed archangel Michael, we humbly beseech you, Lord, that we may attain in mind those whom we honor. Through the Lord.

**Over the people.**—(489) Be present to your people, merciful God, and, so that they may receive the greater benefits of your grace, grant that they may be lifted up through the humble prayers of the blessed archangel Michael. Through our Lord.

## The Nones of October

**Feast of Saint (490) Mark the Pope.**

Hear our prayers, Lord, we ask, and, with your blessed confessor and pontiff Mark interceding, favorably heed our supplications. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0144A] **Over the offerings.**—May your abundant blessing, Lord, descend; through the prayers of your holy confessor and pontiff Mark, may it make our gifts acceptable to you and make the sacrament of redemption for us. Through our Lord.

**At the Completion.**—Grant, we ask, Lord, that your faithful peoples may always rejoice in the veneration of your saints and be protected by their perpetual prayer. Through the Lord.

## The Day before the Ides of October

**Feast of Saint Callistus the Pope.**

God, who see us failing because of our weakness, mercifully restore us to your love through the examples of your saints. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—May the mystical offering profit us, Lord, so that it may both free us from our guilt and strengthen us with everlasting salvation. Through you.

**At the Completion.**—We ask, almighty God, that the consecrated gifts cleanse our guilt and bring about in us the effect of living rightly. Through our Lord.

## 15 Days before the Kalends of November

[Note: In the Swedish Royal Codex, after the office of Saint Callistus everything is omitted until the Kalends of November; there the feast celebrated is not that of all the saints but only the birthday of Saint Caesarius. The Calense Codex does not know the feasts of Saint Luke, Saints Simon and Jude, or Saint Thomas.]

**Feast of Saint Luke the Evangelist.**

May your holy evangelist Luke intercede for us, Lord, we ask—he who continually bore in his body the mortification of the cross for the honor of your name. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Grant, we ask, Lord, that through the heavenly gifts we may serve you with a free mind, so that the gifts we offer, with your blessed evangelist Luke interceding, may bring us both healing and glory. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and praise, bless, and proclaim you in the glorious merits of your saints: for you, King of glory, strengthened them with unconquerable virtue as they fought against the devices of the ancient serpent and the allurements of their own bodies. Among them your blessed evangelist Luke, (491) taking up the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Holy Spirit, fought courageously against the incitements of vices and (492) poured forth for us the streams of evangelical sweetness. Therefore we ask your boundless mercy, Lord: since you endowed him with so many distinctions of merit, [Col. 0144D] may you form us by his example and help us through his merits. Through Christ.

**A Blessing is to be sought for the feast.** (See note 508.)

**At the Completion.**—Grant, we ask, almighty eternal God, that what we have received from your holy altar may sanctify our souls through the prayers of your blessed evangelist Luke, so that through it we may be kept safe. Through you.

## 6 Days before the Kalends of November

**Vigil of the Apostles Simon and Jude.**

[Col. 0145A]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, just as we anticipate the glorious feast of your apostles Simon and Jude, so they may anticipate us before your Majesty in obtaining your benefits.

**Over the offerings.**—With our gifts we precede the feast of the apostles Simon and Jude, humbly asking that what is hindered by obstacles in our conscience may be made acceptable through their merits. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, because you are wondrous in all your saints: you made them illustrious through confession of your name and glorious through the suffering they accepted for you. Therefore, just as they contended by fasting and prayer so that they might obtain this victory, so may we (493) be formed by their examples, so that we may be found fit to celebrate the present feast and, through their intercession, be judged worthy to receive the eternal rewards. Through Christ.

**At the Completion.**—Having received the sacrament, Lord, we humbly beseech you that, with the blessed apostles interceding, what we undertake temporally may be received by us unto eternal life. Through you.

**At Vespers.**—Almighty and eternal God, Creator and ruler of the world, who exalted the blessed apostles through the glory of your name, hear, we ask, Lord, your people praying to you with the protection of your saints, so that you may grant us the gift of peace and cause it continually to advance the increase of faith and charity. Through our Lord.

## 5 Days before the Kalends of November

**Feast of the Holy Apostles Simon and Jude.**

God, who granted that through your blessed apostles we should come to knowledge of your name, grant us to celebrate eternal glory by advancing, and to advance by celebrating. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—As we venerate the everlasting glory of your holy apostles, Lord, we ask that, cleansed by the sacred mysteries, we may celebrate it more worthily. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, glorifying you in the honor of your apostles: for you granted them everlasting blessedness and provided such intercessors for our weakness (494) that we might obtain your assistance and reach the rewards you have promised. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—R. Q. (that is, “Seek what is above.”)

**At the Completion.**—Having received the sacraments, Lord, we humbly ask you that, with your blessed apostles interceding, what we undertake in reverence for their holy suffering may profit us as a remedy. Through you.

**Another prayer.**—Hear us, God our salvation, and protect us by the defenses of your apostles, whose teachings you granted your faithful people to follow. Through you.

## The Day before the Kalends of November

**Vigil of All Saints.**

Lord our God, multiply your grace over us, and grant us to follow with joy in holy profession those whose glorious solemnities we anticipate. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—We heap your altar, Lord God, with the gifts offered; grant, we ask, that through the prayers of all your saints they may contribute to our salvation, whose coming solemnity we anticipate. [Col. 0146B] Through you.

**At the Completion.**—With the sacraments and joys of the desired celebration completed, we ask that we may be aided by the prayers of those whose commemorations are being presented. Through you.

**Over the people.**—Instruct your people, we ask, Lord, with spiritual instruments, and make those whose solemnities you grant us to anticipate devoted through their remembrance and secure through their protection. Through you.

## (495) The Kalends of November

**Feast of Saint Caesarius the Martyr.**

[Note: It is found in our codices and in the Swedish Royal manuscripts, which make no mention at all of the solemnity of All Saints.]

(496) God, who gladden us with the annual solemnity of your blessed martyr Caesarius, mercifully grant that, as we celebrate his feast, we may also imitate his deeds. Through you.

[Col. 0146C] **Over the offerings.**—Kindly accept, Lord, the sacrifices dedicated to you through the merits of your blessed martyr Caesarius, and grant that they may come to us as perpetual assistance. Through you.

**At the Completion.**—We ask, almighty God, that we who have received heavenly nourishment may, with your blessed martyr Caesarius interceding, be protected through these gifts against every adversity. Through the Lord.

**On the Same Day.**—(497) **Feast of All Saints.**

[Note: We are surprised that Pamelius notes the office of this day as being found in all the manuscripts; the same appears in Gussanville’s edition. Certainly it is omitted in the Swedish Royal Codex, in two others indicated here by Menard, and in the Roman Calendar.]

Almighty and eternal God, who granted us to venerate the merits of all the saints in a single celebration, we ask that, through their multiplied intercessions, you bestow upon us the abundance of your desired favor. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—We offer you, Lord, the gifts of our devotion; may they be acceptable to you in honor of all your saints and, by your mercy, be made salutary for us. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and humbly beseech your clemency that you may join our joys to those of the saints rejoicing in the dwelling places of the heavenly kingdom. Although we cannot follow those whom we venerate in the imitation of virtue, may we reach them through the affection of due reverence. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—May the Lord cause you to be blessed through the merits of his saints and, through their intercession, protect you against every adversity. Amen. May their intercessions make you happy, whose feast day you celebrate with rejoicing. Amen. May you imitate their examples and thus be able to attain the heavenly promises. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

**At the Completion.**—God, grant us, we ask, the glorious confession of all the saints, so that through these holy things we have received, admitted to the fellowship of your saints, we may be nourished with the food of your mercy. Through you.

**Another prayer.**—Grant, we ask, Lord, that your faithful peoples may always rejoice in the veneration of all the saints and be protected by their perpetual prayer. Through you.

(498) These are the names of the Four Crowned Martyrs: Severus, Severianus, Victorinus, and Carpophorus. (499) Their birthday could not be found because it had been neglected through carelessness; therefore it was decreed that in their church the feast of these five saints, who are recited in the Mass, should be celebrated, so that their memory also might be commemorated together with theirs.

## 6 Days before the Ides of November

**Feast of the Four Crowned Saints.**

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, since we have recognized the glorious martyrs (500) Claudius, Nicostratus, (501) Symphonianus, Castorius, and Simplicius as steadfast in their confession, we may experience them as devout advocates for us before you. Through you.

[Col. 0147C] **Over the offerings.**—May your abundant blessing, Lord, descend; through the prayers of your saints, may it make our gifts acceptable to you and make the sacrament of redemption for us. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, as we celebrate the feast of the Crowned Saints; for, whenever we honor through them the glory of your name, we grow in the increase of our faith. Through Christ.

**At the Completion.**—Refreshed by heavenly sacraments and joys, we humbly beseech you, Lord, that we who glory in their triumphs may be protected by their assistance. Through you.

## 5 Days before the Ides of November

**Feast of Saint Theodore the Martyr.**

[Col. 0147D]

God, who surround and protect us with the glorious confession of your blessed martyr Theodore, grant that we may advance through his imitation and be strengthened by his prayer. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, Lord, the prayers of the faithful together with the offerings of Victims, and, with your blessed martyr Theodore interceding, may we pass through these devout acts of worship to heavenly glory. Through you.

**At the Completion.**—Grant us, Lord, we ask, with your blessed martyr Theodore interceding, that what we have touched with our mouth we may receive with a pure mind. Through you.

## 3 Days before the Ides of November

**Feast of Saint Menas the Martyr.**

[Col. 0148A]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who celebrate the feast of your blessed martyr Menas may be strengthened in the love of your name through his intercession. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—As we recall the solemnity of your blessed martyr Menas, Lord, we ask that, with his help, we may receive your benefits, for whom we offer you sacrifices of praise. Through you.

**At the Completion.**—May your blessing, God, fill the hearts of the faithful and make them such that they both honor the sufferings of the martyrs and, with those same martyrs as patrons, attain the remedies of eternal salvation. Through you.

**On the Same Day.**—**Feast of Saint Martin the Confessor.**

[Note: In the Theodorian manuscript, the feast of Saint Martin is placed before the feast of Saint Menas and is preceded by a solemn vigil.]

God, who see that we subsist through none of our own virtue, mercifully grant that, through the intercession of your blessed confessor and pontiff Martin, we may be protected against every adversity. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—May the devout prayer of the blessed pontiff Martin, Lord, not be lacking for us; may it both reconcile our gifts and always obtain your forgiveness for us. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: by whose (502) gift the blessed Martin, confessor and priest alike, both grew through the increase of good works, abounded in various gifts of virtue, and shone through miracles. What he taught in words he completed by the display of his works, and by instruction as well as example he provided his subjects with guidance for journeying to the heavenly kingdoms. Therefore we ask your clemency: may we be formed for good action by the examples of him who pleased you, strengthened by his merits, aided by his intercessions, and, with him intervening and you assisting, deserve to reach the heavenly kingdom. Through Christ.

**At the Completion.**—As we receive your holy things, Lord, we humbly beseech you that we may experience the protection of those whose confession we venerate. Through you.

**Over the people.**—Hear your people, Lord, wholly subject to you in mind, and guard them through the prayer of the blessed pontiff Martin, so that, protected in body and heart, they may seek what they piously believe and obtain what they justly hope for. Through you.

## 10 Days before the Kalends of December

[Note: In the earlier Theodorian manuscript, this feast is celebrated together with a vigil.]

**Feast of Saint Cecilia.**

[Col. 0148D]

God, who gladden us with the annual solemnity of your blessed martyr Cecilia, grant that, as we honor her in worship, we may also follow her example in devout conduct. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—May this Victim of reconciliation and praise, Lord, we ask, with your blessed martyr Cecilia interceding, always make us worthy of your favor. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you perfect strength in weakness and conquer the enemy of the human race not only through men but also through women. By your gift the blessed Cecilia was strengthened both in her commitment to virginity and in her confession of faith, so that she was not turned from her purpose by the instability of youth, nor softened by carnal allurements, nor frightened by the frailty of her sex, nor overcome by the savagery of tortures; but, preserving the integrity of body and mind, she deserved to attain eternal blessedness with the crown of virginity and martyrdom. Through Christ.

**At the Completion.**—May your grace, Lord, we ask, always exercise us in this way: may it renew our hearts through divine mysteries and gladden us through the commemoration of your holy martyr Cecilia. Through our Lord.

## 9 Days before the Kalends of December

**Feast of Saint Clement.**

[Col. 0149B]

Almighty and eternal God, who are wondrous in the virtue of all your saints, grant us joy in the annual solemnity of the blessed Clement. He was a martyr and pontiff of your Son; what he performed in ministry he proved by testimony, and what he preached with his mouth he confirmed by his example. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—We offer you a sacrifice of praise, Lord, for the celebration of Saint Clement, so that, through the intercession of this devout advocate, we may obtain your forgiveness, which we do not deserve through our own works. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and on this day, which the passion of the blessed Clement consecrated and made venerable for us: he, instructed by apostolic preaching, educated in heavenly teachings, distinguished by the dignity of succession, shone forth as an eminent martyr and priest. Through Christ our Lord.

**At the Completion.**—Grant, we ask, Lord our God, that just as we rejoice in the temporal observance of the commemoration of your saints, so we may rejoice in their perpetual vision. Through you.

**On the Same Day.**—**Feast of Saint Felicitas.**

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, as we recall the solemnity of your blessed martyr Felicitas, we may be protected by her merits and prayers. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive the vows of your servants, Lord, and, being appeased, look favorably upon the sacrifice of peaceful offering made to you for the commemoration of the blessed Felicitas. Through you.

**At the Completion.**—We humbly ask you, almighty God, that, with your saints interceding, you may both multiply your gifts within us and order our times. Through you.

## 8 Days before the Kalends of December

**Feast of Saint Chrysogonus the Martyr.**

Be present to our supplications, Lord, so that we who recognize ourselves to be guilty because of our iniquity may be freed through the intercession of your blessed martyr Chrysogonus. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—Be appeased, Lord, by the gifts offered, and, with your blessed martyr Chrysogonus interceding, defend us from every danger. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you console us through the continual sufferings of the martyrs and cause their triumphant blood—which, for confessing your name, they delivered up to be shed by unbelievers—to pass over into the assistance of your faithful.

**At the Completion.**—Through receiving your sacrament, Lord, may we be cleansed from our hidden faults and freed from the ambushes of our enemies. Through you.

## 3 (503) Days before the Kalends of December

**Feast of Saint Saturninus the Martyr.**

[Col. 0150B]

God, who grant us to enjoy the birthday of your blessed martyr Saturninus, grant that we may be helped by his merits. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—Sanctify the gifts dedicated to you, Lord, and, with your blessed martyr Saturninus interceding, graciously look upon us through them. Through our Lord.

**At the Completion.**—May the reception of your sacrament sanctify us, Lord, we ask, and, through the intercession of the saints, make us acceptable to you. Through you.

**On the Same Day.**—**Vigil of Saint Andrew.**

We ask, almighty God, that the blessed apostle Andrew may implore your help for us, so that, absolved from our guilt, we may also be stripped of every danger. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0150C] 143 **Over the offerings.**—(504) We offer you, Lord, a sacred gift, by which, as we recall the solemnity of the blessed Andrew, we also implore purification for our minds. Through you.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and (505) humbly implore your Majesty: as we anticipate the feast of the blessed apostle Andrew with solemn fasts and devout observances, may we be aided by his merits before your Majesty and instructed by his examples. Through Christ.

[Col. 0150D] **At the Completion.**—Having received the sacraments, Lord, we humbly implore you that, with your blessed apostle Andrew interceding, what we undertake in reverence for his holy suffering may profit us as a remedy. Through you.

**Another prayer.**—Guard us, merciful God, and continually guide us by the protection of your apostle Andrew, whose feast we anticipate. Through our Lord.

**At Vespers.**—May the blessed apostle Andrew help your Church, Lord, by pleading with you, and may he become a devout intercessor, since he was a preacher of your name. Through the Lord.

**At Matins.**—God, who are the wondrous splendor of your saints and who consecrated this day through the martyrdom of the blessed Andrew, grant your Church continual joy in his feast, so that we may be protected by his examples and merits before your mercy. Through you.

## The Day before the Kalends of December

**Feast of Saint Andrew.**

[Note: In the Roman Calendar the Gospel passage “Jesus walking beside the sea” is prescribed; Saint Gregory’s fifth homily is said to have been delivered on it.]

We humbly implore your Majesty, Lord, that, just as the blessed apostle Andrew was a preacher and ruler of your Church, so he may be a perpetual intercessor for us before you. Through you.

**Over the offerings.**—May the holy prayer of the blessed Andrew reconcile our sacrifice to you, Lord, so that what is solemnly presented in his honor may be made acceptable through his merits. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: (506) for the day of the votive mystery of the glorious apostle is present for us, on which the venerable apostle Andrew showed himself to be the brother of your glorious apostle Peter both in preaching Christ your Son and in manner of life. What he had preached with free voice, he did not keep silent even while (507) hanging on the cross; and he deserved both to follow the Author of eternal life in this life and to imitate him in the manner of his death. Thus, by whose command he had crucified earthly desires in himself, by that one’s example he himself was fastened to the gibbet.

Therefore the two brotherly fishermen are both raised by the cross to heaven, so that those whom your grace had bound with so many bonds of loving-kindness during the course of this life might be joined by an unfading crown in the kingdom of heaven. And for those who had one cause of struggle, may there also be one recompense of reward. Through him, your Majesty.

[Col. 0151C] **A Blessing is to be sought for the feast.** (508)

**At the Completion.**—We have received the divine mysteries, Lord, rejoicing in the feast of the blessed Andrew; perfect them so that, just as they benefit your saints unto glory, so, we ask, they may benefit us unto pardon. Through the Lord.

**At Vespers.**—Grant us, we ask, Lord our God, to be lifted up through the intercessions of your apostle Andrew, so that, through those (509) by whom you bestowed upon your Church the beginnings of heavenly grace, you may provide perpetual aids to salvation. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.**—Hear your people, Lord, praying with the protection of your holy apostle Andrew, so that through your help they may always serve you with secure devotion. Through you.

## On the Ides of December—The Feast of Saint Lucia, Virgin

Hear us, O God our Savior, so that, just as we rejoice in the feast of blessed Lucia [Col. 0152A], so we may be instructed by the effect of devout dedication. Through [the Lord].

### Over the Offerings

We beseech you, God of the heavenly powers, that the sacrifices brought for the solemnity of your holy Lucia may teach us to hold temporal desire in contempt and make us seek the gifts of heavenly joys. Through [the Lord].

### At the Conclusion

Lord, we have joyfully received the heavenly sacraments. May they profit us unto eternal life, with your martyr, blessed Lucia, interceding for us. Through the Lord.

### Another Prayer

May the votive intercession of your holy martyr Lucia sustain us, we beseech you, O Lord, so that we may both celebrate her hallowed feast in temporal life and behold eternal things. Through our Lord.

## The Twelfth Day before the Kalends of January—The Feast of Saint Thomas the Apostle

[Note: [Col. 0151D] Nothing concerning Saint Thomas is found here in the Swedish Royal Codex, in the Calense, or in the Roman Calendar, where four Sundays before Christmas are assigned after the feast of Saint Lucia. In Pamelius, agreeing with the Calense manuscript, one reads: “On the Advent of the Lord, Sunday 1,” and consequently “Sunday 2,” and so on. After the Saturday in the twelve lessons, or the four Ember seasons, Pamelius inserts the office of Saint Thomas, but encloses it in brackets. An office for the Sundays of Advent is found below in the edition of Angelo Rocca and in another by Hugo Menard, which we follow.]

[Col. 0152B]

Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord, to glory in the solemnities of your blessed apostle Thomas, so that we may always be strengthened by his patronage and follow the faith with fitting devotion. Through.

### Over the Offerings

We humbly return the debt of our service, earnestly beseeching you, O Lord, to safeguard your gifts within us through the intercessions of blessed Thomas the apostle. In honoring his confession, we offer you sacrifices of praise. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for you granted that your Church should stand upon apostolic foundations. As we celebrate the solemnity of your apostle blessed Thomas, one of their company, may we not be silent concerning your praises, O Lord. Through our Lord.

R. Q. Blessing at the feast.

### At the Conclusion

Preserve your people, O Lord, and grant them to rejoice in perpetual remedies—you who never cease to assist them through the protection of your saints. Through.

### Over the People

Grant your people, we beseech you, O Lord, the Spirit of truth and peace, so that, with your apostle blessed Thomas interceding, they may know you with their whole mind and follow with all their heart what pleases you. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

---

(510) **HERE BEGINS THE ORDER FOR DEDICATING A CHURCH**

[Note: [Col. 0152D] Our manuscripts do not treat the dedication of a church at this point, but do so elsewhere at great length, especially the Gemetian manuscript, where the entire nocturnal office for a dedication is also described, with twelve Psalms assigned, each with its own Antiphon, according to the rule of Saint Benedict. The Psalms are not taken from the weekday office but selected from Psalms belonging to different weekdays. From this it is clear how the provision in chapter 14 of the rule of Saint Benedict was then understood: “On the feasts of saints, or on all solemnities, let it be done as we have said it should be done on Sunday, except that the Psalms, Antiphons, or lessons belonging to that day are to be said.” In Pamelius’s edition the office for a dedication is more abbreviated and altogether different. The Swedish Royal Codex has still less. But both Theodorian manuscripts have much more, and longer material. In them there is a blessing for the church’s sign, which is called “a little vessel prepared for inviting the children of the Church”; and wherever its little bell should sound, may the power of the enemies withdraw far away. Below, the sign that is blessed is called a little bell. Similar material is not found in the blessing of the sign that our Edmund Martène inserted from the Gemetian Codex in his *Ancient Rites of the Church*, vol. III, book II, p. 269.]

First, before the bishop enters the church, let twelve candles be lighted around the church [Col. 0153A], and let him put on the sacred vestments. When they have come to the church door, let the bishop strike the threshold three times with his crozier, saying before the gate the Antiphon, “Lift up your gates, you princes.” Let them sing the entire Psalm before the door; and when the door has been opened, let them enter, saying, “Peace to this house.” Then let the clergy begin the litany. When the priests or deacons have come before the altar, let them prostrate themselves on the coverings with the bishop until “Lamb of God” is said. When they have risen from prayer, let the bishop say not “The Lord be with you,” but only “Let us pray.” Let the deacon say, “Let us bend our knees”; after they have prayed, let him say, “Rise.” Then follows the Prayer.

Magnify yourself, O Lord our God, in your saints, and appear in this temple of your building, so that you who work all things in the children of adoption may yourself always be praised in your inheritance. Through our Lord Jesus Christ your Son.

(517) Then the bishop begins at the left-hand corner on the east, writing on the pavement with his crozier, “A, B, C,” as far as the right-hand corner on the west. Beginning again in the same way at the right-hand corner on the east, he writes “A, B, C” as far as the left-hand corner on the west of the basilica. [Col. 0153B]

Then, coming before the altar, let him say:

“O God, come to my assistance; O Lord, hasten to help me. Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and always will be, throughout the ages of ages. Amen”—without “Alleluia.”

Then follows the exorcism of the water.

[Col. 0153C]

Depart, unclean spirit, from all the sacraments by which our faith makes use of the religious office. Do not put forward the guilt of sin, you who acknowledge the power of the Savior. Confidence rests not on merit but on command, although the very power of the ministry is the dignity of the minister. Therefore I address you, creature of water, through the common God, so that, while the movement of your sensible nature is preserved, you may understand that you are subject to the service by which we strive to please God and may not refuse it. Purge from yourself every communion with demons and every fellowship of wickedness. Destroy every stain of phantoms, being capable of the Lord’s protection, so that, having obtained the grace of sanctification, you may serve our Creator and yours alike with the service owed to him; and wherever you are sprinkled, may you cast down all the wickedness of evil spirits and pour forth an abundance of holy blessing. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire.

Then let him say this prayer:

(524) Be sanctified by the word of God, heavenly flood; be sanctified, water trodden by the footsteps of Christ. You are not enclosed when pressed by mountains; you are not shattered when dashed against rocks; you do not fail when spread over the earth. You support the dry land, you bear the weight of mountains, yet you do not submerge them. You are held at the summit of the heavens; poured around the whole world, you wash everything, yet are not washed. When the Hebrew peoples fled, you were hardened into a solid mass and held together; then, loosened again into the salty whirlpools of the Nile, you destroyed its inhabitants and pursued the hostile multitude with the sea raging. You are one and the same salvation for the faithful and vengeance for the guilty. The rock struck by Moses vomited you forth, nor could you remain hidden in the cliffs when, commanded by the authority of Majesty, you were ordered to emerge. Carried by clouds, you make the fields fruitful with joyful rain.

(526) Through you, for bodies dried by heat, a sweet drink is poured forth for grace and a salutary one for life. Springing from hidden veins, you provide either life-giving breath enclosed within, or fertile sap, lest, when its inward parts have been drained dry, the earth refuse its customary produce. Through you beginning rejoices; through you, ending—or rather, your origin is from God, so that we may know no limit. But you, almighty Lord God [Col. 0154B], whose powers we do not fail to recognize, while we proclaim the merits of water, proclaim also the marvels of your work: author of blessing and source of salvation, we humbly beseech and implore you to pour the rain of your grace upon this house, together with the abundance of your blessing; grant every good thing, bestow prosperity, repel adversity. Destroy the demon who fosters evils; appoint the angel of light as friend, provider, and defender of good things. May your blessing confirm this house, begun in your name and completed with you as helper, so that it may endure for a long time. May these foundations merit your protection, its roof your covering, its doors entrance, and its inner chambers access. By the shining of your countenance, may there be human welfare and stability of the walls; may the unconquered cross be placed upon the thresholds; may both doorposts be marked with the inscription of your grace; and through the abundance of your mercy, may there be peace with abundance for those who visit this house, sobriety with restraint, and overflowing plenty with mercy. May every disturbance and calamity withdraw far away; may want, pestilence, sickness, infirmity, and attacks of evil spirits depart through your continual visitation. And may the prayer of our supplication, poured out in this place, pass through its extended boundaries and the surrounding courts; may the blessing given flow through every corner and recess by the purification of this flood, so that here there may always be the joy of tranquility, the grace of hospitality, abundance of crops, reverence for religion, and an abundance of salvation. Wherever your holy name is invoked, may an abundance of good things follow, and may the temptations of evil flee far away. May we merit an angel of peace, chastity, and truth, who may always guard, protect, and defend us from every evil. Through the Lord.

### Blessing of the Water

(527) Lord God, almighty Father, establisher and creator of all the elements, who through Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, willed that this element of water should be for the salvation of the human race, we humbly beseech you: having heard our prayers, sanctify it through the regard of your mercy. Let the assault of every unclean spirit withdraw from it, so that wherever it is sprinkled in your name, the grace of your blessing may come, and all evils may withdraw far away through your favor. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ.

[Note: [Col. 0155] This exorcism, together with the following blessing, is found in the ancient Gallican Sacramentary, and is preceded by: “Exorcism for making sprinkled salt.”]

### Exorcism of the Salt

(528) I exorcise you, creature of salt, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, who commanded you to be put by Elisha into the water so that barren waters might be healed; (529) who, by the divine word of his mouth, said to his disciples: “You are the salt of the earth”; and (530) through his apostle, the Chosen Vessel: “Let your speech be seasoned with salt.” Therefore make this salt exorcized, so that you may be for the remission of sins and the health of minds, for the protection of soul and body, and for the strengthening of salvation; to drive away and exclude all temptations of demons, in the name of God the almighty Father, and of Jesus Christ his Son, and of the Holy Spirit, living throughout the ages of ages. [Col. 0155B]

### Blessing of the Salt

We beseech the unconquerable strength of your power, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God. Among all the necessities which you commanded to be created through Jesus Christ our Lord, you deigned to grant salt no small grace, so that by it all the things might be seasoned which you created through the same Son, our Lord, for food for everyone. Therefore we humbly implore you to regard this salt, so that through the power of your Majesty it may receive strength against every unclean spirit. Let it drive from every place where it has been sprinkled at your invocation whatever may be harmful, so that it may display the full effect of salvation. Let it frighten away every deception of the enemy and cause every kind of monstrous thing to flee far away. (531) Let it restrain every heaviness and every phantom, and through the sign of the cross of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, grant the most faithful protection to those who desire it. He lives and reigns with you as God.

(532) Salt and ash are mixed; and, making the sign of the cross over the water three times with it, he says this prayer:

### Let Us Pray

(533) Eternal and almighty God, who distinguished for us, in faith, the creature of water created by you, so that it might provide simple liquid for washing and salty solidity for seasoning—so that filth might be washed away and the foolish might be imbued, original guilt removed and error corrected toward the way of salvation—we, by the performance of our undeserving office, humbly beseech you: may this mixture of salt and water, made in your name, be sanctified by the regard of your mercy. Whatever it symbolically supplies as beneficial for baptism, hostile to the transmission of guilt, suited to wisdom, and opposed to error, make sanctified through the holiness of your Holy Spirit; and let no contagion make unclean what we believe has been made blessed by your Majesty. Rather, through you, may it provide the full effect of sanctification, so that wherever it is released by hand after your name has been invoked, or taken in by any means, once every ambush of the opposing power has been expelled and scattered, and all the devices of demons have been driven away and brought to an end from that place, the protection of the holy angels may always remain established there. Through.

Then wine is mixed with water, and he says this prayer:

### Let Us Pray

(535) Creator and preserver of the human race, giver of spiritual grace, bestower of eternal salvation, you, O Lord, (536) send your Holy Spirit upon this wine mixed with water, so that (537), armed with the power of heavenly defense, they may be of benefit for the consecration of this church or altar. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

(538) Then, with the water itself, he makes the sign of the cross with his finger on the right-hand side, (539) over the four corners of the altar. Then, coming before the altar, (540) with hyssop he sprinkles the altar seven times while singing the Antiphon “Sprinkle me, Lord, with hyssop, and I shall be clean” [Col. 0156B], with the Psalm itself. He goes around the altar, sprinkling it. Then, on the right-hand side, along the walls of the church, (542) until, coming before the altar, he again sprinkles above and around the altar, (543) singing the Antiphon “Let God arise,” with the Psalm itself. Then, coming again before the altar, he sprinkles above and around the church, (544) singing the Antiphon “The Lord has sanctified his tabernacle, for this is it,” the Psalm “God, our God,” and “Behold, now.” He sends two or three ministers or clerics to sing the Psalm outside the church walls with one voice. Meanwhile the bishop goes from the altar, sprinkling through the length and breadth of the church, (546) making a cross on the pavement with the Antiphon “My house shall be called a house of prayer,” with the Verse “I will declare your name to my brethren.” Also the Verse “Lord, I have loved,” with the Gloria. Coming to the middle of the church, he says, “Let us pray.” The deacon says, “Let us bend our knees,” and afterward says, “Rise.” Then he says the Prayer.

(547) O God, who sanctify places dedicated to your name, pour your grace of sanctification upon this house, so that all who invoke you here may experience the assistance of your mercy. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Again he says, “Let us pray,” and the deacon, “Let us bend our knees”; afterward he says, “Rise.” (548) Then follows the prayer:

God of sanctifications, almighty ruler, whose mercy is felt without end; God, who governs heavenly and earthly things alike, preserving your mercy for your people who walk before the sight of your glory: hear the prayers of your servants, so that your eyes may be open over this house day and night. In your most merciful compassion dedicate this basilica, established in honor of holy [N.], for sacred mysteries; illuminate it in mercy and make it radiant with your own splendor. Graciously admit every person who comes here to worship; mercifully deign to regard them; and, for the sake of your great name, your strong hand, and your exalted arm, willingly protect those who beseech you in this dwelling, graciously hear them, and preserve them by eternal defense, so that, always happy and always rejoicing in your worship, they may steadfastly persevere in the Catholic faith of the Holy Trinity. Through our Lord Jesus Christ your Son, who lives and reigns with you as God in the unity of that same Trinity.

(549) When this has been completed, he begins the Antiphon “I will go in to the altar of my God,” singing it with the Psalm itself. He goes before the altar (550) and pours at its base whatever remains of the water. The altar is wiped with a linen cloth; (551) afterward incense is offered, and he places oil upon the altar, (552) making a cross in the middle and over the four corners while singing the Antiphon “Jacob erected,” with the Psalm (553) “Its foundations.” (554) He anoints the stone with his own hand, while another priest continually incenses around the altar. After (555) the Psalm has been completed, he again places oil in the same way as before, singing the Antiphon “Jacob, rising in the morning” [Col. 0157B], with the Psalm “It is good to give thanks to the Lord.” When it is completed, (557) he places chrism in the same way, singing the Antiphon “Behold, the fragrance of my Son,” with the Psalm “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem.” Also the Antiphon “The Lord has anointed you,” with the Psalm “My heart has uttered.” Then, around the church walls, from right to right, he makes a cross with his thumb using the chrism itself, with the Antiphon “The Lord has sanctified,” the Psalm “Great is the Lord,” and “Behold, now.” He also says the Antiphon “Precious stones,” with the Psalm “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem.” (559) Then, making a cross of incense over the altar, he says, “Let us pray.” The deacon responds as above. And he says the Prayer over the altar:

Let us implore the mercy of God the almighty Father, dearest brothers, so that, moved by the office of our voice, he may sanctify this altar, which is to be consecrated for spiritual sacrifices, by the present blessing; so that he may deign always to bless and sanctify upon it the offerings of his servants, placed there through the zeal of their devotion; and, appeased by spiritual incense, may he stand ready to hear the prayers of his family. Through our Lord Jesus Christ your Son, who is to come. Again he says, “Let us pray.” The deacon responds as above.

### The Blessing Follows

Almighty God, in whose honor we, unworthy, consecrate this altar under the invocation of your name, mercifully and graciously hear the prayers of our humility. Grant that upon this table there may be offerings acceptable, pleasing, and rich to you, always moistened with the dew of your Holy Spirit, so that at every time and in this place you may relieve the anxieties of your family supplicating you, cure illnesses, hear prayers, receive vows, confirm desires, and grant requests. Through [Col. 0157D] the Lord.

Then he says the Antiphon “Confirm this, O God,” with the Gloria.

(561) Then, while the subdeacons or acolytes hold the linens, or all the ornaments of the church, or whatever sacred vessels appear to belong to the worship of God and the church, the bishop blesses them.

### Blessing for the Linens or for Everything Used in the Basilica
