(563) Almighty and merciful God, who from the beginning created useful and necessary things for human beings, who willed that temples made by human hands should be dedicated to your holy name and called places of your dwelling, and who through your servant Moses decreed that episcopal, priestly, and Levitical vestments, as well as ornaments of every other kind, should be made for the worship and adornment of your tabernacle and altar: graciously hear our prayers, and through the service of our humility deign to purify, sanctify, bless, and consecrate all these ornaments of various kinds, prepared for the use of this basilica or altar and for your honor and glory, (564) so that they may be suitable for divine worship and sacred ministries, and so that they may be used in worthy service for the making of the body and blood of Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord. He lives and reigns with you.

### Another Prayer

(565) Almighty and eternal God, from whom all unclean things are purified and in whom all purified things shine forth, we, your suppliant servants, invoke your omnipotence: let every confused unclean spirit depart far from this vessel or garment which your servants, [N.], offer to you; and, through the blessing of faith, let these things be perfected for your holy altar and remain sanctified and useful for the work of your ministry, with you as helper. Through our Lord Jesus.

(566) [Note: [Col. 0157D] This blessing is found in nearly the same words in the ancient Gallican Sacramentary.]

### Blessing over a Gift Offered by Someone to the Church

God, by whose word and power all things were made, and by whose gift we receive the things we possess for the remedy of life, we earnestly beseech you: come from the seat of your Majesty as sanctifier to this offering of the faithful. Receive from the hand of your servants, [N.], the gift offered, which, blessed by your mercy, may remain consecrated for the use of this sanctuary of yours. May these things be willingly accepted in your sight, as once the gifts of Abel, your fosterling, and of Melchizedek were pleasing to you when offered. And because, for love of your honor, they strive to adorn your church with the highest acts of service, recompense them greatly, O Lord, for small things: receiving their devotion, forgive their sins, fill them with faith, cherish them with pardon, protect them with mercy, destroy adversities, and grant prosperity. May they have in this age an example of good action, zeal for charity, and the effect of holy love; and in the future may they attain the everlasting kingdom with the holy angels. Through the Lord.

151 **Another Prayer**

Hear us, O Lord, we beseech you, and deign to bless and sanctify these linens and other garments, as well as the vessels prepared for your holy altar, your church, and every use of the sacred ministry. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

### For Consecrating the Paten

(568) We consecrate and sanctify this paten, [Note: [Col. 0158D] In the two Theodorian manuscripts: “For breaking upon it the body,” etc.] for preparing upon it the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, who suffered the cross for the salvation of us all, who lives and reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

(569) Then, making the sign of the cross with holy oil over the paten, he says:

May you deign, O Lord, to consecrate and sanctify this paten through this anointing and our blessing, in Christ Jesus our Lord, who live, etc.

### Blessing of the Paten

(570) Lord God almighty, who through your servant Moses consecrated the altar of your tabernacle and all the vessels to divine worship, we humbly beseech your mercy: make this vessel suitable for your worship and worthy of your altars, so that, sanctified in your name, it may be appointed as the precious dish of your body. You live and reign with the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

### For Blessing the Chalice

(571) [Note: [Col. 0159D] This Prayer and the following two are found in both Theodorian manuscripts.]

Let us pray, dearest brothers, that the Lord our God may sanctify the chalice, which is to be consecrated for the use of his ministry, through the inspiration of heavenly grace, and may adapt it to human blessing by the fullness of divine favor. Through the Lord.

### Another Prayer

Let us pray. Deign, O Lord, to pour upon this chalice, fashioned for the use of your ministry through the devout piety of your servant, [N.], the sanctification with which you poured out the sacred chalice of your servant Melchizedek. May what cannot be made worthy of your altars by craftsmanship or metal become precious through your blessing. Through.

### Another Prayer

(573) [Note: [Col. 0159D] In the ancient Gallican Sacramentary this Prayer, with some alterations, is used for the blessing of the chalice and paten, and also of the tower. The purpose of this tower was to carry the sacred ministry. Mabillon teaches in *The Gallican Liturgy* and in his commentary on the *Roman Ordo*, §20, that Christ’s body itself was customarily carried in the tower; this view is confirmed by Gregory of Tours, *On the Glory of the Martyrs*, book I, chapter 86: “And taking the tower, in which the mystery of the Lord’s body was contained.”]

God, who on Mount Horeb, when arranging precepts to be observed by your people through your servant Moses, instructed how your holy temple should be built, and also taught which sacred vessels were to be brought to your altar, modeled on the heavenly vessels: we beseech you to sanctify this chalice, in which we are to celebrate the most sacred mysteries, with the heavenly blessing of the outpouring of your Holy Spirit. Regard it as pleasing and acceptable, and bless it; joined worthily to your vessels, may it offer acceptable service and be worthily consecrated to your mysteries. Through our Lord Jesus Christ your Son.

(574) Then they go to the place where the relics were kept during the preceding night with vigils, and they lift them up.

152 **Prayer When the Relics Are Lifted**

Let us pray. (575) Take away from us, we beseech you, O Lord, our iniquities, so that we may deserve to enter the holy of holies with pure minds. Through the Lord.

### Another Prayer

Make us worthy, O Lord, to touch the specially dedicated members of your saints, whose patronage we desire to have without ceasing. Through the Lord.

When this prayer has been completed, let them lift the relics with their bier, singing with great honor these Antiphons: (576) “Walk, saints of God”; the Antiphon “From Jerusalem”; the Antiphon “Behold the people”; and the Antiphon “With rejoicing” (577)—with crosses, censers, candlesticks, and many lights. Let them come to the basilica in which the relics are to be deposited, and as soon as they have set foot inside, let him say this Prayer:

[Col. 0160A]

Let us pray. (578) Enter your house mercifully, we beseech you, O Lord, and establish an everlasting dwelling for yourself in the hearts of your faithful, so that it which stands through your building may become glorious through your indwelling. Through the Lord.

### Another Prayer

Let us pray. O God, author of the gifts consecrated to you, pour your blessing upon this house of prayer, so that all who invoke your name here may experience the help of your protection. Through our Lord Jesus Christ the Son.

Then let them proceed to the altar where the relics are to be placed. (579) With a veil extended between them and the people, let the bishop place the relics in the altar with his own hand, (580) singing the Antiphon “The saints shall rejoice in glory” [Col. 0160B], with the Psalm “Praise the Lord from the heavens.” Also the Antiphon “Sing to the Lord a new song,” with the same Psalm. Also the Antiphon “You have received seats beneath God’s altar,” with the Psalm “Praise the Lord in his saints.” When this has been completed, let him say this prayer:

Let us pray. O God, who from the harmonious joining of all the saints build for yourself an eternal dwelling, grant heavenly growth to your building, so that we who embrace their relics here with devout love may always be assisted by their merits. Through the Lord.

(582) After this the altar is clothed (583) with the Antiphon “In the shelter of your wings,” and the Psalm “My God, to you I keep vigil at dawn.” Then let this Prayer be said:

Let us pray. May your Holy Spirit descend, we beseech you, Lord our God [Col. 0160C], upon this altar, sanctifying the gifts of your people and graciously cleansing the hearts of those who receive them. Through the Lord.

Then (584) let the bishop return to the sacristy with his attendants, and let them put on other solemn vestments. Meanwhile let the church be adorned and many lights kindled; and let the cantor begin the Introit Antiphon: “How awesome is this place.” Let the bishop proceed from the sacristy with his attendants, as is customary on feast days. (585) Mass shall be celebrated there solemnly, in the customary manner and order, with “Glory to God in the highest.” (586) Throughout the entire week public Masses shall be celebrated in the church.

## Prayers for Masses at the Dedication of a Church

God, who invisibly contain all things and yet visibly display the signs of your power for the salvation of the human race, illuminate this temple with the Majesty of your indwelling, so that all who come here to pray, and cry out to you from whatever tribulation, may receive the benefits of your consolation. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Almighty and eternal God, sanctify the altar dedicated to your name with the blessing of heavenly power, and show the gift of your help to all who hope in you, so that here the power of the sacraments and the fulfillment of vows may be obtained. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: through whom we humbly beseech you to sanctify this altar, prepared for holy uses, by heavenly dedication. And just as you received with wondrous favor the offering of Melchizedek, the preeminent priest, so may you deign always to regard as acceptable the gifts placed upon this new altar, so that the people who have gathered into this holy house of the Church, saved through these offerings by heavenly sanctification, may also attain the perpetual salvation of their souls. Through whom your Majesty [is praised].

### Another Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: although you are wholly present everywhere and contain all things with your entire Majesty, you nevertheless willed that places suited to your mysteries should be consecrated to you, so that the houses of prayer themselves might rouse the minds of suppliants to invoke your name. Pour your grace, we beseech you, upon this place, and show the gift of your help to all who invoke you, so that here the power of the sacraments may strengthen the hearts of all the faithful. Through the same Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0161D] The Benedictional does not contain this blessing.]

### Blessing

May the almighty Lord bless and keep you, and may he deign to illuminate this house by the presence of his gift and to open over it the eyes of his mercy day and night. Amen.

And may he graciously grant that all of you who have devoutly gathered for the dedication of this basilica, with blessed [N.] and his other saints interceding—whose relics are venerated here among you with devout love—may be able to carry away from here the forgiveness of your sins. Amen.

Thus, through their intervention, may you yourselves be made a temple of the Holy Spirit, in which the holy God, the Trinity, may deign continually to dwell, and, after the course of this fleeting life, may you deserve happily to reach eternal joys. Amen.

May he himself deign to grant this.

154 ### At the Conclusion

We beseech you, almighty God, that in this place, which we unworthy have dedicated to your name, you may incline the ears of your mercy to all who ask. Through.

### Another Prayer

Trusting in the prayers of your saints, we beseech you to grant that through what we have received we may obtain eternal remedies. Through.

### Over the People

May the Christian people obtain abundant benefits, we beseech you, O Lord, so that those who devotedly come to you at the sacred thresholds consecrated in honor of your saints may receive the supports of the present life and find the grace of eternal redemption. Through.

### Another Prayer

Grant strength to your people, O Lord, and make us a temple of the Holy Spirit, so that we may prepare for you an acceptable holocaust from a pure heart. Through.

(587) **ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE DEDICATION OF A BASILICA**

O God, who each year renew for us the day of the consecration of this holy temple of yours, and continually represent us unharmed in the sacred mysteries, hear the prayers of your people [Col. 0162A], and grant that whoever enters this temple to seek benefits may rejoice that all have been obtained. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Grant our prayers, we beseech you, O Lord, so that all of us who are enclosed within the bounds of this temple, whose anniversary of dedication we celebrate, may please you with complete and perfect devotion of body and soul; and, while we render these present vows, may we deserve, with your help, to reach eternal rewards. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and to render you due honor for the yearly devotion owed to this tabernacle, through Christ our Lord, whose power is great and whose mercy abundant. Look down, we beseech you, from heaven, see, and visit this house, so that if anyone supplicates your name here, you may willingly hear and willingly forgive those who make satisfaction. Here let your priests offer you the sacrifice of praise; here let the faithful people fulfill their vows; here let the burdens of sins be laid down; here let holy faith be strengthened; here let perfect devotion return; here let corrected wickedness depart. May whoever comes here seeking refuge in satisfaction, overcome by conscious grief and washing your altars with streams of tears, find with you, O Lord, a place of pardon. Here, if your people ever gather sad and sorrowful, consent to be entreated and, when entreated, forgive those who ask. Through whom.

### At the Conclusion

Multiply, O Lord, we beseech you, through these holy things which we have received, your truth in our hands, so that we may continually adore you in the holy temple and glory in your sight with the holy angels. Through.

155 ### Over the Offerings

O God, who have deigned to call your Church the bride of your Only-Begotten, and who granted that she should have grace through devotion of faith and also have piety from the name itself, grant that all this people serving your name may deserve to be worthy of sharing this title. And may your Church, gathered to you in the temple whose anniversary of dedication is celebrated, fear you, love you, and follow you, so that, while it continually walks in your footsteps, it may deserve to reach the heavenly promises under your guidance. You who live and reign with [the Father].

(588) **ON THE VIGIL OF THE APOSTLES**

Grant us, we beseech you, almighty God, to anticipate with fitting honor the approaching solemnity of your apostle, [N.], and to celebrate it when it comes with worthy devotion. Through.

### For the Offerings

May the offering of our devotion be acceptable to you, Lord, and make us come to the apostolic feast purer. Through Christ.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and that, anticipating with due service the coming feast of the birth of your blessed apostle N., we should humbly beseech you to let us experience him as a patron with you in your clemency—the one whom, by the gift of your grace, we have been found worthy to receive as a minister of eternal salvation. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

Grant us, eternal Giver, to be everywhere protected by the prayer of him whose feast we anticipate with votive service through these holy things that we have received. Through.

### At Vespers

May the solemnity of your holy apostle N., Lord, which we are anticipating, protect us, for we appeal to your name with the greater confidence the more frequently we are strengthened by the intercessions of the apostles. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** God, glory of your righteous ones, grant, we beseech you, that we may experience the help of your holy one, N., whose day of passion we anticipate by celebrating it. Through.

### At Matins

God, who are the wondrous splendor of all your saints, and who consecrated this day through the martyrdom of your blessed apostle N., grant that your Church may rejoice in the feast of so great a solemnity, so that she who flourished through the preaching of your apostles may be fortified by their examples and assisted by their intercessions. Through our Lord.

[Note: No Mass from the Common of the Apostles is read here, as below from the Common of Martyrs; perhaps this is because all the apostles had their own Mass.]

## MASS ON THE VIGIL OF ONE MARTYR

We beseech you, almighty God, that our devotion, which precedes the feast of the blessed martyr N., may increase his patronage for us. Through.

### 156. For the Offerings

Lord, we commemorate the solemnity of the blessed N.; approaching it with ready hearts, we both receive and offer beforehand the gifts that have been presented. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and that, anticipating the holy contests of the glorious martyr N., whose solemnity returns each year with honorable observance and is always both everlasting and new—for in the sight of your Majesty the precious death of your righteous ones endures, and the increase of joy is renewed whenever the beginnings of eternal happiness are recalled. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

May your holy things, Lord, refresh us in the precious passion of the blessed martyr N., which we are anticipating—those things by which we are continually nourished and with which we always desire to be filled. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who anticipate the solemnity of your holy martyr N. may also imitate his virtues. Through.

### At Vespers

God, who permit us to anticipate the glorious feast of the birth of your blessed martyr N., grant, we beseech you, that we may always be anticipated by his benefits and assisted by his prayers. Through.

**Another prayer.** God, who permit us to anticipate the feast of your blessed martyr N., grant that we may be assisted by his merits. Through.

### At Matins

Almighty and eternal God, strength of those who contend and crown of martyrs, look favorably upon this day’s solemnity, and cause your Church to rejoice in continual celebration, so that what she does not presume to attain through merits she may be found worthy to obtain through the intercession of your blessed martyr N. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** God, Creator and ruler of the world, who consecrated this day through the martyrdom of N., graciously grant that all who venerate the merits of his martyrdom may be freed through his intercessions from the eternal fires of Gehenna. Through.

## MASS ON THE FEAST OF ONE MARTYR

May the feast of the birth of your blessed martyr N. always receive us in votive devotion, Lord, we beseech you; may it pour into us the joy of his glorification and make us acceptable to you. Through our Lord.

### For the Offerings

Look upon these gifts now present with serene kindness, Lord, we beseech you, so that they may be filled with the blessing of the Holy Spirit and may pour more powerfully into our hearts that love through which the holy martyr N. overcame every torment of the body. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord; and that on this present feast of your holy martyr N. we should confess you by offering sacrifices of praise, and implore your immeasurable kindness: just as you gave him the heavenly palm of triumph, so, with his intercession, grant us amendment and pardon for sin, so that we may rejoice in you through mercy, in whom he rejoices in glory. Through Christ.

**Another Preface.** It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and praise you in the triumphs of all the martyrs. For by your gifts and presents we venerate today the passion of your blessed martyr N.; for confessing Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, he endured various punishments and, overcoming them, earned the crown of perpetuity. Through him.

**Another Preface.** It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. By his grace he chose blessed N. for the priesthood, instructed him through teaching for preaching, and strengthened him through power for perseverance, so that through the priestly insignia he might attain the palm of martyrdom. Teaching his subjects, instructing them by the example of his life, and strengthening them through suffering, he reached you to be crowned, having fearlessly overcome the threats of his persecutors. We beseech you that his intervention may cleanse us from our sins—he who pleased you through so many prerogatives of gifts. Through him, your Majesty.

[Note: This is read in the *Benedictional*, where it is assigned to the feast of one martyr.]

### Blessing

May the Lord bless you through the intercession of his blessed martyr N. and defend you from every evil. Amen. May he extend over you the right hand of his favor, he who received him through the punishments of his passion. Amen. May you be found worthy to share in heaven with him whose triumph you celebrate on earth with devoted hearts. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom—

### At the Conclusion

We have received the heavenly sacraments, Lord, in the solemnity of the holy martyr N.; grant, we beseech you, through his intercessions, that what we undertake in time we may attain in eternal joys. Through.

### Over the People

Grant, we beseech you, Lord our God, that, with your blessed martyr N. interceding, your people may rejoice in devotion to you, for happiness is perpetual and complete if we serve the Author of every good thing. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

### Other Prayers

May the holy prayer of your martyr N., Lord, reconcile us to you; it shines forth as venerable through sacred virtues. Through our Lord.

### 158. Another Prayer

We beseech you, Lord, that we may be assisted by the prayers of your blessed martyr N., and that, worthily celebrating his solemnity, you may make us always devoted to your name. Through.

**Another prayer.** May the patronage granted by your blessed martyr N., Lord, not abandon us; through his prayers and merits may it protect our frailty. Through.

**Another prayer.** God, who have made the holy solemnity of this day for the commemoration of your blessed martyr N., attend to the prayers of your household, and grant that we who celebrate his feast today may be assisted by his merits and intercessions. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** May your people, Lord, magnify you through the glorification of your holy martyr N.; and, with him always praying, may we be found worthy to have you as our ruler. Through our Lord.

## MASS ON THE VIGIL OF MANY MARTYRS

We beseech you, Lord, that your devoted Church may receive the venerable feasts of the birth of the blessed martyrs N. and N., and become more devoted through love of their great glorification. Through.

### For the Offerings

May this Sacrifice, Lord, cleanse our sins, and sanctify the bodies and minds of your subjects for the coming celebration of the feast of so many martyrs, your N. [Note: The Vatican and Gussanville editions read *of the saints*.] Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: giver of mercy and author of every goodness, who grant through fasts, prayers, and almsgiving remedies for sins and increases of every virtue. We pray to you with humble devotion: since you gave your saints N., whose feasts we anticipate, the crown of martyrdom, grant us through their intercessions tireless effectiveness for carrying out these observances. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

Feed us everywhere, Lord, with the joys of your saints, for our salvation is increased whenever honor is offered to those in whom you are proclaimed wonderful. Through.

### Over the People

Protect your people, Lord, and by the prayers of the righteous grant that the people whom you have made devoted through the continual feast of your martyrs N. may always become pleasing to you. Through.

**Another prayer.** May the offerings of our fast be pleasing to you, Lord, we beseech you, for we present them worthily in the commemoration of the saints N. only if we likewise follow their deeds. Through.

### 159. Another Prayer

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that your people may be prepared by the feasts of the birth of the blessed martyrs N. for the affection of complete devotion, and that, through the favor won by their patronage, they may receive an increase of complete security. Through the Lord.

**Another prayer.** God, who permit us to attend each year the solemnities of the blessed martyrs N., grant, we beseech you, that we may celebrate them with devoted hearts and be assisted by their intercessions. Through our Lord.

### At Matins

God, who consecrated this day through the martyrdom of your saints N., grant us health of mind and body, so that the passion of those saints may be honored through our devotion and help may come to us from their most holy intercession. Through.

## ON THE FEAST OF MANY MARTYRS

Almighty and eternal God, who raised martyrs through the battles of glorious combat to immortal triumphs, grant our hearts fitting joy for their commemoration, so that we who embrace their memory with devoted love may be assisted by their prayers.

### For the Offerings

We offer you, Lord, the gifts of our devotion. May they be pleasing to you in honor of your righteous ones, and, by your mercy, may they be made salutary for us. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: you who lead the holy contests of your martyrs to abundant victory and grant them everlasting triumph, so that they may always be examples for your Church. Grant us, we beseech you, through the intercession of those whose feasts we celebrate, to receive the gifts of your mercy. Through Christ.

### Blessing

[Note: In the *Benedictional*, where these words are found, the reading is “may the Lord bless you.”]

May the Lord bless you through the intercession of his blessed martyrs N. and free you from every adversity. Amen. May their glorious intercession commend you to him, in whose sight the death of his saints is precious. Amen. Just as they received the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom through various kinds of torments, so may you be found worthy to share in their fellowship through the practice of good works. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

### At the Conclusion

Grant us, Lord, we beseech you, that what we have accomplished for the blessed passion of your martyrs N. may become salutary for us through their intercession, in whose feasts these things have been joyfully fulfilled. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** Almighty and eternal God, who kindle the flame of your love in the hearts of your saints, grant our minds the same virtue of faith and charity, so that we who rejoice in their triumphs may advance through their examples. Through.

**Another prayer.** Extend the right hand of your Majesty, Lord, for the defense of the faithful, we beseech you, and, so that they may be fortified by the perpetual protection of your mercy, may the continued intercession of the holy martyrs never be lacking for them. Through.

**Another prayer.** Almighty and merciful God, light of the souls of the faithful, graciously attend to the prayers of today’s solemnity, and favorably breathe upon your Church’s joys conceived from the glory of the blessed martyrs N., so that our hearts may be inflamed by their passion and we may be assisted before your mercy by the merits of those whose examples gladden us. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we may share also in the rewards of the holy martyrs whose victories we celebrate. Through our Lord.

## ON THE VIGIL OF ONE CONFESSOR

### 161

Grant us, we beseech you, almighty God, to anticipate with fitting honor the coming solemnity of your blessed confessor N. and to celebrate it when it comes with worthy devotion. Through our Lord.

### For the Offerings

May the offering of our devotion be acceptable to you, Lord, and make us come purer to the feast of your holy confessor N. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and humbly entreat your Majesty that we who anticipate the feast of your blessed confessor N. with solemn fasts and devoted observances may be assisted by his merits before your Majesty and instructed by his examples. Through.

Having been entreated by the intercessions of your blessed confessor N., Lord, defend us through the power of your sacrament, which we have received. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

May we receive the grace of your blessing, Lord, with your holy confessor N. interceding, so that, while we celebrate in advance the glory of him whose help we implore, we may experience it. Through our Lord.

### At Vespers

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the examples of your holy confessor N. may summon us to a better life, so that we may imitate the deeds of him whose solemnity we anticipate and be assisted by his intercessions. Through.

**Another prayer.** Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that just as we anticipate the glorious feast of the birth of your confessor N., so he may anticipate us before your Majesty in obtaining your benefits for us. Through.

### At Matins

Attend to your people, Lord, so that, receiving the illustrious merits of your blessed confessor N., they may always be assisted by his patronage and merits in obtaining your mercy. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** Absolve the sins of your peoples, Lord, we beseech you, and, with your blessed confessor N. interceding, free us from the bonds of sins that we have contracted through our frailty. Through our Lord.

## MASS ON THE FEAST OF ONE CONFESSOR

### 162

Mercifully bestow your mercy upon us, Lord, we beseech you, with your blessed confessor N. intervening, and be favorable to us sinners through his intercessions. Through.

### For the Offerings

Be favorable, Lord, we beseech you, to our supplications, and, with your holy confessor N. intervening for us, grant that, serving you through these heavenly sacraments, we may be free from every fault, so that, as your grace purifies us, we may be cleansed by the same mysteries in which we serve. Through.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and on this day, which you consecrated through the holy passing of your blessed confessor N., we therefore beseech your clemency: grant us to follow the teaching that he both taught in word and fulfilled in deed, so that we may experience his examples and merits assisting us before your mercy. Through Christ our Lord.

**Another Preface.** It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and praise you in the virtue of your saints, to whom you have granted the rewards of blessedness according to their merits. For they are always in your hand, and the torment of death will not touch those whom, while you guard them, the bosom of blessedness encloses; there they rejoice forever with perpetual exultation, and there your blessed confessor N. also rejoices in fellowship with them. We therefore ask that he may remember our miseries and obtain for us from your mercy a share in his blessedness. Through Christ.

### Blessing

May almighty God grant you an abundance of blessing—he who took blessed N. to himself through the power of confession. Amen. And may he who made him shine with miracles adorn you with an increase of good works. Amen. Thus, instructed by his examples and strengthened by his intercession, may you be able to be joined in the heavenly region to him whose day of burial you celebrate. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

### At the Conclusion

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, giving thanks for the gifts we have received, we may obtain greater benefits through the intercession of your blessed confessor N. Through.

### Over the People

Incline the ears of your mercy, Lord, to our prayers, so that we who are struck by the scourges of our sins may, with your blessed confessor N. interceding, be freed by the grace of your compassion. Through.

**Another prayer.** Protect us, we beseech you, Lord, by the safeguards of your holy confessor N., so that we may always be assisted by his intercessions. Through.

**Another prayer.** Attend, Lord, we beseech you, to our prayers, which we offer in the commemoration of your holy confessor N., so that we who have no confidence in our own righteousness may be assisted by the prayers of him who pleased you. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** Let us rejoice, we beseech you, Lord our God, in the solemnity of your blessed confessor N., so that, celebrating his holy feast, we may always be assisted by his patronage in obtaining your mercy. Through.

**Another prayer.** Almighty and eternal God, to whom all the elements serve, graciously hear our prayer, with your confessor N. interceding for us, and grant us your mercy; and whatever you command us to do, help us yourself to fulfill. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** Grant us, Lord, to be strengthened by the supplications of your holy confessor N., so that we whose annual observance celebrates his burial may be assisted before you by his intercessions and merits. Through.

### 163

As we anticipate the feasts of the birth of your blessed confessors N., Lord, we humbly ask you to grant that those whom you have exalted in heavenly glory may be present to your faithful. Through.

May the sacrifice that our devotion offers for your blessed confessors N. increase for us, by your gift, the help provided through their merits. Through.

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: as we anticipate the solemnity of your saints N., graciously grant that those who became so glorious through your gifts may be suitable intercessors for us before you. Through Christ.

We beseech you, Lord, that, filled with saving mysteries, we may be assisted by the prayers of those whose solemnity we anticipate. Through.

Preserve your household, Lord, we beseech you, and graciously purify it with the abundance of your blessings, so that through the intercession of your blessed confessors N. it may always increase through your teachings and gifts. Through our Lord.

Through.

**Another prayer.** God, who have made your blessed confessors N. equal in merit with your saints, grant us to rejoice in their celebration, so that we may advance through imitation of those whose commemoration we observe and be raised up by their intercessions. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## ON THE FEAST OF MANY CONFESSORS

Grant, Lord, we beseech you, that just as the feasts of the birth of your saints N. do not abandon us when they are celebrated, so they may continually accompany us through their intercessions. Through.

### For the Offerings

May the gifts of your people, Lord, we beseech you, become pleasing through the intercessions of your blessed confessors N.; and, since they are offered to your name for their triumphs, may they be completed worthily through their merits. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and humbly entreat your Majesty that through the favor of your blessed confessors N., whose feasts we celebrate today, we may be found worthy to obtain your help. Through Christ.

**Another Preface.** It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and glorify you in honor of your saints N., who granted them everlasting blessedness for their steadfastness in combat and provided such intercessions for our weakness that, through their merits, you may graciously hear us. Through Christ.

[Note: The same words occur in the *Benedictional* for the feast of many confessors.]

### Blessing

May the Lord cause you to be blessed through the merits of his holy confessors N., and fortify you against every adversity through their intercession. Amen. May he make you happy through the help of those whose feast you joyfully celebrate. Amen. Thus, imitating their examples, may you be able to attain the heavenly promises. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

### 164. At the Conclusion

Strengthened both by the feasts of the saints and by the sacramental gift, Lord, we beseech you to grant that we may enjoy eternally the good things by which we are now refreshed through your grace. Through our Lord.

### Over the People

Attend, Lord, to the prayers of your people who supplicate you with the patronage of your saints N., so that what they do not presume to obtain through their own confidence they may attain through the merits of those who assist them. Through.

**Another prayer.** Magnifying your mercy, Lord, we humbly entreat you: since you grant us to participate in the frequent feasts of your saints, grant us also to participate in their everlasting fellowship. Through.

**Another prayer.** Grant us, almighty God, always to praise you in the commemoration of your saints, for you will take care to refresh those whom you permit to persevere in your honor. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** We implore the intercessions of your saints N., Lord, so that we may be freed from every offense. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** Hear us, almighty and merciful God, and everywhere protect us by the safeguards of your saints. Through.

**Another prayer.** Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that your saints may continually pray for us; and may you always graciously deign to hear them. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** May your saints, Lord, continually ask you both for pardon and for progress on our behalf. Through.

## ON THE VIGIL OF VIRGINS

Grant that we may be strengthened, Lord, by the supplications of your holy martyr N., so that, while we anticipate her venerable solemnity with our observance, we may be commended through her intercessions and merits. Through Christ.

### For the Offerings

We anticipate the feast of your holy martyr N. with our gifts, Lord. Grant, we beseech you, that what is hindered by the obstacles of our sins may be made acceptable through her merits. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and, anticipating the feast of the birth of blessed N., to praise, proclaim, and bless you for her whom you exalted with so great a gift that you bestowed upon her both the crown of virginity and the palm of martyrdom. We beseech you that her intervention may cleanse us from our sins and make us share in the fellowship of the citizens above. Through Christ.

### 165. Another Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God; and, anticipating the feast of the birth of blessed N., to praise, proclaim, and bless you for her whom you exalted with so great a gift that you bestowed upon her the crown of virginity and the palm of martyrdom. Thus she flourished in the power of faith and the beauty of chastity, so that as both virgin and martyr she entered the heavenly kingdom. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

We beseech you, almighty God, that you make us true imitators of those whose memories you grant us to share. Through.

## ON THE FEAST OF VIRGINS

God, who among the other miracles of your power also bestowed the victory of martyrdom upon the weaker sex, graciously grant that we may walk toward you by the example of her whose feast we celebrate. Through our Lord.

### For the Offerings

On the precious feast of the holy virgin N., proclaiming your wonders, Lord, we bring votive gifts. Grant, we beseech you, that just as her merits are pleasing to you, so the services of our devotion may be made acceptable. Through our Lord.

### Preface

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Blessed N., both virgin and martyr, feared him and loved him, and loved him through fearing him; she was joined to him by dying, to whom she had consecrated herself by living chastely; and for his sake strove to endure temporal punishment, so that she might receive eternal glory from him.

When she desired to receive a double palm in the contest of sacred combat—both for bodily integrity and for purity of faith—she judged it more arduous to endure the long temptations of the ancient enemy than quickly to lose the present life through torments. For while the prospect of martyrdom presents things that terrify, the pleasures of the flesh present things that soothe; the hidden enemy is endured with greater difficulty than the openly hostile one is overcome.

Since, therefore, in both victories it is your gift that she conquered—for human frailty is powerless unless your mercy helps it—may she who received from you the power to conquer intercede for us, we beseech you, with your mercy. And may she who was found worthy to enter the bridal chamber of your Only-Begotten, through her intercession, grant us help amid the adversities of this world. Through him, your Majesty.

**Another Preface.** It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Through the ardor of his love, she and all the holy virgins, receiving from blessed Mary the example of virginity, despised the pleasures and delights of the present age.

For it was accomplished by your gift that, after the Virgin came forth from the Virgin, the weaker sex became strong, and that where there had been an ease of sinning, there was the happiness of conquering. And may the ancient enemy, who boasted that through the ancient virgin he had conquered the human race, now be overcome through the holy virgins, who are followers of Mary rather than of Eve. Let his confusion increase all the more because even the weaker sex now triumphs over him.

Therefore we humbly ask your immeasurable mercy, so that through the intercession of those who overcame both their sex and the world, and pleased you both by the beauty of virginity and the strength of suffering, we may be found worthy both to overcome the invisible enemy and to cling to your Only-Begotten, our Lord. Through him, your Majesty.

[Note: This blessing is assigned in the *Benedictional* to the feast of one virgin, and the following one to the feast of many virgins.]

### Blessing

May the Lord bless you, he who granted blessed N. both the beauty of virginity and the glory of suffering. Amen. By whose help she was found worthy to overcome both the weakness of her sex and the fury of her persecutor; may you likewise be able to overcome both the allurements of your bodies and the schemes of the ancient enemy. Amen. Just as she, though of the weaker sex, strove to enter manly combat and, after the contest, to triumph over her enemies, so may you, while living in this mortality, be able to overcome the ancient enemy and reach the heavenly kingdoms. Amen. May he himself grant this.

**Another Blessing.** May almighty God deign to bless you, with his holy virgins N. interceding—he who willed to triumph over the ancient enemy not only through men but also through women. Amen. And may he who willed to grant them the fruit yielding a hundredfold through the beauty of virginity and the contest of martyrdom deign both to cleanse you from the filth of vices and to adorn you with the lamps of virtues. Amen. Thus may the lamps of your hearts be filled so completely with the oil of virtue that with them you may be able to enter the bridal chamber of the heavenly Bridegroom. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom and dominion—

### Another Prayer at the Conclusion

May the mysteries we have received assist us, Lord, and, with your blessed martyr N. interceding, strengthen us with eternal protection. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** May blessed N., your martyr, who was always pleasing to you through the merit of chastity and the confession of your power, implore pardon for us, Lord. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son.

### 599. Another Mass

God, who gladden us today with the annual solemnity of your holy virgin N., graciously grant that we may be assisted by the merits of her whose examples of chastity enlighten us. Through our Lord.

### For the Offerings

May this offering of your people be pleasing to you, Lord, which we offer in honor of your holy virgin N.; may it benefit all for salvation. Through.

### At the Conclusion

May these holy mysteries that we have received, and the venerable intercession of your blessed virgin N., assist us, Lord, we beseech you. Through.

## 167. Blessing of a Virgin’s or Widow’s Garments

God, most faithful Promiser and most certain Fulfiller of eternal goods, who promised your faithful a saving garment and clothing of everlasting joy, we humbly beseech your clemency: graciously + bless these garments, which signify humility of heart and contempt for the world, and by which your servant N. is visibly to be formed for a holy purpose. May she preserve unharmed, under your protection, the habit of blessed chastity that she has received at your inspiration; and may you cause her whom you clothe temporarily in the garments of a venerable profession to be clothed with blessed immortality. Through our Lord.

**Another prayer.** God, giver of good virtues and generous pourer-out of every blessing, hear our prayers, and deign to + bless and sanctify this garment, with which your servant N. asks to be covered as a sign of preserving chastity. Through the Lord.

### Blessing of a Virgin’s Garment

Hear our prayers, almighty God, and drench this garment, with which your servant N. asks to be covered, with the rain of the richest blessing, just as you drenched the edges of Aaron’s garments with blessing flowing from the head down upon the beard like ointment. And just as you blessed the garments of all religious persons who please you in every respect, so deign to bless this garment; and grant, most merciful Father, that for the aforementioned servant of yours this garment may be a salutary protection, a knowledge of religion, a beginning of holiness, and a strong defense against every weapon of the enemy, so that she may be enriched by the abundance of the hundredfold gift through persevering continence. Through our Lord.

### 601. Blessing of a Virgin to Be Pronounced by a [602] Bishop

[603] This is performed at Epiphany, [604] or on Easter Monday, or [605] whenever the feasts of the apostles are celebrated; [606] and they wear black garments externally.

[Col. 0173D] Look favorably, Lord, upon this servant of yours N., so that she may preserve, under your guidance, the purpose of holy virginity that she has undertaken at your inspiration. Through.

### Consecration

God, gracious inhabitant of chaste bodies and lover of incorrupt souls, who restore in your Word, through whom all things were made, the human substance corrupted in the first human beings by the devil’s deceit—restoring it not only to the innocence of its first origin, but also leading it to the experience of certain goods that are to be possessed in the new age—and who already raise those still bound by mortal condition to the likeness of angels: look upon this servant of yours N., who offers her devotion to you, from whom she herself also received this same vow.

Let there be in her, Lord, through the gift of your Spirit, prudent modesty, wise kindness, dignified gentleness, and chaste freedom. Let her burn with love and love nothing apart from you. Let her live commendably and not desire to be praised. Let her fear you and serve you with love. Be her honor, her joy, her consolation in sorrow, her counsel in uncertainty, her defense in injury, her patience in tribulation, her abundance in poverty, her food in fasting, and her medicine in sickness.

Through you, whom she desires to love above all things, may she preserve what she has professed, so that she may overcome the ancient enemy and cleanse away the filth of vices; and thus, by your gift, may she be found worthy to be adorned with the hundredfold fruit of virginity, decorated with the lamps of virtues, and joined to the fellowship of your chosen virgins. Through the same one.

## MASS FOR THE CONSECRATION OF A VIRGIN

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, to your servant N., whom you have deigned to adorn with the honor of virginity, the consummated effect of the work begun; and grant that, in order to offer you complete fullness, she may be found worthy to bring her beginnings to their end. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Having offered these sacrifices, O Lord, we beseech you, grant your handmaid Ill. perseverance in perpetual virginity, so that, when the doors are opened at the coming of the supreme King, she may deserve to enter the heavenly kingdom with joy. Through him.

[Col. 0174C] **At the Conclusion.**—Look upon the dutiful service of your handmaid Ill., O Lord, so that amid the uncertainties of human frailty she may not be overcome by any adversities, since she trusts in your protection. Through him.

### Prayer for Making an Abbess

Hear our prayers, O Lord, and send upon this handmaid of yours Ill. the Spirit of your blessing, so that, enriched by a heavenly gift, she may be able both to obtain the grace of your Majesty and to offer others an example of good living. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

### Prayer for Veiling the Handmaids of God

(613) [Note: In the old Gallican Sacramentary there is an order for consecrating nuns and for veiling a virgin. The blessing of an abbess follows, as well as a blessing over a widow changing her clothing.]

May your mercy, O Lord, protect your handmaids, so that, under your protection, they may preserve unharmed the resolve of holy virginity which they have undertaken at your inspiration. Through [Col. 0174D] the Lord.

(614) ### Prayer for Making an Abbot

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, and accompany with the gift of your grace your servant Ill., whom we have chosen to govern souls, so that, by your granting it, we may please you through our choice of him. Through the Lord.

[Note: In Pamel’s edition nothing concerning the Sundays after Pentecost appears. But after the office for the dedication of a church there follows: “On the birthday of the pope. At the ordination of a presbyter. For blessing a bride. Prayers for sins,” and so forth. The same is also read in the Royal Swedish Codex, from which many errors in Pamel’s edition can be corrected—for example, on page 384, in the Prayer for the Tonsure: “You have deigned to call [us] to the new grace of being shorn,” instead of “to the grace of cutting the hair,” as this manuscript codex presents it. The Sundays after Pentecost are likewise omitted in the Roman Calendar. Their Masses are assigned in the same order in two Theoderic manuscripts and in our printed editions. In the Codex of Jumièges, however, they are found immediately after the octave of Pentecost.]

## (615) Second Week after Pentecost

God, strength of those who hope in you, mercifully be present to our invocations; and because mortal weakness can do nothing without you, grant the help of your grace, so that in following your commandments we may please you both in will and in action. Through him.

[Col. 0175A] **169. Over the Offerings.**—Mercifully accept and sanctify our offering, we beseech you, O Lord, so that through its sanctification salvation and everlasting defense may come to us. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for just as you never cease to instruct the children of your Church, so you never cease to help them, so that, by your mercy, they may receive the knowledge of doing what is right and the ability to carry it out. Through Christ.

[Note: It is read in the Blessing Book and is entitled “Blessing for weekdays.”]

**Blessing.**—May the Lord bless you and keep you. Amen. May he make his face shine upon you and have mercy on you. Amen. May he turn his countenance toward you and give you peace. Amen. May he deign to grant this, whose kingdom and dominion endure without end, forever and ever. Amen. May the blessing of God the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, and the peace of the Lord, always be with you. And with your spirit.

**At the Conclusion.**—Filled with such gifts, O Lord, we beseech you to grant that we may also receive saving gifts and never cease from your praise. Through him.

**Over the People.**—May the desired blessing confirm your faithful, O Lord; may it cause them never to depart from your will and always rejoice in your benefits. Through the same Lord our God.

## Third Week after Pentecost

Grant that we may possess perpetual fear and love of your holy name, O Lord, because you never abandon those whom you establish in the firmness of your love. Through the Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—May the offering dedicated to your name purify us, O Lord, and transfer us from day to day into the practice of heavenly life. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: through whom we humbly beseech your Majesty to drive away from your Church whatever is harmful and grant what is salutary to it; and, while you mercifully bestow your grace upon us, grant us to preserve a reasonable humility against proud spirits; and do not abandon us to the uncertainties of human counsel, but order us by your guidance, which cannot be deceived. Through him.

[Note: I have found this blessing nowhere.]

**Blessing.**—May the Lord be reconciled to all your iniquities and heal all your diseases. Amen. May he redeem your soul from destruction and satisfy your desire with good things. Amen. May he take from you a heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Having received your gifts, O Lord, we beseech you that, as we frequently celebrate the mystery, the effect of our salvation may increase. Through the Lord.

**Over the People.**—God, who declares that you dwell in upright and sincere hearts, grant by your grace that we may become such as you may deign to dwell in. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## Fourth Week after Pentecost

Mercifully hear our supplication, we beseech you, O Lord, and grant the help of defense to those to whom you give the disposition to pray. Through the Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—Sanctify the gifts offered, O Lord, so that they may become for us the body and blood of your Only-Begotten. Through the Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: whose wondrous work and saving mystery this was, that we, once lost and cast down by the devil and the sting of death, should be called to this glory, in which we are now called a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a people of possession, and a holy nation. Therefore, giving unceasing thanks and proclaiming your holy generosity, we bring these sacred gifts to your Majesty, which Christ himself, the author of our salvation, established for us. Through whom we beseech your Majesty.

[Note: These too are entirely unknown from other codices. Let the same be understood of the other things that follow, unless we indicate that the matter is otherwise.]

**Blessing.**—May the Lord bless you through the address of our mouth, and join your hearts in the perpetual bond of sincere love. Amen. May you flourish in the abundance of present goods, acquired through justice, and rejoice forever in the fruits of the most sincere charity. Amen. May the Lord grant you enduring gifts, so that, [616] after times have happily been prolonged, you may receive everlasting joys. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Having received the sacred gifts, O Lord, we beseech you that by their power you may cleanse us from every vice and continually fill us with the gifts of your grace. Through our Lord.

**Over the People.**—Favour our times, we beseech you, O Lord, with gracious kindness, and mercifully grant continual help to those for whom you grant a more generous course. Through our Lord.

## Fifth Week after Pentecost

[Col. 0176D] **171.** God, protector of those who hope in you, without whom nothing is strong and nothing is holy, multiply your mercy upon us, so that, with you as our ruler and guide, we may pass through temporal goods in such a way that we do not lose eternal ones. Through our Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—Look upon the gifts of the supplicating Church, O Lord, and grant that they may be received through perpetual sanctification for the salvation of believers. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and continually implore your omnipotence, so that you may grant us both the support of the present life and the everlasting reward of the eternal one. May we receive mutable gifts in such a way that through them we may be able to attain immutable gifts; may the times of temporal joy pass in such a way that everlasting joys may follow them. Through Christ our Lord.

**Blessing.**—May the Lord cleanse your consciences from every wickedness and fill you with perpetual sanctification. Amen. May he graciously attend to your vows and, being reconciled, forgive all your sins. Amen. In his mercy may he grant what you devoutly desire, and, as a gracious defender, drive far away what you fear. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May your holy gifts, O Lord, received by us, give us life and prepare us, purified, for everlasting mercy. Through our Lord.

**Over the People.**—Look graciously upon your people, O Lord, and raise those subject to you with their whole heart by the defenses of unconquerable mercy. Through the Lord.

## Sixth Week after Pentecost

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that the course of the world may be peacefully directed for us according to your ordering, and that your Church may rejoice in tranquil devotion. Through the Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—May the prayers of our humility ascend, we beseech you, O Lord, into the presence of your mercy; and may the power of your divinity descend upon these offerings, which you may also grant to our minds for their purification. Through the Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: humbly imploring your Majesty to graciously grant your aid to those who ask it, and benevolently bestow what will benefit those who desire it. Through Christ our Lord.

[Note: It occurs in the Blessing Book after the blessing for weekdays.]

**Blessing.**—May almighty God bless you with his mercy and pour into you the understanding of saving wisdom. Amen. May he nourish you with the teachings of the catholic faith and make you steadfast in holy works. Amen. May he turn your steps away from error and show you the way of peace and charity. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May the holy mysteries purify us, O Lord, and protect us by their gift. Through him.

**Over the People.**—Hear us, our saving God, and order our days in your peace, so that, freed from every disturbance, we may serve you in tranquil service.

## Seventh Week after Pentecost

God, who have prepared invisible good things for those who love you, pour the affection of your love into our hearts, so that, loving you in all things and above all things, we may attain your promises, which surpass every desire. Through him.

**Over the Offerings.**—Be gracious to our supplications, O Lord, and kindly receive these offerings of your male and female servants, so that what each has offered to the honour of your name may benefit all for salvation. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord, the true and eternal high priest, and [617] the only priest without the stain of sin, by whose blood the hearts of the faithful are cleansed, by whose institution of reconciliation we sacrifice to you offerings not only for the sins of the people but also for our own offenses; asking your mercy that every sin which we have contracted through the frailty of the flesh may be dissolved, with that supreme Bishop interceding for us. Through whom.

**Blessing.**—May the Lord remove from you the stains of every hostility and imbue you with the gifts of pure love. Amen. May he subdue within you the resistance of flesh and blood and grant the aid of perpetual chastity. Amen. May he make you love in the present age what will not separate you from the inheritance of the heavenly paradise. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Whom you have satisfied, O Lord, with a heavenly gift, grant, we beseech you, that we may be cleansed from our hidden faults and freed from the snares of our enemies. Through him.

**Over the People.**—Protect, we beseech you, O Lord, your supplicating people with your right hand, so that, passing through the present life under your governance, they may deserve to find everlasting life. Through our Lord.

## Eighth Week after Pentecost

God of hosts, [618] to whom belongs everything that is good, implant the love of your name in our hearts and grant an increase of religion within us, so that you may nourish what is good and, through devotion to piety, guard what has been nourished. Through him.

**Over the Offerings.**—Be gracious to our supplications, O Lord, and kindly receive these offerings of your people; and, so that no one’s vow may be fruitless and no one’s petition empty, grant, we beseech you, that what we faithfully ask we may effectively obtain. Through the Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and offer you the sacrifice of a contrite heart, [619] sacrifice to you the victim of a humbled breast, from whom we receive every good and draw every joy. Therefore we pray that our conscience may serve you and, so that it may grow better day by day in you, submit itself undefiled to your grace. Empty us, we beseech you, O Lord, of our evils, and fill us in all things with your goods, so that, having received grace which our merits do not demand, freed from every adversity and strengthened in every good, we may deserve to be joined to the citizens above. Through Christ.

[Note: It is found in the Blessing Book near the end.]

**Blessing.**—May the Lord incline his ear to the prayers of your humility and give you the grace of his blessing and the reward of everlasting salvation. Amen. May you always and everywhere have the Lord as your gracious protector and exult in his praises. Amen. May he loose the bonds of all your sins and cause you to attain everlasting glory. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Filled with your gifts, O Lord, we beseech you that by their effect we may be cleansed and by their help protected. Through the same Lord.

**Over the People.**—Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that, truly trusting in your grace, we may ask for what is worthy and continually receive what we have asked. Through him.

## Ninth Week after Pentecost

God, whose providence is not deceived in its ordering, we humbly beseech you to remove every harmful thing and grant us everything that will benefit us. Through him.

**Over the Offerings.**—God, who established the distinctions among legal sacrifices through the perfection of one sacrifice, [620] receive the sacrifice from servants devoted to you and sanctify it with an equal blessing, as you did the gifts of Abel, so that [621] what each has offered to the honour of your Majesty may benefit all for salvation. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and implore your mercy with all our strength, lest you condemn us for our iniquity, but, because of your goodness, always order us along the right way; and lest you be angry with us who sin as we deserve, but come to the aid of our frailty with unconquerable goodness. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—May the grace of the Lord sanctify you and guard you from every evil. Amen. May he keep every evil thing away from you and purify your spirits and bodies. Amen. May he bind you to himself with the bond of charity, and may his peace abound in your hearts. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May your healing work, O Lord, mercifully free us from our perversities and lead us to what is right. Through him.

[Col. 0179D] **Over the People.**—Turn the hearts of your people always toward you, O Lord, so that those whom you cause to be helped by such great protections you may never cease to govern with perpetual defenses. Through him.

## Tenth Week after Pentecost

Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, always [622] the spirit of thinking and doing what is right, so that we who cannot exist without you may be able to live according to you. Through him.

**Over the Offerings.**—Receive the gifts which we bring from your generosity, O Lord, so that these most holy mysteries, through the working power of your grace, may both sanctify us in the conduct of the present life and lead us to everlasting joys. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and implore your mercy, so that, with your consent, we may be able to avoid what is evil and consequently accomplish what is good; and because you have made us belong to your sacraments, [623] mercifully work their gift within us. Through Christ.

[Note: In the Blessing Book it has its place among those read from the common collection.]

**Blessing.**—May the Lord multiply in you the abundance of his blessing and strengthen you in the hope of the heavenly kingdom. Amen. May he correct your actions, improve your life, order your conduct, and lead you to the inheritance of the heavenly paradise. Amen. May you be able to be filled with such an intention that you may please him forever. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Having received the gifts of your institution, O Lord, we beseech you to cleanse us by their purity and defend us by their powerful strength. Through the Lord.

**Over the People.**—Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, running along your way with devoted mind, [624] we may escape the snares of creeping sins. Through our Lord.

## Eleventh Week after Pentecost

Grant, we beseech you, almighty and merciful God, that amid the darkness of this life we may neither be plunged into error through ignorance nor hasten to sin through rash will; but to those to whom you grant confidence in hoping for your mercy, kindly grant the fulfillment of the mercy they desire. Through him.

**Over the Offerings.**—Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord, worthily to celebrate these mysteries, because whenever the commemoration of this Victim is celebrated, [625] the work of our redemption is carried out. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and repay you the service owed to you through the fulfillment of this ministry, because you grant forgiveness not only to sinners but also rewards to those who ask. And what we deserve to suffer through evil works you drive away with magnificent goodness, so that you may compel us to worship your reverence by fear and lead us to it by love. [626] Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—May God, who is the life of mortals and the salvation of sinners, remove from you all stains of sin. Amen. May he clothe you with the beauty of virtues, sanctify your minds, purify your wills, and grant you the fellowship of the holy angels, so that, approved in faith and immaculate in deed, you may reach the eternal inheritance of heavenly joys. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May the communion of your sacrament, O Lord, grant us purification and bestow unity. Through him.

[Col. 0181A] **Over the People.**—Preserve the hearts of your faithful, we beseech you, O Lord, and strengthen them by the power of your grace, so that they may be devoted in supplication to you and sincere in mutual love. Through our Lord.

## Twelfth Week after Pentecost

God, who manifest your omnipotence above all by sparing and showing mercy, multiply your mercy upon us, so that, running toward your promises, you may make us sharers in heavenly goods. Through our Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—May the sacrifices dedicated to you, O Lord, be returned to you, which you granted to be brought to the honour of your name so that you might make them remedies for us. Through the Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: whose first sign of mercy is that you make us subject to you with our whole heart and pour into us a spirit of such devotion that you may graciously grant the help that follows. Through Christ.

[Note: It is presented in the Blessing Book among the common blessings, that is, those assigned to no particular day.]

**Blessing.**—May the Lord graciously attend to your devotion and grant you the gifts of his blessing. Amen. May he fortify you with such assistance in the present age that in the future he may make you inhabitants of paradise. Amen. Thus may he bless your hearts by sanctifying them, and sanctify them by blessing them, so that he may delight to dwell with you, indeed within you. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—We beseech you, O Lord our God, not to abandon with your kindness those whom you never cease to restore through divine sacraments. Through the Lord.

**Over the People.**—Purify your faithful, O Lord, in body and mind alike, so that, pierced by your inspiration, they may prevail in avoiding harmful pleasures and, lest they be captured by their enticements, may always be nourished by your sweetness. Through him.

## Thirteenth Week after Pentecost

Almighty and everlasting God, whose abundant goodness surpasses both the merits and the vows of those who supplicate you, pour out your mercy upon us, so that you may forgive what conscience fears and add what prayer does not presume to ask. Through our Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—Look graciously upon our service, O Lord, we beseech you, so that what we offer may be an acceptable gift to you and a support for our frailty. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: who heal us by chastising us and mercifully instruct us by restoring us, since you prefer that we should be saved when corrected rather than perish when cast down. Through Christ our Lord.

**Blessing.**—May the Lord enrich you with his grace and multiply you with heavenly blessing. Amen. May he defend you from every adversity and always guard you with compassionate mercy. Amen. May he graciously attend to your petitions and mercifully grant you forgiveness of all faults. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May we feel, O Lord, we beseech you, through receiving your sacrament, support for mind and body, so that, saved in both, we may glory in the fullness of heavenly remedy. Through him.

**Over the People.**—Protect your people, O Lord, and, since they are always helped by saving defenses, raise them up with continual benefits of mind and body. Through him.

## Fourteenth Week after Pentecost

Almighty and everlasting God, through whom what did not exist began to exist and [627] what was hidden became visible, cleanse the foolishness of our heart and purify the secrets of vice within us, so that we may serve you, the Lord, with a pure mind. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0182B] **Over the Offerings.**—We offer you, O Lord, a sacrifice of appeasement and praise, humbly imploring you both to look upon it with appeased goodness and to hear the prayers of those who offer it with merciful generosity. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because, always making strength in our weakness, [628] you granted your Church to grow amid adversities, so that when it was thought to be oppressed, then it might rather prevail when exalted; while affliction simultaneously reveals the testing of faith, and devotion, with your help, always perseveres most victoriously. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—May the Lord give you the gift of his blessing and fill you with the spirit of truth and peace. Amen. May you run along the way of salvation with such a devoted mind that you may healthfully escape the snares of creeping sins. Amen. May you become devoted in supplication to him and sincere in mutual love, so that you may reach the heavenly kingdom securely. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May participation in this holy mystery give us life, we beseech you, O Lord, and grant us both expiation and protection. Through him.

**Over the People.**—Almighty and merciful God, from whose gift it comes that your faithful serve you worthily and laudably, grant, we beseech you, that we may run without offense toward your promises. Through him.

## Fifteenth Week after Pentecost

[Col. 0182D] **178.** Almighty and everlasting God, grant us an increase of faith, hope, and charity; and, so that we may deserve to attain what you promise, make us love what you command. Through him.

**Over the Offerings.**—Be gracious, O Lord, to your people and to their offerings, so that, appeased by this offering, you may grant us forgiveness and grant what we ask. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: who lead us from the gifts of temporal goods to the reception of eternal ones, granting both these and those, so that we may already begin to be joined to what endures and not be held by what passes away. For it is by your gift that we live; although our nature has been corrupted by the wound of sin, it is nevertheless your work that we, born earthly, are reborn for heavenly things. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—May the Lord’s blessing accompany you everywhere and always make you cling to him. Amen. May he himself save you by his blessing, he who deigned powerfully to shape you. Amen. And may he grant you to live happily in such a way that he makes you coheirs of heavenly blessedness. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Having been satisfied with heavenly gifts, O Lord, we beseech you to deign continually to grant us both the will to live piously and rightly and the power and effectiveness to accomplish it. Through the Lord.

**Over the People.**—Preserve your people, we beseech you, O Lord; and grant that those whom you never cease to help with saving defenses may rejoice forever in the benefits of both mind and body. Through our Lord.

## Sixteenth Week after Pentecost

Guard your Church, O Lord, we beseech you, with perpetual appeasement; and because human mortality falls without you, may it always be withdrawn from harmful things by your help and directed toward what is salutary. Through the Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—Bringing you the sacrifice of a unique offering, O Lord, we ask that by its power you cleanse us from sins and make us worthy of your sanctification. Through the Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who, by the eternity of his priesthood, sanctifies all priests who serve you, since, surrounded by mortal flesh, we need daily forgiveness of sins, so that the blood of that same High Priest may plead with you not only for the people but also for us. Through whom.

[Note: It is found in the Blessing Book, namely in the series of common or daily blessings.]

**Blessing.**—May almighty God grant you the gift of his blessing, he who knows your weakness. Amen. And [629] may he who grants you the disposition to pray grant you the help of consolation. Amen. May you receive from him support for both the present and future life, from whose goodness you believe yourselves to have been created. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

[Col. 0183D] **At the Conclusion.**—Grant us, merciful God, to implore your appeasement with ready minds, and, through the sacraments we have received, obtaining forgiveness of sins, free us from harmful assaults. Through our Lord.
