**Over the People.**—Be gracious to your people, O Lord, and absolve them from all sins, so that what we deserve through our offenses may be driven away by your indulgence. Through him.

## Seventeenth Week after Pentecost

May continual mercy cleanse and protect your Church, O Lord; and because it cannot stand safe without you, may it always be governed by your [630] gift. Through the Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—May your sacraments guard us, O Lord, and always defend us against diabolical assaults. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and pray to you without ceasing, so that, since we subsist by your authorship, we may be directed by your dispensation. May we [631] not be left to our own senses, but, always brought back to the path of your truth, may we strive to carry out what you command, so that we may be able to receive the gifts you promise. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—May almighty God cleanse the stains of your sins and enlighten you with his blessing. Amen. May he fill you with the gifts of spiritual virtues and make you persevere in your good resolve. Amen. May he mercifully accept your humility, so that he may enrich you with the reward of his mercy. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May the working of the heavenly gift, O Lord, possess our minds and bodies, [632] so that not our own understanding but its effect may continually precede us. Through the Lord.

**Over the People.**—Be present to our supplications, O Lord, and, with ineffable mercy, come to the aid of those who presume nothing from their own conscience, so that what the confidence of merits does not possess your unconquerable generosity of gifts may provide. Through him.

## Eighteenth Week after Pentecost

[Col. 0184C] **180.** Absolve the sins of your peoples, we beseech you, O Lord, and by your goodness free us from the bonds of the sins which we have contracted through our frailty. Through him.

**Over the Offerings.**—Offering you a sacrifice of praise for the increase of our service, we beseech you, O Lord, [633] graciously to carry out what you have bestowed upon us undeservedly. Through the Lord.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: because, although you do not need our praise, the devotion of your servants is nevertheless pleasing to you; nor do our praises increase you, but they benefit us for salvation. For just as passing by the fountain of life is a cause of dying, so continually being replenished by it is the effect of living without end. Through Christ.

**Blessing.**—May almighty God surround you with heavenly protection and enrich you with the gift of his blessing. Amen. And may he grant you, who rely upon the sole hope of heavenly grace, to be fortified also by heavenly protection. Amen. Thus may you receive the comforts of mortal life in the present age and be able to attain everlasting joys. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—Renewed by participation in the saving Victim, we beseech you, almighty God, to make us, by its singular power, an everlasting holocaust to you. Through him.

**Over the People.**—Grant your people, we beseech you, O Lord, both a mind by which they may remain devoted to you, an understanding by which they may ask for what is just, and your appeasement, through which you may perfect what is beneficial for those who devoutly desire it. Through him.

## Nineteenth Week after Pentecost

Almighty and everlasting God, show your mercy to those who supplicate you, so that we who distrust the [634] quality of our merits may experience not your judgment but your indulgence. Through the Lord.

**Over the Offerings.**—By the offering of this gift, O Lord, we seek to appease you, and by its working may we be made sharers in everlasting life. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: who conquered the devil and the world, restored humanity to paradise, and opened the gates of life to believers. Through whom.

[Note: It is in the Blessing Book at the place already indicated.]

**Blessing.**—May almighty God continually surround you with the help of his right hand and fill you with the gift of his blessings. Amen. May he defend you from every depravity and grant you to abound in heavenly gifts. Amen. Thus purified in body and mind, may you offer him such service that you may be able to obtain his appeasement. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

**At the Conclusion.**—May the most holy draught of the heavenly table, O Lord, always cleanse and nourish our hearts. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0185C] **Over the People.**—Be present, O Lord, to your peoples who trust in your protection and humbly bow before your right hand; preserve them with perpetual defense. Through him.

## Twentieth Week after Pentecost

Make us subject to you, O Lord, we beseech you, with a ready will, and always stir up our wills to supplicate you. Through him.

**Over the Offerings.**—Cleanse us, O Lord, by the effect of the present sacrifice, and, in your mercy, perfect within us that we may deserve to share in it. Through him.

**Preface.**—It is truly right and just, fitting and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: and humbly implore your Majesty, so that Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, may protect and preserve us by his grace; and because without him we can accomplish nothing rightly, may we receive through his gift the ability always to please you. Through whom we beseech your Majesty.

[Note: This blessing is placed after the preceding one in the Blessing Book.]

**Blessing.**—May almighty God purify the hidden places of your hearts and grant you increase through his blessing. Amen. May you be stripped of all the dangers of the present life and clothed with the ornaments of spiritual virtues. Amen. Supported by his help, may you serve him on earth in such a way that you may be able to be joined to him in heaven. Amen. May he deign to grant this.

[Col. 0186A] **At the Conclusion.**—Purify our minds graciously, we beseech you, O Lord, and renew them through heavenly sacraments, so that we may consequently receive both present and future aid for our bodies. Through him.

At the Prayer over the People.—Look favorably, O Lord, upon the service which your people owe you, so that amid the uncertainties of human frailty those who trust in your protection may not be overwhelmed by any adversities. Through our Lord.

## Twenty-First Week after Pentecost

Grant, we ask, O Lord, that your people may avoid the contagion of the devil and follow you alone, the Lord, with a pure heart. Through.

At the Offering.—We humbly beseech your Majesty, O Lord, that these holy offerings which we perform may free us both from past offenses and from future ones. [Col. 0186B] Through.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and earnestly entreat you: so instruct us with your everlasting gifts that you may also deign to console us with temporal ones; so refresh us amid present things that you may lead us to abiding joys. Through Christ.

Blessing.—May almighty God, in his mercy, drive every adversity away from you [Note: [Col. 0186D] The entire phrase *universa* is absent in the edition; we have added it from a manuscript and from the Benedictional.] and pour upon you the gifts of his blessing. Amen. May he make your hearts attentive to sacred teachings, so that they may be filled with everlasting benefits. Amen. Thus, understanding what must be done and doing what you have understood, may you be found unharmed amid the adversities of the world and become coheirs of the blessed spirits. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—May the sacrifice which we have offered to your goodness, Lord God, benefit us for the forgiveness of our sins and always grant us the comfort of your mercy. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

At the Prayer over the People.—May your faithful people receive your blessing, O Lord, by which, saved in body and mind, they may always offer you grateful service and always find the benefits of your favor. Through our Lord.

## Twenty-Second Week after Pentecost

Direct our hearts, we ask, O Lord, by the working of your mercy, because without you we cannot please you. [Col. 0186D] Through.

At the Offering.—O God, who through the venerable exchange of this sacrifice make us participants in the one supreme divinity, grant, we ask, that we may know your truth and attain it through minds and conduct worthy of it. Through our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for this reason you justly punish those who go astray and mercifully sustain those who have been chastised, so that you may draw us away from evil works and turn us toward doing good, because you do not wish to find something to condemn, but rather something to crown. Although we continually deserve to be afflicted according to our merits, you nevertheless temper judgment for correction and do not exercise perpetual punishment. For you correct justly and forgive mercifully, truthful in both, merciful in both. You order us under this law: by restraining us, you do not allow us to perish forever, and by sparing us, you grant time for correction. Therefore you chastise us with present evils so that you may lead us to future goods; therefore you console us with temporal goods so that you may make us more certain of eternal ones. Thus may we always praise you with devout confession both in prosperity and in adversity. Through Christ our Lord.

Blessing.—May almighty God order your days in his peace [Note: [Col. 0187D] In the Benedictional this is the final blessing.] and grant you the gifts of his blessing. Amen. May he free you from every disturbance and strengthen your minds with the tranquillity of his peace. Amen. Thus, adorned with the gems of hope, faith, and charity, may you pass through the present life unharmed and reach the eternal life securely. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—Strengthened by the sacred gift, we give you thanks, O Lord, and beseech your mercy to make us worthy of participating in it. Through the Lord.

At the Prayer over the People.—Be the protector of your household, we ask, O Lord, and grant your mercy to those who seek it, so that they may always be obedient to you and receive your gifts. Through.

## Twenty-Third Week after Pentecost

[Col. 0187C]

Almighty and merciful God, in your mercy remove from us everything opposed to us, so that, freed in mind and body alike, we may carry out what belongs to you with unencumbered minds. Through our Lord.

At the Offering.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that through these sacred gifts we may so merit your forgiveness that we correct our transgressions, and so forgive the offense of those who confess that we restrain those obstinate in their wickedness. Through.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and humbly implore your mercy: that your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, who promised to be with his faithful until the end of the age, may neither abandon those whom he redeemed through the mysteries of his bodily presence [Col. 0187D] nor leave them without the benefits of his Majesty. (638) Through whom your Majesty.

Blessing.—May the grace of the Lord’s blessing always protect you and defend you from every evil. Amen. May he cleanse you from every guilt of sins and make you pleasing to himself forever. Amen. May the Lord, favorably disposed, meet you everywhere and graciously grant you the help of his blessing. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—May your healing work, O Lord, mercifully free us from our perversities and always make us cling to your commandments. [Col. 0188A] Through.

At the Prayer over the People.—May your right hand perpetually surround your household with help, O Lord, we ask, so that, defended from every wickedness, it may be accompanied by heavenly gifts. Through our Lord.

## Twenty-Fourth Week after Pentecost

Mercifully grant your faithful forgiveness and peace, O Lord, we ask, so that they may be cleansed alike from every offense and serve you with a tranquil mind. Through.

At the Offering.—May these mysteries, we ask, O Lord, provide us with heavenly medicine and cleanse the vices of our hearts. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0188B] Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, humbly beseeching your Majesty: that, once the unleavened things of old have been driven out, we may be satisfied with the food and drink of that Lamb who both restored our likeness and promised us his grace—Jesus Christ, your Son.

Blessing.—May the almighty Lord open your hearts to his law and humble your souls so that they may receive the heavenly commandments. Amen. Whatever the mouth of our mortality proclaims to you for the salvation of your souls, may divine goodness make acceptable to you. Amen. Thus, animated by divine words together with those who keep watch for you, may you merit to reach eternal blessedness unharmed. [Col. 0188C] Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—As we offer you, Lord our God, the sacrifice of our salvation, we ask that you grant us, with purified minds, always to celebrate the mystery of your goodness. Through our Lord.

At the Prayer over the People.—Grant, we ask, O Lord, salvation of mind and body to your people, and fill the hearts of your faithful with perpetual consolations, so that, lifted up by your protection, they may both please you through devout dedication and always obtain your benefits. Through our Lord.

185 [Note: [Col. 0187D] In the Calensian manuscript only the Sunday of the Twenty-Fourth Week after [Col. 0188D] Pentecost is assigned; in the Gemetian, the Twenty-Fifth after the octave of Pentecost; in the earlier Theodulfian manuscript, the Twenty-Fifth after Pentecost, and in the other, the Twenty-Sixth.]

## Twenty-Fifth Week after Pentecost

O God, who preserve us by governing us and justify us by sparing us, rescue us from temporal tribulation and lavish eternal joys upon us. Through our Lord.

At the Offering.—Receive these offerings favorably, O Lord, by which you wished both to be appeased and to restore salvation to us through your powerful goodness. Through.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: through him the holy and blessed name of your Majesty is everywhere venerated, adored, proclaimed, and worshiped; he is the source of salvation, the way of virtue, and the appeasement of your goodness. Through whom.

[Col. 0189A] (639) The blessing is required.

At the Conclusion.—Having received the nourishment of immortality, we ask, O Lord, that we may pursue in mind what we have received with our mouth. Through our Lord.

At the Prayer over the People.—Guard your household, we ask, O Lord, with continual goodness, so that, free from every adversity under your protection, it may be devoted to your name in good works. Through.

## Twenty-Sixth Week after Pentecost

O God, our refuge and strength, be present to the devout prayers of your Church, as the very author of goodness, and grant that we may effectively obtain what we faithfully ask. Through.

At the Offering.—Grant, merciful God, that this saving offering may continually free us from our own guilt and guard us from every adversity. Through our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and render you the praises due to you with devout honor, celebrating the ineffable proclamations of your wonders with the veneration of a devoted mind. We praise you, bless you, and adore you, the ineffable and invisible God. Through Christ our Lord.

The blessing is required.

At the Conclusion.—Go before us always and everywhere with heavenly light, we ask, O Lord, so that we may behold with a pure gaze and receive with worthy devotion the mystery of which you have willed us to be participants. [Col. 0189C] Through.

At the Prayer over the People.—O God, protector of those who hope in you, save your people, so that, freed from sins and secure from the enemy, they may always persevere in your grace. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## Twenty-Seventh Week after Pentecost

Stir up, O Lord, we ask, the wills of your faithful, so that, more eagerly carrying out the fruit of divine work, they may receive the greater remedies of your goodness. Through.

At the Offering.—Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and, having accepted the offerings and prayers of your people, turn all our hearts toward you, so that, freed from earthly desires, we may pass to heavenly longings. Through.

[Col. 0189D] Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, whose work it is that we have been created, whose gift it is that we live, and whose goodness it is that we recognize your gifts toward us. Although our nature has been corrupted by the wound of sin, nevertheless, through your ineffable gift it is raised from earthly things to heavenly ones. Through Christ.

The blessing is required.

At the Conclusion.—Grant us, O Lord, we ask, that whatever is defective in our mind may be healed by the medicine of the sacrament which we have received. [Col. 0190A] Through.

At the Prayer over the People.—Stir up the hearts of your faithful, O Lord, so that, attentive to sacred teachings, they may both understand what they should follow and, by following it, faithfully attain it. Through our Lord.

(640) [Note: [Col. 0189D] In the Roman Calendar only four weeks are assigned before the Nativity of the Lord, and likewise four in the Calensian manuscript; I find no more in the Gemetian and Theodulfian manuscripts.]

## Fifth Week before the Nativity of the Lord

(641) Stir up your power, O Lord, and come, and mercifully accomplish until the end of the age what you promised to your Church. You who live and reign with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God. Through all ages.

At the Offering.—Look favorably, O Lord, upon the sacrifice to be celebrated for you, so that it may both cleanse us from the vices of our condition and make us acceptable to your name. Through.

[Col. 0190B] Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, 187 through Christ our Lord: that you may make us celebrate the mystery of his first coming with worthy praises and duties, and lead the present life blamelessly, so that we may await the second coming without fear. Through whom your Majesty.

Blessing.—May the Lord grant you the reward of sincere charity, so that you may always live in peace with everyone. Amen. May you overcome the snares of all enemies and conduct the present life with complete sincerity. Amen. May you also be free from the guilt of conscience, so that you fear nothing on the day of the judgment to come. May he himself.

At the Conclusion.—May our souls, we ask, almighty God, attain this desire: that they may be inflamed by your Spirit, so that, like lamps filled by divine generosity, we may shine as bright lights before the presence of Christ your Son who is coming. Through the same.

At the Prayer over the People.—Mercifully hear the prayers of your people, we ask, O Lord, so that those who rejoice in the coming of your only-begotten Son according to the flesh may, at his second coming in his Majesty, receive the reward of eternal life. Through.

## Fourth Week before the Nativity of the Lord

Stir up your power, we ask, O Lord, and come, so that, with you protecting us, we may merit to be rescued from the imminent dangers of our sins and, with you freeing us, to be saved. You who live and reign.

At the Offering.—Look upon this singular sacrifice, we ask, O Lord, so that, by participating in this mystery, we may receive, once awaited, what we believe must be hoped for. Through the Lord.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, (643) for it is proper and unique to you that you are good and that you are never changed by any alteration. Be favorable, we ask, to our supplications, and show your mercy, which your Church entreats, manifesting to your people the mystery of the incarnation of your only-begotten Son and the wondrous sacrament of his coming, so that among all the nations it may be evident (644) that what was formerly promised through the oracles of the prophets has been fulfilled, (645) and that those whom the confession of truth adorns may receive the dignity of adoption. (646) Through whom.

Blessing.—May almighty God, whose only-begotten Son’s coming you believe to have occurred in the past and await in the future, sanctify you by the illumination of that same coming and enrich you with his blessing. Amen. May he defend you from every adversity in the course of the present life and show himself favorable to you in judgment. Amen. Thus, freed from every contagion of sins, may you await without fear the day of that dreadful examination. Amen. May he himself.

[Col. 0191B] 188 At the Conclusion.—May we receive your mercy, O Lord, in the midst of your temple, and precede the coming solemnities of our restoration with fitting honors. Through.

At the Prayer over the People.—Give your people, we ask, O Lord, the Spirit of truth and peace, so that they may know you with their whole mind through the coming of your only-begotten Son and follow with all their heart what is pleasing to you. Through the same Lord our Lord.

## Third Week before the Nativity of the Lord

Stir up our hearts, O Lord, to prepare the ways of your only-begotten Son, so that, with minds purified, we may merit to serve you through his coming. God, who lives and reigns with you.

At the Offering.—Be appeased, O Lord, we ask, by the prayers and offerings of our humility, and where no support of merits is available, come to our aid through the resources of your indulgence. Through.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: for (647) through your ineffable gift you granted that human nature, created in your likeness but made unlike you through sin and death, should not perish in eternal damnation; rather, from the source where it had contracted sin and death, your boundless goodness restored life, and (648) the new and undefiled virgin Mary atoned for the deed of the ancient virgin. She, greeted by the angel and overshadowed by the Holy Spirit, merited to give birth to him who by his will granted that all things should be born. She marveled both at the integrity of her body and at the fruitfulness of conception, and rejoiced that she was about to bear her own parent, Jesus Christ our Lord. Through whom.

Blessing.—(649) May God, whose coming in the incarnation is believed to have occurred in the past and whose coming for judgment is awaited in the future, cleanse you from every contagion of sin before he comes. Amen. May he first wash away in you everything that he will punish in that future examination, so that, when the just judge comes, he may find nothing in you to condemn. Amen. When he comes, may you not incur eternal punishment but be rewarded with everlasting gifts. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

[Col. 0192A] At the Conclusion.—Filled with the food of spiritual nourishment, we humbly beseech you, O Lord, that through participation in this mystery you may teach us to despise earthly things and love heavenly ones. Through our Lord.

At the Prayer over the People.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, to your entire household this will: to meet Christ your Son, our Lord, who is coming, prepared by just deeds, so that, joined to his right hand, they may merit to possess the heavenly kingdom. Through the same Lord our Lord.

## Second Week before the Nativity of the Lord

Bend your ear, we ask, O Lord, to our prayers, and illumine the darkness of our mind by the grace of your visitation. Through our Lord.

At the Offering.—May the Victim of our devotion, we ask, O Lord, be continually offered to you; may it both carry out the ordinances of the sacred mystery and wonderfully accomplish your salvation in us. Through the same Lord our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: by whose incarnation the salvation of the world was accomplished and by whose passion redemption was procured for created humanity. May he himself, we ask, lead us to the eternal reward—he who redeemed us from the darkness of hell—and justify us at his second coming, he who redeemed us at his first; so that the exalted one may defend us from every evil, whose humility raised us to life. Through whom your Majesty.

Blessing.—May almighty God look upon you with a favorable face and pour into you the gift of his blessing. Amen. May he who made these days solemn through the incarnation of his only-begotten Son render you unharmed from all adversities of the present and future life. Amen. May you who rejoice with devout mind in the coming of our Redeemer according to the flesh be enriched with the rewards of eternal life at his second coming, when he comes in Majesty. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—We implore your mercy, O Lord, that these divine aids may prepare us, cleansed from vices, for the coming feasts. Through.

## Tenth Month, Wednesday

[Note: [Col. 0191D] In the Roman Calendar, the station is at Saint Mary. The Gospel *Missus est* is read, as it is also today. The station is likewise at this place in the Calensian manuscript.]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the coming solemnity of our redemption may both bring us the aids of the present life and bestow the rewards of eternal blessedness. [Col. 0192D] Through the Lord.

Another.—Hasten, we ask, O Lord; do not delay, and grant us the help of heavenly power, so that those who trust in your goodness may be lifted up by the consolations of your coming. You who live and reign.

At the Offering.—May the gifts by which the mysteries of our freedom and life are celebrated be pleasing to you, O Lord. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

190 Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: he who was awaited by the ancient fathers, announced by the angel, conceived by the Virgin, and presented to humanity at the end of the ages. As the feast of his Nativity approaches, may he, we ask, be favorable to us in such a way that he may come to us with you and with the Holy Spirit and remain with us forever. Through whom.

At the Conclusion.—May your gifts preserve us, we ask, O Lord, and through the coming of your only-begotten Son grant us eternal life. You who live with the Father.

At the Prayer over the People.—Grant the abundance of your grace, we ask, O Lord, to your suppliants, so that, following your commandments with your help, they may receive the consolation of the present life and of the future one. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0193D] From the same Calendar and the Calensian codex, the station is at the Apostles. The Gospel assigned to this feria is *Exsurgens Maria abiit in montem* (“Mary arose and went into the hill country”).]

## Friday

Stir up your power, we ask, O Lord, and [Col. 0193B] come, so that those who trust in your goodness may quickly be freed from every adversity. You who live and reign.

At the Offering.—Grant, O Lord, we ask, that we may offer an effect of devotion corresponding to the dedicated gift. Through.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: you are the sanctifier and institutor of abstinence, whose end and number are without limit. Pour out, we ask, upon us during the days of our fasts the Spirit of saving grace, and preserve us by your protection from all the disturbances of this age, so that we who celebrate the coming of your only-begotten Son may experience his continual help. Through whom your Majesty.

[Col. 0193C] At the Conclusion.—May the mysteries we have received benefit us, O Lord, and at the same time both free us from sins and raise us up through the protections of your favor. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0193D] In the Roman Calendar, a station is prescribed at Saint Peter. The Gospel to be read is specified: “In the fifteenth year of Tiberius.” Saint Gregory’s Homily 20 on this Gospel reading is said to have been delivered in the basilica of Saint John the Baptist. In the Calensian manuscript, after this Saturday one reads: “Sunday is vacant.”]

## Saturday with Twelve Lessons of the Tenth Month

O God, who see that we are afflicted because of our perversity, mercifully grant that we may be consoled by your visitation. Through.

Another.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that since we are oppressed under the yoke of sin by ancient servitude, we may be freed by the awaited new birth of your only-begotten Son. God, who lives and reigns with you.

191 Another.—Make us, we ask, your unworthy servants—whom the guilt of our own actions grieves—rejoice at the coming of your only-begotten Son. You who live with the Father.

[Col. 0193D] Another.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the coming solemnity of your Son may both bring us remedies for the present life and grant eternal rewards. Through the same.

Another.—Mercifully hear the prayers of your people, we ask, O Lord, so that we who are justly afflicted for our sins may be consoled by the visitation of your goodness. Through the Lord.

(650) Another at Mass.—O God, who softened the flames of fire for the three young men, mercifully grant that the flame of vices may not burn us, your servants. [Col. 0194A] Through our Lord.

At the Offering.—Sanctify the gifts of your Church, O Lord, and grant that through these venerable mysteries we may merit to be refreshed with heavenly bread. Through our Lord.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: you not only forgive sins but also justify sinners themselves; you not only release the guilty from sins but also lavish gifts and rewards. We humbly implore your goodness: may we who anticipate the Nativity of your only-begotten Son with fasts and solemn vows, through his gift both be free from the disturbances of the present life and receive eternal gifts. Through whom your Majesty [Col. 0194B].

At the Conclusion.—We ask, Lord our God, that you make the sacred mysteries which you have granted for the protection of our restoration both a present remedy and a future one. Through.

(651) ## First Sunday before the Nativity of the Lord

Stir up your power and come, O Lord, and come to our aid with great strength, so that through the help of your grace you may hasten, by the indulgence of your favor, what our sins impede. You who live and reign with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God. Through all ages.

At the Offering.—Kindly accept and sanctify these offerings made to you, O Lord, so that by receiving them we may be cleansed from guilt and merit to await without fear the glory of the coming of your Son. Through the same Lord our [Col. 0194C] Lord.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and profitable for salvation that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord: John went before him by being born, by preaching in the deserts of the wilderness, by baptizing in the streams of the Jordan, and by descending to the underworld. May the solemnity of his venerable Nativity, which is soon to come, render us pleasing to you, we ask, so that with the fruit of good works it may lead us into the heavenly kingdoms; so that, preparing the way of the Lord in our hearts and producing worthy fruits of repentance, we may obey the admonitions of our Savior through John’s preaching. Thus may we come through the son of the barren woman to the Son of the Virgin, through John, a great man, to that same Lord of ours, the man who is God; just as he came to us secretly to redeem us, so may he justify us when he comes openly to judge. Through whom.

Blessing.—May God, who restored you through the grace of his first coming and promised to give you a kingdom with the holy angels at his second, sanctify you by the illumination of his coming. Amen. May he dissolve your bonds before he comes, so that, freed from the bonds of sins, you may await without fear his dread coming. Amen. May you who believe that he came on earth for your salvation and await him as coming to judgment merit fearlessly to behold the glory of his coming. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.

At the Conclusion.—Grant us, O Lord, satisfied by the power of the heavenly table, both to desire what is right and to receive what we desire. Through.

At the Prayer over the People.—Help the frailty of your people, O Lord, so that, being guided also in body, it may attain the desired fulfillment of the great festival and, with devoted mind, reach perpetual grace. Through.

(652) [Note: [Col. 0195D] In the Vatican and Gussanville editions: “Prayer.”]

## Prayers concerning the Coming of the Lord for the Weekdays

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may celebrate with a favorable outcome the coming solemnities of the great festival, and that we may at the same time be attentive to heavenly disciplines and more joyful concerning our times. Through.

Another.—Purify our consciences, we ask, O Lord, by visiting them, so that Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, when he comes, may find in us a dwelling prepared for himself. You who live with the Father.

Another.—Be near, O Lord, to all who await you in truth, so that at the coming of your Son, our Lord, we may be presented to you through deeds pleasing to you. Through the same Lord our Lord.

Another.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, this grace to your people: to await the coming of your only-begotten Son with the utmost vigilance, so that, as the author of our salvation himself taught, we may prepare our souls like shining lamps to meet him. Through.

Another.—Illumine our minds, we ask, O Lord, with the light of your visitation, so that, by your generosity, we may merit to be humble amid prosperity and secure amid adversity. Through the Lord.

Another.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the coming solemnity of your Son may bring us remedies for the present life and grant eternal rewards. God, who lives and reigns with you.

Another.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that since we are oppressed under the yoke of sin by ancient servitude, we may be freed by the awaited new birth of your only-begotten Son. You who live with the Father.

Another.—We ask, almighty God, look upon our prayers and bestow upon us the depths of your goodness, so that we who are afflicted because of our guilt may breathe freely when our Savior comes. You who live with the Father.

[Col. 0195D] Another.—Bend the ears of your goodness, we ask, O Lord, to our voice, and illumine the darkness of our heart with the light of your visitation. You who live.

Another.—Stretch out to us, O Lord, the right hand of your veneration, and come, and in your favor absolve our sins. You who live and reign.

Another.—Stretch out to us, O Lord, the right hand of your veneration, and come, and in your favor absolve our sins. You who live and reign.

Another.—As we hasten to meet your Son, our Lord, almighty God, may no earthly works impede us; rather, may the instruction of heavenly Wisdom make us his companions. You who live with the Father.

Another.—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that since we deserve to be afflicted for our sins, we may be freed from every adversity through the coming of your Son. Through.

Another.—O God, who see that we are always deprived by our weakness, guard us through the visitation of your Son when he comes. You who live and reign with the Father.

Another.—Be present, we ask, almighty God, and in all our actions both go before us by inspiring us and guard us by helping us. You who live.

Another.—May your grace always go before us, we ask, almighty God, and follow after us, so that through the coming of your only-begotten Son, whom we await with the deepest desire of our heart, we may obtain both the supports of the present life and those of the future. You who live and reign with the Father, God.

Another.—O God, who see that we trust in your goodness, mercifully grant that through the coming of your only-begotten Son we may always rejoice in heavenly protection. You who live and reign with the Father, God.

Another.—May your mercy come to our aid, O Lord, so that, when you come, we may merit to be saved from the imminent dangers of our sins. You who live and reign.

Another.—Stir up your power, O Lord, and come, so that we may be saved by your favor. You who live.

Another.—Hasten; do not delay, Lord our God, and powerfully free us from the devil’s fury. You who [Col. 0196C] live.

Another.—Let us all rejoice, we ask, Lord our God, gathered in unity of faith, all upright of heart, so that when our Savior, your Son, comes, we may meet him undefiled in the company of his saints. You who live with the Father.

Another.—Make us, we ask, O Lord, reject our evils with all our heart, so that when your Son, our Lord, comes, we may be able to receive his goods. You who live and reign.

Another.—Gird, we ask, Lord our God, the loins of our mind powerfully with your divine strength, so that when our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, comes, we may be found worthy of the banquet of eternal life and may merit to receive from him the pledges of heavenly dignities. [Col. 0196D] You who live and reign.

Another.—Make us, we ask, Lord our God, watchful and attentive in awaiting the coming of Christ your Son, our Lord, so that when he comes knocking, he may find us not sleeping in sins but awake and rejoicing in his praises. You who live and reign, God.

[Note: [Col. 0195D] In Pamel’s edition there are also many prayers for sins, but they differ entirely from ours, except for a few. Although the Royal Codex of Saint Pamel usually agrees with the printed editions, there are nevertheless quite a few passages in which the readings are varied and different. Thus, in Prayer 6, page 373, where it reads “may we serve you with free minds,” the manuscript codex should be followed: “may we always glory in your benefits.” In Prayer 8, on the same page, where the edition has “daily calamities,” the manuscript better reads “long-lasting calamities.” On page 174, line 18, where it reads “so that from merit there may be joy of your mercy,” it should be restored from the cited codex as “so that from sorrow there may be joy,” and so forth. We have noted these few examples so that it might be clear that many things in Pamel’s edition can be corrected from the Royal Codex of Saint Pamel, whose variant readings we possess. In the Calensian manuscript, prayers for sins—morning prayers, daily prayers, and so on—are also presented here, as they are in some of our other manuscripts.]

(653) ## Here Begin the Prayers for Sins

Come to the aid of your suppliant people, we ask, O Lord, and graciously grant your help to the sick, so that, devoted to you with sincere mind, they may rejoice in the remedies of the present life and of the future. [Col. 0197A] Through the Lord.

Another.—O God, who are justly angry and mercifully forgive, look upon the tears of your afflicted people; and in your favor turn away the anger of your indignation, which we justly deserve. Through the Lord.

195 Another.—We ask, almighty God, that we who are wearied by our offenses and afflicted by the merit of our iniquity may merit to attain the grace of your goodness. Through.

Another.—O God, whose proper work is always to show mercy and spare, receive our supplication, and may your merciful goodness release those whom the chain of sins binds. Through our Lord.

Another.—Grant us, we ask, O Lord, joy from tribulation, so that we who have long been afflicted for our sins may, through the intercession of blessed N., your martyr, breathe freely in your mercy. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Another.—Graciously hear the prayers of those who cry out to you, we ask, O Lord, so that just as you spared the Ninevites when they were placed in affliction, you may likewise come to our aid in the present tribulation. Through.

Another.—Mercifully look upon our tribulation, we ask, O Lord, and in your favor turn away the anger of your indignation, which we justly deserve. Through the Lord.

Another.—O God, who do not wish the souls of sinners to perish, but rather their sins, restrain the anger which we deserve and pour out upon us the mercy which we ask, so that we may merit to obtain, from sorrow, the joy of your mercy. [Col. 0197C] Through.

Another.—We ask, almighty God, look upon the tears of your afflicted people and turn away the anger of your indignation, so that we who acknowledge the guilt of our weakness may be freed by your consolation. Through.

Another. — O God, who are offended by sin and appeased by repentance, mercifully regard the prayers of your suppliant people, and turn away the scourges of your anger which we deserve for our sins. Through the Lord.

Another. — Spare, O Lord, spare your people, so that, chastised by deserved scourges, they may recover breath in your mercy. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Another. — O God, refuge of the poor, hope of the humble, and salvation of the wretched, mercifully hear the supplications of your people, so that those whom the justice of scourges has afflicted may be consoled by an abundance of remedies. [Col. 0197D] Through.

Another. — Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who recognize our offense through the scourges may feel the grace of your consolation. [Col. 0198A] Through our Lord.

Another. — Do not despise, almighty God, your people crying out in affliction, but, for the glory of your name, mercifully come to the aid of the afflicted. Through.

—Another. Hear, O Lord, the groaning of your people; may the offense of those who sin not prevail with you more than your mercy, granted in response to the tears of those who plead. Through our Lord.

Another. — Almighty God, mercifully bestow your mercy upon us, so that we who incur guilt by despising you may obtain pardon by confessing. Through.

Another. — May the affection of the people subject to you move your goodness, we ask, O Lord; and may faithful supplication obtain your mercy. Through.

[Col. 0198B] Another. — Turn away your anger from us, we ask, O Lord, once appeased, and drive away our crimes by which we provoke your indignation. Through the Lord.

Another. — Remember, we ask, O Lord, human frailty, and you who justly scourge sinners, mercifully spare the afflicted. Through.

Another. — Incline the ears of your goodness, we ask, O Lord, to our prayers, so that we who are struck by the scourges of our sins may be freed by the grace of your mercy. Through.

(654) [Note: In the edition of Pamel, *prayers for the daily offices*. But in [Col. 0198D] Codex Regius S., the title is the same as in the edition of Menard, although in nearly all other respects it agrees with the edition of Pamel. From it, nevertheless, many things lacking in this edition can be restored. Thus, on p. 376, three lines from the end, it reads: “and to whom you grant the hope of mercy.” But the manuscript supplies: “to whom you grant confidence in the hope of mercy.” In the edition of Angelo Rocca, printed at the Vatican press and often reprinted elsewhere, most recently under the care of Peter Gussanville, this long series of daily, evening, morning, and other prayers is found, with only a few exceptions.]

Here begin the Daily Prayers.

May the voice of the Church crying out ascend to the ears of your goodness, O Lord, we ask, so that, having received forgiveness of sins, she may become devoted through your working and secure under your protection. [Col. 0198C] Through our Lord.

Another. — Be gracious to our supplications, O Lord, and be ready to be entreated by your suppliants, so that, once the pardon we ask has been granted, we may forever glory in the gift of your mercy. Through our Lord.

Another. — Be gracious, O Lord, to our times, we ask, so that both the security of Rome and Christian devotion may be directed by your gift. Through our Lord.

Another. — Look graciously upon our days, we ask, O Lord; and mercifully absolve us from sins and kindly rescue us from every adversity. Through.

197 Another. — We ask, almighty God, that your mercy not abandon us, but always remove our errors and drive away every harmful thing. Through.

[Col. 0198D] Another. — Grant, we ask, almighty God, that amid the countless errors of the present life we may always be guided by your direction. Through our Lord.

Another. — Guard in perpetual peace, we ask, O Lord, [Col. 0199A] those whom you have granted to hope in you. Through the Lord.

Another. — Be present to us, merciful God, and, once appeased, grant us the gifts of your goodness. Through.

Another. — Mercifully govern our wills, O Lord, so that they may neither become entangled in their own iniquities nor be subjected to those of others. Through our Lord.

Another. — Restrain, O Lord, we ask, the harmful assaults that continually arise, and mercifully grant peaceful security in our times. Through.

Another. — Defend us always, we ask, O Lord, from every adversity, and protect us with continual safeguards. Through the Lord.

Another. — Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who, conscious of our weakness, trust in your power may always rejoice under your goodness. [Col. 0199B] Through our Lord.

Another. — Make us rejoice, we ask, Lord our God, in devotion to you, because happiness is perpetual and complete if we serve the Author of every good. Through.

Another. — Almighty and everlasting God, make us always bear a will devoted to you and serve your Majesty with a sincere heart. Through our Lord.

Another. — O God, from whom all good things proceed, grant your suppliants that, with you inspiring us, we may think what is right and, with you guiding us, do the same. Through.

Another. — May our voice always plead with you, O Lord, and ascend to the ears of your goodness. Through the Lord.

Another. — Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may serve you with minds set free. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0199C] Another. — So that we may obtain your mercy, O Lord, make us devoted to you with our whole heart. Through.

198 Another. — Receive our prayers, O Lord, and mercifully regard the pious hearts of those crying out to you. Through.

Another. — Always drive every iniquity away from us, O Lord, so that with a secure mind we may hasten along the way of eternal salvation. Through our Lord.

Another. — Look upon us, our Redeemer, O God, and grant that we may continually serve you. Through our Lord.

Another. — O God, ruler of heaven and earth, kindly bestow upon us the help of your protection. Through.

Another. — Grant, we ask, merciful God, that we may serve you with a mind pleasing to you. Through our Lord.

Another. — May your forgiveness purify us, O God, and always guard us from every iniquity. [Col. 0199D] Through.

Another. — Be present to us, merciful God, and, once appeased, preserve your gifts toward us. Through.

Another. — Strip us, O Lord, of all our iniquities, and make us rejoice in your peace. Through.

Another. — Break apart, we ask, O Lord, the bonds of human wickedness, so that with a free mind we may hasten to confess your name. Through.

Another. — May your grace, O Lord, bless us and lead us to eternal life. Through our Lord.

Another. — Look upon our weaknesses, O Lord, and come swiftly to our aid in your goodness. Through our Lord.

Another. — Make us, we ask, O Lord, reject our evils with our whole heart, so that we may be able to receive your good things. [Col. 0200A] Through.

Another. — Be gracious to us, O God, so that your mercy may follow us. Through our Lord.

Another. — May your mercy precede us, we ask, O Lord, and may the kindness of your appeasement anticipate our voices. Through.

Another. — Come swiftly to our aid in your goodness, we ask, O Lord, so that the devotion of those who plead may pass into thanksgiving. Through.

Another. — Wipe away our offenses, O Lord, by which adversities dominate us, and guard us everywhere by your mercy. 199 Through.

Another. — Loosen, we ask, O Lord, the bonds of our sins, and turn away whatever we deserve on account of them. [Col. 0200B] Through.

Another. — May our prayers ascend to you, O Lord, and drive every wickedness from your Church. Through.

Another. — Mercifully hear us crying out to you, O God, so that you may rescue us from the depths of iniquity and lead us to eternal joys. Through.

Another. — Grant us, we ask, O Lord, forgiveness of our offenses, and overcome those who strive to attack you. Through.

Another. — May your grace, O Lord, both precede and follow us always, and continually make us attentive to good works. Through.

Another. — Look upon us, merciful God, and make us truly obedient to your name. Through.

[Col. 0200C] Another. — Protect us, heavenly ruler, and defend our frailty with your safeguards. Through.

Another. — So that we may restrain ourselves from our offenses, O Lord, grant that we may continually practice your commands. Through.

Another. — Take away from us, we ask, O Lord, our wickedness, so that we may experience not your indignation but your forgiveness. Through.

Another. — So that you may cherish us with every aid, mercifully make us suited to your disciplines. Through.

Another. — May our eyes always look toward you, O Lord, so that we may feel your help and mercy. Through.

Another. — Remembering human condition, forgive our sins, we ask, O Lord, and turn away whatever we deserve in repayment for them. Through.

[Col. 0200D] Another. — Stretch out your right hand to us, O God, and the help of heavenly power. Through.

Another. — Hear us, Lord our God, and govern your Church, tossed amid the storms of the world, with merciful direction. Through.

200 Another. — Regard your suppliants, O Lord, we ask, and kindly grant us both forgiveness and joy. Through.

Another. — Look upon us, almighty and merciful God, and, once appeased, free us from every tribulation. Through.

Another. — Do not regard our iniquities, O God, but let your mercy alone benefit us, unworthy as we are. Through.

Another. — Make us, Lord our God, obey your commands, [Col. 0201A] because all good things will then come to us if we follow you, the author of our entire life. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0201D] In the edition of Pamel, the Morning Prayers precede these, and there are far more of them here, and they are almost entirely different. In the old Gallican Sacramentary only two of these prayers are found, [Col. 0202D] namely the first, “Almighty,” etc., and the sixth, “Be gracious,” etc.]

Other Evening Prayers (655).

Almighty and everlasting God, at evening, morning, and midday we humbly beseech your Majesty that, having driven the darkness of sins from our hearts, you may bring us to the true light, which is Christ. Through.

Another. — As we perform the offices of evening praise, we humbly ask your kindness, O Lord, that, under your protection, we may overcome the deceits of the nocturnal assailant. Through.

Another. — Be gracious to our evening supplications, O Lord, and make us appear before you in the morning praises without any guilt. Through.

[Col. 0201B] Another. — Hear your servants, O Lord, as they render evening vows to your name, and graciously deign to guard through the night’s rest those whom you have preserved at every moment of the day. Through.

(656) Prayers at the Cross.

We ask, Lord our God, that through the standard of the holy cross of your Son you may establish us in the security of your protection, so as to crush the ambushes of our adversaries. Through the same Lord.

Another. — We humbly ask your kindness, almighty God, that you defend from the evil enemy those whom you ordained to triumph, through the wood of the holy cross of your Son, with the weapons of righteousness for the salvation of the world. Through the same Lord.

[Col. 0201C] Another. — O God, who willed that your Son undergo the punishment of the cross for our sake, so that you might drive away the enemy’s power from us, grant us, your servants, that, overcoming the ambushes of the ancient enemy by the power of so great a mystery, we may serve you forever with the most sincere mind. Through the same Lord.

201 Another. — O God, whose Son graciously redeemed the world through the trophy of the cross, mercifully grant that we who rejoice in redemption may deserve to enjoy eternal joys. Through the same Lord.

Another. — O God, who through the blood of the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, gave peace to humanity and the fellowship of the heavenly angels, grant us both to be filled with the abundance of your peace and to rejoice in the unity of angelic society. Through the same Lord.

[Col. 0201D] (657) Prayers at Compline.

May the dawn of righteousness arise within us as darkness is born, O Lord, and, when the day is completed, may we give you humble thanks and may you graciously regard us also when we offer our vows in the morning. Through.

Another. — We give you thanks, O Lord, for having been guarded through the day; we offer you thanks for being guarded through the night. Present us, we ask, O Lord, unharmed at the morning hours, so that you may have us as your praisers at all times. Through our Lord.

Another. — Enlighten our darkness, we ask, O Lord, and graciously drive away all the ambushes of the night. [Col. 0202A] Through.

Another. — We ask, Lord our God, that you sustain the troubles of the day with the rest of night, so that, as the necessary succession of times follows, our weakness may be restored. Through.

Another. — Be present to our prayers, O Lord, and protect us day and night, so that amid whatever alternations of time we may always be strengthened by your unchangeableness. Through our Lord.

Another. — O God, who illumine the night and make light follow darkness, grant us to pass through this night without Satan’s hindrance and, returning to your altar in the morning hours, to render thanks to you, God. Through.

[Col. 0202B] Another. — The day is yours, O Lord, and the night is yours; grant us to pass through this night, etc., as above.

Another. — The day is yours, O Lord, and the night is yours; grant that the sun of righteousness may remain in our hearts, to drive away the darkness of wicked thoughts. Through.

(658) Here begin the Morning Prayers.

Enlighten, O Lord, we ask, the hearts of those who believe in you, so that we may always be protected by your defense and your help. Through.

Another. — May your truth, O Lord, always enlighten us and defend us from every wickedness. Through the Lord.

202 Another. — Save us, almighty God, and grant us perpetual light. Through our Lord.

Another. — Hear us, merciful God, and reveal the light of your grace to our minds. [Col. 0202C] Through.

Another. — Mercifully regard the morning vows of those who plead, O Lord, and illuminate the hidden places of our heart with the remedy of your goodness, so that dark desires may not possess those whom the light of heavenly grace has restored. Through.

Another. — Send, we ask, O Lord, your light into our hearts, so that, having received the law of your commandments, we may walk in your way and suffer no error. Through.

Another. — Almighty and everlasting God, before whom nothing is obscure and nothing dark, send your light into our hearts, etc., as above.

Another. — O God, who reward with a heavenly recompense those who keep vigil in your praises, deign to remove darkness from our hearts, [Col. 0202D] so that we may always rejoice in the splendor of your light. Through.

Another. — Rising from our beds, we implore the help of your grace in our morning prayers, O Lord, so that, when the darkness of vices has been dispersed, we may deserve to walk in the light of virtues. Through.

Another. — We beseech you, O Lord, as the true light and author of light, to deign to drive the darkness of vices away from us and glorify us with the light of virtues. Through.

Another. — Increase your faith in us, O Lord, we ask, and always kindle within us the light of the Holy Spirit. [Col. 0203A] Through.

Another. — O God, who dispel the darkness of ignorance by the light of your word, increase in our hearts the virtue of the faith you have given, so that the fire which your grace has caused to be kindled may not be extinguished by any temptations. Through.

Another. — Hear with your ears, O Lord, we ask, the words of our mouth, and, as a merciful examiner, understand our morning cry, so that our devotion in praying to you may be steadfast, and that your contemplation and the desired remission of all sins may be granted to us at daybreak. Through.

Another. — May your truth shine in our hearts, we ask, O Lord, and may every falsehood of the enemy be destroyed. Through our Lord.

Another. — Mercifully pour your holy light into our understanding, we ask, O Lord, [Col. 0203B] so that we may always be devoted to you, by whose wisdom we were created and by whose providence we are governed. Through.

(659) Likewise at Matins, at daybreak.

O God, who distinguish day from night, distinguish our actions from the darkness of obscurity, so that, always meditating on what is holy, we may continually live in your light. Through our Lord.

Another. — We give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, who have graciously brought us from the passage of the night to the morning hours. We ask that you grant us to pass through this day without sin, so that at evening and always we may render thanks to you, God. Through.

Another. — We give thanks to your indescribable goodness, [Col. 0203C] almighty God, who, having driven away the darkness of night, have brought us to the beginning of this day and, having cast away the blindness of ignorance, have recalled us to the worship of your name and to knowledge. Enter into our understanding, almighty Father, so that, walking in the light of your commandments, we may follow you as guide and ruler. Through.

Another. — O God, who have brought us to the beginning of this day, grant us to pass through this day without sin, so that we may in no respect turn aside from your paths; rather, may our words always proceed toward the practice of your righteousness. Through.

At Prime. — Deign to direct, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, our hearts and bodies today toward the works of your commandments, so that on this day we may turn aside to no sin, but always [Col. 0203D] meditate on what is holy, complete it in deed, and everywhere be strengthened by your help. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you as God in the unity of the same Spirit.

Mass for Sins.

Hear, we ask, O Lord, the prayers of those who plead, and spare the sins of those who confess to you, so that you may kindly grant us both forgiveness and peace. Through our Lord.

Over the Offerings. — Be present to us, we ask, O Lord, and kindly hear our prayers, so that what has no confidence in our merits may obtain acceptance through the appeasement of the Offerings. Through.

Preface. — It is truly fitting and just, right and [Col. 0204A] salutary, that we always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, humbly imploring you to rescue us mercifully from all sins and kindly protect us from every enemy. Through Christ.

Within the Canon. — Therefore, O Lord, we ask that you graciously accept this offering which we offer to you for our sins and offenses, so that we may deserve to obtain remission of all our offenses, and that you may order our days in your peace.

204 At the Dismissal. — Grant us, everlasting Savior, that, receiving forgiveness of sins through this gift, we may thereafter avoid sins. Through the Lord.

Another. — May your holy things, we ask, O Lord, strip us of [Col. 0204B] sins and strengthen us with the vigor of heavenly life. Through.

Prayers in Time of War.

Almighty and merciful God, we ask that you make us peaceful amid the turmoil of wars, because you will grant us every good thing if you give peace to both mind and body. Through.

Another. — Almighty God, restrain the enemies of the Christian name by the power of your Majesty, we ask, so that your people may rejoice in the integrity of faith and always exult in the tranquility of the times. Through.

Mass in Time of War.

O God, ruler of all kingdoms and kings, who both heal us by striking us and preserve us by forgiving, extend your mercy to us, so that, with the tranquility [Col. 0204C] of peace established by your power, we may use the remedies of correction. Through.

Another. — O God, whose kingdom is the kingdom of all ages, mercifully hear our supplications and protect the kingdom of Christians subject to you, so that, trusting in your power, they may please you and excel above all kingdoms. Through.

Another. — O God, who crush wars and overcome those who attack those hoping in you by the power of your defense, aid those imploring your mercy, so that, when the savagery of all nations has been subdued, we may praise you with unwearied thanksgiving. Through.

Over the Offerings. — Regard, O Lord, the sacrifice which we offer, so that it may strip us of every wickedness of war and establish us in the security of your protection. Through [Col. 0204D] the Lord.

Preface. — It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary, that we always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, humbly prostrate before you with our whole heart and imploring you to grant us forgiveness for past sins and continually protect us from every assault of mortality. For we do not doubt that your defense will be present when you graciously drive away from us those things by which we offend you. Through Christ.

At the Dismissal. — Strengthened by the nourishment of the most holy Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, we humbly ask you, almighty God, that by this unique remedy you purify us from the contagion [Col. 0205A] of every sin and fortify us against the assault of every danger. Through the same.

205 Another. — Look upon us, O God, our protector, and defend us from the dangers of our enemies, so that, when every disturbance has been removed, we may serve you with minds set free. Through the Lord.

Another Mass.

We ask, O Lord, that you shatter the pride of our enemies and cast them down by the strength of your right hand. Through.

Over the Offerings. — By the power of this mystery, O Lord, we ask, may we be cleansed from our hidden faults and freed from the ambushes of our enemies. Through.

Preface. — It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary, that we always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, who glorify the powers subject to you. Mercifully receive our prayers, we ask, [Col. 0205B] and add strength to our rulers, so that those who seek to be protected by your right hand may be overcome by no adversity. May your invincible defense also fortify your faithful people by your power, so that, ever devoted to you with pious affection, they may be freed from hostile enemies and persevere continually in your grace. Through Christ.

At the Dismissal. — May participation in your holy mystery give us life, we ask, O Lord, and grant us both purification and protection. Through our Lord.

Another Mass.

O God, who by your providence govern heavenly and earthly things together, be gracious to the affairs of Christians and to their kings, [Col. 0205C] so that, while you fight for us, every strength of the enemies may be broken. Through the Lord.

Another. — O God, strength of kingdoms that serve you, be ever graciously present to the rulers of Christians, so that the power of those whose humility is subject to you may everywhere be the greater. Through.

Over the Offerings. — Be gracious, O Lord, to the prayers and Offerings of your servants, and, for the sake of your name, defend the rulers of the Christian name, so that the safety of the rulers who serve you may be the peace of your peoples.

Preface. — It is truly fitting and just, right and salutary, that we always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, under whose authority the power of all kingdoms is contained [Col. 0205D]. We humbly beseech you to deign to be graciously present to our rulers, so that those who seek to be defended by your protection may be stronger than all enemies. Through Christ.

At the Dismissal. — Protect your servants, O Lord, with the aids of peace and of the body; nourish them with spiritual food, and make them secure from all enemies. Through.

Mass for Peace.

O God, from whom holy desires, right counsels, and just works come, give your servants that peace which the world cannot give, so that our hearts may be devoted to your commandments and, with fear of enemies removed, our times may be tranquil under your protection. Through.

[Col. 0206A] Another. — O God, creator of the world, under whose authority the order of the ages proceeds, be present to our invocations and grant peace and tranquility to the present times, so that we may rejoice in unceasing exultation in the praises of your mercy. Through.

Over the Offerings. — O God, who allow no terrors to shake peoples who believe in you, deign to receive the prayers and Offerings of the people dedicated to you, so that, once your peace has been granted through your goodness, it may make the borders of Christians secure from every enemy. Through the Lord.

At the Dismissal. — O God, author and lover of peace, to know whom is to live and to serve whom is to reign, protect your suppliants from every attack, so that we who trust in your defense may fear the weapons of no hostility. Through.

Another. — O God, who by the powerful aid of your mercy [Col. 0206B] both grant prosperity and drive away adversity, overcome every obstacle that opposes your servants, so that, when the terror of wars has been removed, both secure freedom and peaceful religion may prevail. Through.

Mass for Any Tribulation.

O God of infinite mercy and boundless goodness, be gracious to our iniquities and heal all the sicknesses of our souls, so that, having received forgiveness of our sins, we may always rejoice in your blessing. Through.

Over the Offerings. — Mercifully protect us, O Lord, by the divine sacraments, and powerfully grant that we may serve them suitably. Through the same.

Blessing. — May God, the comfort of the sorrowful and refuge of the afflicted, cherish you with his arm and, in his mercy, make you unharmed from the dangers [Col. 0206C] threatening you. Amen. May he fortify you with the shield of the right hand of the almighty and surround you with the impregnable wall of his strength against the tribulation at hand. Amen. Once appeased, may he turn away from you the anger of his judgment, and, granting you the harbor of salvation, establish you secure and unafraid in the safety of his protection. Amen. Which he himself may grant.

At the Dismissal. — May the life-giving reception of the sacrament, we ask, O Lord, fortify your faithful and make them, freed from every vice, advance in holy devotion. Through.

Another Mass.

O God, under whose gaze every heart trembles and every conscience is afraid, be gracious to the sufferings [Col. 0206D] of all who groan and heal the wounds of all, so that, just as none of us is free from guilt, so no one may be excluded from forgiveness. Through.

207 Another. — Almighty and everlasting God, who are felt in fear, worshiped in love, and appeased by confession, pour out your mercy upon those who plead, so that we who distrust the quality of our merits may experience not your judgment but your forgiveness. Through.

Over the Offerings. — Receive, O Lord, once appeased, the Offerings by which you willed both to be appeased and for salvation to be restored to us through the endurance of your goodness. Through.

At the Dismissal. — Protect by divine aid those whom you refresh with a heavenly gift, O Lord, so that, enjoying your mysteries, we may be subjected to no adversities. Through.

Another Mass.

[Col. 0207A]

O God, comforter of the humble and strength of the faithful, be gracious to those who plead, and grant that human frailty, which is naturally inclined toward ruin, may through you always be restored to forgiveness. Through.

Another. — Receive, merciful Lord, the prayers of those who plead, and, according to the multitude of your acts of forgiveness, absolve us from all sins, so that, with you sparing us, we may be restored to every work of goodness; and make those whom forgiveness has made innocent effective through your aid.

Over the Offerings. — May this Offering, O Lord, we ask, always free your Church from hidden guilt and suitably cleanse it from manifest faults. Through.

At the Dismissal. — May the sacraments we have received purify us, O Lord, and make us absolved from every vice. [Col. 0207B] Through.

Another Mass.

We ask your kindness, almighty God, so that where no confidence in our actions is available, your abundant grace may shine forth, both when it forgives sins in the unworthy and when it bestows benefits on the undeserving. Through the Lord.

Another. — Merciful and compassionate Lord, who sustain us by sparing us and sanctify us by forgiving, grant forgiveness for our sins and allow those who serve the heavenly sacraments to be free from every guilt. Through the Lord.

Over the Offerings. — We offer you Offerings of appeasement, O Lord, so that, in your mercy, you may both absolve our offenses and direct wavering hearts. Through the Lord.

At the Dismissal. — We humbly ask you, almighty [Col. 0207C] God, that you graciously shape those whom you refresh with your sacraments into conduct pleasing to you. Through the Lord.

Prayer in a Time of (God forbid) Mortality.

We ask, almighty God, that you graciously regard the assembly of your Church; and may your mercy rather than your anger precede us, because if you wish to observe our iniquities, no creature will be able to stand. But, in the admirable goodness by which you made us, forgive sinners, so that you do not allow the work of your hands to perish. Through.

Another. — Hear our prayers, O Lord, and do not wish to enter into judgment with your servants, because just as no righteousness is found in us on which we can presume, so we acknowledge you as the fountain of goodness, from whom we trust that we may be absolved from our sins and freed from our necessities. [Col. 0207D] Through the Lord.

Over the Offerings. — Through these sacraments, we ask, O Lord, may the effect of our redemption come, which may always draw us back from human transgressions and lead us to all things that bring salvation. Through our Lord.

At the Dismissal. — May the working of this sacrament, we ask, O Lord, always purify and fortify us. Through.

Another Mass.

O God, by whose mercy even the powers of heaven are in need, and in whose sight no human being is without stain and punishment for sin, mercifully turn away the offense of your people, we ask, so that the guilt of their own conscience, which accuses them, may by the patience of your goodness make them worthy of forgiveness. [Col. 0208A] Through our Lord.

Another. — O God, whose goodness is so great that, when one sinner is converted, you cause the greatest joy to be held in heaven, look upon the small portion of your people, so that, when every affliction has been driven away, your inheritance may increase in number and advance in devotion. Through our Lord.

Over the Offerings. — May the saving Offering protect us, O Lord, we ask, and may that which is sacrificed to the honor of your name benefit us unto forgiveness. Through.

At the Dismissal. — May your holy things, once received, give us life, O Lord, and prepare us, purified, for eternal mercy. Through the Lord.

Another Mass.

Hear, O Lord, we ask, your people supplicating your [Col. 0208B] mercy for forgiveness of their evils; and because you are powerful to forgive sins, by the power of your goodness turn away the punishments which we deserve for our works. Through.

Another. — We ask, O Lord, in your mercy turn your anger away from your people, which we indeed deserve because of our works but cannot endure in our human frailty. Therefore contain us within that goodness which you are accustomed to bestow upon the undeserving. Through.

Over the Offerings. — Grant us, O Lord, we ask, that this saving Offering may become both the cleansing of our sins and the appeasement of your power. Through.

209 At the Dismissal. — Look graciously upon the people subject to your name, O Lord, and deign continually to work your consolations in them through heavenly grace. [Col. 0208C] Through the Lord.

Another Mass.

O God, who desire not the death but the repentance of sinners, mercifully convert your people to yourself, we ask, so that, while they remain devoted to you, you may remove from them the scourges of your anger. Through.

Another. — We ask, almighty God, receive your people, fleeing from your anger to you, with fatherly goodness, so that those who fear the scourges of your Majesty may deserve to rejoice in your forgiveness. Through.

Over the Offerings. — May the working of the present sacrifice come to our aid, O Lord, we ask, and powerfully absolve us from every error and rescue us from the assault of total destruction. Through the Lord.

At the Dismissal. — Protect us, O Lord, we ask, as we receive [Col. 0208D] your holy things, and mercifully defend us from every iniquity. Through.

Another. — Hear us, Lord our God, and, with your blessed martyr N. interceding, free your people from the terrors of your anger and make them secure through the abundance of your mercy. Through our Lord.

Prayers for Asking for Rain.

Pour heavenly waters upon your land, O Lord, which we see wasting away because of our iniquities; and irrigate it with the benefits of eternal grace. Through the Lord.

Another. — Give us, O Lord, we ask, saving rain, and graciously pour heavenly streams upon the dry face of the earth. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0209A] Another. — Almighty and everlasting God, who save all and desire no one to perish, open the fountain of your goodness and graciously pour flowing heavenly waters upon the dry earth. Through.

Another. — We ourselves recognize our offenses, O Lord, as the foulness of the earth itself reveals the excess of transgression. But you, most merciful Father, who closed heaven against the stubborn and ungrateful, grant to the humble and contrite who plead the help of rains from the opened heavens, and bestow abundance upon the sorrowful. Through the Lord.

Another. — Grant consolation to those placed in the greatest affliction, fountain of most abundant goodness; may saving rain descend, we ask, so that everything beneath heaven may be irrigated by the waters. Feed your servants with the customary rains, [Col. 0209B] those whom you have graciously created for the praise of your Majesty. Through.

210 Another. — Almighty God, who alone send waters from the heavens, grant your servants the benefit of saving rain, so that what is held back because of our crime may now be prolonged by your gratuitous gift. Through.

Mass for Asking for Rain.

O God, in whom we live, move, and exist, grant us suitable rain, so that, sufficiently assisted by present supports, we may pursue eternal things with greater confidence. Through.

Another. — In your mercy absolve the offenses of our frailty, O Lord, we ask, and provide the support of heavenly waters, by which our earthly condition, renewed, may endure. Through.

[Col. 0209C] Over the Offerings. — Be appeased, O Lord, by the gifts offered, and grant us the timely aid of sufficient rain. Through our Lord.

At the Dismissal. — Protect us, we ask, O Lord, as we receive your holy things, and mercifully absolve us from every sin. Through the Lord.

Another Mass.

Almighty and everlasting God, by whose gift all the elements are renewed, remember your mercies and mercifully grant life-giving rains to the human race, so that the whole earth may rejoice in the nourishment of your fruitfulness. Through.

Over the Offerings. — Be appeased, O Lord, by gifts that are always accepted, and moderate the long-lasting drought with abundant rains. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0209D] **Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, earnestly imploring your mercy: that the parched fields may be watered by fruitful rains, by which the summer heat may likewise be tempered, and the burning force of raging diseases extinguished, and health come to human beings and beasts; and that, by your generosity, we may deserve these things, forgive the sins that oppose us. You who rain upon the just and the unjust: once our offenses too have been forgiven, may you bestow the expected gifts of the clouds, by which both health and nourishment may be provided for us. Through Christ.

**For the conclusion.**—Look favorably, we ask, upon the prayers of your people, Lord, that you may grant pardon for human transgressions and kindly extend your help to the afflicted. Through our Lord.

## Prayers for requesting clear weather

Lord God, who through the ministry of water established for us the mysteries of your salvation, hear the prayer of your people and command the terrors of overflowing rains to cease; turn the scourge of this element toward the accomplishment of your mystery, so that those who rejoice that they have been reborn through regenerating waters may rejoice that they have been corrected through these chastisements. Through.

**Another.**—We ask, almighty God, that you restrain the overflowing rains and deign to grant us the cheerfulness of your countenance. Through the Lord.

## Mass for requesting clear weather
