Hear us, Lord, as we cry out to you, and grant clear air to us who beseech you, so that although we are justly afflicted for our sins, we may, with your mercy going before us, experience your clemency. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—May your grace, we ask, always go before us, Lord, and follow us; and kindly receive these offerings, which we bring to be consecrated to your name for our sins, so that through the intercession of your saints they may benefit us all for salvation. Through.

**For the conclusion.**—May your people, Lord, receive an increase of holy blessing and be raised up by the abundant help of your benefits, since they are assisted by such great prayers of intercession. Through.

## Prayer to repel a storm

God, who through the very movements of the air establish the nature of all things that serve you for the worship of your Majesty, grant us the tranquility of your mercy, with the terrors removed, so that we may experience the clemency of him whose anger we have feared. Through.

## Prayer against lightning

Almighty and eternal God, spare those who fear and show favor to those who entreat you, so that, after the destructive fires of the clouds and the violence of the storms, the threat of your power may pass into material for praise. Through.

**Another.**—God, by whose command everything is governed by a word and everything is changed by prayer, spare those who fear and show favor to those who entreat you, so that, after the destructive fires of the clouds and the whirlwinds of the storms, the threat of your power may pass into material for praise. Through our Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0209D] Since no prayers against an earthquake are found here or elsewhere, it seemed appropriate to append, by way of an appendix, a collect composed most elegantly by the most holy Lord Clement XI, pope. At the beginning of the year 1703, when most of Italy and Rome itself were shaken by earthquakes four times and disfigured by ruins.

[Col. 0210D] Collect for a time of earthquake.

**Prayer.**—Almighty and eternal God, who look upon the earth and make it tremble, spare those who fear and show favor to those who entreat you, so that we may continually experience the clemency of him whose anger, shaking the foundations of the earth, we have feared, and whose clemency heals its shattered places. Through the Lord.

**Secret.**—God, who founded the earth upon its stability, receive the offerings and prayers of your people; and, when the dangers of the trembling earth have been entirely removed, turn the terrors of your divine anger into remedies for human salvation, so that those who are from the earth and will return to the earth may rejoice to be made heavenly through holy conversion. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0212D] **After Communion.**—Protect us, Lord, we ask, as we receive your holy things; and strengthen by heavenly grace the earth that we have seen trembling on account of our iniquities, so that mortal hearts may recognize that such scourges proceed from you when you are angry and cease when you show mercy. Through the Lord.]

[Col. 0211A] **Prayer for brothers being directed on a journey**

God, who always bestow your mercy upon those who love you and are never far away from those who serve you, direct the way of your servant N., according to your will, so that, with you as protector and guide, he may walk without stumbling along the paths of righteousness. Through the Lord.

**Another.**—Hear our prayers, Lord, and graciously accompany the journey of your servant N.; and, since you are everywhere, bestow your mercy everywhere upon him, so that, defended by your help from every adversity, he may obtain the fulfillment of righteous desires and return thanks to you. Through.

**Another.**—God, who lead to life and guard those who trust in you with a father’s protection, we ask that you grant the servant now departing from us the company of an angel, so that, protected by his assistance, he may be shaken by fear of no evil, oppressed by no anguish of adversity, and troubled by no ambushes of the attacking enemy; but, after completing the necessary stages of his journey with prosperous steps and being happily restored to his own places, may he find everyone safe and sound and render due thanks to your name. Through the Lord.

## Mass for those undertaking a journey

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and arrange the way of your servant N. in the prosperity of your salvation, so that amid all the changes of this road and of this life he may always be protected by your help. Through the Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Show favor, we ask, Lord, to our supplications, and kindly receive these offerings that we offer to you for your servant N., so that you may direct his way with your grace going before him and deign to accompany him with your grace following after, so that we may rejoice over his conduct and safety according to the supports of your mercy. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: from whom to turn away is to die, and before whom to walk is to live. You lead your faithful along your way and, in your most gracious mercy, bring them into truth; you willed to be the guardian, guide, and companion of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob throughout the course of this present journey and life, and you prepared an angel to go before your servant Tobias. We implore your immeasurable mercy with the humblest prayers, that you may deign to direct the journey of your servant N. and his companions in prosperity, and to guard him amid all the changes of this journey and life, so that, supported by the protection of your angels and fortified also by the intercession of your saints, defended by your mercy from every adversity, and granted happiness in his departure and return, he may obtain the fulfillment of his righteous prayers and rejoice in the forgiveness of his sins and those of his companions. Through Christ.

[Col. 0212A] **213 Blessing.**—May the Lord direct your journey according to his good pleasure, and may the most gracious guardian remain inseparably with you. Amen. May he give you the archangel Raphael as your guide, and, in his favor, remove from you every misfortune and opposition. Amen. May he mercifully fulfill the pious desires of your hearts, so that here you may deserve to obtain good things and happily reach eternal blessedness. Amen. May he himself grant this.

**For the conclusion.**—God of infinite mercy and boundless Majesty, whom neither distances of place nor intervals of time separate from those whom you protect, be present to your servant N., who trusts in you everywhere, and deign to be his guide and companion throughout every road he is to travel; may no adversity harm him, no difficulty hinder him; may all things be wholesome and all things prosperous for him; and, under the help of your right hand, may he quickly obtain whatever he seeks with a just desire. Through.

## Prayers for making a cleric

Let us pray, beloved brothers, to our Lord Jesus Christ for this servant of his, N., who hastens, for love of him, to have the hair of his head cut off: that he may give him the Holy Spirit, who will preserve the religious habit in him perpetually and defend his heart from the world’s entanglements and from secular desire; so that, just as his appearance is changed, his right hand may grant him an increase of virtue, open his eyes from every spiritual blindness, and give him the light of eternal glory. He lives with God the Father in the unity of the same Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

**Another.**—Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and deign to bless this servant of yours, upon whom in your holy name we place the habit of sacred religion, so that, by your generosity, he may deserve both to persevere devotedly in the Church and to receive eternal life. Through the Lord.

While tonsuring him, say the antiphon: “You are the one, Lord, who will restore my inheritance to me.” Verse: “The Lord is the portion of my inheritance,” and the Gloria. Another antiphon: “This is the generation,” and the Gloria. Another antiphon: “This one shall receive a blessing.”

**Prayer after the tonsure.**—Grant, almighty God, to this servant of yours, N., whose head of hair we have cut off today for divine love, that he may remain perpetually in your love and that you may guard him forever without blemish. Through the Lord.

## Prayers and petitions over a penitent confessing his sins in the customary manner

[Note: [Col. 0212D] Many formulas of confession collected by us formerly may be read in the French treatise on Confession, part, chapters 12, 14, and 19. We proved especially in chapter 21 that there was formerly a great abundance of penitential books, in which the rites both of confession and of priestly absolution were taught. If desired, one may consult very many Orders for imposing penance and reconciling penitents, collected by our Edmund Martene in his work *On the Ancient Rites of the Church*, part two, chapter 6, article 7.]

(662) Hear our prayers, Lord, and spare the sins of those who confess to you, so that those whom the guilt of conscience accuses may be absolved by the indulgence of your mercy. Through the Lord.

**214 Another.**—(663) May your mercy, we ask, go before this servant of yours, Lord, so that all his iniquities may be erased by swift pardon. Through.

**Another.**—(664) Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and let the mercy of your clemency not be far from this servant of yours. Heal his wounds and forgive his sins, so that, separated from you by no iniquities, he may always be able to cling to you, the Lord. Through.

**Another.**—(665) Our Lord God, (666) whom our offense does not conquer, (667) but whom satisfaction appeases, look, we ask, upon this servant who confesses to you that he has sinned grievously. It is yours to grant cleansing from crimes and pardon to sinners, you who said that you preferred the repentance of sinners to their death. Grant, therefore, Lord, that he may keep vigil in penance for you and, once his actions have been corrected, rejoice that eternal joys have been conferred upon him by you. Through.

**Another.**—(669) I beseech, Lord, (670) the clemency of your Majesty and name: deign to grant pardon to this servant of yours who confesses his sins and crimes, and to release the debts of his former offenses. You brought back upon the shoulders of your Son the lost sheep to the folds; (672) you were appeased by the prayers or confession of the publican. Do you also, Lord, be appeased toward this servant of yours; kindly assist him in his prayers, so that, remaining in tearful confession, he may quickly entreat your clemency and, restored to the holy altars, (675) may be renewed in the hope of eternal life and heavenly glory. Through the same Lord.

(677) ## Prayers for reconciling a penitent

(678) Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and mercifully hear me, who am also the first to need your mercy; and, although you appointed me minister of this work not through any merit of election but by the gift of your grace, grant me confidence to carry out your commission, and yourself work in our ministry what belongs to your goodness. Through the Lord.

**Another.**—(679) Grant, we ask, Lord, to this servant of yours worthy fruits of penance, so that, having strayed through sin from the integrity of your holy Church, he may be restored harmless through obtaining pardon for his offenses. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0213D] **Another.**—God, most kind creator of the human race and most merciful restorer, who redeemed with the blood of your only Son the human being cast down from eternity by the devil’s envy, give life to this servant, whom you by no means desire to die and whom you do not abandon when he goes astray; receive him now corrected. May the tearful sighs of this servant of yours move your compassion, Lord, we ask. Heal his wounds; extend to him, as he lies prostrate, your saving hand, lest your Church be ravaged in any part of its body, lest your flock suffer loss, lest the enemy rejoice over the damage to your household, lest a second death take possession of him who has been reborn in the saving bath. To you, therefore, Lord, we pour out our suppliant prayers; to you we pour out the tears of our hearts. Spare him who confesses, so that, with your help, he may lament his sins in this mortal life in such a way that on the day of the terrifying judgment he may escape the sentence of eternal condemnation; and may he not know what terrifies in the darkness and what crackles in the flames. Having turned back from the way of error to the path of righteousness, may he never again be wounded by injuries; but may what your grace has bestowed and what your mercy has restored remain whole and perpetual for him. Through the same Lord Jesus.

## Mass for a deceased bishop

[Note: [Col. 0213D] The same Mass is read in Pamelius’s edition, with the agreement of Codex Regius S., where the reading of the printed edition is not corrupt—something that often happens. Thus, in the prayer that follows, Pamelius reads *educens* instead of *educis*, or *eduxisti*, as Codex Regius S. has. Above, in the final prayer concerning the death of animals, where one reads *ut sine quibus non habetur hum. conditio*, which gives no sense, the text is very correctly written: *ut sine quibus non alitur hum.*, and so forth. In the ancient Gallican Sacramentary there is one Mass for the deposition of a priest and another for the dead generally.]

Grant us, Lord, that you may admit the soul of your servant N., the bishop, whom you lead out of the laborious struggle of the world, to share in the company of your saints. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Grant us, Lord, that this offering may benefit the soul of your servant N., the bishop, since by offering it you granted that the sins of the whole world should be forgiven. Through our Lord.

**Within the Canon.**—Therefore, Lord, we ask that you graciously receive this offering, which we offer to you in commemoration of the deposition of the soul of your servant N., the bishop; and, having willed him, while constituted in the body, to preside over the apostolic see’s governance, place him among the number of your chosen priests; and our days…

**Over the diptychs.**—Remember also, Lord, your servants N., who went before us and sleep in the sleep of peace.

(681) **Also after the lesson.**—For these and for all who rest in Christ, we beseech the gift of a place of refreshment, light, and peace. Through Christ.

**For the conclusion.**—By these sacrifices, we ask, almighty God, may the purified soul of your servant N., the bishop, deserve to reach pardon and eternal refreshment.

## Another Mass for a deceased bishop

[Col. 0214D] God, who caused your servant N., the bishop, to be counted among the apostolic priests, grant, we ask, that he may rejoice forever in heaven in the company of those whose place he held on earth for a time. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—May this offering, Lord, free the soul of your servant N., the bishop, from all the faults of human condition; it is the offering that, once sacrificed, also bore away the sin of the whole world. Through.

**216 Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: with devoted hearts beseeching your clemency, that you may command the soul of N., the bishop, to stand rejoicing among the number of your chosen pontiffs, so that he who here humbly served your altar for them may there rejoice with them in your glorious praise. Through Christ our Lord.

**Within the Canon.**—Therefore, Lord, we ask that you graciously receive this offering of our service, which we offer to you in commemoration of the soul of your servant N., the bishop, and grant him a share in eternal blessedness with the bishops of apostolic dignity, whose office he followed, and cause him to be counted among the distinguished members of the supreme Shepherd; and our days…

**For the conclusion.**—Grant pardon, Lord, we ask, through these holy mysteries, to the soul of your servant N., the bishop, so that it may not be terrified by an evil encounter but be protected by your help. Through.

**Another.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the soul of your servant N., the bishop, whom you adorned with sacred gifts while he dwelt in this world, may exult in a glorious heavenly dwelling. Through the Lord.

## Another Mass for a deceased bishop

Receive, Lord, we ask, our prayers for the soul of your servant N., the bishop, so that he may rejoice in the everlasting dwelling of the pontiffs pleasing to you. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—We offer, Lord, sacrifices of appeasement and praise, so that, through the generosity of everlasting mercy, you may cause the soul of your servant N., the bishop, to rejoice in the realm of eternal light.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: humbly imploring the unspeakable power of your clemency, so that your servant N., established in the tabernacles of the blessed, may boast that he has escaped the bodily afflictions and may await the day of judgment with a prayer of rejoicing. Through Christ our Lord.

**Within the Canon.**—Therefore, Lord, we ask that you graciously receive this offering, which we offer to you for the soul of your servant N., the bishop; and command that he whom you granted to serve your altars belong to the company of blessed priests; and our days…

**For the conclusion.**—We ask, almighty God, that you command the soul of your servant N., the bishop, to share in eternal blessedness in the assembly of the righteous. Through our Lord.

## Another Mass for a deceased bishop

God, who caused your servant N. to flourish with priestly dignity among the apostolic priests, grant, we ask, that he also may forever be gathered into their company. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, Lord, we ask, for the soul of your servant N., the priest, the sacrifices that we offer, so that to him to whom you granted pontifical merit you may also grant its reward. Through the Lord.

**For the conclusion.**—Graciously hear, Lord, we ask, the prayers that we offer at the deposition of your servant N., the bishop, so that he who faithfully performed ministry in your name may rejoice in the everlasting fellowship of the saints. Through the Lord.

## Mass for a deceased bishop

God, who caused your servant N. to flourish with pontifical dignity among the apostolic priests, grant, we ask, that he may forever be gathered into their company. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—May this offering, Lord God, free the soul of your servant N. from all the faults of human condition; it is the offering that, once sacrificed, also takes away the sin of the whole world. Through.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: with devoted hearts beseeching your clemency, that you may rejoice to see the soul of your servant N. stand among the number of your chosen pontiffs, so that he who humbly served your altar for them may there rejoice with them in glorious praise. Through Christ our Lord.

**For the conclusion.**—God, whose mercy is without number, receive our prayers for the soul of your servant N., the priest, and grant him the realm of light and joy in the company of your saints. Through our Lord.

## Mass for a deceased priest

[Col. 0216C]

Grant, we ask, Lord, that the soul of your servant and priest N., whom you adorned with sacred gifts while he dwelt in this world, may always exult in a glorious heavenly dwelling. Through the Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Receive, Lord, we ask, the sacrifices for the soul of your servant and priest N., so that to him to whom you granted pontifical reward you may also grant merit. Through the Lord.

**218 For the conclusion.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you command the soul of your servant and priest N. to share in eternal blessedness in the assembly of the righteous. Through the Lord.

## Mass for one deceased person

[Col. 0216D] Almighty and eternal God, to whom no one ever prays without hope of mercy, show favor to the soul of your servant N., so that you may cause him, who departed this life in confession of your name, to be added to the number of your saints. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Show favor, we ask, Lord, to the soul of your servant N., for whom we offer you sacrifices of appeasement; and, since he remained in the Catholic faith in this light, may his recompense be granted in the life to come. Through our Lord.

**For the conclusion.**—Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you may cause the soul of your servant N., received by the angels of light, to be led into the prepared dwelling places of the blessed. Through the Lord.

## Mass on the day of the deposition of the deceased, or on the third, seventh, or thirtieth day

[Note: [Col. 0217D] The two Theodori have substantially this title, but their prayers and Preface are entirely different.]

[Col. 0217A]

Be present, Lord, we ask, for the soul of your servant N., for whose deposition we perform this office of commemoration; if any worldly stain clung to him or any worldly vice infected him, forgive and cleanse him by the gift of your goodness. Through our Lord.

**Another.**—We ask, Lord, for your servant N., whose third, seventh, or thirtieth day after death we commemorate: grant him the company of your saints and chosen ones, and pour upon him the perpetual dew of your mercy. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—Be present, Lord, to our supplications; and graciously and kindly receive this offering, which we offer on the third, seventh, or thirtieth day of the deposition, for the soul of your servant N.

**Preface.**—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Through him come the salvation of the world, the life of human beings, and the resurrection of the dead. Through him we humbly beseech you, Lord, that you may deign to grant perpetual pardon to the soul of your servant N., whose third, seventh, or thirtieth day of deposition we celebrate, and, freed from the contagions of mortality, restore it to a share in eternal salvation. Through him to your Majesty…

**219 For the conclusion.**—Almighty and eternal God, deign to place the body and soul of your servant N., whose third, seventh, or thirtieth day of deposition we celebrate, in the bosoms of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so that, when the day of recognition of you has come, you may command him to be raised among your saints and chosen ones. Through our Lord.

## Mass on the anniversary of the deposition of one deceased person

Grant, Lord, we ask, that the soul of your servant N., whose annual day of deposition we celebrate, cleansed by these sacrifices, may likewise receive everlasting pardon and rest. Through the Lord.

**Over the offerings.**—Show favor, Lord, we ask, to our supplications for the soul and spirit of your servant N., whose annual day is observed today and for whom we offer a sacrifice of praise, that you may deign to join it to the company of your saints. Through the Lord.

**For the conclusion.**—Receive, Lord, our prayers for the soul of your servant N., so that, if any stains from earthly contagions have clung to it, they may be erased by the remedy of your forgiveness.

## Mass for many deceased persons

Show favor, we ask, Lord, through everlasting mercy to the souls of your servants, men and women, N. and N., so that, freed from mortal bonds, eternal light may possess them. Through.

**Over the offerings.**—We bring you, Lord, with humble appeasement, sacrifices, so that through these rites of appeasement the souls of your servants, men and women, may obtain your mercy. Through.

**For the conclusion.**—May the souls of your servants, men and women, N. and N., and of all who rest in Christ, find a share in eternal light—those who, placed in this light, attained your sacrament. Through.

(683) [Note: [Col. 0217D] The same things are read afterward in the Vatican and Gussanville editions. Whoever wishes to know more about this subject should consult our Edmund Martene, *On the Ancient Rites of the Church*, chapter 8, concerning the rites pertaining to the sacrament of orders, article 11. There he presents twenty-three orders, excerpted chiefly from manuscript books, which teach how ministers of the Church are ordained among the Latins, Greeks, Maronites, Nestorian Syrians, Jacobite Syrians, Eutychians, and Copts.]

# HERE BEGINS THE ORDER FOR BLESSING THE SACRED ORDERS

(685) The higher grades are conferred before the Gospel, but the lower after Communion; the lower, indeed, on Sundays, if necessary, but the higher only on the Saturdays of the twelve readings during the four Ember seasons.

## Ordination of a doorkeeper

[Note: [Col. 0218D] Almost all these things are found in the first Theodorus, where the text is not mutilated; nevertheless, it reads in the plural: “Orders of readers, exorcists,” and so forth.]

(688) When the doorkeeper is ordained, after the archdeacon has instructed him how he ought to conduct himself in the house of God, the bishop, at the archdeacon’s prompting, hands him the keys of the church, saying: “Act as though you were going to render an account to God for the things opened by these keys.” And the deacon hands him the door of the church.

**Preface of the doorkeeper.**—(692) Let us humbly beseech God the almighty Father to deign to bless this servant of his, N., whom he has deigned to choose for the office of doorkeeper, so that he may keep the most faithful watch by day and night, at the appointed division of the hours, to invoke the name of the Lord; with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with him lives and reigns as God in the unity of the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.

(694) **Blessing of the same.**—Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, deign to bless this servant of yours, N., the doorkeeper, so that among the gatekeepers of the Church he may perform his duties and deserve to have a share of your reward among your chosen ones. Through our Lord.

## Ordination of a reader

(696) When the reader is ordained, the bishop shall speak about him to the people, indicating his faith, life, and ability; afterward, in the presence of the people, (698) he shall hand him the book from which he is to read, saying:

(700) Receive this, and be a messenger of the word of God. If you faithfully and beneficially fulfill your office, you will have a share with those who have ministered the word of God. Your brothers choose you to be a reader in the house of your God. Recognize your office and fulfill it; for God is able to increase grace for you.

[Col. 0219A] **Blessing of the reader.**—(701) Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, deign to bless this servant of yours for the office of reader, so that, distinguished and ordered by constant reading, he may both proclaim what must be done and fulfill in deed what he has proclaimed, and in both respects serve the holy Church. Through the Lord.

## Ordination of an exorcist

(704) When the exorcist is ordained, he shall receive from the bishop’s hand a booklet in which exorcisms are written, while the bishop says to him:

(706) Receive this, commit it to memory, and have the power to lay your hand upon one possessed, whether baptized or a catechumen.

(708) **Preface of the exorcist.**—(709) Let us humbly beseech God the almighty Father to deign to bless this servant of his, N., for the office of exorcist, so that he may be a spiritual commander for driving demons from possessed bodies, together with all their manifold wickedness, with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with him lives and reigns as God in the unity of the Holy Spirit.

**221 Blessing of the exorcist.**—(710) Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, deign to bless this servant of yours, N., for the office of exorcist, and deign to choose him for the ministry of the laying on of hands and of the mouth, so that he may have authority to restrain unclean spirits and may be an approved physician of the Church, strengthened by the power of the grace of healings. Through the Lord.

## Ordination of an acolyte

[Col. 0219C] (714) When the acolyte is ordained, (715) he shall first be taught by the bishop how he ought to act in his office; but (716) he shall receive from the archdeacon a candlestick with a candle, so that he may know that he is assigned to light the lamps of the church, (718) with these words addressed to him:

(719) Receive this bearer of light, so that through it you may be able to drive away the darkness of your adversaries and faithfully find the truest light, which enlightens every person coming into the world.

(720) He shall also receive an empty vessel (721) for pouring (722) wine into the Eucharist of the body.

**Blessing of the acolyte.**—(723) Almighty and eternal God, source of light and origin of goodness, who through Jesus Christ your Son, the true light, enlightened the world and redeemed it through the mystery of his passion, deign to bless this servant of yours, whom we consecrate to the office of acolyte. We ask your clemency that you may illuminate his mind with the light of knowledge and water it with the dew of your loving-kindness, so that he may perform the ministry he has received in such a way that he may deserve to attain eternal reward. Through the same Lord our Lord.

(724) ## Ordination of a subdeacon

**Chapter of Saint Gregory.**—(725) Just as one who, when invited, refuses, and, when sought, withdraws, is to be removed from the sacred altars, so one who seeks office voluntarily or thrusts himself forward importunately is without doubt to be rejected. For one who strives to climb to higher things—what does he do except decrease as he increases? Why does he not consider that the blessing is turned into a curse for the one who is promoted in order to become a heretic?

[Note: [Col. 0219D] Thus Hugo Menardus reads, as is clear from his note. In the printed Vatican and Gussanville editions, however, the reading is *admovendus* (“to be advanced”); this reading is confirmed by the letters of Saint Gregory, both printed and copied by hand. Moreover, scarcely any suitable meaning can be fitted to Menardus’s reading.]

(727) When the subdeacon is ordained, since he does not receive the laying on of hands, let him receive from the bishop’s hand an empty paten and an empty chalice; from the archdeacon’s hand let him receive a cruet with a basin and a towel. Let the empty paten and chalice be displayed in the bishop’s sight, and let the bishop say:

(732) See what ministry is entrusted to you; therefore, if until now you have been slow to attend the Church, from now on you must be assiduous; if until now sleepy, from now on watchful; if until now drunk, from now on sober; if until now dishonorable, from now on chaste. The offerings that come to the altar are called the bread of offering. Of these offerings only as much ought to be placed on the altar as can suffice for the people, lest anything rotten remain in the sacristy. The cloths that are on the underlaying cloth must be washed in one vessel, and the corporal cloths in another. Where the corporal cloths have been washed, no other linen ought to be washed there; the water itself must be poured into the baptistery. Therefore, I admonish you: present yourself as one who can please God.

And he shall hand him the chalice and paten.

[Col. 0220C] **Ordination of the subdeacon.**—(735) Let us pray to God and our Lord that upon his servant N., whom he has deigned to call to the office of subdeacon, he may pour out his blessing and grace, so that, faithfully serving in his sight, he may attain the rewards predestined for the saints, with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with him lives and reigns as God.

**Blessing of the subdeacon.**—(736) Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, deign to bless this servant of yours, whom you have deigned to choose for the office of subdeacon, so that you may establish him as an energetic and diligent soldier in your holy sacristy and in the heavenly warfare, and so that he may faithfully assist at the holy altars; and may the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and fortitude, the Spirit of knowledge and piety, rest upon him. Fill him with the Spirit of your fear and strengthen him in divine service, so that, obedient in deed and submissive in word, he may obtain your grace. Through our Lord, and so forth, in the unity of the same Spirit.

(737) **Order of how deacons and priests are to be ordained in the Roman Church**

[Note: [Col. 0220D] In the first Theodorus all these things are omitted up to “Let us pray, beloved,” in the following column, which is preceded by “Prayers for ordaining deacons.” The remaining material concerning the ordination of a priest and bishop is presented according to the same rite.]

In the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth months, on the Saturday of the twelve readings, at Saint Peter’s, where Masses are celebrated, after they have said the Entrance Antiphon and the prayer has been given, the archdeacon comes and offers the one who is to be ordained to the pontiff, saying:

“Holy mother, the Catholic Church, requests that you ordain this present subdeacon to the burden of the diaconate, or this deacon to the burden of the priesthood.”

The bishop asks: “Do you know that he is worthy?”

The one presenting him responds:

“As far as human frailty permits us to know, I both know and testify that he is worthy of this burden of office.”

Then the pontiff announces to the people, saying:

“With the help of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ.”

Again he says:

“With the help of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, we choose for the order of the diaconate or priesthood N., a subdeacon or deacon, from the titular church of N.; N., a priest, from the titular church of N. (738) But if anyone has anything against these men, let him come forward confidently, for God and on account of God, and speak. Nevertheless, let him remember his own condition.”

After a short interval, all immediately begin “Kyrie eleison,” with the litany. When this has been completed, the elected men themselves ascend to the bishop’s seat, and he blesses them for the office to which they have been called. After receiving the blessing, they descend and stand in their proper order. (741)

223 When a deacon is ordained, only the bishop who blesses him should place his hand upon his head, because he is consecrated not to the priesthood but to the ministry. (742) In ordaining a deacon and a priest, the first prayer is said by reading it. And the prayer follows. “It is truly worthy” is not said in the consecration. [Col. 0221C]

Prayer.—Let us pray, beloved, to God the almighty Father, that he may graciously pour out the grace of his blessing upon this servant of his, whom he deigns to admit to the sacred order, and grant him the gift of consecration, through which he may lead him to eternal rewards, with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with him. (743)

Let us pray.—Hear our prayers, O Lord, and send upon this servant of yours the Spirit of your blessing, so that, enriched with a heavenly gift, he may be able to obtain the grace of your Majesty and offer others an example of living well. Through the Lord, etc., in the unity of the same. (744)

Consecration.—Be present, we ask, almighty God, giver of honors, distributor of orders, and arranger of offices. You who, remaining in yourself, renew all things, and who, arranging everything through your Word, Power, and Wisdom, Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, prepare and distribute everything by eternal providence according to what is suitable for each time. You grant that his body, your Church, distinguished by the variety of heavenly graces and joined together by the ordered distinction of its members, united by the wonderful law of the whole structure, may grow and expand for the increase of your temple; and you establish the service of the sacred ministry to serve your name in three grades of ministers.

From the beginning you chose the sons of Levi, who, remaining faithfully at watch in the mystical works of your house, were to possess by perpetual lot the inheritance of eternal blessing. [Col. 0222A]

Look graciously also, we ask, upon this servant of yours, O Lord, whom we humbly dedicate to serve in your sanctuaries in the office of deacon. We, indeed, as human beings ignorant of divine understanding and supreme reason, judge his life as far as we can. But you, O Lord, do not overlook what is unknown to us, nor do hidden things deceive you. You are the knower of secrets and the searcher of hearts. You can examine his life by the heavenly judgment in which you always prevail, both cleansing what has been committed and granting what must be done. (746–747)

Send upon him, O Lord, we ask, the Holy Spirit, by whom he may be strengthened for faithfully carrying out the work of the ministry through the gift of your sevenfold grace. May the complete pattern of every virtue abound in him: modest authority, steadfast sense of shame, purity of innocence, and spiritual observance of discipline. May your commandments shine forth in his conduct, so that the holy people may gain an example for imitation from his chastity; and, giving a good testimony of conscience, may he remain firm and steadfast in Christ. May he deserve, through your grace, to attain greater things by worthy advancement from the lower degree. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ. [Col. 0222B]

(748) When you clothe him with the stole, say:

“By this sign we humbly impose upon you the office of the diaconate, so that you may be able to be, like the supports of columns, a firm support of the divine table, and may deserve to become irreproachable heralds of the heavenly King.” (749)

[Col. 0222C] When a priest is ordained, while the bishop blesses him and keeps his hand upon his head, all the priests who are present are also to hold their hands upon his head beside the bishop’s hand.

Prayer for the ordination of priests.

Let us pray, beloved, to God the almighty Father, that he may multiply heavenly gifts upon this servant of his, whom he has chosen for the office of the priesthood, and that, with the help of the Lord our Jesus Christ, he may carry out with his assistance what he receives through God’s favor. (750)

Let us pray.—Hear us, we ask, O Lord our God, and pour out upon this servant of yours the blessing of the Holy Spirit and the power of priestly grace, so that you may preserve forever, through the generosity of your gift, the one whom we present for consecration before the gaze of your loving-kindness. [Col. 0222D] Through the Lord. (751)

Consecration.—Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, author of honors and distributor of all dignities, through whom all things advance and through whom all things are made firm, while the growth of rational nature is always enlarged for the better according to an appropriate order arranged by reason. (753–754) Thus also the priestly ranks and the offices of the Levites, established through mystical sacraments, increased, so that, after appointing supreme priests to govern the peoples, you might choose men of the next order and second rank to assist their fellowship and work. (755)

Thus, in the wilderness, you extended the spirit of Moses through the minds of seventy prudent men, and with these helpers he easily governed innumerable multitudes among the people. Thus, in Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron, you poured forth the abundance of their father’s fullness, so that the ministry of the priests might suffice for saving sacrifices and the sacraments of more frequent service.

By this providence, O Lord, you added to the apostles of your Son, the teachers of faith, companions through whom they filled the whole world with secondary preachers. Therefore grant these helps also to our weakness, O Lord, since the more fragile we are, the more we need them.

Grant, we ask, almighty Father, the dignity of the priesthood to this servant of yours. Renew within him the Spirit of holiness, so that he may retain the gift of second merit received from you, O God, and, by the example of his conduct, instill moral discipline. Let him be a worthy co-worker in our order, and let the whole pattern of justice shine in him, so that, destined to render a good account of the stewardship entrusted to him, he may attain the rewards of eternal blessedness. Through the same Lord. [Col. 0223B]

(756) Here clothe him with the chasuble.—“May the blessing of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit descend upon you, so that you may be blessed in the priestly order and offer appeasing sacrifices for the sins and offenses of the people to almighty God, to whom are honor and glory forever and ever.”

225 Consecration of the hands.—May these hands, we ask, O Lord, be consecrated and sanctified through this anointing and our blessing, so that whatever they bless may be blessed, and whatever they sanctify may be sanctified. Through. (757)

[Note: In the Vatican Edition and others, before the prayer for the ordination of a bishop, the following is placed here: “Examination to be made in the ordination of a bishop before the litany.” Namely, the man to be ordained bishop is questioned about the articles of faith.] [Col. 0223D]

[Col. 0223C] When a bishop is ordained, two bishops are to place and hold the Book of the Gospels upon his head; while one pours out the blessing over him, all the other bishops who are present are to touch his head with their hands. (758–761)

Prayer for the ordination of bishops. (762)

Let us pray, beloved, that the kindness of almighty God may grant the abundance of his grace to these men chosen to provide for the benefit of the Church. Through our Lord. (763–764)

Blessing of bishops.—Be present to our supplications, almighty God, and may what must be carried out through the ministry of our humility be fulfilled by the effect of your power. Through. (765)

Another.—Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and, bending over this servant of yours the horn of priestly grace, pour out upon him the power of your blessing. Through. (766) [Col. 0223D]

[Note: Before this consecration, the cited editions also include prayers for giving the ring and for giving the staff, that is, the pastoral staff.] [Col. 0224D]

Consecration.—God, author of all honors, God of all dignities that serve your glory through consecrated orders, God who, among the other instructions of heavenly worship, taught your servant Moses through the speech of intimate counsel, and commanded the chosen Aaron to be clothed in mystical garments amid the sacred rites, so that succeeding posterity might derive understanding from the examples of those who came before, and no age might lack the instruction of your teaching—since among the ancients the very appearance of the symbols possessed reverence, while among us the realities themselves provide more certain evidence than the enigmas of figures—for the garment of that former priesthood is the adornment of our mind, and the glory of the pontiff is now commended to us not by the honor of garments but by the splendor of souls, since those things which then delighted carnal eyes rather demanded that what was contained within them should be understood: (767–772)

Therefore grant, we ask, O Lord, to this servant of yours, whom you have chosen for the ministry of the high priesthood, this grace: whatever those coverings signified through the gleam of gold, the brilliance of gems, and the variety of manifold workmanship, may shine forth in his character and actions. [Col. 0224B]

Here you receive the chrism.—“Complete, O Lord, in your priest the fullness of your mystery, and, furnished with the ornaments of complete glorification, sanctify him through the flower of heavenly ointment.” [The source marks *sanctifica* (“sanctify”) with a critical sign: +sanctifica.] (773–774)

Here you pour it upon his head.—“May this +flow abundantly upon his head; may this +run down upon the parts beneath his mouth; may this descend to the extremities of his whole body,” [the critical signs mark *influat* (“flow”) and *decurrat* (“run down”), respectively], “so that the power of your Spirit may both fill his inner being and encompass his exterior. May steadfastness of faith, purity of love, and sincerity of peace abound in him. Grant him, O Lord, the episcopal chair for governing your Church and the whole people. Be his authority; be his firmness; be his power. Multiply your blessing and grace upon him, so that, always fit by your gift to plead for your mercy, he may always be devoted through your grace. Through.” (775–777) [Col. 0224C]

(778) If a pope has been ordained, the following must be added where the text says:

“And therefore grant, we ask, O Lord, to this servant of yours, whom you have given as the bishop of the apostolic see, the primate of all priests throughout the world, and the teacher of your universal Church, and whom you have chosen for the ministry of the high priesthood, this grace.” (779)

Over the offerings.—May this offering, O Lord, cleanse our offenses, and may the sacrifice to be celebrated sanctify the bodies and minds of those subject to you. Through our Lord. (780)

Within the Canon.—Therefore, O Lord, graciously receive this offering of our service, and also of your whole household, which we offer to you for your servant N., whom you have deigned to advance to the order of the episcopate; and mercifully preserve your gifts in him, so that what he has obtained through a divine gift he may carry out through divine effects; and grant that our days, etc. (781) [Col. 0224D]

At the Completion.—May this communion, O Lord, cleanse us from guilt and make us sharers in heavenly healing. [Col. 0225A] Through our Lord Jesus Christ. (782)

Prayer on the birthday of the pope. (783)

God, who, although you are great in great things, nevertheless gloriously perform wonderful works in the smallest, grant that I, your unworthy servant, may serve the sacred mysteries appropriately, and in all things may your mercy protect me, whom the guilt of conscience accuses. Through.

Another.—God, who care for your peoples through indulgence and rule them through love, give the Spirit of wisdom to those to whom you have entrusted the governance of discipline, so that the pastors may find eternal joys in the progress of the holy sheep. Through our Lord.

Over the offerings.—I offer you, O Lord, a sacrifice of praise, humbly imploring that, through the intercession of your blessed apostle Peter, you may mercifully carry out what you have conferred upon me undeservedly. Through.

Preface.—It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, because, since our days and life rest in your hand, just as you grant us unworthy men the honor of the ministry, so also, in your mercy, grant an increase of rational service. Preserve your gifts in us, so that through the intercession of the one in whose place you have wished me to preside over your Church today I may always be found acceptable to you. Through Christ. [Col. 0225B]

At the Completion.—Filled with the nourishment of the sacred Body and precious Blood, we ask, O Lord our God, that through the intercession of your blessed apostle Peter you may mercifully guard and strengthen the gift of your grace, which you have conferred upon us undeserving. Through our Lord. [Col. 0225C]

(784) Proper Mass on the day of his ordination.

God, who commanded me to preside over your household not through merits that support me but solely through the gift of your ineffable grace, grant that I may worthily render to you the ministry of priestly office, appropriately serve in ecclesiastical ministries, and grant that I may govern the people entrusted to me, while you protect me in all things. Through.

Another.—God, Creator and ruler of the world, look favorably upon the prayers of my humility, and make me, your servant, whom you have allowed to serve the heavenly mysteries not through any supporting merits but through the immense generosity of your kindness, a worthy minister at the sacred altars, so that what is spoken by my voice for celebration may be confirmed by your sanctification. Through our Lord. [Col. 0225D]

Over the offerings.—As we return each year to the festivals of the beginning of the priesthood for the glory of your name, O Lord, we offer you a sacrifice of praise, humbly asking that, though we unworthily serve you in the office of his ministry, we may be made acceptable through his intercessions. Through.

Within the Canon.—Therefore, O Lord, graciously receive this offering which I, your servant and priest, offer to you on the day on which you have deigned to establish me as a priest in the sacred ministry; humbly beseeching your Majesty, I ask that you graciously preserve in me what you have deigned to bestow. Through. [Col. 0226A]

[Note: In the Benedictional there is another prayer for the anniversary of the consecration of a bishop.] [Col. 0225D]

Blessing.—May almighty God, who uses the ministry of priests among his people, grant you the gift of his favor and blessing. Amen.

“And may he who, although I possess no merits, wished through his free loving-kindness to place me over this Church, through the intercession of his saints absolve me from every bond of sins and make me an energetic and worthy minister at his holy altars. Amen.

“So that, walking in the examples of the holy priests who pleased him in this see and in this ministry, and, with his help, governing the flock entrusted to us according to his will, we may deserve, together with our subjects, to receive from Christ the Lord, the Shepherd of all shepherds, the rewards promised to the saints, and to be joined to the number of the elect. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this.” [Col. 0226B]

228 At the Completion.—May the hearts of your faithful, O Lord, be filled with your consolations, and may they likewise give thanks both for the bishop of the Church and for the fullness of their prayers. Through.

Prayers for an attained dignity.

God, whom every power and dignity serves, grant to your servant N. a prosperous exercise of his dignity, in which he may always fear you and continually strive to please you. Through the Lord.

Another.—O Lord, fountain of all good things and of righteous advancement, grant, we ask, that your servant N. may exercise well the dignity he has attained and prove through good works that it has been granted to him by you. Through our Lord. [Col. 0226C]

(785) Prayer for making an abbot.

[Note: Absent from the other editions.] We ask, almighty God, that you accompany your servant N., whom we have chosen to govern souls, with the gift of your grace, so that, by your giving, we may also please you through our election itself. Through.

(786) [Note: This apology, together with the following one, is contained in the Vatican and Gussanville editions. In the old Gallican Missal another apology is found, although it scarcely differs in sense.] [Col. 0226D]

BEGIN THE APOLOGIES.

(787–793) The duty of ministering impels me to offer the saving sacrifice of the people for sin; my conscience terrifies me because of the guilt of an unmerited priesthood. If I, the *peripsema* (offscouring) of all priests, offer the sacrifice, the crime of a polluted conscience is increased. If it is not offered to the Judge of all flesh, to so great a Majesty, the guilt of negligence is charged against me.

Amid these things I implore the balance of your mercy, almighty God, whose day of vengeance I dread because my conscience accuses me. Do not, I ask, judge unworthy of your mercy the one whom you do not exclude from the time of repentance. Suspend the axe until the cultivator of the vineyard brings a basket of manure to the root of the fruitless tree.

Spare me, most merciful Lord, a penitent, you who mercifully recalled David to forgiveness after his fall; you who, in your mercy, regarded Peter’s tears as he wept bitterly; you who, by divine grace, enlightened the thief, guilty of so great a crime, on the gibbet of the cross. His confession openly acknowledged the Son of God; faith won a reward, punishment forgiveness, and lamentation everlasting joys, since, a confessor on the cross, he became possessor of paradise after the cross.

But since my words require your forgiveness and the works of an unworthy priest do not commend them, at least receive the prayers of those standing here, so that through their prayers before you I may receive forgiveness, and through their merits the sacrifices of our wounds may beneficially bring us healing. Since you, almighty God, became an offering for sins on behalf of all, be our sanctification in the sacrifice for offenses, Christ, Savior of the world, who with the eternal Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign as God. Through all ages of ages.

Another apology.—Before your eyes, O Lord, I stand as a guilty man with my conscience as witness; I scarcely dare to ask what I do not deserve to obtain. For you know, O Lord, everything that is done within us. We blush to confess what we do not fear to commit through ourselves. We serve you only with words, we lie with our heart, and by our actions we prove that we do not want what we say we want. (795–800)

Spare us, O Lord; forgive us who confess. We have sinned; have mercy, we ask you. And because my understanding is weak in your sacraments, grant, we ask, that although you do not receive the words of our hard heart from us, you may grant us forgiveness through yourself. Through the Lord. (801–805)

Another apology.—Although our conscience trembles, almighty God, we approach your altar, yet we retain confidence in the mercy of your loving-kindness. And although we are always found unworthy to celebrate sacrifices, if we withdraw, we fear being condemned for disobedience. Therefore deign, through paternal mercy, to look upon us with a favorable face and cleanse the inner depths of our heart.

And although we are bound and constrained by the weight and guilt of our sins, nevertheless, through the appeal of our prayers, may the mysteries to be consecrated be pleasing to you in all things, we ask, O Lord. Through. (806–809)

Another apology.—Forgive, O Lord, forgive me: while I am compelled to pray, while I take your holy name upon unclean lips, and while I confess the secrets of shameful deeds, I have no words before you that are free from guilt. For you know the wounds of my conscience and the hidden things of my thoughts, and you alone recognize my uncleanness.

Have mercy on me, O Lord, have mercy on me. Forgive me as I handle the secrets of your mystery, and do not judge unworthy of your mercy the one whom you permit to pray for others. Although you do not acknowledge in me the testimony of a good work, at least do not reject the office of the stewardship entrusted to me. Through our Lord. (810–815)

Another.—I ask you, most high God of Sabaoth, holy Father, to deign to gird me with the tunic of chastity, surround my loins with the belt of your love, and burn the inward parts of my heart with the fire of your charity, so that I may be able to intercede for my sins and merit forgiveness for the sins of the people standing here. As I approach you boldly, do not allow me to perish, but deign to wash me, adorn me, and receive me gently. Through our Lord Jesus. (816–817) [Col. 0228A]

Another.—Before the presence of the eternal King Christ, our unworthy proclamations approach, though they are capable of obtaining forgiveness for the people’s offenses. Conscience is tortured by resentment, because it thrusts itself, guilty, into the offering of the sacred mysteries; and, when it looks upon what it has committed, it is terrified to stand confused before your sight.

But I, a humble guilty man, ask this: because I return to you astray after my fall, lie wounded, and, worthless, breathe in you, good physician, wounded as I am, may you, who command that clean sacrifices be offered upon your altars, sanctify, together with the merits of those who offer, the polluted lips of an unworthy priest—since you recognize that I, wretched one, need your mercy, Christ, illustrious Savior. You live and reign. (818–819) [Col. 0228B]

230 Another on the feast of the saints.—May the intercession of your saints deliver us, we ask, O Lord; and just as you forgave the sins of the people through your servant Moses, so through the intercession of your saints command that the sins of us all be released. Through the Lord. (820)

Daily apologies proper to a priest.—

[Note: In the cited editions this is read together with the following two, “Through the stings,” etc., and “I confess myself unworthy,” etc. The earlier Theodulf also presents apologies of this kind, partly similar and partly different. Among them, the following should be noted, which is still familiar to us with a few changes: “Open, O Lord, my mouth to bless your name; and cleanse my heart from every varied and wicked thought, so that I may deserve to be heard when I pray to you for the people whom you have chosen.”] [Col. 0228D]

Warned by the stings of an accusing conscience and by the memory of our sins, we implore you, God of forgiveness, that whatever has been committed in word, deed, or thought, whether through the impulse of slippery youth or through the error of ignorance, our Lord Jesus Christ may deign to loosen and forgive. Through. (821–825) [Col. 0228C]

Another.—I confess, O Lord, that I am unworthy of your sacred things, since I am darkened daily by countless sins. What do I presume to ask you with flattering words, when I so often offend you by wicked deeds? You pour medicine into me, while I do what is contrary to my health. I read your law inscribed upon the sacred pages, but in my misery I neglect sound discipline.

I approach your altar, to be sure, as though devoted; yet with a rebellious heart I depart from your commandments. Grant me, therefore, O Lord, a contrite heart, by which I may truly hate sin. If you grant it, it is mine to mourn my offenses; it is yours also quickly to wipe away that cloud, so that I, who have lost this palm because the enemy defrauded me, may at least attain forgiveness through your mercy, O Lord.

For to you, God, belongs honor, King of all kings, who reign throughout all ages of ages. (826–834)

Another.—We are cast down, O Lord, under condemnation for our deeds: give water to our head and pour into our eyes a fountain of tears, so that, washing away the stains of sin, we may overcome the flames of avenging punishments through the abundance of our weeping, because nothing that we do is hidden from you.

Let there be in us, O Lord, not merely confession of the mouth but also of sorrow; not an excuse for crimes but lamentation for sins. The wanton sight of the world has violated the chaste eyes of our body. Our morals are corrupt, discipline is spoiled, there is pretense in the face, deceit in words, fraud in the heart, fickleness on the tongue, foolish action, a doubtful mind, carnal desire, concern for the flesh, forgetfulness of the soul, neglect of holiness; and, beyond these, the fear of death has increased.

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us. Grant forgiveness for the past, correction for the present, and protection for the future. Through. (835–843) [Col. 0229A]

Another.—Thus, O Lord, guilty of immense crime, with conscience as witness, we are confounded, so that we can approach your office neither securely nor freely. For who, weighing his sin, would not wish to hide himself from your face, if it were permitted to turn away from the eyes of such great Majesty—if one could escape by lying hidden or evade punishment by concealment?

Or who would not rather desire to see you, if he did not fear even more that you already see here whatever he does while sinning? Therefore, because you find us everywhere, we flee to you, from whom we cannot flee. For the wretched there remains not concealment but tears. May indulgence cherish those whom offense terrifies. Power threatens, but may mercy console. From you comes the one who frees; through you comes the one who excuses.

Spare us, almighty Father; and may you deign to reward with recompense those whom you see humbled by guilt. Those whom you understand to be wretched through confession, do not make confused in the examination. Through the Lord. (844–846) [Col. 0229B]

Another in tribulation.—[Note: This apology is read, with some changes, in certain old Gallican Sacramentaries.] [Col. 0229C]

If, O Lord, we compare before your eyes the offenses we have committed with the wounds we suffer, what we endure is less than what we deserve. We feel the punishment of sin, yet do not avoid the obstinacy of sinning. Under your scourges our frailty is broken, but our iniquity is not changed. The sick mind is tormented, but the stiff neck is not bent. Life sighs in pain, but does not improve in conduct.

If you wait, we are not corrected; if you avenge, we do not endure. Under correction we confess what we have done; at the visitation we forget what we wept over. If you press your hand upon us, we promise to do what is required; if you suspend the sword, we do not fulfill our promises. If you strike, we cry out that you should spare us; if you spare us, we again provoke you to strike. If distress comes, we ask for time to repent; if mercy comes to our aid, we abuse the patience that spared us.

The inflicted wound has scarcely passed, yet the ungrateful mind does not even remember what it endured. If you hear us quickly, we grow insolent through mercy; if more slowly, we murmur through impatience. O Lord, we want you to preserve what you have made, but we do not fear observing what you have commanded.

You have before you guilty people who confess; spare us, because you are compassionate. We know that unless you forgive, you would rightly punish us. But with you there is abundant mercy and overflowing propitiation. Grant without merit what we ask, you who made from nothing those who would ask you.

As we cry out to you, “O Lord, have mercy,” may a faithful and tearful voice move your mercy; and may that loving-kindness in which we place all our hope not count what we have offended, while it regards what we ask. Although it is a great misery that we are guilty, may it be a greater mercy for you that we are wretched.

As suppliants, with your help, we place before you both the evils of our crime and our sorrows; by praying to you we await the mercy which we rejected by sinning. Grant as forgiveness what you are asked to grant to those whom you recognize as having no confidence in your justice.

Raise us up, O Lord our God, and lift us up in your mercy, so that, through communion in salvation and the joy of love, while we ourselves desire to be saved by your gift, we may also rejoice in the faith and peace of all who govern. Through the Lord. (847–868) [Col. 0230B]

Another.—Forgive, O Lord, the one made filthy by the defiled path of conscience and held captive by the confusion of crimes, who deserves nothing for himself but stands to pray for others. If you deign, O Lord, receive from me the groans of captives, the tribulations of peoples, the dangers of nations, the distress of the poor, the needs of travelers, the want of the weak, the despair of the sick, the decline of the aged, the sighs of the young, the vows of virgins, and the laments of widows.

And since the same chain that binds your people also binds me, and I mourn our common sufferings, may a prayer burdened by sins not harm your people. Through me the vow is offered to you; through you may my duty be fulfilled. Through. (869–876) [Col. 0230C]

232 Another.—God, to whom we desire to draw near, and for whose glory we ask to be purified in honor of your martyrs, prepare us for yourself as a living offering. Wash the hidden places of our hearts from every crime, and fill us with spiritual joy.

May we who groan before you both for our own offenses and for those of our brothers deserve to be heard by you without delay, so that we may be punished neither for our own sin nor for another’s, and, clothed in justice and holiness, may be presented to you unharmed on the day of judgment. (877)

Another.—Forgive, O God, whatever the careless rebuke of our mouth has bitten into our subjects through the intemperance of an accusing tongue. Spare whatever we have said that fell short of perfection in goodness; forgive whatever we have spoken improperly or with insufficient restraint. Let not presumption punish me for having been unwary; rather, let the mercy of your compassion absolve me, who acknowledge my iniquities. [Col. 0230D]

And because I have no confidence elsewhere except in your mercy, arm my mouth also with the proclamation of truth [the manuscript reads *per arma*, “through weapons”], and sanctify my work with fuller abundance, so that you may save me, though unworthy, and justify the flock entrusted to me through your loving-kindness.

Whatever you see corrupted in them, heal; whatever you see defective in me, cure. If through the fault of my lukewarmness or through negligence they have contracted or are contracting any stain, overlook it. If, whether without my knowledge or knowingly, they have fallen into sin, and if they have collapsed through the offense of my example, forgive them; and for such faults do not repay wretched me with punishment.

Yet for those whom I seem to have subjected to the judgment of rebuke, may the rebuke itself also profit them for salvation, and may this prayer, intervening for the offense, recall them from error, so that they may not suffer the tortures of hell to which, as mortals, we imposed the laws of penance. Thus, sparing both sides from their harms, grant forgiveness to their iniquities and wash away the offense I have contracted through the difficulty of carrying out my office.

Give ear, O God, to our sacrifices, and write me and those entrusted to me in your records, so that, together with the flock committed to me, I may be cleansed from every crime and deserve to reach you in peace. Make peaceful, O God, the dwelling of our hearts by expelling carnal vices.

And may I, who strive to exercise the highest virtues among my subjects, deserve, when you judge, to be crowned peacefully with the angels, once the afflictions of minds and bodies have been pacified. Therefore, we ask, gracious God, make us, as we look toward you in your presence, aflame through the gift of your grace, so that zeal for your house may consume us.

And so, through the strength of the Holy Spirit, may we temper our governance of our subjects, so that they may gain profit from the disciplines of our rule, their hardness may be broken, and their life sanctified. Receive, O Lord, the libations of our vows, and through them may we rejoice that whatever correction we impart to our subjects by word or merit has profited both us and them—not toward discord but toward everlasting joy of sweetness.

Wash us, O God, from both another’s offense and our own, so that, receiving in both cases the efficacy of spiritual grace, we may pray to your name with greater confidence. Through the Lord. (878–893) [Col. 0231C]

(894) Prayers for visiting the sick.

First, let the priests prepare blessed water with salt sprinkled into it, and let them sprinkle it, with the antiphon and prayers, over the sick person himself and over his house. (895–896)

233 Exorcism of salt.—I exorcize you, creature of salt, by the living God, by the true God, by the God who commanded you to be cast into the water by the prophet Elisha so that the barrenness of the water might be healed, so that you may become exorcized salt for the salvation of believers and be health of soul and body to all who take you. May every phantom and wickedness, every deceit of diabolical fraud, and every unclean spirit adjured by him who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire flee and depart from every place where you are sprinkled. (897) [Col. 0231D]

Blessing of salt.—We humbly implore your immense clemency, almighty eternal God, that in your loving-kindness you may deign to bless and sanctify this creature of salt, which you have given for the use of the human race, so that it may be salvation of mind and body for all; and so that whatever is touched or sprinkled with it may be free from every uncleanness and every assault of spiritual wickedness. Through.

Exorcism of water.—I exorcize you, creature of water, [Col. 0232A] in the name of God the almighty Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ, his Son, our Lord, so that you may become exorcized water, able to drive away every power of the enemy and to uproot and tear out the enemy himself with his apostate angels, through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire.

### Blessing of Water

God, who for the salvation of the human race established the greatest sacraments in the substance of water, attend to our invocations and pour out the power of your blessing upon this element, prepared by manifold purifications, so that this creature of your mystery, serving you for the expulsion of demons and the driving away of diseases, may receive the effect of divine grace; so that whatever this water sprinkles in the houses or places of the faithful [Col. 0232B] may be free from every impurity and delivered from harm. Let no pestilential spirit remain there, nor any corrupting breath; let every ambush of the hidden enemy depart; and if there is anything that either envies the safety of the inhabitants or their peace, may it flee at the sprinkling of this water, so that the health sought through the invocation of your name may be defended from every assault. Through Christ.

### Blessing of Salt and Water Together

Here salt is put into the water.

God, author of unconquerable power, and King of an inseparable dominion, ever-glorious triumphant victor, who restrain the powers of the opposing dominion, who overcome the savagery of the roaring enemy, who powerfully defeat hostile wickedness: we trembling and suppliant beseech you, Lord, and ask that you graciously receive this creature of salt and water, kindly enlighten it, and sanctify it according to the custom of your loving-kindness, so that wherever it has been sprinkled, through the invocation of your holy name, every assault of the unclean spirit may be cast away, [Col. 0232C] and the terror of the poisonous serpent driven far off; and may the presence of the Holy Spirit graciously deign to be everywhere with us who ask for mercy. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0231D] Thus in the Codex, although Pamelius thinks that *invictae* should be read *insuperabilis* (“unconquerable”). Shortly afterward, [Col. 0232D] in the Codex of Grimold, one also reads *more*, not *rore* (“dew”), as in the printed Missals.]

### Prayer When Water Is Sprinkled in a House

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and deign to send your holy angel from heaven, to guard, cherish, protect, visit, and defend all who dwell in this habitation. Through Christ.

### Blessing of a House

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and illuminate this house with the serene eyes of your loving-kindness. May the abundant blessing of your grace descend upon its inhabitants, so that, dwelling safely in these dwellings made by human hands, they themselves may always be your habitation. Through the Lord.

### Another

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, so that whatever adversities or hostilities there may be in this house of your servant N., may be driven away by the authority of your Majesty. Through Christ.

### (898) Blessing of Grapes or (899) Broad Beans

Bless, Lord, these new fruits of grapes or broad beans, which you, Lord, have deigned to bring to maturity through the dew of heaven, the abundance of rains, and seasons serene and tranquil, so that we may receive them with thanksgiving in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Who lives and reigns with you.

### Blessing for New Fruits

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who created heaven and earth and all things, we humbly beseech you to bless and sanctify this new fruit, and to multiply it abundantly for those who offer it to you, so that you may fill their storehouses with the strength of grain and wine, and so that, rejoicing in these things, they may render praises and thanks to you, almighty God. Through Christ.

### Blessing for Anything You Wish

Bless, Lord, this creature, so that it may be a salutary remedy for the human race; and grant, through the invocation of your name, that whoever partakes of it may receive health of body and protection of soul. Through Christ.

### Blessing of Bread

Bless, Lord, this creature of bread, as you blessed the five loaves in the desert, so that all who taste it may receive health both of body and of soul. You who live with God the Father in unity.

[Note: The same prayer is found in the edition of Pamelius, but in a much different order.]

### (901) Prayer for Cutting the Hair

(902) Almighty and eternal God, look favorably upon this servant of yours, N., whom [Note: [Col. 0233D] In the Royal Swedish Codex: “for the grace of cutting the hair.”] you have deigned to summon to the grace of a fresh cutting of the hair, granting him remission of all sins and [making him] a partaker of heavenly gifts and precepts. (903) Through Christ.

### 235 Prayer for Cutting the Beard

[Col. 0233C] God, at whose spirit every mature creature rejoices together, hear our prayers for this servant of yours, N., rejoicing in the beauty of youthful age. At the first beginning of his tonsure, hear, Lord, that, fortified in all things by the help of your protection, he may receive heavenly blessing and rejoice in the defenses both of the present life and of the eternal one. Through Christ.

[Note: The old Gallican Sacramentary contains a blessing over him who is tonsured for the first time in the Church; its meaning is almost the same as that of this prayer.]

### Prayer for Anointing a Sick Person

I anoint you with holy oil, as Samuel anointed David king and prophet. Work, creature of oil, in the name of the almighty Father, so that no unclean spirit may lie hidden there, neither in his limbs, nor in his marrow, nor in any joint of his members; but may the power of Christ Most High and of the Holy Spirit dwell in you. Through the same Christ.

### [Col. 0233D] Prayer for Visiting a Sick Person

God, who granted your servant Hezekiah fifteen additional years of life, may your power likewise raise your servant N. from the bed of illness to salvation. Through Christ.

### Another

Look, Lord, upon your servant N., laboring under bodily illness, and refresh the soul which you created, so that, purified by chastisements, it may immediately feel itself saved by your healing. Through Christ.

### Another

God, who always rule your creation with loving tenderness, incline your ear to our supplications and, appeased, look upon your servant N., laboring under adverse bodily health; visit him with your salvation, and grant him the medicine of heavenly grace. Through Christ.

### Another

God, who have bestowed upon the human race both the remedy of salvation and the gifts of eternal life, preserve in your servant N. the gifts of your virtues, and grant that he may feel your healing not only in body but also in soul. Through Christ.

### Another

God of the heavenly powers, who by the authority of your command drive every sickness and every disease from human bodies, graciously be present to this servant of yours, N., so that, his illnesses driven away and his strength restored, he may immediately bless your holy name with renewed health. Through our Lord.

### Another

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal [Col. 0234B] God, who strengthen the frailty of our condition through the gracious infusion of your power, so that our bodies and limbs may be invigorated by the salutary remedies of your loving-kindness, look favorably upon this servant of yours, N., so that, every bodily necessity of illness having been removed, the grace of his former health may be perfectly restored in him. Through our Lord.

Then the priest is to say this prayer:

Lord God, who spoke through your apostle: “Is anyone among you sick? Let him bring in the presbyters of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with holy oil in the name of the Lord; and the prayer of faith will save the sick man, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him”; we beseech you, our Redeemer, that by the grace of the Holy Spirit you cure the illnesses of this sick person, heal his wounds, forgive his sins, drive away all pains of heart and body, and mercifully restore to him complete inward and outward health, so that, restored and healed by the help of your mercy, he may be renewed for the former duties of your loving service. Through Christ.

And thus the sick person is to bend his knee or knees and stand at the priest’s right hand, and this antiphon is to be sung:

The Lord spoke to his disciples: “In my name cast out demons; and lay your hands upon the sick, and they shall be well.” Psalm: “The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken.” And it is repeated: “In my name,” etc.

### The Prayer Follows

Let us pray to our Lord Jesus Christ, and with every supplication let us beseech him to deign to visit, gladden, and strengthen this servant of his, N., through his holy angel.

### The Antiphon Follows

Come to the aid of this sick person, N., Lord, and heal him with spiritual medicine, so that, restored to his former health, he may, once well, render thanks to you. Psalm: “To the Lord, when I was in distress.” Another antiphon follows: Heal, Lord, this sick person, whose bones are troubled and whose soul is exceedingly troubled; but you, Lord, turn and heal him, and deliver his soul. Psalm: “Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger,” with the Gloria; and they repeat: “Heal, Lord.”

And thus he is to anoint the sick person with sanctified oil, making crosses on the neck and throat, between the shoulders, and on the chest; or he is to anoint more extensively wherever the pain is more severe. While the sick person is being anointed, one of the priests is to say this prayer:

### The Prayer Follows

I anoint you with holy oil in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, so that no unclean spirit may remain in you, neither in your limbs, nor in your marrow, nor in any joint of your members; but may the power of Christ Most High and of the Holy Spirit dwell in you, so that through the working of this mystery, through this anointing with consecrated oil, and through our supplication, having been healed or comforted by the power of the Holy Trinity, you may deserve to recover your former and improved health; [Col. 0235B] healed or comforted, [you may deserve] to receive your former and improved health. Through the same Christ.

### The Following Prayer
