Lord God, our Savior, who are true salvation and medicine, and from whom all health and healing come, and who instruct us through the teaching of the apostle to touch the sick with the liquid of oil while praying, look favorably upon this servant of yours, N.; him whom illness bends toward death and weakness of strength draws toward decline, may the healing of your grace restore to salvation.

Heal also, we beseech you, O healer of all, the torments of his fevers and every illness; dissolve his sickness and the sufferings of all pains; heal the inward parts of his viscera and hearts, as well as of his marrow and thoughts; heal the ravages of ulcers; empty out the corruptions of vanities; cover with scars the old wounds of consciences and sores; remove immense sufferings; reform the substance of flesh and blood; grant forgiveness of all sins. May your loving-kindness continually guard him, so that health may never lead him to correction, nor illness now, with your help, lead him to destruction. May this sacred anointing with oil become for him the expulsion of his present disease and illness, and the desired remission of all sins. Through our Lord.

### Another

May the Lord be gracious to all your iniquities, heal all your illnesses, redeem your life from destruction, and satisfy your desire with good things—he who alone, one God in the Trinity, lives and reigns through immortal ages of ages. [Col. 0235D] Amen.

Then he is to receive the body and blood of the Lord. And they are to do this for him for seven days, if necessity requires, both regarding Communion and the other office; and the Lord will raise him up, and, if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him.

The priests and ministers of the holy Church should also, with the greatest reverence, sing Vespers and Matins for the sick each day, with the hymn “Christ, heavenly medicine of the Father,” and the rest, together with the antiphons, responsories, readings, and prayers pertaining to this.

[Col. 0236A] Many priests also anoint the sick in the five senses of the body: on the eyebrows of the eyes, inside the nostrils and on the tip of the nose or externally, on the outer lips, and on the outer hands—that is, on the outside. On all these members they are to make a cross with consecrated oil, saying: “In the name of the +Father, and of the +Son, and of the +Holy Spirit.”

They are to do this so that, if any stain has adhered to the five senses of the mind and body, it may be healed by this medicine of God.

### Prayer at the Conclusion of This Office

Almighty and eternal God, who come to the aid of those laboring in dangers and necessity, we humbly beseech your Majesty to deign to send your holy angel, [Col. 0236B] who may lift up your servant N., laboring in distress and need, by your consolations, through which he may obtain help in the present and attain eternal remedies. Through our Lord.

## Mass for a Bishop or a Congregation

Almighty and eternal God, who alone perform great wonders, extend over your servant N. and over all entrusted to him the spirit of saving grace, and pour upon them the perpetual dew of your blessing, so that they may truly please you. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Look favorably, Lord, upon the offerings of your servant N. and of all entrusted to him, and may they feel that the offerings which we devoutly celebrate for them in honor of your name advance their healing. [Col. 0236C] Through the Lord.

### At the Conclusion

Accompany your servant N. and all entrusted to him perpetually, Lord, with these heavenly gifts as their protection; never cease to cherish them, and grant that they may be made worthy of eternal redemption. Through Christ.

## Another Mass

Almighty and eternal God, have mercy on your servant N., and direct him according to your clemency in the way of eternal salvation, so that, by your gift, he may desire what pleases you and accomplish it with all his strength. Through Christ.

### Over the Offerings

May this offering which we humbly present to your Majesty, Lord, advance, we beseech you, toward the salvation of your servant N., so that your providence may direct his life everywhere amid adversity and prosperity. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

Having received the sacraments of perpetual salvation, we beseech your clemency, Lord, that through them you protect your servant N. from every adversity. Through Christ.

### Another at the Conclusion

Guard your servant N. always, we beseech you, Lord, with your protection, so that he may serve you with a free mind and, under your protection, be secure from every evil.

[Note: In the Cal. Codex there are many votive Masses, namely, one of the Most Holy Trinity; one of wisdom; one for requesting the grace of the Spirit; one in honor of Saint Mary; one for requesting angelic intercession; one of Saint John the Baptist; one of Saint Peter; one of Saint Stephen; one of the holy cross, and so forth; a special Mass for a priest; for the welfare of the living; for relatives; for the king, and so forth.]

## Votive Mass

God, who justify the ungodly and do not desire the death of sinners, we humbly beseech your Majesty graciously to protect your servant N., who trusts in your mercy, with heavenly aid, and to preserve him through continual protection, so that he may always serve you and not be separated from you by any temptations. Through Christ.

### Over the Offerings

By the power of this mystery, Lord, cleanse us from our own sins, we beseech you, and absolve your servant N. from all sins. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

May the sacraments which we have received purify us, Lord, we beseech you, and grant that your servant N. may be free from every guilt, so that, since he is bound by the guilt of conscience, he may glory in the fullness of heavenly healing. Through Christ.

## Special Mass of a Priest

Make me, I beseech you, almighty God, so clothed in righteousness that I may deserve to rejoice in the exultation of your saints, so that, cleansed from every filth of sin, I may obtain fellowship with pleasing priests, and so that your mercy may strip me of every vice, though the guilt of my own conscience weighs me down. Through Christ.

### Over the Offerings

God, who command that you be entreated by sinners and that a sacrifice of a contrite heart be offered to you, deign to accept this sacrifice which I offer with unworthy hands, so that, in your mercy, I may deserve to be both victim and sacrifice to you, and through the performance of this ministry may receive forgiveness of all sins. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

May the reception of this sacrament, Lord, be for me the forgiveness of sins and the desired favor of your loving-kindness, so that, with your help, I may through it become worthy of the sacred mysteries, which, trusting in your goodness, I, unworthy, presume to celebrate. Through Christ.

## Mass for the Welfare of the Living

Extend, Lord, your mercy and the right hand of heavenly aid to your servants and handmaids, N., so that they may seek you with their whole heart, obtain what they rightly ask, and feel your healing not only in body but also in soul. Through Christ.

### Over the Offerings

Be favorable, Lord, to our supplications, and graciously receive these offerings of your servants and handmaids, which we offer to you for their safety. Grant, we beseech you, that no vow may be fruitless and no petition empty, so that what we faithfully ask we may effectively obtain. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

Grant your servants and handmaids, we beseech you, Lord, constancy in your faith and sincerity, so that, strengthened in divine charity, they may not be torn away from its integrity by any temptations. Through Christ.

## Mass for Relatives

God, who have poured the gifts of charity through the grace of the Holy Spirit into the hearts of your faithful, grant your servants, for whom we beseech your clemency, health of mind and body, so that they may love you with all their strength and accomplish with complete love the things that please you. Through Christ.

### Over the Offerings

Have mercy, we beseech you, Lord God, on your servants, for whom we offer this sacrifice of praise to your Majesty, so that through these holy gifts they may obtain the grace of heavenly blessing and acquire the glory of eternal blessedness. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

Having partaken of the divine mysteries, we beseech you, Lord, that these salutary sacraments may advance toward prosperity and peace those for whose love we have offered them to your Majesty. Through the Lord.

## Daily Mass for the King

[Note: The old Gallican Sacramentary contains a Mass for the prince.]

(924) We beseech you, almighty God, that your servant N., who by your mercy has received the governance of the kingdom, may also receive an increase of every virtue, by which, nobly adorned, he may be able both to avoid the monsters of vice and to reach you graciously—you who are the way, the truth, and the life. Through Christ.

### [Col. 0238B] Over the Offerings

Sanctify, Lord, we beseech you, the gifts offered, so that they may become for us the body and blood of your Only-Begotten, and so that, by your generosity, they may everywhere advance King N. toward the salvation of soul and body and toward the fulfillment of the office entrusted to him. Through the Lord.

### At the Conclusion

May this salutary prayer, Lord, protect your servant N. from every adversity, so that he may obtain the tranquility of ecclesiastical peace and, after the passage of this time, reach the eternal inheritance. Through Christ.

## Mass for Peace

God, from whom holy desires, right counsels, and just works come, grant your servants that peace which the world cannot give, so that our hearts, devoted to your commandments, and the fear of our enemies removed, our times may be tranquil under your protection. Through Christ.

### Over the Offerings

God, who permit peoples believing in you to be shaken by no terrors, deign to receive both the prayers and the offerings of the people dedicated to you, so that the peace granted by your loving-kindness may make the boundaries of Christians secure from every enemy.

### At the Conclusion

God, author and lover of peace, to know whom is to live and to serve whom is to reign, protect your suppliants from every assault, so that we who trust in your defense may fear the weapons of no hostility. Through Christ.

## Mass for Any Tribulation

Kindly show us your ineffable mercy, Lord, so that you may both free us from sins and rescue us from the punishments which we deserve for them. Through Christ.

### Over the Offerings

May the offering of this gift purify us, Lord, we beseech you, and make us worthy of participation in sacred things. Through Christ.

### At the Conclusion

Grant, Lord, we beseech you, that, cleansed of earthly affections, we may strive toward the fullness of the heavenly sacrament whose holy gifts we have tasted. Through Christ.

## Mass for the Sick

Almighty and eternal God, eternal salvation of believers, hear us on behalf of your servants N., for whom we implore the help of your mercy, so that, health having been restored to them, they may render thanks to you in your Church. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

God, under whose commands the moments of our life pass, receive the prayers and offerings of your servants, for whose sickness we implore the help of your mercy, so that we may rejoice in the health of those whose dangers we fear. Through the Lord.

### At the Conclusion

God, singular refuge of human weakness, show the power of your help upon our sick, so that, aided by the support of your mercy, they may deserve to be restored to your holy Church. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son.

[Col. 0239]

# APPENDIX TO THE BOOK OF THE SACRAMENTARY OF SAINT GREGORY THE GREAT (C, S)*

[Note: The notes of Hugo Menardus on the Appendix have been printed by Migne as a separate document at columns 263–582. Each number in parentheses in the text of the Appendix refers to the number of the note in that separate document.]

## OLD MASS

From the Codex of Abbot Ratold of Corbie. Sunday, on the holy day of Easter.

[Col. 0239A]

[Col. 0239B] 241 First, before the bishop celebrates Mass, he is to enter a certain oratory and offer himself to God through the libation of prayer, according to the compunction of his heart. Let him say this prayer:

Way of all the saints, Jesus Christ, who have bestowed the joy of brightness upon those coming to you, fill the entrance of this temple with the light of the Holy Spirit—you who consecrated this place by the name or blood of your holy martyrs. Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that all these intercessors may obtain pardon for their offenses, be delivered from every distress, obtain whatever they ask for their needs, and always prevail in pleasing your eyes, so that, fortified through you and through your holy soldier Peter, we may deserve to enter the hall of paradise. Through Christ.

At the third hour of the day, the priestly vestments are to be brought to him. He is to put them on outside the choir, on the left side, in the place of the sacristy. When he has entered the sacristy, let him say this prayer:

Almighty and merciful God, who deign to use the ministry of priests for serving and supplicating you, we beseech your boundless clemency: whatever we now visit, may you visit; whatever we bless, may you bless; and at the entrance of our humility may there be, through the merits of your saints, the flight of demons and the entrance of the angel of peace. Through Christ.

First, let the minister bring leggings extending to the knee, and say: “Lord, we ask you to command that all things be blessed.” The bishop responds:

Almighty God, author of all seemliness, command that these leggings be sanctified through the mystery of our service [possibly: ministry], to restrain the craftiness of the ancient enemy, so that the truth of the Gospel may shine forth in our step and the integrity of faith may be exercised in our mind. Through all ages.

Then let the minister give him sandals and say as above. The bishop responds:

Clothe me, Lord, with the footwear of righteousness, whom John saw clothed in a long robe, so that I may serve you at all times with fear. Through all ages.

[Col. 0240A] After this he is to adorn himself with the remaining vestments, and the minister is to bring the shoulder-cloth and say: “Command, Lord, that it be blessed.” The bishop responds:

Supreme God, excellent ruler of all,

Bless our amice, with which we are now adorned,

[Col. 0240B] So that we may be able to serve you with a pure heart.

Through all ages.

Afterward let him bring him the alb and say as above.

Clothed in angelic garments, O King of mercy,

May we be able to offer a pious offering of fragrance,

And, mercifully, cleanse the contagions of a wicked mind.

And more swiftly remove the contagions of an evil mind.

Through all ages.

Afterward let him bring him the belt and say as above.

Searcher of the heart and lover of a chaste mind,

Gird my loins, intimate God and judge,

Mortifying wicked movements in a chaste body.

Through all ages.

[Col. 0240C] Then let the belt of chastity be given to him, and let the minister say as above. The bishop responds:

I ask you, Most High God Sabaoth, holy Father, to deign to chastise me, gird me, surround my loins with the belt of your fear, and burn the kidneys of my heart with the fire of your charity, so that I may intercede for my sins, obtain pardon for the sins of the standing people, and offer peaceful sacrifices for each person. Through Christ.

Then let the minister bring him the stole of joy, bearing the life of twofold contemplation. Let him say as above. The bishop responds:

To your sacred yoke, O gracious God, my necks must be subjected,

To whose worthy tomb, made precious by death,

[Col. 0240D] Angelic power had taken its seat in ordered ranks,

Through all ages.

243 Above these, let the tunic be brought to him, splendidly fashioned with circles and bells, and let the minister say as above. The bishop responds:

Sanctify this tunic with which I am now clothed,

Almighty eternal God, without whose divinity

No human devotion possesses the power to accomplish anything.

And since you have willed that I use sacred vestments,

[Col. 0241A] Grant me to serve you, merciful judge, with a faithful mind.

Through all ages.

Then let water for the hands and a comb for the head be brought to him, and let the minister say as above. The bishop responds:

Almighty and merciful God, I beseech your clemency: do not let me perish as I approach boldly, but deign to wash me, adorn me, and receive me gently. Through all ages.

Then let the sleeves [or arm-coverings] be brought to him, as above.

May worthy custody by Christ guard our hands,

So that they may be able to handle the memorials of our salvation.

Through all ages.

Afterward let a ring be given to him on his right hand, over the sleeve. Let the minister say as above. The bishop responds:

Guard me, marked with the pledge of faith and the earnest of peace,

with your right hand, O blessed King.

Through all ages.

Afterward let the chasuble be brought to him, and finally the breastpiece [*rationale*], fastened together with the shoulder-cloth. Let the minister say as above. The bishop responds:

O God, eternal and certain hope and salvation of all,

Remember me, who seek you with my whole heart,

So that I may perform worthily the duties of heavenly life.

And while the mystical power is handled by my hands,

May whatever the ancient order had contracted perish.

Through all ages.

Let the maniple of chastity also be given to his left hand, and let the minister say: “Command, Lord, that it be blessed.” The bishop responds:

You who sit above the stars, who guard the scepters of the kingdom,

Supreme God, be present to me as I follow your commands;

And gently bring your right hand in an embrace to my head,

And graciously grant me your help in all things,

So that I may be able to stand before you throughout a chaste life.

Through all ages.

With every diligence, the bishop is also to be honored by his attendants. Once he has been rationally [or: properly; the reading is uncertain] vested in the flammeum [possibly a particular vestment], the entire procession is to approach in ordered fashion: seven, or five, or three, even if there is no presbyter, and a deacon. The presbyter is on the right and the deacon on the left. The subdeacon is to hold the Gospel before his eyes; he is also to be accompanied by two acolytes, or more, with candlesticks [Col. 0241D] and censers.

Meanwhile let the schola prepare itself, and the cantor, standing in the middle, with the bishop’s assent, begins the antiphon “I Have Risen.” Psalm: “Lord, you have examined me.” As the bishop hastens to the vestibule of the church and to the door of the sacristy, let him kiss the Gospel, and afterward let them proceed with all diligence. When the Introit is finished, let the pontiff enter in the middle with the procession. As he stands and prays, let him say this prayer:

Receive my confession, the one hope of my salvation, my Lord and my God, because I have been destroyed by gluttony, drunkenness, fornication, lust, sloth, sadness, sleepiness, negligence, anger, greed, envy, malice, hatred, detraction, perjury, falsehood, lying, vainglory, frivolity, and pride; and I am utterly extinguished in thought, speech, action, and all the senses. You who justify the ungodly and give life to the dead, give me life, raise me up, and have mercy on me, my God.

With the bishop’s assent, the cantor begins the Psalm, with the Introit being sung responsively. Meanwhile he is also to kiss all those standing around him, beginning on the left and proceeding alternately to the right.

When this has been completed, the bishop is to signal with his finger, and the cantor begins “Glory to the Father.” The bishop is to hasten to the altar, accompanied by the ministers, and say this prayer:

I confess, Lord, that I am unworthy of your sacred things, for I am daily stained by countless sins. Why do I presume to entreat you, Lord, with flattering words, when I so often offend you by wicked deeds? For you, Lord, administer medicine to me in my sickness, while I do things contrary to my health. I read your law, Lord, inserted in the sacred pages, but in my misery I neglect sound discipline. I approach your altar as though devoted, yet I depart from your commands with a stubborn heart. Grant me, therefore, Lord, I beseech you, a contrite heart that truly hates sin. If you grant it, it is mine to mourn my offenses; it is yours swiftly to erase them like snow. And although I have lost the palm because the enemy defrauded me, may I at least reach pardon through your mercy. To you, God, be honor; to the King of all, who rules all things through ages of ages. Amen.

After a pause for the prayer, the presbyters and deacons, in the order in which they have been arranged, are to kiss the corners of the altar, one after another. Finally the bishop, while they minister to him, is to kiss the Gospel, lifted up and opened by them and placed in the middle of the altar by the subdeacon. Then “Lord, have mercy” is sung. With them leading, the bishop proceeds to the throne. Then he begins “Glory to God in the highest.” After this the Mass is sung according to his own judgment [perhaps: use]. And the bishop announces: “Peace be with you.” Response: “And with your spirit.”

### Prayer

God, who on this day, through your Only-Begotten Son, etc.

From there the subdeacon is to proceed to the ambo and read the Epistle, “Purge Out.” Response: “This is the day. Alleluia, our Passover.”

The deacon is to proceed with a censer, and another minister with incense; kneeling at the knees of the seated bishop, he is to place in it incense, the smoke of a sweet fragrance, and say:

I place incense into the fragrance of sweetness and in the name of the holy and undivided Trinity.

The deacon, bowing his head, asks for a blessing and says: “Command, Lord, that it be blessed.” The bishop responds: “May the Lord be in your heart and in your mouth for proclaiming the Gospel reading.”

Taking the Gospel, he is to kiss it and the altar. And he is to ascend the ambo to announce [possibly: for announcing] the words of eternal blessedness. Let the Gospel of Mary Magdalene be read. When the Gospel is finished, let the Gospel book be carried by the subdeacon, so that the bishop may kiss it, and afterward everyone else. And the bishop says: “The Lord be with you.” Response: “And with your spirit.” [Col. 0243A] “Let us pray.” Then the Offertory begins: “The Earth Trembled.”

245 When this has been completed and the offering received, let him return with the entire procession to the throne, remove the sleeves [or arm-coverings], wash his hands, and thus enter the place of propitiation. Let the entire procession offer its offering to him, and finally incense. While he is being incensed, let him say these prayers:

Lord our God, with humble devotion we beseech you: just as you received the offerings of Abel, Noah, Aaron, Zechariah, and Samuel, and of all your saints, so may you deign to receive this incense from our sinful hand as a fragrance of sweetness and for the remission of all our sins. Through the Lord.

### Another

May this incense or perfume appease, Lord, your anger against me, against this place, and against this people; and graciously grant that we may be like smoke of good fragrance to you, for attaining eternal life. Through Christ.

Afterward let them arrange themselves according to ecclesiastical custom: the deacons before the altar, the subdeacons behind, and the bishop in the middle, since “in the mouth of two or three every word is established.” Let them bow their heads until “through all ages of ages.” Response: “Amen.” And let him say this prayer over the offerings:

Receive, Lord, we beseech you, the prayers of your people together with the offerings of sacrifices. See the corresponding text above under Holy Saturday.

Then they rise after this, and the acolytes bring water for the deacon’s hands and a towel. The pontiff says in a loud voice: “Through all ages of ages.” Response: “Amen.” “Lift up your hearts.” Response: “We have them with the Lord.” “Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.” Response: “It is worthy and right.”

### Preface

It is truly worthy and right, equitable and salutary: to you indeed at all times, as above.

While the Sanctus is being said, everyone bows, and meanwhile the bishop says this prayer:

God, who desire not the death but the repentance of sinners, do not reject me, miserable and fragile sinner, from your loving-kindness. Do not look upon my sins, my crimes, and my unclean and shameful thoughts, by which I am tearfully separated from your will, but look upon your mercy and upon the faith and devotion of those who, through me, a sinner, seek your mercy. And since you have willed that I, unworthy as I am, become a mediator between you and your people, make me worthy to be such, so that I may be able to implore your mercy for myself and for this same people of yours. Join our voices to the voices of your holy angels, so that, just as they praise you incessantly and tirelessly in eternal blessedness, so we too, through their intercession, may deserve to praise you blamelessly in this pilgrimage. Through the Lord.

Therefore, most merciful Father.

In communion, and venerating the memory, as above.

Therefore, this offering of our service, as above.

Before “Through whom all these things [are]…,” (977) Blessing of the flesh:

God of all flesh, who Noah and his sons.

[Col. 0244A] Through whom you always create all these good things, O Lord: +you sanctify them, +you give them life.

246 The acolyte, however, shall stand with the paten behind the deacons, bowing with the deacons until the bishop says, “To us also, sinners.” The deacon who reads the Gospel (978) shall therefore take care that the bishop makes the sign of the cross over the chalice, and (979) shall anticipate [him] (980) by lifting the chalice in the sight of the Lord, and shall quickly return to his place. The subdeacons, meanwhile, proceeding from behind the altar, where they have named or recited the memorial (981), or the names of the living and the dead, shall follow the deacon, bowing their heads. When the Lord’s Prayer has ended, the subdeacon shall receive the paten from the acolyte’s hand and give it to the deacon, who shall carry it to the bishop. After this they shall reestablish themselves in the place where they had been before the Gospel was read, until the Blessing and kiss of peace have been completed. Then, when the bishop says, “Through all ages of ages,” and the response has been made, “Amen,” after the Lord’s Prayer, when he has finished “Deliver us from evil,” with the bishop’s assent (982) the deacon shall say: (983) “Bow down for the Blessing”; and the people shall respond, “Thanks be to God.” And the bishop shall give this Blessing:

(984) May almighty God bless you, with today’s intervening paschal solemnity, etc.

Then, taking a portion of the Lord’s body, he shall say: “The peace of the Lord be always with you.” (985) Response: “And with your spirit.” With the bishop’s assent, the cantor shall say: “Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world.” (986) Meanwhile he shall kiss the archdeacon and the others. Then, turning toward the altar, he shall say this prayer: “The Lord be with you.” Response: “And with your spirit.”

[Col. 0244C] (987) May this most holy commingling of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be (988) salvation of mind and body for all who receive it, and a saving preparation for attaining eternal life. Through the Lord.

While the body is broken.—Deign, O Lord, to send your holy angel to the sacred and immortal mystery, namely, your body and blood. For we are breaking it, O Lord; deign to bless it, and grant that we may be able to handle it with undefiled senses and hands, and to receive it worthily. Through our Lord. Send your angel, O Lord, that he may deign.

After this, therefore, (989) let all communicate individually, [Col. 0244D] including the bishop; (990) and after he has communicated, let him say these prayers:

May the reception of your body and blood, Lord Jesus Christ, which I, unworthy, presume to receive, not come to me for judgment and condemnation, but, through your mercy, profit me for the protection of mind and body, you who are with the Father in unity.

Another.—Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who by the will of the Father and with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit gave life to the world through your death, deliver me through this sacred body and blood of yours from all my iniquities and every evil, and make me obedient to your commandments, and never let me be separated from you forever. You who are with the Father.

[Col. 0245A] Another.—Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, grant me to receive this body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ 247 in such a way that through it I may deserve to receive remission of all my sins and be filled with your Holy Spirit, for you are blessed, and besides you there is no other, whose glorious kingdom endures forever and ever. Amen.

And (991) let the bishop communicate the priests and deacons with the kiss of peace, (992) but with the sacrifice unmixed, and the subdeacons without the kiss, with the sacrifice mixed (993). Let the deacons and priests briefly taste from the chalice, while the subdeacon holds it, of the blood itself. Meanwhile, with the bishop’s assent, the cantor shall begin: (994) Communion: “Our Passover”; Psalm: “Lord, you have searched me,” with the Gloria. When this has been completed, the bishop shall sit on the throne, and, having washed his hands [Col. 0245B] for the third time, shall return to the altar and say the Collect.

248 For the Completion.—“The Spirit to us, O Lord.” Then the bishop, turning toward the people, shall say: “The Lord be with you.” Response: “And with your spirit.” With the bishop’s assent, the deacon shall say: “Go, (995) the Mass is ended.” Response: “Thanks be to God.” The bishop himself shall kiss the altar and silently say this prayer:

Let us pray.—(996) May the Holy Trinity be pleased with you; for Saint John, at Vespers: “Grant, we ask, almighty God”; [at the fonts:] “Grant, we ask, almighty God, that those who…”; [at Saint Andrew:] “Grant, we ask, almighty God, that those who receive grace…” Thus far the Paschal Mass.

## ANOTHER OLD MASS

From the Tilian Codex.

247 (997) Here begins the Order of the Pontiff when he prepares [Col. 0245C] for Mass. (998) When he washes his hands, he shall say this prayer:

Grant to our senses, almighty Father, that just as the defilements of the hands are washed away outwardly, so the pollutions of our minds may be cleansed inwardly by you, and that the increase of holy virtues may grow within us. Through [Christ our Lord].

Afterward (999) the bishop begins to put on his sandals, and says this prayer:

Shoe my feet, O Lord, in preparation for the Gospel of peace, and protect me under the shelter of your wings.

(1000) Then let him sing the following psalms with those standing around him:

“How lovely”; “You blessed, O Lord”; “Incline, O Lord,” with the prayers: “Arise, O Lord”; [Col. 0245D] “Let your mercy be upon us, O Lord”; “You will turn, O God”; “Show us, O Lord”; “Do not enter into judgment”; “Be gracious toward our sins”; “O Lord, hear my prayer.”

Incline the ears of your mercy to my prayers, most gentle God, and enlighten my heart with the grace of the Holy Spirit, so that I may be able to minister worthily in your ministries and deserve to love you with eternal charity. Through [Christ our Lord].

Prayer of the priest preparing for Mass.—Overshadow my head, O Lord, with the shade of holy faith, and drive away from me the clouds of ignorance. Amen.

For the alb.—Clothe me, O Lord, with the garment of salvation, and surround me with the breastplate of strength. Amen.

For the girdle.—Gird me, O Lord, with the safeguard of my [Col. 0246A] mind, and let my mind itself not be bent by the spirit of pride. Amen.

For the stole.—Surround my neck, O Lord, with the stole of righteousness, and purify my mind from every corruption of sin. Amen.

For the chasuble.—Clothe me, O Lord, with the adornment of charity and peace, 248 so that, fortified on every side by virtues, I may be able to resist vices and the enemies of mind and body.

After taking the maniple.—Give me, O Lord, right understanding and a pure voice, so that I may be able to fulfill your praise.

After he enters the church, (1001) let him kiss two priests and two deacons, (1002) beginning by himself, “I will go in to the altar of God,” with the Psalm “Judge me, O God.” [Col. 0246B] Meanwhile, while the Verse at the Introit is sung, he says these prayers. (1003) Take away our iniquities, that with pure minds we may enter into the holy of holies [read: “we may deserve”].

Another prayer.—(1004) Almighty God, who have willed that I, a sinner, should stand at the sacred altars and praise the power of your holy name, grant, we ask, through the mystery of this sacrament, forgiveness of my sins, so that I may deserve to minister worthily to your Majesty. Through [Christ our Lord].

(1005) Then, when he kisses the Gospel, let him say:

May the peace of Christ, which he has handed down to us through his Gospel, strengthen and preserve our hearts and bodies unto eternal life. Amen.

(1006) The priest’s confession before the altar.

[Col. 0246C] Receive my confession, the one hope of my salvation, O Lord my God. I am ruined by gluttony, drunkenness, fornication, lust, sadness, acedia, drowsiness, anger, covetousness, envy, malice, hatred, slander, perjury, falsehood, lying, vainglory, fickleness, and pride; and I am destroyed by every thought, word, and action, and by all evils. But you, who justify the ungodly and give life to the dead, give me life and raise me again, my God.

Prayer of the priest before the altar before he begins Mass.—God, be gracious to me, a sinner, because you are the immortal and only sinless God. Lord my God, forgive me, your unworthy servant, because I am a sinner and unworthy, who presume to approach your holy altar and invoke you—who [Col. 0246D] have sinned before you and before your angels. But grant 249 forgiveness of my offenses and strengthen me in your holy Church, in the faith of the orthodox, and teach me to do your will all the days of my life. You who live.

(1007) Likewise, the prayer said while “Glory to God in the highest” is sung.—Lord Jesus Christ, Redeemer of the world, be gracious to me, a sinner lying in sin in every way, because you alone, Lord our God, are immortal and without sin. Forgive me, most wretched, who presume to approach your holy altar and invoke you, because I have sinned from my infancy until now before you and before all your saints. But through their intercession, may divine [Col. 0247A] mercy grant me forgiveness of my sins, and teach me to do your will all the days of my life. You who live and reign.

(1008) After the Collect and until the Gospel, as he sees fit, he says these prayers:

God, who make the worthy from the unworthy, the righteous from sinners, the clean from the unclean, cleanse my body and my heart from every contagion and filth of sin, and make me a worthy minister at your holy altars. In your mercy grant that on this altar, to which I, unworthy, approach, I may offer pleasing sacrifices to your goodness for my sins and offenses, for my countless daily transgressions, for the flock entrusted to me, for your servant N. and spouse, and the people subject to him, for all who stand around, for all joined to me by familiarity, and for all who pursue me with hateful cursing, who oppose your Church entrusted to me, and for all the faithful Christians together. And through him may my vow and sacrifice be acceptable to you, God the Father, he who offered himself to you as a sacrifice, Jesus Christ our Lord.

Forgive me, O Lord, because I am compelled to ask you while I take up your holy name through my unclean lips, so that when I confess the secrets of my shameful deeds, I have no words before you without guilt. For you know the wounds of my conscience and the hidden things of my thoughts, and you alone recognize my uncleanness. Have mercy on me, O Lord, have mercy on me. Forgive me as I handle the secrets of your mystery, and do not judge unworthy of your mercy the one whom you permit to pray for others; [Col. 0247C] and in one in whom you do not recognize the testimony of a good work, at least do not refuse the office of the stewardship entrusted to him, Savior of the world. You who live.

When (1009) he puts incense into the censer before the Gospel is read, let him say:

May the Lord, with the fragrance of his heavenly inspiration, kindle and fill our hearts for hearing and fulfilling the commands of his Gospel. He who lives.

(1010) Then the priest shall say to the deacon who is bowing:

May the Lord be in your heart and on your lips, so that you may suitably proclaim the Gospel of peace.

(1011) After the Gospel has been read, let it be brought to the bishop for veneration, and let him say:

Through these words of the holy Gospel of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, may the Lord forgive our [Col. 0247D] sins.

When (1012) the altar has been adorned, before the prelate receives the offerings of the priests and deacons, while the Offertories are sung, let him ascend to the altar and say this prayer with utmost humility:

250 Before your eyes, O Lord, I stand guilty, a witness against my own conscience. I do not dare to ask for what I do not deserve to obtain. For you know, O Lord, what is done within us. We are ashamed to confess what we do not fear to commit. With words alone do we obey you; in our hearts we lie. What we say we wish, our actions prove that we do not wish. But spare those who confess, O Lord; forgive sinners; have mercy on those who ask you. And because my understanding is weak concerning your sacraments, and [Col. 0248A] sinners have no words without guilt before you, grant, O Lord, that if you do not accept the words of us unworthy sinners, hard of heart, you may nevertheless grant us forgiveness through yourself. You who live and reign, God, forever and ever, world without end.

Then (1013) let him turn to receive the offerings of the priests or deacons who are offering them, (1014) and let each one say this prayer:

To you, Lord God, my Creator, I offer a sacrifice for the forgiveness of all sins, and of all your faithful.

When the deacon receives the libation of the chalice, let him say:

May this sacrifice be acceptable to almighty God.

Then the priest shall return to the altar; and before the altar, before saying the Secret, (1015) let him first accuse himself tearfully, [Col. 0248B] and say this prayer:

(1016) Before the presence of your divine Majesty I stand guilty, presuming to invoke your holy name. Have mercy on me, O Lord, a sinful man; forgive the unworthy priest through whose hands this offering appears to be offered; spare one polluted beyond others by the stain of capital sins. Do not enter into judgment with your servant, burdened, that is, by vices and the pleasures of the flesh. Remember, O Lord, that I am flesh. Even the heavens are not clean in your sight—how much less are we mortal human beings. I am unworthy to be alive. You who do not desire the death of a sinner, grant forgiveness to me who am established in the flesh, so that through the labors of repentance I may enjoy eternal life in heaven through you, Jesus Christ.

(1017) Then, with a pure heart, let him offer to the Lord the offerings placed upon the altar, [Col. 0248C] saying:

(1018) Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for me, a sinner, for the salvation of our congregation, for all the Christian people, for all who give alms to us, and also for those who have commended themselves to our prayers, and for those who remember us in their prayers: that here we may receive forgiveness of sins and in the future deserve to obtain eternal rewards. Amen.

(1019) Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer, first of all, as is right, in memory of the Incarnation, Nativity, Passion, Resurrection, and Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in honor of all your saints who have pleased you from the beginning of the world, whose names and relics [Col. 0248D] are contained here, and of those whose feast is celebrated on earth, so that it may benefit them unto honor and us unto salvation, and so that all those whose memory we make on earth may deign to intercede in heaven.

(1020) Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for the soul of your servant, so that, with you granting it, after receiving forgiveness of sins, it may also deserve to receive the boundless joys of eternal life.

251 (1022) Receive, Holy Trinity, this offering, which I offer to you for the souls of your male and female servants, so that, purified through this saving sacrifice, they may deserve to be joined to the company of your saints.

[Col. 0249A] (1024) Then the deacon shall offer the chalice to the priest upon the altar and say:

Offer to God a sacrifice of praise and repay your vows to the Most High. May the Lord be your helper; may he make you clean. When you pray to him, may he hear you.

And (1025) the bishop, offering the chalice to the Lord, shall say:

(1026) Lord Jesus Christ, who willed that blood and water flow from your side in the passion of your cross, by which you would consecrate the Church to yourself, receive this sacrifice placed upon your altar, and grant, most mercifully, that it may ascend before your divine Majesty with the fragrance of your sweetness for our redemption and also for that of the whole world, Jesus Christ.

For (1027) mixing wine with water:

God, who wonderfully created the dignity of human substance and reformed it more wonderfully, grant us, we ask, through the mystery of this water and wine, to share in the divinity of him who deigned to become a participant in our humanity, Jesus Christ.

(1029) Then, raising his hand, let him bless both:

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, may this sacrifice be immaculate and united and blessed by you, the living and true God.

(1030) Afterward, taking incense, let him place it in the censer, saying:

Through the intercession of the holy archangel Gabriel, who stands at the right of the altar of incense, and of all his elect, may the Lord deign to bless this incense and receive it as an odor of sweetness.

(1031) Then let him place incense upon the sacrifice and say around the altar:

[Col. 0249C] May this incense, blessed by you, ascend to you, O Lord, and may your mercy descend upon us. May my prayer be directed like incense in your sight.

(1032) When the fragrance of that incense is offered to the bishop or to the others, let each one say:

May the Lord kindle within us the fire of his love and the flame of eternal charity.

(1033) Then let the priest turn with utmost humility toward those standing around and say:

Pray for me, a wretched sinner, to our Lord Jesus Christ, that my sacrifice and yours may be acceptable in the sight of divine goodness.

(1034) Then let each one say:

[Col. 0249D] May all the saints of God pray for you. May the Lord remember all your sacrifice, and may your burnt offering be made rich. May the Lord hear you praying for us. May almighty God have mercy on you and forgive you all your sins.

(1035) After the priest begins “You, therefore,” let the deacons and subdeacons sing these psalms:

“May the Lord answer you”; “To you, O Lord, I lifted up”; “Have mercy on me, O God”; “The one who dwells,” with the prayers: “Save your servant”; “The desire of the heart”; “He asked life of you”; “The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous”; “Let there be mercy”; “O Lord, hear my prayer.”

252 Prayer for the priest.—May your servant rejoice, Lord God, in the benefits obtained; and to him to whom you have granted confidence [Col. 0250A] in hoping for your mercy, graciously grant the effect of the mercy he desires.

Likewise, a prayer for all.—We ask, O Lord, incline the ears of your mercy to our prayers, and, knower of hidden things, graciously hear the prayers of those who entreat you, so that, by your generosity, we may attain eternal forgiveness.

(1036) When the Secret and (1037) the Lord’s Prayer have been completed, and he has said, “The peace of the Lord be always with you,” let the Lord’s body be mixed with the blood.

May this holy commingling of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ be for all of us a saving preparation of mind and body for attaining eternal life. Through [Christ our Lord].

(1038) After the episcopal blessing has been [Col. 0250B] completed, taking the portion that he previously broke off and holding it over the chalice, let him break it and say:

May the commingling of the holy blood with the holy body of our Lord Jesus Christ profit all who receive it unto eternal life.

(1039) When he takes the Lord’s body into his hands, let him say: “I will receive the heavenly bread and call upon the name of the Lord.”

For receiving the Lord’s body:

(1040) May the reception of your body, Lord Jesus Christ, which I, unworthy, presume to receive, not come to me for judgment and condemnation, but, through your mercy, profit me for the protection of mind and body. You who live.

(1041) When he takes the chalice, let him say:

“What shall I repay the Lord,” etc., as in the Roman Missal.

After receiving it, secretly:

May the communion and strengthening of your holy blood, Lord Jesus Christ, profit me for the remission of all sins and preserve me unto eternal life.

(1042) Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who by the will of the Father, (1043) with the saints cooperating [read: “with the Holy Spirit cooperating”], gave life to the world through your death, deliver me through this sacred body and blood of yours, so that it may not be for me unto judgment or condemnation, but may profit as a remedy for my soul. Deliver me from all my iniquities, O God, and make me obedient to your commandments, and never let me be separated from you and your saints forever. You who live.

(1044) Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal [Col. 0250D] God, grant me to receive this body and blood of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, in such a way that through it I may deserve to receive forgiveness of sins and be filled with your Holy Spirit, because you are, and besides you there is no other, whose glorious name endures forever and ever. Amen.

(1045) Then, when he begins to communicate the clergy or the people, let him say to each one:

(1046) May the reception of the body of our Lord be life and salvation for you, and redemption from all your sins.

Prayer of Saint Gregory the pope.—May the body of our Lord Jesus Christ profit me for the remission of all sins unto eternal life.

[Col. 0251A] (1047) When the Mass has ended, after the deacon says, “Go, the Mass is ended,” 253 let the priest come before the altar and, having kissed it, say:

May the service of my servitude please you, Holy Trinity, and grant that this sacrifice, which I, unworthy, have offered before the eyes of your Majesty, may be pleasing to you and, through your mercy, propitiatory for me and for all on whose behalf I offered it. You who live.

(1048) Another prayer.—Through the merits and intercessions of all his saints, may almighty God have mercy on us.

(1049) When everything has been completed, the bishop, returning to the sacristy 254 with the deacons and the others, shall sing the hymn of the three boys and “Praise the Lord in his holy places.” (1050) Then the prayers: “Let all your works confess to you, O Lord, and your saints”; “The righteous shall rejoice”; “Let the righteous rejoice”; “Not to us, O Lord, not to us”; “I will clothe the priests”; “Do not enter into judgment”; “Lord God of hosts”; “May God, God, bless us”; “O Lord, hear.” (1051) Then the prayer: God, who appeased the flames of the fires for the three boys, graciously grant, through their intercession and that of all the saints, that the flame of vices may not consume us, your servants. Through [Christ our Lord].

## THE ANCIENT RITE OF CELEBRATING MASS

From an ancient manuscript codex of the priory of Salicosan (Ugo Sausensis) among the Velocasses, belonging to the order of the Augustinian Canons, not far from Vernon. The beginning of this codex is:

253 To the truly holy and worthy of honor for his merits, (1052) Maurilius, venerable archbishop of the holy Church of Rouen, (1053) John of Avranches, least of all [Col. 0251C] bishops in merit, offers the service of complete obedience in body and spirit, etc.

Let the Mass of the day be celebrated in this order. First, on weekdays let two bells be rung; on feast days, all of them. At the “Glory be to the Father,” while the choir sings the Introit instituted by Saint Celestine, the priest (1054) in the vestment room, and the other ministers, shall put on the sacred vestments according to rank: the deacon, the alb, stole, and dalmatic; the subdeacon, the alb, tunic, and maniple; the others only albs—namely, two acolytes, one to sing the Gradual and carry the candelabrum, the other to sing the Alleluia and carry the censer. When the psalm has been said and the choir begins “Glory be to the Father,” the priest and the other ministers shall proceed in this manner to the altar. The deacon shall precede the priest; the subdeacon, preceding the deacon, shall carry the Gospel; the candle-bearer with a candle [Col. 0251D] shall precede the subdeacon; the bearer of the censer shall precede the candle-bearer. When, therefore, they have come before the altar, the subdeacon shall place the Gospel on the right corner of the altar, where it shall remain until the Gospel. The altar signifies Jerusalem, in which, from the beginning of the Lord’s coming, evangelical teaching resounded and from there went forth publicly, as it is written: “From Zion the law shall go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

Afterward the subdeacon shall pass to the priest’s left and the deacon to his right. There, after confession has been made mutually, (1055) the priest shall kiss the deacon and subdeacon. For Christ first gave peace to the apostles and transmitted it through them to the world. After this the priest and the other ministers shall pray briefly behind the altar, standing in their proper order. Then, first rising from prayer, (1056) [Col. 0252A] he shall bow to the deacon who bows to him; the deacon to the subdeacon who bows to him; and the subdeacon to the choir which bows to him. After bowing, the deacon shall kiss both corners of the altar and (1057) offer the Gospel to 254 the priest, who is kissing the middle of the altar, to be kissed. For through the Gospel Christ, blotting out the bond of transgression, gave peace to the world, reconciling to himself through its heralds both peoples, the Jewish and the Gentile. The altar that the priest kisses signifies the Jewish people dwelling in Jerusalem, whom Christ reconciled to himself; through the Gospel, the Gentile people. Then the priest proceeds to the right corner of the altar; for Christ always lived on the right, and by the right hand heavenly glory is acquired. The deacon shall stand behind him, imitating the same life, until he [Col. 0252B] signals him to sit.

(1058) The bishop’s seat, according to the decrees of Pope Urban and the Council of Carthage, ought to be higher than those of the others; in it the episcopal chair shall be honorably established, etc. (1059) The candle-bearers shall hold the candelabra from south to north until “Kyrie eleison”; when it begins, they shall set them down there. By the south, which is a warm wind, the fervor of the Holy Spirit is signified; this fervor, at the rising of the true Sun, spreads from east to west, illuminating the world. A third candle shall be placed in the middle, signifying that where two or three are gathered in the Lord’s name, the Lord is present. By the fact that the candles are set down when “Kyrie” begins, it is shown that while we implore the Lord we ought to humble ourselves with contrite heart. When the priest greets the people, let them hold them there again. When the prayer is finished, let them place them from east to west. [Col. 0252C] For the four regions of the world are illuminated by the two Testaments. Seven candelabra on feast days signify the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit.

When the subdeacon begins the Epistle, let the priest sit beside the altar and signal the deacon to sit in his place. The subdeacon, except during the time of his ministry, shall remain in the choir. As the end of the Gospel approaches, let the priest place incense in the censer; after the altar has been incensed, let it be carried before the Gospel. By the censer, which emits a fragrant odor, the fame of good works that preceded Christ’s teaching is signified.

The deacon, having received a blessing from the priest, shall take the Gospel from the altar and place it upon his left shoulder. 255 For the left shoulder signifies temporal life, in which the Gospel ought to be preached. The subdeacon shall carry a cushion before him. [Col. 0252D] By the cushion that precedes him, the Law that preceded the Gospel is represented; by the feathers hidden within, the mysteries contained in the Law; by the lightness of the feathers, the commandments of the old law, light in comparison with the new. In the former it is said, “You shall not kill”; in the new, “Whoever is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment.”

(1060) And so, with the candle-bearer and the bearer of the censer preceding, let him proceed in procession to the lectern. After the Gospel has been placed beneath and incensed, let him turn toward the north and read the Gospel. For by the north the unbelief of the nations is signified, to whom the Gospel is preached by the apostles, kindled with the fire of the Holy Spirit. When it has been read, let the candelabra be extinguished. For at the immolation of the true prefigurative Lamb, the immolation ceased, as did the other mysteries contained in the Law and the prophets, which are signified by the candelabra [Col. 0253A].

Let incense be offered to the priest in the censer, and let him kiss the Gospel first, handed to him by the subdeacon; afterward the deacon shall kiss it. On feast days, let it also be presented by the subdeacon to all the clergy, with the incense preceding. After the Gospel has been read, let the priest greet the people. (1061) Let the Offertory begin; when it has ended, let the Verse (1062) follow. Meanwhile, let the subdeacon offer the bread and wine to the deacon, and the deacon offer them to the priest. On feast days, let the cantor carry water covered with a cloth to the deacon, and let the deacon mix it with the wine. For by the cantor’s sweet modulation the people are kindled with devout reverence and divine love, and thus run to the Lord and become one body in Christ. By the wine Christ is signified; by the water, the people; by the linen covering of the water, the labor of the cantor’s singing, by which the people are freed from the perversity of their thoughts—for labor is expressed by linen.

[Col. 0253B] (1063) Water mixed with wine unites the people to Christ. On other days the acolyte shall minister it. (1064) The priest shall arrange the offering in such a way that he places the chalice on the right side of the Host; for from the Lord’s right side blood and water flowed down. Then, covering it with the corporal, he shall offer incense over it, and thus present it to the deacon. The deacon, however, shall carry it around the altar, then return it to the priest, and thereafter hand it back to the minister, so that he may carry it to the clergy and people. Moreover, taking the paten from the altar, he shall hand it to the subdeacon, and the subdeacon, if one is present, to the acolyte. For no one may remove anything sacred from the altar except a deacon or priest.

(1065) Then, bowed before the altar, the priest alone shall pray, asking that he may be worthy to approach the altar and persist in divine worship. The other ministers, however, shall stand in prayer in their proper order. After this, facing the people, he shall admonish them to pray; then, turning toward the altar, he shall say the Secret Prayer. When it has been completed, he shall utter *Vere dignum*, etc., with devout mind and sweet voice. At its conclusion, the choir shall respond with the hymn *Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus*, instituted by blessed Sixtus. The deacon and ministers shall remain behind the priest, bowed, from *Te igitur*, etc., until *Sed libera nos*. For the apostles sympathized with the suffering Lord in grief and fear. The inclination of the deacons signifies the apostles’ sorrow; that of the subdeacons signifies the holy women. The subdeacons likewise shall remain bowed in the priest’s sight. They represent the holy women who, while the Lord was suffering and the disciples had fled—though struck with fear and grief—were attentive to what was happening to him; but after the Lord had been taken down from the cross and buried, they departed and prepared spices for the burial. Thus the subdeacons shall leave that place and hasten to minister to Christ’s body and blood, offering the paten through the hand of the deacon to the priest, in order that the Lord’s body may be broken upon it, etc.

When, therefore, he has reached these words, namely, *Per quem haec omnia, Domine, semper bona*—“Through whom, O Lord, you always create all these good things”—then the deacon shall approach and take the right corner of the corporal with his right hand, and uncover it together with the priest. While saying *Per ipsum*, etc., the priest shall touch (1066) the four parts of the chalice. For by the immolation of Christ’s body the four regions of the world were redeemed. (1067) Likewise, when the Prayer has been completed, (1068) both shall lift the chalice, set it down together, and cover it. Then the deacon shall kiss the altar, and afterward the priest’s right shoulder. The priest’s shoulder signifies the stone on which the angel sat at the tomb. For the angel must always be believed to be present at the immolation of Christ’s body. Through (1069) the deacon Joseph is represented; through the priest, Nicodemus; through the lifting from the altar, Christ’s removal from the cross; through the replacing again upon the altar, Christ’s burial.

After this the priest shall recite the Lord’s Prayer in a loud voice. The elevation of the Lord’s Prayer demonstrates the unity of our brotherhood. For God our Father, the teacher of peace and concord, taught us to pray for all as one, just as he bore all in the One. While the clergy respond, *Sed libera nos a malo*, “But deliver us from evil,” (1070) he shall complete the rite of consecration. When *Sed libera* has been said, the deacon and subdeacon shall rise and fix their eyes upon the consecration of the Lord’s body. For the Evangelist says that his acquaintances stood at a distance, beating their breasts.

When, therefore, he has reached the place *Da propitius pacem*, “Graciously grant peace,” (1071) the one who, clothed in a napkin, had held it [Perhaps read: “the paten”] shall offer it to the subdeacon; the subdeacon to the deacon; and the deacon to the priest. Upon it the priest shall divide the Lord’s body into three parts. Placing one of the parts into the chalice and saying *Pax Domini* in a loud voice, he shall immediately add secretly: (1072) “May this mingling of the body and blood of the Lord be for us who receive it unto eternal life.” With another he shall communicate himself, the deacon, and the subdeacon. The third he shall reserve in the paten as viaticum, if necessary, until the end of the Mass. (1073)

The particle of the offering inserted into the chalice signifies Christ’s body, which rose from the dead; that eaten by the priest or people signifies Christ’s intercourse with his disciples after the Resurrection, giving them life in God. The third, which remains on the altar, holy Church calls “viaticum” for the dying, to show that those who die in Christ are not to be considered dead but sleeping, since, with such a great guide, they are led to eternal life. If it is not necessary, the priest or one of the ministers shall consume the third part.

The priest shall not communicate by dipping the bread, but, (1074) according to the decree of the Council of Toledo, he shall communicate separately with the body and separately with the blood, (1075) except for the people, who are permitted to communicate with dipped bread—not by authority, but because of the extreme necessity arising from fear of shedding Christ’s blood. While the priest is offering communion to the ministers, he shall first kiss each one; afterward, the person who is to communicate shall kiss the priest’s hand and receive communion from him.

[Col. 0254D] (1076) Finally, the priest shall consume the particle that remained in the chalice. Then he shall hand the chalice to the deacon for cleansing and for consuming what remains. The deacon shall carry the chalice with the paten to the left corner of the altar, where he shall take a portion for himself and give a portion to the subdeacon. After both vessels have been cleansed, both shall partake. The acolyte shall bring another chalice to the priest for washing his fingers. The subdeacon shall assist the deacon in cleansing the chalice and paten. After the paten and chalice have been cleansed, the acolyte shall keep both wrapped in a napkin until the completion of the first Postcommunion, while the other ministers perform their respective duties.

As we said above, after dividing the Lord’s body, the priest shall proclaim *Pax Domini* in a loud voice. One of the canons shall receive the peace from him and distribute it to the senior members in both choirs. They, in turn, shall offer it to the others in such a way that no one leaves his place: each shall receive it from the person above him and give it to the person below him. One of the juniors of each choir shall receive it from the seniors and distribute it to the others according to the prescribed order. Let them hold firmly to this, in accordance with the Apostle—“in honor, anticipating one another”—that those who give and receive the peace always bow.

The kiss of peace signifies the benefit of our faith. The choir shall sing *Agnus Dei*, which Pope Sergius ordered to be sung at the time of the breaking of the Lord’s body, for the immolation of this Lamb redeemed the world. When it has begun, the candles shall be lit: the world was illumined by the Lamb’s Passion, etc.

## THE RITE FORMERLY OBSERVED

[Note: In the first Theodorian manuscript there are Prayers for blessing the king. But they do not agree in any way with ours. Among them the following is worthy of notice, entitled: “The Prayer by which the apostolic lord John (the eighth) blessed Louis [surname: the Stammerer], son of the emperor Charles the Younger, at the city of Troyes. ‘Pour forth, we beseech you, O Lord, the Spirit of sanctification upon Louis, our king,’ etc.”]

## AT THE ANOINTING OF THE KINGS OF THE FRANKS

From the Codex of Abbot Ratold.

[Col. 0255B]

257 Here begins the inquiry or election of the bishops and clergy, as well as of the people, (1077) for consecrating or blessing the king.

### Admonition to the bishops, clergy, or people, to be addressed to the king

It shall be read in this manner by one bishop before everyone:

(1078) “We ask you to grant that you preserve for each one of us and for the Churches entrusted to us their canonical privilege, the law and justice due to them, and that you provide protection, just as a king in his kingdom ought rightly to provide it for each bishop and Church entrusted to him.”

(1080) The king’s response.—“I promise and grant you that I shall preserve for each one of you and for the Churches entrusted to you canonical privilege, the law and justice due to them, and that, insofar as I am able, with the Lord’s help, I shall provide protection, just as a king in his kingdom ought rightly to provide it for each bishop and Church entrusted to him.”

(1081) Then let two bishops address the people in the church, asking their consent; and, if they are in agreement, (1082) let them give thanks to almighty God, (1083) singing *Te Deum laudamus*. The two bishops shall take him by the hands and lead him before the altar, and he shall prostrate himself until the end of *Te Deum laudamus*.

### Invocation over the king

(1084) “We invoke you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, that you may cause this servant of yours, N., whom, through the providence of your divine dispensation, you permitted to grow from the beginning of his formation until this present day, rejoicing in youthful bloom, enriched by the gift of your kindness and filled with the grace of truth, to advance from day to day toward better things before God and human beings; (1085) so that, rejoicing in the generosity of heavenly grace, he may receive the throne of supreme government and, fortified on every side by the wall of your mercy against the hostility of enemies, may be deemed worthy happily to govern the people entrusted to him with the peace of your favor and the strength of victory. Through the Lord.”

[Col. 0256A] 258 Likewise, a prayer.—(1086) “O God, who care for your peoples by your power and rule them in love, give this servant of yours the Spirit of wisdom together with disciplined governance, so that, devoted to you with his whole heart, he may always remain capable in ruling the kingdom, and so that, by your gift, the security of the Church may be guided during his time, and Christian devotion may remain in tranquility; that, persevering in good works, he may reach the eternal kingdom under your guidance. Through.”

Another.—“In his days, may equity and justice arise for all; assistance for friends; a barrier for enemies; consolation for the humble; correction for the exalted; instruction for the rich; compassion for the poor; peace-making for strangers; peace and security for his own people in their homeland. May he govern each person moderately according to his measure, (1088) and diligently learn to govern himself, so that, watered by your compunction, he may be able to offer the whole people examples of life pleasing to you; and, walking along the way of truth with the flock subject to him, may he abundantly acquire modest prosperity, and receive from you all things granted for the salvation not only of bodies but also of hearts.

“Thus, ordering every thought and counsel of his mind toward you, may he always be found able to hold the reins of the people’s government with both peace and wisdom. With your help, may he receive length of life in the present age and reach a good old age; and, freed by the generosity of your mercy from all bonds of vice at the complete end of this frailty, may he attain the rewards of infinite prosperity and everlasting fellowship with the angels. Through.”

[Col. 0256C] (1089) The king’s consecration.—“Almighty and eternal God, Creator and governor of heaven and earth, founder and disposer of angels and human beings, King of kings and Lord of lords, who caused your faithful servant Abraham to triumph over his enemies, who granted manifold victory to Moses and Joshua, leaders of your people, who also exalted your humble servant David to the height of kingship, and delivered him from the mouth of the lion, from the hand of the beast and of Goliath, and also from the evil sword of Saul and all his enemies, and enriched Solomon with the ineffable gift of wisdom and peace: look favorably upon the prayers of our humility, and multiply the gifts of your blessings upon this servant of yours, whom with suppliant devotion we jointly choose (1090) for the kingdom of N. of all Albion—that is, of all the Franks. Surround him always and everywhere with the right hand of your power, (1091) so that, strengthened by the faithfulness of the aforesaid Abraham, relying upon the gentleness of Moses, fortified by the courage of Joshua, exalted by the humility of David, and adorned with the wisdom of Solomon, he may please you in all things; may always walk with unhindered step along the path of justice; and may henceforth nourish, teach, fortify, and instruct the Church of all Albion together with the peoples attached to it. Against all visible and invisible enemies, may he administer it powerfully and royally under the rule of your strength, (1091) so that he does not abandon the royal throne and the scepters of the Franks, but, with your assistance, restores their minds to the harmony of their former faith and peace. Supported by the due submission of both peoples and glorified with fitting love, may he, by your mercy, be worthy to establish and govern together, throughout a long span of life, the height of his father’s glory. Fortified by the helmet of your protection, continually defended by an invincible shield, and surrounded by heavenly weapons, may he happily gain the triumph of a desired victory over his enemies, strike terror into the unbelieving, and joyfully bring peace to those who serve you in warfare.

“Adorn him also with the virtues with which you adorned your aforesaid faithful servants, with a manifold blessing of honor; raise him sublimely in the government of the kingdom; and anoint him with the oil of the grace of the Holy Spirit.”

Here (1092) let him be anointed with oil.

Antiphon: “Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed Solomon king at Gihon, and, approaching joyfully, they said: ‘May the king live forever!’ From this you anointed priests, kings, and prophets, and martyrs who conquered kingdoms through faith, practiced justice, and obtained the promises. (1093) May this most sacred anointing flow down upon his head, descend into his inward parts, and penetrate the depths of his heart; and by your grace may he be made worthy of the promises obtained by the most victorious kings; so that he may reign happily in the present age and reach their fellowship in the heavenly kingdom, through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who was anointed with the oil of gladness above his companions, who by the power of the cross defeated the powers of the air, destroyed Tartarus, overcame the kingdom of the devil, and ascended victoriously to heaven. In his hand are victory, all glory, and power; and with you he lives and reigns, God, in the unity of the same Spirit. Through.”

Another.—(1094) “O God, strength of the chosen and exaltation of the humble, who at the beginning willed to punish the crimes of the world by the pouring out of the Flood, and by the dove bearing an olive branch demonstrated that peace had been restored to the earth; who again consecrated your servant Aaron through anointing with oil, and afterward, through the pouring out of this ointment, perfected priests, kings, and prophets to govern the Israelite people; and who, through the prophetic voice of your servant David, foretold that the face of the Church would be gladdened by oil: therefore, we beseech you, almighty Father, through the richness of this created substance, graciously sanctify this servant of yours with your blessing, (1095) and grant that, in the likeness of the dove, he may bestow the peace of simplicity upon the people entrusted to him; diligently imitate Aaron’s example in the service of God; consistently attain the heights of kingship through counsels of knowledge and equity of judgment; and, with your help, cause him to have the countenance of joy, through this anointing with oil, prepared for the whole people.” (1096)

Another.—(1097) “May God the Son, Christ our Lord, who was anointed by the Father with the oil of gladness above his companions, through the present pouring out of sacred ointment pour the blessing of the Paraclete Spirit upon your head and cause it to penetrate into the depths of your heart; so that through this visible and tangible gift you may perceive invisible things, carry out temporal kingdoms [Perhaps read: ‘the temporal kingdom,’ as in the coronation of Henry IV] with just moderation, and be worthy to reign eternally with him. Through.”

Here (1098) the ring is to be given.—(1099) “Receive the ring, the seal, namely, of holy faith, the stability of the kingdom, and the increase of power, by which [The correction reads: ‘whom,’ as in the coronation of Henry IV] you may know how to repel enemies with triumphant power, destroy heresies, unite your subjects, and be joined to the perseverance (1100) of the Catholic faith. Through.”

(1101) Prayer after the ring has been given.—“O God, to whom belong all power and dignity, grant your servant the effect of the Spirit of his dignity, in which, with you as his rewarder, he may remain; and may he always fear you and continually strive to please you. Through.”

Here (1102) the archbishop shall gird the sword upon him.—(1103) “Receive this sword, bestowed upon you with God’s blessing, by which, through the power of the Holy Spirit, you may be able to resist and drive away all your enemies, defend and protect all adversaries of God’s holy Church and the kingdom entrusted to you, and guard the camp of God, through the help of our unconquered triumphant Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, forever and ever.”

(1104) Prayer after the sword.—“O God, who by your providence govern heavenly and earthly things together, favor (1105) our most Christian king, so that the strength of all his enemies may be broken by the power of the spiritual sword and completely crushed as you fight on his behalf. [Col. 0258C] Through.”

Here (1106) let him be crowned.—(1107) “May God crown you with a crown of glory, with the honor of justice, and with the work of fortitude, so that through the ministry of our blessing, with right faith and the manifold fruit of good works, you may reach the crown of the everlasting kingdom, by the gift of him whose kingdom endures forever and ever.”

Prayer after the crown.—“O God, guide of the virtues of perpetuity, victor over all enemies, bless this servant of yours who bows his head to you. Preserve him in lasting health and prosperous happiness; and wherever he invokes your help, be quickly present, protect him, and defend him. Grant him, we beseech you, O Lord, the riches of your grace. Fulfill his desire with good things; crown him with mercy and compassion, and may he serve you, the Lord, with devout dedication. Through our Lord.”

261 Here the scepter is to be given.—(1108) “Receive the scepter, the emblem of royal majesty, namely, the straight rod of the kingdom, the rod of power, by which you may conduct yourself well, defend with royal strength the holy Church and the Christian people entrusted to you by God against the wicked, correct the perverse, bring peace to the upright, and direct them with your help so that they may keep to the straight way; so that from the temporal kingdom you may reach the eternal kingdom, with the help of him whose kingdom and dominion endure without end forever and ever.”

Prayer after the scepter.—“O Lord, source of all good things and God, founder of every increase, grant, we beseech you, that your servant N. may govern well the dignity he has attained, and graciously strengthen the honor appointed for him by you. Honor him above all the kings of the earth; enrich him with abundant blessing; and establish him securely upon the throne of the kingdom. Visit him in his offspring; grant him length of life; let justice always arise in his days, so that with joy and gladness he may rejoice eternally in the kingdom. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Then the rod is given to him.—(1109) “Receive the rod of power and equity, by which you may understand how to soothe the devout and terrify the reprobate. Teach the way to the one who has gone astray; extend your hand to those who have fallen; destroy the proud and raise up the humble. May Jesus Christ our Lord open the door for you, who said of himself: ‘I am the door; if anyone enters through me, he will be saved.’ May he himself, who is the key of David and the scepter of the house of Israel, who opens and no one shuts, who shuts and no one opens, be your helper. He brings the captive out of the prison house, those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, so that you may be worthy to follow him in all things, of whom the prophet David sang: ‘Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; the rod of equity is the rod of your kingdom.’ In imitation of him, who says: ‘Love justice and hate iniquity,’ may this be fulfilled: ‘Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness,’ after the example of him whom, before the ages, he anointed above his companions, Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Then let the Blessing be said.—(1110) “May almighty God extend the right hand of his blessing over you, pour out upon you the gift of his protection, and surround you with a wall of happiness and the guardianship of his favor. Through the interceding merits of holy Mary, (1111) of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, (1112) of holy Gregory, (1113) apostle of the Angles, and of all the saints, may the Lord forgive you all the evils you have committed. Amen.

“And may he grant you the grace and mercy that you humbly ask of him, and deliver you from every adversity and from the snares of all visible and invisible enemies. Amen.

“May he appoint his good angels always and everywhere to go before you, accompany you, and follow after you for your protection; and by his power may he free you from sin and the sword and from every danger. Amen.

262 (1115) “May he turn your enemies toward the kindness of peace and charity, and make you gracious and beloved by all good people; and may he clothe those who persist in pursuing and hating you with salutary confusion. May everlasting sanctification flourish over you. Amen.

“May he always make you victorious and triumphant over invisible and visible enemies; continually pour the fear and love of his holy name into your heart; make you steadfast in right faith and good works; and, granting peace in your days, lead you with the palm of victory to the eternal kingdom. Amen.

“And may he who willed to establish you as king over his people and make you prosperous in the present age grant you fellowship in eternal happiness. Amen.

“May he himself deign to grant this.”

[Col. 0260A] Another Blessing.—(1116) “Bless, O Lord, (1117) this prince and ruler, who govern all the kingdoms of kings from eternity. Amen.

“And glorify him with such a blessing that he may hold the scepter of salvation with Davidic elevation [variant: Davitic], and be found enriched with the gift of holy favor. Amen.

“Grant him, from your inspiration, to rule the people, just as you caused Solomon to obtain a peaceful kingdom. Amen.

“May he himself deign to grant this.”

### The king’s position is indicated

Stand (1118) and henceforth retain (1119) what until now you have held at your father’s (1120) prompting, delegated to you by hereditary right through the authority of almighty God and through this present handing-over by us, namely, by all the bishops and the other servants of God.
