May almighty God deign so to direct the course of your journey, etc., as in the printed edition, with the Gemet manuscripts and others agreeing.

### Another Blessing

[Col. 0609B] Look down, Lord, from heaven, see, and visit this vineyard that your right hand planted. May they display spiritual fruits, love heavenly deeds, and pass their life in this age without fault, so that they may deserve the everlasting one. Amen. Make the fragile firm; raise up the broken; strengthen the weak and confirm the strong. Support with piety, build up with charity, cleanse with chastity, enlighten with wisdom, preserve with mercy. Amen. May vigilance in faith, perseverance in your love, moderation in conduct, foresight in mercy, and discipline in action advance in accordance with this command, so that, after the pardon of your compassion has been granted, you may not reject them from the munificence of your promise, but lead to forgiveness those whom here you adopted through grace. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on Sexagesima

May the Lord grant you to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Another Blessing

May the eternal Ruler look upon you, [Col. 0609C] and preserve in you the grace he poured forth. Amen. May he govern the mind, direct the ways, kindle holy thoughts, approve actions, confirm works, forgive the past, amend the present, and regulate the future. Amen. May the Lord’s hand be your helper, and his holy arm assist you. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on Quinquagesima

May almighty God confirm you with his blessing and make you fit for the approaching forty-day abstinence [Note: [Col. 0609D] In Gemet: *abstinentia* (“abstinence,” nominative, for *abstinentiae*, “of abstinence”).]. Amen, etc., as in the printed edition.

### Another Blessing

Bless, Lord, this people of yours with good fruits and blessed works. Amen. Make it sprout such offspring that it may remain in the dignity of your paradise. Amen. Plant it in the bosom of Mother Church with firm roots, so that it may be able to enter the palaces of the heavenly kingdom. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing at the Beginning of the Fast

May the Lord Jesus Christ bless you, who willed to be blessed by you. [Col. 0609D] Amen. And he who consecrated by his own fast this forty-day cycle, whose beginning you undertake today, may he accept your fast and fill you with every good. Amen. May he give you complete faith and such salutary abstinence that neither the flesh, conquered by foods, grows wanton, nor the afflicted mind degenerates. Amen. But may your fast be so sanctified in divine fear that you impose the reins of abstinence alike upon vices and bodies, and that all of you [perhaps: safely] always remain unharmed from the attacks of the enemy; [Col. 0610A] and may quiet peace continually remain in your dwellings. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing During the Week

[Note: [Col. 0609D] It is found in Gemet, preceded by this: “Here begins how penitents ought to be received by bishops and priests.” The following passage must not be passed over without attention: “Just as no one except bishops and priests, to whom the keys of the heavenly kingdom have been entrusted, ought to offer sacrifice, so others ought not usurp these judgments. But if necessity should arise and no priest be present, let a deacon receive the penitent for holy Communion.” After this admonition are appended prayers and psalms to be said over penitents, followed by the blessing of ashes.] Look upon this flock, good Shepherd, and grant that those who abstain from earthly foods may be nourished with spiritual sustenance; and graciously absolve from every sin him whom you grant to be refreshed by the divine sacraments. Amen. Grant that during the days of fasting they may so order their lives that their wills may not be found unlike your will, but that they may always obey all your commands. Amen. And so sanctify this entire household with your blessing that their fasts may always be acceptable to the eyes of your mercy, and that, through your goodness, you may command them to be presented with pure heart and body on the desired day of your holy Resurrection. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Second Sunday in Lent

Almighty God, of the fast and the rest …, etc. In the Gussanville printed edition it ends with the words “a gracious hearer.” [Col. 0610B] The omission must be supplied from other printed and handwritten copies; everywhere else one reads: “So that our minds …,” etc., as in the Sacramentary.

### Blessing During the Week

O God, who are the guardian of souls and bodies, deign to protect this family of yours with the arm of your defense, so that you may not allow our bodies to be deceived by the snares of our ancient enemy, but that we may always remain unharmed with our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son. Amen. Grant this family of yours the warmth of faith, the rigor of self-restraint, the love of brotherhood, and the virtue of abstinence. Amen. And may your piety, kindness, clemency, and mercy deign to dissolve and forgive whatever they have sinned in word, deed, or thought. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Third Sunday in Lent

Almighty God, of the fasts, etc., as in the printed editions.

630 ### Another

May almighty God grant you an abundance of his blessing and bestow upon you the reward of eternal salvation. [Col. 0610C] Amen. May he make the fasts begun in observance of Lent pleasing to himself, so that you may be able to receive from him the imperishable gifts he promised. Amen. May the mercy of the sacred Trinity and undivided Unity grant this, whose kingdom and dominion remain without end forever and ever. Amen.

### Blessing on the Fourth Sunday in Lent

O God, who called you to present things, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Another Blessing During the Week

May almighty God bless you and train you toward the full perfection of every upright observance. Amen. May there be in you zeal for chastity, modesty of conduct, sincerity of an innocent life, integrity of faith, charity of concord, the virtue of self-restraint, and kindness of affection. May they turn their eyes toward you, receive heavenly things from you, seek you in their vows, and adorn themselves with illustrious deeds. Amen. Thus, having afterward obtained with the saints the rewards of these and many other good deeds, may we give thanks to God and to the giver of present blessings. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing at the Opening of the Ears

[Note: [Col. 0610D] On this ancient rite, see the notes to the Sacramentary, book, cols. 366 and 381.] Be present, almighty God, with this people of yours, instructed today by mystical words, so that there may be illumination of mind and restoration of heart in them. Amen. May your blessing, poured into them, advance more fully toward salvation, for on this day they have received from your sacred rites the *inaures* (“ear-openings” or “earrings”) of heart and body. Amen. Be their protector and Lord forever, as you were for the Israelites, at Moses’ warning, for their assistance, and for the Egyptians in destruction, so that they might not be oppressed by burdensome service. Amen. And lest they be further weighed down by the mass of sins, deign to impart divine protection around them, so that they may be able to serve you forever. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Fifth Sunday in Lent

May he kindle in you, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Blessing During the Week

May almighty God bless you; and may the gracious teacher instruct your minds in understanding good action and grant you the will to do what he has commanded. May he inspire what he loves and grant what is fitting; may he enrich you with every good of spiritual gifts together with the provision of present things. Amen. May he strengthen you in faith, aid you in temptation, correct you in conduct, multiply you in virtue, lift you up in weakness, and gladden you in anxiety. Amen. May he prepare you in prosperity, amend you in wrongdoing, exalt you in tranquility; may he pour in grace, forgive offense, and impose discipline. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Holy Day of Easter

May almighty God bless you, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Blessing for Monday

O God, who undertook insult for you, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Blessing for Tuesday

O God, who washed you with the water of his side, etc., as in the printed edition.

### Blessing for Wednesday

May the Lord our God lead you, etc., as in the printed edition.

631 ### Blessing for Thursday

With the blessings of almighty God and our Lord, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Blessing for Friday

[Col. 0611C] [Note: [Col. 0611D] In Gemet: “May almighty God bless you from heaven,” etc.] May almighty God bless you from heaven, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Blessing on Saturday in White

[Note: [Col. 0611D] No blessing is assigned in the printed edition of the Sacramentary. The one read in the Gemet codex for the office of this day differs entirely from this one.] O God, who, after the sixfold number had been completed, rested from all works on the holy Sabbath day, wishing to prepare for yourself in the human being you had created a dwelling in which you might rest, hear the prayers of your suppliants who faithfully hasten to your gifts of mercy. Amen. Prepare their senses to receive you, so that they may truly deserve to become your temple. Amen. And so protect these servants who are present in this life that, as ruler, you may admit them with yourself into eternal rest. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Sunday within the Octave of Easter

O God, whose Only-Begotten …, etc., as in the printed edition.

### Another Blessing

O God, who through the Resurrection of your Only-Begotten …, etc., as in the printed edition.

### Blessing on the First Sunday after Easter

[Col. 0611D] May almighty God bless you, who created you by gratuitous mercy, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Blessing for Fasting

Almighty God, devotion, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Another Blessing

Look upon, Lord, this family of yours subject to you, asking for the gifts of your blessings; rule it from your heights and grant it an abundance of crops. Amen. Free it from evil days and from the disturbance of wars, and give it peaceful and tranquil times, so that, with you as its ever-watchful guardian and eternal Shepherd, it may remain secure in the present age and reach eternal joys. [Col. 0612A] Amen. And you who once, in mercy, pitied the crowd that remained with you for three days, now likewise have mercy on this people that supplicates you, relying upon fasts and hymns. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Second Sunday after Easter

[Note: [Col. 0612D] For the Sundays after Easter, the Gemet codex presents blessings entirely different from these and from the commonly used versions.] O God, who in the generosity of your mercy and the majesty of your power visited the earth from heaven to come to humanity’s aid, and, bearing the punishment of the cross in the flesh, broke the law of Tartarus and ascended from the underworld to the heavens, grant that your family may pass through this life in such a way that, with you leading, they may enter that everlasting life. Amen. May they possess such fervor of catholic faith that they may await your holy coming without fear. Amen. And may all who deserved to be cleansed here by the water of baptism be presented to you, the merciful Judge, as candidates clothed in white. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Third Sunday after Easter

Almighty God, who always adorn your Church with diverse flowers, grant your people, reborn for heavenly glory and the honor of immortality, an adornment worthy of the renewal of their mind. Amen. Guard it from the assault of the dreadful serpent with your customary mercy, so that it may always be continually devoted to your service. Amen. Thus, with your help in the present age, may it be able to direct its life and implore your mercy, so that, with you as Shepherd and guide, it may happily reach eternal joys that endure without end. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

632 ### Blessing on the Fourth Sunday after Easter

Bless, we ask, Lord, the whole family of yours, happily summoned to the joys of everlasting resurrection. Amen. May they hold to the most upright path of catholic faith and stand firm in the one confession of the Trinity. Amen. May no impiety of corrupt assertion cause them to deviate from the rectitude of ecclesiastical doctrine, nor strip them of the protection of truth under the pretext of the Christian name; but, remaining in the same faith of unity, may they deserve to become heirs of the heavenly kingdom. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Day of the Ascension

[Col. 0612C] May God bless you, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Blessing on the Sunday after the Lord’s Ascension

May the Lord pour upon you the rain of his blessings, etc., as in the printed editions, for the First Sunday after the Lord’s Ascension.

### Another Blessing

O God, who, rising again, broke Tartarus and, ascending, opened the heavens, so that peoples might ascend there through faith, where the apostles saw you enter, look upon those for whom you deigned to descend into the underworld as you ascend into heaven. Amen. May your exaltation be their protection, for whom your humiliation was the sole remedy. Amen. May they not be numbered among the left at the day of judgment, since they confess that you sit in heaven at the Father’s right hand. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing at Pentecost

O God, who on this day …, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Blessing During the Week of Pentecost

Almighty [Col. 0612D] God, who prefigured the fiftieth day by the gift of future remission, when the apostles, intoxicated with the grace of the Holy Spirit, spoke with one mind in different languages, look upon this Church, which you signified would be gathered from the nations through the diversity of tongues. Amen. Give consolation amid the pressures of the world, you who sent us the Spirit, a Comforter equal to yourself. Amen. And, with you propitious, may he now be the guardian of this people, who then gave teaching to the disciples. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing at the Twelve Readings, in the Fourth Month

[Note: [Col. 0612D] That is, on the Saturday of the Twelve Readings.] May almighty God bless you, who created all things from nothing, as in the Sacramentary edited by us, for the Saturday of the Twelve Readings in the fourth month. In Gemet the same blessing is assigned for the entire week.

### Blessing on the Octave of Pentecost

Almighty Trinity, one and true God, etc., as in the printed editions.

### Another Blessing

Lord Jesus Christ, who gave your disciples the Holy Spirit, bestow gifts upon your catholic Church, so that all who have been reborn of water and the Holy Spirit may always be protected by it. Amen. May the charity poured out through the Holy Spirit overflow in them, covering and surpassing the whole multitude of sins. Amen. And may he graciously rest in these people who once rested gloriously in the apostles. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the First Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost

Bless, Lord, this entire family that desires to find the grace of your blessing; send your own hand from heaven and touch the head of each person. Amen. May the grace of your blessing descend upon all these people, just as dew descended upon the face of the earth. Amen. May they feel the touch of your hand and receive the joy of the Holy Spirit, so that, once blessed, they may remain forever. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Second Sunday after Pentecost

May the Lord be reconciled to all your iniquities, etc., as in the printed edition for the Third Sunday after Pentecost.

### Blessing on the Third Sunday after Pentecost

May our Lord bless you with the speech of his mouth, etc., as for the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost.

### Blessing on the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost

May the Lord cleanse your consciences, etc., as for the Fifth Sunday after Pentecost.

### Blessing on the Fifth Sunday after Pentecost

May the Lord recognize in you his own sign and bestow upon you the gift of his mercy. Amen. May he restrain wars, remove famine, grant peace, and drive the enemy’s snares far away. Amen. May he see the groans of those who mourn; may he hear the voice of your grief and wipe away tears from every face. Amen. May he grant you everlasting love and bestow perfect charity. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost

May the Lord remove from you every stain of hostility, etc., as for the Seventh Sunday after Pentecost.

### Blessing on the Seventh Sunday after Pentecost

May almighty God bless you and strengthen your heart through the abundance of his mercy. Amen. May he sanctify your mind, enlarge your life, adorn your chastity, and always build up your senses in good works; may he grant prosperity, bestow peace, confer salvation, nourish quiet, unite charity, and always defend you by his protection and power from every demonic and human ambush. Amen. And, being propitious, may he always accept your devotion, so that whatever you ask of him he may mercifully grant. May he remove all the evils you have committed and grant the grace for which you always ask. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Eighth Sunday after Pentecost

May the grace of the Lord sanctify you, etc., as for the Ninth Sunday after Pentecost in the printed edition.

### Blessing on the Ninth Sunday after Pentecost

Hear the petitions of your people, Lord, and swiftly help those placed amid calamities. Amen. Let those whom you see laboring under too great a burden rejoice in their own deliverance. May they exult and rejoice in you when they see themselves saved by you. Amen. Send them, Lord, the unconquerable [perhaps: victorious] weapons of your defense, with which they may lay all wars low. [Col. 0614A] Amen. May they be visited by your help at every moment, so that, having overcome the powers of their enemies, they may be strengthened. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Tenth Sunday after Pentecost

O God, who are the life of mortals and the salvation of sinners, etc., as for the Eleventh Sunday after Pentecost in the printed edition.

### Blessing on the Eleventh Sunday after Pentecost

May the Lord grant you the gift of charity, the fruit of forgiveness, and fellowship in eternal life. Amen. May he wipe away from you all stains of sins, so that you may deserve to recognize him vigilantly, worship him faithfully, and await him desirably. Amen. May he illumine his grace over you and have mercy on you, just as he illumined Moses and the children of Israel in the pillar of fire and cloud. May he give you the gift of perpetual grace and grant the joy of the angels. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

634 ### Blessing on the Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost

[Col. 0614B] May the Lord enrich you with the gift of his grace and guard you with heavenly blessing, etc., as in the printed edition of the Sacramentary, where, with the Gemet codex agreeing, one nevertheless reads: “May the Lord enrich you with his grace.”

### Blessing on the Thirteenth Sunday after Pentecost

May the Lord, ruler and creator of the heavens, bless you and give you tranquility of times, health of bodies, and salvation of souls. Amen. May he grant you the joy of frugality, the reward of eternity, and the brightest everlasting light. Amen. And may he grant you the help of his mercy, so that the mind may see with thought, the tongue speak with its voice, and action may not defend the deed. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Fourteenth Sunday after Pentecost

May the blessing of the Lord accompany you, etc., as in the printed editions for the Fifteenth Sunday after Pentecost.

### Blessing on the Fifteenth Sunday after Pentecost

[Col. 0614C] Bless, Lord, this people of yours, and preserve all these people in concord, quiet, peace, and safety. Amen. Grant that they may pursue not destruction but life, not the flesh but the spirit, not temporal things but eternal things. Amen. So that, absolved not only through their works but also justified, they may be worthy to earn life and glory. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Sixteenth Sunday after Pentecost

May almighty God cleanse the stains of your sins, etc., as for the Seventeenth Sunday after Pentecost in the printed edition.

### Blessing on the Seventeenth Sunday after Pentecost

Bless, Lord, your people, and look upon their devotion; see their humility, receive their groans, and command that those who grieve be consoled with fatherly compassion. Amen. Raise up the prostrate, gather the scattered, preserve those brought together, feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, and water them all together [Col. 0614D] with heavenly gifts. Amen. Erase every stain of sin in them, so that, with you governing them, they may reach everlasting glory. Amen. Sanctify with the blessing of your right hand all heads bowed before you, and, by blessing, release sins. Pour out the gifts of the Holy Spirit, so that they may fulfill the commands of your Majesty without any offense and, with your help, reach eternal life. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Saturday of the Twelve Readings, in the Seventh Month, and on Wednesday

O God, fountain of forgiveness, graciously receive the sacrifice of your abstinence. Amen. Fill your hearts with delight in his sacrifices and grant you the power to obey his commands. Amen. So that what you cannot accomplish because of bodily weakness, you may deserve to fulfill through the abundance of his grace. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

[Col. 0615A] ### Blessing on the Eighteenth Sunday after Pentecost

May the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ bless you and, in consideration of heavenly mercy, protect you under the shadow of his power. Amen. May he give you compunction of soul, undefiled faith, and purity of conscience. Amen. May he direct your senses, pierce your hearts with compunction, assist you in prosperity, extend his hand in adversity, and bring comfort in labors. Amen. May he multiply the merits of his virtues, call forth right counsels, and remove from you the burdens of earthly things. Amen. May he fill your hearts with spiritual gifts and always make you abound in increases of perfect grace. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost

Invisible, immeasurable, infinite, everlasting, immense God, our creator and redeemer, alien in nature to both beginning and end: illumine this solemn assembly of your people as a pledge of your own blood. Amen. 635 Govern the aged minds of widows, [Col. 0615B] the concerns of virgins, the vows of married people, the desires of orphans, the needs of children, and the falls of little infants. Amen. For you are the rest of good minds, the guardian of fortunate young people, the bridegroom of holy virgins, the defender of faithful widows, the fidelity of honorable spouses, the father of laboring orphans, the teacher of progressing children, and equally the receiver and nourisher of infants. Amen. In you may old age begin, adulthood be strengthened, and long life be brought to completion. Through you may integrity rejoice that it is not corrupted; through you may chastity know that it is restored, pure faith not destroyed, a displeasing life amended, mercy practiced, self-restraint preserved, and innocence not overcome. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Twentieth Sunday after Pentecost

May the divine Majesty of the Trinity, the one Godhead—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—bless you and find you on the day of examination as those whom the fountain of rebirth sent forth. Amen. May the Lord bless you, who is the author of all things and everlasting creator. May he preserve your body undefiled and mercifully protect your souls. Amen. And may he render you innocent of every crime of sin, so that the Holy Spirit may remain in you and you may await his coming without fear. Amen. May he bless you from heaven, who deigned to redeem you on earth with his most holy blood. Amen. The blessing of God the Father, etc.

### Blessing on the Twenty-First Sunday after Pentecost

Lord Jesus Christ, good Shepherd, who laid down your life for the sheep, defend the purchase of your blood; graciously deign to visit your flock; feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, seek what was lost, convert what has gone astray, bind up what is broken, strengthen what is weak, and preserve what is strong. Amen. Make them live in justice before your sight and, if they have guarded themselves, be judged with mercy. Grant them belief in faith, strength in labor, devotion in affection, prosperity in action, abundance in sustenance, joy in peace, grace in conduct, and victory in struggle. Amen. So that, walking on the path pleasing in your sight, they may pass through the present time with happiness and receive the future with gladness. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Twenty-Second Sunday after Pentecost

May the grace of the Lord’s blessing always protect you, etc., as in the printed edition for the Twenty-Third Sunday after Pentecost.

### Blessing on the Twenty-Third Sunday after Pentecost

May almighty Lord open your mouth in his law, etc., as in the printed edition for the Twenty-Fourth Sunday after Pentecost; in Gemet it is assigned to the Twenty-Third Sunday.

### Blessing on the Twenty-Fourth Sunday after Pentecost

May the Lord look upon you and bless you; may the eternal King guard you on every side and give you an angel of light, [Col. 0616A] and preserve in you the grace he poured forth. Amen. May he govern the mind, direct the ways, instruct holy thoughts, furnish actions [*praebeat*, “furnish”; perhaps *probeat*, “approve”], confirm works, forgive the past, amend the present, and regulate the future. Amen. May the Lord’s hand be your helper, and his holy arm assist you; may his mercy be upon you, and his loving kindness follow you. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Twenty-Fifth Sunday after Pentecost
Bless you and sanctify you, O Lord, from Zion, who in your wisdom made heaven and earth, with the eternal blessing with which you blessed all our holy fathers and patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Amen. May he multiply spiritual grace in you, just as he multiplied their offspring like the stars of heaven and like the sand upon the seashore. Amen. May he himself protect and defend you throughout all the days of your life, and lead you into his kingdom of glory. Amen. [Col. 0616B] May he himself grant this, etc.

**636. Blessing for the Twenty-Sixth Sunday after Pentecost**

O God, founder and ruler of your people, drive away the sins by which they are assailed. Guard them with perpetual protection and defend them from every adversity. Amen. Visit them through the intercession of all the saints, as you visited Moses in the bush, Joshua in the field, and Samuel in the temple; and pour over them that wisdom which blessed King David received in the Psalter, and Solomon in his son, when you bestowed it from heaven. Amen. And finally preserve them with fatherly mercy, so that, rejecting whatever is perverse, they may be strengthened in holy conduct and, freed from sins, may not be crushed by any adversities. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for the Twenty-Seventh Sunday after Pentecost**

May God the Father bless you, who in the beginning created all things from nothing. Amen. May the Son of God bless you, who descended most humbly from his heavenly seat. Amen. May the Holy Spirit bless you, who in the likeness [Col. 0616C] of a dove rested upon Christ in the river Jordan, and may he himself sanctify you in the Trinity, whom all nations await as the one who is to come. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for the Twenty-Eighth Sunday after Pentecost**

We beseech you, O Lord, that abundant blessing may descend upon your people. Amen. May forgiveness come and consolation be granted. Amen. May holy faith increase and eternal redemption be confirmed. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for the Fifth Sunday before the Nativity of the Lord**

May the Lord grant you the reward of the most sincere charity, etc., as in the printed editions.

**Blessing for the Fourth Sunday after the Nativity of the Lord**

Almighty God, whose Only-Begotten Son’s advent, etc., as in the printed edition.

**Another Blessing.**—Open, O Lord, the gates of heaven and [Col. 0616D] visit your people in peace. Send forth your Spirit from on high, water the earth, and let it bring forth spiritual fruit. Amen. Sanctify your people, O Lord, you who were given to us from the Virgin, and bless your inheritance in peace. Amen. Grant them always the seasons of salvation which the holy prophet John foretold before your advent, so that here they may receive them faithfully and in the future may obtain eternal life and the kingdom with your saints and elect. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for the Third Sunday before the Nativity of the Lord**

God, whose incarnate advent, etc., as in the printed editions.

**Another Blessing.**—May the Lord Jesus Christ, who in his most sacred advent deigned to come to the world’s aid, purify your souls and bodies from sin. Amen. May he grant you, through the power of the Holy Spirit, to grasp the precepts of his law, so that you may await [Col. 0617A] his advent without fear. Amen. And may he render you free from every guilt, so that when he comes he may not strike you down in terror, but receive you to be rewarded in glory. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for the Second Sunday before the Nativity of the Lord**

May Almighty God regard you with a favorable countenance, etc., as in the printed editions.

**Another Blessing.**—Stir up your power, O Lord, and come for the salvation of your people, whom you acquired with your blood, lest that savage enemy of the human race rejoice in their destruction—the one whom, by the power of your advent, you long ago freed through grace. Amen. May the strength of your right hand be for the protection of this family of yours, for whose sake you deigned at this time to put on virginal flesh. Amen. And although your mercy does not fail to recognize our weakness, protect this whole Church of yours with the shield of your divinity, so that you may free us from the temptation of that savage ancient enemy, and so moderate the ferocity of the nations that [Col. 0617B] their arrows may be able to cause none of your people any loss. Amen. But you, good Shepherd, who gave yourself for our sake as the price, defend the purchase of your blood in such a way that they may always feel you going before them here, and, with you as their rewarder, may deserve to receive their reward in eternal blessedness. Amen. Therefore, almighty Lord Jesus Christ, drench them with the dew of blessings, so that, while placed in the present life, they may have you as their deliverer from all enemies, and here and forever may always experience you as their protector. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for the First Sunday before the Nativity of the Lord**

God, who you and of the former advent, etc., as in the printed editions.

**Another Blessing.**—O God, who through your angel announced that Christ would come into the world, grant, we beseech you, that your people may now deserve to meet him who is coming with joy. Amen. May he who said, “Let there be light,” before the ages, direct your hearts through the seasons. Amen. And may he grant you forgiveness of sins, who poured out his own blood on the cross for human salvation. Amen. May he bless you from heaven, he who came on earth to redeem us through the cross of his [Col. 0617C] passion. Amen. The blessing of God the Father.

**January 25. The Conversion of Saint Paul**

O God, who by your grace Paul, etc., as in the printed editions.

**Blessing at the Purification of Saint Mary**

Almighty God, who, etc., as in the printed editions.

[**Note:** [Col. 0617D] It exists in the Gemet manuscript, where the blessing for the feast of Saint Vedast follows it immediately.]

**Blessing on the Feast of Saint Agatha**

Sanctify your Church, O Lord, who acquired blessed Agatha, virgin and martyr, through faith, honored her through modesty, and glorified her through struggle. Amen. May this people be filled with that Spirit who was present with your martyr Agatha when fire scorched her, when the claw scraped her, when the pointed instrument pierced her, and when the breast was tortured. Amen. So that, while she denies herself for love of you, she may place herself in your right hand, by whose choosing she was called to glory. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

[**Note:** It is found in the same Gemet manuscript.]

**Blessing on the Chair of Saint Peter, February 22**

O God, who made your blessed apostle Peter so pre-eminent that he received the primacy among the princes of faith, and, having received the power of the seat in this [Col. 0617D] world, became the doorkeeper of heaven, so that he may admit into the kingdom as citizens those whom he wishes: look upon your people with your customary mercy. You strengthened the step of the holy apostle on slippery ground and washed away his faults through lamentation. Amen. May he obtain favor with you for the correction of sins, who was a remedy for the lame in directing their footsteps. Amen. And through his intercession and with him as their rewarder, may the flock entrusted to him be led by forgiveness to that place where the same shepherd and doorkeeper rejoices with you, rewarded in glory. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

[Col. 0618A] **Blessing on the Feast of Saint Matthias the Apostle, February 24**

O God, who granted that you should stand upon apostolic foundations, etc., as in the printed editions. It is absent from Gemet.

**Blessing on the Finding of the Holy Cross**

May Almighty God bless you, who through the Only-Begotten Son’s, etc., as in the printed editions.

**Blessing on the Nativity of Saint Medard**

[**Note:** [Col. 0617D] The same blessing is assigned in the Gemet manuscript for the feast of Saint Vedast, with only the saint’s name changed.]

O God, founder of faith, giver of the priesthood, gathering of the people, sanctification of the confessor, who armed blessed Medard with such strength that he might serve you as a soldier in faith: grant this family, for its own sake, this intercessor whom you gave as a bishop. Amen. May he now be a constant intercessor for us with you, who then stood forth as your defender against heretics. Amen. So that, with you as the giver of recompense, what the priest labored for in faith may increase among the people without number. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

[**Note:** [Col. 0618D] It is read in the Gemet manuscript.]

**Blessing on the Vigil of Saint John the Baptist**

[Col. 0618B] O God, who announced blessed John the Baptist as great through an angel and declared him greatest through the Word; who, while enclosed in the womb, rendered service to the Lord, filled his mother with joy, and released his father’s tongue from its bond: look with a kindly face upon the people who today throng to meet so great a herald. Amen. May his voice rise to the ears of the Most High, for he knew how to confess the Lord of the world in his mother’s womb before he was born. Amen. So that through his intercession this people may be cleansed from guilt—the author of the washing, whom his sacred right hand baptized in the font. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Feast of the Apostles Peter and Paul**

May he bless you, etc., as in the printed edition.

**Another Blessing.**—O God, who caused Peter’s tears and Paul’s writings to shine in the members of the Church like a doubled light by which darkness might be avoided, grant that this family of yours may obtain happy gifts through its tireless petitions. Amen. And look favorably upon it from the heavenly seats, you who caused the heavens to be opened: to Peter by the key, [Col. 0618C] to Paul by doctrine. Amen. So that, with such leaders going before them, the flock may be able to reach the place to which both of them arrived together—the one as shepherd through hanging, the other as teacher through the sword. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Feast of Saint Lawrence the Martyr**

[**Note:** Another blessing is assigned in the Gemet manuscript, namely: “May the blessing of the Holy Trinity descend upon you,” etc.]

Strengthen your flock, tower of strength, who first adorned blessed Lawrence in heart, then in speech, and honored him with confession before you adorned him with martyrdom. Amen. Pour into those standing here the spirit of faith, which was present with the confessor, lest wounds make them fearful, punishment weary, or flame overcome. Amen. So that, through his intercession and with you as his rewarder, this people may shine with that light with which the levite shone in prison, and gleam with that faith by which the victorious martyr entered heaven on this day. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Assumption of Saint Mary**

[Col. 0618D] O God, who through the childbirth of blessed Mary the virgin deigned to redeem the human race, etc., as in the Sacramentary.

**Blessing on the Feast of Saint Bartholomew**

[**Note:** [Col. 0618D] It exists in the Gemet manuscript.]

O God, who granted that your Church should stand upon apostolic foundations, we beseech you that the blessed apostle Bartholomew may intercede for us, so that, absolved from our sins, we may also be freed from every danger. Amen. Pour into our minds the ability to retain the apostolic teachings, by which we may contemplate you with a serene mind. Amen. Mercifully grant to the people standing here that, at that terrifying time of judgment, they may be defended [Col. 0619A] by the protection of those whose command they have been taught. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Beheading of Saint John the Baptist**

O God, who grants us [the feast] of blessed John the Baptist, etc., as in the printed edition.

**Another.**—Rule the hearts of your people, O Lord, with the weapons of righteousness. Let one who is attentive and diligent regarding life flee the wantonness of sinful flesh. Amen. [**Perhaps:** “diligent regarding eternal life, let him flee the wantonness.”] Wash away their sins through the merits of your Baptist, who, slain for you in prison, rejoices with you in the kingdom. Amen. And may he be an intercessor with you for the people whom you made equal to Elijah in merits and whom you set above all others in purity of offspring. Amen. Look upon the desires of your people, O merciful judge, with the face of one who pardons rather than of a judge. Amen. May he obtain gifts of forgiveness from you who devoutly preached repentance to the peoples, so that, at his request and by your gift, they may deserve to enter the palaces of the heavenly court. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

[Col. 0619B] **Blessing on the Nativity of Saint Mary**

[**Note:** A blessing for this solemnity is also assigned in the Gemet Pontifical, but it is different and begins: “Almighty God, who through the incarnate Only-Begotten Word,” etc. Another is added: “May Almighty God deign to bless you with his protection,”—]

O God, whom the heavens cannot contain, yet who deigned to be enclosed in the temple of a virginal womb, so that an untouched mother might have both fruit from the Spirit and incorruption from childbirth: give this people the guardian angel who foretold the Son of Mary while she conceived him through faith. Amen. May that blessing sanctify your flock which formed the Virgin’s Redeemer in her womb without human seed. Amen. So that, while you protect her, the Church may rejoice over the gathered people, just as Mary merited glory from the sacred fruit. Amen. And since on this day we devoutly celebrate the nativity of your most sacred virgin mother Mary, whom you placed above the choirs of virgins in the seats of paradise, command that, after casting off the burden of the flesh, we may be led by her intercessions to eternal kingdoms. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Exaltation of the Holy Cross**

[**Note:** [Col. 0620D] The same blessing is read in Gemet.]

O God, who redeemed the human race through the gallows of the blessed [Col. 0619C] cross, so that what had formerly been punishment for the wicked might become life for the converted and redeemed: grant your people to be saved by the protection of that cross whose standard arms them. Amen. May the cross be for them the foundation of faith, the assistance of hope, defense in adversity, and help in prosperity. Amen. May victory endure against the enemy, concord in the city, protection in the field, and support in the home, so that it may preserve the flock unharmed in the future—that cross which, with the Lamb victorious, has been turned for us into salvation. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Feast of Saints Cornelius and Cyprian**

Hear the prayers of those who entreat you, reward of the nations, restoration of those who confess. Amen. May this family of yours have the gifts of acquiring salvation and of offering vows of speech to your Majesty. Amen. So that, through the intercession of the blessed martyrs Cornelius and Cyprian, this devoted people may come by forgiveness to the place where those same martyrs deserved to arrive through torments. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Michael**

[Col. 0619D] O God, who for your salvation permits you to use the ministry of his angels, etc., as in the printed edition.

**Another Blessing.**—Be present to your people, merciful God, who have gathered in the greatest devotion for today’s solemnity; and, so that they may receive the more excellent benefits of your grace, cause them to be lifted up through the supplications of the blessed archangel Michael, whose solemn feast is being celebrated. Amen. Defend them from every stain of sins and lead them to your eternal promises. Amen. Remove from them the deadly flatteries of the serpent and implant continually in their hearts the salutary commands of your precept. Amen. Direct their actions according to your will, so that, with your [Col. 0620A] help, they may attain the rewards of eternal life. Amen. Finally, deign to be for them light, salvation, and always a merciful protector in every adversity; and, to obtain all these things, may the blessed archangel Michael, whose solemn feast we celebrate, approach you, O Lord, as an intercessor forever. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**640. Blessing on the Feast of Saints Remigius, Germanus, Vedast, and Bavo**

[**Note:** [Col. 0620D] It is found in Gemet in the same words.]

O God, who so glorified your blessed confessors Remigius, Germanus, Vedast, and Bavo through their merits that they live in glory through many miracles: mercifully grant to the family standing here that it may experience your benefits as it celebrates today the feasts of the holy bishops. Amen. Pour the Holy Spirit into the breasts of those who entreat you, whom you teach through the examples of the blessed, whom you enrich through the protection of confessors, so that, as you excel in the virtues of your blessed confessors and surpass them in power, you may deign, with all enemies laid low, to save your people from Satan’s attack. Amen. And through their intercession [Col. 0620B] may this people obtain forgiveness, since, with you as their rewarder, they reached everlasting glory. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

[Col. 0620B] **Blessing on the Nativity of All Saints**

Through the merits of all his saints, etc., as in the printed edition. It is absent from Gemet, where three blessings for this day are assigned that are entirely different from those printed and from those assigned in the following Theodulf manuscript.

**Another Blessing.**—Look down, we beseech you, O Lord, from the lofty throne of your majesty, you who through the wound of your own passion gathered the Church from the redeemed. Amen. Protect it under the governance of your name, so that you may acquire a people through the merits of blessed life. Amen. May your cross be extended, so that it may shine before you as most beautiful and glorious. Amen. And may it, which rejoices over today’s solemnity of all your saints, not be overwhelmed by the trials of this world. Amen. Therefore grant, O Lord, that all those who bow beneath the blessing of our lips may, while you protect them, be freed from every [Col. 0620C] evil. Amen. May they be vigorous in your commands, strongest in adversity, and moderate in prosperity, so that, made participants in all the saints whose solemn feasts we celebrate today, they may obtain the glory of the heavenly kingdom as heirs. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Feast of Saint Martin**

[**Note:** [Col. 0620D] It exists in the Gemet manuscript, with a few changes.]

Almighty God, who predestined blessed Martin as your bishop so that you might command him to be bound perpetually to your grace, raise up the prayers of the people to whom you granted the glorious merits of your confessor. Amen. May whatever they embrace in the priest for the praise of your name advance them toward fruitfulness, and may this people obtain through his intercession forgiveness, since, with you as his rewarder, he reached glory through faithful service. Amen. May that confessor himself be the constant guardian of this people, who today, at your call, entered the heavens. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle**

[**Note:** [Col. 0620D] In the Gemet Pontifical there is another blessing both for the vigil and for the feast day of Saint Andrew.]

O God, who granted that your Church should stand upon apostolic [Col. 0620D] foundations, we beseech you that the blessed apostle Andrew may intercede for us, so that, absolved from our sins, we may also be freed from every danger. Amen. Pour apostolic teachings into our minds, by which we may contemplate you with a serene mind. Amen. Mercifully grant to the people standing here that, at that terrifying time of judgment, they may be defended by the protection of those whose command they have followed. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Feast of Saint Eligius**

O God, who joined your most blessed bishop Eligius to yourself with such intimacy that, while he still [Col. 0621A] dwelt bodily on earth, he was already wholly in heaven in heart: look upon the prayers of the present family, which rejoices to celebrate the solemn feast of so great a patron. Amen. Deign, through his intercession, to pour out upon it those petitions which you freely choose to fulfill. Amen. And may it experience on earth the arrival of this feast which it longs by its prayers to behold in heaven. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Nativity of Saint Nicasius**

O God, who with your powerful right hand open the royal hall of heaven to martyrs triumphing through you, and who so refine those fighting for you in bodily hardships that you receive them above like gleaming gold: hear the prayers of the present people, to whom you granted victory in combat through your holy martyr Nicasius. Amen. May glory be full for this family on account of his triumph; may his passion obtain forgiveness for sin; and pour over them the gifts of spiritual virtues, so that the enemy may neither seize anything from them by force nor deceive them by fraud. Amen. And, with your blessed martyr Nicasius obtaining [Col. 0621B] favor for us—for whose passion’s feast we celebrate today—may we deserve to reach your grace through perseverance in good conduct. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Nativity of Saint Thomas the Apostle**

Lord God of all graces, deign to look upon all this people of yours, who serve you in divine [Col. 0621B] offices in your honor; and whatever profited your holy apostle Thomas toward blessedness on this day, may it profit this Church as an example. Amen. So that, through his intercession, there may be among them upright faith, an imitable pattern, chaste sobriety, hospitable charity, spiritual prudence, lofty wisdom, a humble mind, and an exalted life. Amen. And when they stand in your presence before the fearful day of judgment, may they hear from your mouth not a sentence of condemnation but the gentle sentence of absolution. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Nativity of One Confessor**

May Almighty God grant you, etc., as in the printed editions.

[Col. 0621C] **Blessing on the Dedication of a Church**

May Almighty God bless and keep you, and illuminate this house through the presence of his gift, etc., as in the printed editions.

**Another Blessing.**—O God, who upon the mystical rock of apostolic power promised that the gates of hell would never prevail against the Church you established as the principal one: mercifully remove from it every error, so that whatever the presumption of falsehood raises against it, the Spirit of truth may overcome. Amen. Direct it by heavenly administration, so that it—which has always been prepared in your presence before the beginning of the world—may, under your governance, reach the fullness of promised glory. Amen. Mercifully deign to enter this house, we beseech you, and build for yourself an everlasting dwelling in the hearts of your faithful, so that this people, which with its face cast down upon the earth asks for the gift of your blessing, may receive eternal reward from you. Amen. [Col. 0621D] Grant, O Lord, that this basilica, whose foundations we begin today, or whose dedication we celebrate, and also the people who have gathered for its solemnities, may always become splendid through your habitation, since it subsists through your building. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Anniversary of a Church’s Dedication**

Bless this family of yours, O Lord, redeemed by the outpouring of precious blood and reborn through holy baptism. Amen. Give it, O Lord, this gift of your grace: that it may love you, cherish you, and follow you. Amen. May it reject evil, pursue good, desire what is everlasting, despise earthly things, scorn what is perishable, and long for heavenly things. Amen. And while it gathers with devoted minds in your holy name for this day of the dedication of this temple, may it, under your governance, reach the place of your glorious dwelling. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

[Col. 0622A] **642. Blessing for Ordinary Days**

May the Lord give you the gift of his blessing and fill you, etc., as in the preceding appendix, where, instead of “May the Lord give you the gift,” etc., we read: “May Almighty God give you grace,” etc.

**Another.**—May Almighty God surround you with heavenly protection and enrich you with the gift of his blessing. Amen. And may he grant that you who rely upon the hope of heavenly grace alone may also be fortified by heavenly protection. Amen. So that in the present world you may receive the consolations of mortal life and be able to attain everlasting joys. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Another.**—May Almighty God [give you] the right hand of his, etc., as in the appendix.

**Another.**—May Almighty God purify, etc., as in the said appendix.

**Another.**—May Almighty God [do] all things, etc., as in the preface to the appendix.

**Another.**—May Almighty God [bless] your days, etc., in the same place.

[Col. 0622B] **Blessing over a King**

May the Lord bless you and keep you; and just as he willed to establish you as king over his people, so may he grant you to be happy in the present world and to share in eternal happiness. Amen. May he cause the clergy and people whom he willed to gather through his assistance and your sanction to be governed happily for long ages through his administration and your rule. Amen. So that, obeying divine admonitions, free from every adversity, overflowing with every good, and serving you with joyful love through your ministry, they may enjoy the tranquility of peace in the present world and, together with you, deserve to attain fellowship with the eternal citizens. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing in Any Tribulation**

May God, the consolation of the sorrowful and refuge of the afflicted, cherish you [Col. 0622C] with his arm and mercifully make you unharmed from the dangers that threaten. Amen. May he fortify you with the shield of the right hand of the Almighty and surround you with the impregnable wall of his strength against the tribulation at hand. Amen. May he, reconciled to you, turn away the anger of his judgment from you, and, granting you the harbor of salvation, establish you fearless in the security of his protection. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Another Blessing.**—O God, founder and ruler of your people, drive away the sins by which they are assailed, so that, always pleasing to you, they may be secure under your protection. Amen. Give your people the affection of constant devoutness, so that, rejecting whatever is perverse, they may be strengthened in holy conduct and, freed from sins, may not be crushed by any adversities. Amen. Come to the aid, O Lord, we beseech you, of the people who entreat you, and kindly grant your help to the weak, so that, devoted to you with a sincere mind, they may rejoice in the remedies of the present life and of the future. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing on the Dedication of a Baptistery**

O God, who through the gift of holy baptism inspire the hearts of the faithful with hope, strengthen them in faith, and fortify them with charity, we beseech you with poured-out prayers in this [Col. 0622D] house of the baptistery, whose solemn rites we are beginning, that you may preserve forever the grace you granted this people through the washing. Amen. And join by your mercy to the assemblies of the saints those whom you watered with saving waters through grace; and command that all whom you led unharmed from the water of renewal, through the outpouring of the Spirit, the Paraclete, may become coeternal with your saints. Amen. Remember, hear the prayers, fulfill the vows of your servants, and write in the book of life the names of those who seek you, so that in every consecration the presence of the altar, of the people, of the temple, and of the baptistery may be effected not by the voice or tongue of mortals, but by your power, whom we serve. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**643. Blessing at a Gathering of Bishops**

[Col. 0623A] O God, who, after that glorious ascent of the resurrection, promised never to be absent from your worshipers, grant to us your priests, or to this priest, that grace by which we may be perfect, or by which he may be perfect, fervent in governance, or fervent in governance, and perfect in charity. Amen. Through the merits of these, or of this one, forgive the people their sins, whom you make just for the crown. Teach them, or him, holy doctrines, and multiply the fruits of righteousness in their works, or in his. Amen. So that, fortified, or fortified, by the shepherd’s care, they may escape, or may escape, the punishments of Tartarus and deserve, or deserve, to attain the glory of the everlasting kingdom. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing when a Holy Religious Virgin Is Blessed and Mass Is Celebrated in a Nunnery**

[Col. 0623B] Pour your heavenly blessing, O Lord, upon this people prostrate before you, or upon this virginal company which humbles itself beneath your right hand. Protect them with divine protection, so that they may flee every sin and always strive to fulfill your commands. Amen. May they know that good desires have been prepared for them, so that they may seek the heavenly kingdom in a holy place; may they always obey the divine commands, and, with your help, conquer the fires of the flesh. Amen. May they overcome every lust for wicked pleasure through love of honorable charity. May they always have within themselves the oil of holiness, so that they may rejoice at the bridegroom’s coming with their lamps. Amen. May they carry sacred torches in their hands, so that with the wise virgins, with Christ as their guide, they may deserve to enter with him into the wedding feast. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing over the Handmaids of God**

[Col. 0623C] Eternal Lord God, who mercifully redeemed both sexes from the destruction of everlasting death through Jesus Christ your Son, born of Mary ever-virgin, deign to bless these your handmaids, who serve you with devoted minds, with every heavenly blessing. Amen. May they have complete faith in you and always persevere in the precepts of your law; may they despise earthly and transitory things and seek inward and invisible things with attentive meditation. Amen. And may they remain among the number of holy virgins, so that they may confidently go out to meet the heavenly Bridegroom with unquenchable lamps. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for Those Setting Out on a Journey**

[Col. 0623C] May the Lord direct your journey according to his good pleasure, and may the most kind guardian remain inseparably with you. Amen. May he provide the archangel Raphael as your guide, and, being reconciled to you, remove every inconvenience and opposition from you. Amen. May he mercifully fulfill the devout desires of your hearts, so that you may deservedly attain good things here and happily reach eternal blessedness. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Another Blessing.**—May the God of our salvation make your journey prosperous, and lead you along straight paths over mountain heights, through valley slopes, across level fields, through river fords, and into the secluded places of forests. May the Lord’s help protect you, so that no stumbling block of the enemy may prevail [Col. 0623D] against you. Amen. By day may the shadow of the Lord’s salvation surround you; by night may friendly rest cherish you and bring you grace; may the Lord’s right hand lead you wondrously, and may he place before your face an angel of divine peace as your companion. Amen. May the devil be absent from you on the road, together with the cause of loss, the ruin of sin, the mishap of inconvenience, and the lot of danger; and may the one God of the undivided Trinity alone take care to lead you out to aid and protection and to bring you back. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Another Blessing.**—O God, who make all things work together for good for those who love you, and who are distant in no region from those who serve you: pour the grace of your blessing over this family and direct your servant N., who is proceeding according to your will. Amen. Grant, therefore, O Lord, that this people may always deserve to have you as its protector, and that your aforesaid servant, while placed in this life, may have you as his companion on the journey. Amen. So that both the people mentioned above [Col. 0624A] and those who undertake this journey, preceded by your help, may walk along the paths of righteousness without the offense of sin. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Another Blessing.**—May the Lord bless you with the gift of his divinity, so that you may proceed successfully toward deeds of the firmest security. Amen. May he watch over your journey, follow behind and go before, direct your steps, and lead you without offense to the places of just administration. Amen. So that you may faithfully honor his glory on the journey of this world and, returning to the homeland of paradise, rejoice without end in the angelic choirs. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing in Time of War**

We beseech you, almighty God, be reconciled to the sins of your people and turn away from us the terrors of every hostility, so that the secure freedom of the Christian name may always rejoice in devotion to you and serve you in submissive service. Amen. Strike down the pride of all our adversaries and overthrow the [Col. 0624B] defiance of our enemies through the power of your right hand. Amen. May invincible defense by your power fortify this faithful people, so that, always devoted to you with pious affection, it may be freed from hostile enemies and continually persevere in your grace. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for Asking for Rain**

[Col. 0624B] Incline, we beseech you, O Lord, the ears of your mercy to the prayers of your people, and deign to water the face of the whole earth with abundant rains. Amen. Grant healthful breezes and restore their former health to the sick, so that souls thirsting for your promises may always be filled more abundantly from your overflowing charity. Amen. Give us, we beseech you, saving rain, and graciously pour heavenly streams upon the dry face of the earth. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing for Asking for Fair Weather**

[Col. 0624C] We humbly implore your magnificence, O Lord, that you who powerfully frightened your people with the dangers of the rains that threatened may command the same people, prostrate beneath the blessing of your mouth, to be consoled by the granting of fair weather. Amen. So that, having received prosperity in human affairs, we may rejoice in earthly consolations. Amen. And may we not cease to seek heavenly joys; rather, may whatever burden obstructs temporal gladness be driven away by eternal instruction. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing in a Time of Mortality, God Forbid**

[Col. 0624C] O God, who always desire not the death but the repentance of sinners, mercifully turn your people, prostrate beneath the power of your hand, back to yourself, and, being reconciled, defend them from impending death. Amen. So that, while they remain devoted to you, you may remove from them the scourges of your anger and defend them from the deadly destroyer. Amen. Grant, therefore, O Lord, that just as the holy archangel Michael stands gloriously in your presence, so he may also deign to intercede there for your people, so that everywhere they may always deserve to have your grace present. [Col. 0624D] Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

**Blessing when a Votive Offering Is Presented**

[Col. 0624D] Divine mercy, fatherly goodness, immeasurable majesty, we humbly beseech you that your blessing may be upon your servants who bow their necks before you, and grant them the abundant petition of your blessing which they ask for themselves with a devout mind. Amen. Give also to your servant for whom we offer votive sacrifices to you a mind pure in your sight, perfect charity, and the purest continence; and grant him, O Lord, together with all these things, remission of sins, abundance of fruits, and fraternal charity. Amen. Add to them, O Lord, strength in their work, sincerity in their actions, and discipline in their conduct; and guard them with such fatherly mercy that they may never again attempt to commit anything harmful. Amen. May he deign to grant this, etc.

[Col. 0625A] **Blessing of New Fruit when It Is Consecrated [perhaps: “when it is consecrated”].**
To you, most merciful God, we humbly pour forth prayers: bless and sanctify your household, prostrate beneath the power of your right hand. Amen. Grant them faith, peace, and humility in abundance, so that, by the gift of your clemency, keeping what you command, they may deserve to obtain what you promise. Amen. And sanctify them by the illumination of your only Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the blessing of the Holy Spirit, so that, when the snares of the ancient enemy have been driven away and cast aside, they may healthfully take from this anniversary solemnity of the present day the first fruits of all the earth’s produce and offer them to you, and thereafter eat everything in your holy name. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

### Blessing when one goes aboard a ship

May this people of yours, O Lord, be guided by your help and protected by the arm of your Majesty; may they not be disturbed by the waves of the raging sea, nor terrified by the face of the storm. Amen. Establish for them a ship of salvation, so that their hearts may be filled with an increase of saving faith; may they hold fast the anchor of the catholic faith, so that they may pass safely through the waves of the raging world. Amen. May they conduct the commerce of a divine way of life and always fulfill the pledge of their faith; fill their hand with your gifts, so that they may have a place among the communities of the saints. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

### Blessing at the Mass of a deceased priest

O God, who are the generous rewarder of those who confess you and the merciful propitiation of the dead, hear the humble prayers of your household, and grant that your servant N., bishop, who faithfully discharged ministry in your name, may rejoice in the perpetual fellowship of your saints. Amen. And just as he succeeded to the see of blessed N. in the office of a vicar, so, through your gracious generosity, may he receive a perpetual share in the glory of that dignity. Amen. May this people also, who keep faithful watch before you on his behalf, having been drenched with the abundance of your blessing, carry away the abundant grace that they ask. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0625] In the manuscript of Gembloux, very many blessings concerning the king are found, entirely different from these.]

### Royal blessing when he is raised up as king

Look with serene eyes, almighty God, upon this glorious king N.; and just as you blessed Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so graciously irrigate and drench him with the abundant blessings of spiritual grace and with the fullness of your power, so that, from the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth, you may grant him an abundance of grain, wine, and oil, and an opulence of all crops, through the generosity of the divine gift, for long ages. Amen. While he reigns, may there be health of bodies throughout the homeland, inviolable peace in the kingdom, and glorious dignity; may the royal palace, with the greatest splendor of royal power, flash and shine before the eyes of all with the clearest radiance, as though the most splendid lightning-flashes were suffused with the greatest light. And grant him, almighty God, to be the strongest protector of the homeland and the comforter of holy churches and monasteries, with the greatest piety of royal munificence; may he also be the strongest triumphant conqueror of the kingdom’s enemies, for the crushing of rebellious and pagan nations of every kind. Amen. May he be sufficiently terrifying to his enemies through the close-at-hand strength of royal power; and to the nobles, the eminent princes, and the faithful of his kingdom may he be generous, lovable, and merciful, and may he be feared and loved by all. May kings also proceed from his loins through the successions of future ages, to rule the kingdom of the Franks; and, after the glorious and happy times of the present life, may he deserve to possess everlasting joys in perpetual blessedness. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

### Another royal blessing

May God the Father of glory be your helper, and may the Almighty bless you. Amen. May he hear your prayers in all things and fill your life with length of days. Amen. May he continually strengthen the throne of your kingdom and preserve your nation and people forever. Amen. May he clothe your enemies with confusion, and may the sanctification of Christ flourish over you. Amen. May he who has granted you earthly rule himself bestow upon you the merit of the angels in heaven. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

### Blessing for those setting out on a journey

May the most kind Guardian remain inseparably with you, and may he mercifully direct your journey according to his good pleasure. Amen. May he provide you with the archangel Raphael as guide, etc., as above.

### Blessing after supper

May the Lord send upon you the repose of holy sleep, and may he guard you as the pupil of his eye beneath the wings of his protection. Amen. Thus may you sleep in body and rest in the flesh, so that in heart and mind you may be able to keep worthy watch for God. Amen. And when the hour comes for you to rise from sleep, may you be able to gird yourselves with divine power. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

[Col. 0626B] ### Prayer for signing infants

Almighty and eternal God, who have deigned to regenerate this servant of yours—or these male and female servants of yours—from water and the Holy Spirit, and who have given him—or them—remission of all sins, send down upon him—or upon them, male and female—your sevenfold Holy Spirit, the holy Paraclete, from heaven: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and fortitude, the Spirit of knowledge and piety. Fill him—or them, male and female—with the spirit of your fear, and, being propitious, mark him—or them, male and female—with the sign of the cross of Christ unto eternal life. Through the same, etc. In the unity of the same, etc.

I sign and confirm you with the sign of the cross, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

Peace be with you.

R/. And with your spirit.

O God, who gave the Holy Spirit to your apostles and willed that through them and their successors it should be handed on to the other faithful, look upon the service of our humility, and grant that the Holy Spirit, coming upon the mind of him—or of them, male or female—whose forehead, or foreheads, we have anointed with the most holy chrism and confirmed or sealed with the sign of the cross, may graciously perfect that mind by dwelling in it as the temple of his glory. He lives and reigns in the unity of the same, etc.

### Another blessing

May almighty God, who created all things from nothing, bless you—or you all—and grant you, in baptism through the Holy Spirit, forgiveness of sins. Amen. May he who gave that same Spirit to his disciples in tongues of fire illumine your heart—or your hearts—with his radiance and continually kindle it—or them—with love of himself. Amen. Thus, cleansed by his gift from every vice, and defended by his assistance from every adversity, may you deserve—or may you all deserve—to become his temple. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

The blessing of God the Father.

### Blessing on the feast of blessed Theoderic, abbot

O God, who have gathered this people to celebrate the annual [The word *solemnitatem* (“solemnity”) is to be supplied] feast of your holy confessor Theoderic, by the aid of his merits absolve us from all sins. Amen. May they grow in such a way through the seed of virtues that they may deserve to be found steadfast in good works. Amen. Thus, by performing every good deed, may they happily be able to obtain the crown of the rewards of eternal blessedness together with the company of the saints. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

### Another blessing

O God, who at the entreaty of your servant Moses spared the sinful people, so, with your confessor Theoderic interceding—whose deeds [Possibly: *feast*] we celebrate today—absolve our sins. Amen. We ask you, look upon this household of yours with the eyes of your serenity, and drench it with abundant blessings. Amen. Direct its steps along the way of eternal salvation, so that it may follow the sacraments of the faith with sincere service. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

[Col. 0627A] ### Blessing at the ordination of a pope

May almighty God, who uses the ministry of priests among his people, grant you the gift of his propitiation and blessing. Amen. And may he who, though I possessed no merits, willed by his gratuitous goodness that I should preside over this Church, through the prayers of his saints absolve me from all bonds of sin and make me a vigorous and worthy minister at his holy altars. Amen. Thus, walking according to the examples of the holy priests who pleased him in this see and in this ministry, and, with his help, ruling the flock entrusted to them according to his will, may they deserve, together with their subjects, to receive from Christ the Lord, the Shepherd of all shepherds, the rewards promised to the saints and to be joined to the number of the elect. Amen. May he himself grant this, etc.

### Blessing to be said for a deceased person

The Lord Jesus Christ, who commanded that he should be entreated by sinners, may himself inspire what is to be asked, and in this special offering may he free his servant from the torments of hell. Amen. May he cherish him with the delight of paradise, and shape you through upright conduct. Amen. After the burial of the flesh, may he grant him places of blessedness, and to you, in the length of your pilgrimage, forgiveness of sin. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, etc.

[Col. 0627]

## BENEDICTIONAL ATTRIBUTED TO SAINT GREGORY THE GREAT BY KOLLAR, IN HIS *VINDOBONENSES ANALECTA* [Note: [Col. 0627] Consult the editor’s notice prefixed to this volume. EDITOR.] (C)*

[Col. 0627B] ### Blessing on the vigil of the Nativity of the Lord

Almighty God, who by the incarnation of his only-begotten Son drove away the darkness of the world and illumined this most holy night by his glorious Nativity, may he drive away from you the darkness of vices and illumine your hearts with the light of virtues. Amen. And may he who willed that the great joy of his most holy Nativity should be announced by angels to shepherds pour over you the most pleasing shower of his blessing, and, with that Shepherd himself, lead you to the eternal pastures of everlasting joys. Amen. And may he who through his Incarnation joined earthly things to heavenly fill you with the nectar of inward peace and good will, and make you companions of the heavenly army. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, whose kingdom and dominion remain without end for ages of ages. Amen.

The blessing of God the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, and the peace of the Lord, be always with you.

### Blessing on the day of the Nativity of the Lord

May almighty God bless you and raise your minds toward heavenly things, he who made this most holy day solemn through the Nativity of his Son. Amen. And may he who made him who is the bread of angels to be the food of the faithful animals in the manger himself cause you, in the present age, to taste the sweetness of everlasting joys, and in the future lead you to the fullness of eternal rewards. Amen. And may he who willed that his infancy should be clothed in humble rags himself clothe you with the adornments of heavenly garments. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Nativity of Saint Stephen the Martyr

May God, who crowned blessed Stephen the protomartyr both with confession of faith and with the struggle of martyrdom, surround your minds and lead you in the present age to the crown of righteousness and in the future to the crown of glory. Amen. Through his intercession may he grant you always to abound in love of God and neighbor—the love that Stephen strove to maintain even amid the assaults of those who stoned him. Amen. Thus, strengthened by his example and protected by his intercession, may you deserve to be blessed by him whom Stephen saw standing at the right hand of God. Amen. May he himself grant this, who, with the Father, etc.

### On the Nativity of Saint John the Evangelist

May almighty God deign to bless you through the intercession of blessed John the apostle and evangelist, through whom he willed to reveal to the Church the secrets of his word. Amen. May he grant us that, what John, filled with the gift of the Holy Spirit, poured into your ears, you may be able to grasp in your minds through the gift of that same Spirit. Amen. Thus, instructed by his teaching about the divinity of our Redeemer, loving what he handed down, preaching what he taught, and carrying out what he commanded, may you deserve to attain the gifts that the same Jesus Christ our Lord promised. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Nativity of the Holy Innocents

Almighty God, for whose only-begotten Son’s venerable infancy the murderous cruelty of Herod slaughtered the bands of innocent infants, may he grant you the most gracious gifts of his blessing. Amen. And may he who granted them to confess his only Son, our Lord, not by speaking but by dying, grant you that the true faith confessed by your tongue may also be confessed by upright conduct and blameless life. Amen. And may he who received them as the first fruit of his holy Church bring you, with the fruit of good works, to the joys of the eternal homeland. Amen. May he himself grant this, as above.

### Blessing on the octave of Our Lord

Almighty God, whose only-begotten Son today, so as not to abolish the law that he had come to fulfill, received bodily circumcision, may he cleanse your minds through spiritual circumcision from every incitement to vice and pour his blessing upon you. Amen. And may he who gave the law through Moses, so that through our Mediator he might give blessing, strip you of the mortification of vices and make you persevere in the newness of virtues. Amen. Thus may you live in this age in the perfection of the number six, and rest among the ranks of blessed spirits in the number seven, so that, renewed in the resurrection on the eighth day and enriched by the remission of the Jubilee, you may reach joys that will endure without end. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Theophany

O God, true light, who today willed to reveal your only-begotten Son to the nations with a star as guide, may you deign to enrich us with your blessing. Amen. Following the example of the Magi, may you offer mystical gifts to the Lord Jesus Christ, despise the ancient enemy and the contagions of vices, and be able to return to the eternal homeland by the way of virtues. Amen. May he who willed that the Holy Spirit should be shown over his only-begotten Son in the form of a dove grant you true innocence of mind; and may your minds be trained by that power to understand the mysteries of the divine law by which water was changed into wine at Cana in Galilee. Amen. May he himself deign to grant this, etc.

### Blessing on the Purification of Saint Mary

Almighty God, who today willed that his only-begotten Son, in assumed flesh, should be presented in the temple, may he cause you, supported by the gift of his blessing, to be adorned with good works. Amen. And may he who willed to make him a minister of the law in order to fulfill the law instruct your minds with the spiritual teachings of his law. Amen.
