There too are noted both the vigil and the feast of Saint Benedict, namely the thirteenth day before the Kalends of March and the twelfth.] The Chair of Saint Peter.

Antiphon: The Lord established him.

Psalm: The mercies of the Lord.

Responsory: He swore: “You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church.” Verse: “And the gates of hell will not prevail against it; and I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven.” Verse: “And whatever you bind on earth will be bound also in heaven.” Verse: “And whatever you loose on earth will be loosed also in heaven.”

Offertory: My truth.

Communion: You are Peter.

Psalm as above.

## The Annunciation of Saint Mary

Antiphon: All the rich among the people will entreat your countenance. [Col. 0655B]

Psalm: My heart has uttered.

Responsory: Grace has been poured upon your lips.

Verse: Therefore.

Offertory: Hail, Mary, full of grace.

Verse 1: How will this happen to me?

Verse 2: Therefore, the one who will be born from you.

Communion: Behold, a virgin will conceive. [Note: [Col. 0655D] In the Compendium: “Communion: You loved righteousness.” Psalm as above.]

Psalm as above.

## 666 — Sunday in Septuagesima

Antiphon: The groans of death surrounded me; the pains of hell surrounded me; and in my tribulation I called upon the Lord, and he heard my voice from his holy temple.

[Note: [Col. 0655D] For this Sunday Alcuin cites the Antiphoner, p. 41, and on p. 42 interprets this very office. [Col. 0656D] He also explains the offices that follow on the succeeding pages. Pamel.]

Psalm: I will love you, O Lord, my strength; the Lord is my firmament, my refuge.

Responsory: A helper in times of need, in tribulation; let those who know you hope in you, for you do not abandon those who seek you, O Lord.

Verse: For the poor man will not be forgotten forever; the patience of the poor will not perish for eternity. Arise, O Lord; let man not prevail.

Tract: [Note: [Col. 0656D] Amalarius, citing the Antiphoner, treats of why it is called a Tract and why Alleluia is omitted in the season of Septuagesima; there too he explains this office and, in the following chapter, those that follow. PAMEL.] From the depths I have cried to you, O Lord; Lord, hear my voice.

Verse: Let your ears be attentive to the prayer of your servant.

Verse: If you observe iniquities, O Lord, Lord, who will endure?

Verse: For with you there is forgiveness, and because of your law I have waited for you, O Lord.

Offertory: It is good to confess to the Lord and to sing praise to your name, O Most High.

Verse 1: How greatly your works have been magnified, O Lord! Your thoughts have become exceedingly deep!

Verse 2: Behold, your enemies, O Lord, will perish, and all who work iniquity will be scattered.

Verse 3: My horn will be exalted like that of the unicorn, and my old age will be in abundant mercy, because my eye has looked upon my enemies, and your ear has heard those who rise up against me and speak evil.

Communion: Let your face shine upon your servant, and save me in your mercy, O Lord; I will not be put to shame, for I have called upon you.

Psalm: In you, O Lord, I have hoped.

[Note: [Col. 0656D] In the Compendium and Theoderic: Station at Saint Paul.]

## Sunday in Sexagesima

[Col. 0656A]

Antiphon: Arise; why do you sleep, O Lord? Arise, and do not reject us forever. Why do you turn your face away? Do you forget our tribulation? Our belly has clung to the earth; arise, O Lord, help us and deliver us.

Psalm: O God, with our ears we have heard; our fathers have declared it to us.

Responsory: Let the nations know that your name is God; you alone are Most High over all the earth.

Verse: My God, make them like a wheel and like straw before the face of the wind.

Tract: You have shaken the earth, O Lord, and troubled it; heal its fractures, for it has been shaken.

Verse: So that your chosen ones may flee from the face of the bow and be delivered.

Offertory: Make my steps firm in your paths, so that my footsteps may not be moved; incline your ear and hear my words. You who save those who hope in you, O Lord, show forth your mercies.

Verse 1: Hear, O Lord, my righteousness; attend to my prayer; receive my supplication with your ears.

Verse 2: Guard me, O Lord, as the apple of the eye; protect me beneath the shadow of your wings; deliver me, O Lord, from the wicked.

Verse 3: But I shall appear in your sight with righteousness; I shall be satisfied when your glory is revealed.

Communion: I will enter the altar of God, to God who gives joy to my youth.

Psalm: Judge me, O God.

[Note: [Col. 0656D] In the manuscripts: Station at Saint Peter.]

## 667 — Sunday in Quinquagesima

Antiphon: Be for me a protecting God and a place of refuge, so that you may save me. For you are my strength and my refuge; and for the sake of your name you will guide me and nourish me.

Psalm: In you, O Lord, I have hoped; let me never be put to shame. In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me.

Responsory: You are God who alone works wonders; you have made your power known among the nations.

Verse: By your arm you delivered your people, the children of Israel and Joseph.

Tract: Sing joyfully to God, all the earth; serve the Lord in gladness.

Verse: Enter into his presence with exultation.

Verse: Know that the Lord himself is God. [Note: [Col. 0656D] The Compendium adds: “He himself made us, and not we ourselves.” And in the verse “But we,” it adds: “and the sheep of his pasture.”]

Verse: But we are his people.

Offertory: Blessed are you, O Lord; teach me your ordinances. With my lips I have proclaimed all the judgments of your mouth.

Verse 1: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. Blessed are those who search out his testimonies and seek him with their whole heart. Take away from your people reproach and contempt, for we have not forgotten your commandments, O Lord.

Verse 2: I have delighted in the way of your testimonies as in all riches.

Verse 3: Remove from me the way of iniquity, O Lord, and have mercy on me according to your law. I have chosen the way of truth; I have not forgotten your judgments or your righteousness. [Note: [Col. 0657D] These two words are absent from the Compendium manuscripts but are found in Pamel’s edition.] I have run in the way of your commandments, when you enlarged my heart. [Note: [Col. 0657D] Compendium: “When you enlarged my heart.” It also has “Take away,” etc.]

Communion: They ate and were exceedingly filled; the Lord granted them their desire, and they were not deprived of what they desired.

Psalm: Hearken, my people, to my law.

## Beginning of the fast

[Note: [Col. 0657D] Absent from the Compendium manuscript. At the blessing of the ashes. In the second Theoderic manuscript one reads: “Station at Saint Anastasia.” In the Compendium: “At Saint Sabina.” Perhaps one station was for the blessing of the ashes and the other for the Mass.] For the blessing of the ashes.

Antiphon: Hear us, O Lord, for your mercy is kind; according to the multitude of your mercies, look upon us.

[Note: [Col. 0657D] The Antiphons for the blessing of the ashes are expressly mentioned in the Roman Order, as is the Antiphon for the procession: “Beside the vestibule.” Likewise in Alcuin, p. 52; the Micrologus also cites it as Gregory’s, chapter 41. Pamel.]

Psalm: Save me, O God, for the waters have entered even to my soul.

Antiphon: Let us change our garb into ashes and sackcloth; let us fast and weep before the Lord, because our God is very merciful in forgiving our sins.

Antiphon: Beside the vestibule and the altar the priests and ministers of the Lord, the Levites, were weeping, saying: Spare, O Lord, spare your people, and do not destroy the mouths of those crying out to you, O Lord. [Note: [Col. 0657D] In the Compendium the Antiphon “Let us change” is resumed here.]

## At the Mass

Antiphon: You have mercy on all, O Lord, and you hate nothing that you have made, overlooking the sins of human beings for the sake of repentance and sparing them, because you are the Lord our God.

Psalm: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for my soul trusts in you.

Responsory: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for my soul trusts in you.

Verse: He sent from heaven and delivered me; he gave those trampling me over to reproach.

[Note: [Col. 0657D] The Micrologus notes, chapter 50, that this Tract is sung not so much according to the Roman Order as according to custom. Pamel.]

Tract: O Lord, do not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities.

Verse: O Lord, do not remember our former iniquities; may your mercies quickly precede us, for we have become exceedingly poor.

Verse: Help us, O God our Savior, and for the glory of your name, O Lord, deliver us; and be propitious toward our sins for the sake of your name.

Offertory: I will exalt you, O Lord, because you have received me, and you have not made my enemies rejoice over me. O Lord, I cried to you, and you healed me.

Verse 1: O Lord, you drew my soul up from the underworld; you saved me from those descending into the pit.

Verse 2: But I said in my abundance, “I shall never be moved.” O Lord, in your favor you established strength for my beauty. [Note: [Col. 0657D] In the Compendium, “O Lord, I cried,” etc., is repeated here.]

Communion: Whoever meditates on the law of the Lord day and night will yield his fruit in its season.

Psalm: Blessed is the man.

[Note: [Col. 0657D] Compendium and Theoderic: Station at Saint George.]

## Thursday

Antiphon: When I cried out to the Lord, he heard my voice from those approaching me, and he will humble them—he who is before the ages and remains forever. Cast your care upon the Lord, and he himself will nourish you.

Psalm: Hear, O God, my prayer, and do not despise my supplication.

Responsory: Cast your care upon the Lord, and he himself will nourish you.

Verse: When I cried out to the Lord, he heard my voice from those approaching me.

Offertory: To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; I shall not be put to shame.

Verse 1: Guide me in your truth and teach me, for you are God my Savior, and I have waited for you all day.

Verse 2: Look upon me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and poor.

Communion: You will accept the sacrifice of righteousness, offerings and whole burnt offerings; calves upon your altar. [Note: [Col. 0658D] Compendium: “Upon your altar, O Lord.”]

Psalm: L.

[Note: [Col. 0658D] In the Compendium and Theoderic, a station is appointed at Saints John and Paul.]

## Friday

Antiphon: He heard, and the Lord had mercy on me; he became my helper.

Psalm: I will exalt you, O Lord, because you have received me, and you have not made my enemies rejoice over me. [Note: [Col. 0658D] In the Compendium: “Over me, O Lord, you became a refuge for us,” etc.; earlier it has “Before the mountains were made, or the earth was formed,” etc., and “I asked for one thing.”]

Responsory: I asked one thing of the Lord; this I will seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord.

Verse: That I may see the will of the Lord and be protected by his holy temple.

Offertory: Give me life, O Lord, according to your word, so that I may know your testimonies.

Verse 1: Deal with your servant, O Lord, according to your great mercy, and do not take the word of truth from my mouth.

Verse 2: I am your servant; give me understanding, O Lord, so that I may learn your commandments, and make the offerings of my lips pleasing to you. [Note: [Col. 0658D] Compendium: “Make me pleasing to you, O Lord.”]

Communion: Serve the Lord in fear and rejoice in him with trembling; embrace instruction, lest you perish from the righteous way.

Psalm: II.

[Note: [Col. 0658D] In the Compendium and Theoderic: station at Saint Peter.]

## The first Sunday of Lent, station at the Lateran

Antiphon: He called upon me, and I will answer him; I will rescue him and glorify him; I will fill him with length of days.

Psalm: He who dwells in the help of the Most High will abide under the protection of the God of heaven.

669 Responsory: [Note: [Col. 0658D] Thus the very ancient Blandinian manuscript; but the Utrecht manuscript has: “Responsory: God has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways;” and Verse: “They will carry you in their hands, lest you perhaps strike your foot against a stone.” Alcuin, p. 47, agrees with it. Pamel. The same is also read in the Compendium and Theoderic manuscripts.] You have held my right hand; in your will you have led me, and with glory you have received me.

Verse: How good is the God of Israel to the upright in heart! But my feet were almost moved; my steps nearly slipped, because I was jealous of sinners, seeing the peace of sinners.

Tract: He who dwells in the help of the Most High will abide under the protection of the God of heaven.

Verse: He will say to the Lord, “You are my protector and my refuge; my God, I will hope in him.”

Verse: For he himself will deliver me from the snare of hunters and from the harsh word.

Verse: He will overshadow you with his shoulders, and beneath his wings you will hope.

Verse: His truth will surround you like a shield; you will not fear the terror of the night.

Verse: Nor the arrow flying by day, nor the affair moving about in darkness, nor ruin, nor the demon of noonday.

Verse: A thousand will fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not approach you.

Verse: For he has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.

Verse: They will carry you in their hands, lest you ever strike your foot against a stone.

Verse: You will walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you will trample the lion and the dragon.

Verse: Because he hoped in me, I will deliver him; I will protect him, because he knew my name. He called upon me, and I will answer him; I am with him in tribulation.

Verse: I will rescue him and glorify him.

Verse: [Note: [Col. 0659D] Compendium: “I will fill him with length of days.” The same is also read in the preceding Antiphon at the Introit, “He called upon me.”] I will fill him with length of days, and I will show him my salvation.

Offertory: The Lord will overshadow you with his shoulders, and beneath his wings you will hope. His truth will surround you like a shield.

Verse 1: He will say to the Lord, “You are my protector”; you will not fear the terror of the night or the arrow flying by day.

Verse 2: For he has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you, lest you ever strike your foot against a stone.

Verse 3: You will walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you will trample the lion and the dragon; because he hoped in me, I will deliver him. [Note: [Col. 0659D] In the Compendium, “His truth will surround you,” etc., is repeated.]

Communion: He will overshadow you with his shoulders, and beneath his wings you will hope. His truth will surround you like a shield.

Psalm as above.

[Note: [Col. 0659D] In the Compendium: “At the Chains, at Saint Peter.” In Theoderic: “Station at Saint Peter at the Chains.”]

## Monday

Antiphon: As the eyes of servants are toward the hands of their masters, so are our eyes toward the Lord our God, until he has mercy on us. Have mercy on us, O Lord; have mercy on us.

Psalm: To you I have lifted up my eyes, you who dwell in the heavens.

Responsory: Look upon us, O God our protector, and look upon your servants.

Verse: O Lord, God of hosts, hear the prayers of your servants.

Offertory: Open my eyes, and I shall consider your wonders, O Lord; teach me your righteousness. Give me understanding, so that I may learn your commandments.

Verse 1: Establish a law for me, O Lord, and I will seek the way of your ordinances, and I will exercise myself in your commandments.

Verse 2: May your mercies come upon me, for your law is my meditation, and your ordinances are my consolation.

Communion: With my voice I cried out to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain; I will not fear the thousands of people surrounding me.

Psalm: III.

## 670 — Tuesday

[Note: [Col. 0659D] In Theoderic: “Station at Saint Anastasia.” In the Compendium: “At Saint Anastasia.”]

Antiphon: O Lord, you have become our refuge from generation to generation; from age to age you are.

Psalm: Before the mountains were made, or the earth was established, from age to age you are God.

Responsory: Let my prayer be directed like incense in your sight, O Lord.

Verse: The lifting up of my hands is an evening sacrifice.

Offertory: In you I have hoped, O Lord. I said, “You are my God; my times are in your hands.”

Verse 1: Let your face shine upon your servant, and save me because of your mercy. O Lord, let me not be put to shame, for I have called upon you.

Verse 2: How great is the multitude of your sweetness, O Lord, which you have hidden for those who fear you! But you have perfected it for those who hope in you, in the sight of the children of men.

Communion: When I called upon you, you heard me, O God of my righteousness; in tribulation you enlarged me. Have mercy on me, O Lord; hear my prayer. [Note: [Col. 0659D] The Compendium omits “of my righteousness.”]

Psalm: Have mercy on me, O Lord. [Note: [Col. 0659D] Compendium: “Psalm: Sons of men.”]

[Note: [Col. 0660D] In Theoderic: “Station at Saint Mary Major.” In the Compendium: “At Saint Mary at the Crib.”]

## Wednesday

Antiphon: Remember your mercies, O Lord, and your compassion, which are from eternity; may our enemies never rule over us. Deliver us, God of Israel, from all our straits.

[Note: [Col. 0660D] The office of this day, and of the Friday and Saturday of this week, is explicitly mentioned by the Micrologus, chapter 24, as being from the Antiphoner of Saint Gregory. Pamel.]

Psalm: To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; I shall not be put to shame.

Responsory: The troubles of my heart have multiplied; deliver me from my necessities, O Lord.

Verse: See my humiliation and my labor, and forgive all my sins.

Tract: Deliver me from my necessities, O Lord. See my humiliation and my labor, and forgive all my sins.

Verse: To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; I shall not be put to shame, and let not my enemies mock me.

Verse: For all who wait for you will not be put to shame; let all who act vainly be put to shame. [Note: [Col. 0660D] Compendium: “Those who do evil.”]

Offertory: I will meditate on your commandments, which I have loved exceedingly, and I will lift up my hands toward your commandments, which I have loved.

Verse 1: My portion, O Lord, I have said, is to keep your law. With my whole heart I have entreated your face.

Verse 2: I have entreated your face. Have mercy on me according to your word, because I considered my ways and turned my feet toward your testimonies. [Note: [Col. 0660D] Compendium: “Because I considered my ways.”] [Note: [Col. 0660D] Here the Compendium resumes: “And I will lift up my hands.”]

Communion: Understand my cry; attend to the voice of my prayer, my King and my God, for to you I will pray, O Lord.

Psalm: My words.

[Note: [Col. 0661D] In the first Theoderic manuscript: “Station at Saint Lawrence outside the walls.” In the other: “At Saint Lawrence in Formosa.” The Compendium agrees.]

## Thursday

[Col. 0661A]

Antiphon: Confession and beauty are in his presence; holiness and magnificence are in his sanctuary.

Psalm: Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth.

Responsory: Guard me, O Lord, as the apple of the eye; beneath the shadow of your wings protect me.

Verse: From your face let my judgment proceed; let your eyes see equity.

Offertory: [Note: [Col. 0661D] Compendium: “The Lord sends an angel.”] The Lord will send an angel around those who fear him, and he will deliver them; taste and see that the Lord is sweet.

671 Verse 1: I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth.

Verse 2: In the Lord my soul will be praised; let the meek hear and rejoice. Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.

Verse 3: Draw near to him, and be enlightened; your faces will not be put to shame. This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him and delivered him from all his tribulations. [Note: [Col. 0661D] In the Compendium, “Taste and see,” etc., is repeated here.]

Communion: The bread that I will give is my flesh for the life of the world.

Psalm as above.

[Note: [Col. 0661D] In Theoderic and the Compendium: “Station at the Apostles,” or “At the Apostles.”]

## Friday

Antiphon: Deliver me from my necessities, O Lord; see my humiliation and my labor, and forgive all my sins.

Psalm: To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; I shall not be put to shame. [Note: [Col. 0661D] In the Compendium: “Responsory: Save your servant, my God, who hopes in you. Verse: Hear, O Lord, my prayer. Responsory: Have mercy.”]

Responsory: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak; heal me, O Lord.

Verse: All my bones are troubled, and my soul is exceedingly troubled.

Offertory: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and do not forget all his rewards; your youth will be renewed like that of the eagle.

Verse 1: He who forgives all your iniquities and redeems your life from destruction, who crowns you with mercy and compassion.

[Note: [Col. 0661D] In the Compendium: “Verse 2: His righteousness is upon the children’s children for those who keep his covenant and his commandments, to do them. The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven, and his kingdom will rule over all,” followed by “and your youth will be renewed,” etc.]

Verse 2: The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and greatly merciful.

Communion: Let all my enemies be put to shame and troubled; let them be turned back and be very quickly put to shame.

Psalm: VI.

[Note: [Col. 0662D] In the Compendium: “Psalm: O Lord, our Lord.” In the Vatican and Guss editions it simply reads “Psalm.” We have added the number from Pamel.]

[Note: [Col. 0662D] In the Compendium and Theoderic: “Station at Saint Peter.”]

## Saturday with twelve lessons

Antiphon: Let my prayer enter into your presence; incline your ear to my prayer, O Lord.

Psalm: O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I have cried out and by night before you.

[Note: [Col. 0662D] In the Compendium this title is read: “Four responsories belonging to the same day and to the blessing.” That these responsories are authentic is clear from the Micrologus.]

Responsory 1: Look upon us, O God our protector, and look upon your servants.

Verse: O Lord, God of hosts, hear the prayers of your servants.

Responsory 2: Be propitious.

Verse: Help.

Responsory 3: Let it be directed.

[Col. 0661D]

Verse: The lifting up.

Responsory 4: Save your people.

Verse: To you, O Lord, I have cried.

Hymn: Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers, and worthy of praise; or, “Blessed are you in the firmament of heaven.”

Verse: Bless the Lord, all works of the Lord; bless the Lord, heavens; bless the Lord, angels of the Lord.

Verse: Bless the Lord, waters that are above the heavens; bless the Lord, all powers of the Lord; bless the Lord, sun and moon.

Verse: Bless the Lord, stars of heaven; bless the Lord, rain and dew; bless the Lord, all spirits.

Verse: Bless the Lord, fire and heat; bless the Lord, nights and days; bless the Lord, darkness and light.

Verse: Bless the Lord, cold and heat; bless the Lord, frost and snow; bless the Lord, lightning and clouds.

Verse: Let the earth bless the Lord. Bless the Lord, mountains and hills; bless the Lord, all things growing upon the earth.

Verse: Bless the Lord, seas and rivers; bless the Lord, springs; bless the Lord, whales and all that move in the waters.

Verse: Bless the Lord, birds of heaven; bless the Lord, beasts and all cattle; bless the Lord, children of men.

Verse: Let Israel bless the Lord; bless the Lord, priests of the Lord.

Verse: Bless the Lord, spirits and souls of the righteous; bless the Lord, holy and humble in heart.

Verse: Bless the Lord, Ananias, Azariah, Mishael.

Verse: Singing a hymn.

Tract: Praise the Lord, all nations, and praise him together, all peoples.

Verse: For his mercy has been confirmed upon us, and the truth of the Lord remains forever.

Offertory: O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I have cried out and by night before you. Let my prayer enter into your presence, O Lord.

Verse 1: Incline your ear to my prayer. O Lord, you have put those who know me far from me; I have cried out to you, O Lord; all day I have stretched out my hands to you.

Verse 2: And I have cried out to you, O Lord, and in the morning my prayer will precede you. I am needy amid troubles from my youth.

Verse 3: I have become like a man without help, free among the dead; I have been handed over, and I did not go out.

Communion: O Lord, my God, in you I have hoped; deliver me from all those pursuing me and rescue me.

Psalm: The same.

Sunday is vacant.

## The second Sunday of Lent

[Note: [Col. 0662D] The office for this Sunday is not found in the Compendium, Vallicellian, and Theoderic manuscripts, though they assign the Collect and other prayers belonging to the Mass. Perhaps Mass was celebrated on this Sunday, but, because of the excessive labor of the preceding Saturday, nothing was sung.]

Antiphon: Remember your mercies, O Lord.

Psalm: To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.

Tract: From my necessities.

Verse: To you, O Lord.

Verse: For all.

Tract: Jesus said to the Canaanite woman: “It is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs to eat.”

Verse: But she said: “Yes, Lord, for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from the tables of their masters.”

Verse: Jesus said to her: “O woman, great is your faith; let it be done for you as you have asked.”

Offertory: I will meditate.

Communion: Understand my cry.

[Note: [Col. 0663D] In the Compendium and Theoderic: “Station at Saint Clement.”]

## Monday

Antiphon: Redeem me, O Lord, and have mercy on me; for my foot has stood on the straight path; in the churches I will bless the Lord.

Psalm: Judge me, O Lord, for I have entered in my innocence; and, hoping in the Lord, I shall not be weakened.

Responsory: Be my helper and deliverer, O Lord; do not delay.

Verse: Let my enemies be put to shame and reverence, who seek my soul.

Offertory: I will bless the Lord, who has given me understanding; I kept God always before me, for he is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.

Verse: Preserve me, O Lord, for I have hoped in you. I said, “You are my God”; the Lord is the portion of my inheritance.

Verse: You have made known to me the ways of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence, and delights are at your right hand forever.

Communion: O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name throughout all the earth!

Psalm: The same.

[Note: [Col. 0663D] In the cited manuscripts: “Station at Saint Balbina.”]

## Tuesday

Antiphon: My heart has said to you: “I have sought your face.” Your face, O Lord, I will seek; do not turn your face away from me.

Psalm: The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?

673 Responsory: Cast your care.

Offertory: Have mercy on me, O Lord, according to your great mercy; blot out my iniquity, O Lord.

Verse 1: For I acknowledge my iniquity, and my sin is always before me.

Verse 2: Against you alone I have sinned and done evil in your sight; have mercy on me, O Lord, so that you may be justified in your words. [Note: [Col. 0663D] Compendium: “So that you may be justified by your mercies, O Lord.”]

Communion: I will recount all your wonders; I will rejoice and exult in you; I will sing praise to your name, O Most High.

Psalm: I will confess to you, O Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0663D] In the manuscripts: “Station at Saint Cecilia.”]

## Wednesday

Antiphon: Do not abandon me, O Lord my God; do not depart from me. Attend to my help, O Lord, the strength of my salvation.

Psalm: O Lord, do not rebuke me in your fury, nor correct me in your anger.

Responsory: Save your people, O Lord, and bless your inheritance.

Verse: To you, O Lord, I have cried; my God, do not be silent toward me, and I shall become like those descending into the pit. [Note: [Col. 0663D] Compendium: “I will cry out.”]

Offertory: To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul. [Note: [Col. 0663D] In the same source two verses are added: 1. “Guide me.” 2. “Look upon me.”]

Communion: The Lord is righteous, and he has loved righteousness; his countenance has seen equity.

Psalm.

[Note: [Col. 0663D] In the manuscript: “Station at Saint Mary across the Tiber.”]

## Thursday

Antiphon: O God, attend to my help; O Lord, hasten to help me. Let those who seek my soul be put to shame and reverence.

Psalm: Let those who wish me evil be turned back and put to shame.

Responsory: Be propitious, O Lord, toward our sins, lest the nations ever say, “Where is their God?”

Verse: Help us, O God our Savior, and for the honor of your name, O Lord, deliver us.

Offertory: Moses prayed before the Lord his God and said: “Why, O Lord, are you angry with your people?” [Note: [Col. 0664D] Compendium: “Spare your angry soul.”] “Spare the anger of your spirit. Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to whom you swore that you would give a land flowing with milk and honey.” And the Lord was appeased concerning the evil which he had said he would do to his people.

Verse 1: The Lord said to Moses: “You have found favor in my sight, and I know you above all others.” And Moses, hastening, bowed toward the earth and worshiped, saying: “I know that you are merciful among thousands, taking away iniquity and sins.”

Verse 2: [Note: [Col. 0664D] In this manuscript it reads, “Moses said to Aaron.” Likewise Exodus 16:9: “Moses also said to Aaron: Say to the whole congregation.”] Moses and Aaron said to the whole assembly of the children of Israel: “Draw near before God.” The majesty of the Lord appeared in the cloud, and he heard your murmuring at the appointed time.

Communion: Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him, says the Lord.

Psalm: O God, attend to my help.

[Note: [Col. 0664D] In the manuscripts: “Station at Saint Vitalis.”]

## Friday

Antiphon: But I shall appear with righteousness in your sight; I shall be satisfied when your glory is revealed.

Psalm: Hear, O Lord, my righteousness; attend to my supplication.

Responsory: To the Lord, when I was in tribulation, I cried, and he heard me.

Verse: O Lord, deliver my soul from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue.

Offertory: Look toward my help, O Lord; let those who seek my soul to take it be put to shame and reverence.

Verse 1: Let those who plot evil against me be turned back and put to shame.

Verse 2: Waiting, I waited for the Lord; he looked upon me and heard my supplication. [Note: [Col. 0664D] In the Compendium, “Look toward my help, O Lord,” is repeated here.]

Communion: You, O Lord, will preserve us and guard us from this generation forever.

Psalm: XI.

[Note: [Col. 0664D] According to the manuscripts, the station is at Saints Marcellinus and Peter. In the Compendium “the seventh day” is read for “Saturday.”]

## Saturday

Antiphon: The law of the Lord is blameless, converting souls; the testimony of God is faithful, giving wisdom to the little ones.

Psalm: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament announces the works of his hands.

Responsory: It is good to confess to the Lord and to sing praise to your name, O Most High.

Verse: To announce your mercy in the morning and your truth throughout the night.

Offertory: Enlighten my eyes, lest I ever sleep in death, lest my enemy ever say, “I have prevailed against him.”

Verse 1: How long, O Lord, will you forget me forever? How long shall I place counsels within my soul?

Verse 2: Look upon me and hear me; I will sing to the Lord, who has bestowed good things upon me.

Communion: Son, you ought to rejoice, because your brother was dead and has come to life; he was lost [Note: [Col. 0665D] In the Compendium: “and has been found forever.”] and has been found.

Psalm as above.

[Note: [Col. 0665D] This Sunday is called the second in the Compendium, for no other reason than that the second Sunday is omitted, as is also read in the printed editions. In the manuscripts the station of this Sunday is at Saint Lawrence. Theoderic adds “outside the walls.”]

## The third Sunday of Lent
Antiphon. My eyes are always toward the Lord, for he himself will draw my feet out of the snare; look upon me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and poor. Psalm. To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; I shall not be put to shame.

Responsory. Arise, O Lord; let man not prevail; let the nations be judged in your sight. Verse. When my enemy turns back, they shall grow weak and perish before your face.

Tract. To you I have lifted up my eyes, who dwell in the heavens. [Col. 0665B] Verse. Behold, as the eyes of servants are toward the hands of their masters. Verse. And as the eyes of a maidservant are toward the hands of her mistress. Verse. So our eyes are toward the Lord our God, until he has mercy on us. Verse. Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us.

Offertory. The ordinances of the Lord are upright, gladdening hearts, and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb; for your servant also keeps them. Verse 1. The commandment of the Lord is radiant, enlightening the eyes; the fear of God is holy, enduring for ever and ever; the judgments of the Lord are true. [Note: In the Compendium, “and sweeter” is added.] Verse 2. And the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart shall be pleasing in your sight always. [Note: In the same source, “and sweeter” is added.]

Communion. The sparrow has found a house for itself, and the turtledove a nest where it may place its young. Your altars, O Lord of hosts, my King and my God. Blessed are those who dwell in your house; for ever and ever they shall praise you. [Col. 0665C] Psalm. How lovely.

[Note: In the manuscripts it is assigned: Station at Saint Mark.]

## Monday

Antiphon. In God I shall praise the word; in the Lord I shall praise the utterance; in God I have hoped: I shall not fear what man can do to me. Psalm. Have mercy on me, O God, for man has trampled me underfoot; all day long, attacking me, he has afflicted me.

Responsory. O God, I have declared my life to you; you have placed my tears in your sight. 675 Verse. Have mercy on me, O Lord, for man has trampled me underfoot; all day long, warring against me, he has afflicted me.

Offertory. Hear my prayer, O God, and do not despise my supplication; attend to me and hear me. Verse 1. [Note: The Compendium reads, “They were troubled at the voice,” etc.] I am troubled by the voice of the enemy and by the affliction of the sinner; and I was awaiting the one who would save me. Verse 2. But I cried out to God: deliver my soul, [Col. 0665D] and you will stretch out your hand in requital against them. [Note: The same manuscript reads, “And stretching out your hand in requital,” etc.]

Communion. [Note: The Compendium reads, “Who will give salvation from Zion?”] And he will give salvation to Israel from Zion. When the Lord turns back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad. [Note: In the same source: Psalm. “The fool has said.”]

Psalm. Psalm 52.

[Note: In the manuscripts: Station at Saint Potentiana.]

## Tuesday

[Col. 0666A]

Antiphon. I cried out, for you heard me, O God; incline your ear and hear my words. Guard me, O Lord, as the apple of the eye; protect me under the shadow of your wings.

Psalm. Hear, O Lord, my justice; attend to my supplication.

Responsory. Cleanse me from my secret faults, O Lord, and spare your servant from those of others. Verse. If they do not rule over me, then I shall be blameless and cleansed from the greatest fault.

Offertory. The right hand of the Lord has done valiantly. Verse 1. In tribulation I called upon the Lord. Verse 2. [Note: The Compendium reads, “I was driven and tossed about.”] I was driven.

Communion. O Lord, who shall dwell in your tabernacle, or who shall rest upon your holy mountain? He who walks without blemish and practices righteousness.

Psalm. Psalm 14.

[Note: The manuscripts: Station at Saint Sixtus.]

## Wednesday

[Col. 0666B]

Antiphon. But I have hoped in the Lord; I shall exult and rejoice in your mercy, for you have regarded my humility.

Psalm. In you, O Lord, I have hoped; let me never be confounded; in your righteousness deliver me.

Responsory. Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak; heal me, O Lord. Verse. All my bones are troubled, and my soul is greatly troubled.

Offertory. O Lord, deal mercifully with me for your name’s sake, for your mercy is sweet. Verse 1. O God, do not be silent about my praise, for the mouth of the sinner and the deceitful man has been opened against me. Verse 2. Instead of loving me, they slandered me; but I prayed. [Note: In the Compendium is added: “for your mercy is sweet.” This manuscript contains many similar repetitions, which we shall not mention further below.] Verse 3. They spoke against me with a deceitful tongue; they surrounded me with words of hatred and attacked me without cause.

Communion. You have made known to me the paths of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence, O Lord. [Col. 0666C]

Psalm. Psalm 11.

[Note: In the manuscripts the station is assigned to Saints Cosmas and Damian.]

## Thursday

Antiphon. I am the salvation of the people, says the Lord. From whatever tribulation they cry out to me, I shall hear them, and I shall be their Lord for ever.

Psalm. Attend, my people, to my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth.

Psalm. The eyes of all hope in you, O Lord, and you give them food at the proper time. Verse. You open your hand and fill every living creature with blessing.

Offertory. If I walk in the midst of tribulation, you will revive me, O Lord, and against the wrath of my enemies you will stretch out your hand; your right hand has saved me. Verse 1. On whatever day I call upon you, hear me, O Lord; [Col. 0666D] you will multiply your strength within my soul. 676 Verse 2. I shall worship toward your holy temple and confess your name, O Lord, because of your mercy and your truth.

Communion. You commanded that your commandments be kept exceedingly. Would that my ways might be directed toward keeping your statutes.

Psalm. Blessed are the undefiled.

[Note: In the manuscripts: Station at Saint Laurence. In the Theoderician manuscripts is added, “at Lucina.”]

## Friday

Antiphon. Give me, O Lord, a sign for good, so that those who hate me may see it and be confounded, because you, O Lord, have helped and comforted me.

Psalm. Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear me, for I am needy and poor.

Responsory. My heart hoped in God, and I was helped; my flesh flourished again, and of my own will I shall confess to him. Verse. To you, O Lord, I cried out; my God, do not be silent, do not depart from me.

Offertory. Attend to the voice of my prayer, my King and my God, for to you I shall pray, O Lord. Verse 1. Give heed to my words with your ears, O Lord; understand my cry and hear me. Verse 2. Direct my way in your sight [Note: The Compendium reads, “my ways”], and let all who hope in you rejoice, O Lord; those who love your name, O Lord, shall glory for ever.

Communion. Whoever drinks the water that I shall give him, says the Lord, will become in him a fountain of water springing up into eternal life. [Note: The same source adds, “says the Lord to the Samaritan woman.”]

Psalm. As above.

[Note: The manuscripts assign Saint Susanna as the station.]

## Saturday

Antiphon. Give heed to my words with your ears, O Lord; understand my cry; attend to the voice of my prayer.

Psalm. For to you I shall pray, O Lord; in the morning you will hear my voice.

Responsory. If I walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for you are with me, O Lord. Verse. Your rod and your staff themselves have comforted me.

Offertory. Direct my steps according to your word, so that no iniquity may rule over me, O Lord. Verse 1. The declaration of your words gives light [Col. 0667C] and grants understanding to the simple. Verse 2. I have known, O Lord, that your judgments are equitable; and in your truth you have humbled me, so that no iniquity may rule over me, O Lord.

Communion. Has no one condemned you, woman? No one, Lord. Neither will I condemn you; now sin no more.

Psalm. As above.

[Note: In the manuscripts it reads, “at Jerusalem.”]

## Fourth Sunday of Lent

Antiphon. Rejoice, Jerusalem, and gather together, all you who love her; rejoice with joy, you who were in sorrow, so that you may exult and be filled from the breasts of your consolations.

Psalm. I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord.

Responsory. I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord. Verse. Let peace be in your strength, [Col. 0667D] and abundance in your towers.

Tract. Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion; he shall not be moved for ever, who dwells in Jerusalem. Verse. Mountains surround it, and the Lord surrounds his people, from this time forth and for ever.

[Col. 0668A]

Offertory. Praise the Lord, for the Lord is gracious; sing praise to his name, for he is sweet; he has done all that he willed in heaven and on earth. Verse 1. You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God: for I have known that the Lord is great, and our God is above all gods. 677 Verse 2. O Lord, your name is for ever, and your memorial from generation to generation. The Lord shall judge his people, and he shall take comfort in his servants. Verse 3. You who fear the Lord, bless him. Blessed is the Lord from Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem.

Communion. Jerusalem, which is built as a city, whose parts are joined together as one; for there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, to confess your name, O Lord.

Psalm. I rejoiced.

[Note: In the same source, the station is given as “at the Four Crowned Saints.”]

## Monday

[Col. 0668B]

Antiphon. Save me, O God, by your name, and judge me by your strength. O God, hear my prayer. [Note: The Compendium has Psalm: “He himself.”]

Psalm. Behold, God. Turn the evils against my enemies, and in your truth destroy them.

Responsory. Be to me a protecting God and a place of refuge, so that you may save me. Verse. In you I have hoped, O God; O Lord, let me never be confounded.

Offertory. Sing joyfully to God, all the earth. [Note: After the Offertory, the Compendium assigns two verses: 1. “He himself made us.” 2. “Praise.”]

Communion. Cleanse me from my secret faults, O Lord, and spare your servant from those of others. [Note: In the same manuscript: Psalm. “The heavens declare.”]

Psalm. Psalm 18.

[Note: In both Theoderician manuscripts: Station at Saint Laurence in Damascum. But this is an error, and it should read “in Damasum,” as the Compendium manuscript also has, or rather “in Damaso.”]

## Tuesday

Antiphon. Hear, O God, my prayer, and do not despise my supplication; attend to me and hear me.

Psalm. [Note: The Compendium: “I was troubled in the exercise.”] I was sorrowful in my exercise [Col. 0668C] and troubled by the voice of the enemy.

Responsory. Arise, O Lord; bring help to us and deliver us for your name’s sake. Verse. O God, with our ears we have heard; our fathers declared to us the work that you performed in their days, in ancient days.

Offertory. Waiting, I waited for the Lord; he regarded me and heard my supplication, and he put a new song in my mouth, a hymn to our God. Verse 1. He set my feet upon a rock and directed my steps. Verse 2. You have done many wonders, O my God, and in your thoughts there is none like you. I have proclaimed your righteousness in the great assembly. Verse 3. O Lord God, you have known; [Note: The Compendium: “my righteousness.”] I have not hidden your righteousness in my heart; I have spoken of your truth and your salvation: you are my helper and my protector, O Lord.

Communion. We shall rejoice in your salvation, and in the name of the Lord our God we shall be magnified. [Note: In the same source: Psalm. “May he hear you.” The same appears in Theoderic.]

Psalm. Psalm 19.

[Note: The station is at the tomb, according to the Compendium manuscript, and at Saint Paul, according to two Theoderician manuscripts.]

## Wednesday

Antiphon. When I have been sanctified among you, I shall gather you from all the lands; I shall pour clean water upon you, and you shall be cleansed from all your impurities, and I shall give you a new spirit.

Psalm. I shall bless the Lord at all times; his praise shall always be in my mouth.

Responsory. [Note: Amalarius cites this Responsory, book I, chapter 8. Pamelius.] Come, children, hear me; I shall teach you the fear of the Lord. Verse. Draw near to him and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be confounded.

Responsory. Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord chose for himself as an inheritance. Verse. By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the breath of his mouth all their host. 678

Offertory. Bless the Lord our God, O nations, [Note: The Compendium: “and obey the voice of his praise.”] and obey the voice of his praise, who has appointed my soul for life and has not allowed my feet to be moved. Blessed is the Lord, who has not removed my prayer and his mercy from me. Verse 1. Sing joyfully to God, all the earth. Sing a psalm to his name; give glory to his praise. Verse 2. In the multitude of your power your enemies shall lie to you; let all the earth adore you and sing to you, O Most High. Verse 3. Come and see the works of the Lord, how terrible he is in his counsels toward the children of men. To him I cried out with my mouth, and I exulted under my tongue. Therefore God heard me and attended to the voice of my prayer.

Communion. The Lord made clay from spittle and anointed my eyes, and I went, washed, saw, and believed God.

Psalm. As above.

[Note: The manuscripts agree in assigning the station to Saint Sylvester.]

## Thursday

Antiphon. Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice; seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face always.

Psalm. Confess to the Lord and call upon his name; declare his works among the nations.

Responsory. Look upon your covenant, O Lord, and do not forget the souls of your poor for ever. Verse. Arise, O Lord, judge your cause; remember the reproach brought upon your servants.

Offertory. [Note: In the Theoderician manuscripts and the Compendium: “O Lord, look to my assistance.”] O Lord, look to help me; let those who seek my soul to take it be confounded and put to shame. Verse 1. Let those who devise evil against me turn back and be ashamed. Verse 2. Waiting, I waited for the Lord; he regarded me and heard my supplication.

Communion. I shall remember your righteousness alone, O Lord. O God, you have taught me from my youth; and until old age and grey hairs, O God, do not abandon me.

Psalm. In you, O Lord, I have hoped.

[Note: In the same manuscripts, the station is assigned to Saint Eusebius.]

## Friday

[Col. 0669D]

Antiphon. The meditation of my heart is always in your sight, O Lord, my helper and my redeemer.

Psalm. The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament announces the works of his hands.

Responsory. It is good to trust in the Lord rather than to trust in man. It is good to hope in the Lord rather than to hope in princes. Verse. To declare your mercy in the morning and your truth throughout the night.

Offertory. You will save the humble people, O Lord, and you will humble the eyes of the proud, for who is God besides you, O Lord? Verse 1. My cry entered into his ears in his sight. Verse 2. My deliverer from angry nations: from those rising up against me you will exalt me.

Communion. When the Lord saw the sisters of Lazarus weeping at the tomb, he wept before the Jews, [Note: Thus the manuscripts; but in the editions of Pamelius, the Vatican manuscript, and Gussanville, exclamabat (“he cried out”) is read instead of et clamabat (“and he cried out”).] and he cried out: Lazarus, come outside. And he came forth, his hands and feet bound; he had been dead for four days.

Psalm. Psalm 21.

[Note: As the station, both Theoderician manuscripts indicate Saint Laurence outside the walls. In the Compendium it reads: “Saturday at the body of Saint Laurence.”]

## Saturday

Antiphon. You who thirst, come to the waters, says the Lord, [Col. 0670B] and you who have no money, come; [Note: The Compendium: “eat with gladness.”] drink 679 with gladness.

Psalm. Attend, my people, to my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth.

Responsory. To you, O Lord, the poor man is abandoned; you will be the helper of the orphan. Verse. Why, O Lord, have you gone far away? Why do you despise us in times of need, in tribulation? While the wicked man grows proud, the poor man is set aflame.

Offertory. The Lord became my strength, my refuge, and my deliverer; [Note: After these words, the Compendium reads: “Verse 1. You girded me with strength for battle and subdued my enemies beneath me; and you gave me the backs of my enemies, and you destroyed those who hate me, etc. Verse 2. Let him pursue my enemies, and I shall not turn back, etc.”] I shall hope in him. Verse 1. I shall pursue my enemies and overtake them; I shall not turn back until they fail. Verse 2. And you girded me with strength for battle, and you subdued my enemies beneath me; you gave me the backs of my enemies, and you destroyed those who hate me.

Communion. The Lord rules me, and I shall lack nothing; in a pasture of grass, there he has placed me; beside restful water he has led me. [Col. 0670C] [Note: The Compendium: “Psalm. He led me.”]

Psalm. He himself.

[Note: The manuscripts unanimously assign the station to Saint Peter, where this Sunday is also called “in the Passion.”]

## Fifth Sunday of Lent

Antiphon. Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from an unholy nation; from the unjust and deceitful man deliver me, for you are my God and my strength.

Psalm. Send forth your light and your truth; they themselves have led me and brought me to your holy mountain and to your tabernacles.

Responsory. Deliver me, O Lord, from my enemies; teach me to do your will. Verse. My deliverer, O Lord, from angry nations: from those rising up against me you will exalt me; from the unjust man you will deliver me.

Tract. Often they have attacked me from my youth. Verse. Let Israel now say: Often they have attacked me from my youth. Verse. Indeed, they could not prevail against me; sinners built upon my back. Verse. They prolonged their iniquity; the just Lord shall cut off the necks of sinners.

Offertory. I shall confess to you, O Lord, with all my heart. Deal bountifully with your servant, that I may live and keep your words; revive me according to your word, O Lord. Verse 1. Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. Blessed are those who search his testimonies and seek him with their whole heart. Verse 2. I have chosen the way of truth; give me understanding, and I shall search out your law and keep it with my whole heart. Incline my heart to your testimonies and not to avarice. Revive me in your way, for your judgments are delightful. I have entreated your face with all my heart, because I have loved your law.

Communion. This is my body, which is given for you. This is the cup of the new covenant in my blood, says the Lord. Do this whenever you receive it in remembrance of me. [Note: That is, Psalm “Judge me, O God,” as is explained in Theoderic.]

Psalm. As above.

[Note: In the manuscripts: Station at Saint Chrysogonus.]

## Monday

[Col. 0671B]

Antiphon. Have mercy on me, O Lord, for man has trampled me underfoot; all day long, warring against me, he has afflicted me.

Psalm. My enemies have trampled me underfoot all day long, for many are warring against me.

Responsory. O God, hear my prayer; give heed to the words of my mouth. Verse. Save me, O God, by your name, and judge me by your strength.

Offertory. O Lord, turn and deliver my soul; save me for the sake of your mercy. Verse 1. O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor correct me in your fury. Verse 2. Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak; heal me, O Lord, for all my bones are troubled.

Communion. The Lord of hosts himself is the King of glory. [Note: In Theoderic: Psalm. “The earth is the Lord’s.”]

Psalm. He himself.

[Note: In the manuscripts: Station at Saint Cyriacus.]

## Tuesday

[Col. 0671C]

Antiphon. Wait for the Lord, act manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, and endure the Lord.

Psalm. The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?

Responsory. Distinguish my cause, O Lord; from the unjust and deceitful man deliver me. Verse. Send forth your light and your truth; they themselves have led me and brought me to your holy mountain.

Offertory. Let all who know your name hope in you, O Lord, for you do not abandon those who seek you. Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion, for he has not forgotten the prayer of the poor. Verse 1. You sit upon the throne, judging equity; you rebuked the nations, and the wicked man perished. He shall judge the people with justice, and he has become a refuge for the poor. Verse 2. The Lord shall be known as one who makes judgments, for the patience of the poor shall not perish for ever; God has heard the desire of the poor.

Communion. Redeem me, O God of Israel, from all my distresses. [Note: Thus it is read in the manuscripts, both the printed editions and those of Pamelius, the Vatican, and Gussanville; they have only “Psalm,” without designation.]

Psalm. To you, O Lord, I have lifted up.

## Wednesday

Antiphon. My deliverer from angry nations: from those rising up against me you will exalt me; from the unjust man you will deliver me, O Lord.

Psalm. I shall love you, O Lord, my strength; the Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer.

Responsory. I shall exalt you, O Lord, because you have taken me up and have not made my enemies rejoice over me. Verse. O Lord my God, I cried out to you, and you healed me. O Lord, you drew my soul up from the underworld; you saved me from those descending into the pit.

Offertory. Deliver me from my enemies, O my God, and free me, O Lord, from those rising up against me. Verse 1. [Note: This verse is not in the Compendium. It is in Theoderic, but as the second verse; and “For you have become,” etc., is the first.] For behold, they have lain in wait for my soul and the strong have rushed upon me. Verse 2. For you have become my helper and my refuge on the day of my tribulation.

Communion. I shall wash my hands among the innocent and go around your altar, O Lord, that I may hear the voice of your praise and declare all your wonders. [Col. 0672B] [Note: In the Compendium: Psalm. “Deliver me from my enemies”; in Theoderic: Psalm. “Judge me.”]

Psalm. Psalm 25.

[Note: In the Compendium and in the second Theoderician manuscript: Station at Saint Apollinaris. In the first Theoderician manuscript: Station at Saint Mary.]

## Thursday

Antiphon. All that you have done to us, O Lord, you have done in true judgment, because we have sinned against you and have not obeyed your commandments; but give glory to your name and deal with us according to the multitude of your mercy.

Psalm. Great is the Lord and exceedingly praiseworthy in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.

Responsory. Take up sacrifices and enter his courts; adore the Lord in his holy hall. Verse. The Lord shall reveal the dense places, and in his temple all shall say, “Glory.”

Offertory. Beside the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept when we remembered you, Zion. Verse 1. Upon the willows in its midst we hung our instruments, because there those who had led us captive asked us for words of songs; 681 [Note: The Compendium: “the words of songs.”] and those who had carried us away said, “Sing us a hymn from the songs of Zion.” [Note: The Compendium: “Sing us a hymn of God.”] How shall we sing the song of the Lord in a foreign land? Verse 2. If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget me; may my tongue cling to my throat if I do not remember you. Those who said: “Beside the rivers of Babylon.” Verse 3. Remember, O Lord, the sons of Edom on the day of Jerusalem. Those who said.

Communion. Remember your word to your servant, O Lord, in which you gave me hope. This has comforted me in my humility.

Psalm. Blessed are the undefiled.

[Note: In the manuscripts: Station at Saint Stephen.]

## Friday

Antiphon. Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am in tribulation; deliver and rescue me from the hands of my enemies and from those who persecute me. O Lord, let me not be confounded, [Col. 0672D] for I have called upon you.

Psalm. In you, O Lord, I have hoped; let me not be confounded for ever; in your righteousness deliver me.

Responsory. My enemies spoke peacefully to me, and in anger they were troublesome to me. Verse. You have seen, O Lord, my God; do not be silent, do not depart from me.

Offertory. Blessed are you, O Lord; teach me your statutes, and do not hand me over to proud slanderers, and I shall answer the one reproaching me with a word. Verse 1. I saw those who did not keep the covenant, and I wasted away. O Lord, when will you execute judgment upon those who persecute me? Verse 2. Those who persecute me have drawn near to iniquity; let them be confounded and put to shame, for they have unjustly committed iniquity against me.

Communion. Do not hand me over, O Lord, to the souls of those afflicting me, for unjust witnesses have risen against me, and iniquity has lied to itself. [Note: In the same source: Psalm. “The Lord is my light.”]

Psalm. Psalm 26.

[Note: In the Compendium: “Saturday is vacant when the Roman pope gives alms.” In the first Theoderician manuscript: “Saturday is vacant. The Lord Pope gives alms.” In the other: “On Saturday the station is at Saint Peter, when alms are given.” Vallicelliana agrees with the printed editions. Pamelius observes that this feria is so titled—“Saturday is vacant”—in the Antiphonary, as Amalarius testifies, book I, chapter 8. In Theoderic, although nothing is prescribed to be sung, all the prayers pertaining to the Mass are nevertheless assigned, as on the other days.]

## Saturday is vacant

[Note: Antiphon for the procession: see the Roman Ordo, pp. 46–48, and Alcuin, p. 53. In the Compendium: Station at the Lateran; in Theoderic: at Saint John in the Lateran; in the first Theoderician manuscript, before this heading you find: “Blessing of palms or branches.” This blessing is also found in part in the other Theoderician manuscript, but not in this place.]

## Palm Sunday

Antiphon. O Lord, do not make your help far from me; look to my defense. Deliver me from the mouth of the lion [Note: In the Compendium, with the printed edition of Pamelius agreeing: “and from the horns of unicorns.” The same is also read below in the Tract.] and from the horns of unicorns, my humility.

Psalm. O God, my God, look upon me; why [Col. 0673B] have you abandoned me?

Responsory. You have taken hold of my right hand; in your will you have led me, and with glory you have received me. Verse. How good is the God of Israel to the upright in heart? But my feet were almost moved; my steps were nearly poured out. For I was jealous of sinners, seeing the peace of sinners.

Tract. O God, my God, look upon me; why have you abandoned me? Verse. The words of my sins are far from my salvation. Verse. My God, I shall cry out by day, and you will not hear; and by night, and it shall not be foolishness to me. Verse. But you dwell in the holy place, the praise of Israel. In you our fathers hoped; they hoped, and you delivered them. Verse. They cried out to you and were saved; they hoped in you and were not confounded. Verse. But I am a worm and not a man, the reproach of men and the outcast of the people. [Col. 0673C] Verse. All who saw me mocked me; they spoke with their lips and shook their heads. Verse. He hoped in the Lord; let him deliver him; let him save him, because he desires him. Verse. They themselves looked and gazed upon me; they divided my garments among themselves and cast lots for my clothing. Verse. Deliver me from the mouth of the lion and from the horns of unicorns, my humility. Verse. You who fear the Lord, praise him; magnify him, all the offspring of Jacob. Verse. The coming generation shall be announced to the Lord, and the heavens shall declare his righteousness. Verse. To the people who shall be born, whom the Lord made.

Offertory. My heart expected reproach and misery; I awaited one who would grieve together with me, and there was none; I sought someone to comfort me, and found none; and they gave me gall for food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. Verse 1. Save me, O God, for the waters have entered even to my soul. Verse 2. Those who sat at the gate were exercising themselves against me, and those who drank wine sang against me. Verse 3. But I directed my prayer to you, O Lord, at the acceptable time, O God; in the multitude of your mercy.

Communion. Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will be done.

Psalm. As above.

[Note: In the manuscripts: Station at Saints Nereus and Achilleus. In the second Theoderician manuscript, however, it is assigned to Saint Praxedes.]

## Monday

Antiphon. Judge, O Lord, those who harm me; attack those who attack me. Take up arms and shield, and arise to my help, O Lord, the strength of my salvation.

Psalm. [Note: The Compendium: “Pour out the sword”; as though the expression were turned toward the sword and commanded the shedding of blood.] Pour out the sword, and bar the way against those who persecute me.

Responsory. Arise, O Lord, and attend to my judgment, my God and my Lord, to my cause. Verse. Pour out the sword, and bar the way against those who persecute me.

Offertory. Deliver me from my enemies, O Lord; to you I have fled. Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Verse. Hear me in your righteousness, and do not enter into judgment with your servant, O Lord.

At the Communion. Let those who rejoice at my misfortunes be ashamed and confounded together; let those who speak evil against me be clothed with shame and reverence. [Note: In Theoderic: Psalm. “Judge me.” In the Compendium: Psalm. “Judge, O Lord, those who harm me.”]

Psalm. Psalm 34.

[Note: The manuscripts agree in assigning the station to Saint Prisca.]

## Tuesday

Antiphon. But we must glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, in which is our salvation, life, and resurrection, through whom we have been saved and delivered.

Psalm. May God have mercy on us and bless us; may he illuminate his face upon us and have mercy on us.

Responsory. But when they troubled me, [Note: The Compendium: “I clothed myself in sackcloth.” We believe this is also read in other manuscripts, but we have only a brief account of their variant readings.] I clothed myself in sackcloth; I humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer shall return into my bosom. Verse. Judge, O Lord, those who harm me; attack those who attack me. Take up arms and shield, and arise to my help.

Offertory. Guard me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner, and from unjust men deliver me, O Lord. Verse 1. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man; from the unjust man set me free. Verse 2. Those who planned to trip up my steps hid a proud snare for me. Verse 3. I said to the Lord, “You are my God”; hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication.

Communion. Those who sat at the gate were exercising themselves against me, and those who drank wine sang against me; but I directed my prayer to you, O Lord, at the acceptable time, O God, in the multitude of your mercy. [Note: In the manuscripts: Psalm. “Save me, O God.”]

Psalm. Psalm 73.

[Note: The manuscripts: Station at Saint Mary. The Theoderician manuscript adds “the greater.”]

## Wednesday

[Col. 0675A]

Antiphon. [Note: This office is expressly mentioned in the Roman Ordo, p. 49, and the following offices on the subsequent pages. It is also mentioned by Alcuin, p. 54 and following, and by Amalarius, book I, chapter 11 and following. Pamelius.] In the name of the Lord let every knee bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth; because the Lord became obedient unto death, even death on a cross. Therefore the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

Psalm. O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.

Responsory. Do not turn your face from your servant, for I am troubled; hear me quickly. Verse. Save me, O God, for the waters have entered even to my soul; I am stuck in the mire of the deep, and there is no firm ground.

Tract. O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you. Verse. Do not turn your face from me; [Note: The Compendium: “On whatever day I am troubled, hear me quickly.” Verse: “For my days have failed.”] on whatever day I am troubled, incline your ear to me. Verse. On whatever day I call upon you, hear me quickly. Verse. For my days have vanished like smoke, and my bones have been scorched like something cooked in a frying pan. Verse. I have been struck like grass, and my heart has dried up, because I forgot to eat my bread. Verse. You will arise, O Lord, and have mercy on Zion, for the time to have mercy on her has come.

Offertory. O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you. Verse 1. Do not turn your face from me. Verse 2. For I forgot to eat my bread. Verse 3. You will arise and have mercy on Zion, for the time to have mercy on her, for the time has come.

Communion. I mingled my drink with weeping, because you lifted me up and dashed me down, and I dried up like grass; but you, O Lord, remain for ever. You will arise and have mercy on Zion, for the time to have mercy on her has come. [Note: The Compendium: Psalm. “O Lord, hear my prayer and let my cry come.” Theoderic: Psalm. “O Lord, hear.” The first Theoderician manuscript, that is, the first that begins in this way, has Psalm 101.]

Psalm. Psalm 101.

[Note: Only in the first Theoderician manuscript is it read: Station at Saint Peter.]

## Thursday, the Lord’s Supper

[Col. 0675C]

Antiphon. But we must glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, in which is our salvation, life, and resurrection; through whom we have been saved and delivered.

Psalm. Sing to the Lord.

Responsory. Christ became obedient for us unto death, even death on a cross. Verse. Therefore God also exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name.

Offertory. The right hand of the Lord has done valiantly; the right hand of the Lord has exalted me. I shall not die, but live, and I shall recount the works of the Lord. Verse 1. In my tribulation I called upon the Lord, and the Lord heard me in spaciousness. Verse 2. I was driven and overturned so that I might fall, and the Lord received me.

Communion. After the Lord Jesus had eaten with his disciples, he washed their feet and said to them: Do you know what I have done for you? I am the Lord and teacher; I have given you an example, so that you also may do likewise.

Psalm. Blessed are the undefiled.

## Friday, Good Friday

[Col. 0676A]

Antiphon. “Lord, I have heard your report, and I was afraid; I considered your works, and I trembled.”

Verse 1. “You will be made known in the midst of the two living creatures; when the years draw near, you will be recognized; when the time comes, you will be revealed.”

Verse 2. “His majesty covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.”

Verse 3. “God will come from Lebanon, and the Holy One from the shadowy and densely wooded mountain.”

Verse 4. “When my soul is troubled within me, in wrath you will remember mercy.”

[Note: The Tract was missing from the Blandiniensis Codex; the Utrecht Codex, however, contained it, though according to Roman usage it was customarily sung first: the Tract, “He who dwells,” as above on Palm Sunday. This is clear from the Roman Ordo, p. 66, and from Alcuin, p. 58, who adds that this Tract, “Deliver me,” had only recently been compiled. The same is shown by Amalarius, book I, chapter 13, and book IV, chapter 34.]

Tract. “Deliver me, Lord, from the evil man; free me from the unjust man.”

Verse. “They devised wickedness in their heart; all day long they were preparing battles.”

Verse. “They sharpened their tongues like serpents; the poison of asps is under their lips.”

Verse. “Guard me, Lord, from the hand of the sinner, and free me from unjust men.”

Verse. “Those who plotted to trip up my steps hid proud snares for me.”

Verse. “They stretched out ropes as a snare for my feet; beside the path they placed a stumbling block for me.”

Verse. “I said to the Lord: You are my God; hear, Lord, the voice of my prayer.”

Verse. “Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation, shelter my head on the day of battle.”

Verse. “Do not hand me over to the sinner’s desire; they have plotted against me. Do not abandon me, lest they ever be exalted.”

Verse. “The head of those who surround them—the toil of their lips—will cover them.”

Verse. “Yet the righteous will give thanks to your name, and the upright will dwell in your presence.”

[Note: In the Compendium, immediately after this verse follows: Antiphon, “Behold the wood of the cross, on which the salvation of the world hung. Come, let us adore.” Psalm, “Blessed are those who are undefiled,” etc.; “Blessed are those who search out,” etc., as much as is necessary—that is, for as long as the adoration of the cross continues. Afterwards follows: “Likewise, they adore his cross,” etc.; Psalm, “May God have mercy on us,” etc.; “Sing, my tongue.”]

### Antiphon for the adoration of the cross

[Note: These antiphons can also be found in the Roman Ordo, pp. 65–66. Alcuin likewise mentions them and the adoration of the cross in *On the Divine Offices*, p. 57 and following, as does Amalarius, *On the Ecclesiastical Offices*, book I, chapter 14. Pamel(ius).]

“We adore your cross, Lord, and we praise and glorify your holy resurrection; for behold, through the cross joy has come into the whole world.”

Psalm. “May God have mercy on us.”

Antiphon. “Behold the wood of the cross, on which the salvation of the world hung. Come, let us adore.”

Psalm. “Blessed are those who are undefiled in the way.”

Antiphon. [Note: This is missing from the Compendium.]

“When the Maker of the world was suffering the punishment of death on the cross, crying out with a loud voice, he gave up his spirit; and behold, the veil of the temple was torn, the tombs were opened. For a great earthquake occurred, because the world cried out that it could not bear the death of the Son of God.”

Verse. “When the soldier’s lance had opened the side of the crucified Lord, blood and water flowed out for the redemption of our salvation.”

Verse. “O wondrous price, by whose weight the captivity of the world was redeemed! The infernal gates of Tartarus were shattered; the door of the kingdom was opened to us.”

Hymn. “Sing, my tongue, the battle of the glorious struggle; and over the trophy of the cross proclaim the noble triumph: how the Redeemer of the world, sacrificed, conquered.”

Verse. “The Maker, grieving over the fraud of the first-formed parent, when he fell into death through the bite of the harmful fruit, himself marked the wood at that time, so that by the wood he might undo the damage caused by the wood.”

Verse. “The order of our salvation had demanded this work: the many-formed craft of the traitor was to be defeated by a counter-craft, and healing was to come from the very source from which the enemy had inflicted the wound.”

Verse. “When, therefore, the fullness of sacred time came, the Creator of the world, born from the Father’s citadel, was sent forth and, having become human in a virgin’s womb, appeared.”

Verse. “The infant wails, enclosed in a narrow manger; the virgin mother wraps his limbs in swaddling clothes, binding his hands and feet; a band encircles his tightly bound legs.”

Verse. “After six periods of five years had now been completed, fulfilling the appointed time of his bodily life, he was born for this purpose by his own will and, devoted to his passion, was raised upon the wood of the cross to be sacrificed as a lamb.”

Verse. “Here are vinegar, gall, reed, spittle, nails, and lance; the gentle body is pierced; blood and water flow forth—a stream by which earth, sea, stars, and the world are washed.”

Verse. “Bend your branches, lofty tree; relax your taut fibers, and let that stiffness soften which your birth gave you, so that the limbs of the heavenly King may be stretched upon the wood.”

Verse. “You alone were worthy to bear the price of the world and to prepare a haven for the shipwrecked world, which the sacred blood poured from the Lamb’s body has anointed.”

Verse. “Glory and honor to God, the Most High, forever; equal glory to the Father and the Son and the illustrious Paraclete, to whom belong praise and power throughout the everlasting ages.”

[Note: In the order recorded by us, these four canticles are cited by name by the Roman Ordo, p. 73; by Alcuin, pp. 62–63; and by Amalarius, book I, chapter 18. Pamel(ius). In the margin we have indicated the sources from which these canticles are taken, as they are read in the Compendium.]

### Canticles on Holy Saturday

1. “Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously magnified: horse and rider he has cast into the sea. He became my helper and protector for my salvation. This is my God [Note: The Compendium has ‘and I will honor him.’ Below it likewise has: ‘The Lord is his name.’], and I will honor him; the God of my father, and I will exalt him: the Lord, who crushes wars. The Lord is his name.” (Exodus)

2. “Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words from my mouth. Let my discourse be awaited like rain, and let my words descend like dew, like snow upon grass, like showers upon herbage. For I have invoked the name of the Lord: give greatness to our God. God’s works are true, and all his ways are judgments. God is faithful, and there is no iniquity in him; the Lord is just and holy.” (Deuteronomy)

3. “A vineyard was made for the beloved on a fertile hill [Note: The Compendium has: ‘and I surrounded it with a hedge.’], and I surrounded it with a hedge and dug around it; I planted a vine of Soreth, and built a tower in its midst, and dug a winepress in it. For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel.” (Isaiah)

4. “As the deer longs for springs of water, so my soul longs for you, O God. My soul thirsted for the living God; when shall I come and appear before the face of my God? My tears have been my bread by day and by night, while it is said to me [Note: The Compendium omits ‘every day’]: ‘Where is your God?’” (Psalm 41)

### Mass on Holy Saturday

Glory to God in the highest.

[Note: In Pamel(ius)’s edition and the others, the Alleluia is absent; we have restored it from the manuscripts.]

Alleluia. “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.”

Tract. “Praise the Lord, all nations, and praise him together, all peoples, for his mercy has been confirmed over us, and the truth of the Lord remains forever.”

Neither the Office nor the Agnus Dei nor the Communion is sung; but, when everything has been completed, it is said: “Go, the Mass is ended.”

[Note: In the Compendium and the earlier Theoderic: “Station at Saint Mary.” In the other Theoderic: “Station at Saint John.”]

### Easter Sunday at Saint Mary’s

Antiphon. “I have risen, and I am still with you, alleluia; you have laid your hand upon me, alleluia; your knowledge has become wondrous, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Lord, you have examined me and known me; you have known my sitting down and my rising.”

Response. “This is the day that the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.”

Verse. “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.”

Verse 1. “Let Israel now say: He is good, for his mercy endures forever.”

Verse 2. “Let the house of Aaron now say: His mercy endures forever.”

Verse 3. “Let those who fear the Lord now say: His mercy endures forever.”

Verse 4. “The right hand of the Lord has done valiantly; the right hand of the Lord has exalted me.”

Verse 5. “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this was done by the Lord, and it is wondrous in our eyes.”

Verse 6. “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. The Lord is God, and he has shone upon us.”

Alleluia. “Christ our Passover has been sacrificed.”

Verse. “Let us feast on the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.”

Offertory. “The earth trembled and was still when God arose for judgment, alleluia.”

Verse 1. “God is known in Judea; his name is great in Israel, alleluia.”

Verse 2. “His place came to be in peace, and his dwelling in Zion, alleluia.”

Verse 3. [Note: So read Pamel(ius)’s edition, the Vatican edition, Gussanville’s edition, and others. In our manuscripts, however, it reads: ‘There he broke the horns, the bow, the shield, and the sword, illuminating …’ The Compendium has: ‘Breaking the horn, bow, shield, and sword, and illuminating …’] “Therefore he broke the powers, the bow, the shield, the sword, and the battle, illuminating them wondrously from the everlasting mountains, alleluia.”

Communion. “Christ our Passover has been sacrificed; therefore let us feast on the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, alleluia.”

[Note: That is, “Lord, you have examined me,” as indicated in the Compendium. It adds there: “For you have also understood all my ways.” This verse is to be inserted here.]

Psalm. As above. “Purge out.”

[Note: The two Theoderic manuscripts: “Station at Saint Peter.”]

### Monday

Antiphon. “The Lord brought you into a land flowing with milk and honey, alleluia, and so that the law of the Lord might always be in your mouth, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.”

Response. “This is the day.”

Verse. “Let Israel now say.”

Alleluia. “The Lord has reigned; he has clothed himself with beauty.”

Offertory. “The angel of the Lord descended from heaven and said to the women: ‘He whom you seek has risen, as he said,’ alleluia.”

Verse 1. “Go to Galilee and tell his disciples: ‘Behold, he will go before you into Galilee; there you will see him, as he said,’ alleluia.”

Verse 2. “Jesus stood in their midst and said: ‘Peace be with you; see that it is I myself,’ alleluia.”

At the Communion. “The Lord has risen and appeared to Peter, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

[Note: In all the manuscripts: “Station at Saint Paul.”]

### Tuesday

Antiphon. “The water of wisdom gave them to drink, alleluia; it will be established in them and will not bend, alleluia; and he will exalt them forever, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good.”

Response. “This is the day.”

Verse. “Let the house of Aaron now say.”

[Note: So in all printed editions. In the Compendium: “Alleluia. The Lord has sent redemption to his people.” In Theoderic nothing is assigned.]

Alleluia. “Whichever you wish.”

Offertory. “The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice, and springs of water appeared, alleluia.”

Verse 1. “I will love you, Lord, my strength; the Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer.”

Verse 2. “My deliverer from angry nations; you will exalt me above those rising against me; you will rescue me from the unjust man.”
