At the Communion. “If you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, alleluia, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God; set your minds on the things that are above, alleluia, alleluia.”

[Note: In the Compendium: Psalm, “Sing to the Lord,” verse 1.]

Psalm. As above.

### Wednesday

[Note: In all the manuscripts: “Station at Saint Lawrence.”]

Antiphon. “Come, you blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom, alleluia, which has been prepared for you from the foundation of the world, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth.”

Response. “This is the day.”

Verse. “Let those who fear the Lord say.”

[Note: Theoderic: “Alleluia. Come, you blessed.” Compendium: “Alleluia. The Lord has reigned; let the earth rejoice; let the many islands be glad,” repeated three times.]

Alleluia. “Whichever you wish.”

Offertory. “The Lord opened the gates of heaven and rained manna upon them for food; he gave them the bread of heaven; man ate the bread of angels, alleluia.”

Verse 1. “Attend, my people, to my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth.”

Verse 2. “I will open my mouth in parables; I will speak propositions from the beginning of the world.”

At the Communion. “Christ, rising from the dead, dies no more, alleluia; death will no longer rule over him, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

[Note: The manuscripts: “Station at the Apostles.”]

### Thursday

Antiphon. “Your victorious hand, Lord, they praised together, alleluia, because wisdom opened the mouth of the mute and made the tongues of infants eloquent, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. [Note: Theoderic: Psalm, “The Lord has reigned,” number 2, that is, the second. Compendium: Psalm, “Give thanks.”] “The Lord has reigned; let the earth rejoice; let the many islands be glad.”

Response. “This is the day.”

Verse. [Note: So in Pamel(ius)’s edition and the others, but in the manuscripts the verse is: “The stone that the builders rejected,” etc. Pamel(ius) says that in the Utrecht Codex verse 5 reads: “Blessed is he who comes,” and rightly so, on the authority of the *Micrologus*, chapter 54.] “The right hand of the Lord has done valiantly.”

Alleluia. [Note: In the Compendium: “Alleluia. For God is the great Lord and the great King above all gods,” repeated three times. In Theoderic: “Alleluia. On the day of the Resurrection.”]

“Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.”

Offertory. “On the day of your solemnity, says the Lord, I will bring you into a land flowing with honey and milk, alleluia.”

Verse 1. “Hear, my people, and I will speak: Israel, if you will hear me, I will give you the desires of your hearts.”

Verse 2. [Note: The editions have: “You shall not adore.” We have emended the text from the manuscripts, with many other witnesses supporting it.] “You shall not worship a foreign god, for I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.”

At the Communion. “You are a people of possession; proclaim his mighty deeds, alleluia, who called you out of darkness into his wondrous light, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

### Friday at Saint Mary’s

[Note: So read the manuscripts. Theoderic adds: “At the martyrs.”]

Antiphon. “The Lord brought them out in hope, alleluia, and the sea covered their enemies, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Attend, people.”

Response. “This is the day.”

Verse. [Note: In all the manuscripts: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. The Lord is God, and he has shone upon us.” Pamel(ius).] “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.”

[Note: In the Compendium: “Alleluia. Praise, Jerusalem, the Lord; praise your God, Zion.” In Theoderic: “Alleluia. The angel of the Lord.”]

Alleluia. “Whichever you wish.”

Offertory. “This day shall be a day of remembrance for you, alleluia; and you shall celebrate it as a solemn feast to the Lord throughout your generations, a perpetual ordinance, alleluia.”

Verse 1. “Keep in mind this day on which you came out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery; for by a mighty hand the Lord delivered you.”

Verse 2. “Moses said to the people: ‘Be of good courage, and salvation will come to you from the Lord God, and he will fight for you.’”

At the Communion. “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth, alleluia; go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

[Note: In the manuscripts: “Station at Saint John.”]

### Saturday

Antiphon. “The Lord brought out his people with rejoicing, alleluia, and his chosen ones with gladness, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name.”

Response. [Note: In Theoderic there are two Alleluias: the first, “This is the day”; the second, “The Lord brought out.”] “This is the day.”

Verse 1. “Praise the Lord, servants; praise the name of the Lord. May the name of the Lord be blessed, from this time forth and forever.”

Offertory. “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; we have blessed you from the house of the Lord. The Lord is God, and he has shone upon us, alleluia, alleluia.”

Verse 1. [Note: In the Compendium the first verse is “This is the day”; the second, “The stone.”] “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this was done by the Lord, and it is wondrous in our eyes.”

Verse 2. “This is the day that the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.”

At the Communion. “All who have been baptized in Christ have put on Christ, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

[Note: In the second Theoderic this is called “the Lord after the White Days,” and the station is assigned at Saints Cosmas and Damian.]

### Sunday of the Octave of Easter

Antiphon. “Like newborn infants, alleluia, long for rational, guileless milk, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Rejoice in God our helper; shout for joy to the God of Jacob.”

At the Response. “And he fed them.”

[Note: In the manuscripts the first Alleluia is “This is the day”; the second, “Christ our Passover.”]

Alleluia. “Whichever you wish.”

Offertory. “The angel of the Lord.”

At the Communion. “Put out your hand and examine the places of the nails, alleluia; and do not be unbelieving but faithful, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

### First Sunday after the Octave of Easter

Antiphon. “The earth is full of the mercy of the Lord, alleluia; by the word of God the heavens were made, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.”

[Note: In the Compendium: “Alleluia. The Most High has risen from the tomb, he who hung for us upon the wood.” Likewise: “Alleluia. The Lord has reigned; he has clothed himself with beauty.”]

Second Alleluia. “Whichever you wish.”

Offertory. “O God, my God, to you I keep vigil from the dawn, and in your name I will lift up my hands, alleluia.”

Verse 1. “My soul thirsted for you; how greatly my flesh also longed for you, that I might see your power and your glory.”

Verse 2. “In the morning I will meditate on you, for you have become my helper, and in the shelter of your wings I will rejoice.”

At the Communion. “I am the good shepherd, alleluia, and I know my sheep, and mine know me, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

### Second Sunday after the Octave of Easter

Antiphon. “Shout joyfully to God, all the earth, alleluia; sing a psalm to his name, alleluia; give glory to his praise, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Say to God: How fearsome are your works, Lord; because of the greatness of your power your enemies will pretend submission to you.”

“Shout joyfully.” [Note: In the same source: “Alleluia. Praise the Lord, servants,” as above.]

Alleluia. “Whichever you wish.”

Offertory. “Praise the Lord, my soul; I will praise the Lord in my life; I will sing to my God as long as I exist, alleluia.”

Verse 1. “He keeps the truth forever; he executes judgment for those who suffer wrong; he gives food to the hungry.”

Verse 2. “The Lord raises up those who are bowed down; the Lord releases those in chains. The Lord guards the resident alien and the orphan; he will receive the widow, and he will destroy the ways of sinners. The Lord will reign forever: your God, Zion, for ever and ever.”

At the Communion. “A little while, and you will not see me, alleluia; again a little while, and you will see me, because I am going to the Father, alleluia, alleluia.”

### Third Sunday after the Octave of Easter

Antiphon. “Sing to the Lord a new song, alleluia, for the Lord has done wondrous things, alleluia; before the nations he has revealed his righteousness, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “His right hand will save for him, and his holy arm.”

[Note: In the Compendium: “Alleluia. Come, blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom with joy.” “Second Alleluia. For God is great.”]

Alleluia. “My heart is ready.”

Alleluia. “I will give thanks to you, Lord; whichever you wish.”

Offertory. “Shout joyfully to God, all the earth.”

Verse 1. “I will pay my vows to you.”

Verse 2. “My mouth has spoken.”

At the Communion. “When the Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

### Fourth Sunday after the Octave of Easter

Antiphon. “Announce the voice of joy, and let it be heard, alleluia; announce it to the ends of the earth: the Lord has delivered his people, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Shout joyfully to God, all the earth; sing, rejoice, and sing psalms.”

[Note: In the Compendium: “First Alleluia. Redemption.” “Second Alleluia. He heals the brokenhearted.”]

Alleluia 1. “For the Lord is a great God and a great King.”

Alleluia 2. “Whichever you wish.”

Offertory. “Bless the Lord, peoples, our God.”

Verse 1. “Shout joyfully to God, all the earth.”

Verse 2. “Because of the greatness of your power.”

Verse 3. “Come and see the works of the Lord.”

Communion. “Sing to the Lord, alleluia; sing to the Lord; bless his name; announce his salvation from day to day, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “He himself.”

### Feast of the holy martyrs Tiburtius and Valerian

Antiphon. “Your holy ones, Lord, will bless you; they will speak of the glory of your kingdom, alleluia.”

Psalm. “I will exalt you, my God and King, and I will bless your name forever and ever.”

[Note: In the Compendium a double Alleluia is assigned: the first, “Your holy ones, Lord”; the second, “Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.” In Theoderic there is one only: “Your holy ones.”]

Offertory. “Rejoice in the Lord and exult, you righteous, and glory, all you upright of heart.”

Verse. “For this every holy one prayed to you at the appropriate time.”

Communion. “Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord; praise is fitting for the upright, alleluia.”

Psalm. “He himself.”

### Feast of Saint George

Antiphon. “You have protected me, God, from the assembly of the wicked, alleluia; from the multitude of those who practice iniquity, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm. “Hear, God, my prayer when I plead; deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.”

[Note: In Theoderic, the Alleluia “Blessed is the man” is assigned before the Offertory.]

Offertory. “The heavens will proclaim your wonders, Lord, and your truth in the assembly of the saints, alleluia, alleluia.”

Verse 1. “I will sing your mercies, Lord, forever; from generation to generation I will proclaim your truth with my mouth, alleluia.”

Verse 2. “For who among the clouds is equal to the Lord? Or who will be like God among the sons of God? God is glorified in the council of the saints, alleluia.”

Communion. “The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and hope in him; and all the upright of heart will be praised, alleluia.”

Psalm. As above.

### In the greater litany: Collect at Saint Lawrence in Lucina

### Antiphons for the procession

[Note: All of this is absent from the Compendium manuscript up to the feast of Saint Vitalis. Some of these antiphons, however, are found elsewhere at the end, such as “Remnants go out from Jerusalem,” “Walk, holy ones,” and similar items. In that same manuscript Saint Mark is not mentioned at all. The situation is different in Theoderic.]

“Rise, Lord; help us and deliver us for the sake of your name, alleluia; save your people.”

“Rise, holy ones, from your dwelling places; sanctify these places, bless the people, and guard us, humble sinners, in peace, alleluia.”

“With joy you will go out, and with gladness you will be led forth; for even the mountains and hills will go out, awaiting you with joy, alleluia.”

“Remnants go out from Jerusalem, and salvation from Mount Zion; therefore this city will have protection, and it will be saved for the sake of David, his servant, alleluia.”

“Walk, holy ones, along the way you have chosen; hasten to the place prepared for you. We sing on earth; we proclaim the praises of the saints; we carry the saints, while the angels rejoice in heaven, alleluia.”

“In the name of the Lord our God we will walk, we and all the peoples; for the law has been made in Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. The Lord will reign forever, alleluia.”

“I am the God of your fathers, says the Lord. I have surely seen the affliction of my people, and I have heard its groaning, and I have come down to deliver them, alleluia.”

“People of Zion, turn back to the Lord our God and say to him: ‘You are powerful, Lord, to forgive our sins, so that our iniquities may not overtake us, our God,’ alleluia.”

“Lord our God, who performed great wonders with our fathers and glorify yourself in our times, who sent your hand from on high and delivered us, alleluia.”

“Give thanks to the Lord, children of Israel, for there is no other God besides him. He himself will deliver us through his mercy. Look at what he has done with us, and let us recount all his wonders, alleluia.”

“Let us cry out to the Lord, saying: ‘We have sinned against you, Lord; have patience with us, and rescue us from the evils that daily increase upon us,’ alleluia.”

“Spare, Lord, spare your people, whom you redeemed, Christ, with your blood, so that you will not be angry with us forever, alleluia, alleluia.”

“Lord, today we have been diminished because of our sins; but in a contrite heart and humble spirit may we be received, and deal with us according to your gentleness, because there is no shame for those who trust in you, alleluia, alleluia.”

“Our iniquities, Lord, have multiplied over our heads; our offenses have grown up to the heavens. Spare us, Lord, and incline your mercy over us.”

“Fear and trembling in the city of Nineveh, the great city, through which fasting was imposed upon the sinful people, and the turbulent crowd was clothed in sackcloth. It also happened that the noble king descended from his throne, so that he might be humbler than all who mourned; and he commanded throughout the whole kingdom: ‘Let no man or woman taste anything; let oxen and cattle not feed on the grasses of the earth; let children and calves not suck their mothers’ breasts; but let them cry out to God with all their strength for three days, lest we perish like Sodom.’ But you, almighty God, merciful and compassionate, had mercy on the wretched. We are your works, whom you gave to your Son as his inheritance. Do not close your ear to our prayers; instead, mercifully lift up our affliction, recalling what you promised us when you said: ‘Turn back to me, and I will return to you,’ alleluia.”

“Let us pray, most beloved, to God the almighty Father, that he may cleanse the whole world from all errors, remove diseases, drive away famine, open the prison, break chains, grant travelers a return, the sick health, and those at sea a safe harbor; that he may grant peace in our days, repel our rising enemies, and deliver us from the hand of hell for the sake of your name, alleluia, alleluia.”

“Turn back to God, all of you together, with pure heart and mind, in prayers, fasts, and many vigils. Pour out your prayers with tears, so that the written charges of your sins may be erased before sudden destruction comes upon us, before the depths of death swallow us, so that when our Creator comes, he may find us prepared, alleluia.”

“Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors; and do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil, from every evil. Amen, alleluia.”

“We acknowledge, Lord, that we have sinned; we ask for forgiveness, which we do not deserve. Stretch out your hand to those who have fallen—you who opened the gate of paradise to the confessing thief, alleluia.”

“Be gracious, Lord, toward our sins for the sake of your name, lest the nations ever say: ‘Where is their God?’”

“Upon your people, we beseech you, Lord, may abundant blessing descend; may forgiveness come; may consolation be granted; may holy faith increase; may eternal redemption be established, alleluia.”

“Savior of the world, save us all. Holy Mother of God, ever-virgin Mary, pray for us. Through the prayers also of all the apostles, martyrs, and confessors, and of the holy virgins, we humbly ask that we may be delivered from every evil and deserve now and always to enjoy every good, alleluia.”

“Deliver, Lord, your people from the hand of death, and may your right hand protect this assembly, so that, living, we may bless you, Lord our God.”

“Lord God, almighty King, deliver us for the sake of your name, and grant us a place for repentance.”

“Lord, there is no other God besides you; and since you care for all things, and you are Lord of all, spare your people, for you grant generosity to sinners so that they may turn from wickedness to goodness.”

“Have mercy, Lord, on your people, over whom your name has been invoked, so that all who dwell on earth may know that you are the God of your peoples.”

“Forgive, Lord, the sins of your people according to the abundance of your mercy. As you were gracious to our fathers, be gracious also to us.”

“Most mercifully hear your people, Lord. May God have mercy. The whole earth will be filled with glory.”

“Almighty God, consolation of the sorrowful and strength of those who labor, may the prayers of those crying out to you from every tribulation reach you, so that all may rejoice that your mercy has been present to them in their needs, alleluia.”

“We beseech you, Lord, in all your mercy, that your fury and your wrath may be taken away from this city of yours and from your holy house, for we have sinned, alleluia.”

“Savior of the world, save us, your suppliants; defend the people redeemed by your blood. Deliver us, Christ, from dangers, granting us eternal life.”

“Christ, who reigns in heaven and sits at the right hand of the Father and dwells among angels and archangels, thrones and dominations, your apostles praise you, and the martyrs sing a hymn to you. The confessors join their voices in paradise and say: ‘O blessed are all who proclaim glory to God and dwell with him in peace, for all who labored for God on earth you lead to the heavenly kingdoms.’ But we ought to praise and bless you, because you have deigned to call us from earth to heaven, alleluia.”

“Lord King, God of Abraham, give us rain upon the face of the earth, so that this people may learn that you are the Lord our God. Is there among the idols of the nations one that gives rain, except you, God? The heavens cannot give rain unless you will it. You are the Lord our God, whom we awaited; give us rain.”

“The holy ones will go from strength to strength; the God of gods will be seen in Zion, alleluia.”

Beside the vestibule. “Let us be changed.”

“We have sinned, Lord; we have sinned against you. Spare our sins and save us. You who guided Noah over the waves of the flood, hear us. You who recalled Jonah from the abyss, deliver us. You who stretched out your hand to Peter as he sank, help us, Christ, Son of God.”

“Hear us, Lord, who heard Jonah from the belly of the whale. Hear us as we cry out—you who heard David prostrate and lying in sackcloth—as we cry out and say: ‘Spare, spare, defend your creature, our God,’ alleluia.”

“Walk, saints of God, to the appointed place prepared for you from the foundation of the world. Walk, saints of God; enter the city of the Lord. For a new church has been built for you, where the people are to adore the Majesty of the Lord.”

“Peter was walking upon the waves of the sea. A strong wind arose, and the water was troubled. In fear he cried out: ‘Command me to come to you.’ Jesus said to him: ‘Come, you of little faith; why did you doubt?’”

“Jerusalem, the holy city, is pleasing, adorned with the ornament of the martyrs, whose streets resound with praises from day to day.”

“You are the Lord Savior, who healed with a single word the paralytic lying for a long time. Command, therefore, Lord, that we be delivered from the evil time. We have sinned against you; now we beseech you, most merciful Father, grant us forgiveness, alleluia.”

“When the Son of Man comes on the throne of his majesty and begins to judge the world by fire, then the whole choir of angels will stand before him, and all nations will be gathered before him. Then he will say to those who are on his right: ‘Come, blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.’ And the impious will go into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life, and they will reign with God forever.”

“Announce his glory among the nations, alleluia; for the Lord is great, alleluia; they will rejoice.”

“Our God is glorious among the saints. Who is like you? Your sanctuary, O Lord, which your hands prepared—O Lord, who reigns for ever and ever, and all things that are in them—alleluia.”

“As a shepherd carried the lost sheep, so I carried and embraced you, says the Lord. I made you; I will carry you. I created you; I redeemed you; I will restore you. I sustained you; I will forgive your sins. Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of hosts, who through the Holy Spirit descended into the Virgin’s womb and was born as the Son of God, the Redeemer of Israel.”

“Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance; shepherd them and lift them up forever, alleluia.”

“Almighty God, we humbly ask and beseech you that the intercession of the archangels—Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael—may be made for us before the Lord, so that we may worthily offer sacrifices to the Lord at the altar and appear before the Savior through the intercession of the nine orders of angels. May thrones, dominations, principalities, and powers, and cherubim and seraphim also intercede for us, who never cease to cry out: ‘Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of hosts,’ who reign without end. Deign to hear your servants today, alleluia.”

“May the triple Majesty of the Lord bless us; may the Holy Spirit bless us, who in the form of a dove rested upon Christ in the river Jordan. May he bless us who deigned to descend from heaven to earth and redeemed us with his holy blood. May the Lord bless our priesthood and our entrance, alleluia.”

[Note: In Pamel(ius)’s edition, after this blessing follows the Mass, “He heard,” etc., as at the feast of Saint Mark and during the Rogation days. After that Mass, in that edition, follows the vigil of the Ascension. The feasts, or natal days, of Saint Vitalis and of the holy apostles Philip and James, etc., had preceded.]

### Feast of Saint Vitalis
Antiphon: You have protected me, O God. Psalm: Hear me. [Note: [Col. 0686D] The two Alleluias that follow are not in the Compendium. In Theoderic there is one only, namely “Blessed is the man.”] Alleluia: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in his commandments. Alleluia: The righteous man will not be disturbed, because the Lord strengthens his hand. Offertory: We have been filled in the morning with your mercy, and we rejoice and are glad, alleluia. Verse 1: Lord, you have been our refuge from generation to generation. Verse 2: Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world were formed, from age to age you are God, alleluia. Communion: I am the true vine, and you are the branches; whoever remains in me, and I in him, bears much fruit, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: Hear, O God, my prayer.

## The Nativity of the holy apostles Philip and James

Antiphon: They cried out to you, O Lord, in the time of their affliction, and you heard them from heaven, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: Rejoice in the Lord, O you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright. [Col. 0687A] [Note: [Col. 0687D] These two Alleluias are likewise absent from the Compendium. In Theoderic a single Alleluia is read: “They will confess.”] Alleluia: They will confess. Alleluia: They have been greatly honored. Offertory: The heavens will confess your wonders, O Lord, and your truth in the assembly of the saints. Verse 1: Your mercies, O Lord. Verse 2: For who among the clouds? Communion: For so long I have been with you, and you have not known me? Philip, whoever sees me sees the Father, alleluia. Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: As above.

[Note: [Col. 0687D] In the manuscripts the office of the saints Alexander, Eventius, and Theodulus is placed first; afterward one reads: “On the same day, the Finding of the holy Cross.” There is no mention of Saint Juvenal.]

## The Finding of the holy Cross

Antiphon: [Note: [Col. 0687D] Compendium: “But we ought to glory.”] But we ought to glory. Psalm: The Lord has reigned; he has clothed himself with beauty; the Lord has clothed himself with strength and girded himself with power. Alleluia: [Note: [Col. 0687D] Before the Alleluia, the Compendium reads: “Response: Christ became obedient for us,” etc. Verse: “Therefore God also,” etc. Afterward: “Alleluia: The Lord reigns from the wood.”] Tell it among the nations: the Lord has reigned from the wood. Offertory: The right hand of the Lord has shown strength; the right hand of the Lord has exalted me; I shall not die, but live, and shall declare the works of the Lord. [Col. 0687B] [Note: [Col. 0687D] Two verses are appended there after the Offertory.] Communion: But we ought to glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

## On the same day: the Nativity of the holy Juvenal, Alexander, and Eventius

Antiphon: The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them, and delivered them from all their tribulations. Psalm: I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth. Response: Glorious is God in his saints, wondrous in his majesty, performing miracles. Verse: Your right hand, O Lord, has been glorified in strength; your right hand has crushed the enemy. [Note: [Col. 0687D] Theoderic, after the Response and Verse, has: “Alleluia: Your saints.”] Offertory: We have been filled in the morning with your mercy. Verse 1: Lord, our refuge. Verse 2: Before the mountains were made. Communion: [Note: [Col. 0687D] In Theoderic the Communion is “But the souls of the righteous.”] The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of wickedness will not touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died, but they are in peace. Psalm: Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord.

## The Nativity of the holy Gordian and Epimachus

Antiphon: Your saints, O Lord, will bless you. Psalm: I will exalt you, my God and King, and I will bless your name forever and ever. Response: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God. Verse: They seemed to have died in the eyes of the foolish. [Note: [Col. 0688D] This Alleluia is absent from the Compendium. It is read in Theoderic.] Alleluia: The saints will rejoice in glory; they will exult in their resting places. Offertory: Wondrous is God in his saints; the God of Israel himself will give strength and power to his people. Blessed be God. Verse 1: Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered, and let those who hate him flee from his presence. Verse 2: Let sinners perish from the face of God; but let the righteous feast, exulting in the presence of God and delighting in gladness. Communion: The souls of the righteous. Psalm: As above.

## The Nativity of the holy Nereus, Achilleus, and Pancratius

[Col. 0688A]

Antiphon: Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him, who hope in his mercy, alleluia, that he may deliver their souls from death, for he is our helper and protector, alleluia, alleluia. [Note: [Col. 0688D] In the Compendium: “Psalm: I will bless the Lord.”] Psalm: Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord. Response: The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them, and delivered them from all their tribulations. Verse: The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit. [Note: [Col. 0688D] There: “Alleluia: The righteous will shine, and like sparks they will run through the stubble forever.”] Alleluia: Your saints, O Lord, will bless you; they will speak of the glory of your kingdom. Offertory: The heavens will confess. Verse 1: Your mercies, O Lord. Verse 2: For who among the clouds? Communion: Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord. Verse: Let your mercy be upon us, O Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0688D] In the manuscripts “for the martyrs” is added. On this feast, see note 372 to the Sacramentary.]

## The Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary

[Col. 0688B] Antiphon: This place is awesome; this is the house of God and the gate of heaven, and it will be called the hall of God, alleluia. [Note: [Col. 0688D] In Theoderic: “Its foundations are in the holy mountains.”] Psalm: The Lord has reigned; he has clothed himself with beauty. Response: This place was made by God; it is an immeasurable sacrament; it is irreproachable. Verse: O God, before whom the choir of angels stands, hear the prayers of your servants. 695 Alleluia: I will adore toward your temple.

Offertory: O Lord God, in the simplicity of my heart I have gladly offered everything, and I have seen your people, who have been found here, with great joy. O God of Israel, preserve this intention. O Lord God. Verse 1: The majesty of the Lord built the temple, and all the children of Israel saw the glory. [Note: [Col. 0688D] The Compendium adds: “The glory of the Lord descending upon the house; and they adored and praised the Lord, saying: ‘God of Israel,’” etc.] Verse 2: Solomon held a solemn celebration at that time. [Note: [Col. 0688D] The Compendium continues: “And he prospered; and the Lord God of Israel appeared to him.”] Communion: My house will be called a house of prayer, says the Lord; in it everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened. Psalm: As above.

## The Nativity of Saint Potentiana

Antiphon: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness. Psalm: My heart has poured forth. Response: You have loved righteousness. Verse: Therefore he anointed. Alleluia: In your beauty. Offertory: Virgins will be offered to the king. [Note: [Col. 0688D] The Compendium adds: “Verse 1: My heart has poured forth. Verse 2: They will be led”; and after the Communion it adds: “Psalm: My heart has poured forth.”] Communion: Grace has been poured forth.

## At Mass on the Greater Litany and during the Rogations

Antiphon: He heard my voice from his holy temple, alleluia, and my cry in his presence entered his ears, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: I will love you, O Lord, my strength; the Lord is my foundation, my refuge, and my deliverer. Alleluia: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is forever. Offertory: I will confess the Lord exceedingly with my mouth, and in the midst of many I will praise him, who stood at the right hand of the poor, to save my soul from those who pursued me, alleluia. [Col. 0689A] Verse 1: Help me, O Lord my God; save me because of your mercy, that they may know that this is your hand; you, O Lord, have made it. Verse 2: Let those who rise up against me be put to shame; your servant will rejoice. Let those who slandered me be clothed with reverence. Communion: Ask, and you will receive; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened, alleluia.

## The Vigil of the Lord’s Ascension

Antiphon: [Note: [Col. 0689D] Micrologus thinks that on this day the antiphon “A voice of gladness” ought to be read, chapters 40 and 57; he also reports that in former times it was customary to fast during the vigil, chapter 55. PAMELIUS.] Clap your hands, all you nations; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. Psalm: He subjected peoples to us and nations beneath our feet. Alleluia: All you nations.

Offertory: Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up into heaven? This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him ascending into heaven, alleluia. Verse: And while they were looking intently toward heaven as he went, behold, two men stood beside them in white garments, and they said: He will come in the same way as you saw him ascending into heaven, alleluia. [Note: [Col. 0689D] The Compendium and Theoderic assign “I will not leave you” for the Communion.] Communion: Father, while I was with them, I kept those whom you gave me, alleluia. But now I am coming to you; I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you preserve them from evil.

## 696 On the holy day of the Ascension

Antiphon: Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up into heaven? alleluia. As you saw him ascending into heaven, so he will come, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: All you nations, clap your hands, shout joyfully. Response: God has ascended amid jubilation, and the Lord amid the sound of the trumpet. Verse: Sing praises to our God; sing praises, sing praises with understanding. Alleluia: God has ascended amid jubilation, and the Lord amid the sound of the trumpet. Another Alleluia: The Lord is in Sinai, in the holy place; ascending on high, he led captivity captive.

Offertory: God has ascended amid jubilation; the Lord amid the sound of the trumpet, alleluia. Verse 1: All you nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. Verse 2: For the Lord is most high, awesome, a great king over all the earth. Verse 3: He subjected peoples to us and nations beneath our feet. [Note: [Col. 0689D] In the manuscripts there is no second Offertory, and all this is omitted up to the Communion.] Another Offertory: Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up into heaven? Verse: And while they were looking intently, as above.

Communion: Sing praises to the Lord, who ascended above the heaven of heavens toward the East, alleluia. [Note: [Col. 0689D] This too is not found at all in the manuscripts; instead, after the Communion one reads: “Psalm: Let God arise.” In Pamelius, however, after “toward the East, alleluia,” follows: “Psalm 67. Response: Give glory to God over Israel.”] Response: Give glory to God over Israel.

## Sunday after the Ascension

[Col. 0689D] Antiphon: Hear, O Lord, my voice with which I cried to you, alleluia. My heart said to you: I sought your face; your face, O Lord, I will seek. Do not turn your face away from me, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? [Note: [Col. 0689D] In the Compendium there are two Alleluias: the first, “The Lord has reigned over all”; the second, “The Lord has reigned; he is clothed with beauty.” In Theoderic there is likewise a double Alleluia, but entirely different: the first is “God has ascended,” the second “The Lord is in Sinai.”] Alleluia: Those who trust in the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0690D] The Compendium has a double Offertory: the first, “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? As you saw him,” etc.; the second is “Praise,” as in the printed editions. Only the latter is assigned by Theoderic.] Offertory: Praise the Lord, my soul. Communion: Father, while I was with them.

## The Nativity of Saint Urban

Antiphon: May your priests, O Lord, [Note: [Col. 0690D] Compendium: “May they clothe themselves.”] clothe themselves with righteousness, and may your saints rejoice. For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed. Psalm: Remember, O Lord, David and all his gentleness. Response: I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him. For my hand will help him, and my arm will strengthen him. Verse: The enemy will accomplish nothing against him, and the son of wickedness will not harm him. Alleluia: Remember, O Lord, David, etc. Offertory: My truth and my mercy are with him, and in my name his horn will be exalted. [Col. 0690B] Verse: I have placed help in one who is mighty, and I have exalted the chosen one from my people. [Note: [Col. 0690D] The second verse is in the Compendium, namely, “Mercy.”] Communion: The faithful and prudent servant whom the Lord appointed over his household, to give them their measure of wheat at the proper time. Psalm: As above.

## Saturday, the vigil of Pentecost, station at Saint John

At the Introit [Note: [Col. 0690D] The Roman Ordo also mentions the Litany, p. 82] a litany. Then:

[Note: [Col. 0690D] In the Compendium: “Alleluia: Give thanks.”] Response: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is forever. Tract. 697 Praise the Lord, all nations; praise him, all peoples. Verse: For his mercy has been confirmed over us, and the truth of the Lord remains forever. [Col. 0690C] Offertory: Send forth your spirit, and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth; may the glory of the Lord endure forever. Verse 1: Bless the Lord, my soul. O Lord my God, you have been greatly magnified. [Note: [Col. 0690D] At the end of this verse and the following one, “May the glory of the Lord endure forever” is to be repeated, according to the Compendium manuscript.] Verse 2: You have clothed yourself with confession and beauty, wrapped in light as in a garment. Verse 3: You stretch out the heavens like a skin; you cover its upper parts with waters; you make the clouds your ascent. Communion: On the last day of the feast Jesus said: Whoever believes in me, rivers of living water will flow from his belly. Now he said this about the Spirit whom those who believed in him were to receive, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: Bless the Lord, my soul.

## Pentecost Sunday

Antiphon: The Spirit of the Lord has filled the world, alleluia; and that which contains all things has knowledge of the voice, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 67. Response: Confirm this, O God. Alleluia: Send forth your spirit, [Col. 0691A] and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth. [Note: [Col. 0691C] The manuscripts give as the second Alleluia: “The Spirit of the Lord has filled the world, and that which contains all things has knowledge of the voice.”] Response: This is the day which. Offertory: Confirm, O God, what you have worked in us; from your temple, which is in Jerusalem, kings will offer gifts to you. Verse 1: Sing to God; [Note: [Col. 0691D] The Compendium: “Bless his name.”] sing a psalm to his name; make a way for him who ascends over the setting sun; the Lord is his name. Verse 2: In the churches bless the Lord God from the springs of Israel. [Note: [Col. 0691D] This verse is absent from the Compendium manuscript.] Verse 3: Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord, who ascended above the heaven of heavens toward the East. Communion: Suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a violent wind arriving, where they were sitting, alleluia; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, speaking the mighty works of God, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: As above.

[Note: [Col. 0691D] In Theoderic: “Station at Saint Peter ad vincula.” In the Compendium only “ad vincula” is read.]

## Monday

Antiphon: He fed them with the fat of wheat, alleluia; and he satisfied them with honey from the rock, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. [Col. 0691B] Psalm: Rejoice in God our helper; shout joyfully to the God of Jacob. Alleluia: Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us shout joyfully to God our salvation. Verse: Let us come before his face with confession, and let us shout joyfully to him in psalms. [Note: [Col. 0691D] In the manuscripts the Alleluia is “Send forth the Spirit.”] Alleluia: Praise the Lord, you servants.

Offertory: The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice, and the springs of waters appeared, alleluia. Verse 1: I will love you, O Lord, my strength; the Lord is my foundation and refuge, and my deliverer. Verse 2: My deliverer from angry nations. Communion: The Holy Spirit will teach you, alleluia, whatever I have said to you, alleluia. Psalm 80.

[Note: [Col. 0691D] In the manuscripts: “Station at Saint Anastasia.”]

## Tuesday

Antiphon: Receive the joy of your gladness [Note: [Col. 0691D] Compendium: “Of your glory.”] and happiness, [Col. 0691C] 698 alleluia, giving thanks to God, alleluia, who called you to the heavenly kingdoms, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: Hear, my people, my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth. Alleluia: [Note: [Col. 0691D] There: “Alleluia: The Spirit of the Lord has filled.” In Theoderic it reads “Whatever you wish.”] Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion. Alleluia: Praise the Lord, my soul; I will praise the Lord during my life; I will sing to my God as long as I exist.

Offertory: The Lord opened the gates of heaven, and rained down manna upon them to eat; he gave them the bread of heaven; man ate the bread of angels. Verse 1: Hear, my people, my law. Verse 2: I will open my mouth in a parable; I will speak riddles from the beginning. [Col. 0692A] Communion: The Spirit who proceeds from the Father, alleluia, he will glorify me, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: As above.

[Note: [Col. 0691D] In the manuscripts: “Station at Saint Mary,” namely the Major Basilica, as Theoderic also indicates.]

## Wednesday

Antiphon: [Note: [Col. 0691D] Micrologus cites these Wednesdays, Fridays, and Saturday from the Antiphoner of Saint Gregory, chapters 25 and 28; but instead of the Offertory “I meditated,” he asserts that “Send forth your spirit” ought to be read, as also below, on Saturday, instead of the Offertory “O Lord God.” PAMELIUS.] O God, when you went out before your people, alleluia, making a way for them, alleluia, dwelling among them, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered, and let those who hate him flee from his presence. [Note: [Col. 0691D] In the Compendium: “Alleluia: May the glory of the Lord endure.” Theoderic agrees with the printed editions.] Alleluia: Whatever you wish, if it should occur on days of fasting.

Response: [Note: [Col. 0691D] This Response and the rest up to the Offertory are absent from the Compendium; the situation is different in Theoderic.] Our protector. Verse: Lord God of hosts. Response: Turn back, O Lord. Verse: Lord, you have been our refuge. Offertory: I meditated on your commandments, which I loved. Verse: I said, “The Lord is my portion”; I have resolved to keep your law. Communion: I give you my peace, alleluia; I leave you my peace, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: As above.

[Note: [Col. 0692C] Nothing is assigned for this feria in the Compendium either; but in Theoderic the Antiphons, Responses, Alleluias, etc., which are given in the printed editions for Friday, belong to Thursday, and the office of Friday is taken from the preceding Wednesday. See Micrologus, chapter 50.]

## Thursday is vacant

[Note: [Col. 0692D] The station is at the Apostles, according to the manuscripts.]

## Friday

[Col. 0692B]

Antiphon: May my mouth be filled with your praise, alleluia, so that I may sing, alleluia; my lips will rejoice when I sing to you, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: In you, O Lord, I have hoped; I shall not be put to shame forever. In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me. Alleluia: [Note: [Col. 0692D] Theoderic has the same, but the Compendium assigns “Send forth your Spirit.”] Whatever you wish, if it should occur on days of fasting.

Response: [Note: [Col. 0692D] This Response, with the following verse, is absent from the Compendium.] It is good to confess to the Lord and to sing praise to your name, O Most High. Verse: To proclaim your mercy in the morning and your truth throughout the night.

Offertory: Praise the Lord, my soul; I will praise the Lord during my life; I will sing to my God as long as I exist. Verse 1: He keeps truth forever; he executes judgment for those who suffer wrong; he gives food to the hungry. Verse 2: The Lord raises up those who are cast down; the Lord loves the righteous. [Col. 0692C] Communion: The Spirit breathes where he wishes, and you hear his voice, alleluia; but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: As above.

[Note: [Col. 0692D] In the manuscripts: “Station at Saint Peter.”]

## Saturday with twelve readings

Antiphon: The charity of God has been poured into our hearts, alleluia, through his Spirit dwelling within us, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm: O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I have cried out and by night before you. Response. 699 [Note: [Col. 0692D] In the Compendium these four Responses with their verses are not read; it merely notes: “Response IV belonging to the same day, and the Blessing,” meaning that four Responses and the hymn “Benedictus” are to be said, as on the other Ember Saturdays. In Theoderic it reads “Response: whatever you wish,” that is, as I infer, “Responses as you wish.” Here Pamelius notes that Micrologus asserts that Alleluias ought to be read in place of these Responses, namely: “The Spirit of the Lord, the Paraclete”; “Send forth”; “By the word”; “Come, Holy Spirit.” The same Pamelius notes at the end of the office of this day that the octave of Pentecost is missing. Berno sufficiently indicates this in his book On the Mass, chapter 5. It is clear that it was omitted because the antiphon and office are the same as on Pentecost Sunday.] Our protector. Verse: Lord God of hosts. Response: Be merciful, O Lord. Verse: Help us, O God our savior. [Note: [Col. 0644D] In the manuscript: “Station at the Holy Apostles.”] [Note: [Col. 0671D] According to the manuscripts, the station is at Saint Marcellus.] [Col. 0693A] Response: Turn back, O Lord. Verse: Lord, you have been our refuge. Response: Let my prayer be directed. Verse: May the lifting up of my hands be an evening sacrifice. Response: Blessing, etc.

Offertory: O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I have cried out and by night before you; let my prayer enter into your presence, O Lord. Alleluia: Incline your ear to my prayer, for my soul is filled with evils, and my life has drawn near to hell; I have been counted among those who descend into the pit. Verse 1: I have become like a man without help, free among the dead. Verse 2: Like the wounded sleeping in tombs, of whom no one remembers any longer; and they have been rejected from your hand. Communion: I will not leave you orphans; I will come to you again, alleluia, and your heart will rejoice, alleluia, [Col. 0693B] alleluia. Psalm: Hear, my people.

[Note: [Col. 0693D] Before this feast Theoderic assigns: “On the Kalends of June, the Dedication of the church of Saint Nicomedes.” In the second Theoderic one reads: “The Nativity of Saint Nicomedes.”]

## The Nativity of the holy martyrs Marcellinus and Peter

Antiphon: The righteous cried out, and he heard them, and delivered them from all their tribulations. Psalm: I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth. Response: The righteous cried out. Verse: The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit. Alleluia: Your saints, O Lord, will bless you; they will speak of the glory of your kingdom.

Offertory: [Note: [Col. 0693D] In the Compendium there follows: Verse 1: Blessed are those; Verse 2: For this he will pray.] Rejoice in the Lord and exult, O righteous, and glory, all you upright of heart. [Note: [Col. 0693D] In Theoderic, for the Communion: “But the righteous.”] Communion: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of wickedness will not touch them. They seemed to have died in the eyes of the foolish, but they are in peace.

## The Nativity of the holy martyrs Primus and Felician

Antiphon: Let the peoples recount the wisdom of the saints, and let the Church proclaim their praise; but their names will live forever and ever, alleluia. Psalm: Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord; praise is fitting for the upright. Response: The saints will exult in glory; they will rejoice in their resting places. Verse: Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise is in the assembly of the saints. Alleluia: Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord; praise is fitting for the upright.

Offertory: Wondrous is God in his saints; the God of Israel himself will give strength and power to his people. Blessed be God, alleluia. Verse 1: Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered, and let those who hate him flee from his presence. Verse 2: Let sinners perish from the face of God; but let the righteous feast, exulting in the presence of God and delighting in gladness. Communion: I chose you from the world so that you might go and bear fruit, and that your fruit might remain.

[Note: [Col. 0693D] The office of Saint Basilides is not separately present in the Compendium manuscript; but he is mentioned in the following feast, where one reads: “The Nativity of the saints Basilides, Cyrinus, etc.” Theoderic likewise has this.]

## The Nativity of Saint Basilides the martyr

[Col. 0693D]

Antiphon: You crowned him, O Lord, with glory and honor, and appointed him over the works of your hands. Psalm: The king will rejoice in your strength, O Lord, and will exult exceedingly in your salvation. Offertory: 700 In [Col. 0694A] your strength, O Lord, the righteous man will rejoice. Verse 1: He asked for life. Verse 2: Great is his glory in your salvation. Communion: You placed upon his head, O Lord, a crown of precious stone.

## On the same day: the Nativity of the holy Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius

Antiphon: Let the groaning of the bound enter your presence, O Lord; repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom; avenge, O Lord, the blood of your saints that has been poured out. Psalm: O God, the nations have entered your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a place for keeping fruit. Response: Avenge, O Lord, the blood of your saints that has been poured out. Verse: They gave the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of heaven, the flesh of your saints [Col. 0694B] to the beasts of the earth. Alleluia: [Note: [Col. 0693D] In the Compendium: “Alleluia: Let the righteous feast.” Concerning the entire office of this day, Pamelius notes that it is absent from the Codex Blandinianus.] The saints rejoiced in glory; they will rejoice in their resting places.

Offertory: The saints will rejoice in glory; they will rejoice in their resting places; the exultations of God are in their throats. Verse: Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise is in the assembly of the saints. Let Israel rejoice in him who made him, and let the daughters of Zion exult in their king. Communion: They gave the corpses of your servants, O Lord, as food to the birds of heaven, the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth; according to the greatness of your arm, possess the children of those put to death.

## The Nativity of the holy Mark and Marcellian

Antiphon: The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, and he is their protector in the time of tribulation. Psalm: Do not be envious of evildoers, nor jealous of those who commit iniquity. Response: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God [Col. 0694C] and the torment of wickedness will not touch them. Verse: They seemed to have died in the eyes of the foolish, but they are in peace. Alleluia: [Note: [Col. 0694D] In the Compendium: “Alleluia: Avenge, O Lord, the blood … which has been poured out upon the earth.” Theoderic: “Alleluia: Your servants.” Perhaps “Your saints” should be read, as in the Vulgate editions.] Your saints, O Lord.

Offertory: Our soul has been rescued like a sparrow from the snare of the hunters; the snare has been broken, and we have been freed. Verse 1: If it had not been that the Lord. Verse 2: Our soul has passed through the torrent.

Communion: Amen, I say to you: whatever you did for one of the least of mine, you did for me. Come, blessed ones of my Father; possess [Note: [Col. 0694D] Compendium: “Possess the kingdom prepared for you from the origin of the world.”] the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world. Another: I chose you from the world, so that you may go and bear fruit, and that your fruit may remain. Psalm: As above.

## The Nativity of the holy Gervasius and Protasius

Antiphon: The Lord will speak peace [Note: [Col. 0694D] Compendium: “to his people.”] to his people, and to his saints, and to those who are converted to him. Psalm: You have blessed your land, O Lord; you have turned back the captivity of Jacob. Response: Glorious is God in his saints, wondrous in his majesty, performing miracles. Verse: Your right hand, O Lord, has been glorified in strength; your right hand has crushed the enemies. [Note: [Col. 0694D] In the Compendium: “Alleluia: The saints will rejoice in glory; they will rejoice in their resting places.” In Theoderic: “Alleluia: Rejoice, you righteous,” as Pamelius and the Vatican editions have. Gussanville: “Rejoice in the Lord.”] Alleluia: [Col. 0695A] Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord.

Offertory: Rejoice in the Lord and exult, O righteous, and glory, all you upright of heart. [Note: [Col. 0695D] This verse is omitted in the Compendium.] Verse: For this every holy person will pray to you at a suitable time. 701 Communion: They gave the corpses.

## On the vigil of Saint John the Baptist

Antiphon: Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard, and Elizabeth your wife will bear you a son, and you will call his name John. He will be great before the Lord, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb, and many will rejoice at his birth. Psalm: The king will rejoice in your strength, O Lord, and will exult exceedingly in your salvation. Response: There was a man sent by God whose name was John; he came. Verse: To bear witness to the light and to prepare for the Lord a perfect people. Offertory: Glory and [Col. 0695B] honor. Verse: O Lord, our Lord. [Note: [Col. 0695D] After this verse the Compendium assigns: Verse 2: What is man, that you remember him?] Communion: Great is his glory. Psalm: As above.

## At the first Mass during the night

Antiphon: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree; he will multiply like a cedar of Lebanon, planted in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. Psalm: It is good to confess to the Lord and to sing praise to your name, O Most High. Response: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree; he will multiply like a cedar of Lebanon in the house of the Lord. Verse: It is good. Offertory: In your strength, O Lord. Communion: You placed, O Lord. Psalm 20.

## VIII Kalends of July: At the Nativity mentioned above

Antiphon: From my mother’s womb the Lord called me by my name, and he made my mouth like a sharp sword; he protected me under the shelter of his hand; he made me like a chosen arrow. Psalm: It is good to confess to the Lord. Response: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree. Response: Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; and before you came forth from the womb, I sanctified you. Verse: The Lord sent forth his hand and touched my mouth, and said to me. Alleluia: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in his commandments.

Offertory: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree. Verse 1: It is good. Verse 2: To proclaim in the morning. Verse 3: Planted in the house of the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0695D] This Offertory and the following verses, “Elizabeth,” are not read in the Compendium.]

Another Offertory: Zechariah the priest entered the house of the Lord at the hour of incense. The angel said to him: Do not be afraid, because your prayer has been heard, and Elizabeth your wife will bear you a son, and you will call his name John, because many will rejoice at his birth, alleluia. Verse: The time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son, because the Lord had magnified his mercy toward her. When they came to circumcise the child, they were calling him by his father’s name, but his mother replied: By no means. They gestured to his father, asking what he wished him to be called. He wrote, saying: “His name will be John.” And they were all amazed, because his mouth and tongue had been opened, and he spoke, blessing God, because many would rejoice at his birth.

Communion: And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. Verse: To give knowledge.

## At the Nativity of the holy martyrs John and Paul

Antiphon: Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and the Lord delivered them from all of them. The Lord guards all their bones; not one of them will be broken. Psalm: I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth. 702 Response: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together as one; like ointment on the head, which descends upon the beard, the beard of Aaron. Verse: The Lord has commanded blessing and life forever. [Note: [Col. 0695D] In our manuscripts: “Alleluia: Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord; praise is fitting for the upright.”] Alleluia: Whatever you wish.

Offertory: All who love your name will glory in you, for you, O Lord, bless the righteous. [Col. 0696B] O Lord, you have crowned them with the shield of your good will. Verse 1: Give ear, O Lord, to my words; understand my cry. Attend to the voice of my prayer, my King and my God. Verse 2: For to you I will pray, O Lord; to you I will cry, O Lord. In the morning you will hear my voice. Communion: Although they suffered torments in the sight of men, God tested them; like gold in a furnace he proved them, and like a holocaust he received them. Psalm: As above.

## The Vigil of Saint Peter

Antiphon: The Lord says to Peter: When you were younger, you girded yourself and walked where you wished; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and lead you where you do not wish to go. He said this to signify by what death he would glorify God. Psalm: The heavens proclaim the glory of God. [Col. 0696C] Response: Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. Verse: The heavens proclaim the glory of God, and the firmament announces the work of his hands.

Offertory: Your friends have been greatly honored, O God; their dominion has been greatly strengthened. Verse 1: O Lord, you have tested me and known me; you know my sitting down and my rising up. [Note: [Col. 0696D] Compendium: Verse 2: “Behold, O Lord, you have known,” etc. Verse 3: “You understood my thoughts from afar; you investigated my path.”] Verse 2: You understood my thoughts from afar; you investigated my path and my direction. Verse 3: Behold, O Lord, you have known all things, the last and the first; you formed me and placed your hand upon me. Communion: You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church.

## III Kalends of July: The Nativity of Saint Peter

Antiphon: Now I know truly that the Lord sent his angel [Col. 0696D] and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the Jewish people. Psalm: You have tested me, O Lord. Response: You will appoint them rulers over all the earth; they will remember your name, O Lord. Verse: In place of your fathers, sons have been born to you; therefore the peoples will confess to you. [Note: [Col. 0696D] In the Compendium: “Alleluia: Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.” Theoderic agrees with the common editions.]

Alleluia: You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church. Another Alleluia: Your friends have been greatly honored, O God; their dominion has been greatly strengthened. [Col. 0697A] Offertory: You will appoint them rulers over all the earth; they will remember your name throughout every generation and age. Verse 1: My heart has poured forth a good word; I speak of my works to the King. Verse 2: My tongue is the pen of a swift-writing scribe; you are beautiful beyond the sons of men; grace has been poured forth upon your lips. Verse 3: Therefore God has blessed you forever; gird your sword upon your thigh, O Most Mighty.

Communion: Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these? Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you. Feed my sheep. Psalm: As above.

### June 30 — Feast of Saint Paul

**Antiphon:** I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to preserve my deposit for that day. [703]  
**Psalm:** Lord, you have tested me.  
**Responsory:** He who worked through Peter for the apostolate also worked through me among the Gentiles, and they recognized the grace of God that was given to me.  
**Verse:** The grace of God in me was not in vain, but his grace always remains in me.  
**[Note: [Col. 0697D] Compendium: Alleluia, “The heavens declare.” Theoderic’s manuscripts agree with the printed editions.]**  
**Alleluia:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.  
**Offertory:** But to me your friends are exceedingly honored, O God; their authority has been greatly strengthened.  
**[Note: [Col. 0697D] In the Compendium, three verses are assigned: 1. “Lord, you have tested me”; 2. “You have understood”; 3. “Behold, you, Lord.” Pamelius observes that this day’s office is expressly cited from the Gradual and Sacramentary books of Saint Gregory by the Micrologus, chapter 42.]**  
**Communion:** Amen, I say to you: you who have left everything and followed me will receive a hundredfold and will possess eternal life.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saints Processus and Martinianus

**Antiphon:** The saints judge nations and rule over peoples; their Lord God will reign forever.  
**Psalm:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.  
**Responsory:** The saints will exult in glory.  
**Verse:** Sing to the Lord.  
**[Note: [Col. 0697D] Compendium: Alleluia, “The saints will exult.” Theoderic: Alleluia, “Your saints, O Lord.”]**  
**Alleluia:** Our Lord is wonderful in his saints.  
**Offertory:** All will glory in you.  
**Verse:** My words.  
**Communion:** Our soul has been rescued like a sparrow from the snare of the hunters. [Col. 0697C]  
**Psalm:** Unless the Lord had been with us.

### July 6 — Octave of the Blessed Apostles Peter and Paul

**Antiphon:** Let the peoples recount the wisdom of the saints, and let the Church proclaim their praises; but their names will live forever and ever.  
**[Note: [Col. 0697D] Compendium: Psalm, “The heavens declare.”]**  
**Psalm:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.  
**Responsory:** The souls of the righteous.  
**Verse:** They seemed, in the eyes of the foolish, to die.  
**Alleluia:** Your saints, O Lord, will bless you; they will speak of the glory of your kingdom.  
**Offertory:** The saints will exult in glory.  
**[Note: [Col. 0697D] In the Compendium this Offertory is followed by the verses: “Sing to the Lord a new song, his praise in the assembly of the saints. Let Israel rejoice in him who made him, and let the children of Zion exult in their king; let them exult.” Pamelius notes that the Micrologus mentions this Octave in chapter 44.]**  
**Communion:** The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God.  
**Psalm:** As above.

**[Note: [Col. 0697D] In Pamelius’s edition, the feast of the seven holy martyrs precedes the Octave of the holy apostles.]**

### The Seven Holy Brothers

**Antiphon:** Praise the Lord, children; praise the name of the Lord, who makes the barren woman dwell in her house as a joyful mother of children.  
**Psalm:** May the name of the Lord be blessed, from this time forth and forever. [Col. 0698A]  
**Responsory:** Our soul.  
**Verse:** The snare has been broken.  
**Alleluia:** Praise the Lord, children.  
**[Note: [Col. 0698D] This Alleluia is absent from the Compendium manuscripts.]**  
**Offertory:** Our soul.  
**Verse:** Unless the Lord had been with us.  
**Communion:** Whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven is my brother, sister, and mother, says the Lord.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Benedict

**[Note: [Col. 0698D] The Blandinian Codex does not contain this office either. Pamelius: it is also absent from the Compendium manuscripts.]**

**Antiphon:** The righteous will flourish like the palm.  
**Psalm:** It is good to give thanks.  
**Responsory:** I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him. For my hand will help him, and my arm will strengthen him.  
**Verse:** The enemy will accomplish nothing against him, and the son of iniquity will do him no harm.  
**Alleluia:** I have made a covenant with my chosen ones; I have sworn to David my servant.  
**Offertory:** I have found David.  
**Communion:** Blessed is the servant whom, when the Lord comes, he finds watching. [Col. 0698B] Amen, I say to you: he will set him over all his possessions.

### Saint Praxedes

**[704]**

**Antiphon:** I spoke of your testimonies before kings and was not put to shame; and I meditated on your commandments, which I loved exceedingly.  
**Psalm:** Blessed are the undefiled in the way.  
**Responsory:** You loved righteousness and hated iniquity.  
**Verse:** Therefore God, your God, anointed you with the oil of righteousness.  
**[Note: [Col. 0698D] This Alleluia is missing in the Compendium.]**  
**Alleluia:** In your appearance and beauty, direct your course, proceed prosperously, and reign.  
**Offertory:** Grace has been poured forth.  
**[Note: [Col. 0698D] There, after the Offertory, one reads: Verse 1, “My heart has uttered”; verse 2, “In your appearance.”]**  
**Communion:** The kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking good pearls; when he had found one precious pearl, he gave away all that he had and bought it.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Apollinaris

[Col. 0698C]

**Antiphon:** Priests of God, bless the Lord; holy and humble of heart, praise God.  
**[Note: [Col. 0698D] This office is cited by the Micrologus from the Gradual book of Saint Gregory, chapter 43. Pamelius.]**  
**Psalm:** Remember, O Lord, David and all his gentleness.  
**[Note: [Col. 0698D] In the Compendium: Psalm, “Bless the Lord, all his works.”]**  
**Responsory:** I have found David my servant.  
**Verse:** The enemy will accomplish nothing against him.  
**Alleluia:** Remember, O Lord, David.  
**[Note: [Col. 0698D] This Alleluia is not in the Compendium.]**  
**Offertory:** My faithfulness and my mercy.  
**[Note: [Col. 0698D] After this Offertory, the cited manuscript has the verses: 1. “I have set help”; 2. “Mercy.”]**  
**Communion:** Once I swore by my holiness: his offspring will endure forever; and his throne will be like the sun before me, and like the moon established forever, and a faithful witness in heaven.  
**Psalm:** The mercies of the Lord.

**[Note: [Col. 0698D] The Micrologus also cites this office there, chapter 43. Pamelius. Nevertheless, this feast is absent from the Compendium manuscript.]**

### Feast of Saint Felix

**Antiphon:** Let his priests be clothed with righteousness, and let his saints exult with exultation.  
**Psalm:** Remember, O Lord, David.  
**Responsory:** Behold the great priest, who in his days pleased God.  
**Verse:** No one like him was found who would keep the law of the Most High.  
**Offertory:** My faithfulness and my mercy are with him, and in my name his horn will be exalted. [Col. 0699A]  
**Communion:** Blessed is the servant.  
**Psalm:** As above.

**[Note: [Col. 0699D] The Blandinian Codex does not contain this office either. Pamelius. The feast, or nativity, does exist in the Compendium Codex, but its office is different: Antiphon, “His priests I will clothe with salvation”; Psalm, “Remember, O Lord, David”; Responsory, “Behold the great priest”; Verse, “No one was found”; Alleluia, “The saints will exult”; Offertory, “Rejoice”; Communion, “The souls of the righteous.”]**

### On the Same Day: Feast of Saints Simplicius, Faustinus, and Beatrix

**Antiphon:** Let the peoples recount the wisdom of the saints.  
**Psalm:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.  
**Responsory:** The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them, and delivered them from all their tribulations.  
**Verse:** The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and the humble in spirit will be saved.  
**Alleluia:** Your saints, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** All will glory in you.  
**Communion:** I have chosen you.

### Feast of Saints Abdon and Sennen

**Antiphon:** Let the groaning of the prisoners enter your presence, O Lord. [Col. 0699B]  
**Psalm:** O God, the nations have entered your inheritance.  
**Responsory:** Glorious is God in his saints.  
**Verse:** Your right hand, O Lord.  
**Alleluia:** Your saints, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** God is wonderful in his saints. [705]  
**[Note: [Col. 0699D] In the Compendium two verses follow: “Let God arise,” and “Let them perish.”]**  
**Communion:** They made the mortal remains of your saints food for the birds of heaven.  
**[Note: [Col. 0699D] There: Communion, “Blessed are the pure in heart.”]**  
**Psalm:** O God, the nations have entered your inheritance.  
**[Note: [Col. 0699D] There: Psalm, “Blessed are the undefiled.”]**

**[Note: [Col. 0699D] This feast and the following one are omitted in the Compendium Codex. Theoderic’s manuscripts contain both.]**

### Saint Peter in Chains

**Antiphon:** The salvation of the people.  
**Psalm:** Hearken, my people, to my law.  
**Responsory:** Save your people.  
**Verse:** To you, O Lord, I cried out.  
**Alleluia:** You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church.  
**Offertory:** You will save the humble people and humble the eyes of the proud.  
**Communion:** Lord, if you are he.

### Feast of Saint Stephen, Pope

**Antiphon:** The righteous will flourish like the palm.  
**Psalm:** It is good to give thanks to the Lord.  
**Responsory:** The righteous will not be shaken, because the Lord strengthens his hand. [Col. 0699C]  
**Verse:** All day long he is merciful and lends, and his offspring will be in blessing.  
**Alleluia:** I have made a covenant with my chosen ones; I have sworn to David my servant.  
**Offertory:** I have found David my servant.  
**Communion:** Lord, you gave me five talents; behold, I have gained five more. Well done, faithful servant: because you were faithful over a little, I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your lord.

### Another Form

**Antiphon:** I will clothe his priests with salvation.  
**Psalm:** Remember, O Lord, David.  
**Responsory:** The mouth of the righteous will meditate on wisdom, and his tongue will speak judgment.  
**Verse:** The law of his God is in his heart, and his steps will not be overturned.  
**Offertory:** I have found David.  
**Verse 1:** You are powerful, O Lord.  
**Verse 2:** My faithfulness and my mercy. [Col. 0699D]  
**Communion:** Lord, you gave me five talents.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Xystus, Pope

**Antiphon:** Priests of God, bless the Lord.  
**Psalm:** Remember, O Lord, David.  
**[Note: [Col. 0700D] In the Compendium: Responsory, “The mouth of the righteous will meditate on wisdom”; Verse, “The law of his God”; Offertory, “My faithfulness.”]**  
**Responsory:** I will clothe his priests with salvation, and his saints will exult with exultation. [Col. 0700A]  
**Verse:** There I will cause David’s horn to spring forth; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.  
**Alleluia:** I have found David.  
**Offertory:** I have found David.  
**Communion:** The faithful and prudent servant whom the Lord set over his household, to give it a measure of wheat at the proper time.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### On the Same Day: Feast of Saints Felicissimus and Agapitus

**Antiphon:** The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, and he is their protector in time of tribulation.  
**Psalm:** Do not be jealous of evildoers.  
**[Note: [Col. 0700D] In the Compendium: Responsory, “The saints will exult”; Verse, “Sing to the Lord”; Alleluia, “Your saints, O Lord.” Theoderic assigns the same Alleluia and otherwise agrees with the printed editions.]**  
**Responsory:** The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God.  
**Verse:** They seemed, in the eyes of the foolish, to die.  
**Alleluia:** Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise is in the assembly of the saints.  
**Offertory:** All who love your name will glory in you, for you, O Lord, will bless the righteous; O Lord, you have crowned us as with a shield of your good will. [Col. 0700B]  
**Verse 1:** Give heed to my words.  
**Verse 2:** For to you I will pray, O Lord.  
**Communion:** I chose you from the world.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Cyriacus

**Antiphon:** Fear the Lord, all his saints, for those who fear him lack nothing; the rich have become needy and hungry, but those who seek the Lord will lack no good thing. [706]  
**[Note: [Col. 0700D] Compendium: “They will not be deprived of any good.”]**  
**Psalm:** I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise is always in my mouth.  
**Responsory:** Fear the Lord, all his saints, for those who fear him lack nothing.  
**Verse:** Those who seek the Lord will lack no good thing.  
**Alleluia:** The saints will exult in glory; they will rejoice in their dwelling places. [Col. 0700C]  
**[Note: [Col. 0700D] There: Alleluia, “Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.” The printed editions agree with the Theoderic manuscripts.]**  
**Offertory:** Rejoice in the Lord and exult.  
**Verse 1:** Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven.  
**Verse 2:** For this every holy person will pray to you.  
**Communion:** These signs will accompany those who believe in me: they will cast out demons; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will be well.

### Vigil of Saint Lawrence

**Antiphon:** He distributed and gave to the poor; his righteousness endures forever and ever; his horn will be exalted in glory.  
**Psalm:** Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in his commandments.  
**Responsory:** He distributed and gave to the poor; his righteousness endures forever and ever.  
**Verse:** His offspring will be mighty on the earth; the generation of the upright will be blessed.  
**Offertory:** My prayer is pure, and therefore I ask that a place be given to my voice in heaven, because there is my judge and my witness [**Note: [Col. 0700D] Compendium: “forever”**] on high; let my supplication ascend to the Lord.  
**Verse:** The Lord tested me like gold; I guarded his ways and did not depart from his commandments.  
**[Note: [Col. 0700D] Absent from the manuscripts.]**  
**Another form. Offertory:** Glory and honor.  
**Communion:** Whoever wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. [Col. 0701A]  
**Psalm:** As above.

### On the Feast of Saint Lawrence

**[Note: [Col. 0701D] This is placed first in the Compendium and in the two Theoderic manuscripts, in the first Mass. In the Compendium this Mass is: Antiphon, “You have tested the heart”; “and in me no iniquity was found.” Psalm, “Hear, O Lord, my righteousness.” Responsory, “The righteous will flourish like the palm.” Verse, “To proclaim.” Offertory, “In your strength.” Verse, “He asked for life.” Communion, “Great is his glory.” There is another Mass for the day: “Confession,” etc.]**

**Antiphon:** Confession and beauty are before him; holiness and magnificence are in his sanctuary.  
**Psalm:** Sing to the Lord.  
**Responsory:** You tested my heart, O Lord, and visited me by night.  
**Verse:** You tested me with fire, and no iniquity was found in me.  
**Alleluia:** Blessed is the man.  
**Offertory:** Confession and beauty.  
**Verse 1:** Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth.  
**Verse 2:** Sing to the Lord and bless his name; proclaim his salvation from day to day.  
**Communion:** Whoever serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also will my servant be.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Tiburtius

[Col. 0701B]

**Antiphon:** The righteous will flourish like the palm, [**Note: [Col. 0701D] Compendium: “Like the cedar of Lebanon.”**] and will multiply like the cedar that is in Lebanon.  
**Psalm:** It is good to give thanks to the Lord and to sing praises to your name, O Most High.  
**Responsory:** The mouth of the righteous will meditate on wisdom.  
**Verse:** The law of his God is in his heart.  
**[Note: [Col. 0701D] Thus the Theoderic manuscripts; in the Compendium: Alleluia, “I have made a covenant.”]**  
**Alleluia:** You crowned him with glory and honor, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** The righteous will rejoice in your strength.  
**Communion:** You placed, O Lord, upon his head.  
**Psalm:** O Lord, in your strength.

### Feast of Saint Hippolytus and His Companions

**Antiphon:** Let the righteous feast and exult before God, and let them delight in gladness.  
**Psalm:** Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his presence. [707]  
**[Note: [Col. 0701D] Compendium: Responsory, “The righteous cried out”; Verse, “The Lord is near”; Alleluia, “Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.” In Theoderic there is only an office for Saint Hippolytus the martyr: Antiphon, “The righteous will flourish like the palm”; Psalm, “Let God arise”; Responsory, “The souls of the righteous,” etc., as in the printed editions.]**  
**Responsory:** The souls of the righteous. [Col. 0701C]  
**Verse:** They seemed, in the eyes of the foolish, to die.  
**Alleluia:** Your saints, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** Our soul is like a sparrow.  
**Communion:** But I say to you, my friends: do not fear those who persecute you.  
**Another form:** Amen, I say to you: whatever you did for one of the least of mine, you did for me.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Eusebius

**[Note: [Col. 0701D] Compendium: Burial of Saint Eusebius the confessor. Theoderic: Feast of Saint Eusebius the priest.]**

**Antiphon:** The mouth of the righteous will meditate on wisdom, and his tongue will speak judgment; the law of his God is in his heart.  
**Psalm:** Do not be jealous of evildoers.  
**Responsory:** The mouth of the righteous will meditate.  
**Verse:** The law of his God.  
**Alleluia:** The righteous will not be shaken.  
**[Note: [Col. 0702D] This Alleluia is absent from the Compendium and is found in Theoderic.]**  
**Offertory:** The desire of his soul.  
**Verse 1:** He asked for life.  
**Verse 2:** You will make him glad.  
**Verse 3:** Let your hand be found.  
**Communion:** Blessed is the servant.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Assumption of Saint Mary

**[Note: [Col. 0702D] As will be noted below in Book I of the Sacramentary, this feast seems in antiquity to have once been called by Saint Gregory the Dormition. Pamelius: it is called the Assumption in the Compendium Codex and others.]**

[Col. 0702A]

**Antiphon:** All the rich among the people will entreat your face; virgins will be brought to the king after her; her companions will be brought to you amid gladness and exultation.  
**Psalm:** My heart has uttered a good word.
