**Responsory:** Because of truth and gentleness and righteousness, your right hand will lead you wondrously.  
**Verse:** Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear, because the King has desired your beauty.  
**Alleluia:** In your appearance and beauty, direct your course, proceed prosperously, and reign.  
**Offertory:** Virgins will be offered to the King after her; her companions will be offered to you.  
**Communion:** You loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, my God, anointed you.  
**Psalm:** As above.  
**[Note: [Col. 0702D] After this office the Compendium has another, namely: Antiphon, “Let us rejoice”; Psalm, “My heart has uttered”; Responsory, “Because of truth”; Verse, “Hear, daughter”; Alleluia, “They will be brought”; Offertory, “Grace has been poured forth”; Communion, “Blessed are you, Virgin.”]**

### Octave of Saint Lawrence

**[Note: [Col. 0702D] In the Compendium here and elsewhere one consistently reads *Octabas*, not *Octava*.]**

[Col. 0702B]

**Antiphon:** You tested my heart, O Lord, and visited me by night; you tested me with fire, and no iniquity was found in me.  
**Psalm:** Hear, O Lord, my righteousness; attend to my supplication.  
**[Note: [Col. 0702D] Compendium: Responsory, “The righteous will flourish like the palm”; Verse, “To proclaim”; Alleluia, “The righteous will not be shaken.”]**  
**Responsory:** You placed, O Lord, upon his head a crown of precious stone.  
**Verse:** You granted him the desire of his soul, and did not deprive him of the will of his lips.  
**Alleluia:** You crowned him with glory and honor, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** The righteous will rejoice in your strength, O Lord, and will exult greatly in your salvation. You granted him the desire of his soul.  
**Communion:** Whoever wishes to come after me.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Agapitus

**Antiphon:** The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and hope in him, and all the upright of heart will be praised.  
**Psalm:** Hear, O God, my prayer, when I entreat you; rescue my soul from fear of the enemy. [Col. 0702C]  
**[Note: [Col. 0702D] Compendium: Responsory, “You placed”; Verse, “The desire.”]**  
**Responsory:** The righteous will not be shaken.  
**Verse:** All day long he is merciful and lends.  
**Alleluia:** Blessed is the man who fears the Lord.  
**[Note: [Col. 0702D] This Alleluia is absent from the Compendium. In Theoderic the same office is assigned as in the printed editions.]**  
**Offertory:** The righteous will rejoice in your strength.  
**Communion:** Blessed is the servant.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saints Timothy and Symphorian

[708]

**Antiphon:** The salvation of the righteous.  
**Psalm:** Do not be jealous of evildoers.  
**Responsory:** Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.  
**Verse:** I believed, and therefore I spoke; but I was greatly humbled.  
**Alleluia:** Your saints, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** God is wonderful in his saints, the God of Israel himself will give strength and power to his people. Blessed be God, alleluia.  
**Communion:** I chose you from the world.

**[Note: [Col. 0703D] This office and the following one are not found in the Blandinian and Compendium Codices.]**

### Feast of Saint Genesius

[Col. 0703A]

**Antiphon:** You crowned him with glory and honor, O Lord, and set him over the works of your hands.  
**Psalm:** O Lord, our Lord.  
**Responsory:** You went before him, O Lord.  
**Verse:** He asked for life.  
**Alleluia:** The righteous will not be shaken, because the Lord strengthens his hand.  
**Offertory:** You granted him the desire of his soul, O Lord, and did not deprive him of the will of his lips; you placed upon his head a crown of precious stone.  
**Communion:** Whoever wishes to come after me.

### Feast of Saint Augustine

**Antiphon:** The Lord says: The words that I placed in your mouth will not depart from your mouth. For the name is present, and your gifts will be accepted upon my altar.  
**Psalm:** Lord, hear.  
**Responsory:** The Lord has sworn.  
**Verse:** The Lord said to my Lord. [Col. 0703B]  
**Alleluia:** Remember, O Lord, David and all his gentleness.  
**Offertory:** I have found David.  
**Communion:** The faithful servant.

### Feast of Saint Hermes

**Antiphon:** The righteous will not be shaken, because the Lord strengthens his hand; all day long he is merciful and lends, and his offspring will be in blessing.  
**Psalm:** Do not be jealous of evildoers.  
**[Note: [Col. 0703D] In the Compendium: Responsory, “The righteous will not be shaken”; Verse, “All day long”; Alleluia, “I have found”; Communion, “You placed.”]**  
**Responsory:** The righteous will flourish like the palm.  
**Verse:** To proclaim your mercy in the morning.  
**Alleluia:** Blessed is the man who endures temptation.  
**Offertory:** In your strength, O Lord.  
**Communion:** A multitude of sick people and those troubled by unclean spirits came to him, because power went out from him and healed them all.  
**Psalm:** As above.

**[Note: [Col. 0703D] Pamelius observes that this office is lacking in the Blandinian Codex. The same must be said of the Compendium.]**

### Beheading of Saint John the Baptist

[Col. 0703C]

**Antiphon:** The righteous will rejoice in your strength, O Lord.  
**Psalm:** He asked for life.  
**Responsory:** You went before him, O Lord.  
**Verse:** He asked for life.  
**Alleluia:** Blessed is the man.  
**Offertory:** The righteous will flourish like the palm.  
**Communion:** Great is his glory.

### Feast of Saint Sabina

**Antiphon:** I know, O Lord, that your judgments are just, and in your truth you have humbled me; pierce my flesh with your fear, and do not cast me away from your commandments.  
**Psalm:** Blessed are the undefiled in the way.  
**[Note: [Col. 0703D] Compendium: Responsory, “You loved righteousness”; Verse, “Therefore”; Alleluia, “They will be brought.” Theoderic favors the printed editions.]**  
**Responsory:** In your appearance.  
**Verse:** Because of truth and gentleness.  
**Alleluia:** Grace has been poured forth.  
**Offertory:** The daughters of kings are in your honor; the queen stood at your right hand in a garment of gold, surrounded with variety. [709]  
**Communion:** Princes persecuted me without cause, and my heart feared your words; I will rejoice over your sayings, like one who finds abundant spoils; my soul desired your testimonies, O Lord, and loved them exceedingly. [Col. 0703D]  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saints Felix and Adauctus

**Antiphon:** The wisdom of the saints.  
**Psalm:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous. [Col. 0704A]  
**[Note: [Col. 0703D] Compendium: Responsory, “The saints will exult”; Verse, “Sing to the Lord.” Theoderic does not differ from the printed editions; where they differ, we will note it.]**  
**Responsory:** Glorious is God in his saints.  
**Verse:** Your right hand, O Lord.  
**Alleluia:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.  
**Offertory:** Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord.  
**Communion:** What I tell you in darkness, speak in the light, says the Lord; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim upon the housetops.

### Feast of Saint Mary

**[Note: [Col. 0703D] It is not found in the Compendium. It exists in Theoderic.]**

**Antiphon:** Your face, O Lord.  
**Psalm:** My heart has uttered.  
**Responsory:** You loved righteousness.  
**Verse:** Because of truth.  
**Alleluia:** Virgins will be brought to the king after her; her companions will be offered to you amid gladness.  
**Offertory:** Virgins will be offered to the king.  
**Communion:** Grace has been poured forth.

### Feast of Saint Adrian

**Antiphon:** The righteous will rejoice in the Lord.  
**Psalm:** Hear, O God, the prayer. [Col. 0704B]  
**Responsory:** You went before him, O Lord.  
**Verse:** He asked life of you.  
**Alleluia:** Blessed is the man.  
**[Note: [Col. 0704D] Compendium: Alleluia, “The righteous will flourish like the palm”; below: Offertory, “The desire.”]**  
**Offertory:** You crowned him with glory and honor.  
**Communion:** You placed, O Lord.

**[Note: [Col. 0704D] This office is absent from the Blandinian Codex. Pamelius. It exists in the Compendium, where instead of the verse “The desire” there is the verse “He asked for life.” The Alleluia is “The righteous will not be shaken.” Communion: “Great is his glory.”]**

### Feast of Saint Gorgonius

**Antiphon:** You crowned him with glory and honor, and set him over the works of your hands.  
**Psalm:** O Lord, our Lord.  
**Responsory:** You placed, O Lord.  
**Verse:** The desire of his soul.  
**Alleluia:** Glory and honor.  
**Offertory:** You placed, O Lord, upon his head a crown of precious stone; he asked life of you, and you granted it to him.  
**Verse:** You granted him the desire of his soul, and did not deprive him of the will of his lips.  
**Verse:** Great is his glory in your salvation; you will place glory and great beauty upon him.  
**Communion:** You placed, O Lord.

### Feast of Saints Protus and Hyacinth

[Col. 0704C]

**Antiphon:** The saints judge nations and will rule peoples; their Lord will reign forever.  
**Psalm:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.  
**Responsory:** Vindicate, O Lord, the blood of your saints that has been shed.  
**[Note: [Col. 0704D] Compendium: Responsory, “The souls of the righteous”; Verse, “They seemed”; Alleluia, “Let the righteous feast”; Offertory, “Glory and honor”; Communion, “Whoever wishes to come.”]**  
**Verse:** They set the mortal remains of your servants as food for the birds of heaven, and the flesh of your saints for the beasts of the earth.  
**Alleluia:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.  
**Offertory:** All who love your name will glory in you, for you, O Lord, will bless the righteous; O Lord, you have crowned us as with a shield of your good will.  
**Communion:** Our soul has been rescued like a sparrow from the snare of the hunters.  
**Or:** Whoever wishes to come after me.

**[Note: [Col. 0704D] In Theoderic, the feast of Saints Cornelius and Cyprian precedes the feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, although both occur on the same day.]**

### Exaltation of the Holy Cross

[Col. 0704D]

**Antiphon:** But we must glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, in which is our salvation, life, and resurrection; through him we have been saved and liberated. [710]  
**Psalm:** The Lord has reigned; he is clothed with beauty.  
**Responsory:** Christ was made. [Col. 0705A]  
**Verse:** For this reason God also.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] Compendium: Alleluia, “The Lord has reigned; he is clothed with beauty.” Offertory, “For God has established.”]**  
**Alleluia:** Tell it among the nations: the Lord has reigned from the wood.  
**Offertory:** The right hand of the Lord.  
**Communion:** But we must glory in the cross.

### Feast of Saints Cornelius and Cyprian

**Antiphon:** Priests of God.  
**Psalm:** Remember, O Lord, David.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] Compendium: Psalm, “Bless the Lord, all his works.”]**  
**Responsory:** His priests.  
**Verse:** There I will cause David’s horn to spring forth.  
**Alleluia:** I have made a covenant with my chosen ones.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] This Alleluia is not in the Compendium.]**  
**Offertory:** My faithfulness.  
**Communion:** Lord, you gave me five talents; behold, I have gained five more. Well done, faithful servant: because you were faithful over a little, I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your lord.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Nicomedes

**Antiphon:** The righteous will rejoice in the Lord.  
**Psalm:** Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] Compendium: Psalm, “Hear, O God,” III.]** [Col. 0705B]  
**Responsory:** You placed, O Lord.  
**Verse:** The desire of his soul.  
**Alleluia:** The righteous will not be shaken.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] Absent from the Compendium.]**  
**Offertory:** Glory and honor.  
**Communion:** Whoever wishes to come after me.  
**Psalm:** As above.

### Feast of Saint Euphemia and Saints Lucia and Geminianus

**Antiphon:** They will entreat your face.  
**Psalm:** My heart has uttered.  
**Responsory:** Grace has been poured forth.  
**Verse:** Because of truth and gentleness.  
**Alleluia:** In your appearance.  
**Offertory:** Virgins will be offered to the king.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] Compendium: “They will be brought,” etc.]**  
**Communion:** The kingdom of heaven is like.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] The Compendium Codex does not contain this.]**  
**Another form:** My soul is in your salvation.  
**Psalm:** Blessed are the undefiled in the way.

### Vigil of Saint Matthew

**Antiphon:** But I am like a fruitful olive tree [**Note: [Col. 0705D] Compendium: “I bore fruit.”**] in the house of the Lord; I have hoped in the mercy of my God, and I will await your name, for it is good in the presence of your saints. [Col. 0705C]  
**Psalm:** Why do you boast in wickedness, you who are powerful in iniquity?  
**Responsory:** The righteous will flourish like the palm.  
**Verse:** It is good to give thanks to the Lord.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] There: Verse, “To proclaim.”]**  
**Offertory:** Glory and honor.  
**Communion:** You placed, O Lord.

### Feast of Saint Matthew

**Antiphon:** The mouth of the righteous will meditate on wisdom, and his tongue will speak judgment; the law of his God is in his heart.  
**Psalm:** Do not be jealous of evildoers, nor envy those who commit iniquity.  
**Psalm:** Blessed is the man who fears the Lord.  
**Verse:** His offspring will be mighty on the earth.  
**Alleluia:** I have found David.  
**Offertory:** You placed, O Lord.  
**Verse 1:** The desire of his soul.  
**Verse 2:** Great is his glory.  
**Communion:** Great is his glory.  
**Psalm:** Psalm 20.

**[Note: [Col. 0705D] Absent from the Compendium and from the Blandinian Codex, as Pamelius observes.]**

### Feast of Saint Maurice

[Col. 0705D]

**Antiphon:** Let it enter your presence, O Lord.  
**Psalm:** O God, the nations have entered your inheritance.  
**Responsory:** Glorious is God.  
**Verse:** Your right hand, O Lord.  
**Alleluia:** The saints will exult in [Col. 0706A] glory.  
**Offertory:** Rejoice in the Lord.  
**Communion:** They set the mortal remains.

[711]

### Feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian

**Antiphon:** Let the peoples recount the wisdom of the saints.  
**Psalm:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.  
**Responsory:** The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them.  
**Verse:** The Lord is near.  
**Alleluia:** Your saints, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** They will glory.  
**Communion:** They set the mortal remains.

### Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Michael

**Antiphon:** Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word, obeying the voice of his commands.  
**Psalm:** Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless his holy name.  
**Responsory:** Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word.  
**Verse:** Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all my inward parts, bless his holy name. [Col. 0706B]  
**Alleluia:** Praise the Lord, all his angels; praise him, all his powers.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] This Alleluia is lacking in the Compendium.]**  
**Alleluia:** I will confess to you, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** I will sing praise to you before the angels.  
**Verse 1:** I will confess to you, O Lord.  
**Verse 2:** Let all the kings of the earth confess to you, O Lord.  
**[Note: [Col. 0705D] There: Offertory, “The angel stood beside the altar of the temple, holding a golden censer in his hand; and much incense was given to him, and the smoke of the fragrant offering ascended in the presence of God.” Alleluia. Verse 1: “In the presence of the angels I will sing to you, O Lord, and I will worship toward your holy temple, and I will confess your name, O Lord”; and it ascended, etc.]**  
**Communion:** Bless the Lord, all the angels of the Lord; sing a hymn and highly exalt him forever. [Col. 0706D]  
**[Note: Compendium: “Proclaim well,” and “exalt him.” At the end is added: Psalm, “Bless the Lord, all his works.”]**

### Feast of Saint Mark

**Antiphon:** Priests of God, bless the Lord.  
**Psalm:** Bless the Lord, all the works of the Lord.  
**Responsory:** I have found David.  
**Verse:** The enemy will accomplish nothing.  
**Alleluia:** Remember David.  
**[Note: [Col. 0706D] Compendium: Alleluia, “I have made a covenant,” as above.]**  
**Offertory:** My faithfulness.  
**Communion:** Blessed is the servant.

**[Note: [Col. 0706D] These two offices are Gallican; therefore they are rightly omitted in the Blandinian Codex. Pamelius.]**

### Vigil of Saints Dionysius and His Companions

[Col. 0706C]

**Antiphon:** The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, and he is their protector in time of tribulation.  
**Psalm:** Do not be jealous of evildoers.  
**Responsory:** Vindicate, O Lord.  
**Verse:** They set the mortal remains.

### Feast of Saint Dionysius

**Antiphon:** Let it enter your presence, O Lord.  
**Psalm:** O God, the nations have entered your inheritance.  
**Responsory:** Glorious is God.  
**Verse:** Your right hand, O Lord.  
**Alleluia:** Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord.  
**[Note: [Col. 0706D] Compendium: Alleluia, “The saints will exult.”]**  
**Offertory:** God is wonderful.  
**Communion:** Our soul.

### Feast of Saint Callixtus

**[Note: [Col. 0706D] Absent from the Compendium Codex.]**

**Antiphon:** His priests.  
**Psalm:** Remember, O Lord, David.  
**Responsory:** His priests.  
**Verse:** There I will cause the horn to spring forth.  
**Alleluia:** I have found David my servant.  
**Offertory:** I have found David my servant.  
**Communion:** Blessed is the servant.

### Vigil of the Apostles Simon and Jude

[Col. 0706D]

**Antiphon:** Let it enter your presence.  
**Psalm:** O God, the nations have entered your inheritance.  
**Responsory:** Vindicate, O Lord, the blood of your servants. [Col. 0707A]  
**Verse:** They set the mortal remains of your servants. [712]  
**Offertory:** The saints will exult.  
**Communion:** The souls of the righteous.

### At Mass

**Antiphon:** But to me your friends are exceedingly honored, O God; their authority has been greatly strengthened.  
**Psalm:** Lord, you have tested me and known me; you have known my sitting down and my rising up.  
**Responsory:** But to me your friends are exceedingly honored, O God; their authority has been greatly strengthened.  
**Verse:** I will count them, and they will be multiplied beyond the sand.  
**Alleluia:** Your saints, O Lord.  
**[Note: [Col. 0707C] There: Alleluia, “Exceedingly honored are your friends.”]**  
**Offertory:** Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.  
**Verse:** The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the works of his hands.  
**Communion:** You who have followed me will sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. [Col. 0707B]  
**Psalm:** As above.

### November 1 — Feast of Saint Caesarius

**Antiphon:** Confession and beauty are before him.  
**Psalm:** Sing to the Lord.  
**Responsory:** The righteous will not be shaken, because the Lord strengthens his hand.  
**Verse:** Every day he is merciful and lends, and his offspring will be in blessing.  
**[Note: [Col. 0707C] In the same manuscript, before the Offertory is assigned: Alleluia, “I have found David.” After the Offertory two verses follow, “He asked for life” and “Great is his glory.” [Col. 0707D]]**  
**Offertory:** In your strength, O Lord.  
**Communion:** Whoever wishes to come after me.  
**Psalm:** As above.

**[Note: [Col. 0707D] These two following offices, as more recent than Gregory, are omitted in the Blandinian Codex. Pamelius.]**

### Vigil of All Saints

**Antiphon:** The saints judge nations.  
**[Note: [Col. 0707D] Compendium: Antiphon, “Let the peoples recount the wisdom of the saints,” as above; Responsory, “Fear the Lord”; Verse, “Those who seek”; Alleluia, “Let the righteous feast”; Communion, “The souls of the righteous.”]**  
**Psalm:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.  
**Verse:** Glorious is God.  
**Verse:** Your right hand, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** The saints will exult in glory.  
**Communion:** But I say to you, my friends: do not fear those who persecute you.

### On the Day, at Mass

[Col. 0707C]

**Antiphon:** Let us all rejoice in the Lord, celebrating a feast in honor of all the saints, whose solemnity the angels rejoice in and praise the Son of God.  
**Psalm:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.  
**[Note: [Col. 0707D] In the Compendium Codex: Psalm, “My heart has uttered”; Responsory, “Glorious is God”; Verse, “Your right hand, O Lord.”]**  
**Responsory:** Fear the Lord, all his saints, for those who fear him lack nothing.  
**Verse:** Those who seek the Lord will lack no good thing.  
**Alleluia:** Let the righteous feast and exult before God, and let them delight in gladness.  
**[Note: [Col. 0707D] This is absent from our Compendium Codex.]**  
**Offertory:** God in his saints.  
**[Note: [Col. 0707D] Offertory, “Rejoice,” with Verse 1, “Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven,” and Verse 2, “Test the heart,” is assigned in the Compendium.]**  
**Communion:** Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.

### November 9 — Feast of the Four Crowned Martyrs

**Antiphon:** Let the groaning enter your presence, O Lord. [Col. 0708A]  
**Psalm:** O God, the nations have entered your inheritance.  
**Responsory:** Vindicate, O Lord, the blood of your servants.  
**Verse:** They set the mortal remains.  
**Alleluia:** Your saints, O Lord.  
**Offertory:** Our soul is like.  
**Communion:** They set the mortal remains.

### Feast of Saint Theodore

**Antiphon:** In your strength, O Lord.  
**Psalm:** He asked for life.  
**Responsory:** You went before him, O Lord.  
**Verse:** He asked for life.  
**Alleluia:** Blessed is the man.  
**[Note: [Col. 0707D] In the Compendium: Alleluia, “Your saints.” Offertory, “You placed, O Lord, upon his head,” etc., with the verses “The desire” and “Great is his glory.” In Theoderic everything is as noted in the printed editions, except for the Alleluia, “Blessed is the servant.”]**  
**Offertory:** Glory and honor.  
**Communion:** You placed, O Lord.

[713]

### Feast of Saint Menas

**Antiphon:** The mouth of the righteous will meditate.  
**Psalm:** Do not be jealous of evildoers.  
**[Note: [Col. 0707D] Compendium: Responsory, “I have found”; Verse, “The enemy will accomplish nothing”; Alleluia, “I have made a covenant”; Offertory, “Glory and honor.” In Theoderic: Responsory, “I have found,” as in the Compendium; the rest as in the printed editions.]**  
**Responsory:** Glory and honor.  
**Verse:** And you set him over.  
**Alleluia:** The righteous will not be shaken.  
**Offertory:** The desire of his soul.  
**Communion:** Great is his glory.

[Note: [Col. 0708C] The Blandin Codex does not have this office, for it is Gallican. PAMELIUS. This feast is found in the Compendium, but with a different office, namely: Antiphon: “He established.” Psalm: “Mercies.” Responsory: “The mouth of the righteous meditates.” Alleluia: “The Lord has chosen you.” Offertory: “My faithfulness.” Also an Offertory: “Martin therefore foresaw his death long beforehand, and told the brothers that the dissolution of his body was impending, because he judged that he was already being released.” Verse 1: “O how great the mourning of all.” Three lines are missing here. Communion: “The faithful servant.”]

On the same day, the feast of Saint Martin.

[Col. 0708B]

Antiphon: “Your priests.” Psalm: “Remember, Lord, David.” Responsory: “I have found David.” Verse: “He shall not prosper.” Alleluia: “I have made a covenant.” Offertory: “I have found David my servant.” Communion: “Lord, you delivered five talents to me.”

The feast of Saint Cecilia.

Antiphon: “I spoke of your testimonies before kings, and was not put to shame; and I meditated on your commandments, which I loved exceedingly.” Psalm: “Blessed are the undefiled in the way.” Responsory: “Hear, O daughter, and see.” Verse: “In your beauty.”

[Note: [Col. 0708D] In the Compendium: Alleluia: “Virgins shall be brought.” In the Theodoric: Alleluia: “In your beauty.”]

Offertory: “Virgins shall be offered to the king.” Communion: “Let the proud be put to shame, because they have wrongfully committed iniquity against me; but I will exercise myself in your commandments, in your ordinances, so that I may not be put to shame.”

Another: “He has done judgment and righteousness; Lord, let not the proud slander me; I was directed toward all your commandments; I hated every way of iniquity.”

The feast of Saint Clement.

[Note: [Col. 0708D] Compendium: Antiphon: “The Lord says: The words that I have put in your mouth shall not depart from your mouth; for your name is present, and your gifts shall be accepted upon my altar.”]

Antiphon: “The Lord says: If anyone keeps my testimony.” Psalm: “I will sing the mercies of the Lord forever.” Responsory: “The Lord has sworn.” Verse: “The Lord said to my Lord.” Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0708D] Compendium: Alleluia: “I have found David.” The Theodoric agrees with the printed editions; nevertheless, instead of the Psalm “Mercies,” it assigns “Lord, hear.”]

“I have made a covenant.” Offertory: “My faithfulness and my mercy are with him.” Communion: “Blessed is the servant.” Another: “Lord, five talents.” Psalm: as above.

The feast of Saint Chrysogonus.

Antiphon: “The righteous shall rejoice.” Psalm: “Hear, O God, my prayer, when I plead.” Responsory:

[Note: [Col. 0709D] Compendium: Responsory: “The righteous shall not be shaken.” Verse: “All day long.” Alleluia: “I have found David.” Offertory: “Desire.” Communion: “Whoever wishes to come.”]

“Blessed is the man.” Verse: “Powerful on earth.” Alleluia: “The righteous shall not be shaken.” Offertory: “With glory and honor.” Communion: “You have set him, Lord.”

Vigil of Saint Andrew the Apostle.

Antiphon: “The Lord, beside the Sea of Galilee, saw two brothers, Peter and Andrew, and called them: Come after me; I will make you become fishers of men.” Psalm: “The heavens declare.” Responsory: “They have been honored exceedingly.” Verse: “I will number them.” Offertory: “With glory and honor.” Communion: “Come after me,”

[Note: [Col. 0709D] Compendium: “I will make you fishers of men.”]

“I will make you become fishers of men.” Psalm: as above.

At his feast.

Antiphon: “But to me exceedingly.” Verse: “Lord, you have tested me.”

[Col. 0709B]

Responsory: “You shall appoint them princes over all the earth; they shall remember your name, Lord.” 714 Verse: “Instead of your fathers, sons have been born to you; therefore the peoples shall confess you.” Alleluia: “Your friends, O God, have been honored exceedingly; their rule has been strengthened exceedingly.” Offertory: “But to me exceedingly.” Communion: “Andrew says to his brother Simon: We have found the Messiah, which is translated ‘Christ’; and he brought him to Jesus.” Psalm: as above.

[Note: [Col. 0709D] Compendium: “At the vigil of a bishop.”]

At the ordination of a pontiff.

Antiphon: “He called upon me.” Psalm: “He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High.” Responsory: “I have found David.”

[Note: [Col. 0709D] The Compendium joins another Offertory to this one, namely, “My faithfulness.”]

Offertory: “I have found David my servant.” Communion: “The faithful and prudent servant whom the Lord appointed over his household.”

[Note: [Col. 0709D] In the Compendium: “At the feast of a bishop. Antiphon: ‘The Lord has chosen you for himself as a great priest,’ and, ‘Opening his excellent treasure, he will make you abound in all good things …’ Alleluia: ‘May the Lord send you help.’”]

At the ordination of a bishop.

[Col. 0709C]

Antiphon: “The Lord has chosen you.” Psalm: “May the Lord hear you in the day of tribulation; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you.” Responsory: “May the Lord remember all your sacrifice, and may your burnt offering be made fat.” Verse: “May he send you help from the sanctuary, and may he protect you from Zion.” Alleluia: “The Lord has chosen you.”

If it occurs in Lent: Tract: “You have granted him the desire of his soul, and have not deprived him of the will of his lips.” Offertory: “May the Lord remember.” Verse: “May the Lord hear you.” Communion:

[Note: [Col. 0709D] What is noted here and below in the printed editions is found complete in the Compendium manuscript from the opening words. Pamelius also notes that all these offices may be seen at greater length in the Roman Order, pp. 97 and following, through p. 107.]

“Oil upon the head.”

Another.

Antiphon: “As it was with Moses.” Psalm: “May the Lord hear you.” Responsory: “May the Lord send you.” Verse: “May the Lord hear you.” Alleluia: “I have made a covenant with my chosen ones; I have sworn to David my servant.” Offertory: “My faithfulness and my mercy are with him.” Communion: “We shall rejoice.”

Another.

[Col. 0710A]

Antiphon: “He has blessed you today.” Psalm: “The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and called the earth.” Responsory: “Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High.” Verse: “Gather his saints to him, those who establish his covenant over sacrifices.” Alleluia: “Grace has been poured forth.”

If it occurs in Lent: Tract: “The desire of his soul.” Offertory: “Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless his holy name.” Communion: “Go into all the world and preach the Gospel to every creature: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; but whoever does not believe will be condemned.”

At the ordination of several bishops.

Antiphon: “Gather his saints to him.” Psalm: “The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken.” Responsory: “Offer to God a sacrifice of praise.”

[Col. 0710B]

Verse: “Gather his saints to him.” Alleluia: “Your saints, Lord.” Offertory: “Bless, O my soul.” Communion: “The harvest indeed is abundant, but the laborers are few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send laborers into his harvest.”

[Note: [Col. 0710D] After these Masses the Compendium follows with a Mass for weddings.]

715 The first week after the octave of Pentecost.

Antiphon:

[Note: [Col. 0710D] Pamelius notes that Berno remembered this office in his book On Masses, chapter 5, and that it is also mentioned by the Micrologus, chapter 59.]

“Lord, I have hoped in your mercy; my heart has rejoiced in your salvation; I will sing to the Lord, who has dealt generously with me.” Psalm: “How long, Lord, will you forget me forever? How long will you turn your face from me?” Responsory: “I said: Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.” Verse: “Blessed is he who understands concerning the needy and the poor; on the evil day the Lord will deliver him.”

[Note: [Col. 0710D] This Responsory and the following Verse are absent from the Compendium. There: Alleluia: “God, a strong and patient judge.”]

Another Responsory: “Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak; heal me, Lord.” Verse: “All my bones are troubled, and my soul is greatly troubled.”

[Col. 0710C]

Alleluia: “The Lord reigns; he is clothed with beauty; the Lord is clothed with strength and has girded himself with power.” Offertory: “Attend to the voice of my prayer.” Verse 1: “Hear my words with your ears, Lord.” Verse 2: “Direct my way in your sight.” Communion: “I will recount all your wonders; I will rejoice and exult in you; I will sing to your name, O Most High.” Psalm IX.

[Note: [Col. 0710D] Perhaps “Sunday” is better read in the manuscripts here and elsewhere, instead of “week.” In the Theodoric it reads here “the third Sunday,” and thereafter the fourth, fifth, and so on. For what is called the first in the other books is the second in the Theodoric.]

The second week.

Antiphon: “The Lord became my protector and brought me out into a broad place; he saved me, because he desired me.” Psalm: “I will love you, Lord, my strength; the Lord is my firmness, my refuge, and my deliverer.” Psalm: “To the Lord, when I was in distress, I cried, and he heard me.” Verse: “Lord, deliver my soul from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue.”

Another:

[Note: [Col. 0710D] This Responsory and the following Verse are omitted in the manuscripts.]

Responsory: “Lord, our Lord, how wondrous is your name in all the earth!” Verse:

[Col. 0711A]

“For your magnificence has been exalted above the heavens.” Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0711D] In the Compendium: Alleluia: “I will love you, Lord, my strength,” and so forth.]

“God, a just, strong, and patient judge: is he angry every day?” Offertory: “Turn, Lord, and rescue my soul; save me because of your mercy.” Verse 1: “Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor chastise me in your fury.” Verse 2: “Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak; heal me, Lord, for all my bones are troubled.” Communion: “I will sing to the Lord, who has dealt generously with me, and I will sing to the name of the Lord Most High.” Psalm XII.

The third week.

Antiphon: “Look upon me and have mercy on me, Lord, for I am alone and poor; see my humiliation and my labor, and forgive all my sins, my God.” Psalm: “To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; I shall not be ashamed.”

[Col. 0711B]

Responsory: “Cast your care upon the Lord, and he himself will nourish you.” Verse: “When I cried to the Lord, he heard my voice from those who approached me.”

Another:

[Note: [Col. 0711D] This Responsory with the following Verse is absent from the manuscripts; the same should be understood of the other offices unless otherwise noted.]

Responsory: “A helper in times of trouble: let those who know you hope in you, for you will not forsake those who seek you, Lord.” Verse: “For the poor man will not be forgotten forever; the patience of the poor will not perish for ever. Arise, Lord; let man not prevail.”

Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0711D] Compendium: Alleluia: “In you, Lord, I have hoped.”]

“I will love you, Lord, my strength; the Lord is my firmness, my refuge, and my deliverer.” Offertory: “Let all who know your name hope in you, Lord, for you do not forsake those who seek you. Sing praises to the Lord, who dwells in Zion, for he has not forgotten the prayer of the poor.”

716 Verse 1: “You sit upon the throne, judging”

[Note: [Col. 0711D] Compendium: “equity.” There are many other differing readings, all of which it is not worthwhile to record.]

“justice; you rebuked the nations, and the wicked perished; you blotted out their name forever and ever; their memory perished with a roar, and the Lord remains forever. Verse 2: ‘The Lord will be known when he executes judgments; the sinner has been caught in the works of his hands.’” Communion: “I cried out, for you heard me, O God; incline your ear to me and hear my words.” Psalm: “Hear, Lord, my justice.”

The fourth week.

Antiphon: “The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid? My enemies who afflict me have grown weak and fallen.” Psalm: “The same. Though armies encamp against me, my heart will not fear.” Responsory: “Be gracious, Lord, to our sins, lest the nations should ever say: Where is their God?” Verse: “Help us, O God our Savior, and for the honor of your name, Lord, deliver us.”

Another Responsory: “Arise, Lord; let man not prevail; let the nations be judged in your sight.” Verse: “When my enemy turns backward, they will grow weak and perish before your face, for you have executed my judgment and my cause.”

[Note: [Col. 0712D] In the Compendium: Alleluia: “All nations, clap your hands.”]

Alleluia:

[Col. 0712A]

“Praise the Lord, O my soul; I will praise the Lord in my life; I will sing to my God as long as I am.” Offertory: “Enlighten my eyes, lest I ever sleep in death, lest my enemy should ever say: I have prevailed against him.” Verse 2: “Look upon me and hear me, Lord my God.” Communion: “The Lord is my firmness, my refuge, and my deliverer, my God, my helper.” Psalm X.

The fifth week.

Antiphon: “Hear, Lord, my voice with which I have cried to you; be my helper; do not forsake me or despise me, O God my Savior.” Psalm: “The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?” Responsory: “Look upon us, our protector, O God, and look upon your servants.” Verse: “Lord God of hosts, hear the prayers of your servants.”

Another Responsory: “Cleanse me, Lord, from my hidden faults, and spare your servant from those belonging to others.” Verse: “If they do not rule over me, then I shall be undefiled, and I shall be cleansed from the greatest offense.”

Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0712D] There: Alleluia: “A hymn befits you, O God, in Zion.”]

“In you, Lord, I have hoped; I shall not be put to shame forever.” Offertory: “I will bless the Lord, who has given me understanding; I kept God always before me, for he is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.” Verse 1: “Preserve me, Lord; I said to the Lord: You are my God, for you have no need of my goods.” Verse 2: “You have made known to me the paths of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence; delights are at your right hand forever.” Communion: “One thing I have asked of the Lord, this I will seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.” Psalm XXXII.

717 The sixth week.

[Col. 0712C]

Antiphon: “The Lord is the strength of his people and the protector of the salvations of his Christ. Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance, and rule them forever.” Psalm: “To you, Lord, I will cry; my God, do not be silent toward me, lest you ever be silent toward me and I become like those descending into the pit.”

Responsory: “Return, Lord, for a little while, and have compassion upon your servants.” Verse: “Lord, you have been our refuge from generation to generation.”

Another Responsory: “One thing I have asked of the Lord, this I will seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.” Verse: “That I may see the will of the Lord and be protected in his holy temple.”

[Note: [Col. 0712D] Compendium: Alleluia: “Attend, my people, to my law.”]

Alleluia: “All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation.” Offertory: “Perfect my steps in your paths, so that my footsteps may not be moved; incline your ear and hear my words; make your mercies wonderful, you who save those who hope in you, Lord.” Verse 1: “Hear, Lord, my justice; attend to my supplication.” Verse 2: “Guard me, Lord, as the apple of the eye; protect me beneath the shadow of your wings from the face of the wicked who have afflicted me.” Verse 3: “But I shall appear in your sight with righteousness; I shall be satisfied when your glory appears.” Communion: “I will go around and offer in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation; I will sing and recite a psalm to the Lord.” Psalm XXVI.

The seventh week.

This week is not in the Roman Antiphonary.

Antiphon:

[Note: [Col. 0713D] This Sunday is marked in the Compendium, Vallicellian manuscript, and others. But in the Theodoric the office of this Sunday is assigned to the eighth Sunday, and the office of the eighth Sunday to the ninth. The sequence continues in the same way.]

“All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation.” Psalm:

[Note: [Col. 0713D] In the Compendium: “The people subjected to us.”]

“For the Lord is Most High, terrible, a great King over all the earth.” Responsory: “Come, children, hear me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.” Verse: “Approach him and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be put to shame.”

Another Responsory: “Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord has chosen as his inheritance.” Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0713D] There: Alleluia: “Exult in God our helper,” and so forth.]

“Deliver me from my enemies,” and so forth. Offertory:

[Note: [Col. 0713D] Berno notes the agreement of this Offertory with the reading for the seventh Sunday after the octave of Pentecost, in his book On Masses. Also with the prayer “O God, whose providence,” in the same place and in the Micrologus, chapter 61. Pamelius.]

“As with the holocaust of rams and bulls, and as with thousands of fattened lambs, so may our sacrifice be today in your sight, that it may please you, because there is no shame for those who trust in you, Lord.” Verse: “And now we follow you with our whole heart, and fear you, and seek your face, Lord; do not put us to shame, but deal with us according to your gentleness and according to the multitude of your mercy, because there is no shame for those who trust in you, Lord.” Communion: “Incline your ear to me; hasten to deliver me.” Psalm XXX.

The eighth week.

Antiphon: “We have received your mercy, O God, in the midst of your temple; according to your name, O God, so also is your praise to the ends of the earth; your right hand is full of righteousness.” Psalm: “Great is the Lord and exceedingly praiseworthy in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.”

Responsory:

[Note: [Col. 0714D] Compendium: Responsory: “Be to me.” Verse: “God, in you I hope.” Alleluia: “Lord God of my salvation.”]

“You have delivered us, Lord, from those afflicting us, and you have put to shame those who hate us.” Verse: “In God we shall be praised all day long, and we shall confess your name forever.”

718 Responsory: “Be to me a God who protects and a place of refuge, so that you may save me.” Verse: “God, in you I have hoped, Lord; I shall not be put to shame forever.” Alleluia: “A hymn befits you, O God, in Zion, and to you a vow shall be paid in Jerusalem.” Verse: “We shall be filled with the good things of your house; holy is your temple, wondrous in equity.” Offertory: “You will save the humble people, Lord, and you will humble the eyes of the proud, for who is God besides you, Lord?” Verse 1: “My deliverer from wrathful nations; you will exalt me above those rising against me; you will rescue me from the unjust man.” Verse 2: “My cry.” Communion: “Taste and see that the Lord is sweet. Blessed is the man who hopes in him.” Psalm: “I will bless the Lord.”

The ninth week.

Antiphon: “Behold, God is my helper, and the Lord is the upholder of my soul. Turn the evils upon my enemies; in your truth”

[Note: [Col. 0714D] Compendium: “Scatter them.”]

“scatter them, my protector, Lord.”

[Col. 0714A]

Psalm: “O God, save me by your name, and judge me by your strength.”

[Note: [Col. 0714D] Compendium: Responsory: “Lord, our Lord.” Verse: “For your magnificence has been exalted,” and so forth. The Theodoric agrees.]

Responsory: “Be to me a God who protects and a place of refuge, so that you may save me.” Verse: “God, in you I have hoped.”

Another Responsory: “Beautiful in form beyond the sons of men, grace has been poured forth upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.” Verse: “My heart has uttered a good word; I speak my works to the King.”

Alleluia: “Attend, my people, to my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth.” Offertory: “The judgments of the Lord are right, gladdening hearts, and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb; for your servant also keeps them.” Verse 1: “The commandment of the Lord is bright, enlightening the eyes; the fear of the Lord is holy, enduring forever; the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.” Verse 2: “And may the words of my mouth be pleasing, and the meditation of my heart always in your sight.” Communion: “Seek first the kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you, says the Lord.” Psalm: as above.

The tenth week.

Antiphon: “When I cried to the Lord, he heard my voice from those who approached me, and he humbled them who is before the ages and remains forever. Cast your care upon the Lord, and he himself will nourish you.” Psalm: “Hear, O God, my prayer, and do not despise my supplication; attend to me and hear me.”

Responsory:

[Note: [Col. 0714D] The Theodoric and the Compendium have: Responsory: “Guard me, Lord.” Verse: “From your face.”]

“Lord, our Lord, how wondrous is your name in all the earth.” Verse: “For your magnificence has been exalted above the heavens.”

Another Responsory: “Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who alone performs great wonders from of old.” Verse: “Let the mountains receive peace for your people, and the hills righteousness.”

[Note: [Col. 0714D] In the Compendium: Alleluia: “Come, let us exult, Lord.”]

Alleluia: “Exult in God our helper; shout joyfully to the God of Jacob; take up a pleasing psalm with the harp.” Offertory: “To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; I shall not be put to shame; nor may my enemies mock me, for all who await you shall not be put to shame.” Communion: “You will accept the sacrifice of righteousness, offerings and holocausts upon your altar, Lord.” Psalm L.

719 The eleventh week.

Antiphon: “God in his holy place, God who makes those of one mind dwell in a house, he himself will give strength and power to his people.” Psalm: “Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his face.”

[Note: [Col. 0714D] In the Theodoric and the Compendium: Responsory: “In God my heart has hoped, and I was helped,” and so forth. Verse: “To you, Lord, I will cry.”]

Responsory: “Guard me, Lord, as the apple of the eye.” Verse: “Let my judgment proceed from your face; let your eyes see equity.”

Another Responsory: “Let the nations know that God is your name; you alone are the Most High over all the earth.” Verse: “My God, set them like a wheel and like stubble before the face of the wind.”

[Note: [Col. 0715D] Compendium: Alleluia: “For God is great, Lord.” In the Compendium and Theodoric: Responsory: “I will bless the Lord at all times,” and so forth. Verse: “In the Lord my soul shall praise,” and so forth. This agrees with Pamelius’s observation concerning the office of this Sunday; for he says that Berno remembered this office and cites the Responsory “I will bless the Lord,” and so forth.]

Alleluia: “Lord God of my salvation, by day I cried and by night before you.” Offertory: “I will exalt you, Lord, because you have received me, and have not gladdened my enemies over me. Lord, I cried to you, and you healed me.” Verse: “Lord, you brought my soul up from the underworld; you saved me from those descending into the pit.” Communion: “Honor the Lord from your substance and from the firstfruits of your crops, so that your granaries may be filled with abundance and your winepresses overflow with wine.” Psalm: as above.

The twelfth week.

Antiphon: “O God, attend to my help; Lord, hasten to help me; let my enemies who seek my soul be put to shame and confounded.” Psalm: “Let those who wish me evil be turned backward and put to shame.”

Responsory: “In God my heart has hoped, and I was helped; my flesh has flourished again, and according to my will I will confess to him.” Verse: “To you, Lord, I cried; my God, do not be silent; do not depart from me.”

Another Responsory: “Our protector.” Verse: “Lord God of hosts.”

[Note: [Col. 0715D] Why does this Sunday lack an Alleluia? Certainly the Compendium assigns: Alleluia: “The Lord reigns, clothed in beauty,” and the Theodoric: “Lord, you have been our refuge.”]

Offertory: “Moses prayed in the sight of the Lord his God and said: Why, Lord, are you angry with your people? Spare the wrath of your heart. Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to whom you swore that you would give a land flowing with milk and honey. And the Lord was appeased concerning the evil which he had said he would do to his people.”

Verse: “The Lord said to Moses: You have found grace in my sight, and I know you above all others. And Moses hastened, bowed to the earth, and worshiped, saying: I know that you are merciful to thousands, taking away iniquity and sins. Moses and Aaron said to the whole assembly of the children of Israel: Draw near before God. The majesty of the Lord appeared in the cloud, and he heard your murmuring in due time.”

Communion: “The earth shall be satisfied with the fruit of your works, Lord, so that you may bring forth bread from the earth, and wine may gladden the heart of man; so that he may brighten his face with oil, and bread may strengthen the heart of man.” Psalm CIII.

The thirteenth week.

Antiphon: “Look upon your covenant, Lord, and do not forsake the souls of your poor forever. Arise, Lord, and judge your cause, and do not forget the voices of those who seek you.” Psalm: “Why, O God, have you rejected us forever? Is your anger enraged against the sheep of your pasture?”

Responsory:

[Note: [Col. 0715D] The Compendium and Theodoric: Responsory: “Look upon us, Lord.” Verse: “Arise, Lord, and judge your cause.”]

“I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise shall always be in my mouth.” 720

[Col. 0715D]

Verse: “In the Lord my soul shall be praised; let the meek hear and rejoice.”

Another Responsory: “Return, Lord, for a little while, and have compassion upon your servants.” Verse: “Lord, you have been our refuge from generation to generation.”

Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0716D] It is absent from the Compendium. In the Theodoric the Alleluia is “Come, let us exult, Lord.”]

“The Lord reigns, in beauty.”

[Col. 0716A]

Offertory: “In you I have hoped, Lord; I said: You are my God. In your hands are my times.” Verse 1: “Make your face shine upon your servant, and save the son of your handmaid.” Verse 2: “How great is the abundance of your sweetness, Lord, which you have stored up for those who fear you.” Communion: “You have given us bread from heaven, Lord, having every delight and every taste of sweetness.” Psalm: as above.

The fourteenth week.

Antiphon: “Look upon us, our protector, O God, and look upon the face of your Christ, because one day in your courts is better than thousands.” Psalm: “How beloved are your dwellings, Lord of hosts? My soul longs for and languishes for the courts of the Lord.”

Responsory:

[Note: [Col. 0716D] In the Compendium: Responsory: “It is good to trust in the Lord.” Verse: “It is good to hope.” In the Theodoric the Responsory is the same, but the Verse is “For proclaiming.”]

“Look upon your covenant, Lord, and do not forget the souls of your poor forever.” Verse: “Arise, Lord; judge your cause; remember the reproach of your servants.”

Another Responsory: “Lord, hear my prayer.”

Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0716D] In the Compendium: Alleluia: “Confess to the Lord.” In the Theodoric: Alleluia: “For God is great.”]

“Come, let us exult in the Lord; let us shout joyfully to God our salvation.” Verse: “Let us go before his face in confession, and let us shout joyfully to him in psalms.” Offertory: “The Lord will send an angel around those who fear him, and he will rescue them. Taste and see that the Lord is sweet.” Communion: “The bread that I will give is my flesh for the life of the world.” Psalm: as above.

The fifteenth week.

Antiphon: “Incline your ear to me, Lord, and hear me; save your servant, my God, who hopes in you; have mercy on me, Lord, for I have cried to you all day.” Psalm: “Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul.”

Responsory: “It is good to confess to the Lord and sing to your name, O Most High.” Verse: “To proclaim your mercy in the morning and your truth throughout the night.”

Another Responsory: “The nations shall fear your name, Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory.” Verse: “For the Lord has built Zion, and he will be seen in his majesty.”

Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0716D] Compendium: Alleluia: “My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready; I will sing and recite a psalm in my glory.” The Theodoric: Alleluia: “The Lord reigns.”]

“For God is a great Lord, and a great King over all the earth.” Offertory: “Waiting, I waited for the Lord, and he looked upon me and heard my supplication; and he put a new song into my mouth, a hymn to our God.” Communion: “Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him, says the Lord.” Psalm: as

[Col. 0716D]

above.

The sixteenth week.

Antiphon: “Have mercy on me, Lord, for I have cried to you all day; for you, Lord, are sweet and gentle, and abundant in mercy to all who call upon you.” Psalm: “Incline your ear to me, Lord, and hear me, for I am needy and poor.”

721 Responsory:

[Note: [Col. 0717D] The Compendium and Theodoric: Responsory: “The nations shall fear.” Verse: “For he has built.”]

“It is good to trust in the Lord rather than to trust in man.” Verse: “It is good to hope in the Lord rather than to hope in princes.”

Another Responsory: “The Lord sent his word.” Verse: “Let them confess to the Lord.”

[Note: [Col. 0717D] Compendium: Alleluia: “Those who fear the Lord hope in him; he is their helper and protector.” The Theodoric: Alleluia: “Confess to the Lord.”]

Alleluia: “The Lord reigns; let the earth rejoice; let the many islands be glad.” Offertory: “Lord, look to my help. Let those who seek my soul to take it be put to shame and confounded. Lord, look to my help.” Verse: “Let those who wish me evil be turned backward and put to shame.” Communion: “Lord, I will remember your righteousness alone. God, you have taught me from my youth, and even to old age and gray hairs; God, do not forsake me.” Psalm LXX.

The seventeenth week.

[Col. 0717B]

Antiphon: “You are righteous, Lord, and your judgment is right. Deal with your servant according to your mercy.” Psalm: “Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.”

Responsory:

[Note: [Col. 0717D] According to the Compendium, the Responsory is “He desired life,” and the Verse, “That I may see.” But in the Theodoric the Responsory is “Blessed is the nation,” and the Verse, “By the word of the Lord.”]

“The nations shall fear.” Verse: “For he has built.”

Another Responsory: “It is good to trust in the Lord.” Verse: “It is good to hope.”

Alleluia:

[Note: [Col. 0717D] The Compendium and Theodoric assign as Alleluia: “Praise the Lord, all nations.”]

“Shout joyfully to God, all the earth; serve the Lord with gladness.” Offertory: “I, Daniel, prayed to my God, saying: Hear, Lord, the prayers of your servant; make your face shine upon your sanctuary, and graciously look upon this people over whom your name has been invoked, O God.” Verse 1: “While I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel.” Verse 2: “I heard a voice saying to me: Daniel, understand the words that I speak to you, for I have been sent to you; indeed, Michael has come to my aid.” Communion: “Vow and pay your vows to the Lord your God, all you who around him bring offerings, to the terrible one and to him who takes away the breath of princes, terrible to all the kings of the earth.” Psalm: “God is known in Judah.”

Wednesday of the seventh month. At Saint Mary’s.

[Note: [Col. 0717D] The Micrologus, chapter 28, mentions these three offices of the fast of the seventh month. PAMELIUS.]

Antiphon: “Rejoice in God our helper; shout joyfully to the God of Jacob; take up a pleasing psalm with the harp; sound the trumpet at the beginning of the month, because it is a commandment in Israel and an ordinance of the God of Jacob.”” Psalm: “He established it as a testimony in Joseph when he went out from the land of Egypt.”

Responsory: “Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high and looks upon the humble in heaven and on earth?” Verse: “Raising the needy from the earth and lifting the poor from the dung heap.”

Responsory:

[Col. 0717D]

[Note: [Col. 0717D] This Responsory is absent from the Compendium.]

“Tribulations.”

Offertory: “I meditated on your commandments, which I loved exceedingly, and I will lift up my hands to your commandments, which I loved.” Verse 1: “The Lord is my portion.” Verse 2:

[Col. 0718A]

“Have mercy on me according to your word.” Communion: “Eat rich foods and drink sweet wine, and send portions to those who have prepared nothing for themselves; for the day of the Lord is holy. Do not grieve, for the joy of the Lord is our strength.” Psalm: as above.

Friday. Station

[Note: [Col. 0717D] Compendium, simply: “At the Apostles.”]

at the holy twelve Apostles.

Antiphon: “Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice, and be strengthened; seek his face always.” Psalm: “Confess to the Lord”

722 “and invoke his name; proclaim his works among the nations.” Responsory: “Return, Lord, for a little while, and have compassion upon your servants.” Verse: “Lord, you have been our refuge from generation to generation.” Offertory: “Bless the Lord, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits; and your youth shall be renewed like that of the eagle.”” Verse: “The Lord is in heaven.” Communion: “Take away from me reproach and contempt, because I have sought your commandments, Lord; for your testimonies are also my meditation.” Psalm: “Blessed are the undefiled in the way.”

Saturday, with twelve readings, at Saint Peter’s.

Antiphon:

[Note: [Col. 0718D] The Blandin Codex has nothing else here except the Antiphon, Offertory, and Communion, as if indicating that the same Responsories should be read here which are given above for the fast of the first month, namely, “Be gracious,” “Our protector,” “Let my prayer be directed,” and “Save your people,” which the Micrologus, chapter 28, considers should be repeated here. Therefore we have enclosed within lines the new Responsories which the Utrecht Codex records, as being less authoritative. PAMELIUS.]

“Come, let us worship God, and fall down before the Lord; let us weep before him who made us, for he is the Lord our God.” Psalm: “Come, let us exult in the Lord; let us shout joyfully to God our salvation.”

[Responsory: “I said: Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.” Verse: “Blessed is he who understands concerning the needy and the poor; on the evil day the Lord will deliver him.” Responsory: “The nations shall fear.” Verse: “For he has built.” Responsory: “It is good to trust in the Lord.” Verse: “It is good to hope in the Lord.” Responsory:

[Col. 0718C]

“You have delivered us, Lord.” Verse: “In God we shall be praised.”]

[Note: [Col. 0718D] This hymn is not in the Compendium, which nevertheless contains the other items that Pamelius considers less authoritative.]

Hymn: “Blessed are you, Lord.” Tract: “Praise the Lord, all nations.”

Offertory: “Lord, God of my salvation, by day I have cried and by night before you; let my prayer enter into your sight, Lord.” Communion: “In the seventh month you shall celebrate feasts, when I made the children of Israel dwell in tabernacles, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.” Psalm: as above.

The eighteenth week.

Antiphon. Grant peace, Lord, to those who wait for you, so that your faithful prophets may be found true; hear the prayers of your servant and of your people Israel.

Psalm. I loved, because the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer.

Response. I rejoiced in what was said to me: “We shall go into the house of the Lord.”

Verse. May peace be within your stronghold, and abundance within your towers.

Alleluia.  
[Note: In the *Compendium*, the Alleluia is “The right hand of the Lord has acted with power.”]

“Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name; proclaim his works among the nations.”

Offertory. Moses sanctified an altar to the Lord, offering burnt offerings upon it; and, sacrificing victims, he made an evening sacrifice as a sweet odor to the Lord God, in the sight of the children of Israel.

Verse 1. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Come up to me on Mount Sinai, and stand upon its summit.” Moses rose and climbed the mountain where God had appointed him; and the Lord descended to him in a cloud and stood before him. When Moses saw him, he fell down and worshiped, saying: “I beseech you, Lord, forgive the sins of your people.” And the Lord said to him: “I will do according to your word.”

Verse 2. Moses prayed to the Lord and said: “If I have found favor in your sight, show yourself plainly to me, that I may see you.” And the Lord spoke to him, saying: “For no human being shall see me and live. But stand upon the height of the rock, and my right hand shall cover you until I pass by. When I have passed by, I shall remove my hand, and then you shall see my glory. But my face shall not be seen by you, because I am God who displays wonders upon the earth.”

At Communion. Take up offerings and enter his courts; worship the Lord in his holy hall. Psalm 95.

## The Nineteenth Week

[Note: See also Berno, in the place cited, for the correspondence of this office with the reading for the Nineteenth Sunday and with the prayer “Almighty and merciful God, who have made all things,” etc. PAMEL.]

Antiphon. I am the salvation of the people, says the Lord. In whatever tribulation they cry out to me, I shall hear them, and I shall be their Lord forever.

Psalm. Hearken, my people, to my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth.  
[Note: In the *Compendium*, the Psalm is “Blessed are the undefiled.”]

Response.  
[Note: This Response and the following Verse are not found in the *Compendium* or in Theodoricus; instead they have the Response “Let my prayer be directed,” and the Verse “The lifting up.”]

I rejoiced in what was said to me: “We shall go into the house of the Lord.”

Verse. May peace be within your stronghold, and abundance within your towers.

Another Response. Let my prayer be directed like incense in your sight, O Lord.

Verse. The lifting up of my hands is an evening sacrifice.

[Note: In the *Compendium*, in place of the assigned Alleluia is “I rejoiced”; in Theodoricus: “I shall confess.”]

Alleluia. My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready; I shall sing and make melody to you in my glory.

Offertory. If I walk in the midst of tribulation, you will revive me, O Lord, and against the anger of my enemies you will stretch out your hand, and your right hand has saved me.

Verse 1. On whatever day I call upon you, hear me; you will multiply strength in my soul.

Verse 2. I shall worship toward your holy temple, and I shall confess to your name.

At Communion. You commanded that your commandments be kept exceedingly; would that my ways were directed toward keeping your statutes! Psalm 118.

## The Twentieth Week

[Col. 0719D] Antiphon. All that you have done to us, O Lord, you have done in true judgment, because we have sinned against you and have not obeyed your commandments; but give glory to your name, and deal with us according to the multitude of your mercies.

Psalm. Blessed are the undefiled in the way.

Response. The eyes of all hope in you, O Lord, and you give them food at the proper time.

Verse. You open your hand, and you fill every living creature with blessing.

Another Response. Deliver me, O Lord, from my enemies.

Verse. My deliverer.

Alleluia.  
[Note: In the *Compendium*: “Out of the depths.” In Theodoricus: “I shall confess to you.”]

The Lord sent redemption to his people; he commanded his covenant forever.

Offertory. Beside the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down and wept when we remembered you, O Zion.

Verse 1. If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand be forgotten.

Verse 2. Remember, O Lord, the sons of Edom on the day of Jerusalem.

At Communion. Remember your word to your servant, O Lord, in which you gave me hope; this has comforted me in my lowliness. Psalm 118, as above.

## The Twenty-First Week

Antiphon. All things are placed in your will, O Lord, and there is no one who can resist your will; for you made all things, heaven and earth, and all that is contained within the circuit of heaven.  
[Note: The *Compendium* adds: “You are Lord of all.”]

Psalm. Blessed are the undefiled.

Response. Lord, you have become our refuge from generation to generation.

Verse. Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world were formed, from age to age you are God.

[Note: In Theodoricus the Alleluia is “Praise the Lord, O my soul.” In the *Compendium*: “I shall confess to you, O Lord.”]

Alleluia. Praise the Lord, servants; praise the name of the Lord.

Verse. May the name of the Lord be blessed, from this time forth and forever.

[Note: Alcuin, p. 70, and Amalarius, book III, chapter 39, make very beautiful mention of this Offertory with its Verses, and also of the Antiphon. PAMEL.]

Offertory. There was a man in the land named Job, simple and upright and fearing God. Satan asked to test him, and power was given him by the Lord over his possessions and his flesh. He destroyed all his substance and his children, and he wounded his flesh with a grievous sore.

Verse 1. Would that my sins were weighed, would that my sins were weighed, by which I deserved wrath, by which I deserved wrath, and the calamity, the calamity, the calamity that I suffer would appear the heavier.

Verse 2. For what is my strength, what is my strength, what is my strength, that I should endure? Or what is my end, that I should act patiently?

Verse 3. Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh bronze? Or is my flesh bronze?

Verse 4. For, for, for my eye shall not return, that I may see good things, that I may see good things, that I may see good things, that I may see good things, that I may see good things, that I may see good things, that I may see good things, that I may see good things, that I may see good things.

At Communion. My soul has failed in expectation of your salvation, and I have hoped in your word. When will you execute judgment upon those who persecute me? The wicked have persecuted me; help me, O Lord my God. Psalm as above.

## The Twenty-Second Week

Antiphon. If you observe iniquities, O Lord, O Lord, who shall endure? For with you there is forgiveness, O God of Israel.

Psalm. From the depths I have cried to you, O Lord, O Lord, hear my voice.

Response. Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together.

Verse. Like ointment upon the head, which runs down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron.

Verse.  
[Note: This Verse is absent from the *Compendium*.]

The Lord has commanded blessing and life forever.

[Note: In the *Compendium*: Alleluia, “Praise the Lord, O my soul.” In Theodoricus: “Who heals the contrite.” Berno, *On the Mass*, book I, chapter 5, is cited by Pamelius for the correspondence of this office with the reading and the prayer “God our refuge.” Micrologus, in its final chapter, teaches that this office is to be repeated if several Sundays occur, but in such a way that the following office is always said on the Sunday immediately preceding Advent.]

Alleluia. Let those who fear the Lord hope in him; he is their helper and protector.

Offertory. Remember me, O Lord, you whose omnipotence rules; give a proper and well-sounding word to my mouth, so that my words may please the prince.

Verse. Turn his heart into hatred of those who oppose us, and of those who agree with them. But deliver us by your hand, O our God, forever.

At Communion. I tell you: there is joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents. Psalm as above.

## The Twenty-Third Week

Antiphon. The Lord says: “I contemplate thoughts of peace and not of affliction; you shall call upon me, and I shall hear you, and I shall bring back your captivity from every place.”

Psalm. You have blessed your land, O Lord; you have turned away the captivity of Jacob.

[Note: This Response and the following Verse are not found in Theodoricus or in the *Compendium*.]

Response. The nations shall fear.

Verse. For he has built.

Another Response. You have delivered us, O Lord, from those who afflict us, and you have put to shame those who hate us.

Verse. In God we shall praise all day long, and we shall confess to your name forever.

[Note: In the *Compendium*: Alleluia, “They shall be praised.” In Theodoricus: “Who established.”]

Alleluia. I loved, because the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer.

Offertory. From the depths I have cried to you, O Lord, O Lord, hear my voice.

Verse 1. Let your ears be attentive to the prayer of your servant.

Verse 2. If you observe iniquities, O Lord, O Lord, who shall endure?

At Communion. Amen, I say to you: whatever you ask for when you pray, believe that you shall receive it, and it shall be done for you.

Psalm. From the depths.

## On the Most Holy Trinity

[Note: It is sufficiently established from Micrologus, chapter 60, that this office is not Gregorian but was composed by Albinus and Stephen of Liège. PAMEL. It is found in Theodoricus and in the *Compendium*, which appears to be of the same period as Stephen of Liège.]

Antiphon. Blessed be the holy Trinity and undivided unity; we shall confess to it, because it has shown us its mercy.

Psalm. Let us bless the Father and the Son with the Holy Spirit; let us praise and exalt him above all forever.

Response. Blessed are you, O Lord, who behold the depths and sit above the cherubim.

Verse. Bless the God of heaven.

Alleluia. Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers, and worthy of praise forever.

Offertory. Blessed be God the Father, and the only-begotten Son of God, and also the Holy Spirit, because he has shown us his mercy.

Verse. Let us bless the Father and the Son with the Holy Spirit; let us praise and exalt him above all forever.

At Communion. Bless the God of heaven, and confess him before all the living, because he has shown us his mercy.

[Note: In Theodoricus, after the Second Sunday, on which the office of the Trinity is celebrated, another Sunday is still noted, followed by five Sundays before the Lord’s Nativity. Afterwards the Mass for a dedication is read.]

[Note: What follows is absent from the *Compendium* manuscript.]

## For Travelers

Antiphon. Blessed be the Lord God.

Psalm. Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his presence.

Response. If I walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, because you are with me, O Lord.

Verse. Your rod and your staff themselves have comforted me.

Response. Deliver me from my enemies, O my God, and free me from those who rise up against me.

Verse. My deliverer from wrathful nations.

Offertory. Perfect my steps in your paths, so that my footsteps may not be moved.

Verse. Direct my steps according to your word, and let no iniquity rule over me.

At Communion. You commanded that your commandments be kept exceedingly. Would that my ways were directed toward keeping your statutes!

## In the Office for the Dead

Antiphon. Grant them eternal rest, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.

Psalm. A hymn befits you, O God, in Zion, and to you a vow shall be rendered in Jerusalem; hear my prayer; all flesh shall come to you.

Response. Grant them eternal rest, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.

Verse. May his soul dwell among good things, and may his offspring inherit the earth.

Offertory. Deliver their souls, O Lord, from every bond of sin, so that they may deserve to be raised among your saints in the glory of the resurrection.

Verse. We earnestly ask your mercy, most merciful God and Father, that you may deign to grant them pleasant and peaceful dwelling places.

At Communion. I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: “Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord; from now on the Spirit says that they may rest from their labors.” For their works follow them.

## Another

Antiphon. Come to his aid, saints of God; hasten to meet him, angels of the Lord, receiving his soul and presenting it before the Most High.

Psalm. May his soul dwell among good things, and may his offspring inherit the earth.

Response. Return, my soul, to your rest, because the Lord has dealt bountifully with you.

Verse. For he has delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from falling.

Offertory. Have mercy on me, O God, according to—

Verse 1. For my iniquity I myself—

Verse 2. Against you alone I have sinned.

Another Offertory. The right hand of the Lord has acted with power; the right hand of the Lord has exalted me. I shall not die, but live, and I shall recount the works of the Lord.

Verse 1. In my tribulation I called upon the Lord, and the Lord heard me in an open place.

Verse 2. I was pushed and overturned so as to fall, but the Lord received me.

Another Offertory. Turn, O Lord, and deliver my soul; save me for the sake of your mercy.

Verse 1. O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor correct me in your wrath.

Verse 2. Have mercy on me, O Lord, because I am weak; heal me, O Lord, because all my bones are troubled.

At Communion. I am the resurrection and the life, says the Lord. Whoever believes in me, even if he has died, shall live.

Offertory. As in a burnt offering.

Response. Bless the Lord.

Offertory. In the sight of the angels.

Antiphon. O Wisdom.

Antiphon. Lord God of our fathers.

Alleluia. The charity of God.

At Communion. The charity of God.
