Antiphon. But for us to glory.  
Psalm. The Lord reigns; he is clothed in splendor.  
Response. Christ became obedient.  
Verse. Because of which—  
Alleluia. The Lord has reigned from the wood.  
Offertory. For God established—  
At Communion. But we—

### Saturday, of Virgins

Antiphon. They shall entreat your countenance.  
Psalm. My heart has uttered.  
Response. Grace has been poured forth.  
Verse. Because of truth.  
Alleluia. In your beauty.  
Offertory. Grace has been poured forth.  
At Communion. You have loved.

Rejoice, hail, O unique, beautiful dove.

The bride joined to the heavenly king; blessed always is the pious Virgin Mary, Mother of God.

[Note: These lines are written out with musical notation for the modulation of the chant. We judged them worthy of publication because the date of the manuscript can be deduced from them, as we stated in the preface.]

A splendid day lies before us, which the returning course of time brings around. This solemnity is the festival of our soul, rightly to be venerated. Let us celebrate it with a resounding tongue, singing aloud the praises due to the Lord. Let us rejoice in it with a devout heart, entreating the Lord with a pure mind to wipe away our sins with his hand. Thus freed, let us sing psalms in the heights. May supreme and holy grace preserve and guard our bodies.

O God, free us from the fierce Norman people, who lay waste our kingdoms. They slaughter old men and young men, virgins and also bands of children. We beseech you, repel every evil from us. Turn us, we beg, as suppliants toward you, O Lord, King of glory; you are true peace, holy salvation, hope and steadfastness. Grant us peace and concord. Bestow upon us hope and complete faith; grant us together true and continual charity, and perfection. By the prayers of the saints, may we be helped to obtain these things. We rejoice in their glorious passion. May the greatest praise, peace, and glory be given through all ages to the Trinity. Amen.

[Note: Afterwards begins: “The Alleluias of the yearly cycle,” seventy-nine in number. Then follow the Antiphons in the Greater Litany; Antiphons for every kind of tribulation, for drought, for excessive rain, for mortality; Antiphons for wartime, for deliverance, and for penitents. They include thanksgivings for deliverance; then Antiphons for the feasts of the saints, Antiphons for the carrying of relics, Antiphons for the Passion of the Lord, and Antiphons for the Resurrection.]

# [THE RESPONSAL.]

## PRELIMINARY OBSERVATIONS ON THE COLLECTION OF RESPONSES, ANTIPHONS, VERSES, ETC.

Since we foresee that few will read this Collection, we shall not hesitate to indicate here the matters in it that seemed especially worthy of notice.

In the Compiègne manuscript this book bears no title. From its Responses it is called by some the *Responsal* (Mabillon, *On the Gallican Course*, p. 398). Amalarius calls it an *Antiphonary*, because of its Antiphons, as is clear from his book *On the Order of the Antiphonary*. Because the complete ecclesiastical office, both nocturnal and diurnal, is described in it, some have called this manuscript the *Official*. Although many have mentioned this book in various places (Amalarius, book IV, *On Ecclesiastical Offices*, chapter 29, and elsewhere), no one among the ancients has yet made the collection of Responses, Antiphons, and so forth public. We have therefore decided to bring it to light, and specifically from a very ancient manuscript, though not free from errors, so that it might serve as a kind of complement to all liturgical books. Whoever wishes to compare it with the Antiphonaries of today will be glad to observe that scarcely anything new has been introduced into our ecclesiastical books, since among the most certain marks of the Church, that which is derived from antiquity holds no last or inferior place.

For the use of which Church our Compiègne manuscript was written is obscure. Certainly, although it contains an office for Saint Benedict—which might perhaps seem to some an indication that Benedictine monks used it—in the number and arrangement of the Psalms, both for the nocturnal and the diurnal hours, and in many other matters, it frequently departs from the rule of Saint Benedict. It contains proper offices for many saints celebrated especially in Gaul and Belgium, such as Saints Remigius, Vedastus, Medardus, and the martyrs Crispinus and Crispinianus, Quintinus, and others. Hence it is conjectured that it originally belonged among the sacred furnishings of some Church in Gaul. On the other hand, what is read in the order for Vespers on the most holy day of Easter appears to have been copied from the Roman Order, as we noted in that place. Weighing all these matters, we believe that the ancient rite of celebrating the divine office observed in the Roman Church, derived from the prescriptions of the earlier supreme pontiffs and especially from Saint Gregory, is here presented adapted to the use of some Gallican Church, with the proper offices of saints added—particularly those saints whose memory is celebrated in Gaul.

In this book, not only are proper Psalms assigned for the greater solemnities, both at the nocturnal and at the morning and evening hours, but also, when an office is prescribed from the Common of the Apostles, Martyrs, Confessors, and so forth, other Psalms are prescribed in place of the ferial Psalms, corresponding to the Antiphons given above, as is still customary in the Roman Church.

Just as certain Prayers are assigned in the Sacramentary for the cross and for the fonts, so this Collection also indicates Antiphons for the cross or for the fonts on the octave of the Epiphany—perhaps because in the Epiphany the memory of Christ’s Baptism was celebrated and Baptism was solemnly administered.

In the office of the Purification, which is entirely for the Most Holy Virgin, this Response deserves notice: “Rejoice, Mary; you alone have destroyed all heresies—‘which [things] of Gabriel,’ etc.”

On the Fifth Sunday of Lent, already called the Sunday of the Passion, these Verses—“Deliver me from the evil man,” “Deliver me from my enemies,” “Rescue me from the sword,” “From the mouth of the lion”—are called *versi declinatorii*. Many others occur elsewhere, including on the most holy day of Easter, with the same title. Why they are so called we have not yet been able to determine, except by mere conjecture, which we cautiously offer until something more certain becomes available. These Verses are entirely different from those inserted in the Responses; their distinctive feature is that they conclude the psalmody, or singing of the Psalms. When they are sung, the face is turned toward the altar, a rite observed by Amalarius. Thus they may have been called *declinatory Verses* both because of the inclination or turning of the face and the whole body toward the East or the altar, and because they indicate the end of the psalmody; for things that tend toward an end are said to decline.

On Palm Sunday the Verse “Glory, praise, and honor,” and so forth, is not read at all.

In the Order for Vespers on Easter Day we read: “And then they go to Saint John at the Vestment.” To explain this passage we have adopted the conjecture of the most learned Mabillon in his notes on the First Roman Order, volume II of the *Museo Italico*, p. 37. Consider another possibility here. In book III, letter 3, Saint Gregory orders that the tunic of Saint John, which was in the possession of a certain bishop, be sent to him. John the Deacon relates that it was brought to Rome as Gregory had wished and placed beneath the altar of Saint John in the Constantinian basilica, book III of the *Life of Saint Gregory*, chapter 57 and following. “These garments,” John says, “are shown even to this day to shine with such great miracles,” and so forth. Perhaps from this sacred tunic the basilica of Saint John, in which it was preserved, was called “Saint John at the Vestment.”

I am not unaware that the testimony of John the Deacon is rejected by the most learned Tillemont (volume I of *Ecclesiastical History*, in the notes, p. 640), as contrary to Gregory himself. But this proves it not at all.

After the office of the Ascension and Pentecost we read: “Antiphons at Matins for Saint Germanus.” Whether this is to be understood of Germanus of Auxerre, of Germanus of Paris, or of some other Germanus is not clearly established. Around that time—namely, on May 28—the feast of Saint Germanus, bishop of Paris, is celebrated. It seems more likely that this feast is meant in the Compiègne manuscript.

In the office of Saint Peter, the final Response of the second nocturn must not be passed over: “You are the shepherd of the sheep, prince of the apostles; God has entrusted all the kingdoms of the world to you, and therefore the keys of the kingdom of heaven have been entrusted to you.”

The office of Saint Hippolytus the martyr, on August 13, is very extensive and among the more solemn offices.

The Antiphons and Responses sung on the feast of Saints Dionysius and his companion martyrs are all taken from their Acts, in which Saint Dionysius is said to have been sent by Saint Clement, successor of the apostle Peter.

In our manuscript there is an office for Saint Andrew compiled from his Acts, much like the one now found in the Roman Breviary.

On the feast of Saint Thomas the Apostle, mention is made of his preaching and martyrdom among the Indians.

Among the Responses collected here, some are designated “of authority.” Amalarius attempts to explain what this means in his book *On the Order of the Antiphonary*, chapter 53. But he touches upon the difficulty without removing it, indeed scarcely even raising it. Since the matter is so obscure, we prefer to remain silent rather than speculate rashly.

You will encounter many other matters not unworthy of notice in the brief notes written at the foot of the columns. We do not think it necessary to repeat or reconsider them here.

# SAINT GREGORY THE GREAT, ROMAN PONTIFF: THE RESPONSAL, OR ANTIPHONARY

*(Copied from the Compiègne manuscript, written toward the end of the ninth century; the name of Pope Saint Gregory is prefixed to it.)*

[Note: These words are written in gold uncial letters on a purple ground, and in red on a white ground.]

IN THE NAME OF THE LORD JESUS CHRIST. Here begin the Responses, or Antiphons, for the yearly cycle. (C)*

[Note: From this point the manuscript is called the Responsal, because it contains these materials.]

## On the Vigil of the First Sunday of the Advent of the Lord. At Vespers

Antiphon. Behold, the name of the Lord comes from afar, and his glory fills the whole earth.

### At the Invitatory

Antiphon. Behold, the King is coming; let us go out to meet our Savior.

Another Antiphon. Come, let us worship the Lord who is to come.

Antiphon. The angel of the Lord announced to Mary, and she conceived by the Holy Spirit, alleluia.

Antiphon. Jerusalem, look toward the East and see, alleluia.

### Tuesday

Antiphon. Before they came together, Mary was found to have conceived in her womb from the Holy Spirit, alleluia.

Antiphon. Seek the Lord while he may be found; call upon him while he is near, alleluia.

### Wednesday

Antiphon. From Zion the law went forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

Antiphon. A stronger one will come after me, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie.

### Thursday

Antiphon. Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.

Antiphon. I shall wait for the Lord my Savior, and I shall await him while he is near, alleluia.

### Friday

Antiphon. Behold, God will come, and a man from the house of David will sit upon the throne, alleluia.

Antiphon. From Egypt I called my son; he will come to save his people.

### Saturday

Antiphon. Zion, do not fear; behold, your God will come, alleluia.

Antiphon. Behold, the Son of Man will come in the clouds of heaven, alleluia.

Antiphon. Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be humbled, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.

Antiphon. Come, O Lord, visit us in peace, so that we may rejoice before you with a perfect heart.

Antiphon. Lift up your eyes, Jerusalem, and see the power of the King. Behold, the Savior comes to release you from your bondage.

Antiphon. Rejoice and be glad, Jerusalem, because your King comes to you—the one of whom the prophets foretold, whom the angels adored, whom the cherubim and seraphim proclaim as “Holy, Holy, Holy.”

## Responses on the Second Sunday

[Note: These are the Responses sung after the lessons of the nocturns.]

Response. Jerusalem, your salvation will soon come; why are you consumed with grief? Is there no counselor for you, because sorrow will renew you? I shall save you and deliver you; do not fear.

[Note: For *innovavit*, just as in another Response *regnavit* is used for *regnabit*, v is used for b, and vice versa . . . Consult Angelo Rocca’s scholia on the Sacramentary, col. 612 A.]

Verse. Israel, if you will hear me, there shall be no new god among you, nor shall you worship a foreign god; for I am the Lord. I shall save you, and so forth.

Response. Behold, the Lord will come, and all his saints with him; and on that day there will be a great light. And they will go out from Jerusalem like pure water; and the Lord reigned forever over all the nations.

Verse. From the rising of the sun and from its setting, from the north and from the sea. And the Lord will reign.

Response. The Lord will teach us his ways, and we walked in his paths, because from Zion the law went forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

Verse. From Zion comes the beauty of his splendor; our God will come openly. Because from Zion—

Response. Jerusalem, arise and stand on the heights; see the joy that will come to you from your God.

Verse. Lift your eyes around you, and see and contemplate.

Verse. City of Jerusalem, do not weep, because the Lord has grieved over you, and he will remove all tribulation from you.

Verse. Behold, the Lord who rules. And he will remove—

Response. Behold, the Lord will come, our protector, the Holy One of Israel, wearing the crown of the kingdom upon his head.

Verse. Behold, the Lord who rules. The crown—

Response. As a mother comforts her children, so I shall comfort you, says the Lord; and from Jerusalem, the city that I chose, help will come to you; and you shall see, and your heart shall rejoice.

Verse. God will come from Lebanon, and the Holy One—

Response. Jerusalem, you shall plant a vineyard on your mountains and shall be exalted, because the day of the Lord will come. Arise, Zion; turn back to your God. Rejoice and be glad, Jacob, because your Savior will come from the midst of the nations.

Verse. God will come from Lebanon, and the Holy One from the shadowy and densely wooded mountain. Rejoice.

Response. The Lord will go forth from Samaria, from the gate that looks toward the East, and he will come to Bethlehem, walking upon the waters of Judah’s redemption. Then every person will be saved, because behold, he will come.

Verse. God will come from Lebanon. Then—

Response. Our King, Christ, is coming, whom John proclaimed to be the Lamb who was to come.

Verse. Behold the Lamb of God; behold him who takes away the sins of the world. Whom John—

## At Morning Praise

Antiphon. Behold, the Lord will come in the clouds of heaven with great power, alleluia.

Antiphon. Zion, the city of our strength: the Savior will be placed within it as a wall and bulwark. Open the gates, because God is with us, alleluia.

Antiphon. Behold, the Lord will appear, and he will not deceive. If he delays, wait for him, because he will come and will not delay, alleluia.

Antiphon. The mountains and hills shall sing praise before God, and all the trees of the forests shall clap their hands, because the Lord will come, the ruler of the eternal kingdom, alleluia, alleluia.

[Note: This is how the Antiphons said before the *Benedictus* are designated, because that canticle is taken from the Gospel. The same is to be said of the Antiphon placed before the canticle *Magnificat*.]

Antiphon. He shall sit forever upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, alleluia.

Antiphon. Blessed are you, Mary, because you believed; the things said to you by the Lord shall be fulfilled in you, alleluia.

### Monday

Antiphon. From heaven the Lord who rules will come, and in his hand are honor and dominion.

Antiphon. Behold, the King, the Lord of the earth, comes, and he himself will remove the yoke of our captivity.

Antiphon. I baptized you with water; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit, alleluia.

### Tuesday

Antiphon. Over you, Jerusalem, the Lord will rise, and his glory will be seen in you.

Antiphon. The voice of one crying in the wilderness: prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God.

### Wednesday

Antiphon. Behold, I send my angel, who has prepared your way before your face.

Antiphon. Zion, you will be renewed and will see your righteous one, who is to come into you.

Antiphon. Our King, Christ, will come, whom John proclaimed to be the Lamb who was to come.

### Thursday

Antiphon. You are the one who is to come, O Lord, whom we have awaited, so that you may save your people.

Antiphon. He who comes after me has been made before me, whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.

Antiphon. My salvation is near, so that it may come, and my righteousness, so that it may be revealed, says the Lord.

### Friday

Antiphon. Say to the fainthearted: “Take courage”; behold, the Lord our God will come.

Antiphon. Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise reaches to the ends of the earth.

### Saturday

Antiphon. The Lord has raised a sign among the nations and has gathered the dispersed of Israel.

Antiphon. Before me no god was formed, and after me there shall be none, because every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess.

## Responses on the Third Sunday of Advent

Response. Behold, the Lord will appear upon a white cloud, and with him thousands of saints. And upon his garment and upon his thigh he bears written: “King of Kings and Lord of Lords.”

Verse. Behold, the Lord who rules will come with power. And upon his garment—

Response. Bethlehem, city of the Most High God, from you will go forth the ruler of Israel, whose going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity. And he will be magnified in the midst of the whole earth. And there will be peace in our land when he comes.

Verse. God will come from Lebanon. And his going forth—

Response. He who is to come will come and will not delay. There will no longer be fear within our borders, because he is our Savior.

Verse. From Zion comes the beauty of his splendor; our God will come openly. Because he is our Savior.

Response. Receive the Word, Virgin Mary, which was sent to you by the Lord through the angel. You will conceive through the ear the Lord together with the man, so that you may be called blessed among all women.

Verse. Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with you. So that you may be called blessed.

Response. Egypt, do not weep, because your ruler will come to you; before his presence the abysses will be shaken. Deliver your people from the hand of the mighty one.

Verse. Behold, the Lord—

Response. His time is near to come, and his days shall not be prolonged; the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and Israel shall be saved.

Verse. He who is to come will come and will not delay. There will no longer be fear within our borders.

Response. The Lord descended like rain upon a fleece; in his days righteousness and an abundance of peace shall arise.

Verse. From the rising of the sun and from its setting. It shall arise.

Response. Come, O Lord, and do not delay; release the sins of your people, and bring back the dispersed to their own land.

Verse. From the rising of the sun. And bring back—

Verse. Behold, the Lord.

Response. Behold the root of Jesse; he has risen for the salvation of the peoples. The nations shall entreat him, and his name shall be glorious.

Verse. God will come from Lebanon. And his name shall be—

Response. The Lord will teach you his ways, and has led you in his paths, because from Zion the law went forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

[Note: Perhaps “and we shall walk.” In many other places this manuscript is corrupt, perhaps through the gross ignorance of the scribe.]

Verse. From Zion comes the beauty of his splendor. And the word—

Antiphon. The Lord will come, and will not delay. He illuminates the things hidden in darkness and will reveal himself to all the nations, alleluia.

Antiphon. Jerusalem, rejoice with great joy, for your Savior will come to you, alleluia.

Antiphon. Mountains and hills will be humbled, crooked places will become straight, and rough places into level paths. Come, Lord, and do not delay, alleluia.

Antiphon. When John heard in prison about the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples and said to him: “Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?”

Antiphon. Go, tell John: “The blind see, the deaf hear, the lame are healed, lepers are cleansed.”

Antiphon. “Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?” Tell John [p. 737] what you have seen: “The blind return to the light, the dead rise, the poor are evangelized,” alleluia.

Antiphon. Arise, arise; clothe yourself with strength, arm of the Lord.

Antiphon. Do you hear, Virgin Mary? The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.

Antiphon. This is the testimony given by John: “He who comes after me has been made before me.”

Antiphon. His dominion will be multiplied, and there will be no end of peace.

Antiphon. The Lord will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign forever.

Antiphon. Behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son, and his name will be called Emmanuel.

Antiphon. Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, for from Zion the law went forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

Antiphon. From Zion the almighty Lord will come, to save his people.

## The Greater Antiphons in the Gospel

Antiphon. O Wisdom, who came forth from the mouth of the Most High, reaching from end to end mightily and ordering all things sweetly, come to teach us the way of prudence.

Antiphon. O Adonai, ruler of the house of Israel, who appeared to Moses in the fire of the flame of the bush and gave him the law on Sinai, come to redeem us with an outstretched arm.

Antiphon. O Root of Jesse, who stand as a sign for the peoples, before whom kings will shut their mouths, whom the nations will entreat, come to free us; now do not delay.

Antiphon. O Key of David and scepter of the house of Israel, who open and no one closes, who close and no one opens, come and lead out the prisoner from the prison house, the one sitting in darkness and the shadow of death.

[Col. 0733A] Antiphon. O Rising Dawn, splendor of eternal light and Sun of righteousness, come and enlighten the one sitting in darkness and the shadow of death.

Antiphon. O King of the nations and their desired one, and cornerstone, who make both one, come and save the human being whom you formed from clay.

Antiphon. O Emmanuel, our King and lawgiver, expectation of the nations and their Savior, come to save us, our Lord God.

Antiphon. O Virgin of virgins, how will this happen, since you have never been seen to have a first like yourself, nor to have a successor? [p. 741] Daughters of Jerusalem, why do you marvel? This is the divine mystery that you behold.

Antiphon. The Savior of the world will rise like the sun, and will descend into the Virgin’s womb like rain upon the grass, alleluia.

[Note: [Col. 0733D] The assignment of only three Psalms for each nocturn shows that the Compendian Codex was not written for the use of a monastery where the Rule of Saint Benedict was observed, since according to this rule six Psalms must be sung at each nocturn. The fact that the course or office prescribed here appears to follow the rite of the Roman Church seems to be suggested by its conformity with the Roman Ordo, which is proved below in the office of Easter.]

Psalm: My heart overflows.

Verse. Like a bridegroom.

Responsory as above.

[Col. 0734A] Responsory. Today the King of heaven deigned to be born for us from a Virgin, so that he might bring the lost human being back to the heavenly kingdoms. The army of angels rejoices, because eternal salvation has appeared to the human race.

Verse. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will.

It rejoices.

Responsory. Today true peace descended for us from heaven; today the heavens became honey-sweet throughout the whole world.

Verse. Glory to God in the highest.

Today throughout.

Responsory. He descended from heaven, sent from the Father’s citadel. He entered our region through the Virgin’s ear, clothed in a purple robe. And through the golden gate the light and beauty of the whole structure of the world went forth.

Clothed.

## At the Third Nocturn

[Col. 0734C] Antiphon. He himself will call upon me, alleluia. “You are my Father,” alleluia, alleluia.

Psalm: The mercies of the Lord forever.

Antiphon. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult before the face of the Lord, because he has come.

Responsory. Rejoice with me, all you who love the Lord, because when I was little, I pleased the Most High, and from my womb I bore God and man.

Responsory. Blessed and venerable Virgin, who, without violation of modesty, was found to be the mother of the Savior. He lay in a manger and shone in heaven.

Verse. Lord, I heard your report and trembled.

He lay.

Responsory. The Virgin, mother of God, holds in her womb him who rules heaven and earth; nobles accompany the heir, through whom the rejoicing world flourishes under Christ its ruler.

Verse. Virgin, mother of God, he whom the whole world cannot contain confined himself in your womb, becoming human. Through him.

Responsory. The Virgin’s heart was strengthened: when the angel announced the divine mysteries, she conceived and received in her chaste womb the one [reforma, uncertain; “beautiful in form”] beyond the sons of men; and, blessed forever, she brought forth for us God and man.

Verse. The house of a chaste breast suddenly becomes the temple of God; untouched, knowing no man, the Virgin conceived a Son.

God.

Responsory. The Virgin mother, knowing no man, bore without pain the Savior of the ages, himself the King of angels; alone, the Virgin nursed him at her breasts, filled from heaven [with a full breast].

Verse. Blessed is the womb.

Responsory. O King of heaven, whom such service attends! He who contains the world is placed in a stable; he lies in a manger and reigns in heaven.

Verse. Lord, I heard your report and was afraid. I considered your works and trembled in the midst of two animals.

Lying.

Responsory. In the Father eternity remains, because virginity will not perish in the mother; and he who was born for the salvation of all came forth through an untouched body. The invisible one did not disdain to be born in the flesh. He did not abandon his dominion.

Verse. Like a bridegroom, the Lord.

Not.

Responsory. The angels praise you, holy mother of God, who did not know a man and carried the Lord in your womb. You conceived our Lord through the ear, so that you might be called blessed among all women.

Responsory. The Word became flesh and dwelt among us; and we saw his glory, glory as of the Only-Begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.

Responsory. Today the Lord deigned to be born from the Virgin’s womb, into whom he went forth to reign [the text is uncertain], in order to redeem us.

Into whom.

Responsory. No one knows the nature of this one who has come, except he alone. He is called the Word of God; he has a splendid garment, and the entire choir of angels in white follows him.

Responsory. Behold, the eternal ruling Lord has come; kingship is in his hand, and power and dominion.

## Antiphons at Matins Lauds

**Antiphon.** This is that disciple who bore witness; we know that his testimony is true.  
**Antiphon.** This is my disciple; I desire him to remain [Col. 0739C] so until I come.  
**Antiphon.** Behold my chosen servant whom I have chosen; I have placed my Spirit upon him.  
**Antiphon.** There are some among those standing here who will not taste death until they see the Son of Man in his kingdom.  
**Antiphon.** I desire him to remain so until I come.  
**Verse.** The righteous shall flourish like the palm.

## At the Gospel

**Antiphon.** In the midst of the Church.  
**Antiphon.** This is John, who reclined upon the Lord’s breast at supper, the blessed apostle to whom the heavenly secrets were revealed.  
**Antiphon.** This is John, who reclined upon the Lord’s breast at supper, whom Jesus loved.  
**Antiphon.** This is John, to whom Christ on the cross entrusted the Virgin Mother.  
**Antiphon.** He was chosen by the Lord as a virgin and loved more than the others, alleluia.  
**Antiphon.** The virgin chosen by the Lord remained a man [virgin] forever, alleluia.

## At Vespers on the vigil of the Innocents

**Verse.** The souls of the righteous.  
**Antiphon.** For theirs is [Col. 0739D] the kingdom of heaven: they despised the life of the world, attained the rewards of the kingdom, and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.

## At the Invitatory

**Antiphon.** The wonderful Lord.  
**Antiphon.** The King of martyrs.

**Antiphon.** His delight was in the law of the Lord, day and night. **Psalm:** “Blessed is the man.”  
**Antiphon.** Proclaiming the commandment of the Lord, he was established on his holy mountain. **Psalm:** “Why did the nations rage?”  
**Antiphon.** With my voice I cried to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain. **Psalm:** “O Lord, how they have multiplied.”

**Responsory.** Beneath the altar of God I heard the voices of those who had been slain: “Why do you not defend our blood?” And they received a divine answer: “Wait a little longer, [Col. 0740A] until the number of your brothers is complete.” **Verse.** I saw beneath the altar of God the souls of the saints, because of the word of the Lord which they possessed; and with a loud voice [p. 749] they said: “Why do you not…”

**Responsory.** They poured out the blood of the saints like water all around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them. **Verse.** Avenge, O Lord, the blood of your servants that has been shed. All around…

**Responsory.** They adored the One who lives forever and ever, casting their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God. **Verse.** Coming, they shall come with rejoicing, bearing their sheaves. Casting…

## At the Gospel

**Antiphon.** Let the little children come to me, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.  
**Antiphon.** They washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.  
**Antiphon.** [p. 750] From two years old and under, Herod killed many boys because of the Lord.  
**Antiphon.** They shall walk with me in white, for they are worthy; and I will not erase their names from the book of life.  
**Antiphon.** These are they who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins, and they follow the Lamb wherever he goes.  
**Antiphon.** Innocent infants were killed for Christ. Nursing children were slain by the wicked King. Praising the spotless Lamb himself, they say always: “Glory to you, O Lord.”  
**Antiphon.** These were purchased [Col. 0741A] from among men as firstfruits for God and the Lamb, and no lie was found in their mouth.

## At Vespers on the vigil of the Octave of the Lord

**Verse.** Like a bridegroom.  
**Antiphon.** O wonderful exchange! The Creator of the human race, taking an animate body, deigned to be born from a Virgin. And, proceeding as a man without seed, he bestowed upon us his divinity.

## At the Invitatory

**Antiphon.** Come, let us adore the Lord who was born King.  
**Antiphon.** The Lord said to me: “You are my Son; today I have begotten you.” **Psalm:** “Why did the nations rage?”  
**Antiphon.** He set his tabernacle in the sun, and he himself, like a bridegroom proceeding from his chamber. **Psalm:** “The heavens declare.”  
**Antiphon.** Lift up, you eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter. **Psalm:** “The earth is the Lord’s.”

## At the second nocturn

**Antiphon.** You are beautiful beyond the sons of men; [Col. 0741B] grace has been poured upon your lips. **Psalm:** “My heart has uttered.”  
**Antiphon.** A man was born in her, and the Most High himself founded her. **Psalm:** “Her foundations.”  
**Antiphon.** All the trees of the forest shall rejoice before the Lord, for he has come. **Psalm:** “Sing to the Lord.”

## At the third nocturn

**Antiphon.** In the beginning and before the ages, the Word was God; today he himself was born, the Savior of the world. **Psalm:** “The Lord reigns.” 1.  
**Antiphon.** Begotten before the morning star and before the ages, the Lord our Savior deigned to be born today. **Psalm:** “Sing to the Lord.” 2.  
**Antiphon.** When the Lord was born, the choir of angels sang, saying: “Salvation belongs to our God who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.” **Psalm:** “The Lord reigns.” 2.

## Antiphons at Matins

**Antiphon.** O wonderful exchange! As above.  
**Antiphon.** When you were ineffably born from a Virgin, then the Scriptures were fulfilled: like rain upon fleece you descended, to save the human race; we praise you, [Col. 0741C] our God.  
**Antiphon.** In the bush that Moses saw unconsumed, we recognized the preservation of your praiseworthy virginity. Mother of God, intercede for us.  
**Antiphon.** The root of Jesse has sprouted; the star has risen from Jacob; the Virgin has borne the Savior. We praise you, Mother of God.  
**Antiphon.** Behold, Mary has borne for us the Savior, whom John saw and cried out, saying: “Behold the Lamb of God; behold him who takes away the sins of the world,” alleluia.  
**Antiphon.** A wonderful mystery is revealed today; natures are renewed; God became man; in him remained what he was (*in quo fuit* [*id quod fuit*], ‘in whom he was’ [‘that which he was’]), and he assumed what he was not, undergoing neither commixture nor division.  
**Antiphon.** A great mystery of inheritance: the womb of a woman who knew no man has become the temple of God. He was not defiled by assuming flesh from her. All nations shall come, saying: “Glory to you, O Lord.”  
**Antiphon.** Blessed is the womb…  
**Antiphon.** He who is from the earth [p. 751] speaks of the earth; he who comes from heaven is above all. What he saw and heard, this he testifies, and no one [Col. 0741D] accepts his testimony; but whoever accepts his testimony has sealed that God is true, alleluia.

## At Vespers on the vigil of the Epiphany of the Lord

**Verse.** All shall come from Sheba.  
**Antiphon.** Your light has come, Jerusalem, and the glory of the Lord has risen over you; and the nations shall walk in your light, alleluia.

## Antiphons at the first nocturn

**Antiphon.** Bring to the Lord, sons of God; adore the Lord in his holy court. **Psalm:** “Himself.”  
**Antiphon.** Sing praises to our God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises wisely. **Psalm:** “All you nations.”  
**Antiphon.** Let all the earth adore you and sing to you; let it sing a psalm to your name, O Lord. **Psalm:** “Shout for joy.”  
**Verse.** Let all the earth adore you, O God.

**Responsories.**

**Responsory.** Today, when the Lord was baptized in the Jordan, the [Col. 0742A] heavens were opened; and the Spirit remained upon him like a dove, and the Father’s voice thundered: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” **Verse.** The heavens were opened, and the Father’s voice was heard: “This is the Son…”

**Responsory.** All shall come from Sheba, bearing gold and frankincense and proclaiming praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. **Verse.** The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall offer gifts; the kings of Arabia and Sheba shall bring presents, alleluia.

**Responsory.** The star which the Magi had seen in the East went before them until they came to the place where the child was. When they saw it, they rejoiced with great joy. **Verse.** Entering the house, they found the child with Mary his mother; and falling down, they adored him. They rejoiced.

## At the second nocturn

**Antiphon.** The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall offer gifts to the King, the Lord. **Psalm:** “O God, give your judgment.”  
**Antiphon.** All the nations that you have made shall come and adore before you, O Lord. **Psalm:** “Incline, O Lord.”  
**Antiphon.** Come, let us [Col. 0742B] adore him, for he is the Lord our God. **Psalm:** “Come, let us rejoice.”

**Responsories as above.**

**Responsory.** Herod questioned the Magi: “What sign did you see above the newborn King?” “A great, shining star, whose brightness illuminates the world; we recognized it and came to adore the Lord.” **Verse.** The Magi come from the East, seeking the face of the Lord and saying: “And we…”

**Responsory.** Shine, shine, Jerusalem; your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen over you. **Verse.** The nations shall walk in your light, and kings in the splendor of your rising. And the glory…

**Responsory.** The Magi come from the East to Jerusalem, seeking and saying: “Where is he who has been born, whose star we saw, and we have come to adore the Lord?” **Verse.** The Magi come from the East, seeking the face of the Lord and saying: “Where is he?”

## At the third nocturn

**Antiphon.** The force of the river makes glad, alleluia, the city of God, alleluia. **Psalm:** “Our God.”  
**Antiphon.** Adore [Col. 0742C] the Lord, alleluia, in his holy court, alleluia, alleluia. **Psalm:** “Sing,” 1.  
**Antiphon.** Adore the Lord, alleluia, all his angels, alleluia, alleluia. **Psalm:** “The Lord reigns,” 1.

**Responsories.**

**Responsory.** There are three precious gifts which the [p. 752] Magi offered to the Lord on this day, and they contain divine mysteries: in the gold, recognize the power of the king; in the frankincense, consider the great priest; and in the myrrh, the Lord’s burial. **Verse.** The kings of Tarshish, as above.

**Responsory.** The sanctified day has dawned upon us; come, nations, and adore the Lord, for today a great light has appeared on earth. **Verse.** Come, let us adore him, for he is the Lord our God. For today…

**Responsory.** When the Magi saw the star, they rejoiced with great joy; and entering the house they found the child with Mary his mother. Falling down, they adored him, and opening their treasures they offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. **Verse.** The kings of Tarshish. Gold…

**Responsory.** This is [Col. 0742D] the glorious day on which the Savior appeared to the world; the prophets foretold him, the angels adored him; when the Magi saw his star they rejoiced and offered him gifts. **Verse.** Entering the house… And gifts…

**Responsory.** Called from paradise, the Jordan runs with joy, questioned by the birds: “Why do you hasten, Jordan?” “So that Christ may be baptized and John crowned.” **Verse.** “What is it to you, sea, that you fled, and to you, Jordan, that you turned back?” “So that Christ…”

**Responsory.** Today the heavens were opened, and the sea was made sweet. The earth rejoices; the mountains and hills exult, because Christ was baptized by John in the Jordan. **Verse.** “What is it to you, sea…”

**Responsory.** The Holy Spirit was seen in the form of a dove, and the Father’s voice was heard: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.” **Verse.** “The voice of the Lord is over the waters; the God of majesty thundered; the Lord is over many waters.” The Father’s… **Verse.** The heavens were opened.

**Responsory.** The shepherds, because of the brightness of the light, were [Col. 0743A] unable to look upon the angel; they were greatly troubled. And a voice came from heaven, saying: “Do not fear; peace be with you. I am Gabriel the angel sent to the Virgin.” **Verse.** I announce to you great joy, which will be for all the people. I am…

**Responsory.** A shining star in the East. They hasten to meet the King, offering him a great treasure: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. **Verse.** The kings of Tarshish.

**Responsory.** A great King has been born in Israel, and the kings of the earth have come to adore him. And they offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. **Verse.** Entering the house… As above. And they offered…

## Antiphons at Matins Lauds

**Antiphon.** Begotten before the morning star and before the ages, the Lord our Savior has appeared today to the world.  
**Antiphon.** There are three gifts which the Magi offered to the Lord: gold, frankincense, and myrrh, to the Son of God, the great King, alleluia.  
**Antiphon.** Opening their treasures, the Magi offered gold, frankincense, and myrrh to the Lord, alleluia.  
**Antiphon.** Seas and rivers, bless the Lord; [Col. 0743B] springs, sing a hymn to the Lord, alleluia.  
**Antiphon.** The Magi saw the star and said to one another: “This is the great [of the great] King’s sign. Let us go and seek him, and offer him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.”  
**Verse.** All shall come from Sheba.

## At the Gospel

**Antiphon.** Today the Church has been joined to the heavenly Bridegroom, for Christ washed away her sins in the Jordan. The Magi hasten with gifts to the royal wedding, and the guests rejoice because water has been made wine, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** The ranks of angels, seeing the Invisible One coming in the waters, were terrified and wondered how the invisible God had assumed the form of a servant and, appearing, illuminated the world. Blessed are you, O Lord, God of Israel.

**Antiphon.** [p. 753] John cried out to the Lord: “Before you the knees of heavenly and earthly beings bow; how do you bow your head before me? If you command the angels, they will baptize.”

**Antiphon.** For they themselves cover their faces with wings. “But how could I dare? I cannot, [Col. 0743C] O Lord; I am afraid, merciful one.” And again your blameless command compels me, O Lord. Glory to you.

**Antiphon.** When the Magi saw the star, they rejoiced with great joy; and entering the house they offered gold, frankincense, and myrrh to the Lord.

**Antiphon.** This star shines like a flame and reveals God, the King of kings. The Magi saw it and offered gifts to the King.

**Antiphon.** The star which the Magi had seen went before them until it came above the place where the child was.

**Antiphon.** From the East the Magi came to Bethlehem to adore the Lord; and opening their treasures they offered precious gifts: gold as to the great King; frankincense as to the true Lord (*Dominum verum* [*Domino vero*], ‘the true Lord’ [‘to the true Lord’]); myrrh for his burial, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** All shall come from Sheba, bearing gold and frankincense, alleluia, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** All nations shall come from afar, carrying their gifts, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** Warned in a dream by an angel, the Magi returned to their own country by another way.

**Antiphon.** We saw his star in the East and came with gifts to adore the Lord.

**Antiphon.** The Magi saw the star and offered gold, frankincense, and myrrh [Col. 0743D] to the Lord.

**Antiphon.** [The antiphon is absent in the manuscript.] You appeared, Christ, as Light from Light; to you the Magi offer gifts, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** Those who insulted you shall come to you and adore the traces of your feet.

## Antiphons at Matins on the Octave of the Theophany

**Antiphon.** The Savior, renewing the old man, came to baptism, so that through water he might restore the nature that had been corrupted, clothing us with an incorruptible [perhaps “incorruptibility”] garment.

**Antiphon.** You who purify human contagion with Spirit and fire, we all glorify you as God and Redeemer.

**Antiphon.** The Baptist trembled and did not dare touch your Holy One, but cried out with trembling: “Sanctify me, Savior.”

**Antiphon.** The Savior crushed the dragon’s head in the river Jordan; he delivered all from its power.

**Antiphon.** A great mystery is revealed today, because the Creator of all [Col. 0744A] purifies our sins in the Jordan.

**Antiphon.** The Forerunner John rejoices when, at the Lord’s baptism in the Jordan, the rejoicing of the whole world took place; the remission of our sins took place, sanctifying the waters. Let us all cry out to him: “Have mercy on us.”

**Antiphon.** The soldier baptizes the King, the servant his Lord, John the Savior. The water of the Jordan was astonished, the dove bore witness, and the Father’s voice was heard: “This is my Son.”

**Antiphon.** The heavens were opened above him, and a voice came from heaven, saying: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

**Antiphon.** A voice sounded from heaven, and the Father’s voice was heard: “This is my Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.”

## Antiphons at the cross or the fonts

**Antiphon.** Today water burns away sin; the Deliverer appears and, by the power of divinity, bedews the whole world.

**Antiphon.** The Father testifies to the Son from heaven; the presence of the Holy Spirit comes, making known the One who is baptized, Christ.

**Antiphon.** Christ is baptized and the whole world is sanctified, [Col. 0744B] and he grants us remission of sins. By water and Spirit we are all purified.

**Antiphon.** Blessed John stood upon the bank of the Jordan, clothed in splendor, baptizing the Savior. “Baptize me, John.” “I baptize you; I bless you, and you, Jordan, receive me with rejoicing.”

**Antiphon.** Today the sting of sin [read: “the sting of sin”] is [p. 754] crushed, when the Lord is baptized; and regeneration has been given to us.

**Antiphon.** The springs of water have been sanctified, when Christ appeared in the glory of the whole world. Draw water from the fountain of the Savior; for Christ our God has now sanctified every creature.

**Antiphon.** Dominion and the honor of kingship have been given to Christ. Every people, tribe, and tongue shall serve him forever.

**Antiphon.** The preacher of truth, humbly supplicating in fear, hesitated to baptize the sinless Lord at his command, and answered him: “I know you to be the Redeemer; sanctify me, Savior, together with those who are in faith and cry to you: ‘Blessed are you, O Lord our God.’ [Variant: printed *eos*, ‘them’; read *eis*, ‘to/with them.’ The printed case leaves the construction irregular.]”

## Gospel antiphons for Sundays

[Col. 0744C]

### First Sunday after the Epiphany

**Antiphon.** “Son, why have you treated us so? Behold, your father and I, grieving, have been seeking you.” “Why were you seeking me? Did you not know that I must be in the things that belong to my Father?”

**Antiphon.** The boy Jesus advanced in age and wisdom before God and men.

### Second Sunday

**Antiphon.** A wedding took place at Cana of Galilee, and Jesus was there with Mary his mother.

**Antiphon.** When the wine failed, Jesus ordered the jars to be filled with water [with waters], and it was changed into wine, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** Every man first…

**Antiphon.** Jesus performed this first sign before his disciples.

**Antiphon.** “What is there between me and you, woman? My hour has not yet come.”

**Antiphon.** Demons were going out from many, crying out and saying: “For you are the Son of God.” And rebuking them, he did not permit them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.

[Col. 0744D]

### Third Sunday

**Antiphon.** When Jesus had come down from the mountain, behold, a leper came and adored him, saying: “Lord, if you will, you can cleanse me.” And stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying: “I will; be cleansed.”

**Antiphon.** “Lord, if you will, you can cleanse me.” And Jesus said to him: “I will; be cleansed.”

**Antiphon.** “Lord, my servant lies paralyzed at home and is grievously tormented.” “Amen, I say to you, I will come and heal him.”

**Antiphon.** “Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant will be healed.”

**Antiphon.** Many shall come from the East and the West and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

### Fourth Sunday

**Antiphon.** As Jesus was leaving in a boat, behold, a great disturbance arose on the sea. His disciples awakened him, saying: “Lord, save us; we are perishing.”

**Antiphon.** “Lord, save us; we are perishing. Command and bring about calm, [Col. 0745A] O God.”

**Antiphon.** “Lord, save us; we are perishing. Command and bring about calm, O God.” But when the men saw what sign he had performed, they said: “What sort of man is this, that even the winds obey him?”

**Antiphon.** “You of little faith, why did you doubt? For I am with you,” says the Lord.

**Antiphon.** Jesus arose and rebuked the winds and the sea, and a great calm arose, and everyone marveled.

**Antiphon.** When those men saw the signs that Jesus performed, they marveled and said to one another: “Who is this? [He commands the winds and the sea, and] the sea obeys him.”

[p. 755]

### Fifth Sunday

**Antiphon.** “Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where, then, does it have weeds?” And Jesus said to them: “An enemy has done this.”

**Antiphon.** “Do you want us to go and gather them?” And Jesus said to them: “No, lest while gathering the weeds…”

**Antiphon.** [The remainder is lacking in the manuscript.] “At harvest time I will say to the reapers: Gather the weeds first and bind them into bundles to burn; but [Col. 0745B] gather the wheat into my barn.”

**Responsory.** Truly a servant of God, in whom no deceit was found: although he was high priest, he did not fear earthly things, but, longing for heavenly things, was therefore placed in humility and became a confessor of the Lord Jesus Christ. **Verse.** No one like him was found who would keep the law of the Most High. Therefore… **Verse.** Although he was high priest, he did not fear earthly things, but gloriously departed to the heavenly kingdoms.

# The Purification of Saint Mary

## At Vespers on the vigil

**Verse.** Simeon received the answer.  
**Antiphon.** When the parents brought in the child Jesus, Simeon took him in his arms and blessed God, saying: “Now you dismiss your servant, O Lord, in peace.”

The antiphons and responsories for the Purification of Saint Mary begin.

[Col. 0745C]

## At the Invitatory

**Antiphon.** Come, let us adore the Lord, King of virgins.  
**Antiphon.** Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. **Psalm:** “O Lord, our Lord.”  
**Antiphon.** Like chosen myrrh you gave forth a pleasant fragrance [an odor of sweetness], holy Mother of God. **Psalm:** “The heavens declare.”  
**Antiphon.** Before the bridal chamber of this Virgin, gather frequently for us sweet songs of the drama. **Psalm:** “The earth is the Lord’s.”  
**Verse.** In your beauty.

**Responsories as above.**

**Responsory.** Adorn your bridal chamber, Zion, and receive Christ the King, whom the Virgin conceived, the Virgin bore, the Virgin after childbirth; she who bore him adored him. **Verse.** Simeon, taking him in his hands, gave thanks and blessed the child, the Lord. Whom the Virgin…

**Responsory.** The old man carried the child, but the child ruled the old man; whom the Virgin… as above. **Verse.** Simeon, taking him…

**Responsory.** Simeon received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had seen the Christ of the Lord. **Verse.** “Now you dismiss your servant, O Lord, in peace, because my eyes have seen [Col. 0745D] your Salvation” [“Saluzare”].

## At the second nocturn

**Antiphon.** In your beauty and loveliness, turn your attention, proceed prosperously, and reign. **Psalm:** “My heart has uttered.”  
**Antiphon.** God will help her with his countenance; God is in her midst, and she shall not be moved. **Psalm:** “God is our refuge.”  
**Antiphon.** As the dwelling place of all our rejoicing, she dwells in you, holy Mother of God. **Psalm:** “Her foundations.”  
**Verse.** Grace has been poured forth.

**Responsories.**

**Responsory.** Simeon took Jesus in his arms, cried out, and said: “You are truly the light for the illumination of the Gentiles and the glory of your people Israel.” **Verse.** Simeon received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had seen the Christ of the Lord. For the illumination…

**Responsory.** Simeon received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had seen [Col. 0746A] the Christ of the Lord. Because my eyes have seen…

**Responsory.** Behold the miracle: the mother of the Lord. The Virgin conceived, not knowing virilem [virile] consortium (“a male union/association”). Mary, standing honored beneath her noble burden, knows herself to be the mother of God, she who does not know herself as a wife. **Verse.** Heavenly grace enters the chaste womb of the parent; the maiden’s belly bears secrets it did not know. And the mother…

**Verse.** God will help her.  
**Verse.** [Col. 0746B] The Lord chose her.

**Responsory.** Rejoice, Virgin Mary: you alone have destroyed all heresies, you who believed the words of the archangel Gabriel; while remaining a virgin, you gave birth to God and man, and after childbirth remained an inviolate virgin. **Verse.** We believe that the archangel Gabriel spoke to you by divine authority. We believe that your womb was made pregnant by the Holy Spirit. Let the wretched Jew be ashamed, who says that Christ was born from Joseph’s seed. While the Virgin…

Antiphon: “The kingdom of heaven will be like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.” Antiphon: “Go you also into my vineyard, and whatever is just I will give you.” Antiphon: “But about the eleventh hour the householder went out and found others standing idle in the marketplace, and he said to them: ‘Go you also into my vineyard.’” Antiphon: “The householder says to his laborers: [Col. 0748A] ‘Why do you stand here idle all day?’ But they answered and said: ‘Because no one has hired us.’ Go you also into my vineyard, and whatever is just I will give you.” Antiphon: “Why do you stand here idle all day? Go you also into my vineyard.” Antiphon: “Why do you stand here idle all day?” They answered and said: “No one has hired us.” Antiphon: “When evening had come, the householder began to give the laborers their wages, beginning with the last and going on to the first.” Antiphon: “Call the laborers and pay them their wages,” says the Lord. Antiphon: “These last worked for one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who bore the burden of the day and the heat.” Antiphon: “But the householder says: ‘Friend, I do you no wrong; did you not agree with me for a denarius? Take what is yours and go.’” Antiphon: “Friend, I do you no wrong; did you not agree with me for a denarius? Take what is yours and go.” Antiphon: “Take what is yours and go, because I am good,” says the Lord. Antiphon: “Am I not permitted to do what I wish? Or is your eye evil because I am good?” says the Lord. Antiphon: “Thus the last will be first, and the first last; for many are called, but few are chosen.” [Col. 0748B] Antiphon: “The first will be last, and the last first; for many are called, but few are chosen,” says the Lord. Antiphon: “Many who are first will be last, and the last first,” Jesus said to his disciples. Antiphon: “For many are called, but few are chosen,” says the Lord.

## The Responsories for Sexagesima Begin

### At the Invitatory

Antiphon: “Let us go before the face of the Lord, and rejoice unto him with psalms.”

### Responsories as above

Responsory: “In the beginning the Lord made heaven and earth, and created in it a human being according to his image and likeness.” Verse: “Then the Lord formed the human being from the clay of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life.” “According to his image.”

Responsory: “In the beginning God made heaven and earth, and created in it a human being according to his image and likeness.” [Col. 0748C] Verse: “Thus the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their adornment.” “According to his image.”

Responsory: “Then the Lord formed the human being from the clay of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life; and the human being became a living soul.” Verse: “Now God had planted a paradise of delight from the beginning, in which he placed the human being whom he had formed.” “And the human being became.”

Responsory: “Therefore the Lord took the human being and placed him in the paradise of delight, to cultivate and guard it.” Verse: “Then he formed him, as above.”

Responsory: “The Lord God said: ‘It is not good for the human being to be alone. Let us make a helper like himself.’” Verse: “But for Adam no one like [variant: simile, ‘a like thing’] him was found.” Then God said: “Let us make.”

Responsory: “The Lord cast a deep sleep upon Adam, and took one of his ribs, and built the rib that the Lord had taken into a woman, and brought her to Adam to see what he would call her. And he called her ‘woman,’ because she was taken from man.” Verse: “This now is bone from my bones, and flesh from my flesh.” “And he called her.”

Responsory: “The Lord said to Adam: ‘From the tree that is in the middle of paradise you shall not eat; in whatever hour you eat from it, you shall die the death.’” Verse: “From every tree of paradise eat, but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil do not eat.” “In whatever hour.”

Responsory: “While the Lord was walking in paradise in the afternoon breeze, he called out and said: ‘Adam, where are you?’ ‘I heard your voice, Lord, and I hid myself.’” Verse: “Lord, I heard your report and was afraid; I considered your works and trembled.” “And I hid myself.”

Responsory: “‘In the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread,’ the Lord said to Adam. ‘When you work the ground, it will not yield its fruits to you, but will produce thorns and thistles for you.’” Verse: “Because you obeyed [variant: listened to] the voice of your wife more than me, cursed is the earth in your work.” “It will not yield its fruits.”

Responsory: “Behold, Adam has become like [one] of us, knowing good and evil. See that he does not perhaps take from the tree of life and live forever.” [Col. 0749A] Verse: “The cherubim and the flaming, turning sword, to guard the way to the tree of life.” “See.”

Responsory: “‘Where is Abel your brother?’ the Lord said to Cain. ‘I do not know, Lord; am I my brother’s keeper?’ And he said to him: ‘What have you done? Behold, the voice of the blood of your brother Abel cries out to me from the earth.’” Verse: “Cursed is the earth in your work, which has opened its mouth and received your brother’s blood [variant: the blood of your brother] from your hand.” “Behold, the voice.”

## The Responsories for Quinquagesima

### At the Invitatory

Antiphon: “For God is the great Lord, and the great King over all the earth.”

### Responsories

Responsory: “For forty days and nights the heavens were opened, and those having [variant: habentium, ‘of those having’] the spirit of life from every flesh entered into the ark. And the Lord shut the door from outside.” Verse: “But Noah, his wife, and the wives of his sons.” “Entered.”

Responsory: “The Lord said to Noah: ‘The end of all flesh has come before me; the earth is filled with their iniquity, and I will destroy them together with the earth.’” Verse: “Make yourself an ark of smoothed wood; you shall make compartments in the ark.” “The earth is filled.”

Responsory: “Noah, a just and perfect man, walked with God, and did everything that God commanded him.” Verse: “And Noah made himself an ark so that he might be saved with all his offspring.”

Responsory: “I will set my bow in the clouds of heaven,” says the Lord to Noah, “and I will remember my covenant that I made with you.” Verse: “And when I cover the heavens with clouds, my bow will appear in the clouds.”

Responsory: “By myself I have sworn,” says the Lord; “I will not add further to the waters of the flood over the earth. I will remember my covenant, so that I will not destroy all flesh with the waters of the flood.” Verse: “I will set my bow in the clouds of heaven, and I will swear by my right hand.”

Responsory: “Noah built an altar to the Lord, offering upon it a burnt offering. The Lord smelled the fragrance of sweetness and blessed them: ‘Increase, multiply, and fill the earth.’” Verse: “Behold, I will establish my covenant with you and with your offspring after you.” “Increase.”

### Responsories concerning Abraham

Responsory: “The Lord spoke to Abraham, saying: ‘Go out from your land and from your kindred, and come into the land that I will show you, and I will make you grow into a great nation.’” Verse: “Blessing I will bless you, and I will multiply you.” “And I will make you.”

Responsory: “Three men appeared to Abraham by the river [variant: oak] of Mambre, and he said to them: ‘Lord, if I have found favor in your eyes, pass by and rest in this place.’” Verse: “I will bring a little water, and let your feet be washed.” “And rest.”

Responsory: “While Abraham was standing at the root of Mambre, he saw three boys descending along the road; he saw three and worshiped one.” Verse: “The Lord said to Abraham: ‘Behold, Sarah your wife will bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac.’” “He saw three.”

Responsory: “God tested Abraham and said to him: ‘Take your son, whom you love, Isaac, and offer him there as a burnt offering upon one of the mountains that I will tell you.’” Verse: “Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.”

Responsory: “The angel of the Lord called to Abraham, saying: ‘Do not stretch out your hand against the boy, because you fear the Lord.’” Verse: “And all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed in you.” “Because you fear.”

Responsory: “The angel of the Lord called to Abraham from heaven, saying: ‘I will bless you, and I will multiply you like the stars of heaven.’” Verse: “And all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in your offspring, because you obeyed my voice.” “And I will multiply.”

Responsory: “God of my lord Abraham, direct my way, so that I may return safely to the house of my lord.” Verse: “May the angel who was with Abraham be with me also.” Verse: “God, before whom my fathers walked, Lord, who have fed me from my youth.” “So that I may return safely.”

Responsory: “Today I came to the spring of water and prayed to the Lord, [Col. 0750B] saying: ‘Lord God of Abraham, you have made my desire prosper.’” Verse: “Therefore, the girl to whom I say: ‘Give me water from your jar to drink,’ and she says: ‘Drink, lord, and I will also give water to your camels’—she is the one whom the Lord has prepared for the son of my lord.” “Lord God.”

Responsory: “A blind man was sitting beside the road while the Lord was passing by, and he cried out to him. The Lord said to him: ‘What do you want me to do for you?’ ‘Rabboni, that I may see the light.’” Verse: “Those who went before rebuked him so that he would be silent, but he cried out all the more: ‘Rabboni.’”

Responsory: “‘Lord, my servant is lying paralyzed in the house and is suffering terribly.’ ‘Amen, I say to you, I will come and heal him.’” Verse: “‘Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant will be healed.’” “Amen, I say.”

## Responsories for the Beginning of Lent

### Responsories as above

Responsory: “Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now are the days of salvation. Let us commend ourselves in great patience, in many fasts, through the weapons of the justice of God’s power.” Verse: “In all things let us present ourselves as God’s ministers, so that our ministry may not be reviled.” “Through the weapons.”

Responsory: “The season of fasting has opened for us the gates of paradise. Let us receive it, praying and entreating, so that on the day of Resurrection we may rejoice in glory with the Lord.” Verse: “Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now are the days of salvation, giving no one any offense.” “So that on the day.”

Responsory: “Let us amend for the better the things in which we have sinned unknowingly, lest, suddenly overtaken by the day of death, we seek time for repentance and be unable to find it. Attend, Lord, and have mercy, because we have sinned against you.” Verse: “We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted unjustly; we have committed iniquity.” “Attend.”

Responsory: “In fasting and weeping the priests prayed, saying: ‘Spare, Lord, spare your people, and do not give your inheritance over to destruction.’” Verse: “Between the vestibule and the altar the priests wept, saying: ‘Spare.’”

Responsory: “In all things let us present ourselves as God’s ministers, in great patience, so that our ministry may not be reviled.”

Responsory: “Behold, now is the acceptable time, as above.” “So that our ministry may not be reviled.”

Responsory: “Hide your alms in the breast of the poor, and it will itself pray for you to the Lord; for just as water extinguishes fire, so almsgiving extinguishes sin.” Verse: “Honor the Lord from your substance, and give to the poor from the firstfruits of your crops.” “For just as.”

Responsory: “I would be troubled if I did not know your mercies, Lord. You have said: ‘I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live’—you who called the Canaanite woman and the tax collector to repentance.” Verse: “And the Lord received Peter as he wept, the merciful Lord.” “Who called the Canaanite woman.”

Responsory: “He has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways. They will carry you in their hands, lest you ever strike your foot against a stone.” Verse: “You will walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you will trample the lion and the dragon.” “They will carry you in their hands.”

Responsory: “‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; now I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.’” Verse: “‘How many hired servants in my father’s house have an abundance of bread, while I am perishing here from hunger? I will arise and go to my father, and I will say to him: Make me.’”

Responsory: “In you, Lord, let all souls hope, saying: ‘God will soon have mercy on us,’ because you, Lord, have spoken, saying: ‘I rejoice [variant: magis, ‘more’] over one repentant sinner than over ninety-nine righteous persons who have no need of repentance.’” Verse: “Call upon me on the day of your tribulation. I will deliver you, and you will glorify me.” But God said to the sinner: “I rejoice.” [Col. 0752A]

Responsory: “I will say to God: ‘You are my protector; my God, I will hope in him,’ because he himself has delivered me from the snare of hunters and from the harsh word.” Verse: “His truth will surround you with a shield; you will not fear the terror of the night.” “My God.”

Responsory: “He will overshadow you with his shoulders, and under his wings you will hope. His truth will surround you with a shield.” Verse: “A thousand will fall at your side, and ten thousand at his right hand.” “With a shield.”

## Antiphons of the Apostles

[Note: Perhaps from the Apostle, since, just as the preceding antiphons have been collected from the Gospel and therefore are said ‘in the Gospel,’ so these too may be said to be from the Apostle, because they are drawn from Paul’s Epistle—at least most of them.]

[Col. 0752C]

Antiphon: “Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now are the days of salvation. Therefore, in these days let us present ourselves as God’s ministers, in great patience, in fasts and vigils, and in sincere love.”

Antiphon: “Let us commend ourselves in great patience, in many fasts, through the weapons of justice.”

Antiphon: “Through the weapons of the justice of God’s power, let us commend ourselves in great patience.”

Antiphon: “The days of repentance have come upon us for redeeming sins, but [for] saving souls.”

Antiphon: “Repent; the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”

### Responsories

Responsory: “When Joseph’s brothers saw him from a distance, they spoke among themselves, saying: ‘Behold, the dreamer is coming. Come, let us kill him and see whether his dreams will benefit him.’” Verse: “When Joseph’s brothers saw that he was loved by his father more than all his brothers, they hated him and could not speak peacefully to him; therefore they said: ‘Come.’”

Responsory: “Judah said to his brothers: ‘Behold, the Ishmaelites are passing by. Come, let us sell him, and let our hands not be defiled; for he is our flesh and our brother.’” Verse: “When Reuben had gone to the pit and did not find him, he tore his clothes and, returning to his brothers, said: ‘The boy is not present, and where shall I go?’” “For he is our flesh.”

Responsory: “Drawing Joseph out of the pit, they sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. When Reuben returned to the pit and did not find him, he tore his garments with weeping and said: ‘The boy is not present, and where shall I go?’” Verse: “But they dipped Joseph’s tunic in blood and sent someone to carry it to his father and say: ‘See whether this is your son’s tunic or not.’” “The boy is not present.”

Responsory: “When Jacob saw Joseph’s garments, he tore his clothes with weeping and said: ‘A most savage beast has devoured my son Joseph.’” Verse: “See whether this is your son’s tunic or not; and when the father had seen it, he said: ‘A most savage beast.’”

Responsory: “When Joseph entered the land of Egypt, he heard a language that he did not know; his hands served in labor, and his tongue spoke wisdom among princes.” Verse: “He turned his back away from burdens.” “His hands.”

Responsory: “Remember me when it goes well with you, so that you may mention me to Pharaoh, that he may bring me out of this prison, because I was stolen away and was innocently thrown into this pit.” Verse: “For there are still three days, after which Pharaoh will remember your service and restore you to your former position; then remember me.” “That you may mention me.”

Responsory: “Take gifts with you from here and go to the lord of the land; and when you find him, worship him upon the ground. May my God make him favorable to you, and may he bring back with you this brother of yours and the one whom he holds in bonds.” Verse: “Take some of the fruits of the earth in your vessels, and carry gifts to the man.” “May my God.”

Responsory: “‘Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me? May God have mercy on you, my son.’ And he hurried into the house and wept, because the tears were bursting forth and he could not contain himself.” Verse: “Joseph lifted his eyes and saw Benjamin standing there. All his inward parts were moved with compassion for his brother.” “Because the tears were bursting forth.”

Responsory: “Reuben said to his brothers: ‘Did I not tell you, “Do not sin against the boy,” and you did not listen to me? Behold, his blood is required.’” Verse: “We rightly suffer these things, because we sinned against our brother, seeing the anguish of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. Therefore this tribulation has come upon us.” “Behold, his blood.”

Responsory: “We rightly suffer these things, because we sinned against our brother, seeing the anguish of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. Therefore this tribulation has come upon us.” Verse: “Reuben said to his brothers: ‘Did I not tell you, “Do not sin against the boy,” and you did not listen to me?’” “Therefore.”

Responsory: “Joseph said to his eleven brothers: ‘I am Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt. Is our aged father still alive, of whom you spoke to me? Go, bring him to me, so that he may live.’” Verse: “It is two years since the famine began in the land; five more still remain.” “Go, bring him.”

Responsory: “Go, tell my father Jacob: ‘Joseph your son is alive, and he rules over the whole land of Egypt.’ When he heard this, his spirit revived, and he said: ‘It is enough for me; I will go and see him before I die.’” Verse: “When Jacob heard that his son was alive, as though awakening from a deep sleep, he said: ‘It is enough.’”

Responsory: “Joseph, speaking to his brothers, said: ‘Peace be with you; do not fear, for the Lord sent me before you for your preservation.’” Verse: “Do not fear, and let it not seem harsh to you that you sold me in these regions.” “For your preservation.”

Responsory: “Our salvation is in your hand, Lord; may your mercy look upon us, and we will serve you without fear.” Verse: “Lord God of hosts, restore us, and show us your face, and we shall be saved.” “And we will serve you without fear.” Verse: “May your life be spared, lord, so that we may not see death or our little ones failing.” “And we will serve you without fear.”

## Responsories for the fourth week in Lent

### At the Invitatory

Antiphon. “Do not rise before the light in vain, for the Lord has promised a crown to those who keep vigil.” Antiphon. “The people of the Lord and the sheep of his pasture.”

### Responsories

**Responsory.** The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: [Col. 0757B] “Go down to Egypt; tell Pharaoh to let my people go.” Pharaoh’s heart has been hardened; he does not wish to let my people go except by a strong hand.  
**Verse.** “I have indeed seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt; I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to deliver them.”  
*Hardened.*

**Responsory.** Moses stood before Pharaoh and said: “Thus says the Lord: Let my people go, so that they may sacrifice to me in the wilderness.”  
**Verse.** “The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you; he says to you: Let [them] go.”  
*Let [them] go.*

**Responsory.** “Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously exalted: horse and rider he has cast into the sea. The Lord has become my helper and protector for salvation.”  
**Verse.** “Pharaoh’s chariots and his army he cast into the sea.”  
*The helper.*

**Responsory.** “In the sea was your way, and your paths in many waters. You led your people like sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.”  
**Verse.** “Your flashes illumined the world; the earth was shaken and trembled.”  
*By the hand of Moses.*

**Responsory.** “Behold, I send my angel, who will go before you and always guard you. Observe and hear his voice, and I will be an enemy to your enemies and afflict those who [Col. 0757C] afflict you; and my angel will go before you.”  
**Verse.** “Israel, if you will listen to me, there will be no new god among you, nor will you worship a foreign god; for I am the Lord.”  
*And my angel will go before you.*

**Responsory.** “Those who persecuted your people, O Lord, you plunged into the depths, and in the pillar of cloud you were their guide, O Lord.”  
**Verse.** “The children of Israel cried out to you, O Lord, in their distress, and you sent them a Savior.”  
*And in the pillar.*

**Responsory.** “Moses, the servant of the Lord, fasted forty days and forty nights, so that he might deserve to receive the law of the Lord.”  
**Verse.** “Moses ascended Mount Sinai.”  
*That he might receive the law.*

**Responsory.** “The face of Moses became radiant while the Lord looked upon him. When the elders saw the splendor of his face, they were greatly afraid in amazement.”  
**Verse.** “Moses descended from the mountain carrying in his hands two stone tablets, both written by the finger of God.”  
*When they saw.*

**Responsory.** “Attend, my people, to my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth.”  
**Verse.** “I will open my mouth in parables; I will speak sayings [Col. 0757D] from the beginning of the world.”  
*Incline.*

**Responsory.** “Hear, Israel, the commands of the Lord, and write them in your heart as in a book; and I will give you a land flowing with milk and honey.”  
**Verse.** “Israel, if you will listen to me, there will be no new god among you, nor will you worship a foreign god.”  
*And I will give you.*

**Responsory.** “You who are about to cross the Jordan, build an altar to the Lord from stones that iron has not touched, and offer upon it a burnt offering and peace offerings to your God.”  
**Verse.** “When you enter the land that the Lord your God is about to give you, [770] build an altar there to your God.”
*Build an altar to your God.*

**Responsory.** “The Lord brought them into the strength of the land; he fed them with the corrupt printed phrase *nascentibus agros* (‘with things springing up—fields’; accusative *agros*), with the variant *in agris* (‘in the fields’); they sucked honey from the rock, and oil from the firm rock.”  
**Verse.** “Butter of cattle and milk of sheep, with the fat of lambs, young cattle, and goats.”  
*They sucked.*

## Responsories concerning Joshua

**Responsory.** “As I was with Moses, so I will be with you,” says the Lord. “Be strong and courageous; you will bring my people into a land flowing with milk and honey.” [Col. 0758A]  
**Verse.** “I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.”  
*Be strong.*  
**Verse.** “For the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”  
*Be strong.*

**Responsory.** “As I was with Moses, so I will be with you,” says the Lord. “Strengthen my people, and do not be afraid. Behold, the Lord your God is with you, and he will not abandon you.”  
**Verse.** “For he is with you,” as above.

**Responsory.** “My people, what have I done to you, or in what have I troubled you? Answer me. For I brought you out of the land of Egypt and from the house of slavery. For forty years I rained manna upon you, and you have forgotten me,” says the Lord.  
**Verse.** “I led you through the wilderness for forty years—I, the Lord.”  
*And you have forgotten me.*

**Responsory.** “I led you through the wilderness for forty years—I, the Lord; your garments have not worn out. I rained manna upon you from heaven, and you have forgotten me,” says the Lord. [Col. 0758B]  
**Verse.** “My people, what have I done to you, or in what have I troubled you? Answer me. For I brought you out of the land of Egypt.”  
*Manna from heaven.*
