## Responsories concerning the Passion of the Lord

### At the Invitatory

Antiphon. “Today, if you hear the voice of the Lord, do not harden your hearts.” [Col. 0759B]

**Responsory.** “These are the days that you must observe at their appointed times. On the fourteenth day, toward evening, is the Passover of the Lord, and on the fifteenth day you shall celebrate the *solemnitatis* [*solemnitatem*, ‘solemnity’] to the Most High Lord.”  
**Verse.** The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them.”  
*The fourteenth.*

**Responsory.** “Those who trouble me have multiplied, and they say: ‘There is no salvation for him in his God.’ Arise, O Lord; save me, my God.”  
**Verse.** “Lest my enemy should say: ‘I have prevailed against him.’”  
*Arise.*

**Responsory.** “Those who guarded my life took counsel together, saying: ‘God has abandoned him; pursue and seize him, for there is no one to deliver him.’ My God, do not withdraw from me; my God, attend to my help.”  
**Verse.** “All my enemies were devising evil against me; they sent an evil word against me, saying…” [772]  
*Pursue.*

**Responsory.** “You are my helper and my protector, O Lord, and I have hoped in your word. Depart from me, evildoers, and I will search out the commandments of my God.” [Col. 0759C]  
**Verse.** “Deliver me from my enemies, my God, and free me from those who rise up against me.”  
*Depart from me.*

**Responsory.** “Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from an unholy nation. Deliver me from an unjust and deceitful man, for you are my God and my strength.”  
**Verse.** “Send forth your light and your truth.”  
*For you are.*

**Responsory.** “You are my God; do not depart from me, for tribulation is near, and there is no one to help.”  
**Verse.** “My God, look upon me; why have you abandoned me? You are far from my salvation.”  
*For tribulation.*

**Responsory.** “My God, deliver me from the hand of the sinner and from the hand of the lawless and unjust man, for you are my patience.”  
**Verse.** “Deliver me from my enemies,” as above.  
*For you are.*

**Responsory.** “Do not destroy my soul with the wicked, O God, nor my life with men of blood; redeem me, O Lord.”  
**Verse.** “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man; free me from the unjust man.”  
*Redeem me.*

**Responsory.** “All day long I went about sorrowing, O Lord, for my soul is full of mockeries, and those who sought my life used violence against me.” [Col. 0759D]  
**Verse.** “Those who sought evil against me spoke empty things, and all day long they devised deceits.”  
*They used violence.*

**Responsory.** “Do not turn your face away from your servant, O Lord, for I am troubled; hear me quickly.”  
**Verse.** “Deliver me from the evil man, for I am troubled.”

**Responsory.** “My tribulation is near, O Lord, and there is no one to help, that they may pierce my hands and my feet (*ut fodiant manus meas et pedes meos*, a purpose clause with an implied ‘they’). Deliver me from the mouth of the lion, that I may declare your name to my brothers.”  
**Verse.** “My God, my God, look upon me; why have you abandoned me? You are far from my salvation.”  
*Deliver me.*

**Responsory.** “Upon you I was cast from the womb; from my mother’s womb you are my God. Do not depart from me, for tribulation is near, and there is no one to help.”  
**Verse.** “Deliver my soul from the sword, O God, and my only one from the hand of the dog.”  
*For tribulation.*

**Responsory.** “See that I am troubled; hear me quickly. Attend to my soul and deliver it because of my enemies. Deliver me, O Lord.”  
**Verse.** “Deliver me from my enemies,” as above. [Col. 0760A]

**Responsory.** “My enemies spoke peacefully to me, but in anger they were troublesome to me. You have seen, O Lord; do not be silent; do not depart from me.”  
**Verse.** “All my enemies were against me.”

**Responsory.** “Give me, O Lord, a sign for good, so that those who hate me may see and be confounded, because you, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.”  
**Verse.** “Look upon me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and poor.”

**Responsory.** “I will teach the wicked your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to you. Deliver me from bloodshed, God of my salvation.”  
**Verse.** “Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will proclaim your praise.”  
*Deliver me.*

**Responsory.** “You girded me with strength for battle and brought down my enemies beneath me. You gave me the backs of my enemies, and you destroyed those who hate me.”  
**Verse.** “I will pursue my enemies and seize them, and I will not turn back until they are exhausted.”  
*And you gave me the backs of my enemies.*

**Responsory.** “My deliverer from angry nations, free me from those who rise up against me.”  
**Verse.** “Deliver me from my enemies.”  
*From those who rise up against me.*

**Responsory.** “Deliver my soul from the sword, O God, and my only one from the hand of the dog—my humiliation.” [Col. 0760B]  
**Verse.** “Deliver me, O Lord, from the man.”

**Responsory.** “Deliver me, O Lord, from the mouth of the lion and from the horns of the unicorns—my humiliation.”  
**Verse.** “Deliver me from the sword.”

**Responsory.** “Princes persecuted me without cause, but my heart feared your words. I will rejoice over your sayings.”  
**Verse.** “As one who finds abundant spoils.” [773]  
*I will rejoice.*

**Responsory.** “How long will my enemy be exalted over me? Look upon me and hear me, O Lord my God.”  
**Verse.** “Those who trouble me will rejoice if I am shaken; but I have hoped in your mercy.”  
*Look upon me.*

Verse. “Deliver me from my enemies, my God.”

Verse. “From the mouth of the lion.”

## Responsories for Holy Week on Palm Sunday

### At the Invitatory

Antiphon. “They themselves did not know my ways, concerning which I swore in my anger that they would not enter into my rest.”

**Responsory.** “On the day when I called upon you, O Lord, you said: ‘Do not fear.’ You judged my cause and delivered me, my God.”  
**Verse.** “My God, deliver me from the hand of the sinner and from the hand of the lawless and unjust man.”  
*You judged.*

**Responsory.** “My brothers have withdrawn far from me, and my acquaintances have departed from me like strangers.”  
**Verse.** “My friends and neighbors drew near and stood.”  
*Like strangers.*

**Responsory.** “Attend, O Lord, to me, and hear the voices of my adversaries. Is evil repaid for good, because they dug a pit for my soul?”  
**Verse.** “The man of my peace, in whom I trusted, enlarged his treachery against me.”  
*Is evil repaid?*

**Responsory.** “The enemy closed my ways; he became a lurking foe like a lion in hiding. He filled me and made me drunk with bitterness. They led my life down into the pit of death and placed a stone against me. See, O Lord, their iniquities, and judge the cause of my soul, defender of my life.” [Col. 0761D]  
**Verse.** “All my enemies were devising evil against me; they sent an evil word against me.”  
*See.*

**Responsory.** “Save me, O God, for the waters have entered even to my soul. Do not turn your face away from me, for I am troubled; hear me, my God.”  
**Verse.** “Attend to my soul and deliver it; because of my enemies, deliver me.”  
*For I am troubled.*

**Responsory.** “Do not be a stranger to me, O Lord. Spare me, O Lord, on the evil day; let all who persecute me be confounded, and let me not be confounded.”  
**Verse.** “Let all my enemies be confounded.”  
*And let me not be confounded.*

**Responsory.** As the Lord entered the holy city, the children of the Hebrews, announcing the resurrection of life, cried out “Hosanna in the highest,” with palm branches. [775] [Col. 0762A]  
**Verse.** “From the mouths of infants and nursing children you have perfected praise.”  
*With palm branches.*

**Responsory.** “The Lord is with me like a mighty warrior; therefore they persecuted me, but they have not understood. Lord, who tests the kidneys and hearts, I have revealed my cause to you.”  
**Verse.** “Those who sought my life used violence, and those who sought evil against me spoke empty things.”  
*But they have not understood.*

**Responsory.** The ungodly, thinking not rightly, said among themselves: “Let us ensnare the just man, because he is opposed to our works. He claims to possess knowledge of God; he calls himself a son of God, and boasts that he has God as his Father. Let us see whether his words are true; and if he is truly the Son of God, let him deliver him from our hands. Let us condemn him to a most shameful death.”  
**Verse.** “Ungodly men said: ‘Let us oppress the just man unjustly, and let us cast lots for his spoils.’”  
*Let us see.*

**Responsory.** “Ungodly men said: ‘Let us oppress the just man unjustly and swallow him up as the underworld swallows the living. Let us remove his memory from the earth, and let us cast lots among ourselves for his spoils.’ [Col. 0762B] For those murderers have stored up evil for themselves; the foolish and wicked have hated wisdom, and they have been found guilty in their thoughts.”  
**Verse.** “The ungodly, thinking not rightly, said among themselves: ‘Let us ensnare the just man.’”  
*And they have been found guilty.*

**Responsory.** “I have become exceedingly a reproach to my enemies; they saw me and shook their heads. Help me, O Lord my God.”  
**Verse.** “I will pursue my enemies and seize them, and I will not turn back until they are exhausted.”  
*Help me, O Lord.*

**Responsory.** “Wicked men rose against me without mercy; they sought to kill me and did not spare spitting in my face. They wounded me with their spears, and all my bones were shaken. But I reckoned myself as one dead upon the earth.”  
**Verse.** “They gave gall as my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.”  
*But I.*

**Responsory.** “The souls of the wicked were raging against me, and my heart was weighed down because of them; and they set a price of thirty pieces of silver, for which I was valued by them.”  
**Verse.** “I endured insults and terrors from those who were my peaceful companions.” [Col. 0762C]  
*And they set a price.*

**Responsory.** “I endured insults and terrors from those who were my peaceful companions, and those guarding my side, saying: ‘Let us deceive him and prevail against him.’ But you, O Lord, are with me like a mighty warrior. They will fall into everlasting disgrace. And I shall see vengeance upon them, because I revealed my cause to you.”  
**Verse.** “All my enemies,” as above.  
*Saying.*

**Responsory.** “I was led like a lamb to be slaughtered, and I did not know it; but they devised a plot against me. Yet you, O Lord, delivered my soul.”  
**Verse.** “All my enemies,” as above.

**Responsory.** “God of Israel, for your sake I endured reproach; reverence covered my face. I became a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to the sons of my mother, because zeal for your house consumed me.”  
**Verse.** “Attend to my soul and deliver it; because of my enemies, deliver me.”  
*Because zeal.*  
**Verse.** “My God, my God, look upon me,” as above.

**Responsory.** “The assembly of the peoples surrounded me, and I did not repay evil to those who repaid me. Let the wickedness of sinners be consumed, O Lord, and direct the just.” [Col. 0762D]  
**Verse.** “But you, O Lord, are my protector, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.”  
*Let it be consumed.*

Antiphon. “The Lord God is my helper, and therefore I am not confounded.”

### In the Gospel

Antiphon. The great crowd that had gathered for the feast cried out [*clamabat*; variant *clamabat ad Dominum*, ‘cried to the Lord’]: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; hosanna in the highest.”  
Antiphon. “Hosanna to the Son of David; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel; hosanna in the highest.” [Col. 0763A]  
Antiphon. The crowds go out with flowers and palms to meet the Redeemer, offering fitting homage to the victorious triumphant one. The nations proclaim the Son of God with their mouths, and voices resound through the clouds in praise of Christ. Hosanna.  
Antiphon. Today, indeed, the foliage of trees served Christ with a human tongue. And although the branches had been rigid, they sent the King the spoils of the trees, bent down. Hosanna.  
Antiphon. The children of the Hebrews spread their garments on the road and cried out, saying: “Hosanna to the Son of David. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.”  
Antiphon. The children of the Hebrews, carrying olive branches, went out to meet the Lord, crying out and saying: “Hosanna in the highest.”  
Antiphon. “I have revealed my cause to you, defender of my life; the Lord my God.”  
Antiphon. “I will call upon your name, O Lord; do not turn your anger [face] away from my cry.”  
Antiphon. “I have been sent to the sheep that had perished from the house of Israel,” says the Lord.  
Antiphon. “All praise your name and will say: ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; hosanna in the highest.’”  
Antiphon. All the crowds who were descending began joyfully to praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen, saying: “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord. Peace in heaven and glory in the highest.” [Col. 0763B]  
Antiphon. “King of Israel, hosanna in the highest.”

### Responsories

**Responsory.** “My friend betrayed me by the sign of a kiss, *osculum* [*osculi*, ‘of a kiss’]; the one whom I kiss is he—seize him. This evil sign performed the deed, fulfilling murder through a kiss. The wretched man abandoned the price of blood and finally hanged himself by a noose.”  
**Verse.** “It would have been better for him if he had not been born.”  
*Who through.*

**Responsory.** “Judas, the worst of merchants, asks the Lord for a kiss. He, like an innocent Lamb, does not refuse Judas’s kiss. For a number of denarii he betrayed Christ to the Jews.”  
**Verse.** “It would have been better.”

**Responsory.** “One of my disciples will betray me today. Woe to him through whom I shall be betrayed. It would have been better for him if he had not been born.”  
**Verse.** “The one who dips his hand with me into the dish is the one who will betray me into the hands of sinners.”  
*It would have been better.*

**Responsory.** “I was like an innocent lamb led to be sacrificed, and I did not know it; my enemies devised a plot against me, saying: ‘Let us put wood in his bread and destroy him from the land of the living.’”  
**Verse.** “All my enemies were devising evil against me; they sent an evil word against me, saying…” [Col. 0765A]

**Responsory.** “You were unable to keep watch with me for one hour, though you were exhorting [one another] to die for me (*exhortabamini mori pro me*; *pro me* means ‘for me’). Or do you not see Judas—how he does not sleep but hastens to betray me to the Jews?”  
**Verse.** “Sleep now and rest; behold, the one who will betray me is drawing near.”  
*Or Judas.*

Antiphon. “I said to the wicked: ‘Do not speak iniquity against God.’”  
Psalm: “We will give thanks.”  
Antiphon. “The earth trembled and was quiet when God rose up for judgment.”  
Psalm: “Known in Judea.”  
Antiphon. “On the day of my tribulation I sought God with my hands.”

### Responsories

**Responsory.** The elders of the people took counsel to seize and kill Jesus by deceit. They went out with swords and clubs, as against a robber. [Col. 0756B]  
**Verse.** “They gathered iniquity for themselves and went out.”  
*With swords.*

**Responsory.** “The heavens will reveal the iniquity of Judas, and the earth will rise up against him; his sin will be made manifest on the day of the Lord’s wrath, together with those who said to my Lord: ‘Depart from us; we do not wish to know your ways.’”  
**Verse.** “Let their table before them become a snare, a retribution, and a stumbling block.”  
*Together with those.*

**Responsory.** “Behold, the crowd, and he who was called Judas came; and as he approached Jesus to kiss him, Jesus said to him: ‘Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss to be crucified?’”  
**Verse.** “The Son of Man indeed goes as it is written concerning him. Woe to that man through whom I shall be betrayed.”  
*To be crucified.*

**Responsory.** “O Judas, who abandoned the counsel of peace, and who took counsel with the Jews: for thirty pieces of silver you sold the righteous blood, and you carried the kiss of peace, *quae* [*quam*], which you did not have in your heart.” [779]  
**Verse.** “The truthful one is handed over to deceivers; the pious man is scourged by the impious.”  
*And of peace.*

**Responsory.** “The tongue of the wicked became deceitful in their mouths, and they spoke falsehood. All lay in wait for blood; they sold the just man to death. But he himself spoke words of peace to the Jews.” [Col. 0765C]  
**Verse.** “Why do you seek to kill a man who has spoken the truth to you?”  
*But he himself.*
**Antiphon:** Be vindicated, O Lord, in your words, and prevail when you are judged.  
**Psalm:** Have mercy on me.

**Antiphon:** The Lord was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and he did not open his mouth.  
**Psalm:** O Lord, you have been our refuge.

**Antiphon:** My heart was broken within me; all my bones trembled.  
**Psalm:** O God, my God.

**Antiphon:** You have exhorted by your strength and by your holy refreshment, O Lord.  
**Psalm:** Let us sing.

**Antiphon:** He himself bore. He was offered because he himself willed it, and our sins.  
**Psalm:** Praise the Lord from the heavens.

**Verse:** Christ became obedient for us.

**Antiphon:** His judgment was taken away in humiliation. Who will declare his generation?

**Antiphon:** Pilate said: “My hands are clean from the blood of this just man; you will see to it.”

# Here begins the order for Vespers

[Col. 0770C]

[Note: Nearly the same things are found in Roman Order 1, edited by Mabillon, *Musaei Italici*, vol. II. See p. 36 and following.]

When the schola has assembled early with the bishops and deacons in the greater church—

[785]

[Note: Namely, where a statue of Christ affixed to the cross had been placed, as it still is in the lower part of the choir.]

—they begin *Kyrie eleison* at the place of the crucified one and proceed as far as the altar. When the deacons have ascended the *podium*—

[Note: Or platform. Cangius understands this as the *lectrum* or *analectrum* in the church, reached by steps, and cites this very passage from the Roman Order. According to Mabillon, in his notes on Roman Order 1, the *pogium* is the place of the screens separating the sanctuary from the choir, so called because it rises gradually by steps.]

—the bishops and priests take their places, and the schola stands before the altar. When *Kyrie eleison* is finished, the archdeacon signals to the first singer of the schola, who bows and begins *alleluia* with Psalm 109, “The Lord said to my Lord.” After this he signals to the second singer, or to whomever he wishes; and he gives the same instruction to all who begin. Let *alleluia* be sung again with Psalm 110, “I will give thanks to you.” After this, the first singer of the schola follows with the *paraphonists* at the fonts, *alleluia*. The paraphonists respond. The subdeacons follow with the children, *alleluia*. “The Lord reigns; he is clothed in beauty”; and the paraphonists always respond and signal the words to the children.

**Verse:** Your throne is prepared.

**Verse:** The rivers have lifted up.

After these verses the first singer of the schola greets the archdeacon; when the archdeacon signals, he begins *alleluia* with melodies for the children. When this is completed, the paraphonists respond first, and it ends.

[Col. 0770D]

After this the third *alleluia* begins with Psalm 1, “Blessed is the man.” This is followed by “Christ our Passover.”

**Verse:** Let us feast.

When this is completed with the Prayer, as above, the archdeacon begins.

**Antiphon:** I know that you are seeking Jesus who was crucified; he has risen, alleluia.

**Antiphon:** Jesus whom you seek is not here, but he has risen. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee, alleluia.

After this the priest says the Prayer, and they descend to the fonts with the antiphon.

[Col. 0771A]

**Antiphon:** On the day of my resurrection, says the Lord, alleluia: I will gather the nations and assemble the kingdoms, and I will pour clean water over you, alleluia.

When they have finished it, the first singer of the schola says *alleluia* with Psalm 112, “Praise the Lord, children”; *alleluia* follows.

In Greek: “The Lord [gives] strength,” etc., with the order completed as above.

Afterward the second deacon proceeds in the Gospel.

**Antiphon:** Come and see the place where the Lord was laid, alleluia.

Then the priest says the Prayer, and they go to Saint John—

[Note: In the Vulgate of Alcuin, “to the fonts,” or “to the vestment.” Perhaps at this place those being baptized removed their clothing, or the baptized put on a white garment.]

—to the vestment, singing the antiphon:

**Antiphon:** The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone, alleluia. This was done by the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes, alleluia, alleluia.

Then *alleluia* with Psalm 113, “When Israel went out.”

Then the first singer of the schola says *alleluia* with the children:

**Alleluia. Come, let us exult before the Lord.**

**Verse 1:** Let us go before him.

**Verse 2:** Today, if you hear the voice of the Lord.

After this the deacon follows:

**Antiphon:** Go quickly and tell the disciples that the Lord has risen, alleluia, alleluia.

Then he prays, always without *Kyrie eleison*. And then they go—

[Note: The basilica of Saint Andrew was near the Vatican basilica.]

—to Saint Andrew, to the cross—

[Col. 0771B]

—singing the antiphon:

**Antiphon:** I saw water flowing from the Temple on the right side, alleluia; and all to whom this water came were saved, alleluia, alleluia.

After this they say *alleluia*: “I loved, because the Lord will hear.”

When this is finished, the first singer of the schola begins *alleluia*: “Come, let us exult,” as above.

**Antiphon:** Go quickly and tell the disciples.

Then the Prayer.

Then the leaders of the church descend to the banquet, invited by the notary of the vicedominus, and drink three times of *de Graeco* wine, *depactissi*, and *procantu*.

[Note: In the Roman Order already cited, *de Graeco*, *de pactis*, and *de procoma*. Mabillon supplies many variant readings for this passage. These words designate places where these kinds of wine were produced.]

After all the priests, deacons, subdeacons, and acolytes in each title-church have drunk, they return to celebrate Vespers, and drink what has been given by the priest. This practice is observed throughout the whole week until the Sunday in White Garments.

[786]

—and the rest.

Then, after Psalm 112, *alleluia* follows.

*Opimenonthon*, etc.

# Sunday of the Octave of Easter
Psalm: “Blessed is the man,” through “O Lord, in your strength,” are to be sung as on the other Sundays at Matins. Versicle: “Shout joyfully to God, all the earth.” Versicle: “Sing to the Lord.” Versicle: “Do not weep, Mary.” Versicle: “Tell it among the nations.” Versicle: “The Lord reigns; he is clothed in beauty.” These are to be said on all the days throughout the whole of the Resurrection season.

The responsories are required from Easter until the octave. [Col. 0774D] You must sing these until the third week. [Col. 0784A]

**Antiphon.** Today the venerable solemnity of the most blessed Germanus is recalled, an exultation for the Christian peoples.

**Antiphon.** When he renews the feasts of the Father, he gladdens the hearts of the disciples; honor is rendered to the teacher.

**Antiphon.** And since blessed Germanus walked in all the commandments of Christ, he traversed the surrounding regions and cities for the sake of exhortation.

**Antiphon.** The sick come to the tomb of blessed Germanus and are healed; there they bless God, saying: “Blessed are you, O Lord.”

**Antiphon.** Let us praise the Lord in the glorious memory of the blessed bishop Germanus; the sick come to his tomb and are healed.

## Antiphons and Responsories at the vigil of the holy and most blessed Medard

This is on the sixth day before the Ides of June. At Vespers.

[Col. 0784B]

*(Three lines are missing in the manuscript.)*

**801 Antiphon.** We could not pass over in silence the life of the most blessed bishop Medard, whose virtues are proclaimed throughout the whole world.

Psalm: “Blessed is the man who has not walked.”

**Antiphon.** Let devotion for the ardor of faith increase in the hearts of all, while the greatness of your saints is revealed.

Psalm: “Why did the nations rage?”

**Antiphon.** Thus Saint Medard, by divine Spirit like a prophet, has already proved what he had foretold.

Psalm: “O Lord, how they have increased.”

Verse: “With my voice I cried to the Lord.”

### Responsories as above

**Responsory.** The life of the most blessed bishop Medard, proclaimed throughout the whole world by the distinction of his virtues, invites us to seek the day of his solemnity with veneration, the principal commemoration of his deposition.

Verse: Let devotion for the ardor of faith increase in the hearts of all, while the greatness of your saints is revealed. Of the solemnity.

**Responsory.** While he was still in school, Saint Medard, small and innocent, said to a certain companion of his named Eleutherius that he would one day be the supreme pontiff of God.

Verse: Thus Saint Medard, by divine Spirit like a prophet, has already proved what he had foretold: that he would one day become supreme.

**Responsory.** Therefore, girded with the fervor of faith, while he went about to the oracles of the churches and moderated the choice of his own will by habits of patience, he undertook the ministry of a priest.

Verse: Converted in mind and manner alike, outstanding in the charity of his conduct.

## Antiphons in the second nocturn

**Antiphon.** They meet the most holy man Medard, and, after the prayer has been said, the things they had brought are loosened; they continue on their journeys.

Psalm: “When I called.”

**Antiphon.** Let this also not pass among the other wondrous signs: a certain man named Tasio was afflicted and oppressed by an infestation of adamant [possibly “a diamond-hard affliction”; the reading is uncertain]; he deserved to be healed, and, when the sign of the man of God had been impressed, he rose up unharmed.

Psalm: “Give ear to my words.”

**Antiphon.** But when he was already shining with many kinds of virtuous practices, his fame, increasing through grace, surpassed others throughout the various regions of the world.

Psalm: “O Lord our Lord.”

Verse: “Glory and honor.”

### Responsories as above

**Responsory.** He immediately became renowned before the bishop of the city, distinguished in conduct among all, sincere in purity of mind. Never did he exalt himself more through an abundance of joy; never did he become disturbed through the bitterness of sorrow.

Verse: Yet may his intercession make all more powerful. Never.

**Responsory.** Blessed Medard was always patient in adversity, gentle in prosperity, preferring everyone to himself through his diligence in obedience, and coming to the aid of the needy with generous compassion.

Verse: Having trampled down every source of vice, he ascended with rising step along the narrow path of holy conduct. Preferring everyone to himself.

**Responsory.** Ascending with rising step along the path of holy conduct, blessed Medard chose whatever was precious, so that he might be regarded as a guest in this world and already be a possessor in heaven.

Verse: Chosen, he undertook the office of the priesthood, passing through it according to the established rule of ecclesiastical conduct.

## In the third nocturn

**Antiphon.** When the bishop of the Vermandois had died, blessed Medard was consecrated bishop in his place.

Psalm: “O Lord, who shall dwell?”

**Antiphon.** As a priest of heavenly conduct and holiness, he became precious in the exercise of his office.

Psalm: “O Lord, in your strength.”

**Antiphon.** He continually endured persecution while the devil fought against him, but as a victor he reached the crown through his merits.

Psalm: “The earth is the Lord’s.”

Verse: “You have placed, O Lord.”

**802 Responsories as above**

**Responsory.** The most holy Medard, chosen, undertook the office of the priesthood according to the established rule of ecclesiastical conduct; tested, he attained it, and so conducted himself in virtues that he was thought to be a foster-son of Christ. [A word is missing in the manuscript.]

Verse: But when he was already shining with many kinds of virtuous practices, his fame surpassed others throughout the various regions of the world, increasing through grace. And so.

**Responsory.** Blessed Medard, as a priest of heavenly conduct and holiness, became precious in the exercise of his office; and except that the executioner of the body was lacking—for as a confessor he fulfilled martyrdom.

Verse: He continually endured persecution while the devil fought against him; he reached the crown as a victor through his merits. And except that.

**Responsory.** Then Saint Medard, wearied by a long life, having begged for rest, lost [sent forth] his spirit, and, a triumphant athlete, ascended the vaulted heights of heaven.

Verse: As a priest of heavenly conduct and holiness, he became precious.

**Responsory.** When Saint Medard received the passage of his body, at that very moment [the reading “of his mouth” is corrupt; the manuscript also gives “of the hour”], the heavens were opened, and the divine lights stood before the little body of the saint for all to see.

Verse: Immediately afterward a great flood shone upon the earth, so that much warm water rained from the cloud of the opened heaven.

**Responsory.** And when the holy limbs of blessed Medard were being carried for burial, a certain man came toward them, condemned by the deafness of his ears; while he kissed the veil of precious cloth, he immediately merited by faith to recover his hearing.

Verse: And at once, astonished, he heard the melody of those singing psalms. While.

**Responsory.** It would be lengthy to recount with how many virtues the cry of the infirm rises to blessed Medard; but, when prayers have been poured out, whatever is sought is obtained without delay through his deeds and prayer.

Verse: Therefore, after the urn of his tomb had been adorned and raised with the greatest splendor, supported by the devotion of the faithful.

**Responsory.** Among the worshipers of Christ whom their deeds have carried to the stars, a great portion is open to you according to your merits, O Medard.

Verse: The world was an exile for you, a muddy cave [the manuscript reads *caventa*, probably *caverna*, “cave”].

**Responsory.** The world was an exile for you, a muddy cave, and now heaven rejoices that you remain as a citizen. Stripped of darkness, you are clothed in a covering of light; after death you enjoy a freer day.

Verse: Among the worshipers of Christ, as above.

**Responsory.** What shall I, mute in speech, recount, you who gave words; you who cast out what burdens and place everything that helps? I do not enumerate all things; your praises overcome me.

Verse: A certain blind man came to him and seized healing by touch. In the midst of darkness, open day shone forth. All things.

## Antiphons as above, at night

[Col. 0785D]

**Antiphon.** Saint Medard, having begged for rest, sent forth [lost] his spirit and, a triumphant athlete, ascended the vaulted heights of heaven.

**Antiphon.** Therefore, after the urn of his tomb had been adorned and raised with the greatest splendor, supported by the devotion of the faithful.

**Antiphon.** When prayers have been poured out, whatever is sought is obtained without delay through his deeds.

**Antiphon.** Blessed Medard became a precious priest; as a confessor he fulfilled martyrdom, and as a victor he reached the crown through his merits.

## Antiphons at Lauds

**Antiphon.** Among the worshipers of Christ whom their deeds have carried to the stars, a great portion is open to you according to your merits, O Medard.

**Antiphon.** A certain blind man came to him and seized healing by touch; in the midst of darkness, open day shone forth.

**Antiphon.** Another man, coming when the holy limbs were already being carried, was laid beneath them and merited to possess sight, though blind.

**Antiphon.** The sick come to the tomb of Saint Medard and are healed; there they bless the Lord, saying: “Blessed are you, O Lord.”

**Antiphon.** Another, bound with strong fetters and handcuffs, immediately touched the veil, and the iron bonds fell away.

**803 Antiphon.** May he who today has granted the world the special adornment of his solemnity provide a universal refuge for those bound, for the forgiveness of sins.

### At the Gospel

**Antiphon.** From heaven, warm water came forth from a cloud; at his passing there was a great mystery.

*(One line is missing in the manuscript.)*

**Antiphon.** The principal commemoration of his deposition has supported the veneration with which his solemn day is sought.

**Antiphon.** When Saint Medard received the passage of his body, at that very moment [the manuscript also reads “of the hour”] the heavens were completely opened, and before the little body of the saint the divine lights stood for about three hours; and there was a great mystery.

**Antiphon.** The city of Soissons, enriched by the reward of so great a gift, deserved to receive the solemn pledge of his body, so that, when the most precious limbs of Saint Medard were to be delivered for burial amid the solemn devotion of all the peoples [perhaps “of all the faithful”], they felt the burden of carrying him to be light.

**Antiphon.** And when the holy limbs of blessed Medard were being placed [buried] in the tomb, heaven was opened, and two doves were seen descending like clouds; and from his mouth there emerged a white dove, like snow.

**Antiphon.** Blessed Medard, through the aid of the Trinity, [the manuscript breaks off] the army of the king . . . . a footprint.

**Antiphon.** Saint Medard, born of noble stock, while still young in age but already mature in goodness, foretold [this].

**Antiphon.** The principal commemoration of his deposition invites us to honor the solemnity of blessed Medard with due veneration. Therefore let devotion for the ardor of faith increase in the hearts of all, while the greatness of the holy confessor of God is revealed.

**Antiphon.** Thus the city of Soissons deserved to receive the solemn pledge of the body of the most blessed Medard, enriched by the reward of so great a gift; and when the most precious limbs were being carried on a bier for burial amid the solemn devotion of all the peoples, they felt the burden of carrying him to be light, with one voice and one cry of joy.

## Antiphons and Responsories at the vigil of Saint Paul the apostle

### In the first nocturn

**Antiphon.** He who worked through Peter for the apostleship also worked through me among the nations; and they recognized the grace that was given to me by Christ the Lord.

Psalm: “The heavens declare.”

Verse: He who set me apart from his mother’s womb [the manuscript also reads “from my mother’s womb”] and called me by his grace.

**Antiphon.** I know in whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to preserve my deposit for that day, the righteous Judge.

Psalm: “I will bless the Lord.”

Verse: For the rest, the crown of righteousness has been reserved for me.

**Antiphon.** For me to live is Christ, and to die is gain; I must glory in the cross of my Lord Jesus Christ.

Psalm: “My heart overflows.”

Verse: Through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.

Verse: “Into all the earth.”

[Col. 0791A]

### Responsories as above

**Responsory.** He who worked through Peter for the apostleship also worked through me among the nations. And they recognized the grace of God that was given to me.

Verse: The grace of God was not fruitless in me, but his grace always remains in me. And they recognized.

**Responsory.** I know in whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to preserve my deposit for that day.

Verse: The crown of righteousness has been reserved for me. Because.

**Responsory.** I have fought the good fight, I have completed the course, I have kept the faith; therefore the crown of righteousness has been reserved for me.

Verse: I know in whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to preserve my deposit. Therefore.

**Responsory.** The governor of the people of King Aretas in Damascus wanted to seize me. I was lowered in a basket through a window by the brothers, and so I escaped his hands in the name of the Lord.

Verse: The God and Father of my Lord Jesus Christ knows that I am not lying. And so I escaped.

### At the Gospel
Antiphon. “You who followed me shall sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel,” alleluia. Verse. “When the Son of Man comes in the seat of his Majesty.” Antiphon. “Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I suffered shipwreck for the name of Christ.” Antiphon. “Night and day I was in the depths of the sea.” Antiphon. “The apostles Peter and Paul, preachers to the nations, taught us your law, O Lord.” Antiphon. “Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.” Antiphon. “You who left everything and followed me shall receive a hundredfold and shall possess eternal life.” Antiphon. “Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul,” says the Lord.

Antiphons and Responsories at the vigil [Note: [Col. 0791D] Namely, on the eleventh day of the month of July, which is now assigned for the celebration of his Translation. Moreover, here [Col. 0792D] and frequently throughout this Codex, “vigil” signifies the nocturnal office and should not be understood as meaning the preceding day.] of Benedict the abbot.—In the first nocturn.

Antiphon. “There was a man of venerable life, Benedict, an abbot by grace.” Psalm: “Blessed is the man.” Antiphon. “From the time of his boyhood, bearing a mature heart, surpassing his age in conduct, he gave his mind to no pleasure.” Psalm: “Why do the nations rage?” Antiphon. “While he was in this world, which he could have used temporarily, he already despised the arid world, with its flower, as though it were withered.” Psalm: “When I called.” Antiphon. “Born in the province of Nursia, he had been entrusted by his parents at Rome to the liberal studies of letters.” Psalm: “Give ear to my words.” Antiphon. “Having left his home and his father’s possessions, desiring [cupiens] to please God alone, he sought the habit of holy conduct.” Psalm: “O Lord, our Lord.” Antiphon. “Therefore he withdrew, knowingly ignorant, and wisely unlearned.” Psalm: “In the Lord I trust.”

Responsories as above.

Responsory. “There was a man venerable for his life, Benedict by grace and by name, from the time of his boyhood bearing a mature heart; for, surpassing his age in conduct, he gave his mind to no pleasure.” Verse. “Therefore he withdrew, knowingly ignorant, and wisely unlearned.” From the time of his boyhood.

Responsory. “When this man, then, had decided to leave behind the studies of letters and seek the wilderness, his nurse, who loved him, followed him alone.” Verse. “Therefore he withdrew,” as above.

Responsory. “When blessed Benedict saw his nurse weeping, he immediately gave himself to prayer with tears; and he restored her sound winnowing tray.” Responsory. “The same tray was also hung at the entrance of the church [printed reading: *suspenso*; variant: *suspensum*], so that everyone, both present and future, might recognize from what a degree of perfection Benedict, while still a boy, had begun his religious life. Then, after taking counsel, they mixed poison into wine; when he had received it, he made the sign [of the cross], and thus it was shattered, as though he had given a stone instead of a sign.” Verse. “The man of God immediately understood that he had received a drink of death, which could not bear the sign of life. And thus.”

In the second nocturn.

Antiphon. “When this man, then, had already decided to leave behind the studies of letters and seek the wilderness, his nurse, who loved him more closely, followed him.” Psalm: “O Lord, who shall dwell?” Antiphon. “The aforesaid nurse asked neighboring women to lend her a winnowing tray for cleaning the grain; by chance it was broken” [Delete: “by chance it was broken”]. Psalm: “Preserve me.” Antiphon. “Moved with compassion for his nurse, the boy Benedict prayed with tears; he restored the winnowing tray.” Psalm: “O Lord, in your strength.” Antiphon. “Benedict, servant of God, performed a great miracle; he poured forth prayers to the Lord and repaired the winnowing tray.” Psalm: “The earth is the Lord’s.” Antiphon. “While he was seeking the wilderness, he met the Roman monk; when he learned of his desire, he both kept his secret and gave him assistance.” Psalm: “Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven.” Verse. “When the devil saw that bread was being lowered, placed in hope, he hurled a stone and broke the little bell.”

Responsory. “After summoning his disciples, blessed Benedict said: ‘May the everlasting God have mercy on you. Did I not previously tell you that this was entirely unsuitable to my character and yours?’” Verse. “Therefore, according to your character, seek a father for yourselves, since you cannot have me. Did I not?”

Responsory. “A certain peasant, carrying in his arms the body of his dead son and burning with the grief of bereavement, came to the monastery. He sought Father Benedict. As soon as he saw him, he began to cry out: ‘Give me back my son, give me back my son!’” Verse. “The man of the Lord stopped at these words and said: ‘Did I take your son away?’ He replied: ‘He is dead; come, raise him.’ Give me back.”

Responsory. “‘Lord, do not regard my sins, but the faith of this man, who asks that his son be raised; and restore to this little body the soul that you have taken.’ When the prayer had been completed, he revived and restored him alive to his father.” Verse. “When the soul returned, the whole little body trembled in this way, and he appeared alive before the eyes of all who were present.” And restored him alive.

Responsory. “When the holy father seemed to have his eyes fixed intently upon the splendor of flashing light, he saw the soul of Germanus, bishop of Capua, being carried to heaven by angels in a sphere of fire.” Verse. “And it happened that the most reverend Germanus was found dead by the man who had been sent.”

Responsory. “In that same year in which he was to depart from this life, he announced the day of his most holy death to some disciples living with him and to others dwelling far away.” Verse. [Supply: “indicating it to those present.”] “So that they might conceal what they had heard in silence, he instructed the absent as to what sign would appear to them when his soul departed from his body.” Of his most holy death.

Responsory. “Six days before his death, he ordered that his grave be opened; then, immediately seized by fevers, he began to be afflicted by severe pain until death.” Verse. “As his illness grew worse each day, on the sixth day he had himself carried by his disciples into the oratory.” Then immediately.

Responsory. “On the sixth day, therefore, he had himself carried by his disciples into the oratory; there he fortified his departure with the Lord’s sacraments, and expired between the hands of his disciples.” Verse. “With his hands raised toward heaven, he stood [the manuscript reads: ‘he made …’], and breathed out his final spirit amid the words of prayer.” And expired.

Responsory. “Today the holy Benedict, by the eastern road, stretched toward heaven before the eyes of his disciples, and is received by angels into glory.” Verse. “Then, just as the disciples who were present saw the death of the holy man, so those who were absent recognized the sign that had been foretold to them.” Before the eyes.

Responsory. “After the death of the most holy man, a woman deranged in mind came to his cave, entered it, and remained there; from that hour she was made well.” Verse. “And she remained in the health she had received throughout all the days of her life.” Verse. “A straight road, by the eastern route, extended from his cell all the way to heaven. A man, splendid above in venerable attire, stood beside it and asked the disciples whose road it was that they saw; but they professed that they did not know.”

Antiphons at the morning Lauds.

Antiphon. “In the dead of night Benedict prayed.” [Perhaps add: “he saw”] “that light poured down from above had driven away all the darkness of night and shone with such splendor that its brightness surpassed the day.” Antiphon. “As he himself related to his disciples, as though beneath a single ray of the sun, the whole world was brought together in an instant before his eyes.” Antiphon. “Saint Benedict prayed: ‘Lord, do not regard my sins, but the faith of this man, who asks that his son be raised.’ And before the eyes of all he restored the living boy to his father.” Antiphon. “Brother Maurus, run quickly, because the boy Placidus is drowning in the river.” Antiphon. “While Placidus was being carried along upon the waves, Maurus hastened amid the waters. With his foot emerging from the water, he rescued the boy.” [The repeated *flumen* (“river”) is redundant in the source.] Antiphon. “In the silence of the dead of night he saw everything, as though beneath a ray of the sun, and beheld the whole world.” Antiphon. “Benedict, servant of God, foreknowing through the indications of the Holy Spirit everything that was to come.”

In the Gospel.

Antiphon. “Today the holy Benedict, by the eastern road, along the straight path, stretched toward heaven before the eyes of his disciples; today, with hands raised, he departed amid the words of prayer. Today he was received into glory by angels.” Antiphon. “A religious woman, when she heard the words of denial, poured forth a prayer, and a flood of rains burst forth.”

At Vespers, at the vigil of Saint Lawrence.

Verse. “The Lord led the righteous.” Antiphon. “When blessed Lawrence was placed above the gridiron and burned, he said to the most wicked tyrant: ‘It is already roasted; turn it over and eat, for the resources of the Church that you seek have been carried by the hands of the poor into the heavenly treasuries.’”

At the Invitatory.

Antiphon. “Come, let us adore the Lord, King of martyrs.” Antiphon. “‘Where are you going without your son, father? Where are you hurrying, holy priest, without your minister?’” Psalm: “Blessed is the man.” Verse. “Blessed Lawrence said.” Antiphon. “‘Do not abandon me, holy father, because I have already spent your treasures, which you entrusted to me.’” Psalm: “Why do the nations rage?” Verse. “‘What, then, have I displeased in your fatherly judgment?’” Antiphon. “‘I am not abandoning you, my son, nor leaving you; but greater contests are owed to you for the faith of Christ.’” Psalm: “O Lord, how many are my foes?” Verse. “Blessed Sixtus said.” Verse. “With glory and honor.”

Responsories as above.

Responsory. “The Levite Lawrence performed a good work: by the sign of the cross he gave sight to the blind, and he gave the treasures of the Church to the poor.” Verse. “He distributed; he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever and ever.” And the treasures.

Responsory. “‘My boy, do not fear, for I am with you,’ says the Lord. ‘If you pass through fire, the flame will not harm you, and the smell of fire will not be upon you.’” Verse. “Until I place your enemies,” as above.

Responsory. “They tightened the limbs of his body, placed upon the gridiron. With coals heaped beneath him, the Levite of Christ exults. Blessed Lawrence, martyr of Christ, intercede for us.” Verse. “This is the man who was not abandoned by the Lord on the day of his contest.” Blessed. Verse. “The executioners, meanwhile, supplied coals beneath the iron grate.”

Responsory. “‘Where are you going without your son, Father? Where are you, holy priest, hurrying without a deacon? You were never accustomed to offer sacrifice without a minister.’” Verse. “‘What, then, have I displeased in your fatherly judgment? Have you judged me degenerate? Surely test whether you have chosen a suitable minister, to whom you entrusted the consecration of the Lord’s blood. You were never accustomed …’”

In the second nocturn.

Antiphon. “Blessed Lawrence prayed, saying: ‘Lord Jesus Christ, God from God, have mercy on me, your servant.’” Psalm: “When I called.” Verse. “Because when accused I did not deny your holy name; when questioned, I confessed you as Christ.” Antiphon. “Romanus said to blessed Lawrence: ‘I see before you a most beautiful young man; hasten to baptize me.’” Psalm: “Give ear to my words.” Verse. “Then, bringing a pitcher with water, he cast himself at his feet.” Antiphon. “Blessed Lawrence said: ‘My night has no darkness, but everything shines in the light.’” Psalm: “O Lord, our Lord.” Verse. “For the Lord himself knows that when accused I did not deny him; when questioned, I confessed Christ.” Verse. “You have placed, O Lord, upon his head.”

Responsories as above.

Responsory. “‘Do not abandon me, holy father, because I have already spent your treasures.’ ‘I am not abandoning you, my son, nor leaving you; but greater contests are owed to you for the faith of Christ.’” Verse. “For we, like old men, receive the course of the lighter battle; but a more glorious triumph over the tyrant awaits you, like a young man. After three days you will follow the priest, Levite.” But greater.

Responsory. “Blessed Lawrence cried out and said: ‘I worship my God and serve him alone; therefore I do not fear your torments.’” Verse. “My night has no darkness, but everything shines in the light.” And therefore.

Responsory. “Upon the gridiron I did not deny you as God, and when applied to the fire I confessed you, Lord Jesus.” Verse. “You have tested my heart, O Lord, and visited me by night.” And when applied to the fire.

In the third nocturn.

Antiphon. “They tightened the limbs of his body, placed upon the gridiron; with coals beneath him, the Levite of Christ exults.” Psalm: “O Lord, who shall dwell?” Verse. “The executioners, meanwhile, supplied coals beneath the iron grate.” Antiphon. “You tested me by fire, and no iniquity was found in me.” Psalm: “Hear, O Lord.” Verse. “You have tested my heart, O Lord, and visited me by night.” Antiphon. “When questioned, I confessed you as Lord. Roasted, I give thanks.” Psalm: “O Lord, in your strength.” Verse. “I give you thanks, O Lord, because I have been found worthy to enter your gates.” Verse. “The Lord led the righteous along straight paths.”

Responsories as above.

Responsory. “‘O Hippolytus, if you believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, I will show you the treasures and promise you eternal life.’” Verse. “He distributed; he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever and ever.” And the treasures.

Responsory. “I rejoice completely, because I have been found worthy to enter your gates, O Christ; because when accused I did not deny you, when questioned I confessed Christ; roasted, I give thanks.” Verse. “You have tested my heart, O Lord, and visited me by night.” Roasted.

Responsory. “The Levite Lawrence desired to be a sacrificial victim; while he was being roasted, he did not deny the Lord, and therefore was found to be a sacrifice of praise.” Verse. “Placed upon the gridiron, he did not deny God; and when applied to the fire, he confessed Christ.” And therefore.

Responsory. “This is the man who was not abandoned by God on the day of his contest; he himself trampled upon the head of the ancient serpent. Now he will be crowned, because he faithfully conquered in the Lord’s commandments.” Verse. “This is he who despised the life of the world and reached the heavenly kingdoms.” Now.

Responsory. “Blessed Lawrence said: ‘I offered myself as a sacrifice to God, for a fragrant odor.’” Verse. “For to you I shall pray, O Lord; in the morning you will hear my voice.” Verse. “I give you thanks, O Lord.”

Responsory. “‘I am your protector; do not fear,’ says the Lord. ‘When you pass through fire, you will not be burned, and the flame will not consume you, because I will hold your hand.’” Verse. “You have delivered my body, O Lord, from destruction and from the pressure of the flame that surrounded me. And in the midst of the fire I was not scorched, because I will hold …”

Responsory. “Blessed is the man Lawrence, who did not pursue gold nor place his hope in treasures of money. For he performed miracles during his life.” Verse. “This is truly a martyr, who poured out his blood for the name of Christ.” He performed.

At the morning Lauds.

[Col. 0796A]

Antiphon. “Lawrence entered as a martyr and confessed the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.” Antiphon. “I rejoice completely, because I have been found worthy to enter the gates of Christ.” Antiphon. “Lawrence performed a good work: by the sign of the cross he gave sight to the blind.” Antiphon. “You have tested my heart, O Lord, and visited me by night.” Antiphon. “My soul clung after you, because my flesh was burned by fire for you, my God.” Antiphon. “The Lord sent his angel and delivered me from the midst of the fire, and I was not scorched.” Antiphon. “Blessed Lawrence prayed, saying: ‘I give you thanks, O Lord, because I have been found worthy to enter your gates.’” Antiphon. “When accused I did not deny your holy name; when questioned, I confessed you as Lord.” Verse. “You have placed, O Lord.”

In the Gospel.

Antiphon. “Upon the gridiron I did not deny the holy Lord, and when applied to the fire I confessed Christ. You tested my heart and visited me by night; you tested me by fire, and no iniquity was found in me.” Antiphon. “I give you thanks, O Lord, because I have been found worthy to enter your gates.” Antiphon. “I give thanks to my God, because I have been found worthy to become Christ’s sacrificial victim. Roasted, I did not deny him; and when questioned, I confessed Christ.” Antiphon. “‘O Hippolytus, if you believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, I will show you the treasures and promise you eternal life?’” Antiphon. “‘If anyone ministers to me, my Father who is in heaven will honor him,’ says the Lord.” Antiphon. “‘Father, I desire that where I am, my minister also may be there.’”

At Vespers, at the vigil of Saint Tiburtius the martyr.

Antiphon. “The renowned martyr Tiburtius, while walking barefoot over burning coals, said to Fabian the prefect: ‘It seems to me that I am walking upon roses, in the name of my Lord Jesus Christ.’”

Of Saint Hippolytus, at Vespers.

Verse. “The Lord led the righteous.” Antiphon. “If anyone ministers to me,” as above.

At the Invitatory.

[Col. 0796C] Antiphon. “Come, let us adore the Lord, King of martyrs.”

In the first nocturn.

Antiphon. “Valerian handed blessed Hippolytus over to Lawrence to guard him.” Psalm: “Blessed is the man who has not walked.” Antiphon. “Hippolytus saw a blind man given sight by blessed Lawrence and immediately believed.” Psalm: “Why do the nations rage?” Antiphon. “Hippolytus placed his hands upon the eyes of the blind, and they were healed.” [Perhaps: “He placed”] Psalm: “O Lord, how many are my foes?” Verse. “With glory and honor.”

Responsories.

Responsory. “The most blessed martyr of Christ, Hippolytus, after receiving the grace of baptism from blessed Lawrence, placed his hands upon the eyes of the blind, and they were healed.” Verse. “When a blind man had been given sight by blessed Lawrence, Hippolytus believed and was found worthy to receive the sacrament of baptism.” He placed.

Antiphon. “Many blind and infirm people came to the custody of blessed Lawrence; holy Hippolytus, praying, laid his hands upon them and healed them. Therefore he was seized by soldiers and led to Decius.” Verse. “Justinus and Hippolytus took the body of Lawrence and buried it.” Therefore.

Responsory. “When holy Hippolytus was questioned by Decius about the body of Lawrence and what he had buried, Hippolytus replied: ‘I am a Christian, and I carefully buried the martyr of Christ.’” Verse. “I am greatly astonished, governor, that with your polluted mouth you have named a martyr.” Replying.

In the second nocturn.

Antiphon. “Caesar Decius summoned Hippolytus and asked why he had stolen the bodies of the saints.” Psalm: “When I called.” Antiphon. “Then Hippolytus entered his house and gave peace to everyone. He was seized by soldiers and led to the governor.” Psalm: “Give ear to my words.” Antiphon. “When Hippolytus had come into the presence of Decius, Decius smiled and said: ‘You have become a magician, since you took away the body of Lawrence.’” Psalm: “O Lord, our Lord.” Verse. “You have placed, O Lord.”

Responsories as above.

Responsory. “Then, returning on the third day, Hippolytus came to his house, gave peace to all his servants, and partook of the sacrifice of the altar of the martyr Lawrence.” Verse. “After the table had been set, before he took food, he was seized by soldiers and brought to the praetorium.” And partook.

Responsory. “While Hippolytus was placing the food of the banquet in his house” [perhaps: “the food of the banquet”], “soldiers sent by Decius seized him and brought him to Decius. When Caesar saw him, he smiled and said: ‘Have you become a magician, since you took away the body of Lawrence?’” Verse. “Decius said: ‘Enjoy my favor lawfully; be our friend.’ Hippolytus said: ‘I am a soldier of Christ, and I desire to keep his commands.’” When he saw him.

Responsory. “Decius stripped Hippolytus of the garment in which he was clothed according to Christian custom, and said to him: ‘Sacrifice to the gods, obey our commands, and live for the reward of military service.’” Verse. “I give thanks to my God, who strengthened me in the presence of rulers.” And he said.

In the third nocturn.

Antiphon. “Hippolytus answered Decius, saying: ‘I am not a magician, but a Christian.’” Psalm: “O Lord, who shall dwell?” Antiphon. “When Decius heard this, seized by fury, he ordered Hippolytus to be beaten with stones.” Psalm: “Hear, O Lord.” Antiphon. “Decius stripped Hippolytus of the garment in which he was clothed according to Christian custom.” Psalm: “O Lord, in your strength.”

Responsories.

Responsory. “Saint Hippolytus prayed in a loud voice and said: ‘I give you thanks, my Lord Jesus Christ, because I see my servants suffering in your presence.’”

Responsory. “Decius, advising Hippolytus, said: ‘Were you once a worshiper of the gods? Sacrifice to the gods; enjoy the reward of military service.’ Hippolytus answered and said: ‘I am a Christian, and I desire to attain the *vestigium* (“footstep”; a further word is lacking in the manuscript).’” Verse. “Then blessed Hippolytus said in a clear voice: ‘My military service is the Christian faith.’”

Responsory. “Decius ordered the soldiers, saying: ‘Strip Hippolytus and beat him with clubs.’ When he was being beaten, he said: ‘I am a soldier of Christ, and I do not fear your blows.’” Verse. “Use the former military service that you have always possessed.” Hippolytus answered and said.

Responsory. “After his servants had been martyred in the presence of Hippolytus, Hippolytus said: ‘I give you thanks, Lord Jesus Christ, because my servants [the verb is missing in the manuscript] in the presence of the saints.’” Verse. “Hippolytus, a soldier of Christ, armed with faith, said in the presence of the judges.”

At Matins.

Antiphon. “Hippolytus said to Decius: ‘You did not strip me; rather, you clothed me more fully.’” Antiphon. “The governor said to Hippolytus: ‘You have become foolish, since you are not ashamed of your nakedness’” [the manuscript reads: “you would be ashamed”]. Antiphon. “Caesar said to Hippolytus: ‘Now you have become a magician.’ Hippolytus answered Decius: ‘I am not a magician, but a servant of my Lord Jesus Christ.’” Antiphon. “Then Valerian ordered his servants to be martyred in the presence of Hippolytus.” Antiphon. “He deserves to become an example.” Verse. “The Lord led the righteous.” [The remainder is absent from the manuscript.]

In the Gospel.

Antiphon. “Saint Hippolytus prayed in a loud voice and said: ‘I give you thanks, my Lord Jesus Christ, because I see my servants suffering in your presence.’” Antiphon. “Blessed Hippolytus offered himself in the presence of Romulus and said in a clear voice: ‘I confess Christ.’” Antiphon. “Hippolytus, servant of Christ, entreated the Lord: ‘Lord Jesus Christ, receive my spirit.’” Antiphon. “The voice of the children was heard, saying: ‘Glory to God in the highest,’ alleluia.” Antiphon. “Caesar Decius summoned Hippolytus and asked why he had stolen the bodies of the saints.” Antiphon. “Then Hippolytus entered his house and gave peace to everyone.” Antiphon. “He was seized by soldiers and led to Decius.” Antiphon. “When Hippolytus had come into the presence of Decius, Decius smiled and said: ‘You have become a magician, because you took away the body of Lawrence.’”

Responsories or Antiphons for the Assumption of Saint Mary.

Responsory. “I saw a beautiful woman, like a dove, ascending above the streams of waters, whose fragrance was exceedingly incomparable upon her garments. And, like a spring day, roses and lilies of the valleys surrounded her.”” Verse. “Who is this who ascends through the wilderness like a column of smoke, from the perfumes of myrrh and frankincense?” And like.

Responsory. “I have been exalted like a cedar in Lebanon and like a cypress on Mount Zion; like choice myrrh I gave the sweetness of fragrance. And like cinnamon and balsam giving forth perfume.”

Responsory. “Grace has been poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.” Verse. “You have become beautiful and sweet in your delights.” Therefore. Verse. “Myrrh and drops and cassia are upon your garments, from ivory houses, by which the daughters of kings delighted in you in your honor.” Therefore.

Responsory. “Come, my chosen one, and I will place my throne in you, because the King has desired your beauty.” Verse. “In your beauty and loveliness, direct yourself, go forth prosperously, and reign.” Because.

Responsory. “Who is this who has come forth like the sun and is beautiful like Jerusalem? The daughters of Zion saw her and called her blessed, and the queens praised her.” Verse. “Who is this?” as above.

Responsory. “This is the beautiful one among the daughters of Jerusalem. As you saw her, full of charity and love” [the manuscript reads: “with charity and love”], “in the beds and gardens of spices.” Verse. “In your beauty,” as above.

Responsory. “All generations shall call me blessed, because the Lord who is powerful has done great things for me, and holy is his name.” Verse. “And his mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear him.”

Responsory. “The Lord desired the daughter of Zion adorned with necklaces; and the daughters of Zion, seeing her, proclaimed her most blessed, saying: ‘Your name is poured-out ointment.’” Verse. “The queen stood at your right hand, clothed in gold and surrounded with variety.”

Responsory. “This is the glorious day, today, on which the blessed virgin Mary, mother of Christ, departed to Christ by a fortunate course. And inquire …” [Two words are missing in the manuscript] “holding the primacy among virgins.” Verse. “This is the blessed virgin Mary, at whose departure the apostles rendered service.” And inquire.

Responsory. “Rejoice, Mary,” as above. Verse. “The archangel Gabriel.”

Responsory. “Blessed are you, virgin Mary, mother of God, who believed the Lord. The things said to you have been fulfilled in you. Behold, you have been exalted above the choirs of angels; intercede for us with the Lord our God.” Verse. “Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with you.” Intercede.

Responsory. “O how beautiful and lovely is Mary, virgin of God, who departed from the world to Christ; among the choirs of virgins she shines like the sun in heavenly power.” Verse. “The angels rejoice, the archangels exult in Mary the virgin.” Who.

Responsory. “Blessed and venerable.” Verse. “Blessed are you among women.”

Responsory. “Blessed are you, Mary, who did not …” Verse. “Hail, Mary.”

Responsory. “This is Zion, which the Lord chose for himself as an inheritance; this is my resting place forever and ever; here I shall dwell,” says the Lord.

(A line is missing in the manuscript.)

Responsory. “You are loved by the Lord above every salvation and every beauty, and you are worthy to be called queen of heaven. The choir of angels—our companions and fellow citizens—rejoices.”” Verse. “We ought greatly to venerate her who is now the holy [a word is missing in the manuscript] and undefiled Virgin.”

Responsory. “This is the wise, prudent, and humble Virgin, who was found worthy to be raised in the King’s palace; for this reason she was also found worthy to be called queen of heaven.” Verse. “Grace has been poured out,” as above.

Antiphons as above. In the first nocturn.

Antiphon. “You have been exalted, holy Mother of God, above the choirs of angels to the heavenly kingdoms.” Psalm: “O Lord, our Lord.” Antiphon. “Through you the gates of paradise have been opened for us; today, glorious, you triumph with the angels.” Psalm: “The heavens declare.” Antiphon. “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” Psalm: “The earth is the Lord’s.” Verse. “In your beauty and loveliness.”

In the second nocturn.

Antiphon. “In your beauty and loveliness, direct yourself, go forth prosperously, and reign.” Psalm: “My heart has uttered.” Antiphon. “God will help her with his countenance; God is in her midst; she shall not be moved.” Psalm: “God is our refuge.” Antiphon. “The dwelling place of all of us who rejoice is in you, holy Mother of God.” Psalm: “His foundations.”

In the third nocturn.

Antiphon. “Rejoice, Mary, virgin; alone you have destroyed all heresies throughout the world.” Psalm: “Sing.” Antiphon. “Grant me to praise you, consecrated Virgin; give me strength against your enemies.” Psalm: “The Lord reigns; let the earth rejoice.” Antiphon. “After childbirth you remained an inviolate virgin; Mother of God, intercede for us.” Psalm: “Sing.” Verse. “The Lord chose her.”

At Matins.

Antiphon. “Mary has been assumed into heaven; the angels rejoice and, praising, bless the Lord.” Antiphon. “The virgin Mary has been assumed into the ethereal bridal chamber, in which the King of kings sits upon a starry throne.” Antiphon. “We run after the fragrance of your ointments; the young women have loved you exceedingly.” Antiphon. “Blessed are you, daughter, by the Lord, because through you we have shared in the fruit of life.” Antiphon. “You are beautiful and comely, daughter of Jerusalem, terrible as an army arranged for battle.” Verse. “In your beauty.”

In the Gospel.

Antiphon. “Who is this who rises like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, chosen as the sun, terrible as an army arranged for battle?” Antiphon. “Today the virgin Mary ascends to the heavens; rejoice, because she reigns with Christ forever.” Antiphon. “Virgin Mary, rejoice always, for you were found worthy to bear Christ, the Creator of heaven and earth, because from your womb you brought forth the Savior of the world.” Antiphon. “O how beautiful and chaste is the generation with splendor.” Antiphon. “This is she who knew no marriage-bed in sin; she will have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.” Antiphon. “For glorious is the fruit of good labors.” Antiphon. “You have become beautiful and sweet in your delights, holy Mother of God.” Antiphon. “Return, return, O Shulammite; return, return, that we may gaze upon you.” Antiphon. “Before the bridal chamber of this Virgin, celebrate for us sweet *capita dragmis*” [the printed wording is corrupt; perhaps *cantica dramatis*, “songs of a drama”]. Antiphon. “Mary chose the best part for herself, which shall not be taken away from her forever.” Antiphon. “Your name is poured-out ointment, Mother of God; and rightly” [or: “the righteous”] “they love you.” Antiphon. “Your eyes, holy Mother of God, are like the pools in Heshbon, which are at the gate of the daughter of the multitude forever.” Antiphon. “I am black but beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem; therefore the King loved me and brought me into his chambers.” Antiphon. “Like chosen myrrh you gave a sweet fragrance, holy Mother of God.” Antiphon. “You are a closed garden, holy Mother of God, a closed garden, a sealed fountain.” Antiphon. “Under your protection we flee; there the weak received strength, and for this reason we sing psalms to you, Virgin Mother of God.” Antiphon. “The gate of paradise was closed to all through Eve, and was opened again through the virgin Mary, alleluia.” Antiphon. “Blessed mother [Note: [Col. 0799D] This means ‘undefiled’; for at times the verb nubere means ‘to have intercourse’ or ‘to fall away from virginity.’ Hence Tertullian, in *On the Flesh of Christ*, chapter 23, says concerning the most holy Virgin: ‘If a virgin conceived, she married in her childbirth’; that is, in the mistaken opinion of Tertullian, she ceased to be a virgin.] and unmarried, glorious queen of the world.” Antiphon. “Mother in flowering, virgin in childbirth, rejoice and be glad, Virgin Mother of the Lord.” Antiphon. “Under your protection we flee, holy Mother of God; do not despise our prayers in our necessities, but always deliver us from dangers, blessed Virgin.” Antiphon. “Rise, north wind, and come, south wind; blow through my garden, and let its spices flow.” Antiphon. “The daughters saw her and proclaimed her most blessed; queens and concubines also praised her forever.” Antiphon. “My beloved, I will seize you and lead you into the house of my mother and into the chamber of my mother. There you will teach me the Lord’s commandments.” Antiphon. “Draw me after you; we shall run after the fragrance of your ointments. Your name is poured-out oil.” Antiphon. “The winter has now passed; the rain has gone and departed. Rise, my beloved, and come.” Antiphon. “Many waters could not extinguish love.” Antiphon. “His left hand is beneath my head, and his right hand will embrace me.” Antiphon. “I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, tell him that I am sick with love.” Antiphon. “Mary rejoiced in spirit and said: ‘I bless you, who rule over every blessing. I bless the dwelling place of your glory. I bless you, for whom a dwelling place was made in my womb; and I bless all the works of your hands, which obey you in complete submission. I bless your love, with which you loved us. I bless all the words that came forth from your mouth, which were given to us. For in truth I shall believe that, just as you have said, so it will be done,’ alleluia.”

Antiphons at Matins for Saint Symphorian.

Antiphon. “For heavenly wisdom illumined him, and simplicity adorned with spiritual gems.” Antiphon. “‘Take up courage again, my son; we cannot fear death, which without doubt leads to life,’ alleluia.” Antiphon. “‘Lift up your hearts; raise your eyes, my son, and look upon him who reigns in heaven.’” Antiphon. “When Symphorian was handed over to the crown of martyrdom, his blessed mother made a vow to God.” Antiphon. “‘You, man Symphorian, raise your mind and your eyes to the stars,’ alleluia, alleluia.” Antiphon. “Found strong in torments during his childhood, he deserved a crown from the hand of the Lord.” Antiphon. “Blessed Augusta prayed diligently from the wall, saying: ‘Lord God, look upon my son, because the Jews have cut off his head.’”

In the Gospel.

Antiphon. “Saint Symphorian, *auctus et apertus* (‘increased and opened’) outside the wall, *se reproferatus voto habuit*” [the surviving Latin is materially uncertain; it must not be expanded into “fulfilled his vow”]. Antiphon. “His glorious mother said to Symphorian: ‘Lift up your hearts; raise yourself, my son; your life is not taken away but changed for the better.’” Antiphon. “Blessed Augusta exhorted Saint Symphorian with tears, saying: ‘Son, go rejoicing; today you will receive the crown of the kingdom,’ alleluia.” Antiphon. “Peter the exorcist said to Artemius: ‘Believe in the living God, the Lord Jesus Christ.’” Antiphon. “‘Artemius, if you believe in the only-begotten Son of God, your daughter will be saved.’” Antiphon. “‘Believe in Christ and you will see the works of the Lord.’” Antiphon. “Candida said to Artemius: ‘If what you assure me has happened, who could doubt that Christ is the true God?’” Antiphon. “The man of God, Peter the exorcist, is present, holding in his hand the triumph of the holy cross.”

In the Gospel.

Antiphon. “Artemius cried out: ‘There is one true God, through whom demons are cast out.’” Antiphon. “An angel of the Lord appeared to the presbyter Marcellinus while he was praying naked, clothed him in his garments, and said to him: ‘Follow me, to where Peter the exorcist was,’ alleluia.”

Of the Martyrdom of Saint John.—At the vigil, at Vespers.

[Col. 0800D]

Verse. “The Lord led the righteous.”

At the Invitatory.

Antiphon. “The Lord, King of martyrs.”

Responsories.

**Vers.** For Herod had seized and bound John and placed him in prison. Because he feared him.  

**Resp.** For John was saying to him: “It is not lawful for you to take a wife.” Because.

**Vers.** Herod, having sent an executioner, ordered John’s head to be cut off in the prison. On account of.

**Vers.** When the girl had gone out, she said to her mother: “What shall I ask for?” But she said: “The head of John the Baptist.”

**Vers.** The mother commanded the dancing girl: “Ask for nothing else except the head of John the Baptist.” When it had been taken away.

## Responsories or Antiphons for the Nativity of Saint Mary, at Vespers

**Ant.** Under your protection we flee for refuge; there the infirm received strength, and for this we sing psalms to you, Virgin Mother of God.

[Col. 0802B] **Responsories as above.**

**Resp.** Today the blessed Virgin Mary was born from the offspring of David; through her the salvation of the world appeared, whose glorious life gave light to the age.  
**Vers.** Let us celebrate with the greatest devotion the nativity of the most blessed Virgin Mary.  

**Resp.** Let us celebrate with the greatest devotion the nativity of the most blessed Virgin Mary, so that she may intercede for us with the Lord Jesus Christ.  
**Vers.** Today the Virgin Mary was born from the offspring of David.  

**Resp.** Recalling with the greatest honor the most worthy birth of the glorious Virgin, whose humility the Lord regarded and, when the angel announced it, conceived the Redeemer of the world.  
**Vers.** Of the most blessed Virgin Mary.  

**Resp.** Your nativity, Virgin Mother of God, announced joy to the whole world. For from you was born Christ our God, the sun of righteousness. By releasing the curse, he gave blessing; and by confounding death, he granted us eternal life.

### Antiphons at Matins Lauds

**Ant.** The nativity of the Virgin Mary, born from the tribe of Judah, illustrious from the stock of David.  
**Ant.** Today is the nativity of holy Mary the Virgin, whose renowned life enlightens all the Churches.  
**Ant.** Mary, arisen from royal offspring, shone forth; with the greatest devotion of mind and spirit we ask to be helped by her prayers.  
**Ant.** With heart and mind let us sing glory to Christ in these sacred solemnities of Mary, the exalted Mother of God.  
**Ant.** Let us celebrate the nativity of blessed Mary with joy, so that she may intercede for us with the Lord our God.  
**Vers.** Grace has been poured forth.

### In the Gospel

**Ant.** Let us celebrate the solemnity of the present nativity of Mary, the perpetual Virgin and Mother of God, from whom the height of the throne proceeded, alleluia.  
**Ant.** Your nativity, Virgin Mother of God, announced joy to the whole world; for from you was born Christ our God, the sun of righteousness. By releasing the curse, he gave blessing; and by confounding death, he granted us eternal life.

## Responsories or Antiphons at the Vigil of Saint Hermes

[Col. 0802D]

**Resp.** I have not lost the prefecture, but have exchanged it. For earthly dignity is either taken away or changed; heavenly dignity, however, is eternal and endures.  
**Vers.** Lord my God, Hermes, look upon your prefecture, and look upon your patrimony. Your house is adorned. Dignity.  

**Resp.** Lord Jesus Christ, who made me sit in the chair of your apostle, grant me that you send your angel, who today, at evening time, may lead me to your servant Hermes.  
**Vers.** And again, at dawn, may he bring me back here without anyone noticing, until I set out. To the servant.

I have not lost the prefecture, but have exchanged it in the name of the Lord.

**Ant.** Saint Alexander, who is held in chains, taught me your commandments here, Lord.  
**Ant.** With hands extended, he prayed to the Lord that he might rescue him from his enemies.  
**Ant.** Heavenly dignity of eternal sublimity truly endures.

**Ant.** Lord Jesus Christ, who made me sit in the chair of your apostle, grant me that you send your angel, who today, at evening time, may lead me to your servant Hermes.

**Ant.** The holy legion of the martyrs of Agaunum [Auganum], while resisting its adversaries, with the sacred leader Maurice intervening, acquired the shortcut to immortality.  
**Ant.** Precious are the wounds of the Theban martyrs, of holy Maurice and his companions, who under Maximian resolved to receive death.  
**Ant.** Behold, that sacred place of the martyrs of Agaunum [Auganum] has become, through the intercession of the saints, the salvation of those now living and the protection of those to come.  
**Ant.** The bodies of the saints were drenched by the stream of sacred blood; the fellowship of the precious martyrs consecrated them. Redonus knows this; in battle he fled.  
**Ant.** A glorious fragrance burned forth from the most blessed martyrs, because, slaughtered by the sword with bowed necks, they were killed by Maximian; the multitude of angels received them with joy.  
**Ant.** The holy martyrs of Christ triumph, who under Maximian resolved to receive death and received the heavenly kingdoms with Saint Maurice.
