## Saint Vedastus, outstanding teacher of Arras

Let Vedastus, the outstanding teacher of Arras, be celebrated in sacred praises, so that he who diligently instructed those whom he taught in the flesh by words and examples may intercede for them with the Lord. May the wolf lying in wait not presume to attack Christ’s sheep.

**Vers.** So that he whom he formed through spiritual zeal and encouraged by admonitions and miracles—diligently.

**Resp.** This is Vedastus, sprung from the *sensibus* of the Aulesci [perhaps: *sentibus* of the Aulerci, “thorns”], whom more celebrated fame proclaimed as one who would preach the word; King Ludovicus took him as a companion on his journey.  
**Note [Col. 0805]:** Ludovicus is Clodovaeus, the first of the Frankish kings who believed in Christ.  
**Vers.** So that on each step of his journey he might be imbued by him with most salutary teachings. Whom more celebrated fame.

**Resp.** Therefore Vedastus was leading the king, who was hastening toward the fountain of life. Bishop Remigius was washing the one who came.  
**Vers.** The two were nearly equal in piety and alike, but Vedastus gave admonitions of salvation. Remigius.

**Resp.** While holy Vedastus was traveling with the king and, speaking no mortal words, was treating of heavenly things, he restored sight to a blind man who came upon them and made the heart of the prince firm in the faith.  
**Vers.** Thus the man of God perceived that heavenly power was present with him and poured himself entirely into sacred prayers. And to the one who came upon them.

**Resp.** He who brought forth from a dry rock a spring of living water for the thirsty people granted through blessed Vedastus that wine should flow from a dry vessel and satisfied his own people with a wondrous cup.  
**Vers.** When the man of the Lord was offering the cups of life to a certain friend, he who changed water into wine at Cana of Galilee—[the same] distinguished preacher, the man of the Lord Vedastus, appointed to the city of Arras, at the very gate of the city raised two sick men from their affliction; for he restored a step to the lame and the light of their eyes to the blind.  
**Vers.** Before he rained down words and shone forth in miracles, he who was free from infirmities bestowed heavenly gifts. For also to the lame.

**Resp.** Where once there had been a haunt of wild beasts, there the supreme bishop, blessed Vedastus, caused a choir of psalm-singers to resound. For he also changed a bear’s den into a hall of sacred worship.  
**Vers.** Just as he changed bestial ways into the practice of lambs, so from foul and shameful things he produced things beautiful and honorable. For he also changed a bear’s den.

**Resp.** Invited to dinner, the holy priest of God, following Christ’s example, did not refuse to give his assent, so that he might pour the word of life of the *artium* [perhaps: *altius*, “more loftily”] into the hearts of the banqueters and drive away the fabrications of demons.  
**Vers.** For, extending his right hand, he impressed the sign of the cross upon the vessel; driving away the apparition from the spilled liquid, he shone forth by a miracle. And the Word.

**Resp.** O blessed bishop Vedastus, whose departure a column of light revealed, so that true Israel might hasten from the toils of Egypt toward the promised kingdoms, destined to receive its rewards.  
**Vers.** For the space of two hours a column of light was seen rising conspicuously from the bishop’s house up to the height of heaven. So that true.

## Antiphons and Responsories for Saint Dionysius with his Companions—At the Vigil, at Vespers

**Ant.** Saint Dionysius, who, when blessed Clement, successor of the apostle Peter, entrusted him with the seeds of the divine word to be brought forth among the nations—  
Psalm: Blessed is the man who does not.

**Ant.** The more he recognized the error of paganism raging there, the more fearlessly he approached it, inflamed by the heat of faith. Under the Lord’s guidance he arrived at Paris.  
Psalm: Why did the nations rage?

**Ant.** Not fearing to encounter the savagery of an unbelieving people, because the memory of his former sufferings strengthened his courage.  
Psalm: Lord, what—  
**Vers.** Rejoice in the Lord.

**Resp.** After the Lord’s Passion, preaching destined to benefit all the nations followed, so that, as faith grew, many deserved to become confessors, whom the Catholic Church afterward rejoices to have deserved to be martyrs.  
**Vers.** When they saw their sufferings approaching, they taught, filled with the grace of the Holy Spirit, what they had learned through the gift of the Lord Jesus Christ. Afterward.

**Vers.** Blessed Dionysius followed, receiving from Clement the seeds of the divine word destined to benefit the nations.

**Resp.** We give you thanks, Lord, because you granted that the darts of the attacking enemy should serve as a test of your faithful and not as wounds, and you grant your martyrs such a reward for their labor that none of yours may rejoice that the enemy was unwarlike.

**Vers.** But the souls of the righteous—

**Resp.** The most blessed martyr of Christ, Dionysius, received from blessed Clement the divine seeds to be brought forth among the nations. And the more he recognized the error of paganism raging there, the more fearlessly he came, armed with the power of faith.  
**Vers.** And under the Lord’s guidance he arrived at Paris, not fearing to encounter the savagery of the unbelieving people. There, fearless.

### In the Second Nocturn

**Ant.** At that time the city was powerful both in its gathering of Germanic peoples and in its nobility, because it had a health-giving breeze, a pleasant climate, rivers rich in water, and lands exceedingly fertile in trees and woods.  
Psalm: When I called.

**Ant.** Therefore the servant of God chose this place and awaited.  
Psalm: My words.

**Ant.** The Lord deigned to perform so many wonders through him that he won the hearts of the rebellious no less by miracles than by preaching.  
Psalm: Lord, our Lord.  
**Vers.** Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord.

### Responsories

**Resp.** For the most sacred day of blessed Dionysius is at hand, on which he completed his victorious contest and deserved to receive the crown of victory from the hand of the Lord.  
**Vers.** The Lord led the just man by straight paths and showed him the kingdom of God. And the crown.

**Resp.** Therefore, in this place the infirm experience how greatly the servants of God ought to be honored, where blindness receives sight, weakness receives the power to walk, and obstructed ears deserve to receive hearing.  
**Vers.** Therefore the servant of God chose this place and awaited. Where blindness receives.

**Resp.** Through blessed Dionysius divine mysteries are celebrated here. Through his prayers the blind are enlightened, demons are driven away on his feast day, and the sick are healed.  
**Vers.** The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of evil shall not touch them.

### In the Third Nocturn

**Ant.** The Church did not yet exist in those places. That people built one, in which it established, according to custom, the offices of serving clerics and increased approved persons in the honor of the second order.  
Psalm: In the Lord I trust.

**Ant.** And, in a wondrous manner, an armed crowd could not resist an unarmed man.  
Psalm: Lord, who shall dwell?

**Ant.** Therefore, girded with faith and putting mercy first, he gradually joined to God those whom he was snatching away from the devil.  
Psalm: Lord, in your power.  
**Vers.** You have established, Lord.

### Responsories

**Resp.** The Lord deigned to perform so many wonders through him that he won the hearts of the rebellious no less by miracles than by preaching.  
**Vers.** And, in a wondrous manner, an armed crowd could not resist an unarmed man. Than by preaching.

**Resp.** These are holy men.  
**Note:** That is: Seek this Responsory in the office of the apostles.  
Seek it in the apostles.

**Resp.** Blessed Dionysius, Rusticus, and Eleutherius, persevering in this steadfastness of faith, gave their bodies to the earth and carried their souls to heaven with joy.  
**Vers.** For by such a confession they deserved to depart to the Lord that, even after their heads had been cut off, their still-trembling tongues were thought to confess the Lord.

### At Matins Lauds

**Ant.** These holy men never endured being absent from the presence of blessed Dionysius; the executioner’s interrogation found them united.  
**Ant.** For by such a confession they deserved to depart to the Lord that, even after their heads had been cut off, their still-trembling tongues were thought to confess the Lord.  
**Ant.** Persevering in this steadfastness of faith, they gave their bodies to the earth and carried their blessed souls to heaven.  
**Ant.** An exceedingly blessed and God-pleasing fellowship: among them neither one could be first nor another third; but, confessing the Trinity, they deserved to adorn it by a threefold martyrdom.  
**Ant.** They chose to commit the bodies of the martyrs to the depths and deep whirlpools of the Seine, to be lost.  
**Ant.** Therefore, in this place the infirm experience how greatly the servants of God ought to be honored, where blindness receives sight, weakness receives the power to walk, and obstructed ears deserve to receive hearing.  
**Vers.** The souls of the righteous.

### In the Gospel

**Ant.** For the most sacred day of blessed Dionysius is at hand, on which he completed his victorious contest and deserved to receive the crown of victory from the hand of the Lord.  
**Ant.** O blessed Dionysius, great is your faith. Intercede for us with the Lord our God.  
**Ant.** Therefore the executioners feared that the converted Christian people might bury the bodies of the saints for themselves as a protection.  
**Ant.** Then a certain matron, although entangled in the error of the pagans, considering that she desired to do something pleasing to the Lord for her conversion—  
**Ant.** By a subtle plan she invited the executioners to a banquet, and, while extending to them the abundance of her hospitality, she drove from their memory the things they had undertaken to do.  
**Ant.** They found Saint Dionysius fighting against the unbelievers at Paris with his companions.  
**Ant.** Almighty God, who bestows the crown of glory on your elect when they contend in the arena, and who gave the reward of the heavenly kingdom to those chosen for it, among whom you consecrated your athletes Dionysius and the most blessed Eleutherius and Rusticus with the palm of martyrdom in your confession: grant, Redeemer of the world, that although we are unable to obtain pardon by our merits, we may attain it through their intercession.

## Antiphons and Responsories at the Vigil of the Holy Martyrs Crispinus and Crispinianus

**Ant.** The holy men of God, Crispinus and Crispinianus, were born at Rome. They came devotedly to Gaul and contended under the cruel examination of Maximian.  
Psalm: Blessed is the man who does not.

**Ant.** The holy martyrs said in prayer: “You are powerful, Lord, to deliver us from the torments of the impious and to bring us unharmed out of this fire.”  
Psalm: Why did the nations rage?

**Ant.** The holy martyrs, rejoicing in hope amid the sharpest pains and enduring in tribulation, prayed to the Lord and said: “Judge our judgment, Lord, and deliver us from the unjust and deceitful man.”  
Psalm: Lord, what?

### Responsories

**Resp.** The holy men of God, Crispinus and Crispinianus, were born at Rome; they came devotedly to Gaul; and under the cruel examination of Maximian they contended.  
**Vers.** *(Missing in the manuscript.)*

**Resp.** These are the two precious martyrs who came from Rome to preach in the name of Christ and, under the cruel ruler Maximian, resolved to receive glorious death.  
**Vers.** Born of noble stock at Rome, they came to Gaul for the love of Christ.  

**Resp.** The most blessed martyrs answered Maximian: “The honors you promise to give us, give to your own. For us, to live is Christ and to die is gain.”  
**Vers.** “The money and honors you promise to give us, give to your own. We rejoice that we once left these things behind for the love of Christ. For us—”

### In the Second Nocturn

**Ant.** While they were praying these things, a drop of boiling lead leaped into the eye of Rictiovarus, torturing him with severe pain and blinding him in his affliction.  
Psalm: When I called.

**Ant.** Immediately, when the prayer was finished, the angel of the Lord brought them both out of the fire without pain.  
Psalm: My words.

**Ant.** O wondrous judgment of divine justice: he who killed many martyrs by fire as they hastened toward heaven himself ended his life in fire and, tortured, reached the eternal fire.  
Psalm: Lord, our Lord.

### Responsories

**Resp.** When the martyrs of Christ, Crispinus and Crispinianus, were in torments, contemplating heavenly things, they said: “Help us, Lord, to complete your work without blemish.”  
**Vers.** Look upon your servants and your works, Lord, and help us. To complete.

**Resp.** “Judge our judgment, Lord, and deliver us from the unjust man.” Then, while they were praying, stakes leapt from their nails and, striking the officers, killed them.  
**Vers.** The martyrs, amid the sharpest pains, rejoicing in hope and patient in tribulation. Then.

**Resp.** The holy martyrs said in prayer: “You are powerful, Lord, to deliver us from the torments of the impious and to bring us unharmed out of this fire.”  
**Vers.** Immediately, when the prayer was finished, the angel of the Lord led them out of the fire without pain. And from this.

### Antiphons in the Third Nocturn

**Ant.** The impious Maximian ordered both of them to be beheaded.  
Psalm: Hear, Lord, justice.

**Ant.** Those whose heads were cut off at the king’s command [perhaps: “to whom the king gave the order”]—the precious death of both saints is in the sight of the Lord.  
Psalm: Lord, in your power.

**Ant.** The holy bodies of Crispinus and Crispinianus were left behind; while Christ guarded them, they remained untouched.  
Psalm: I will bless the Lord.

### Responsories

**Resp.** O wondrous judgment of divine justice: he who killed many martyrs by fire as they hastened toward heaven himself ended his life in fire and, mercifully, commanded them to come to him from the struggle of their contest. He himself.

**Resp.** The holy bodies of Crispinus and Crispinianus were left behind; while Christ guarded them, they remained untouched by the bite of *orum* [perhaps: *ferarum*, “wild beasts”].  
**Vers.** Their souls were carried to heaven by angels, but their bodies were left to the executioners’ beasts. Which.

**Resp.** At the angels’ admonition they buried the bodies of the saints with joy, where the people today adore the Majesty of God.  
**Vers.** In that place Christians later built a great basilica. Where.

### Antiphons at Matins Lauds
Saints Crispinus and Crispinianus, however, boldly answered the impious king, saying: “We confess that we have come for the love of Christ, who is the true God, one in the Trinity; him we serve, devoted in faith and love.”

The most blessed martyrs answered Maximianus, saying: “The honors that you promise to give us, give as gifts to your own people; for us, to live is Christ and to die is gain.”

When the martyrs of Christ were undergoing tortures, contemplating heavenly things, they said: “Help us, Lord, that we may complete your work without blemish.” [Col. 0810A]

Blessed and glorious is the death of the saints, who walked amid blazing flames and sang a hymn, saying: “Help us, O God our salvation.”

The holy martyrs prayed, saying: “We give you thanks, Lord, who, rescuing us from this world, command us to come to you.”

## At the Gospel

The saints of God, Crispinus and Crispinianus, bowed their necks to the executioners and gave their holy souls back to the Lord their Creator. And therefore they are crowned, receive the palm, and live forever.

These are the saints of God, Crispinus and Crispinianus, of noble birth and rich in possessions. They went out from Rome for the love of Christ. They left everything, followed the Lord, and attained the rewards of the kingdom that the Lord promised to those who love him.

At the prompting of an angel they buried the bodies of the saints with joy, where the people today adore the Majesty of God.

The old man hastens to the place where the holy martyrs lay beheaded. [Col. 0810B]

A boy was brought by his parents, blind, deaf, mute, and lame through various illnesses; by Christ’s generosity, he recovered through the prayers of the martyrs.

## At the vigil of Saint Quintinus — Antiphons at Matins

The holy man Quintinus, together with blessed Lucius, transferred themselves from the city of Rome to this region.

And when they had reached the places of the municipality now called Augusta Veremandorum—

Then Rictiovarus, full of fury, ordered him to be stretched out and beaten with rods.

Blessed Quintinus prayed, saying: “Lord God, have mercy on me, your servant.”

And when he saw this, he offered his neck to the executioners, saying: “Now do what has been commanded you.”

## At the Gospel

And a voice from heaven said: “Quintinus, my servant, come and receive the crown that I have prepared for you.”

**832** Blessed Quintinus said to Rictiovarus: “I am a Christian, and I confess Christ. Yet if you wish to know my name with certainty, I am called Quintinus.” [Col. 0810C]

# Antiphons for Saint Brictius

## At Matins

[Col. 0813C]

After the death of the most blessed bishop Martin, blessed Brictius assumed the episcopal see.

In the thirtieth year of his ordination, a lamentable accusation arose against him. For a certain woman who washed the garments of the chamberlains conceived and gave birth, and they brought the entire accusation [possibly: “all the accusations”] against the bishop.

When he denied it, he ordered the infant to be brought. When it had been brought, being thirty days old from birth, Brictius said to it: “I adjure you by God: if I fathered you, declare it before everyone.”

The infant, answering before all the people, said to the blessed man: “You are not,” it said, “my father.”

Saint Brictius, satisfying the people, carried burning coals from the city in his cloak and, casting them down before the tomb of blessed Martin in the presence of the people, displayed his garment unburned. Verse: “Behold the great priest.”

## At the Gospel

When the people did not believe him and expelled him from the episcopate, he went to Rome, weeping and lamenting, and saying: “I suffer these things deservedly, because I sinned against the saint of God.” **836** [Col. 0813D]

# Antiphons and Responsories at the vigil of Saint Andrew the Apostle, at Vespers

Verse: “Into all the earth.”

Come after me, says the Lord; I will make you fishers of men.

### Responsories as above

As the Lord was walking across the sea beside the shore of Galilee, he saw Peter and Andrew casting nets into the sea and called them, saying: “Come after me; I will make you fishers of men.” Verse: “Hear, O God, my supplication; attend to my prayer. From the ends of the earth.” He called.

Come after me; I will make you fishers of men. And they, leaving their nets and boat, followed the Lord. Verse: “As the Lord was walking across the sea beside the shore of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Peter and Andrew, and called them.” And they.

As soon as blessed Andrew heard the voice of the Lord preaching, he left the nets by whose use and work he lived and followed the giver of eternal life. Verse: “At the voice of a single command Peter and Andrew, leaving their nets, followed the Redeemer.” Rewards.

**Responsory. [Note: [Col. 0813D] This and what follows are taken from the Acts of Saint Andrew, whose antiquity and authenticity are disputed. [Col. 0814D] Andreas du Saussay vigorously defends them.]**

Saint Andrew prayed while looking toward heaven; he cried out in a loud voice and said: “You are my God, whom I have seen. Do not allow me to be brought down by an impious judge, because I have recognized the power of the holy cross.” Verse: “You are my teacher, Christ, whom I loved, whom I knew, whom I confessed; only hear me in this utterance. Do not permit me.”

The man of God was led away to be crucified. But the people cried out in a loud voice, saying: “His innocent blood is condemned without cause.” Verse: “The sons of strangers lied to me; the sons of strangers grew old and limped away from their paths. The Lord lives.” Innocent.

O good cross, which received beauty and comeliness from the members of the Lord. Receive me from human beings and restore me to my teacher, so that through you he may receive me, who through you redeemed me. Verse: “Hail, cross, which was consecrated in Christ’s body and adorned with his members as with pearls.”

The good teacher and friend of God, Andrew, is led to the cross. Looking from afar, he saw the cross: “Hail, cross; receive the disciple of him who hung upon you, my teacher Christ.” Verse: “Hail, cross,” as above. Who hung.

I stretched out my hands all day on the cross toward a people that did not believe but contradicted me, walking in evil ways and after its sins. Verse: “The Lord, God of vengeance, the God of vengeance has acted freely. Rise up, judge of the earth; repay the proud.”

This man appeared most gentle among his people, but full of holiness and grace. This is he who prays continually for the people and for this city. Verse: “In return for their love they slandered me, but I was praying.” For the people.

The Lord loved Andrew as an odor of sweetness. While he hung on the cross, he counted him a martyr worthy of himself, whom he had called an apostle while he was on the sea; and therefore he was called a friend of God. Verse: “You are my teacher, Christ,” as above. And therefore.

Blessed Andrew cried out from the cross, saying: “Lord Jesus Christ, do not command me to be taken down from this cross until you have first received my spirit.” Verse: “Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.”

O blessed Cecilia, who converted two brothers, overcame the judge Almachius, and revealed Bishop Urbanus with an angelic countenance. Verse: “Cecilia sent me to you, so that you may show me Urbanus.”

The glorious virgin always carried the Gospel of Christ in her breast and neither by day nor by night ceased from divine conversation and prayer. # At the vigil of Saint Clement, at Vespers

Verse: “The Lord led the righteous.”

When the people had begun the journey across the sea, they cried out in a loud voice: “Lord, save him.” And Clement said with tears: “Receive, Father, my spirit.”

### Responsories as above

As Saint Clement prayed, the Lamb of God appeared to him, from beneath whose foot a living spring flows; the force of the river gladdens the city of God. Verse: “I saw a Lamb standing upon Mount Zion.” From beneath whose.

Pray for us, blessed Clement, that we may be made worthy of Christ’s promise. Verse: “Hope in him, all the assembly of the people; pour out your hearts before him.” That we may be worthy.

You gave your martyr Clement a dwelling in the sea, prepared by angelic hands in the form of a marble temple; providing a path for the people of the earth, so that they might proclaim the wonders of God. Verse: “But coming they shall come with exultation, carrying their sheaves.” Providing a path.

Foebus and Cornelius, the disciples of blessed Clement, said to the people: “Let us all pray to the Lord that he may show us the body of his martyr.”

As Saint Clement prayed, the Lamb of God appeared to him.

They found a dwelling prepared by God in the form of a marble temple.

Responsory. At the dedication of the temple the people sang praise, and a sweet sound resounded from their mouths. Verse. In hymns and confessions they blessed the Lord. And from their mouths. Responsory. The house of the Lord has been founded upon the summit of the mountains and exalted above the hills; all nations shall come to it and say: Glory to you, O Lord. Verse. Bless, O Lord, this house which I have built for your name. And they shall come. Verse. Coming, however, as above. Responsory. If my lord shall have been. Verse. Truly the Lord is in this place. Verse. Therefore, rising early, Jacob took the stone which he had placed beneath his head [Col. 0830B], set it up as a pillar, and poured oil over it, saying: It shall be for me.

## In the second nocturn

Antiphon. This is nothing other than the house of God and the gate of heaven. Psalm: “How lovely.” Antiphon. Jacob saw a ladder whose top touched the heavens, and angels descending, and he said: Truly this place is holy. Psalm: “Its foundations.” Antiphon. Jacob set up a stone as a pillar, pouring oil over it. Psalm: “O Lord, God of my salvation.” Verse. My house.

Responsories as above.

Responsory. The Lord shall be my God. Verse. If the Lord God. Verse. If I return. Responsory. You heard, O Lord, my prayer. Verse. You who reign. Verse. O Lord, who keep the covenant. Responsory. O Lord, if you have turned. Verse. You who reign. Verse. If your people sin against you.

## In the third nocturn

[Col. 0830C]

Antiphon. He who dwells in the help of the Most High shall abide under the protection of the God of heaven. Psalm: “He himself.” Antiphon. The temple of the Lord is holy; it is the worship of God, the building of God. Psalm: “Sing.” 1. Antiphon. Blessed is the glory of the Lord from his place. Psalm: “The Lord reigns; let the earth rejoice.” Verse. This is the house of the Lord.

Responsories as above.

Responsory. You, O Lord of all. Verse. You who reign. Responsory. Hear, O Lord, the hymn. Verse. Look down from the sanctuary. Responsory. Look down, O Lord, upon this house which I have built for your name. Hear, O Lord, the prayers of those coming to this place, from the lofty throne of your glory. 856 Verse. Hear, O Lord, the prayers which your servant pours out before you, that you may open your eyes over this house. Which I have built. Verse. Blessed are those who dwell in your house, O Lord; for ever and ever they shall praise you. Hear. Responsory. You have brought your saints into the preparation which your hands prepared, O Lord. Verse. This is the house of the Lord and the gate of heaven. Responsory. The house of the Lord has been founded upon the summit of Mount Zion, and upon its peak let the mother Church rejoice; all nations shall come to it and rejoice, because in it the voice of gladness shall sing. Verse. Mother Zion shall say: “A man, and a man, was born in her.” And the Most High himself founded her. Responsory. All your walls are precious stones, and the towers shall be built with gems, and its fortifications with pure gold. Verse. There are twelve gates, twelve pearls, and the twelve pearls themselves are precious stones. Verse. This is the house of the Lord and the gate of heaven. And it shall be called the hall of God. Responsory. On Mount Horeb, the mountain of God, [he] saw God’s tabernacle shining with a great light, in which the angels sing, saying: Truly this is the house of God, the dwelling of the saints. Verse. Great is the Lord.

## Antiphons at Matins and Lauds

Antiphon. Holiness befits your house, O Lord, throughout the length of days [Col. 0831A]. Antiphon. My house shall be called a house of prayer. Antiphon. This is the house of the Lord, firmly built and well founded upon a firm rock. Antiphon. The house of the Lord is well founded upon a firm rock. Antiphon. All your walls are precious stones, and the towers of Jerusalem shall be built with gems. Verse. The house has been founded.

## In the Gospel

Antiphon. O how fearful this place is! Truly this is nothing other than the house of God and the gate of heaven. Antiphon. Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, because today I must remain in your house. And he hurried down and received him joyfully in his house. Today salvation from God has come to this house, alleluia. Antiphon. Rising in the morning, Jacob set up the stone as a pillar, pouring oil over it, and made a vow to God. Truly this place is holy, and I did not know it. Antiphon. The Lord sanctified his tabernacle, because this is the house of God, in which his name shall be invoked, concerning whom it is written: “And my name shall be there,” says the Lord [Col. 0831B]. Antiphon. You shall sprinkle me, O Lord, with hyssop, and I shall be clean; you shall wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. Psalm: “Have mercy on me, O God.” Behold, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field which the Lord has blessed. Antiphon. The Lord sanctified his tabernacle; God is in its midst, and it shall not be moved. Psalm: “God is our refuge.”

[Note: [Col. 0831D] Amalarius discusses these antiphons and the following responsories at length in *The Book on the Order of the Antiphoner*, chapter 70 and following.]

## Antiphons from the Hymn of the Three Young Men

Antiphon. Three were walking in the furnace of fire and praising the Lord the King together; singing with one mouth, they said a hymn: Blessed are you, God, alleluia. Antiphon. I see a man like the Son of God strengthening the young men in the furnace of fire, alleluia. Antiphon. Three sang with one mouth to the great King: Glory in the highest to God, alleluia. Antiphon. Three cried out with one mouth in the furnace of fire and sang: Blessed is God. Antiphon. Let us praise glorious men who conquered the kingdoms of the world, alleluia. Antiphon. I see three men walking through the midst of the fire, and the appearance of the fourth is like the Son of God, alleluia [Col. 0831C]. Antiphon. Let us sing a hymn, 857 alleluia, to the Lord our God, alleluia. Antiphon. Blessed are you, O Lord, who behold the abysses and sit upon the cherubim, alleluia. Antiphon. Blessed is the Lord of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who rescued his servants from the furnace of burning fire, alleluia. Antiphon. Three young men were walking in the furnace of fire, and the Son of God was in their midst, and they sang a hymn to God, alleluia. Antiphon. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego sang a hymn to the great King as though with one mouth, alleluia. Antiphon. In the furnace of fire three young men praised God with one mouth, alleluia. Antiphon. Three young men were walking in the furnace of fire, and God the King was among them; and they said: We have God as King. Antiphon. The king’s servants did not cease feeding the flame so that they might burn the holy young men of God. From heaven came something like a spirit of blowing dew; it provided refreshment to the holy ones. Antiphon. Three young men in the furnace, prefiguring the Trinity and trampling underfoot the threats of the fire, sang these praises: Blessed are you, God of our fathers, alleluia. Antiphon. Three young men were thrown into the furnace at the king’s command; they did not fear the flame of the fire, but said: Blessed is God [Col. 0831D]. Antiphon. Ananias, Azariah, Mishael, bless the Lord for ever. Antiphon. Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, great servants of the Most High God. Antiphon. Sing a hymn and exalt him above all for ever, and bless him. Antiphon. Praise and exalt the Lord above all for ever, and bless him. Antiphon. Blessed are you in the firmament of heaven, and praiseworthy, glorious, and exalted above all for ever. Antiphon. In the furnace of burning fire were three young men, and God the King was in their midst. With one voice they said: Blessed are you, God. Antiphon. There is a God in heaven whom we serve (cujus [cui]: “whose [whom]”) [Col. 0832A]. He is able to rescue us from the furnace of fire and deliver us from your hands, O king.

[Five lines are missing in the manuscript.]

[Note: [Col. 0831D] They were sung from the second Sunday after Pentecost until the month of August. See Amalarius, *On the Order of the Antiphoner*, in the prologue [Col. 0832D].]

## Responsories from the Book of Kings

Responsory. The hearer of all is God; he himself sent his angel and took me from my father’s sheep, and anointed me with the anointing of his mercy. Verse. The Lord who rescued me from the mouth of the lion and delivered me from the hand of the beast. And he anointed me. Responsory. The Lord who rescued me from the mouth of the lion and delivered me from the hand of the beast—he himself will rescue me from the hands of my enemies. Verse. God sent his mercy and his truth; he rescued my soul from the midst of lions’ cubs. He himself. Responsory. David prevailed over the Philistine with sling and stone, in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel. Verse. So that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel, because the Lord saves neither by sword nor by spear. Of hosts. Responsory. “I took you from your father’s house,” says the Lord, “and appointed you to make [pascere, “pasture”] the flock of my people, and I was with you wherever you walked, establishing your kingdom for ever.” Verse. O you who rule Israel, attend, you who lead Joseph like a sheep. And I was with you. Responsory. Mountains of Gilboa, let neither dew nor rain come upon you, where the mighty men of Israel fell. Verse. May the Lord visit all the mountains surrounding it; may he pass from Gilboa, where they fell. Responsory. I have sinned beyond the number of the sand of the sea, 858 and my sins have multiplied; I am not worthy to see the height of heaven because of the multitude of my iniquity, for I have provoked your anger and done evil before you. Verse. For I myself acknowledge my iniquity, and my offense is always before me; against you alone I have sinned. Responsory. Remember, O Lord, your covenant, and say to the striking angel: Let your hand now cease, so that the earth may not be laid waste and you may not destroy every living soul. Verse. Let your anger, O Lord, rest from your people and from your holy city. So that. Responsory. You heard, O Lord, the prayer of your servant, that I might build a temple to your name. Bless and sanctify this house for ever, God of Israel [Col. 0832C]. Verse. You who rule, as above. Responsory. O Lord, if your people should turn back and pray toward your sanctuary, you will hear them in heaven, O Lord, and deliver them from the hands of their enemies. Verse. If your people sin against you, and, turning back, do penance, and come and pray in this place. You will hear. Responsory. Hear, O Lord, the hymn and the prayer with which your servant prays before you today, that your eyes may be open and your ears attentive over this house day and night. Verse. You who rule, [Note: [Col. 0832D] This extends to “appear before Ephraim,” etc., in the same psalm: “You who rule.”] until “appear.” Responsory. Prepare your hearts for the Lord and serve him, and he will deliver you from the hands of your enemies. Verse. Remove foreign gods from your midst. And he will deliver you. Responsory. When the Lord was about to take Elijah by a whirlwind into heaven, Elisha cried out, saying: My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its charioteer. Verse. I pray, O Lord, that your spirit may be doubled in me. But he said: If you see me when I am taken from you, it shall be as you have asked. Elisha.

## Antiphons from the same book

[Col. 0832D]

Antiphon. Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening. Antiphon. All, from Dan to Beer-sheba, knew that Samuel was a faithful prophet of the Lord. Antiphon. David prevailed over the Philistine with sling and stone, in the name of the Lord. Antiphon. Is this not David, of whom they sang in the chorus, saying: Saul struck down a thousand, and David ten thousand among his thousands? Antiphon. Angry, Saul said: They gave me a thousand, but to the son of Jesse they gave ten thousand. Antiphon. For who among all [Note: [Col. 0832D] In the manuscript, *d* is often used for *t*, and conversely.] was found faithful like David (sicud [sicut], “like”) in your kingdom, going out and coming back, and proceeding at the king’s command? Antiphon. And all the people said to Samuel: Pray for us to the Lord your God, so that we may not all die for our sins. Antiphon. When David saw the angel striking the people, he said to the Lord: I am the one who sinned; I acted wickedly. What have these people, who are sheep, done? Turn away, I beg you, O Lord, your anger from your people, alleluia. Antiphon. King David, walking with his head covered, mourned his son, saying: Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Who would grant that I might die for you, my son Absalom?

[Note: [Col. 0833D] For the Sundays of August, from the same Amalarius, at the place cited, except the first Sunday.]

## Responsories from the Wisdom of Solomon

Responsory. Send forth, O Lord, wisdom from the seat of your greatness, so that she may be with me and labor with me, that I may know what is acceptable before you at all times. Verse. Give me, O Lord, wisdom, attendant of your thrones. So that. Responsory. Lord, Father and God of my life, do not abandon me to a wicked thought. 859 Do not give me haughtiness of eyes, and turn away from me evil desire (desiderio [desiderium] maligno), O Lord [Col. 0833B]. Take concupiscence away from me, and do not hand me over, O Lord, to an irreverent and undisciplined mind. Verse. Give me, O Lord, as above. And to an undisciplined mind. Responsory. Give me, O Lord, wisdom, attendant of your thrones, and do not reject me from among your children, for I am your servant and the son of your handmaid. Verse. Lord, Father and God of my life, do not abandon me to a wicked thought. Responsory. Alone I traversed the circuit of heaven and walked upon the waves of the sea. Among every nation and every people I held the primacy; by my own power I trampled the necks of the proud and exalted. Verse. I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud. Of the proud. Responsory. The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord; good understanding belongs to those who practice it. Its praise endures for ever and ever. Verse. He distributed and gave to the poor. Its praise. Responsory. Keep wicked and deceitful speech far from me, O Lord; do not give me riches or poverty, but grant me only what is necessary for my sustenance. Verse. Lest, when I am satisfied, I vomit it up and perjure the name of my God. But. Responsory [Col. 0833C]. Do not abandon me, Lord and Father, ruler of my life, lest I fall before my adversaries and my enemy rejoice over me. Verse. Take up arms and shield, as above. Lest he rejoice. Responsory. For your judgments are great, O Lord, and your words beyond telling; you have magnified the people and honored them. Verse. You led your people like sheep, by the hand of Moses and Aaron. You have magnified. Responsory. I loved wisdom above health and every beauty, and I resolved to have her for my light. All good things came to me together with her. Verse. I said to wisdom: You are my sister; and, O my soul, I called prudence. They came. Responsory. Your eyes see what is in the hearts of human beings, O Lord, and everything shall be written in your book. A human being sees the face, but God sees the heart. Verse. Your eyes saw my unfinished state. And in. Responsory. My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes keep watch over my ways, so that grace may be added to your head. Verse. Attend, my son, to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my words. So that grace may be added. Responsory. In the beginning, before God made the earth, before he established the abysses, before he brought forth the springs of waters, before the mountains were set in place, before all the hills, the Lord generated me. Verse. I dwell in the highest places. Before all the hills.

[Three lines are missing in the manuscript.]

## Antiphons from the same book

Antiphon. Solomon, my son, know the God of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and a humble mind. Antiphon. Wisdom built herself a house; she hewed out seven pillars. She subjected nations to herself and by her own power trampled the necks of the proud and exalted. Antiphon. I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud. Antiphon. Wisdom cries out in the streets: If anyone loves wisdom, let him turn aside to me, and he will find her; and when he has found her, he is blessed if he keeps her [Col. 0834A]. Antiphon. The Lord possessed me at the beginning of his ways, before he made anything from the beginning. The abysses did not yet exist, and I was already being brought forth; when he prepared the heavens, I was present, arranging 860 all things with him at all times. Antiphon. All wisdom is from the Lord God, and it was always with him, and exists before the age.

[Note: [Col. 0834D] For the second and third Sundays of September, from the aforementioned Amalarius, in the same place.]

## Responsories concerning blessed Job

Responsory. If we receive good things from the hand of the Lord, why should we not endure evil? The Lord gave, the Lord has taken away; as it pleased the Lord, so it has happened. Blessed be the name of the Lord. Verse. In all these things Job did not sin with his lips, nor did he speak anything foolish against God. Responsory. Before I eat, I sigh, and my roaring is like overflowing waters, because the fear which I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened. Have I not dissembled? Have I not been silent and already rested? And your mercy, O Lord, has come upon me. Verse. Let him not contend with me in great strength, nor crush me with the weight of his greatness; let him set justice before me [Col. 0834B]. Responsory. Would that my sins, by which I deserved anger, and the calamity which I suffer were weighed in a balance! Verse. It would appear heavier than the sand of the sea; therefore my words are full of sorrow. And the calamity. Responsory. Why have you undermined words of truth? You prepare words for rebuke and strive to overthrow your friend. Nevertheless, carry out what you have devised. Verse. A human being’s life upon earth is a warfare, and his days are like the days of a hired laborer. Nevertheless. Responsory. My flesh is clothed with decay, and my skin has dried up and contracted with the filth of dust. Remember me, O Lord, for my life is a breath. Verse. My days have declined like a shadow, and I have dried up like grass. Remember. Responsory. Remember me, God, for my life is a breath; let no human sight look upon me. Verse. From the depths I cried to you, O Lord; Lord, hear my voice. Let no human sight look upon me. Responsory. The shortness of my days is quickly ending. Leave me, O Lord; let me mourn my sorrow a little [Col. 0834C], before I go to a land dark and covered with the shadow of death. Verse. Behold, I sit in dust and sleep in dust; and if you seek me in the morning, I shall not remain. Before I go. Responsory. Do not hide me, O Lord, from your face. Take your hand far from me, and let not your dread terrify me. Verse. Call me, and I shall answer you; or let me speak, and you answer me. Take your hand. Responsory. Who will grant that you protect me in the underworld and hide me until your fury passes, O Lord? Unless it is you, who alone are God, who can appoint a time at which you will remember me? Verse. Are your days like human days, that you seek my iniquity, when there is no one who can rescue from your hand? Unless it is you. Responsory. Does the Lord overturn judgment, or does the Almighty subvert what is just? Deliver me, O Lord, and set me beside you, and let any hand fight against me. Verse. Take up arms and shield, and rise to help me. Deliver me. Responsory. At night my mouth is pierced with pains, and those who devour me do not sleep. By their multitude my garment is consumed [Col. 0834D]. I am compared to clay and made like dust and ashes. Verse. O guardian of human beings, why have you set me against you, and made me burdensome to myself? Spare me, O Lord, for my days are nothing. I am compared. Responsory. I know, O Lord, that you will deliver me to death, where every house of the living has been appointed. I hope in you, O Lord, because you do not stretch out your hand for my destruction; and if I should be plunged into the depths of the underworld, 861 you will deliver me from there. Verse. If I ascend into heaven, you are there; if I descend into the underworld. From there.

## Antiphons from the same book

Antiphon. When Job heard the words of the messengers, he endured patiently and said: If we have received good things from the hand of the Lord, why should we not endure evil? In all these things Job did not sin with his lips, nor did he speak anything foolish against God. Antiphon. In all these things Job did not sin with his lips, nor did he speak anything foolish against God. Antiphon. How many iniquities and sins I have—show me. Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?

[One line is missing in the manuscript.]

[Note: [Col. 0835D] Amalarius assigns these to the last Sunday of September, at the place already cited.]

## Responsories concerning Tobit

Responsory. I ask, O Lord, that you release me from this bond of reproach, or at least take me up from the earth. Do not remember my sins or those of my parents, and do not take vengeance for my sins, because you rescue those who endure you, O Lord. Verse. You who rule Israel, attend, you who lead Joseph like a sheep. Do not remember. Responsory. Bless God at all times, and ask him to direct your ways, and at all times let your plans remain in him. Verse. Remember, son, that we lead a poor life. You will have many good things if you fear God. And at all times. Responsory. Remember, son, that we lead a poor life. You will have many good things if you fear God. Verse. Almsgiving is a great confidence before the Most High God for all who practice it. You will have. Responsory. Our poverty was sufficient for us, as though riches were being counted. Would that that money had never existed, for which you sent our son away, the staff of our old age. Verse. Alas, my son! Why did we send you to travel abroad, the light of our eyes? The staff. Responsory. Bless God, O heavens, and before all the living we shall confess him, because he has shown us his mercy. Verse. It is time for me to return to him who sent me; but you, bless God and recount all his wonders. Verse. Bless God, O heavens, and before all the living we shall confess him. And recount.

## Antiphons from the same book

Antiphon. Do not remember, O Lord, my sins or those of my parents, and do not take vengeance for my sins [Col. 0835C]. Antiphon. Remember, son, that we lead a poor life. You will have many good things if you fear God. Antiphon. Bless God at all times.

[Note: [Col. 0835D] Responsories from Judith and Esther are noted there [Col. 0836D] for the first two Sundays of October.]

## Responsories concerning Judith

Responsory. Adonai, Lord, great and wonderful God, who have given salvation by the hand of a woman, hear the prayers of your servants. Verse. You who rule, as above. Responsory. We have heard of the tribulations of the cities which they suffered, and we have fainted. Fear and dullness of mind fell upon us and upon our children. The mountains themselves do not wish to receive our flight. O Lord, have mercy. Verse. You who rule, as above. Verse. We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted unjustly; we have committed iniquity. O Lord, have mercy. Responsory. The Lord has blessed you by his strength; through you he has 862 reduced our enemies to nothing, so that your praise may not fail from the mouths of human beings. Verse. Blessed are you by the Lord God Most High, above all women. So that your praise may not fail. Responsory. We know no other God besides the Lord, in whom we hope; he does not despise us or remove salvation from our race [Col. 0835D]. Verse. For all the gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens. He does not. Responsory. Lord, ruler of the heavens and earth, creator of the waters, King of all your creation, hear the prayer of your servants. Verse. You who rule. Verse. You, O Lord, whose pleasure has always been in the prayer of the humble and meek. Hear. Responsory. O Lord God, who crushes wars from the beginning, raise your arm over the nations that devise evil against your servants, and let your right hand be glorified in us. Verse. You who rule. Verse. Strike down their strength by your strength; let their power fall in your anger. And your right hand. Responsory. You who are in the towers, open the gates. The almighty Lord has acted with strength and given victory over our enemies [Col. 0836A]. Verse. Praise the Lord our God, who has not abandoned those who hope in him and has fulfilled in me the mercy which he promised to the house of Israel. Verse. Praise the Lord, all nations, and praise him together, all peoples.

## Antiphon from the same book

Antiphon. Adonai, Lord, great and wonderful God, who have given salvation by the hand of a woman, hear the prayers of your servants.

## Responsories concerning Esther

Responsory. Lord, almighty King, all things have been placed under your authority, and no one can resist your will. Deliver us for the sake of your name. Verse. You who rule. Verse. Hear our prayer and turn our mourning into joy. For the sake. Responsory. Strengthen me, King of the holy ones, who hold the sovereignty, and give a right word to my mouth. Verse. Give us, O Lord, a place for repentance, and do not shut the mouths of those who sing to you, O Lord. And give. Responsory. Have mercy, O Lord, on your people, because our enemies desire to destroy us and erase your inheritance. Do not despise your portion, which you redeemed from Egypt. But turn our mourning into joy, so that, while living, we may praise you, O Lord. Verse. You who rule. Verse. Hear our supplication, and be favorable to the lot and measuring-line of your inheritance. But turn our mourning. Responsory. Give us, O Lord, a place for repentance, and do not shut the mouths of those who sing to you, O Lord. Verse. Do not hand over your scepter, O Lord, to those who are nothing, lest they return to our ruin. And do not shut. Responsory. Remember me, O Lord, as above. Verse. You who rule. Responsory. I have never placed my hope in anyone other than you, God of Israel, who become angry and then show mercy, and who forgive all human sins in tribulation. Verse. Lord God of heaven and earth, look upon our humility.

## Antiphon from the same book

Antiphon. Lord, almighty King, all things have been placed under your authority, and no one can resist your will [Col. 0836C].

Responsory. Remember me, O God, for good, and do not blot out 863 my acts of mercy, which I performed in the house of my God and in his ceremonies. Verse. Remember your word to your servant, O Lord, in which you gave me hope. In. Verse. Remember me, O Lord my God. And do not blot out.

## Antiphon from the same book

Antiphon. Remember, O Lord, and show yourself to us in the time of tribulation.

[Note: [Col. 0836D] For the last two Sundays of October, from the same Amalarius.]

## Responsories from the Book of Maccabees
The Lord may open your hearts to his law and his commandments, and grant peace in our days. May he grant you salvation and redeem you from evils.  
**Verse.** May the Lord hear your prayers and be reconciled to you. May he grant it.

**Response.** Yours is the power, yours the kingdom, O Lord. You are over all nations. [Col. 0836D] Grant peace, O Lord, in our days.  
**Verse.** You who rule—you are he.  
**Verse.** God, Creator of all, terrible and strong, just and merciful. Grant peace.

**Response.** The sun shone upon the golden shields, and the mountains gleamed from them, and the strength of the nations was scattered.  
**Verse.** “I shall break the bonds of my people,” says the Lord, “and I shall destroy all the evils that I brought upon him.” And the strength—

**Response.** Do not fear the attack of the enemies. Remember how our fathers were saved. And now let us cry to heaven, and our God will have mercy on us.  
**Verse.** Remember his wonders, which he performed for Pharaoh and his army, whom he cast into the sea. And now—

**Response.** They adorned the façade of the temple with golden crowns and dedicated the altar to the Lord; and great joy arose [Col. 0837A] among the people.  
**Verse.** In hymns and acts of thanksgiving they blessed God. And great joy arose—

**Response.** In hymns and acts of thanksgiving they blessed the Lord, because he has done great things in Israel, and the Lord almighty has given them victory.  
**Verse.** They adorned the façade of the temple with golden crowns and dedicated the altar to the Lord. For he has done great things.

**Response.** Our enemies have gathered together and boast in their strength. Crush their power, O Lord, and scatter them, so that they may know that there is no other who fights for us but you, our God.  
**Verse.** Scatter them by your power and destroy them, our protector, O Lord. So that they may know—

**Response.** Judas said to his brothers: “Choose men for yourself and go; rescue your brothers in Galilee. But I and my brother Jonathan shall go to Gilead. As it is the will in heaven, so let it be.”  
**Verse.** And now let us cry to heaven, and he will have mercy on us. As it is the will—

**Response.** This is the lover of his brothers and of the people of Israel; this is he who prays much for the people and for the whole holy city of Jerusalem.  
**Verse.** Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together. And for the whole—

**Response.** May the Lord hear your prayers and be reconciled to you; and may the Lord your God not abandon you in the time of trouble.  
**Verse.** May the Lord open your hearts to his law and his commandments, and may the Lord grant peace.

**Response.** The nations have gathered in great numbers to fight against us, and we do not know what we should do. O Lord God, our eyes are turned toward you; let us not perish.  
**Verse.** You who rule.  
**Verse.** You know what they are planning against us; how shall we be able to stand before them unless you help us? O Lord God—

**Response.** You, Lord of all, who have no need of anything, have willed that your temple should be made within us. Preserve this house undefiled forever, O Lord.  
**Verse.** You who rule. Preserve it.

### Antiphons for the same.

**Antiphon.** Judah, Israel, mourned with great lamentation and said: “How has the mighty one fallen, who was saving the Lord’s people?”

**Antiphon.** May the Lord open [Col. 0837C] your hearts to his law and his commandments, and grant peace.

**Antiphon.** Yours is the power, yours the kingdom, O Lord. You are over all nations. Grant peace, O Lord, in our days.

**Antiphon.** “I shall break the bonds of my people,” says the Lord, “and I shall destroy all the evils that I brought upon him.”

[Note: [Col. 0837D] For the Sundays of November, according to Amalarius, in the same place.]

### Responses from the Minor Prophets [one from the Major Prophets].

**Response.** I saw the Lord seated upon a high and lofty throne. And the whole earth was full of his majesty; and the things beneath him filled the temple.  
**Verse.** The seraphim also stood beside it: six wings for one and six wings for the other. And the whole earth was full—

**Response.** Look, O Lord, from your holy seat and consider us. Incline your ear, my God, and hear; open your eyes and see our tribulation.  
**Verse.** O Shepherd of Israel, attend; you who lead Joseph like a sheep, you who sit upon the cherubim. Open—

**Response.** Look, O Lord, for the city once full of riches has been laid waste. [Col. 0837D] The mistress of the nations sits in sadness; no one consoles her except you, O God.  
**Verse.** “They say, ‘Lay it bare, lay it bare, even to its foundation!’ O wretched daughter of Babylon.”

**Response.** Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen; all day and all night they shall not cease praising the name of the Lord.  
**Verse.** You who remember the Lord, do not be silent, and do not grant him silence. All day—

**Response.** Surround us, O Lord, with your impregnable wall, and always protect us with the arms of your power. Deliver us, Lord God of Israel, who cry out to you.  
**Verse.** You who rule.  
**Verse.** Deliver us through your wonders, and give glory to your name. And with the arms—

**Response.** We hoped for peace, but it did not come. We sought good things, and behold, trouble. We have acknowledged our sins, O Lord; do not forget us forever.  
**Verse.** We sinned with our fathers; we acted unjustly; we committed iniquity. [Col. 0838A] Do not forget us forever.

**Response.** I, Daniel, prayed to my God, saying: “Hear, O Lord, the prayers of your servant; shine your face upon your sanctuary, and look favorably upon this people, over whom your name has been invoked, O God.”  
**Verse.** You who rule.

**Response.** The Lord sent his angel and shut the mouths of the lions; and they did not defile me, because righteousness was found in me before him.  
**Verse.** God sent his mercy, as above.

**Response.** Distress surrounds me on every side, and I do not know what to choose. It is better for me to fall into the hands of men than to abandon the law of my God.  
**Verse.** For if I do this, death awaits me; but if I do not, I shall not escape your hands.

**Response.** A praiseworthy people whom the Lord of hosts blessed, saying: “You are the work of my hands, my inheritance, Israel.”  
**Verse.** You who rule. The work—  
**Verse.** Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people chosen as his inheritance. The work—

**Response.** The Lord redeemed his people; they shall come and rejoice on Mount Zion, and delight in the good things of the Lord, in grain, wine, and oil; and they shall hunger no more.  
**Verse.** They have multiplied from the fruit of grain, wine, and oil. And they shall hunger no more.

**Response.** At the face of your wrath, O God, the whole earth was troubled; but you, O Lord, have mercy, and do not bring it to an end.  
**Verse.** You who rule.  
**Verse.** Turn us, O God our salvation, and turn your anger away from us. And do not—

*(Three lines are missing in the manuscript.)*

## The antiphons for Sundays begin, from the Octave of Pentecost until the Advent of the Lord

### Sunday 1

[Col. 0841D]

**Antiphon.** There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and feasted splendidly every day. And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus. It happened that the beggar died and was carried by angels into Abraham’s bosom.

**Antiphon.** It happened that the beggar died and was carried by angels into Abraham’s bosom.

**Antiphon.** “Father Abraham,” as above.

**Antiphon.** That rich man.

**Antiphon.** Son, remember.

*(Two lines are missing in the manuscript.)*

### Sunday 2

**Antiphon.** A certain man prepared a great dinner and invited many; and at dinner time he sent his servant to say to those invited that they should come, because everything is ready, says the Lord.

**Antiphon.** Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and compel the poor, the weak, the blind, and the lame to enter, so that my house may be filled, alleluia. [Col. 0842A]

**Antiphon.** I tell you that none of those men shall taste my dinner.

### Sunday 3

**Antiphon.** Which of you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost until he finds it?

**Antiphon.** Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost, says the Lord.

**Antiphon.** Or which woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and overturn the house and search carefully until she finds it?

**Antiphon.** I tell you, there is joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents.

### Sunday 4

**Antiphon.** Be merciful, therefore, just as your Father is merciful, says the Lord.

**Antiphon.** Do not judge, so that you may not be judged; for with the judgment with which you judge, you shall be judged, says the Lord.

**Antiphon.** They will give a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and overflowing, into your lap. [Col. 0842B]

### Sunday 5

**Antiphon.** When the crowds pressed in to hear the word of the Lord, he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret. The fishermen, however, had gone down and were washing their nets for the catch.

**Antiphon.** Jesus went up into the boat and, sitting down, taught the crowds, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** “Teacher, we worked all night and caught nothing; but at your word I shall let down the net.”

**Antiphon.** When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girded his tunic around himself, threw himself into the sea, and cried out in a loud voice, saying: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord.”

**Antiphon.** The Lord said to Simon: “Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching men.”

**Antiphon.** Peter was walking upon the waves of the sea. A strong wind came, and the water was troubled. Crying out in fear, he said: “Lord, command me to come to you.” Jesus said to him: “Come, you of little faith; why did you doubt?” 870

[Col. 0842C] *(Two lines are missing in the manuscript.)*

**Antiphon.** Unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven.

**Antiphon.** You have heard that it was said to the ancients: “You shall not kill”; and whoever kills shall be liable to judgment.

**Antiphon.** If you offer your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go first to be reconciled with your brother. Then come and offer your gift, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers, who also stripped him, inflicted wounds upon him, and went away, leaving him half dead.

**Antiphon.** “Who, in your opinion, was the neighbor of the man who fell among robbers?” And he said to him: “The one who showed mercy toward him.” “Go, and you do likewise,” alleluia.

### Sunday 14

[Col. 0843C]

**Antiphon.** As Jesus was passing through a certain village, ten leprous men met him. They stood at a distance and raised their voices, saying: “Jesus, Teacher, have mercy on us.”

**Antiphon.** Ten leprous men stood at a distance and raised their voices, saying: “Jesus, Teacher, have mercy on us.”

**Antiphon.** One of them, when he saw that he had been cleansed, returned, glorifying God with a loud voice, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** “Were not ten cleansed? And where are the nine? Was no one found to return and give glory to God except this foreigner?” “Go, your faith has saved you,” alleluia.

### Sunday 15

**Antiphon.** Look at the birds of the sky, for they neither sow nor reap, but your heavenly Father feeds them, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They neither labor nor spin. But I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these. [Col. 0843D]

**Antiphon.** Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life—what you will eat—or about your body—what you will wear.

**Antiphon.** Do not be anxious, saying: “What shall we eat?” or “What shall we drink?” For your heavenly Father knows what you need, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** Seek therefore first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

### Sunday 16

**Antiphon.** Jesus approached and touched the bier. Those who carried it stood still. And he said: “Young man, I say to you, arise.” The dead man sat up and began to speak, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** Fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying: “A great prophet has arisen among us,” and “God has visited his people.”

### Sunday 17

**Antiphon.** When Jesus entered the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him. [Col. 0844A]

**Antiphon.** When you are invited to a wedding, recline in the lowest place, so that the one who invited you may say: “Friend, move up higher.” Then you will have honor before all who recline with you, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

### Sunday 18

**Antiphon.** “Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?” Jesus said to him: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart,” alleluia.

**Antiphon.** “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They all said: “David.” Jesus answered and said: “How then does David, in the Spirit, call him Lord, saying: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand’?”

**Antiphon.** For you are all brothers, and do not call anyone your father on earth; for one is your Father, who is in heaven. And do not be called teachers, because one is your teacher, Christ.

**Antiphon.** For one is your teacher, Christ the Lord, who is in heaven. [Col. 0844B]

**Antiphon.** The greater among you shall be your servant, because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, says the Lord.

### Sunday 19

**Antiphon.** The Lord said to the paralytic: “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven,” alleluia.

**Antiphon.** The Lord Jesus said: “Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Rise and walk’?”

**Antiphon.** But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, alleluia—

**Antiphon.** Jesus says to him: “Son, your sins are forgiven; rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.”

**Antiphon.** Then the paralytic took up the bed on which he had lain, glorifying God. And when all the people saw it, they gave praise to God.

**Antiphon.** When the crowds saw it, they were afraid and glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.

### Sunday 20

**Antiphon.** The Lord said to the vineyard worker: [Col. 0844C] “Behold, it is three years since I have been coming, seeking fruit on the fig tree, and I have found none.”

**Antiphon.** Say to those invited: “Behold, I have prepared the meal; come to the wedding,” alleluia.

**Antiphon.** The wedding is indeed ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.

**Antiphon.** Go therefore to the crossroads, and invite to the wedding whomever you find, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** “Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment?” But he was silent. Then the king said: “Bind him hand and foot and cast him into the outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth,” alleluia.

**Antiphon.** There was a certain royal official whose son was ill at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus was coming into Galilee, he begged him to heal his son. “Lord, come down, so that you may heal my son before he dies.” And Jesus said to him: “Go; your son lives,” alleluia. [Col. 0844D]

**Antiphon.** “Wicked servant, I forgave you the entire debt; should you not therefore have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?”

**Antiphon.** For she said within herself: “If I only touch the fringe of his garment, I shall be saved.”

**Antiphon.** If I touch the fringe of his garment, I shall be able to be saved from my illness.

**Antiphon.** But Jesus turned and, seeing her, said: “Take courage, daughter; your faith has saved you,” alleluia.

**Antiphon.** When Jesus raised his eyes and saw a very large crowd coming toward him, he said to Philip: “Where shall we buy bread so that these people may eat?” For he himself knew what he was going to do.

Be perfect; be at peace; and the God of love and peace will be with you, alleluia.

Be strengthened in the grace of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord, alleluia.

For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy of comparison with the future glory that will be revealed in us.

Glorify and bear God in your body.

Be watchful and pray; act manfully, and let all that is yours be done in love.

Let there be for you one heart directed toward God, and one soul.

You know that when you were Gentiles, you went off to mute idols, being led wherever you were led.

[Col. 0845C] Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says, “Anathema to Jesus.” And no one can say, “The Lord Jesus,” except in the Holy Spirit, alleluia.

Let hope, faith, and love remain in us—these three; but the greatest of these is love, alleluia.

The peace of the Lord, which surpasses all understanding, guards your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus our Lord.

For we were buried with Christ through baptism into death, so that, just as he rose from the dead, we too might walk in newness of life, alleluia.

God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God, and God in him.

Let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God, alleluia.

For the wages of sin are death, but the grace of God is eternal life, alleluia.

## On the Nativity of the Lord

[Note: [Col. 0845D] Here there is no mention of Prime or Compline, although it is clear from Amalarius in various passages that these hours belonged at that time to the ecclesiastical course, or office. At Prime and Compline, however, the same Responsories and the same Verses always recur; here, on the other hand, different ones are assigned according to the variety of the feasts, at Terce, Sext, and so forth. [Col. 0846D]]

## On the Lord’s Supper, at the Washing of the Feet

**Antiphon.** I give you a new commandment: that you love one another as I have loved you, says the Lord.  
**Psalm.** Blessed are the undefiled.

**Antiphon.** After the Lord rose from supper, he poured water into a basin and began to wash the feet of the disciples. He left them this example.  
**Psalm.** May God have mercy on us.

**Antiphon.** The Lord Jesus Christ, after he had supped with his disciples, as above.  
**Psalm.** Praise the Lord, for he is good.

**Antiphon.** When the Lord Jesus Christ had risen from supper, he put on his garments. He began to wash the feet of his disciples and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded. Let us therefore imitate him, so that we may have peace in his kingdom.  
**Psalm.** I will bless the Lord.

**Antiphon.** In those days, a woman who was a sinner in the city, when she learned that Jesus was reclining in the house of Simon the leper, brought an alabaster jar of ointment. And standing behind him at the feet of the Lord Jesus, she began to bathe his feet with tears; she wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with ointment.  
**Psalm.** Have mercy on me, O God, according to …

**Antiphon.** Let us love one another, because love is from God, and whoever loves his brother is born of God. And see [he sees] God.  
**Psalm.** Behold, how good …

**Antiphon.** If I, the Lord and Master, have washed your feet, how much more ought you to wash one another’s feet?  
**Psalm.** How lovely …

**Antiphon.** By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.  
**Psalm.** Give thanks to the Lord and call upon him.

**Antiphon.** The Almighty spoke to his disciples, saying: Come and see the deceptive peace that the traitor has brought forth; he pretends to love me with his lips, but the hatred of his heart has brought forth death. Anathema: Aramachamatale [Maranatha, “Our Lord, come”], the disciple.

**Antiphon.** While the Lord was reclining at table, he took bread and gave it to his disciples, saying: Take and eat this bread, and know that this is my body. And this cup also, and drink from it, and know that this is my blood of the new Testament; it is poured out for all [for] the remission of sins.

**Antiphon.** The Lord spoke to his disciples: For I have given you an example, so that you may wash one another’s feet, because by this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.

**Antiphon.** Where charity and love are, there is a holy assembly; there is neither anger nor indignation, but firm love forever. Christ descended to redeem the world, so that he might free humanity from death. He gave his disciples an example, so that they might wash one another’s feet.

**Antiphon.** Lord, do you wash my feet? Jesus answered and said to him: If I do not wash your feet, you will have no part with me.

**Antiphon.** Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head.

**Antiphon.** You call me Teacher and Lord.

**Antiphon.** The woman who was a sinner in the city.

**Antiphon.** But Mary anointed the feet of Jesus.

**Antiphon.** Christ gathered us together to glorify himself. Fill, O Lord, our souls with the Holy Spirit, alleluia.

[Col. 0849]

# Hymns composed by Blessed Pope Gregory (G, S)

## On Sunday

[Col. 0849]

### At Matins

1. On the first of all the days,  
   When the world was created,  
   Or when the Creator, rising again,  
   Frees us after conquering death.

2. Once all torpor has been driven far away,  
   Let us all rise swiftly  
   And seek the merciful one by night,  
   As we know the prophet did.

3. So that he may hear our prayers  
   And extend his right hand,  
   And, cleansed from defilements,  
   Restore us to the dwellings of heaven.

4. So that each of us, during the most sacred  
   Hours of this day,  
   May sing psalms during the hours of rest  
   And be enriched with blessed gifts.

5. Now, Fatherly Brightness,  
   We earnestly ask you:  
   Let sordid desire be absent,  
   And every harmful deed.

6. May the structure of our body  
   Be neither foul nor slippery,  
   Lest through it we ourselves  
   Be burned more fiercely in the fires of hell.

7. For this reason, Redeemer, we ask  
   That you wash away our sins  
   And graciously bestow upon us  
   The blessings of eternal life.

8. So that, exiled from the act of the flesh,  
   Made ourselves celibate,  
   As we await you bowed down,  
   We may sing the melody of glory.

9. Grant this, most merciful Father,  
   O Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,  
   Reigning with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
   Through every age.

### Another

1. Rising at night, let us all keep watch;  
   Let us meditate always in the Psalms, and  
   With all our strength sing sweetly  
   Hymns to the Lord.

2. So that, singing together to the merciful King,  
   We may deserve to enter with his saints  
   The court of heaven, and together  
   Lead a blessed life.

3. May the blessed Godhead of the Father,  
   And of the Son, and likewise of the Holy Spirit,  
   Grant this to us; his glory resounds  
   Throughout the whole world. Amen.

### At Lauds

[Col. 0849]

1. Behold, now the shadow of night grows thin;  
   The shining dawn of light flashes forth.  
   With all our strength let us all beseech  
   The Almighty.

2. May our God, having shown mercy to all,  
   Drive away every sickness and grant salvation;  
   May he also, through the Father’s mercy,  
   Grant us the kingdoms of heaven.

3. May the blessed Godhead grant this to us,  
   As above.

### At Vespers

1. O best Creator of light,  
   Bringing forth the light of day,  
   At the beginnings of new light  
   Preparing the world’s origin.

2. You command the morning joined to evening  
   To be called day;  
   While dreadful chaos pours down,  
   Hear our prayers with tears.

3. May the mind burdened with sin  
   Not be exiled from the gift of life,  
   While it thinks of nothing enduring  
   And binds itself to sins.

4. May it strike the innermost heaven,  
   May it take up the life-giving reward;  
   Let us avoid every harmful thing  
   And cleanse every evil.

# In Lent

### At Matins

1. The bright glory of fasting  
   Is shown to the world from heaven,  
   Which Christ, the author of all,  
   Consecrated by abstaining from food.

2. By this Moses became dear to God  
   And was made the giver of the Law;  
   By this Elijah was raised through the air  
   In a chariot of fire.

3. By this Daniel, conqueror of lions,  
   Had seen the mysteries;  
   Through this the intimate friend  
   Of the Bridegroom, John, became renowned.

4. Grant that we may follow these gifts, O God,  
   These examples of restraint;  
   Increase the strength of our minds,  
   Giving spiritual joy. Amen.

### At Vespers

1. Hear, gracious Creator,  
   Our prayers with tears,  
   Poured out in this sacred  
   Forty-day fast.

[Col. 0850]

2. Loving searcher of hearts,  
   You know the weakness of our strength;  
   To those who return to you  
   Show the grace of forgiveness.

3. We have indeed sinned greatly;  
   But spare those who confess.  
   To the praise of your name  
   Bring healing to the sick.

4. Grant that the body may be worn down outwardly  
   Through abstinence,  
   So that the sober mind may fast  
   Completely from the stain of sins.

5. Grant, blessed Trinity;  
   Bestow, simple Unity,  
   That the gifts of fasting  
   May be fruitful for your people. Amen.

# On Palm Sunday

1. Let every age rejoice  
   With great joy in salvation;  
   Jesus, Redeemer of all,  
   Healed the ailing world.

2. Six days before Easter  
   He came to Bethany,  
   Where, in his goodness, after three days  
   He raised Lazarus.

3. Mary took a pound  
   Of the finest pure nard;  
   She anointed the blessed feet  
   Of the Lord, bathing them with tears.

4. After this, Jesus, the heavenly judge,  
   Sat upon the foal  
   Of a yoked she-ass; he proceeded  
   Toward renowned Jerusalem.

5. O how astonishing the goodness,  
   The wondrous mercy of God!  
   The author of the world  
   Deigns to become the rider of a little donkey.

6. A great crowd had taken green branches,  
   Cut from a tender palm;  
   It went out to meet  
   The eternal King.

7. Honor, power, and dominion  
   Be to the one Trinity,  
   To the Father, the Son, and the Paraclete,  
   Through endless ages. Amen.

# On the Passion of the Lord

1. Christ the King, maker of all,  
   Redeemer also of believers,  
   Be appeased by the prayers  
   Of those who worship you with praises.

2. By whose kindly grace,  
   Through the blessed wounds of the cross,  
   He has broken by his power  
   The bonds of our first parent.

3. You who are the creator of the stars  
   Assumed a covering of flesh,  
   Deigning to endure  
   This most grievous form of suffering.

[Col. 0851]

4. You were bound in order to free  
   The companions of the falling world;  
   By your shame you wiped away the sins  
   Which the world had greatly increased.

5. You are fastened to the cross, Redeemer,  
   Yet you shake the whole earth;  
   You surrender your mighty spirit,  
   And the world grows dark.

[Col. 0852]

6. Soon, shining victorious  
   At the summit of the Father’s glory,  
   Defend us, best of Kings,  
   With the protection of the Spirit.

Amen.

# Appendix

[Note: [Col. 0851] Consult the notice prefixed by us to this volume. EDITOR.]

# Ancient Ritual Books of the Holy Roman Church

[Col. 0851]

# Preliminary Commentary on the Roman Order

## I. Knowledge of the Roman rites is necessary; Amalarius’s commentaries on them assailed. The first edition of the Roman Ritual disapproved; the plagiarism of the elected archbishop of Corcyra exposed.

[Col. 0851A]

Since the Roman Church is the standard and model of the other Churches, especially those of the West, it is of no small importance to the Christian commonwealth that the sacred rites by which, from the beginning of the established religion, it has worshiped the most good and great God should be known and clearly understood by all.
